entries.zh: 四年，大軍伐齊，盛為後一軍總管。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jiande (575), when the great army attacked Qi, Sheng was rear first army commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, when the great army attacked Qi, Sheng was rear first army commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 五年，大軍又東討，盛率所領，拔齊高顯等數城。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jiande (576), when the great army again marched east, Sheng led his command and captured several Qi cities including Gaoxian.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, when the great army again marched east, Sheng led his command and captured several Qi cities including Gaoxian.

entries.zh: 幷州平，進位上柱國。
entries.en: When Bingzhou was pacified, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: When Bingzhou was pacified, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 從平鄴，拜相州總管。
entries.en: Following the pacification of Ye, he was appointed commander-in-chief of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: Following the pacification of Ye, he was appointed Xiangzhou commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 宣政元年，入為大冢宰。
entries.en: In the first year of Xuanzheng (578), he entered office as grand minister of state.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he entered office as grand minister of state.

entries.zh: 汾州稽胡帥劉受邏干反，詔盛率諸軍討平之。
entries.en: Liu Shouluogan, a Ji Hu leader in Fen Province, rebelled; an edict ordered Sheng to lead the armies and pacify him.
entries.literal: Liu Shouluogan, Ji Hu leader in Fen Province, rebelled; an edict ordered Sheng to lead the armies and pacify him.

entries.zh: 大象元年，遷大前疑，轉太保。
entries.en: In the first year of Daxiang (579), he was transferred to grand front advisor and then to grand guardian.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was transferred to grand front advisor and then to grand guardian.

entries.zh: 其年，詔以豐州武當、安富二郡邑萬戶為越。
entries.en: That year, an edict made Wudang and Anfu commanderies in Fengzhou, with ten thousand households, Yue's fief.
entries.literal: That year, an edict made Wudang and Anfu commanderies in Fengzhou, ten thousand households, Yue's fief.

entries.zh: 盛出就國。
entries.en: Sheng went out to take up his fief.
entries.literal: Sheng went out to take up his state.

entries.zh: 二年，朝京師。
entries.en: In the second year of Daxiang (580), he attended court in the capital.
entries.literal: In the second year, he attended court in the capital.

entries.zh: 其秋，為隋文帝所害，并其子忱、悰、恢、懫、忻等五人，國除。
entries.en: That autumn he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his sons Chen, Cong, Hui, Man, and Xin, five in all; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: That autumn he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his sons Chen, Cong, Hui, Man, and Xin, five in all; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 代奰王達，字度斤突。
entries.en: Prince of Dai the Proud Yuwen Da, styled Dujintu.
entries.literal: Prince of Dai the Proud Da, styled Dujintu.

entries.zh: 性果決，善騎射。
entries.en: By nature he was resolute and decisive, skilled in horsemanship and archery.
entries.literal: By nature he was resolute and decisive, skilled in horsemanship and archery.

entries.zh: 武成初，封代國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Dai with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Dai state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 天和元年，拜大將軍、右宮伯，拜左宗衞。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianhe (566), he was appointed grand general and right palace elder, and left guard commander.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, he was appointed grand general and right palace elder, and left guard commander.

entries.zh: 建德初，進位柱國，出為荊淮等十四州十防諸軍事、荊州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jiande (572), he advanced to pillar-of-state and went out as commander-in-chief of military affairs in fourteen provinces including Jing and Huai and ten defenses, and as governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he advanced to pillar-of-state and went out as commander-in-chief of military affairs in fourteen provinces including Jing and Huai and ten defenses, and governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 在州有政績，高祖手勑襃美之。
entries.en: In the province he had administrative achievements; Yuwen Yong personally wrote an edict praising him.
entries.literal: In the province he had administrative achievements; the High Ancestor personally wrote an edict praising him.

entries.zh: 所管灃州刺史蔡澤黷貨被訟，贓狀分明。
entries.en: Cai Ze, governor of Feng Province under his jurisdiction, was sued for corruption; the evidence was clear.
entries.literal: Cai Ze, governor of Feng Province under his jurisdiction, was sued for corrupt taking; the evidence of bribery was clear.

entries.zh: 以其世著勳庸，不可加戮；
entries.en: Because his house was long distinguished in merit, he could not be executed;
entries.literal: Because his house was long distinguished in merit, he could not be put to death;

entries.zh: 若曲法貸之，又非奉上之體。
entries.en: yet bending the law to pardon him would not accord with serving the throne.
entries.literal: yet if the law were bent to pardon him, that would not accord with serving the court.

entries.zh: 乃令所司，精加按劾，密表奏之。
entries.en: He therefore ordered the responsible offices to investigate thoroughly and submitted a secret memorial.
entries.literal: He therefore ordered the responsible offices to investigate thoroughly and submitted a secret memorial.

entries.zh: 事竟得釋，終亦不言。
entries.en: The matter ended in release, yet he never spoke of it.
entries.literal: The matter ended in release, yet in the end he never spoke of it.

entries.zh: 其處事周慎如此。
entries.en: He handled affairs with such thorough caution.
entries.literal: In handling affairs he was this thorough and cautious.

entries.zh: 達雅好節儉，食無兼膳，侍姬不過數人，皆衣綈衣。
entries.en: Da loved frugality: his meals had no double dishes, his serving women numbered only a few, and all wore plain silk.
entries.literal: Da by nature loved frugality: his meals had no double dishes, his serving women numbered no more than a few, and all wore plain silk.

entries.zh: 又不營資產，國無儲積。
entries.en: He also did not accumulate property; his fief had no stores.
entries.literal: He also did not accumulate property; his state had no stores.

entries.zh: 左右嘗以為言，達從容應之曰：「君子憂道不憂貧，何煩於此。」
entries.en: Those around him once spoke of this; Da calmly replied: "The noble person worries about the Way, not poverty—why trouble over this?"
entries.literal: Those around him once spoke of this; Da calmly replied: "The noble person worries about the Way, not poverty—why trouble over this?"

entries.zh: 三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 出為益州總管。
entries.en: He went out as commander-in-chief of Yizhou.
entries.literal: He went out as Yizhou commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 高祖東伐，以為右一軍總管。
entries.en: When Yuwen Yong marched east, he was made right first army commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor marched east, he was made right first army commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 齊淑妃馮氏，尤為齊後主所幸，齊平見獲，帝以達不邇聲色，特以馮氏賜之。
entries.en: Lady Feng, refined consort of Qi, was especially favored by the Later Lord of Qi; when Qi fell she was captured, and because Da did not indulge in music and beauty, the emperor specially bestowed Lady Feng upon him.
entries.literal: Lady Feng, refined consort of Qi, was especially favored by the Later Lord of Qi; when Qi was pacified she was captured, and because Da did not draw near to music and beauty, the emperor specially bestowed Lady Feng upon him.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，進位上柱國。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 大象元年，拜大右弼。
entries.en: In the first year of Daxiang (579), he was appointed grand right assistant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was appointed grand right assistant.

entries.zh: 其年，詔以潞州上黨郡邑萬戶為代。
entries.en: That year, an edict made Shangdang commandery in Luzhou, with ten thousand households, Dai's fief.
entries.literal: That year, an edict made Shangdang commandery in Luzhou, ten thousand households, Dai's fief.

entries.zh: 達出就國。
entries.en: Da went out to take up his fief.
entries.literal: Da went out to take up his state.

entries.zh: 二年，朝京。
entries.en: In the second year of Daxiang (580), he attended court in the capital.
entries.literal: In the second year, he attended court in the capital.

entries.zh: 其年冬，為隋文帝所害，及其世子執、弟蕃國公轉等，國除。
entries.en: That winter he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his heir Zhi and younger brother Duke of Fan Zhuan; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: That winter he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his heir Zhi and younger brother Duke of Fan Zhuan; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 冀康公通，字屈率突。
entries.en: Duke of Ji the Peaceful Yuwen Tong, styled Qushuotu.
entries.literal: Duke of Ji the Peaceful Tong, styled Qushuotu.

entries.zh: 武成初，封冀國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 天和六年十月，薨。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tianhe (571), he died.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tianhe, he died.

entries.zh: 子絢嗣。
entries.en: His son Xuan succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Xuan succeeded.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 大象中，為隋文帝所害，國除。
entries.en: During Daxiang (579–581), he was killed by Yang Jian; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: In the Daxiang era, he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 滕聞王逌，字爾固突。
entries.en: Prince of Teng the Cultivated Yuwen You, styled Er'gutu.
entries.literal: Prince of Teng the Cultivated You, styled Er'gutu.

entries.zh: 少好經史，解屬文。
entries.en: From youth he loved the classics and histories and was skilled in literary composition.
entries.literal: From youth he loved the classics and histories and understood literary composition.

entries.zh: 武成初，封滕國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wucheng (559), he was enfeoffed Duke of Teng with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was enfeoffed Duke of Teng state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 天和末，拜大將軍。
entries.en: At the end of Tianhe (572), he was appointed grand general.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianhe, he was appointed grand general.

entries.zh: 建德初，進位柱國。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jiande (572), he advanced to pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he advanced to pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 六年，為行軍總管，與齊王憲征稽胡。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Jiande (577), he was mobile commander-in-chief and, with Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian, campaigned against the Ji Hu.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was mobile commander-in-chief and, with Prince of Qi Xian, campaigned against the Ji Hu.

entries.zh: 逌破其渠帥穆友等，斬首八千級。
entries.en: You defeated their chieftains including Mu You and took eight thousand heads.
entries.literal: You defeated their chieftains including Mu You and beheaded eight thousand.

entries.zh: 還，除河陽總管。
entries.en: On return, he was made commander-in-chief of Heyang.
entries.literal: On return, he was made Heyang commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 宣政元年，進位上柱國。
entries.en: In the first year of Xuanzheng (578), he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 其年，伐陳，詔逌為元帥，節度諸軍事。
entries.en: That year, on the campaign against Chen, an edict made You supreme commander directing all military affairs.
entries.literal: That year, on the campaign against Chen, an edict made You supreme commander directing all military affairs.

entries.zh: 大象元年五月，詔以荊州新野郡邑萬戶為滕。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Daxiang (579), an edict made Xinye commandery in Jingzhou, with ten thousand households, Teng's fief.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Daxiang, an edict made Xinye commandery in Jingzhou, ten thousand households, Teng's fief.

entries.zh: 逌出就國。
entries.en: You went out to take up his fief.
entries.literal: You went out to take up his state.

entries.zh: 二年，朝京。
entries.en: In the second year of Daxiang (580), he attended court in the capital.
entries.literal: In the second year, he attended court in the capital.

entries.zh: 其年冬，為隋文帝所害，并子懷德公祐、祐弟箕國公裕、弟禮禧等，國除。
entries.en: That winter he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his son Duke of Huaide You, You's younger brother Duke of Ji Yu, and younger brother Lixi; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: That winter he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his son Duke of Huaide You, You's younger brother Duke of Ji Yu, and younger brother Lixi; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 逌所著文章，頗行於世。
entries.en: You's writings circulated widely in his day.
entries.literal: Writings composed by You circulated widely in the world.

entries.zh: 紀厲王康，字乾定。
entries.en: Prince of Ji the Stern Yuwen Kang, styled Qianding.
entries.literal: Prince of Ji the Stern Kang, styled Qianding.

entries.zh: 保定初，封紀國公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Baoding (561), he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji state, fief ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 仍出為總管利始等五州、大小劍二防諸軍事、利州刺史。
entries.en: He then went out as commander-in-chief of Li, Shi, and three other provinces, the defenses of Greater and Lesser Sword, and all related military affairs, and as governor of Li Province.
entries.literal: He then went out as commander-in-chief of Li, Shi, and three other provinces, the two defenses of Greater and Lesser Sword, and all military affairs, and governor of Li Province.

entries.zh: 康驕矜無軌度，信任僚佐盧奕等，遂繕脩戎器，陰有異謀。
entries.en: Kang was arrogant and lawless, trusting aides such as Lu Yi; he repaired weapons and secretly plotted rebellion.
entries.literal: Kang was arrogant and without measure, trusting his aides such as Lu Yi; he then repaired weapons of war and secretly harbored different intent.

entries.zh: 司錄裴融諫止之，康不聽，乃殺融。
entries.en: Recorder Pei Rong remonstrated with him; Kang refused to listen and killed Rong.
entries.literal: Recorder Pei Rong remonstrated and stopped him; Kang would not listen and then killed Rong.

entries.zh: 五年，詔賜康死。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Jiande (575), an edict granted him death.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered Kang to die by grant.

entries.zh: 子湜嗣。
entries.en: His son Shi succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Shi succeeded.

entries.zh: 大定中，為隋文帝所害，國除。
entries.en: During Dading (581), he was killed by Yang Jian; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: In the Dading era, he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 畢剌王賢，字乾陽。
entries.en: Prince of Bi the Impetuous Yuwen Xian, styled Qianyang.
entries.literal: Prince of Bi the Impetuous Xian, styled Qianyang.

entries.zh: 保定四年，封畢國公。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Baoding (564), he was enfeoffed Duke of Bi.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, he was enfeoffed Duke of Bi state.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 出為華州刺史，遷荊州總管，進位柱國。
entries.en: He went out as governor of Hua Province, was transferred to commander-in-chief of Jing Province, and advanced to pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of Hua Province, was transferred to Jing Province commander-in-chief, and advanced to pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 宣政中，入為大司空。
entries.en: During Xuanzheng (578), he entered office as grand minister of works.
entries.literal: In the Xuanzheng era, he entered office as grand minister of works.

entries.zh: 大象初，進位上柱國、雍州牧、太師。
entries.en: At the beginning of Daxiang (579), he advanced to senior pillar-of-state, governor of Yong Province, and grand preceptor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he advanced to senior pillar-of-state, governor of Yong Province, and grand preceptor.

entries.zh: 明年，宣帝崩。
entries.en: The next year Emperor Xuan (Yuwen Yun) died.
entries.literal: The next year, Emperor Xuan died.

entries.zh: 賢性強濟，有威略。
entries.en: Xian was forceful and resolute, with authority and strategic sense.
entries.literal: Xian by nature was forceful and resolute, with authority and strategy.

entries.zh: 慮隋文帝傾覆宗社，言頗泄漏，尋為所害，幷其子弘義、恭道、樹孃等，國除。
entries.en: Fearing Yang Jian would overthrow the dynasty, he let his views slip; soon he was killed, together with his sons Hongyi, Gongdao, and Shuniang; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Fearing that Emperor Wen of Sui would overturn the ancestral temple, his words leaked somewhat; soon he was killed by him, together with his sons Hongyi, Gongdao, and Shuniang, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 酆王貞，字乾雅。
entries.en: Prince of Feng Yuwen Zhen, styled Qianya.
entries.literal: Prince of Feng Zhen, styled Qianya.

entries.zh: 初封酆國公。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Feng.
entries.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed Duke of Feng state.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 大象初，為大冢宰。
entries.en: At the beginning of Daxiang (579), he was grand steward.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was grand minister of war.

entries.zh: 後為隋文帝所害，幷子濟陰郡公德文，國除。
entries.en: Later he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his son Duke of Jiyin Dewen; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Later he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his son Duke of Jiyin commandery Dewen; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 漢王贊，字乾依。
entries.en: Prince of Han Yuwen Zan, styled Qianyi.
entries.literal: Prince of Han Zan, styled Qianyi.

entries.zh: 初封漢國公。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Han.
entries.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed Duke of Han state.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王，仍柱國。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince while remaining pillar-of-state.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince, still pillar-of-state.

entries.zh: 大象末，隋文帝輔政，欲順物情，乃進上柱國、右大丞相。
entries.en: At the end of Daxiang (581), Yang Jian directed the government and, wishing to placate opinion, advanced him to senior pillar-of-state and right grand chancellor.
entries.literal: At the end of Daxiang, Emperor Wen of Sui assisted the government and, wishing to accord with popular sentiment, advanced him to senior pillar-of-state and right grand chancellor.

entries.zh: 外示尊崇，寔無綜理。
entries.en: Outwardly he was honored; in fact he held no real authority.
entries.literal: Outwardly showing honor and esteem, in truth there was no overall governance.

entries.zh: 及諸方略定，又轉太師。
entries.en: When the realm was pacified, he was transferred to grand preceptor.
entries.literal: When the various regions were settled, he was again transferred to grand preceptor.

entries.zh: 尋為隋文帝所害，幷其子淮陽公道德、弟道智、道義等，國除。
entries.en: Soon he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his son Duke of Huaiyang Daode and younger brothers Daozhi and Daoyi; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Soon he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his son Duke of Huaiyang Daode and younger brothers Daozhi and Daoyi; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 秦王贄，字乾信。
entries.en: Prince of Qin Yuwen Zan, styled Qianxin.
entries.literal: Prince of Qin Zan, styled Qianxin.

entries.zh: 初封秦國公。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Qin.
entries.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed Duke of Qin state.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 上柱國、大冢宰、大右弼。
entries.en: He held the offices of senior pillar-of-state, grand steward, and grand right assistant.
entries.literal: Senior pillar-of-state, grand steward, grand right assistant.

entries.zh: 尋為隋文帝所害，并其子忠誠公靖智、弟靖仁等，國除。
entries.en: Soon he was killed by Yang Jian, together with his son Duke of Zhongcheng Jingzhi and younger brother Jingren; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: Soon he was killed by Emperor Wen of Sui, together with his son Duke of Zhongcheng Jingzhi and younger brother Jingren; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 曹王允，字乾仕。
entries.en: Prince of Cao Yuwen Yun, styled Qianshi.
entries.literal: Prince of Cao Yun, styled Qianshi.

entries.zh: 初封曹國公。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Cao.
entries.literal: Initially he was enfeoffed Duke of Cao state.

entries.zh: 建德三年，進爵為王。
entries.en: In the third year of Jiande (574), he was advanced to prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiande, he advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 明帝三男。
entries.en: Emperor Ming (Yuwen Yu) had three sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming had three sons.

entries.zh: 徐妃生畢剌王賢，後宮生酆王貞、宋王寔。
entries.en: Consort Xu bore Prince of Bi the Impetuous Xian; ladies of the rear palace bore Prince of Feng Zhen and Prince of Song Shi.
entries.literal: Consort Xu bore Prince of Bi the Impetuous Xian; the rear palace bore Prince of Feng Zhen and Prince of Song Shi.

entries.zh: 武帝生七男。
entries.en: Emperor Wu (Yuwen Yong) had seven sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu had seven sons.

entries.zh: 李皇后生宣帝、漢王贊，厙汗姬生秦王贄、曹王允，馮姬生道王充，薛世婦生蔡王兌，鄭姬生荊王元。
entries.en: Empress Li bore Emperor Xuan and Prince of Han Zan; Consort Kuhan bore Prince of Qin Zan and Prince of Cao Yun; Lady Feng bore Prince of Dao Chong; Lady Xue bore Prince of Cai Dui; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Jing Yuan.
entries.literal: Empress Li bore Emperor Xuan and Prince of Han Zan; Consort Kuhan bore Prince of Qin Zan and Prince of Cao Yun; Lady Feng bore Prince of Dao Chong; Lady Xue bore Prince of Cai Dui; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Jing Yuan.

entries.zh: 荊王元，字乾儀。
entries.en: Prince of Jing Yuwen Yuan, styled Qianyi.
entries.literal: Prince of Jing Yuan, styled Qianyi.

entries.zh: 宣政元年，封王。
entries.en: In the first year of Xuanzheng (578), he was enfeoffed as prince.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was enfeoffed prince.

entries.zh: 元及兌、充、允等竝為隋文帝所害，國除。
entries.en: Yuan together with Dui, Chong, Yun, and the others were all killed by Yang Jian; their fiefs were abolished.
entries.literal: Yuan together with Dui, Chong, Yun, and the rest were all killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 郢王術，大象二年，封王。
entries.en: Prince of Ying Shu; in the second year of Daxiang (580), he was enfeoffed as prince.
entries.literal: Prince of Ying Shu; in the second year of Daxiang, he was enfeoffed prince.

entries.zh: 與
entries.en: Together with
entries.literal: Together with

entries.en: [variant: Yan]
entries.literal: (Yan)

entries.zh: 衎並為隋文帝所害，國除。
entries.en: Together with Kan they were all killed by Yang Jian; their fiefs were abolished.
entries.literal: Kan they were all killed by Emperor Wen of Sui; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 宣帝三子。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan had three sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan had three sons.

entries.zh: 朱皇后生靜皇帝，王姬生鄴王
entries.en: Empress Zhu bore Emperor Jing (Yuwen Chan); a royal lady bore Prince of Ye
entries.literal: Empress Zhu bore Emperor Jing; a royal lady bore Prince of Ye

entries.en: [variant: Yan]
entries.literal: (Yan)

entries.zh: 衎，皇甫姬生郢王術。
entries.en: Kan, and Lady Huangfu bore Prince of Ying Shu.
entries.literal: Kan, and Lady Huangfu bore Prince of Ying Shu.

entries.zh: 夫皇王迭興，為國之道匪一；
entries.en: Sovereigns and kings rise in succession; the way to found a state is not single;
entries.literal: Sovereigns and kings rise in succession; the way of establishing a state is not one alone;

entries.zh: 賢聖間出，立德之指殊塗。
entries.en: worthies and sages appear in turn; the aim of establishing virtue takes different paths.
entries.literal: the worthy and sage appear in turn; the aim of establishing virtue takes different paths.

entries.zh: 斯豈故為相反哉，亦云治而已矣。
entries.en: Surely this is not deliberate contradiction—it is simply governance.
entries.literal: How could this be deliberately made opposite? It is also said: to govern—that is all.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: How so?
entries.literal: How so?

entries.zh: 五等之制，行於商周之前；
entries.en: The system of five ranks operated before Shang and Zhou;
entries.literal: The system of five ranks operated before Shang and Zhou;

entries.zh: 郡縣之設，始於秦漢之後。
entries.en: the establishment of commanderies and counties began after Qin and Han.
entries.literal: the establishment of commanderies and counties began after Qin and Han.

entries.zh: 論時則澆淳理隔，易地則用舍或殊。
entries.en: Times differ, so decadence and purity are worlds apart; circumstances differ, so what is adopted or abandoned may vary.
entries.literal: Judging the times, then decadence and purity are separated in principle; changing the place, then use and rejection may differ.

entries.zh: 譬猶干戈日用，難以成垓下之業；
entries.en: It is like using arms daily—hard to accomplish the enterprise of Gaixia;
entries.literal: It is like arms used daily—hard to accomplish the enterprise of Gaixia;

entries.zh: 稷嗣所述，不可施成周之朝。
entries.en: what Jisi (Shusun Tong) set forth cannot be applied in the court of accomplished Zhou.
entries.literal: what Jisi set forth cannot be applied in the court of accomplished Zhou.

entries.zh: 是知因時制宜者，為政之上務也；
entries.en: Thus adapting measures to the times is the supreme task of governing;
entries.literal: Thus to adapt measures to the times is the supreme task of governing;

entries.zh: 觀民立教者，經國之長策也。
entries.en: observing the people to establish teaching is the long strategy of ordering a state.
entries.literal: observing the people to establish teaching is the long strategy of ordering the state.

entries.zh: 且夫列封疆，建侯伯，擇賢能，置牧守，循名雖曰異軌，責實抑亦同歸。
entries.en: Demarcating territory, enfeoffing marquises and earls, selecting the worthy, appointing governors and defenders—by name the tracks differ, but in demanding real results they aim at the same end.
entries.literal: Moreover, demarcating territory, establishing marquises and earls, selecting the worthy and able, setting governors and defenders—by name it is called a different track, but in demanding reality it likewise returns to one end.

entries.zh: 盛則與之共安，衰則與之共患。
entries.en: In prosperity they share security; in decline they share calamity.
entries.literal: In prosperity they share security with it; in decline they share calamity with it.

entries.zh: 共安系乎善惡，非禮義無以敦風；
entries.en: Shared security depends on conduct; without ritual and righteousness custom cannot be tempered;
entries.literal: Shared security depends on good and evil; without ritual and righteousness there is no way to temper custom;

entries.zh: 共患寄以存亡，非甲兵不能靖亂。
entries.en: shared calamity rests on survival or extinction; without arms disorder cannot be stilled.
entries.literal: shared calamity rests on survival or extinction; without arms and armor disorder cannot be stilled.

entries.zh: 是以齊、晉帥禮，鼎業傾而復振；
entries.en: Thus Qi and Jin led with ritual, and the royal enterprise tilted yet revived;
entries.literal: Thus Qi and Jin led with ritual, and the tripod enterprise tilted yet revived;

entries.zh: 溫、陶釋位，王綱弛而更張。
entries.en: Huan Wen and Tao Kan relinquished rank, and the royal framework slackened yet was drawn tight again.
entries.literal: Wen and Tao relinquished rank, and the royal net slackened yet was drawn tight again.

entries.zh: 然則周之列國，非一姓也，晉之群臣，非一族也，豈齊、晉強于列國，溫、陶賢於群臣者哉，蓋勢重者易以立功，權輕者難以盡節故也。
entries.en: Zhou's feudal states were not of one surname; Jin's ministers were not of one clan—were Qi and Jin stronger than the other states, and Wen and Tao worthier than other ministers? Heavy power makes merit easy; light authority makes full loyalty hard.
entries.literal: Then Zhou's feudal states were not of one surname, and Jin's ministers were not of one clan—were Qi and Jin stronger than the feudal states, and Wen and Tao worthier than the ministers? It was that heavy power is easy for establishing merit, and light authority is hard for fulfilling loyalty.

entries.zh: 由此言之，建侯置守，乃古今之異術；
entries.en: From this we see that enfeoffing princes and appointing governors are techniques that differ between antiquity and the present;
entries.literal: From this speaking, establishing marquises and setting defenders are techniques of antiquity and the present that differ;

entries.zh: 兵權勢位，蓋安危之所階乎。
entries.en: military authority, power, and position are the steps on which security and danger depend.
entries.literal: military authority, power, and position are surely the steps on which security and danger depend.

entries.zh: 太祖之定關右，日不暇給，旣以人臣禮終，未遑藩屏之事。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai settled Guanzhong, he had no leisure; having died in the status of a minister, he had no time to enfeoff a princely screen.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor settled Guanzhong, days allowed no leisure; having ended in the rites of a subject, he had no time for the screen of the feudal princes.

entries.zh: 晉蕩輔政，爰樹其黨，宗室長幼，竝據勢位，握兵權，雖海內謝隆平之風，而國家有磐石之固矣。
entries.en: Yuwen Hu assisted the government and planted his faction; senior and junior of the imperial house alike held power and grasped military authority—though peace within the realm was gone, the state had the solidity of bedrock.
entries.literal: Jin the Reckless assisted the government and thereupon planted his faction; senior and junior of the imperial clan alike held power and position, grasped military authority—though within the seas the breeze of great peace was gone, yet the state had the solidity of bedrock.

entries.zh: 高祖克翦芒刺，思弘政術，懲專朝之為患，忘維城之遠圖，外崇寵位，內結猜阻。
entries.en: Yuwen Yong cut away rivals, intending to improve governance, punishing court monopoly while forgetting the long-range plan of a princely bulwark; outwardly he honored rank, inwardly he bred suspicion.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor cut away thorns, thinking to expand governing arts, punishing the harm of monopolizing the court while forgetting the far plan of protecting the wall; outwardly he honored favored rank, inwardly he bred suspicion and obstruction.

entries.zh: 自是配天之基，潛有朽壤之墟矣。
entries.en: From then the foundation that should match Heaven secretly held crumbling ruin.
entries.literal: From then the foundation matching Heaven secretly had ground of crumbling ruin.

entries.zh: 宣皇嗣位，凶暴是聞，芟刈先其本枝，削黜遍於公族。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan succeeded; cruelty and violence were notorious; he mowed down the root branches of the clan and cut away the royal kin throughout.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne; cruelty and violence were what was heard; he mowed down first the root branches and cut away throughout the public clan.

entries.zh: 雖復地惟叔父，親則同生，文能附衆，武能威敵，莫不謝卿士于當年，從侯服於下國。
entries.en: Though in title they were the emperor's uncles, born of the same house, able in civil matters to win followers and in martial to awe foes—all alike resigned high office and wore a lesser lord's dress.
entries.literal: Though again in territory they were the emperor's uncles, in kin they were born of the same womb, in civil matters able to win the multitude, in martial able to awe the enemy—none failed to yield ministerial rank in that year and follow marquis's garb in a lesser state.

entries.zh: 號為千乘，勢侔匹夫。
entries.en: Titled lords of a thousand chariots, in power they were no more than commoners.
entries.literal: Called a thousand chariots, in power they matched a common man.

entries.zh: 是以權臣乘其機，謀士因其隙，遷龜鼎速於俯拾，殲王侯烈于燎原。
entries.en: Thus powerful ministers seized their chance, strategists their openings; shifting the sacred tripod was swift as picking something up, and extinguishing princes fierce as a prairie fire.
entries.literal: Thus powerful ministers rode their opportunity, strategists exploited their gaps; moving the sacred tripod was swift as picking up what lay before one, extinguishing princes and kings fierce as a prairie fire.

entries.zh: 悠悠邃古，未聞斯酷。
entries.en: In remote antiquity such cruelty was unheard of.
entries.literal: In remote deep antiquity such cruelty was not heard.

entries.zh: 豈非摧枯振朽，易為力乎。
entries.en: Was it not that withering the withered and shaking the rotten makes change easy?
entries.literal: Was it not that withering the withered and shaking the rotten, change was easy in power?

entries.zh: 大統三年秋，至長安。
entries.en: In the autumn of Datong 3 (537) he reached Chang'an.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Datong, he reached Chang'an.

entries.zh: 自以虧損國威，上書謝罪。
entries.en: Believing he had shamed the state, he wrote to apologize for his failure.
entries.literal: Considering himself to have diminished the state's prestige, he submitted a memorial apologizing for his offense.

entries.zh: 魏文帝付尚書議之，七兵尚書、陳郡王
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Wei referred the matter to the Masters of Writing—the Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei handed the matter to the Masters of Writing for deliberation—the Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery

entries.zh: （王言）
entries.en: [variant: Wang Yan]
entries.literal: (Wang Yan)

entries.zh: 玄等議，以為「邊將董戎，龔行天罰，喪師敗績，國刑無舍。
entries.en: Xuan and others deliberated, saying: "Frontier generals who bear Heaven's mandate to chastise wrongdoers and yet lose their armies—the law knows no mercy.
entries.literal: Xuan and others deliberated, saying: "Frontier generals who marshal troops and carry Heaven's punishment—when they lose the army and fail in the campaign, the state punishment allows no pardon.

entries.zh: 荊州刺史獨孤如願，任當推轂，遠襲襄、宛，斬賊帥辛纂，傳首京師，論功語效，寔合嘉賞。
entries.en: Jing Province governor Du Guxin, entrusted with full command, had raided deep into Xiang and Wan, beheaded the rebel leader Xin Zuan, and sent his head to the capital—a feat that plainly merited reward.
entries.literal: Jing Province governor Dugu Ruyuan, his charge being to push the chariot, made a distant raid on Xiang and Wan, beheaded the bandit chief Xin Zuan, and sent his head to the capital; in reckoning merit and speaking of achievement, he truly deserved fine reward.

entries.zh: 但庸績不終，旋致淪沒，責成之義，朝寄有違。
entries.en: Yet his success was not sustained and he was soon lost; by the rule that a commission must be fulfilled, he had failed the court's trust.
entries.literal: Yet meritorious deeds were not carried through and he soon fell into ruin; the principle of completing the charge—the court's trust was violated.

entries.zh: 然孤軍數千，後援未接，賊衆我寡，難以自固。
entries.en: Still, he had only a few thousand men with no reinforcements, outnumbered and unable to stand alone.
entries.literal: Still, a lone army of several thousand with rear support not yet joined—bandits many, we few—it was hard to hold firm on one's own.

entries.zh: 旣經恩降，理絕刑書。
entries.en: Grace had already been shown him, so the penal code no longer applied.
entries.literal: Since grace in reduction of punishment had already been granted, reason excludes the criminal code.

entries.zh: 昔秦宥孟明，漢舍廣利，卒能改過立功，垂芳竹帛。
entries.en: Qin once spared Meng Ming and Han forgave Li Guangli; both went on to redeem themselves and win lasting fame.
entries.literal: Formerly Qin pardoned Meng Ming and Han spared Guangli; in the end they were able to reform their faults and establish merit, leaving fragrance in the bamboo and silk.

entries.zh: 以今方古，抑有成規。
entries.en: Comparing present with past, there was clear precedent.
entries.literal: Measuring the present against antiquity, there is indeed an established rule.

entries.zh: 臣等參議，請赦罪，復其舊職」。
entries.en: We your ministers therefore ask that his offense be pardoned and his former office restored."
entries.literal: We your ministers jointly deliberate: we request pardon of the offense and restoration to his former office."

entries.zh: 魏文帝詔曰：「如願荊、襄之役，寔展功效。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Du Guxin's campaign in Jing and Xiang did show real service.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Ruyuan's Jing and Xiang campaign truly displayed achievement.

entries.zh: 旣屬強寇，力屈道窮，歸賊不可，還朝路絕，適事求宜，未足稱過。
entries.en: He met a powerful enemy, was spent, and could neither submit to the foe nor find a way home—given the circumstances, he can hardly be blamed.
entries.literal: Having encountered a strong foe, his strength bent and the way was exhausted; to return to the bandits was impossible and the road back to court was cut off—seeking what suited the affair, it is insufficient to call it fault.

entries.zh: 違難如吳，誠貫夷險，義全終始，良可嘉歎。
entries.en: He bore hardship through every danger with constancy from first to last—truly admirable.
entries.literal: Enduring hardship like Wu, his sincerity penetrating easy and perilous, his righteousness complete from beginning to end—truly worthy of praise and sighing admiration.

entries.zh: 復情存謙退，款心謝責。
entries.en: He had shown humility and offered a sincere apology.
entries.literal: Again, his feeling preserved humility and withdrawal; with sincere heart he declined blame.

entries.zh: 甯容議及恩降，止雲免咎，斯則事失權宜，理乖通變。
entries.en: To treat this as no more than a pardon from punishment falls short of what the moment requires.
entries.literal: How could one allow the deliberation to reach only to grace in reduction of punishment and stop at saying merely exemption from blame? That then is the affair losing what suits the moment and reason departing from flexible change.

entries.zh: 可轉驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府，其使持節、儀同三司、浮陽郡公悉如故。」
entries.en: Let him be made grand general of agile cavalry, with attendant-in-ordinary and opening-the-feudatory added; his staff, three-division court equipage, and ducal title of Fuyang shall all stand as before."
entries.literal: He may be transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with the added posts of attendant-in-ordinary and opening-the-feudatory; his bearer of the staff, three-division court equipage, and Duke of Fuyang commandery shall all remain as before."

entries.zh: 趙貴 獨孤信 侯莫陳崇
entries.en: Zhao Gui — Du Guxin — Houmo Chen Chong
entries.literal: Zhao Gui; Du Guxin; Houmo Chen Chong

entries.zh: 後從賀拔岳鎮長安。
entries.en: He later followed Heba Yue in garrisoning Chang'an.
entries.literal: Later he followed Heba Yue in garrisoning Chang'an.

entries.zh: 及岳被害，禦與諸將同謀翊戴太祖。
entries.en: When Heba Yue was murdered, Liang Yu and the other generals plotted to raise up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.
entries.literal: When Yue was killed, Yu together with the generals jointly plotted to support and install the Grand Progenitor.

entries.zh: 從征侯莫陳悅，遷武衛將軍。
entries.en: He followed the campaign against Houmochen Yue and was made martial guard general.
entries.literal: Following in the campaign against Houmochen Yue, he was transferred to martial guard general.

entries.zh: 太祖既平秦隴，方欲引兵東下，雍州刺史賈顯持兩端，通使於齊神武。
entries.en: Once Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had secured Qin and Long, he prepared to march east; but Yong Province governor Jia Xian wavered and opened talks with Gao Huan.
entries.literal: After the Grand Progenitor had pacified Qin and Long, he was about to lead troops east; Yong Province governor Jia Xian hedged between two sides and sent envoys to Gao Huan.

entries.zh: 太祖微知其意，以禦為大都督、雍州刺史，領前軍先行。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw through the maneuver and sent Liang Yu ahead as grand commander and governor of Yong Province with the vanguard.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor slightly knew his intent and made Yu grand commander and governor of Yong Province, leading the vanguard to go first.

entries.zh: 既與顯相見，因說顯曰：「魏室陵遲，天下鼎沸。
entries.en: When he met Jia Xian he urged him: "The Wei dynasty is failing and the empire is in turmoil.
entries.literal: Once he met Xian, he thereupon persuaded Xian, saying: "The Wei house declines and sinks; the realm boils like a cauldron.

entries.zh: 高歡志在凶逆，梟夷非遠。
entries.en: Gao Huan aims at treason, and his downfall cannot be far away.
entries.literal: Gao Huan's intent is toward villainy and rebellion; execution is not far off.

entries.zh: 宇文夏州英姿不世，算略無方，方欲扶危定傾，匡復京洛。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai of Xia Province is a hero of his generation, unmatched in strategy, and is ready to rescue the realm and recover the capital at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Yuwen of Xia Province has heroic bearing unmatched in his age, stratagem without measure, and is about to support the perilous and set the tipping straight and restore the capital and Luoyang.

entries.zh: 公不於此時建立功效，乃懷猶豫，恐禍不旋踵矣。」
entries.en: If you miss this chance to earn your place and keep hesitating, ruin will overtake you before you can turn around."
entries.literal: If you sir do not at this time establish merit and achievement but instead harbor hesitation, I fear disaster will not wait for the heel to turn."

entries.zh: 顯即出迎太祖，禦遂入鎮雍州。
entries.en: Jia Xian went out at once to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, and Liang Yu took up the Yong Province garrison.
entries.literal: Xian thereupon went out to welcome the Grand Progenitor; Yu then entered to garrison Yong Province.

entries.zh: 授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: He was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-division court equipage.
entries.literal: He was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and three-division court equipage.

entries.zh: 魏孝武西遷，除右衛將軍、大都督，進爵魏昌縣伯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Gan Hui became right guard general and grand commander and was raised to Earl of Weichang with five hundred households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was made right guard general and grand commander; his rank was advanced to Earl of Weichang with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 出為北華州刺史，加使持節、驃騎將軍。
entries.en: He was sent out as governor of North Huazhou with full credentials and the rank of grand general of fast cavalry.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of North Huazhou with additional credentials as envoy and grand general of fast cavalry.

entries.zh: 大統初，拜儀同三司，進爵為公，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: At the start of Datong he received three-division court equipage, was raised to duke, and gained five hundred more households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was appointed three-division court equipage, advanced in rank to duke, and his fief was increased by five hundred households.

entries.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，惠每先登陷陣。
entries.en: On the campaigns that took Dou Tai, recovered Hongnong, and broke Shayuan, Gan Hui was always first over the ramparts and into the enemy line.
entries.literal: Following in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shayuan, Hui each time was first to ascend and breach the formation.

entries.zh: 加侍中、開府，進爵長樂郡公，增邑通前二千二百戶。
entries.en: He became palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory, was raised to Duke of Changle, and his combined fief reached two thousand two hundred households.
entries.literal: He was added palace attendant and opening office, advanced in rank to Duke of Changle commandery, and his fief together with the previous total reached two thousand two hundred households.

entries.zh: 四年，魏文帝東巡洛陽，與齊神武戰於河橋，惠力戰破之，大收降卒。
entries.en: In the fourth year Emperor Wen toured Luoyang and fought Gao Huan at Heqiao; Gan Hui fought fiercely, routed him, and took large numbers of prisoners.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Wen of Wei toured east to Luoyang and fought Gao Huan at Heqiao; Hui fought hard and defeated him and greatly gathered surrendered troops.

entries.zh: 七年，遷中領軍。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was made commander of the central guard corps.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to commander of the central guard corps.

entries.zh: 及高仲密舉北豫州來附，太祖帥師迎之。
entries.en: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered North Yuzhou, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched out to receive him.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhongmi offered North Yuzhou in submission, the Grand Progenitor led troops to welcome him.

entries.zh: 軍至洛陽，齊神武於邙山將以邀我，太祖乃徙輜重於瀍曲，夜勒兵襲之。
entries.en: Near Luoyang, Gao Huan waited on Mount Mang to cut them off; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai shifted the baggage train to Chan Bend and struck by night.
entries.literal: When the army reached Luoyang, Gao Huan at Mount Mang was about to intercept them; the Grand Progenitor moved baggage to Chan Bend and at night ordered troops to strike him.

entries.zh: 及戰，惠為右軍，與中軍大破之，逐北數里，虜其步卒。
entries.en: In the battle Gan Hui commanded the right wing; with the center he broke the enemy, chased them north for several li, and took their infantry.
entries.literal: When they fought, Hui was the right army; with the center army he greatly defeated them, pursued north several li, and captured their foot soldiers.

entries.zh: 齊神武兵乃萃於左軍，軍將趙貴等與戰不利，諸軍因之並退。
entries.en: Gao Huan then concentrated against the left wing; Zhao Gui and the other commanders there were beaten, and the whole army fell back.
entries.literal: Gao Huan's troops then massed against the left army; army generals Zhao Gui and others fought unfavorably and all armies thereby retreated together.

entries.zh: 時會日暮，齊神武兵屢來攻惠，惠擊之，皆披靡。
entries.en: At dusk Gao Huan's men attacked Gan Hui again and again; each time Gan Hui drove them off in rout.
entries.literal: As it happened at dusk, Gao Huan's troops repeatedly came to attack Hui; Hui struck them and all were routed.

entries.zh: 至夜中，齊神武騎復來追惠，惠徐乃下馬，顧命廚人營食。
entries.en: At midnight Gao Huan's horsemen caught up with Gan Hui again; Gan Hui calmly dismounted and told the cook to serve a meal.
entries.literal: By midnight Gao Huan's cavalry again came pursuing Hui; Hui leisurely dismounted and turned to order the cook to prepare food.

entries.zh: 食訖，謂左右曰：「長安死，此中死，異乎？」
entries.en: When he had eaten he said to his men: "Death in Chang'an, death here—what difference is there?"
entries.literal: When the meal was finished he said to those beside him: "To die in Chang'an, to die here—how are they different?"

entries.zh: 乃建旗鳴角，收諸敗軍而還。
entries.en: Then he raised his banners, sounded the horns, rallied the scattered units, and marched back.
entries.literal: He then raised banners and sounded horns, gathered the various defeated troops, and returned.

entries.zh: 齊神武追騎憚惠，疑有伏兵，不敢逼。
entries.en: Gao Huan's pursuers feared Gan Hui, suspected a trap, and would not come near.
entries.literal: Gao Huan's pursuing cavalry feared Hui, suspected an ambush, and did not dare press close.

entries.zh: 至弘農，見太祖，陳賊形勢，恨其垂成之功，覆於一簣，於是歔欷不能自勝。
entries.en: At Hongnong he saw Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, described the enemy's dispositions, and wept that victory had slipped away at the last moment.
entries.literal: Reaching Hongnong, he saw the Grand Progenitor, reported the enemy situation, regretted that near-complete achievement was overturned by one basketful of earth, and thereupon sighed and sobbed unable to control himself.

entries.zh: 太祖壯之。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai admired his bearing.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved his spirit.

entries.zh: 及齊神武與魏孝武帝構隙，帝頻勑太祖簡銳卒入衛京邑。
entries.en: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu fell out, the emperor repeatedly ordered Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to send picked troops to guard the capital.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei developed a rift, the emperor repeatedly ordered the Grand Progenitor to select sharp troops to enter and guard the capital region.

entries.zh: 太祖乃令峯與都督趙貴等率輕騎赴洛陽。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then sent Yi Feng with Zhao Gui and others at the head of light cavalry to Luoyang.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor then ordered Feng with area commander Zhao Gui and others to lead light cavalry to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 至潼關，值魏孝武西遷，峯即從太祖拔回洛，復潼關。
entries.en: At Tong Pass they met Emperor Xiaowu fleeing west; Yi Feng at once followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in retaking Luoyang and securing Tong Pass again.
entries.literal: Reaching Tong Pass, it happened that Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west; Feng immediately followed the Grand Progenitor in seizing back Luoyang and recovering Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 拜安東將軍、華州刺史。
entries.en: He was made general who pacifies the east and governor of Huazhou.
entries.literal: He was appointed general who pacifies the east and governor of Huazhou.

entries.zh: 尋轉大都督。
entries.en: He was soon made grand commander.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand commander.

entries.zh: 討曹泥有功，進爵華陽縣公，邑一千戶。
entries.en: For his service against Cao Ni he was raised to Duke of Huayang with one thousand households.
entries.literal: Campaigning against Cao Ni with merit, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Huayang county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 大統［三］年，從太祖破竇泰於小關。
entries.en: In Datong 3 (537) he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Dou Tai at Xiao Pass.
entries.literal: Datong (3) [emended: three] year, following the Grand Progenitor he broke Dou Tai at Xiao Pass.

entries.zh: 還，拜散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: On his return he became regular attendant of scattered cavalry, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and three-division court equipage.
entries.literal: Returning, he was appointed regular attendant of scattered cavalry, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and three-division court equipage.

entries.zh: 又從復弘農，破沙苑，進爵樂陵郡公。
entries.en: He followed again in recovering Hongnong and breaking Shayuan and was raised to Duke of Leiling.
entries.literal: Again following in recovering Hongnong and breaking Shayuan, his rank was advanced to Duke of Leiling commandery.

entries.zh: 仍與元季海、獨孤信復洛陽。
entries.en: He then joined Yuan Jihai and Dugu Xin in recovering Luoyang.
entries.literal: Still with Yuan Jihai and Dugu Xin he recovered Luoyang.

entries.zh: 峯率奇兵至成皋，入其郛，收其戶口而還。
entries.en: Yi Feng took a flying column to Chenggao, entered the suburbs, rounded up the people, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Feng led surprise troops to Chenggao, entered its outer city, gathered its population, and returned.

entries.zh: 東魏遣行臺任祥率步騎萬餘攻潁川，峯復以輕騎五百邀擊之，自是威名轉盛。
entries.en: Eastern Wei sent Ren Xiang at the head of more than ten thousand men against Yingchuan; Yi Feng hit him with five hundred light horse, and his reputation as a fierce commander spread.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei sent mobile headquarters Ren Xiang leading over ten thousand foot and horse to attack Yingchuan; Feng again with five hundred light cavalry intercepted and struck them, and from this his fierce name grew ever greater.

entries.zh: 加授開府儀同三司。
entries.en: He was further given opening-office three-division court equipage.
entries.literal: He was additionally granted opening-office three-division court equipage.

entries.zh: 東魏圍洛陽，峯與季海守金墉。
entries.en: When Eastern Wei besieged Luoyang, Yi Feng and Yuan Jihai held Jinyong.
entries.literal: When Eastern Wei besieged Luoyang, Feng with Jihai held Jinyong.

entries.zh: 太祖至，圍解，即與東魏戰於河橋。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's arrival lifted the siege, and they fought Eastern Wei at once at Heqiao.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived the siege was lifted, and they immediately fought Eastern Wei at Heqiao.

entries.zh: 時峯為左軍，不利，與李遠先還，太祖因此班師。
entries.en: Yi Feng commanded the left wing; the fight went badly, and he withdrew ahead with Li Yuan, whereupon Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai pulled the army back.
entries.literal: At the time Feng was the left army; the battle went badly, and with Li Yuan he returned first; the Grand Progenitor therefore withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 詔原其罪。
entries.en: An edict forgave the fault.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned his offense.

entries.zh: 拜東西北三夏州諸軍事、夏州刺史。
entries.en: He was made commander of the three Xia provinces—east, northwest, and west—and governor of Xia Province.
entries.literal: He was appointed commander of all military affairs of the three Xia provinces of east, northwest, and west, and governor of Xia Province.

entries.zh: 後與于謹討劉平伏，從解玉壁圍，平栢穀塢，竝有功。
entries.en: Later he joined Yu Jin against Liu Pingfu and shared in relieving Yubi and taking Baigu Stockade.
entries.literal: Later, with Yu Jin he campaigned against Liu Pingfu; following in relieving the siege of Yubi and pacifying Baigu Stockade, in each case he had merit.

entries.zh: 涼州刺史宇文仲和反，峯與于謹討之。
entries.en: When Liang governor Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled, Yi Feng marched against him with Yu Jin.
entries.literal: When Liang Province governor Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled, Feng with Yu Jin campaigned against him.

entries.zh: 十五年，東魏圍潁川，峰與趙貴赴援。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan; Yi Feng and Zhao Gui marched to its relief.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan; Feng with Zhao Gui went to relieve it.

entries.zh: 至南陽，遇疾卒，時年五十。
entries.en: He fell ill and died at Nanyang, aged fifty.
entries.literal: Reaching Nanyang, he encountered illness and died; at the time he was fifty.

entries.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，以奉迎功，進封下博縣伯，邑五百戶，行東雍州事。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Wang De was raised to Earl of Xiabo with five hundred households for welcoming the emperor and was put in charge of East Yong Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, for merit in welcoming the emperor he was advanced to Earl of Xiabo county with five hundred households and directed the affairs of East Yong Province.

entries.zh: 在州未幾，百姓懷之。
entries.en: Before long the people of the province came to cherish him.
entries.literal: Not long in the province, the common people cherished him.

entries.zh: 賜姓烏丸氏。
entries.en: He was granted the surname Wuhuan.
entries.literal: He was granted the surname Wuhuan.

entries.zh: 大統元年，拜衞將軍、右光祿大夫，進爵為公，增邑一千戶，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、北雍州刺史。
entries.en: In Datong year one he became guard general and right grand master of splendid happiness, was raised to duke with one thousand more households, and was further given grand general of chariots and cavalry, three-division court equipage, and the governorship of North Yong Province.
entries.literal: In Datong year one he was appointed guard general and right grand master of splendid happiness, advanced in rank to duke and his fief increased by one thousand households, with additional posts as grand general of chariots and cavalry, three-division court equipage, and governor of North Yong Province.

entries.zh: 其後常從太祖征伐，累有戰功。
entries.en: Thereafter he often followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai on campaign and won repeated battlefield honors.
entries.literal: Thereafter he often followed the Grand Progenitor on campaigns and repeatedly had battlefield merit.

entries.zh: 又從破齊神武於沙苑，加開府、侍中，進爵河間郡公，增邑通前二千七百戶。
entries.en: He also shared in defeating Gao Huan at Shayuan, became opening-the-feudatory and palace attendant, was raised to Duke of Hejian, and his combined fief reached two thousand seven hundred households.
entries.literal: Again following in defeating Gao Huan at Shayuan, he was added opening office and palace attendant, advanced to Duke of Hejian commandery, and his fief together with the previous total reached two thousand seven hundred households.

entries.zh: 先是河、渭間種羌屢叛，以德有威名，為夷民所附，除河州刺史。
entries.en: Earlier the tribal Qiang between the He and Wei had rebelled repeatedly; because Wang De had a fierce reputation and the frontier peoples followed him, he was made governor of He Province.
entries.literal: Earlier the tribal Qiang between the He and Wei rivers had repeatedly rebelled; because De had a fierce reputation and was followed by the frontier peoples, he was made governor of He Province.

entries.zh: 德綏撫有方，羣羌率服。
entries.en: Wang De pacified them skillfully and the Qiang largely submitted.
entries.literal: De pacified them with proper methods and the Qiang for the most part submitted.

entries.zh: 十三年，授大都督、原靈顯三州五原蒲川二鎮諸軍事。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was made grand commander with overall military authority over the three provinces of Yuan, Ling, and Xian and the two garrisons of Wuyuan and Puchuan.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was granted grand commander and overall military affairs of the three provinces of Yuan, Ling, and Xian and the two garrisons of Wuyuan and Puchuan.

entries.zh: 十四年，除涇州刺史。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was made governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was made governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 卒於州。
entries.en: He died in the province.
entries.literal: He died in the province.

entries.zh: 諡曰獻。
entries.en: His posthumous name was Xian, "Offering."
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Xian.

entries.zh: 若干惠字惠保，代郡武川人也。
entries.en: Ruogan Hui, styled Huibao, came from Wuchuan in Dai commandery.
entries.literal: Guo Ganhui, styled Huibao, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai commandery.

entries.zh: 其先與魏氏俱起，以國為姓。
entries.en: His ancestors had risen with the Wei and taken the state name as their surname.
entries.literal: His forebears rose together with the Wei clan and took the state as surname.

entries.zh: 父樹利周，從魏廣陽王深征葛榮，戰沒，贈冀州刺史。
entries.en: His father Shulizhou followed the Prince of Guangyang, Shen, against Ge Rong and fell in battle; the court posthumously made him governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: His father Shulizhou followed Wei's Prince of Guangyang Shen against Ge Rong, died in battle, and was posthumously given governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 惠年弱冠，從爾朱榮征伐，定河北，破元顥，以功拜中堅將軍。
entries.en: At twenty Gan Hui followed Erzhu Rong on campaign, secured Hebei, and defeated Yuan Hao; for this he was made general of the central guard.
entries.literal: Hui at the age of weak crown followed Erzhu Rong on campaigns, stabilized Hebei, defeated Yuan Hao, and by merit was appointed general of the central guard.

entries.zh: 復以別將從賀拔岳西征，解岐州圍，擒万俟醜奴，平水洛，定隴右，每力戰有功。
entries.en: As a separate commander under Heba Yue he marched west, lifted the siege of Qi, captured Moqi Chounu, pacified Shuiluo, and secured Long-you, fighting fiercely at every step.
entries.literal: Again as separate commander he followed Heba Yue west, relieved the siege of Qi Prefecture, captured Moqi Chounu, pacified Shuiluo, and stabilized Long-you; each time he fought hard with merit.

entries.zh: 封北平縣男，邑二百戶。
entries.en: He received the viscounty of Beiping with two hundred households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Beiping county with a fief of two hundred households.

entries.zh: 累遷鎮遠將軍、都督、直寢、征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: He rose step by step to general who guards the distant, area commander, direct attendants guard, general who campaigns west, and grand master of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: By successive promotion he reached general who guards the distant, area commander, direct attendants guard, general who campaigns west, and grand master of splendid happiness.

entries.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，惠與寇洛、趙貴等同謀翊戴太祖。
entries.en: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Gan Hui joined Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, and others in raising up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.
entries.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Hui with Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, and others jointly plotted to support and install the Grand Progenitor.

entries.zh: 仍從平悅，拜直閤將軍。
entries.en: He followed the campaign that crushed Houmochen Yue and was made direct-pavilion general.
entries.literal: Still following in pacifying Yue, he was appointed direct-pavilion general.

entries.zh: 王德字天恩，代郡武川人也。
entries.en: Wang De, styled Tian'en, came from Wuchuan in Dai commandery.
entries.literal: Wang De styled Tian'en was a man of Wuchuan in Dai commandery.

entries.zh: 少善騎射，雖不經師訓，而以孝悌見稱。
entries.en: He excelled at riding and archery from youth; though he had no formal schooling, he was praised for filial piety and brotherly respect.
entries.literal: In youth skilled at mounted archery; though he did not receive teacher's instruction, he was acclaimed for filial piety and fraternity.

entries.zh: 魏永安二年，從爾朱榮討元顥，攻河內，應募先登。
entries.en: In Yongan 2 (529) he followed Erzhu Rong against Yuan Hao, attacked Henei, and was first over the wall when volunteers were called.
entries.literal: In Wei's second year of Yongan, he followed Erzhu Rong to campaign against Yuan Hao, attacked Henei, answered the levy and was first to ascend.

entries.zh: 以功除討夷將軍，進爵內官縣子。
entries.en: For this he was made general for punishing the barbarians and raised to Viscount of Neiguan.
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed general for punishing the barbarians and advanced in rank to Viscount of Neiguan county.

entries.zh: 又從賀拔岳討万俟醜奴，平之。
entries.en: He again followed Heba Yue against Moqi Chounu and helped pacify him.
entries.literal: Again he followed Heba Yue to campaign against Moqi Chounu and pacified him.

entries.zh: 別封深澤縣男，邑二百戶，加龍驤將軍、中散大夫。
entries.en: He was separately enfeoffed Baron of Shenze with two hundred households and given general of soaring dragon and palace attendant-in-regular service.
entries.literal: Separately enfeoffed Baron of Shenze county, fief two hundred households; added general of soaring dragon and palace attendant-in-regular service.

entries.zh: 及侯莫陳悅害岳，德與寇洛等定議翊戴太祖。
entries.en: When Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, Wang De and Kou Luo and others resolved to raise up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.
entries.literal: When Houmochen Yue killed Yue, De with Kou Luo and others fixed the plan to support and install the Grand Progenitor.

entries.zh: 加征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫、平涼郡守。
entries.en: He was further made campaign-west general, golden-purple light-in-the-distance grandee, and prefect of Pingliang commandery.
entries.literal: Added campaign-west general, golden-purple light-in-the-distance grandee, and prefect of Pingliang commandery.

entries.zh: 德雖不知書，至於斷決處分，良吏無以過也。
entries.en: Wang De could not read, yet in judgment and administration no capable official could match him.
entries.literal: Though De did not know books, as for decisions and dispositions, fine officials could not surpass him.

entries.zh: 涇州所部五郡，而德常為最。
entries.en: Among the five commanderies under Jing Province, Wang De's district was always ranked first.
entries.literal: Of the five commanderies under Jing Province, De was always ranked first.

entries.zh: 及太祖置十二軍，簡諸將以將之，亮領一軍。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai formed the twelve armies and chose commanders for them, Liu Liang led one corps.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor established the twelve armies and selected various generals to command them, Liang led one army.

entries.zh: 每征討，常與怡峯俱為騎將。
entries.en: On campaign he usually served as cavalry commander alongside Yi Feng.
entries.literal: On every campaign he usually served with Yi Feng together as cavalry generals.

entries.zh: 魏孝武西遷，以迎駕功，除使持節、右光祿大夫、左大都督、南秦州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Liu Liang was rewarded for welcoming the imperial carriage with full credentials, right grand master of splendid happiness, left grand commander, and governor of South Qin Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, for merit in welcoming the imperial carriage he was made bearer of staff of authority, right grand master of splendid happiness, left grand commander, and governor of South Qin Province.

entries.zh: 大統元年，以復潼關功，進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司，改封饒陽縣伯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Datong year one, for recovering Tong Pass, he was raised to grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-division court equipage and re-enfeoffed Earl of Raoyang with five hundred households.
entries.literal: In Datong year one, for merit in recovering Tong Pass, his rank was advanced to grand general of chariots and cavalry and three-division court equipage, and he was re-enfeoffed Earl of Raoyang county with five hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋加侍中。
entries.en: He soon became palace attendant as well.
entries.literal: Soon he was added palace attendant.

entries.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農及沙苑之役，亮竝力戰有功。
entries.en: He shared in capturing Dou Tai and the campaigns to recover Hongnong and at Shayuan, fighting hard each time with merit.
entries.literal: Following in capturing Dou Tai and the campaigns to recover Hongnong and at Shayuan, Liang each time fought hard with merit.

entries.zh: 遷開府儀同三司、大都督，進爵長廣郡公，邑通前二千戶。
entries.en: He was made opening-office three-division court equipage and grand commander, raised to Duke of Changguang, and his combined fief reached two thousand households.
entries.literal: He was transferred to opening-office three-division court equipage and grand commander, advanced in rank to Duke of Changguang commandery, with a combined fief totaling two thousand households.

entries.zh: 以母憂去職，居喪毀瘠。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother and wasted away in grief.
entries.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother and wore himself gaunt in bereavement.

entries.zh: 太祖嗟其至性，每愛惜之。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai admired his deep filial devotion and always treated him with special regard.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed at his utmost filial nature and always cherished him.

entries.zh: 俄起復本官。
entries.en: He was soon recalled to his former post.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled to restore his former office.

entries.zh: 尋拜秦州刺史，未及之部，遷司空。
entries.en: He was soon appointed governor of Qin Province, but before he could take up the post he was transferred to minister of works.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Qin Province; before he could reach his post he was transferred to minister of works.

entries.zh: 惠性剛質，有勇力，容貌魁岸。
entries.en: Gan Hui was forthright by nature, brave and strong, with a towering build.
entries.literal: Hui's nature was firm and plain; he had courage and strength and a towering appearance.

entries.zh: 善於撫御，將士莫不懷恩，人思効節。
entries.en: Skilled at winning men, he earned the gratitude of officers and soldiers alike, and his men were eager to serve him faithfully.
entries.literal: Skilled at comforting and commanding, officers and soldiers all cherished his kindness and men wished to devote their loyalty.

entries.zh: 十二年，東魏將侯景侵襄州，惠率兵擊走之。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Eastern Wei general Hou Jing invaded Xiang Province; Gan Hui led troops and drove him off.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Eastern Wei general Hou Jing invaded Xiang Province; Hui led troops and drove him off.

entries.zh: 明年，景請內附，朝議欲收輯河南，令惠以本官鎮魯陽，以為聲援。
entries.en: The next year Hou Jing asked to defect; the court planned to recover Henan and ordered Gan Hui to garrison Luyang in his existing office as a supporting force.
entries.literal: The next year Jing requested to come over within the borders; court deliberation wished to gather and consolidate Henan, and ordered Hui to garrison Luyang in his former office as supporting force.

entries.zh: 遇疾，薨於軍。
entries.en: He fell ill and died in camp.
entries.literal: He encountered illness and died in the army.

entries.zh: 惠於諸將年最少。
entries.en: Among the generals Gan Hui was the youngest.
entries.literal: Among the generals Hui was the youngest in years.

entries.zh: 早喪父，事母以孝聞。
entries.en: He lost his father early and was known for filial devotion to his mother.
entries.literal: He lost his father early and was famed for serving his mother with filial piety.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗造射堂新成，與諸將宴射。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai once completed a new archery hall and feasted and shot with his generals.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor once built a new archery hall and feasted and shot with the generals.

entries.zh: 惠竊歎曰：「親老矣，何時辦此乎？」
entries.en: Ruogan Hui sighed to himself: "My mother is old—when will I be able to give her something like this?"
entries.literal: Hui secretly sighed and said: "My parents are old—when could I provide such a thing for them?"

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，即日徙堂於惠宅。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai heard this he moved the hall to Gan Hui's home that very day.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor heard this he that very day moved the hall to Hui's residence.

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 及薨，太祖為之流涕者久之。
entries.en: When he died Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wept for him a long while.
entries.literal: When he died the Grand Progenitor wept for him a long while.

entries.zh: 惠喪至，又臨撫焉。
entries.en: When the funeral procession arrived he came in person again to comfort the family.
entries.literal: When Hui's coffin arrived he again came in person to comfort them.

entries.zh: 贈本官，加秦州刺史，諡曰武烈。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted his former offices plus governor of Qin Province, with the posthumous name Wulie, "Martial and Fierce."
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted his former office with addition of governor of Qin Province; his posthumous title was Wulie.

entries.zh: 子鳳嗣。
entries.en: His son Feng succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Feng inherited.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：梁禦等負將率之材，蘊驍銳之氣，遭逢喪亂，馳騖干戈，艱難險阻備嘗，而功名未立。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Liang Yu and the others had the makings of commanders and the mettle of fierce warriors; they endured the chaos of war and every hardship, yet won no lasting fame.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Liang Yu and others bore the talent of commanders, harbored fierce and sharp spirit; encountering disorder and ruin, they galloped amidst arms, tasted every hardship, peril and obstacle, yet fame and achievement were not established.

entries.zh: 及殷憂啟聖，豫奉興王，參謀締構之初，宣力經綸之始，遂得連衡灌、酈，方駕張、徐，可謂遇其時也。
entries.en: When sorrow gave way to a founding sage they served the rising dynasty from the first, counselled at the start of its construction, and labored at the beginning of its ordering—so they could rank with Guan and Li and stand beside Zhang and Xu; they had truly met their moment.
entries.literal: When deep sorrow opened the sage, they beforehand served the founding king, counseled at the beginning of founding construction, displayed strength at the beginning of ordering the realm—thereby they were able to link with Guan and Li, drive abreast with Zhang and Xu; one may say they met their time.

entries.zh: 竝中年即世，遠志未申，惜哉！
entries.en: All died in middle age with their greater ambitions unfulfilled—alas!
entries.literal: Both at middle age passed from the world; distant aspirations were not fulfilled—pity!

entries.zh: 惠、德本以果毅知名，而能率由孝道，難矣。
entries.en: Ruogan Hui and Wang De were famed for bold resolve, yet also lived by filial duty—no small thing.
entries.literal: Hui and De originally were known for resolute courage, yet able to follow filial piety—difficult indeed.

entries.zh: 圖史所歎，何以加焉。
entries.en: Histories can scarcely praise them enough.
entries.literal: What history's records sigh at—how could one add to it?

entries.zh: 勇者不必有仁，斯不然矣。
entries.en: The saying that courage need not bring benevolence does not apply here.
entries.literal: The brave need not have benevolence—this is not so.

entries.zh: 梁禦 若干惠 怡峯 劉亮 王德
entries.en: Liang Yu — Ruogan Hui — Yi Feng — Liu Liang — Wang De
entries.literal: Liang Yu; Guo Ganhui; Yi Feng; Liu Liang; Wang De

entries.zh: 梁將曹義宗圍荊州，勑羆與別將裴衍率兵赴救。
entries.en: When Liang general Cao Yizong besieged Jing Province, an edict sent Wang Pi with separate commander Pei Yan to relieve the city.
entries.literal: Liang general Cao Yizong besieged Jing Province; an edict ordered Pi together with separate commander Pei Yan to lead troops to the rescue.

entries.zh: 遂與梁人戰，大破之。
entries.en: They met the Liang army and routed it.
entries.literal: Thereupon they fought the Liang men and greatly defeated them.

entries.zh: 于時諸方鼎沸，所在凋殘。
entries.en: The realm was in turmoil and every region lay in ruins.
entries.literal: At that time all quarters boiled like a cauldron; everywhere was wasted and ruined.

entries.zh: 荊州新經寇難，尤藉慰撫。
entries.en: Jing Province had just endured invasion and desperately needed reassurance and repair.
entries.literal: Jing Province had newly suffered raids and turmoil and especially needed comfort and soothing.

entries.zh: 以羆為荊州刺史，進號撫軍將軍。
entries.en: Wang Pi was appointed governor of Jing Province and promoted to general who pacifies the army.
entries.literal: Pi was made governor of Jing Province; his title was advanced to general who pacifies the army.

entries.zh: 梁復遣曹義宗衆數萬圍荊州，堰水灌城，不沒者數板。
entries.en: Liang sent Cao Yizong back with tens of thousands of men, dammed the river, and flooded the city until only a few courses of wall stood above the water.
entries.literal: Liang again sent Cao Yizong with a host of tens of thousands to besiege Jing Province; they dammed the water to flood the city, and only several boards of wall remained unsubmerged.

entries.zh: 時旣內外多虞，未遑救援，乃遺羆鐵券，云城全當授本州刺史。
entries.en: With crises on every front the court could spare no relief force, but it sent Wang Pi an iron certificate promising him the governorship if he kept the city intact.
entries.literal: At that time both within and without there were many worries; there was no leisure to send relief; they therefore sent Pi an iron certificate, saying if the city remained whole he would be granted governor of that province.

entries.zh: 城中糧盡，羆煮粥，與將士均分而食之。
entries.en: When food ran out inside the walls, Wang Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally with his officers and soldiers.
entries.literal: Inside the city grain was exhausted; Pi cooked gruel and divided it equally with officers and soldiers to eat.

entries.zh: 每出戰，嘗不擐甲冑，大呼曰：「荊州城，孝文皇帝所置。
entries.en: Whenever he fought he often went without armor and cried out: "This city of Jing Province was founded by Emperor Xiaowen.
entries.literal: Each time he went out to battle he usually did not don armor; he shouted loudly: "Jing Province city was established by Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 天若不佑國家，使賊箭中王羆；
entries.en: If Heaven will not save the realm, let the enemy's arrows find Wang Pi;
entries.literal: If Heaven does not protect the state, let the rebels' arrows strike Wang Pi;

entries.zh: 不爾，王羆須破賊。」
entries.en: If not, Wang Pi will break the enemy."
entries.literal: If not, Wang Pi must break the rebels."

entries.zh: 屢經戰陣，亦不被傷。
entries.en: He fought again and again and was never hurt.
entries.literal: He repeatedly passed through battle formations and was also not wounded.

entries.zh: 彌歷三年，義宗方退。
entries.en: Three years passed before Cao Yizong finally withdrew.
entries.literal: More than three years passed before Yizong finally withdrew.

entries.zh: 進封霸城縣公。
entries.en: He was promoted to Duke of Bachecheng.
entries.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Bachecheng county.

entries.zh: 尋遷車騎大將軍、涇州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Jingzhou (Jing Prefecture).
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 未及之部，屬太祖徵兵為勤王之舉，請前驅效命，遂為大都督，鎮華州。
entries.en: Before he took office, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai mobilized for the rescue of the emperor; Wang Pi volunteered for the vanguard, was made grand commander, and garrisoned Huazhou.
entries.literal: Before he reached his post, it happened that the Grand Progenitor raised troops for the campaign to rescue the ruler; he requested to serve as vanguard and give his life; he thereupon became grand commander and garrisoned Huazhou.

entries.zh: 王羆字熊羆，京兆霸城人，漢河南尹王遵之後，世為州郡著姓。
entries.en: Wang Pi, styled Xiongpi, came from Bachecheng in Jingzhao commandery. He descended from Wang Zun, governor of Henan under the Han, and his family had long been a leading name in the provinces.
entries.literal: Wang Pi, styled Xiongpi, was a native of Bachecheng in Jingzhao commandery, a descendant of Wang Zun, governor of Henan under Han, for generations a prominent surname in the provinces and commanderies.

entries.zh: 羆剛直木強，處物平當，州郡敬憚之。
entries.en: Wang Pi was blunt, stubborn, and scrupulously fair, and officials across the provinces both admired and feared him.
entries.literal: Pi was upright, stubborn, and unyielding; in dealing with things he was fair and even; the provinces and commanderies respected and feared him.

entries.zh: 魏太和中，除殿中將軍。
entries.en: During the Taihe era of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei he was made palace-guard general.
entries.literal: In Wei Emperor Xiaowen's Taihe era, he was appointed palace-guard general.

entries.zh: 先是南岐、東益氐羌反叛，王師戰不利，乃令羆領羽林五千鎮梁州，討平諸賊。
entries.en: When Di and Qiang rebels rose in Southern Qi and East Yizhou and the imperial army faltered, Wang Pi was sent with five thousand Yulin guards to garrison Liang Province and put down the uprisings.
entries.literal: Previously Southern Qi and East Yizhou Di and Qiang had rebelled; the imperial army fought unfavorably; he was then ordered to lead five thousand Yulin guards to garrison Liang Province and pacify the various rebels.

entries.zh: 還，授右將軍、西河內史。
entries.en: On his return he was given the posts of right general and interior minister of West He commandery.
entries.literal: Returning, he was granted right general and interior minister of West He.

entries.zh: 辭不拜。
entries.en: He refused the appointment.
entries.literal: He declined and did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 時人謂之曰：「西河大邦，俸祿殷厚，何為致辭？」
entries.en: People asked him: "West He is a rich commandery with a generous salary. Why turn it down?"
entries.literal: People of the time said to him: "West He is a great commandery; stipend and salary are abundant—why make yourself decline?"

entries.zh: 羆曰：「京洛材木，盡出西河，朝貴營第宅者，皆有求假。
entries.en: Wang Pi answered: "All the timber for Luoyang comes from West He, and every court noble building a mansion comes asking to borrow it.
entries.literal: Pi said: "Timber for the capital at Luoyang all comes from West He; court nobles building mansions all have requests to borrow.

entries.zh: 如其私辦，卽力所不堪，若科發民間，又違法憲。
entries.en: If I pay for it myself, I cannot afford it; if I levy it from the people, I break the law.
entries.literal: If by my own means I supply it, I immediately cannot bear the burden; if I levy it from the common people, I again violate law and charter.

entries.zh: 以此辭耳。」
entries.en: That is why I declined."
entries.literal: For this reason I decline—that is all."

entries.zh: 魏孝武西遷，拜驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Wang Pi received the rank of grand general of fast cavalry, with palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory as well.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Pi was appointed grand general of fast cavalry, with additional posts as palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory.

entries.zh: 嘗修州城未畢，梯在外。
entries.en: Once, while the provincial walls were still under repair, the siege ladders stood outside the unfinished works.
entries.literal: Once when repairing the provincial city walls was not yet complete, the ladders were outside.

entries.zh: 齊神武遣韓軌、司馬子如從河東宵濟襲羆，羆不之覺。
entries.en: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the Yellow River from Hedong by night and strike Wang Pi, who did not detect them.
entries.literal: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the Yellow River by night from Hedong and raid Pi; Pi did not notice.

entries.zh: 比曉，軌衆已乘梯入城。
entries.en: By dawn Han Gui's men were already climbing the ladders into the city.
entries.literal: By dawn, Gui's troops had already mounted the ladders and entered the city.

entries.zh: 羆尚臥未起，聞合外洶洶有聲，便袒身露髻徒跣，持一白挺，大呼而出。
entries.en: Wang Pi was still in bed when he heard uproar at the gate. He threw off his clothes, let down his hair, went barefoot, seized a white club, and charged out shouting.
