entries.literal: Pi was still lying down and had not risen; hearing a clamorous noise outside the inner gate, he bared his torso, loosened his hair, went barefoot, grasped a white club, and shouted as he came out.

entries.zh: 敵見之驚，逐至東門，左右稍集，合戰破之。
entries.en: The enemy fell back in shock. He drove them to the east gate, his men rallied around him, and together they broke the attack.
entries.literal: The enemy seeing him were startled; he drove them to the east gate; his attendants gradually gathered; they joined battle and defeated them.

entries.zh: 軌衆遂投城遁走。
entries.en: Han Gui's force then jumped from the walls and fled.
entries.literal: Gui's troops thereupon leapt from the walls and fled.

entries.zh: 時關中大饑，徵稅民間穀食，以供軍費。
entries.en: Guanzhong was in famine, and grain was requisitioned from the people to feed the army.
entries.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered great famine; grain was levied from among the people to supply military expenses.

entries.zh: 或隱匿者，令遞相告，多被篣棰，以是人有逃散。
entries.en: Anyone hiding grain was to be reported by his neighbors; many were flogged with bamboo, and people fled in fear.
entries.literal: Those who concealed grain were ordered to inform on one another; many were beaten with bamboo rods, and thereby people fled and scattered.

entries.zh: 唯羆信著于人，莫有隱者，得粟不少諸州，而無怨讟。
entries.en: Only in Wang Pi's jurisdiction did people trust him enough to surrender their grain willingly. He collected no less than other provinces, and no one complained.
entries.literal: Only Pi's trustworthiness was renowned among the people; there were none who concealed; the grain obtained was not less than other provinces, yet without complaints and slander.

entries.zh: 時魏孝武在藩，素聞其名，顥軍還，乃引為賓客，遇之甚厚。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu, then still at his princely fief, had long known Wang Sizheng's reputation. When Hao returned, the prince took him on as a client and treated him with great favor.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was at his fief; he had long heard his name; when Hao's army returned, he drew him in as a guest and treated him very generously.

entries.zh: 及登大位，委以心膂，遷安東將軍。
entries.en: When Xiaowu took the throne he made Wang Sizheng one of his closest confidants and promoted him to general who pacifies the east.
entries.literal: When he ascended the great throne, he entrusted him as heart and spine, transferred to general who pacifies the east.

entries.zh: 預定策功，封祁縣侯。
entries.en: For his part in securing the succession he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi county.
entries.literal: He shared in the merit of fixing the succession; was enfeoffed Marquis of Qi county.

entries.zh: 俄而齊神武潛有異圖，帝以思政可任大事，拜中軍大將軍、大都督，總宿衛兵。
entries.en: When Gao Huan began plotting in secret, the emperor judged Wang Sizheng fit for the gravest duties and made him grand general of the central army, grand commander, and overall commander of the palace guard.
entries.literal: Soon Gao Huan secretly had a different design; the emperor because Sizheng could be entrusted with great affairs appointed him grand general of the central army, grand commander, overall commander of palace-guard troops.

entries.zh: 思政乃言於帝曰：「高歡之心，行路所共知矣。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng then told the emperor: "Everyone on the road knows what Gao Huan intends.
entries.literal: Sizheng then spoke to the emperor, saying: "Gao Huan's heart—the road travelers all know it.

entries.zh: 洛陽四面受敵，非用武之地。
entries.en: Luoyang is beset on every side. It is no place to make a stand.
entries.literal: Luoyang on four sides receives enemies—it is not a place for wielding weapons.

entries.zh: 關中有崤、函之固，一人可禦萬夫。
entries.en: Guanzhong has the passes of Xiao and Han, where one man can hold off ten thousand.
entries.literal: Guanzhong has the fortifications of Xiao and Han; one man can oppose ten thousand.

entries.zh: 且士馬精強，糧儲委積，進可以討除逆命，退可以保據關、河。
entries.en: Its soldiers and horses are strong, its granaries full. From there one can advance to crush rebellion or fall back and hold the passes and the Yellow River.
entries.literal: Moreover troops and horses are keen and strong; grain stores piled up; advancing one can campaign to eliminate rebellious mandates; retreating one can hold and secure the passes and the river.

entries.zh: 宇文夏州糾合同盟，願立功效。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai of Xia Province has gathered the allied lords and is ready to serve.
entries.literal: Yuwen of Xia Province has rallied covenant allies and wishes to establish merit and achievement.

entries.zh: 若聞車駕西幸，必當奔走奉迎。
entries.en: If he hears that Your Majesty is moving west, he will hurry to meet you.
entries.literal: If he hears the imperial carriage will move west, he will surely run to meet and welcome it.

entries.zh: 藉天府之資，因已成之業，一二年間，習戰陣，勸耕桑，修舊京，何慮不克。」
entries.en: With the wealth of the western stronghold and a foundation already laid, in a year or two you can drill the army, restore agriculture, rebuild the old capital—what could stop you?"
entries.literal: Relying on the resources of the heavenly repository, following the already established enterprise—in one or two years, training in battle arrays, encouraging farming and sericulture, repairing the old capital—what worry that it cannot be achieved?"

entries.zh: 帝深然之。
entries.en: The emperor was deeply convinced.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply approved it.

entries.zh: 及齊神武兵至河北，帝乃西遷。
entries.en: When Gao Huan's army reached Hebei, the emperor fled west.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan's army reached Hebei, the emperor thereupon moved west.

entries.zh: 進爵太原郡公。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng was promoted to Duke of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Taiyuan commandery.

entries.zh: 沙苑之役，齊神武士馬甚盛。
entries.en: At the Battle of Shaye, Gao Huan's army was overwhelming.
entries.literal: At the Battle of Shaye, Gao Huan's troops and horses were very strong.

entries.zh: 太祖以華州沖要，遣使勞羆，令加守備。
entries.en: Because Huazhou was a vital point, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent an envoy to encourage Wang Pi and told him to strengthen the defenses.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor because Huazhou was strategically critical sent an envoy to encourage Pi and ordered him to increase defensive preparations.

entries.zh: 羆語使人曰：「老羆當道臥，貆子安得過！」
entries.en: Wang Pi told the messenger: "Old Pi lies across the road. What badger cub thinks he can slip by?"
entries.literal: Pi told the envoy: "Old Pi lies across the road—how can a badger cub get past!"

entries.zh: 太祖聞而壯之。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai admired his boldness when he heard this.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor hearing it admired his spirit.

entries.zh: 及齊神武至城下，謂羆曰：「何不早降？」
entries.en: When Gao Huan came beneath the walls he called to Wang Pi: "Why not surrender now?"
entries.literal: When Gao Huan reached beneath the walls, he said to Pi: "Why not surrender early?"

entries.zh: 羆乃大呼曰：「此城是王羆冢，生死在此，欲死者來。」
entries.en: Wang Pi shouted back: "This city is Wang Pi's tomb. Life and death are here. Whoever wants to die, come!"
entries.literal: Pi thereupon shouted loudly: "This city is Wang Pi's tomb; life and death are here—whoever wishes to die, come."

entries.zh: 齊神武遂不敢攻。
entries.en: Gao Huan did not dare press the assault.
entries.literal: Gao Huan thereupon did not dare attack.

entries.zh: 十三年，侯景叛東魏，擁兵梁、鄭，為東魏所攻。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei, held Liang and Zheng with his army, and came under attack from Eastern Wei.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei, held troops in Liang and Zheng, and was attacked by Eastern Wei.

entries.zh: 景乃請援乞師。
entries.en: Hou Jing then asked for help and begged for troops.
entries.literal: Jing thereupon requested aid and begged for troops.

entries.zh: 當時未卽應接。
entries.en: The court did not respond at once.
entries.literal: At the time they did not at once respond and join him.

entries.zh: 思政以為若不因機進取，後悔無及。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng argued that if they missed the moment there would be no recovering it.
entries.literal: Sizheng thought that if they did not seize the opportunity and advance, regret would come too late.

entries.zh: 卽率荊州步騎萬餘，從魯關向陽翟。
entries.en: He at once led more than ten thousand foot and horse from Jing Province through Lu Pass toward Yangzhai.
entries.literal: He at once led more than ten thousand Jing Province foot and horse, went from Lu Pass toward Yangzhai.

entries.zh: 思政入守潁川。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng entered and held Yingchuan.
entries.literal: Sizheng entered and held Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 景引兵向豫州，外稱略地，乃密遣送款於梁。
entries.en: Hou Jing marched toward Yu Province, claiming to seize ground, but secretly offered submission to Liang.
entries.literal: Jing led troops toward Yu Province, outwardly claiming to seize territory, but secretly sent submission to Liang.

entries.zh: 思政分佈諸軍，據景七州十二鎮。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng deployed his forces and seized seven provinces and twelve garrisons from Hou Jing.
entries.literal: Sizheng deployed the various armies and held seven of Jing's provinces and twelve garrisons.

entries.zh: 太祖乃以所授景使持節、太傅、大將軍、兼中書令、河南大行臺、河南諸軍事，回授思政。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then took the titles granted Hou Jing—commissioner bearing the staff, grand tutor, grand general, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, Henan mobile headquarters, and commander of all Henan military affairs—and offered them to Wang Sizheng instead.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon took the titles granted Jing—commissioner bearing the staff, grand tutor, grand general, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, Henan mobile headquarters, and commander of all Henan military affairs—and transferred them back to Sizheng.

entries.zh: 思政竝讓不受。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng declined them all.
entries.literal: Sizheng together declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 頻使敦喻，唯受河南諸軍事。
entries.en: Repeated envoys pressed him; he accepted only commander of all Henan military affairs.
entries.literal: Envoys repeatedly urged and instructed him; he accepted only commander of all Henan military affairs.

entries.zh: 東魏太尉高嶽、行臺慕容紹宗、儀同劉豐生等，率步騎十萬來攻潁川。
entries.en: Eastern Wei's grand commandant Gao Yue, field secretariat Murong Shaozong, acting three-division Liu Fengsheng, and others led a hundred thousand foot and horse against Yingchuan.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei's grand commandant Gao Yue, field secretariat Murong Shaozong, acting three-division Liu Fengsheng, and others led a hundred thousand foot and horse to attack Yingchuan.

entries.zh: 城內臥鼓偃旗，若無人者。
entries.en: Inside the city drums were stilled and banners lowered, as if it were empty.
entries.literal: Within the city drums were stilled and banners lowered, as if there were no one.

entries.zh: 嶽恃其衆，謂一戰可屠，乃四面鼓噪而上。
entries.en: Gao Yue trusted his numbers, thought one assault would overrun the place, and charged in from all sides with a great uproar.
entries.literal: Yue relied on his numbers, thinking one battle could slaughter them, and so from four sides raised a clamor and advanced.

entries.zh: 思政選城中驍勇，開門出突。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng picked the city's best fighters, opened the gates, and struck out.
entries.literal: Sizheng selected the city's fierce and brave, opened the gates, and sallied out in a sudden attack.

entries.zh: 嶽衆不敢當，引軍亂退。
entries.en: Gao Yue's men could not stand against them and broke in disorder.
entries.literal: Yue's host did not dare withstand them and withdrew the army in disorder.

entries.zh: 嶽知不可卒攻，乃多修營壘。
entries.en: Gao Yue saw he could not take the city at a rush and built many camps and ramparts.
entries.literal: Yue knew it could not be taken in a sudden attack and therefore built many camps and ramparts.

entries.zh: 又隨地勢高處，築土山以臨城中。
entries.en: He also piled earthen hills on high ground to overlook the city.
entries.literal: Again, following high ground in the terrain, he built earthen hills to overlook the city.

entries.zh: 飛梯火車，晝夜攻之。
entries.en: Flying ladders and fire carts assaulted it day and night.
entries.literal: Flying ladders and fire carts attacked day and night.

entries.zh: 思政亦作火攢，因迅風便投之土山。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng made fire bundles too and, when the wind rose, hurled them onto the earthen hills.
entries.literal: Sizheng also made fire bundles and, taking advantage of a swift wind, cast them onto the earthen hills.

entries.zh: 又以火箭射之，燒其攻具。
entries.en: He also shot fire arrows and burned their siege engines.
entries.literal: Again with fire arrows he shot them and burned their siege engines.

entries.zh: 仍募勇士，縋而出戰。
entries.en: He still recruited brave men to let themselves down by rope and sally out.
entries.literal: Still he recruited brave men and, lowering ropes, went out to fight.

entries.zh: 嶽衆披靡，其守土山人亦棄山而走。
entries.en: Gao Yue's army was routed, and the men on the earthen hills abandoned them and fled.
entries.literal: Yue's host was routed, and those guarding the earthen hills also abandoned the hills and fled.

entries.zh: 齊文襄更益嶽兵，堰洧水以灌城。
entries.en: Gao Cheng, Wenxiang of Qi, sent more troops to Gao Yue and dammed the Wei River to flood the city.
entries.literal: Wenxiang of Qi further reinforced Yue's troops and dammed the Wei River to flood the city.

entries.zh: 城中水泉湧溢，不可防止。
entries.en: Springs and wells inside the city overflowed and could not be stopped.
entries.literal: Within the city springs and wells overflowed and could not be stopped or blocked.

entries.zh: 懸釜而炊，糧力俱竭。
entries.en: They cooked from pots hung overhead; food and strength were both spent.
entries.literal: They hung cauldrons to cook; grain and strength were both exhausted.

entries.zh: 慕容紹宗、劉豐生及其將慕容永珍共乘樓船以望城內，令善射者俯射城中。
entries.en: Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and their officer Murong Yongzhen rode tower ships to look into the city and had skilled archers shoot down from above.
entries.literal: Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and their general Murong Yongzhen together rode tower ships to look into the city and ordered skilled archers to shoot down into it.

entries.zh: 俄而大風暴起，船乃飄至城下。
entries.en: Soon a great wind rose and the ships drifted below the walls.
entries.literal: Before long a great windstorm arose, and the ships drifted to below the walls.

entries.zh: 城上人以長鉤牽船，弓弩亂髮。
entries.en: Men on the walls hooked the ships with long poles and rained bowshot and bolts on them.
entries.literal: Men atop the walls used long hooks to pull the ships and shot bows and crossbows in confusion.

entries.zh: 紹宗窮急，投水而死。
entries.en: Murong Shaozong, in desperation, threw himself into the water and drowned.
entries.literal: Shaozong, in extremity, threw himself into the water and died.

entries.zh: 豐生浮向土山，復中矢而斃。
entries.en: Liu Fengsheng floated toward the earthen hill and was struck again by an arrow and killed.
entries.literal: Fengsheng floated toward the earthen hill and again was hit by an arrow and died.

entries.zh: 生擒永珍。
entries.en: Murong Yongzhen was taken alive.
entries.literal: Yongzhen was captured alive.

entries.zh: 思政謂之曰：「僕之破亡，在於晷漏。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng told him: "My fall is only hours away.
entries.literal: Sizheng said to him: "My ruin is a matter of hours.

entries.zh: 誠知殺卿無益，然人臣之節，守之以死。」
entries.en: I know killing you does no good, yet a minister's duty is kept even unto death."
entries.literal: I truly know that killing you would be of no benefit, yet a minister's integrity is kept even unto death."

entries.zh: 乃流涕斬之。
entries.en: Then, weeping, he beheaded him.
entries.literal: Thereupon, weeping, he beheaded him.

entries.zh: 幷收紹宗等尸，以禮埋瘞。
entries.en: He also gathered the bodies of Murong Shaozong and the others and buried them with ceremony.
entries.literal: He also gathered the corpses of Shaozong and the others and buried them with rites.

entries.zh: 齊文襄聞之，乃率步騎十一萬來攻。
entries.en: Gao Cheng heard of this and marched with a hundred and ten thousand foot and horse to attack.
entries.literal: Wenxiang of Qi heard of this and thereupon led a hundred and ten thousand foot and horse to attack.

entries.zh: 自至堰下，督勵士卒。
entries.en: He came in person to the dam and urged the troops on.
entries.literal: He himself came to the dam and urged and encouraged the soldiers.

entries.zh: 水壯，城北面遂崩。
entries.en: The water rose, and the north wall of the city collapsed.
entries.literal: The water swelled, and the north face of the city thereupon collapsed.

entries.zh: 水便滿溢，無措足之地。
entries.en: Water flooded everywhere until there was nowhere to stand.
entries.literal: The water then overflowed everywhere, with no place to set a foot.

entries.zh: 思政知事不濟，率左右據土山，謂之曰：「吾受國重任，本望平難立功。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng saw all was lost, took his close attendants to the earthen hill, and told them: "I bore the state's heavy trust and meant to end this crisis and win merit.
entries.literal: Sizheng knew the affair would not succeed, led his close attendants to hold the earthen hill, and said to them: "I received the state's heavy charge and originally hoped to settle calamity and establish merit.

entries.zh: 精誠無感，遂辱王命。
entries.en: Heaven did not answer my sincerity, and I have shamed the throne's charge.
entries.literal: Sincerity moved nothing; I have thus disgraced the royal command.

entries.zh: 今力屈道窮，計無所出。
entries.en: Now my strength is spent and every road is closed; I have no plan left.
entries.literal: Now strength is spent and the way is exhausted; no plan remains.

entries.zh: 唯當效死，以謝朝恩。」
entries.en: I can only die to answer the court's grace."
entries.literal: I can only offer my death to answer the court's grace."

entries.zh: 因仰天大哭。
entries.en: Then he looked up to heaven and wept aloud.
entries.literal: Thereupon he looked up to heaven and wept greatly.

entries.zh: 左右皆號慟。
entries.en: Those beside him all wailed.
entries.literal: Those at his side all wailed in grief.

entries.zh: 思政西向再拜，便欲自刎。
entries.en: Wang Sizheng bowed twice toward the west and was about to kill himself.
entries.literal: Sizheng bowed twice facing west and was about to cut his own throat.

entries.zh: 先是，齊文襄告城中人曰：「有能生致王大將軍者，封侯，重賞。
entries.en: Earlier Gao Cheng had told the city: "Whoever brings in Grand General Wang alive will be made marquis and richly rewarded.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wenxiang of Qi had told the people in the city: "Whoever can bring in Grand General Wang alive shall be enfeoffed marquis and richly rewarded.

entries.zh: 若大將軍身有損傷，親近左右，皆從大戮。」
entries.en: If Grand General Wang is harmed, his close attendants will all be put to death."
entries.literal: If Grand General Wang's person suffers injury, his close attendants and those near him shall all suffer great execution."

entries.zh: 都督駱訓謂思政曰：「公常語訓等，但將我頭降，非但得富貴，亦是活一城人。
entries.en: Area commander Luo Xun said to Wang Sizheng: "You often told us, 'Take my head and surrender—you will win wealth and honor and save a whole city.
entries.literal: Area commander Luo Xun said to Sizheng: "You often told Xun and the others, 'Just take my head and surrender—not only will you gain wealth and honor, you will also save a whole city of people.

entries.zh: 今高相旣有此言，公豈不哀城中士卒也！」
entries.en: Gao Cheng has already said as much—will you not pity the men in the city!'"
entries.literal: Now the High Minister already has this word—will you not pity the soldiers in the city!'"

entries.zh: 固共止之，不得引決。
entries.en: They held him back by force, and he could not kill himself.
entries.literal: They firmly together stopped him, and he could not carry out his resolve.

entries.zh: 齊文襄遣其常侍趙彥深就土山執手申意。
entries.en: Gao Cheng sent his regular attendant Zhao Yanshen to the earthen hill, took Wang Sizheng's hand, and spoke his mind.
entries.literal: Wenxiang of Qi sent his regular attendant Zhao Yanshen to the earthen hill, took his hand, and conveyed his intent.

entries.zh: 引見文襄，辭氣慷慨，無撓屈之容。
entries.en: He was brought before Gao Cheng; his bearing was impassioned and unbroken.
entries.literal: He was led to an audience with Wenxiang; his words and tone were impassioned, with no appearance of bending or yielding.

entries.zh: 文襄以其忠於所事，禮遇甚厚。
entries.en: Gao Cheng honored him greatly for his loyalty to his charge.
entries.literal: Wenxiang, because he was loyal to what he served, treated him with great courtesy.

entries.zh: 王羆 子慶遠 孫述 王思政
entries.en: Wang Pi — Qingyuan — Shu — Wang Sizheng
entries.literal: Wang Pi; his son Qingyuan; his grandson Shu; Wang Sizheng

entries.zh: 誼倜儻有大志，深為高祖所親委。
entries.en: Wang Yi was bold and high-minded, and won the deep trust of High Ancestor Yuwen Yong.
entries.literal: Yi was free-spirited and had great ambition, and was deeply trusted and entrusted by the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 少歷顯職，見重於時。
entries.en: From youth he held conspicuous posts and was respected in his time.
entries.literal: In youth he passed through prominent offices and was valued by the age.

entries.zh: 位至柱國、平陽郡公。
entries.en: He rose to pillar of state and Duke of Pingyang.
entries.literal: His rank reached pillar of state and Duke of Pingyang commandery.

entries.zh: 宣帝卽位，進封揚國公，拜大司空。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was raised to Duke of Yang and made grand minister of works.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Yang state and appointed grand minister of works.

entries.zh: 大象末，襄州總管、上柱國。
entries.en: At the end of the Daxiang era he was governor-general of Xiang and upper pillar of state.
entries.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was governor-general of Xiang Province and upper pillar of state.

entries.zh: 有七子，敬讓璨師寬知名。
entries.en: He had seven sons; Jing, Rang, Can, Shi, and Kuan were well known.
entries.literal: He had seven sons; Jing, Rang, Can, Shi, and Kuan were well known.

entries.zh: 敬少歷顯職，封化隆縣侯。
entries.en: Jing in youth held eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Hualong.
entries.literal: Jing in youth passed through eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Hualong county.

entries.zh: 後襲爵涼國公，位至柱國大將軍、華州刺史。
entries.en: He later inherited the ducal title of Liang, rose to pillar-of-state grand general, and became governor of Hua.
entries.literal: Later he inherited the title Duke of Liang state and rose to pillar-of-state grand general and governor of Hua Province.

entries.zh: 讓，大將軍、鄜州刺史、河東郡公。
entries.en: Rang was grand general, governor of Fu, and Duke of Hedong.
entries.literal: Rang was grand general, governor of Fu Province, and Duke of Hedong commandery.

entries.zh: 璨，開府儀同三司、宜陽縣公。
entries.en: Can held opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol and was Duke of Yiyang.
entries.literal: Can was opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol and Duke of Yiyang county.

entries.zh: 〔建德五年，從高祖于幷州，戰歿，贈上大將軍，追封清都郡公。
entries.en: [In Jiande fifth year Can followed Gaozu at Bing Province, fell in battle, and was posthumously made upper grand general and Duke of Qingdu.
entries.literal: [In Jiande fifth year, following Gaozu at Bing Province, he died in battle, posthumously awarded upper grand general, and posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Qingdu commandery.

entries.zh: 師，尚世宗女，位至上儀同大將軍、幽州刺史、博陵郡公。
entries.en: Shi married Emperor Xiaoming's daughter and rose to upper equal-to-three-division grand general, governor of You, and Duke of Boling.
entries.literal: Shi married Shizong's daughter and rose to upper equal-to-three-division grand general, governor of You Province, and Duke of Boling commandery.

entries.zh: 寬，開府儀同大將軍、武始郡公。
entries.en: Kuan was opening-office equal-to-three-division grand general and Duke of Wuzhi.
entries.literal: Kuan was opening-office equal-to-three-division grand general and Duke of Wuzhi commandery.

entries.zh: 祥弟隆，大將軍、襄樂縣公。〕
entries.en: He Lanxiang's younger brother Long was grand general and Duke of Xiangle.
entries.literal: Xiang's younger brother Long was grand general and Duke of Xiangle county.

entries.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，綱以親戚掌禁兵，除小司馬。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, Wei Chigang, as a kinsman commanding the forbidden troops, was made junior minister of war.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Gang, as a kinsman holding the forbidden troops, was appointed junior minister of war.

entries.zh: 又與晉公護廢帝，語在《護傳》。
entries.en: He also helped Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu depose the emperor; the account is in the Biography of Hu.
entries.literal: He also together with Duke of Jin Hu deposed the emperor; the account is in the Biography of Hu.

entries.zh: 世宗卽位，進位柱國大將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaoming acceded, he was raised to pillar-of-state grand general.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was advanced in rank to pillar-of-state grand general.

entries.zh: 武成元年，進封吳國公，邑萬戶，除涇州總管、五州十一防諸軍事、涇州刺史。
entries.en: In Wucheng 1 (559) Wei Chigang was raised to Duke of Wu with ten thousand households, and made area commander of Jing, commander of military affairs in five provinces and eleven garrisons, and governor of Jing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Wu state with a fief of ten thousand households, and appointed area commander of Jing Province, commander of military affairs in five provinces and eleven garrisons, and governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 是歲，大長公主薨于京師，綱去職。
entries.en: That year, when the Grand Princess died in the capital, Chigang resigned from office.
entries.literal: That year the Grand Princess died in the capital; Gang left office.

entries.zh: 尋起復本官。
entries.en: He was soon recalled to his former post.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled and restored to his former post.

entries.zh: 保定元年，拜少傅。
entries.en: In Baoding 1 (561) he was made junior tutor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Baoding, he was appointed junior tutor.

entries.zh: 俄而授大司空。
entries.en: Before long he was made grand minister of works.
entries.literal: Before long he was granted grand minister of works.

entries.zh: 二年，出為陝州總管、七州十三防諸軍事、陝州刺史。
entries.en: The next year he was sent out as area commander of Shan, commander of military affairs in seven provinces and thirteen garrisons, and governor of Shan.
entries.literal: In the second year, he went out as area commander of Shan Province, commander of military affairs in seven provinces and thirteen garrisons, and governor of Shan Province.

entries.zh: 四年，晉公護東討，乃配綱甲士，留鎮京師。
entries.en: In the fourth year Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu campaigned east; Chigang was given armored troops and left to garrison the capital.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Duke of Jin Hu campaigned east; Gang was assigned armored troops and remained to garrison the capital.

entries.zh: 綱以天子在宮，必無內慮，乃請出外，頓於咸陽。
entries.en: Chigang reasoned that with the emperor in the palace there could be no internal threat, and asked to go out, encamping at Xianyang.
entries.literal: Gang, because the Son of Heaven was in the palace and there would certainly be no internal worries, thereupon requested to go out and encamped at Xianyang.

entries.zh: 大軍還，綱復歸鎮。
entries.en: When the main army returned, Chigang resumed his garrison post.
entries.literal: When the great army returned, Gang again returned to garrison duty.

entries.zh: 天和二年，以綱政績可稱，賜帛千段、穀六千斛、錢二十萬，增邑四百戶。
entries.en: In Tianhe 2 (567), for Chigang's commendable record in office, the court granted one thousand bolts of silk, six thousand hu of grain, two hundred thousand in cash, and four hundred more households.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, because Gang's administrative achievements were commendable, he was granted one thousand bolts of silk, six thousand hu of grain, two hundred thousand in cash, and an increased fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 陳公純等以皇后阿史那氏自突厥將入塞，詔徵綱與大將軍王傑率衆迎衛於境首。
entries.en: When Duke of Chen Chun and others were bringing Empress Ashina from the Turks to enter the frontier, an edict summoned Chigang and Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the frontier.
entries.literal: Duke of Chen, Chun, and others, because Empress Ashina was about to enter the frontier from the Turks, an edict summoned Gang together with Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the border.

entries.zh: 三年，追論河橋之功，封一子縣公，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In the third year, in recognition of his service at River Bridge, one son was enfeoffed county duke with a thousand households.
entries.literal: In the third year, in retrospective recognition of merit at River Bridge, one son was enfeoffed as county duke with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 四年五月，薨于京師，時年五十三。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the fourth year he died in the capital at the age of fifty-three.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, he died in the capital, age fifty-three.

entries.zh: 贈太保、十二州諸軍事、同州刺史。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand tutor, commander of military affairs in twelve provinces, and governor of Tong.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted grand tutor, commander of military affairs in twelve provinces, and governor of Tong Province.

entries.zh: 諡曰武。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Wu (Martial).
entries.literal: Posthumous title Wu.

entries.zh: 第三子安，以嫡嗣。
entries.en: His third son An succeeded as legitimate heir.
entries.literal: The third son An succeeded as legitimate heir.

entries.zh: 大象末，位至柱國。
entries.en: At the end of the Daxiang era he rose to pillar of state.
entries.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached the rank of pillar of state.

entries.zh: 安兄運，別有傳。
entries.en: An's elder brother Yun has a separate biography.
entries.literal: An's elder brother Yun has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 運弟勤，少歷顯位。
entries.en: Yun's younger brother Qin rose young to high office.
entries.literal: Yun's younger brother Qin, in youth passed through eminent posts.

entries.zh: 大象末，青州總管。
entries.en: At the end of the Daxiang era he was area commander of Qing Province.
entries.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he was area commander of Qing Province.

entries.zh: 起兵應伯父迥，事在《迥傳》。
entries.en: He raised troops in support of his uncle Yuchi Jiong; the account is in the "Biography of Yuchi Jiong."
entries.literal: He raised troops in response to his uncle Jiong; the account is in the "Biography of Jiong."

entries.zh: 安弟敬，尚世宗女河南公主，位至儀同三司。
entries.en: An's younger brother Jing married Emperor Shizong's daughter, Princess Henan, and rose to opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes.
entries.literal: An's younger brother Jing married Emperor Shizong's daughter, Princess Henan, and reached opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 椿字千年。
entries.en: Chun, styled Qiannian.
entries.literal: Chun, styled Qiannian.

entries.zh: 世宗時，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: During Emperor Shizong's reign he was made general of chariots and cavalry and opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes.
entries.literal: During Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed general of chariots and cavalry and opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 尋遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，改封永世縣公，邑一千二百戶。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to grand general of flying cavalry and opening-the-feudatory equal in rank to the three dukes, and re-enfeoffed Duke of Yongshi with twelve hundred households.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand general of flying cavalry and opening-the-feudatory equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yongshi county with a fief of one thousand two hundred households.

entries.zh: 保定二年，授幽州刺史。
entries.en: In Baoding 2 (562) he was made governor of You Province.
entries.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he was granted governor of You Province.

entries.zh: 天和初，除左宮伯，進位大將軍。
entries.en: At the start of Tianhe he was made left palace guard and promoted to grand general.
entries.literal: At the start of Tianhe, he was appointed left palace guard, and advanced in rank to grand general.

entries.zh: 魏正光五年，廣陽王深北征，請龜為甯朔將軍，委以帳內兵事。
entries.en: In Wei Zhengguang 5 (524), when Prince Guangyang Shen campaigned north, he asked for Fugui as general who pacifies the north and entrusted him with headquarters military affairs.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang of Wei, Prince Guangyang Shen campaigned north; he requested Gui as General Who Pacifies the North and entrusted him with military affairs within the headquarters.

entries.zh: 尋除善無郡守。
entries.en: He was soon made governor of Shanwu commandery.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Shanwu commandery.

entries.zh: 孝昌三年，又除別將，從長孫稚西征。
entries.en: In Xiaochang 3 (527) he was made separate commander and followed Changsun Zhi on the western campaign.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang, he was again appointed separate commander, following Changsun Zhi on the western campaign.

entries.zh: 以戰功，累遷征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: For battlefield merit he rose in stages to general who campaigns west and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: For battle merit, he was progressively transferred to general who campaigns west and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

entries.zh: 後還洛，授都督，遂為齊神武所寵任，加授大都督。
entries.en: Later he returned to Luoyang, was made commander, and came under the favor of Gao Huan, who additionally made him grand commander.
entries.literal: Later he returned to Luoyang, was granted commander, and thereupon was favored and entrusted by Qi Shenwu, with additional appointment as grand commander.

entries.zh: 沙苑之敗，隨例來降。
entries.en: After the defeat at Shayuan he surrendered as others had done.
entries.literal: After the defeat at Shayuan, he surrendered according to precedent.

entries.zh: 太祖以其豪門，解縛禮之。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, because he came from a great house, had his bonds cut and received him with full ceremony.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because he was of a great house, released his bonds and treated him with ceremony.

entries.zh: 仍以邵惠公女妻之。
entries.en: He also gave him a daughter of Duke Hui of Shao in marriage.
entries.literal: He also gave him Duke Hui of Shao's daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 大統四年，封長樂縣公，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In Datong 4 (538) he was enfeoffed Duke of Changle with a thousand households.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Changle county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 自此常從太祖征討，亟有戰功。
entries.en: From then on he constantly followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai on campaign and won repeated distinction.
entries.literal: From this he constantly followed the Grand Progenitor on campaigns and repeatedly had battle merit.

entries.zh: 八年，出為北雍州刺史，加大都督。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was sent out as governor of North Yong, with the additional rank of grand commander.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he went out as governor of North Yong Province, with additional rank as grand commander.

entries.zh: 尋進位車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was soon raised to general of chariots and cavalry, opening-establishment equal in rank to the three dukes, and attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to general of chariots and cavalry, opening-establishment equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes, and attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.

entries.zh: 十四年，徵拜侍中，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，除恆州刺史，增邑通前一千四百戶。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was summoned as palace attendant, with additional rank as grand general of flying cavalry and opening-the-feudatory equal in rank to the three dukes, and made governor of Heng; his fief was increased to one thousand four hundred households in all.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was summoned and appointed palace attendant, with additional rank as grand general of flying cavalry, opening-the-feudatory equal-in-rank to the Three Dukes, and governor of Heng Province; his fief was increased, together with the previous total of one thousand four hundred households.

entries.zh: 十七年，卒。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he died.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, he died.

entries.zh: 子椿嗣。
entries.en: His son Chun succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Chun succeeded.

entries.zh: 旣而齊神武舉兵入洛，魏孝武西遷，慶謂所親曰：「高歡跋扈，將有篡逆之謀，豈可苟安目前，受其控制也！」
entries.en: Before long Gao Huan raised troops and entered Luoyang, and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west. Yan Qing told his intimates: "Gao Huan is overbearing and will usurp the throne—how can we rest content under his control?"
entries.literal: Before long Qi Shenwu raised troops and entered Luoyang; Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west; Qing said to those close to him: "Gao Huan is overbearing and will have designs of usurpation—how can one be content for the moment and accept his control!"

entries.zh: 遂以大統三年，自宜陽歸闕。
entries.en: In Datong 3 (537) he left Yiyang and returned to court.
entries.literal: Thereupon in the third year of Datong, from Yiyang he returned to court.

entries.zh: 太祖謂慶曰：「高歡逆亂，宇內分崩，羣盜競興，入皆徇己。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Yan Qing: "Gao Huan is in rebellion; the realm is torn apart; bandits rise on every side; every man serves himself alone.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to Qing: "Gao Huan is rebellious and disorderly; within the realm the state is split apart; bandits compete to rise; every man serves himself.

entries.zh: 卿遂能盡忠貞之節，重君臣之義，背逆歸順，舍危就安，雖古人所稱，何以加也。」
entries.en: Yet you kept faith with unstinted loyalty, honored the bond between ruler and minister, turned from rebellion and came over, left danger for safety—though the ancients were praised, what more could be said?"
entries.literal: You were able to fulfill the integrity of loyalty, honor the righteousness of ruler and minister, turn from the rebel and return in submission, leave peril and seek safety—though the ancients were praised, how could one add to this?"

entries.zh: 卽拜中堅將軍、奉車都尉。
entries.en: He thereupon made him resolute general and commandant of the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: He thereupon appointed him resolute general and commandant of the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 河橋之役，以功拜前將軍、太中大夫，遷後將軍，封安次縣子，邑四百戶。
entries.en: At River Bridge, for merit he was made forward general and grand master of palace consultation, then rear general, and enfeoffed Viscount of Anci with four hundred households.
entries.literal: At the campaign of River Bridge, for merit he was appointed forward general and grand master of palace consultation, transferred to rear general, and enfeoffed Viscount of Anci county with a fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 及邙山之戰，先登陷陳。
entries.en: At Mount Mang he was first over the wall and broke the enemy line.
entries.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang, he was first to ascend and break the enemy line.

entries.zh: 拜撫軍將軍、大都督，進爵為伯，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: He was made pacifying-army general and grand commander, raised to earl, and given five hundred more households.
entries.literal: He was appointed pacifying-army general and grand commander, advanced in nobility to earl, and given an increased fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 晉公護母，慶之姑也。
entries.en: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu's mother was Yan Qing's paternal aunt.
entries.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu's mother was Qing's paternal aunt.

entries.zh: 護雖擅朝，而慶未嘗阿附。
entries.en: Although Yuwen Hu monopolized the court, Yan Qing never curried favor with him.
entries.literal: Although Hu monopolized the court, Qing never curried favor with him.

entries.zh: 及護誅，高祖以此重之。
entries.en: When Yuwen Hu was executed, High Ancestor Yuwen Yong highly valued him for this.
entries.literal: When Hu was executed, the High Ancestor highly valued him for this.

entries.zh: 乃詔慶第十二子毗尚帝女清都公主。
entries.en: An edict then had Yan Qing's twelfth son Pi marry the emperor's daughter, Princess Qingdu.
entries.literal: An edict then had Qing's twelfth son Pi marry the emperor's daughter, Princess Qingdu.

entries.zh: 慶雖位望隆重，婚連帝室，常以謙慎自守，時人以此稱之。
entries.en: Though Yan Qing's rank and stature were weighty and his marriage tied him to the imperial house, he always kept himself humble and cautious, and people praised him for it.
entries.literal: Though Qing's rank and stature were weighty and his marriage tied him to the imperial house, he always kept himself with humility and caution, and people praised him for this.

entries.zh: 建德二年，抗表致仕，優詔許焉。
entries.en: In Jiande 2 (573) he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; a gracious edict granted it.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jiande he submitted a memorial resisting further service and requesting retirement; a gracious edict granted it.

entries.zh: 慶既衰老，恆嬰沉痼。
entries.en: Yan Qing had grown old and was constantly afflicted with lingering illness.
entries.literal: Qing had grown old and was constantly afflicted with lingering illness.

entries.zh: 宣帝以其先朝耆舊，特異常倫，乃詔靜帝至第問疾。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan, because he was an elder of the former reign, treated him with exceptional regard and issued an edict for Emperor Jing to visit his residence to inquire after his health.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan, because he was an elder of the former reign, treated him with exceptional regard beyond ordinary custom, and issued an edict for Emperor Jing to visit his residence to inquire after his health.

entries.zh: 賜布帛千段。
entries.en: He was granted one thousand segments of cloth and silk.
entries.literal: He was granted one thousand segments of cloth and silk.

entries.zh: 醫藥所須，令有司供給。
entries.en: Whatever medicine was needed was ordered supplied by the relevant offices.
entries.literal: Whatever medicine was needed was ordered supplied by the relevant offices.

entries.zh: 大象二年，拜上柱國。
entries.en: In Daxiang 2 (580) he was made upper pillar of state.
entries.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was made upper pillar of state.

entries.zh: 隋文帝踐極，又令皇太子就第問疾，仍供醫藥之費。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he again ordered the crown prince to visit his residence to inquire after his health and continued to supply medical expenses.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he again ordered the crown prince to visit his residence to inquire after his health and continued to supply medical expenses.

entries.zh: 開皇二年薨，時年七十七。
entries.en: He died in Kaihuang 2 (582), at age seventy-seven.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang he died, at age seventy-seven.

entries.zh: 贈司空、荊譙淅湖灃廣蒙七州諸軍事、荊州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously made minister of works, commander over military affairs of Jing, Qiao, Xi, Hu, Feng, Guang, and Meng provinces, and governor of Jing.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given minister of works, command over military affairs of the seven provinces of Jing, Qiao, Xi, Hu, Feng, Guang, and Meng, and governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 諡曰成。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Cheng.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Cheng.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：中陽御曆，沛邑多封侯；
entries.en: The historiographer writes: When Liu Bang held the throne from Zhongyang, Pei produced many enfeoffed marquises;
entries.literal: The historiographer says: When Zhongyang held the throne, Pei had many enfeoffed marquises;

entries.zh: 白水配天，南陽皆貴戚。
entries.en: when Guangwu matched Heaven from Baishui, Nanyang was full of imperial kin.
entries.literal: when Baishui matched Heaven, Nanyang was all imperial kin.

entries.zh: 是知階緣近屬，以取寵榮，其來尚矣。
entries.en: Thus one sees that rising through close kinship to win favor and glory is an age-old pattern.
entries.literal: Thus one knows that climbing by close kinship to win favor and glory is a pattern long established.

entries.zh: 王盟等始以親黨升朝，終以才能進達，勤宣運始，位列周行。
entries.en: Wang Meng and the others at first entered court through kinship ties, but in the end rose through ability; from the dynasty's founding they served diligently and took their places at court.
entries.literal: Wang Meng and the others at first rose through kinship factions, but in the end advanced through talent; from the dynasty's founding they labored and took their places in the Zhou court.

entries.zh: 實參迹於功臣，蓋弗由於恩澤也。
entries.en: They truly walked in the footsteps of merit ministers—it was scarcely through favor alone.
entries.literal: They truly shared the tracks of merit ministers—it was scarcely through favor alone.

entries.zh: 王盟字子仵，明德皇后之兄也。
entries.en: Wang Meng, styled Ziwu, was the elder brother of Empress Mingde.
entries.literal: Wang Meng, styled Ziwu, was elder brother of Empress Mingde.

entries.zh: 其先樂浪人。
entries.en: His family came from Lelang.
entries.literal: His forebears were men of Lelang.

entries.zh: 六世祖波，前燕太宰。
entries.en: Six generations back, Bo had been grand preceptor of Former Yan.
entries.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Bo was grand preceptor of Former Yan.

entries.zh: 祖珍，魏黃門侍郎，贈幷州刺史、樂浪公。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhen had served Wei as yellow gate gentleman-attendant and was posthumously made governor of Bing and Duke of Lelang.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhen was yellow gate gentleman-attendant of Wei, posthumously awarded governor of Bing Province and Duke of Lelang.

entries.zh: 父羆，伏波將軍，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。
entries.en: His father Pi, a general who crosses the waves, was posted to Wuchuan as a soldier of good family and made the town his home.
entries.literal: His father Pi was general who crosses the waves; as a good-household youth he garrisoned Wuchuan and settled his family there.

entries.zh: 侯景之渡江，梁元帝時鎮江陵，旣以內難方殷，請脩鄰好。
entries.en: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jiangling; with civil war raging at home, he sought to mend relations with the north.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, Emperor Yuan of Liang was then garrisoning Jiangling; since internal troubles were pressing, he requested to restore neighborly relations.

entries.zh: 其弟武陵王紀，在蜀稱帝，率衆東下，將攻之。
entries.en: His younger brother Xiao Ji, Prince of Wuling, had declared himself emperor in Shu and was marching east to attack him.
entries.literal: His younger brother, Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji, in Shu proclaimed himself emperor, led troops east, and was about to attack him.

entries.zh: 梁元帝大懼，乃移書請救，又請伐蜀。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan of Liang was terrified; he sent appeals for aid and also asked for an expedition against Shu.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang was greatly afraid; he thereupon sent a letter requesting rescue, and also requested a campaign against Shu.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「蜀可圖矣。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "Shu can be taken now.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "Shu can now be taken.

entries.zh: 取蜀制梁，在茲一舉。」
entries.en: Seize Shu and you control Liang—all hangs on this one stroke."
entries.literal: To take Shu and control Liang—here in this one move it lies."

entries.zh: 乃與羣公會議，諸將多有異同。
entries.en: He then convened the senior lords; the generals were divided.
entries.literal: He thereupon met with the assembled lords in council; among the generals many had differing views.

entries.zh: 唯迥以為紀旣盡銳東下，蜀必空虛，王師臨之，必有征無戰。
entries.en: Only Yuchi Jiong argued that with Ji's best troops already marching east, Shu would be hollow; once the imperial army arrived, victory would come without a fight.
entries.literal: Only Jiong held that since Ji had already sent his best troops east, Shu must be empty; when the royal army arrived, there would surely be a campaign but no battle.

entries.zh: 太祖深以為然，謂迥曰：「伐蜀之事，一以委汝，計將安出？」
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai strongly agreed and asked Yuchi Jiong: "The Shu campaign is entirely in your hands—what is your plan?"
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai deeply agreed, and said to Jiong: "The matter of campaigning against Shu I wholly entrust to you—what plan do you propose?"

entries.zh: 迥曰：「蜀與中國隔絕百有餘年，恃其山川險阻，不虞我師之至。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong said: "Shu has been isolated from the heartland for over a century; trusting in its rugged terrain, it will not expect our army.
entries.literal: Jiong said: "Shu and the Central States have been cut off for more than a hundred years; relying on its mountains and rivers, steep and blocked, it does not expect our army's arrival.

entries.zh: 宜以精甲銳騎，星夜襲之。
entries.en: Send elite infantry and swift cavalry and fall upon them in a night march.
entries.literal: We should use picked armor and sharp cavalry and strike by night as if borne on stars.

entries.zh: 平路則倍道兼行，險途則緩兵漸進，出其不意，沖其腹心。
entries.en: On open roads, force the pace; on difficult ground, advance in measured steps—catch them off guard and drive at the heart of the province.
entries.literal: On level roads we should double the stages and march day and night; on dangerous paths we should slow the army and advance step by step; take them unawares and thrust at their vitals.

entries.zh: 蜀人旣駭官軍之臨速，必望風不守矣。」
entries.en: Once the Shu people see how fast the imperial army has come, they will collapse at the first rumor of its approach."
entries.literal: Once the people of Shu are alarmed that the official army has come so swiftly, they will surely see the wind and not hold their posts."

entries.zh: 於是乃令迥督開府元珍、乙弗亞、
entries.en: He then put Yuchi Jiong in command of opening-office Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya,
entries.literal: He thereupon ordered Jiong to supervise opening-office Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya,

entries.en: [variant: wan]
entries.literal: (wan)

entries.zh: 俟呂陵始、叱奴興、綦連雄、宇文升等六軍，甲士一萬二千，騎萬疋，伐蜀。
entries.en: Hou Lüling Shi, Chinu Xing, Qilian Xiong, Yuwen Sheng, and others in six armies—twelve thousand armored foot and ten thousand horse—to invade Shu.
entries.literal: Hou Lüling Shi, Chinu Xing, Qilian Xiong, Yuwen Sheng, and others—six armies—with twelve thousand armored soldiers and ten thousand horses, to campaign against Shu.

entries.zh: 以魏廢帝二年春，自散關由固道出白馬，趣晉壽，開平林舊道。
entries.en: In spring of the Deposed Emperor of Wei's second year he marched from San Pass by the Gudao route through White Horse toward Jinshou and reopened the old Pinglin road.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, from San Pass by the Gudao route through White Horse, he hastened toward Jinshou and opened the old Pinglin road.

entries.zh: 前軍臨劔閣，紀安州刺史樂廣，以州先降。
entries.en: The vanguard reached Jian Pass; Yue Guang, Ji's governor of An Province, surrendered first.
entries.literal: The vanguard reached Jian Pass; Ji's governor of An Province, Yue Guang, surrendered the province first.

entries.zh: 紀梁州刺史楊乾運時鎮潼州，又降。
entries.en: Yang Qianyun, Ji's governor of Liang Province then holding Tong Province, surrendered as well.
entries.literal: Ji's governor of Liang Province, Yang Qianyun, was then garrisoning Tong Province and also surrendered.

entries.zh: 六月，迥至潼州，大饗將士，引之而西。
entries.en: In the sixth month Yuchi Jiong reached Tong Province, held a great feast for his troops, and marched west.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Jiong reached Tong Province, feasted the officers and soldiers greatly, and led them west.

entries.zh: 紀益州刺史蕭撝不敢戰，遂嬰城自守。
entries.en: Xiao Hui, Ji's governor of Yi Province, dared not give battle and shut himself inside the city walls.
entries.literal: Ji's governor of Yi Province, Xiao Hui, did not dare to fight and thereupon closed the city and held firm.

entries.zh: 進軍圍之。
entries.en: The army advanced and laid siege.
entries.literal: The army advanced and besieged it.

entries.zh: 初，紀至巴郡，聞迥來侵，遣譙淹回師，為撝外援。
entries.en: Earlier, when Ji reached Ba commandery and learned that Yuchi Jiong was invading, he sent Qiao Yan back with his army to reinforce Hui.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Ji reached Ba commandery and heard that Jiong was coming to invade, he dispatched Qiao Yan to turn his army back as external support for Hui.

entries.zh: 迥分遣元珍、乙弗亞等以輕騎破之，遂降。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong sent Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, and others with light cavalry to break them, and Qiao Yan surrendered.
entries.literal: Jiong separately dispatched Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, and others with light cavalry to defeat him, and he thereupon surrendered.

entries.zh: 撝前後戰數十合，皆為迥所破。
entries.en: Xiao Hui fought dozens of engagements and was beaten every time by Yuchi Jiong.
entries.literal: Hui fought several dozen engagements before and after, and in all was defeated by Jiong.

entries.zh: 撝與紀子宜都王肅，及其文武官屬，詣軍門請見，迥以禮接之。
entries.en: Xiao Hui came with Xiao Ji's son, Prince Su of Yidu, and his civil and military staff to the camp gate to surrender; Yuchi Jiong received them with full courtesy.
entries.literal: Hui together with Xiao Ji's son, Prince Su of Yidu, and his civil and military officials and attendants came to the camp gate to request audience; Jiong received them with ceremony.

entries.zh: 其吏人等，各令復業。
entries.en: Clerks and commoners alike were told to return to their trades.
entries.literal: Their clerks and common people, each was ordered to return to his occupation.

entries.zh: 唯收僮隸及儲積以賞將士。
entries.en: Only bond servants and stored provisions were seized to reward the troops.
entries.literal: Only bond servants and stored provisions were taken to reward the officers and soldiers.

entries.zh: 號令嚴肅，軍無私焉。
entries.en: Discipline was strict and the army took no private plunder.
entries.literal: Orders and commands were strict and solemn; the army had no private gain.

entries.zh: 詔迥為大都督、益潼等十八州諸軍事、益州刺史。
entries.en: An edict made Yuchi Jiong grand commander over military affairs in eighteen provinces including Yi and Tong, and governor of Yi Province.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Jiong grand commander, military affairs of the eighteen provinces including Yi and Tong, and governor of Yi Province.

entries.zh: 以平蜀功，封一子為公。
entries.en: For pacifying Shu, one of his sons was enfeoffed duke.
entries.literal: For the merit of pacifying Shu, one son was enfeoffed duke.

entries.zh: 自劔閣以南，得承制封拜及黜陟。
entries.en: South of Jian Pass he was empowered to enfeoff, appoint, promote, and dismiss officials by delegated imperial authority.
entries.literal: From Jian Pass southward, he was authorized to act by imperial mandate in enfeoffing, appointing, and promoting or demoting officials.

entries.zh: 迥乃明賞罰，布恩威，綏緝新邦，經略未附，夷夏懷而歸之。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong then made rewards and punishments clear, combined kindness with authority, settled the newly conquered lands, reached out to those still unsubmitted, and won over both barbarian and Chinese alike.
entries.literal: Jiong thereupon made rewards and punishments clear, spread favor and awe, soothed and gathered the new territory, planned strategy toward those not yet submitted, and both barbarians and Chinese cherished him and came to him.

entries.zh: 尉遲迥 王謙 司馬消難
entries.en: Wei Chijiong (Yuchi Jiong); Wang Qian; Sima Xiaonan
entries.literal: Wei Chijiong; Wang Qian; Sima Xiaonan

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，以迥為大前疑，出為相州總管。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Yuchi Jiong was made grand mentor and posted as governor-general of Xiang Province.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jiong was made grand mentor and sent out as governor-general of Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 宣帝崩，隋文帝輔政，以迥望位夙重，懼為異圖，乃令迥子魏安公惇齎詔書以會葬徵迥。
entries.en: After Emperor Xuan's death Yang Jian, later Emperor Wen of Sui, took power as regent; fearing that Yuchi Jiong, long eminent in rank and reputation, might plot against him, he sent Jiong's son Dun, Duke of Wei'an, with an edict summoning Jiong to the capital for the funeral.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) assisted the government; because Jiong's reputation and rank had long been weighty, fearing he might harbor a different design, he ordered Jiong's son, Duke of Wei'an Dun, to carry an edict summoning Jiong on the pretext of attending the funeral.

entries.zh: 尋以鄖公韋孝寬代迥為總管。
entries.en: Soon Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, was sent to replace Yuchi Jiong as governor-general.
entries.literal: Soon after, Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan was sent to replace Jiong as governor-general.

entries.zh: 迥以隋文帝當權，將圖篡奪，遂謀舉兵，留惇而不受代。
entries.en: Seeing that Yang Jian held power and meant to seize the throne, Yuchi Jiong plotted rebellion, kept Dun with him, and refused to yield his post.
entries.literal: Jiong, because Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) held power and was about to usurp the throne, thereupon plotted to raise troops, kept Dun and refused to accept replacement.

entries.zh: 隋文帝又使候正破六汗裒詣迥喻旨，密與總管府長史晉昶等書，令為之備。
entries.en: Yang Jian also sent Houzheng Poliuhan Pu to explain the court's wishes to Yuchi Jiong, and secretly wrote to chief administrator Jin Chang and others at the governor-general's office telling them to stand ready.
entries.literal: Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) also sent Houzheng Poliuhan Pu to Jiong to explain the imperial intent, and secretly wrote to the governor-general's chief administrator Jin Chang and others, ordering them to prepare.

entries.zh: 迥聞之，殺長史及裒。
entries.en: When Yuchi Jiong learned of this, he killed the chief administrator and Pu.
entries.literal: When Jiong heard of it, he killed the chief administrator and Pu.

entries.zh: 乃集文武士庶，登城北樓而令之曰：「楊堅以凡庸之才，藉後父之勢，挾幼主而令天下，威福自己，賞罰無章，不臣之跡，暴於行路。
entries.en: He then gathered officials and commoners on the north city tower and declared: "Yang Jian is a man of ordinary gifts who rides the empress's father's power, controls the boy emperor, and rules as he pleases—reward and punishment are lawless, and his treason is plain for all on the road to see.
entries.literal: He thereupon assembled civil and military officials and common people, ascended the north city tower, and proclaimed to them: "Yang Jian, with commonplace talent, relying on the power of being father-in-law to the empress, holds the young lord and commands the realm; authority and favor are his alone, rewards and punishments without rule—the traces of disloyalty are exposed on the public road.

entries.zh: 吾居將相，與國舅甥，同休共戚，義由一體。
entries.en: I am general and minister; with the imperial uncle we are kin by marriage—we share the same fate, bound as one body.
entries.literal: I stand in the ranks of general and minister, and with the state's maternal uncle we are nephew and uncle; we share fortune and share woe—the righteousness binds us as one body.

entries.zh: 先帝處吾於此，本欲寄以安危。
entries.en: The late emperor posted me here to entrust the realm's safety to my hands.
entries.literal: The late emperor placed me here originally intending to entrust the realm's safety and peril to me.

entries.zh: 今欲與卿等糾合義勇，匡國庇人，進可以享榮名，退可以終臣節。
entries.en: Now I mean to rally loyal men with you to restore the dynasty and protect the people—advance, and we win honor; retreat, and we keep our loyalty intact.
entries.literal: Now I wish together with you to gather righteous volunteers, set the state aright and shelter the people—advancing, one may enjoy glory and fame; retreating, one may preserve ministerial integrity to the end.

entries.zh: 卿等以為何如？」
entries.en: What say you?"
entries.literal: What do you think?"

entries.zh: 於是衆咸從命，莫不感激。
entries.en: The crowd answered as one, every heart stirred.
entries.literal: Thereupon the multitude all followed his command; none failed to be moved and inspired.

entries.zh: 乃自稱大總管，承制署置官司。
entries.en: He then proclaimed himself grand governor-general and, acting by delegated imperial authority, set up offices and appointments.
entries.literal: He thereupon styled himself grand governor-general, and by delegated imperial authority established and appointed official posts.

entries.zh: 于時趙王招已入朝，留少子在國，迥又奉以號令。
entries.en: Prince of Zhao Zhao was already at court, with a younger son left behind; Yuchi Jiong issued orders in the prince's name as well.
entries.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Zhao had already entered court, leaving a younger son in the realm; Jiong again upheld him in issuing orders.

entries.zh: 迥弟子勤，時為青州總管，亦從迥。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong's nephew Qin, then governor-general of Qing Province, joined him too.
entries.literal: Jiong's younger brother's son Qin was then governor-general of Qing Province and also followed Jiong.

entries.zh: 迥所管相、衛、黎、毛、洺、貝、趙、冀、瀛、滄，勤所統青、膠、光、莒諸州，皆從之。
entries.en: The provinces under Yuchi Jiong—Xiang, Wei, Li, Mao, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang—and those under Qin—Qing, Jiao, Guang, and Ju—all rose with him.
entries.literal: The provinces Jiong administered—Xiang, Wei, Li, Mao, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang—and the provinces Qin commanded—Qing, Jiao, Guang, and Ju—all followed him.

entries.zh: 衆數十萬。
entries.en: His forces numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: The host numbered several hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 滎州刺史邵公宇文冑、申州刺史李惠、東楚州刺史費也利進、東潼州刺史曹孝達，各據州以應迥。
entries.en: Yuwen Zhou, Duke of Shao and governor of Xing Province; Li Hui of Shen Province; Feiye Lijin of East Chu Province; and Cao Xiaoda of East Tong Province each held his province for Yuchi Jiong.
entries.literal: Governor of Xing Province, Duke of Shao Yuwen Zhou; governor of Shen Province, Li Hui; governor of East Chu Province, Feiye Lijin; and governor of East Tong Province, Cao Xiaoda—each held his province in response to Jiong.

entries.zh: 迥又北結高寶寧以通突厥；
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong also allied in the north with Gao Baoning to open contact with the Turks;
entries.literal: Jiong also allied in the north with Gao Baoning to reach the Turks;

entries.zh: 南連陳人，許割江、淮之地。
entries.en: in the south he treated with Chen and promised them the Yangtze and Huai regions.
entries.literal: in the south he connected with the Chen people and promised to cede the lands of the Yangtze and Huai.

entries.zh: 初，楊忠之迎消難，結為兄弟，情好甚篤。
entries.en: When Yang Zhong first welcomed Xiaonan, they became sworn brothers and were deeply attached.
entries.literal: At first, when Yang Zhong welcomed Xiaonan, they became sworn brothers and their affection was very deep.

entries.zh: 隋文每以叔禮事之。
entries.en: Yang Jian always treated him with the courtesy due an uncle.
entries.literal: Yang Jian always treated him with the courtesy due an uncle.

entries.zh: 及陳平，消難至京，特免死，配為樂戶。
entries.en: When Chen was pacified, Xiaonan reached the capital; he was specially spared death and assigned to the musicians' households.
entries.literal: When Chen was pacified, Xiaonan reached the capital; he was specially spared death and assigned to the musicians' households.

entries.zh: 經二旬放免。
entries.en: After twenty days he was released.
entries.literal: After twenty days he was released.

entries.zh: 猶被舊恩，特蒙引見。
entries.en: Still owing to past favor, he was specially granted an audience.
entries.literal: Still owing to past favor, he was specially granted an audience.

entries.zh: 尋卒于家。
entries.en: He soon died at home.
entries.literal: Soon he died at home.

entries.zh: 性貪淫，輕於去就。
entries.en: Greedy and licentious by nature, he was fickle in his loyalties.
entries.literal: By nature he was greedy and licentious, and light in his coming and going.

entries.zh: 故世之言反覆者，皆引消難云。
entries.en: Thus when later ages speak of the fickle, they all cite Xiaonan.
entries.literal: Thus when later ages speak of the fickle, they all cite Xiaonan.

entries.zh: 其妻高氏，齊神武之女。
entries.en: His wife, Lady Gao, was a daughter of Gao Huan.
entries.literal: His wife, the Lady Gao, was a daughter of Gao Huan.

entries.zh: 在鄴，敬重之。
entries.en: In Ye he treated her with respect.
entries.literal: In Ye he treated her with respect.

entries.zh: 後入關，便相弃薄。
entries.en: After entering the Pass region, he cast her off and treated her coldly.
entries.literal: After entering the Pass region, he cast her off and treated her coldly.

entries.zh: 消難之赴
entries.en: When Xiaonan went to
entries.literal: When Xiaonan went to

entries.en: [variant: Ang]
entries.literal: (Ang)

entries.zh: 鄖州，留高及三子在京。
entries.en: Yun Province, he left Lady Gao and three sons in the capital.
entries.literal: Yun Province, he left Lady Gao and three sons in the capital.

entries.zh: 高言於隋文曰：「滎陽公性多變詐，今以新寵自隨，必不顧妻子，願防慮之。」
entries.en: Lady Gao said to Yang Jian: "The Duke of Xingyang is changeable and deceitful; now that new favorites accompany him, he will surely abandon wife and children—I beg you to guard against this."
entries.literal: Lady Gao said to Yang Jian: "The Duke of Xingyang's nature is full of change and deceit; now that new favorites accompany him, he will surely not care for wife and children—I beg you to guard against this."

entries.zh: 消難入陳，而高母子因此獲免。
entries.en: When Xiaonan defected to Chen, Lady Gao and her sons were thereby spared.
entries.literal: When Xiaonan entered Chen, Lady Gao and her sons were thereby spared.

entries.zh: 隋文帝於是徵兵討迥，即以韋孝寬為元帥。
entries.en: Yang Jian then raised armies against Yuchi Jiong and made Wei Xiaokuan supreme commander.
entries.literal: Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) thereupon mobilized troops to suppress Jiong, and immediately made Wei Xiaokuan commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 惇率衆十萬入武德，軍於沁東。
entries.en: Dun led one hundred thousand men into Wude and camped east of the Qin River.
entries.literal: Dun led a host of one hundred thousand into Wude and encamped east of the Qin River.

entries.zh: 孝寬等諸軍隔水相持不進。
entries.en: Wei Xiaokuan's armies faced them across the river and held back.
entries.literal: Wei Xiaokuan and the other armies faced each other across the water and did not advance.

entries.zh: 隋文帝又遣高熲馳驛督戰。
entries.en: Yang Jian also sent Gao Jiong by relay horse to take command of the fighting.
entries.literal: Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) also dispatched Gao Jiong by post-horse relay to supervise the battle.

entries.zh: 惇布兵二十裏，麾軍小卻，欲待孝寬軍半度擊之。
entries.en: Dun drew up his line for twenty li, then feigned a slight withdrawal, planning to hit Wei Xiaokuan while half his force was still crossing.
entries.literal: Dun deployed his troops for twenty li, waved the army to fall back slightly, intending to wait until Wei Xiaokuan's army was half across and then strike.

entries.zh: 孝寬因其小卻，鳴鼓齊進，惇大敗。
entries.en: Wei Xiaokuan seized on the feigned retreat, sounded the drums, and charged in unison; Dun was routed.
entries.literal: Wei Xiaokuan, taking advantage of his slight withdrawal, beat drums and advanced together; Dun was greatly defeated.

entries.zh: 孝寬乘勝進至鄴。
entries.en: Wei Xiaokuan pressed the victory on to Ye.
entries.literal: Wei Xiaokuan pressed the victory and advanced to Ye.

entries.zh: 迥與子惇、佑等又悉其卒十三萬，陳于城南。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong mustered all his remaining strength—one hundred thirty thousand men—and formed battle lines south of the city with his sons Dun, You, and the rest.
entries.literal: Jiong together with his sons Dun, You, and the others again mustered all their soldiers, one hundred thirty thousand, and drew up south of the city.

entries.zh: 迥別統萬人，皆綠巾錦襖，號曰黃龍兵。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong personally led ten thousand men in green headbands and brocade jackets, called the Yellow Dragon Army.
entries.literal: Jiong separately commanded ten thousand men, all with green headcloths and brocade jackets, styled the Yellow Dragon troops.

entries.zh: 勤率衆五萬，自青州赴迥，以三千騎先到。
entries.en: Qin marched fifty thousand men from Qing Province to Yuchi Jiong's aid, his three thousand horse arriving first.
entries.literal: Qin led a host of fifty thousand from Qing Province to join Jiong; with three thousand cavalry he arrived first.

entries.zh: 迥舊習軍旅，雖老猶被甲臨陣。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong was a veteran of many campaigns; though aged, he still donned armor and took the field.
entries.literal: Jiong was long practiced in military affairs; though old he still donned armor and faced the battle line.

entries.zh: 其麾下千兵，皆關中人，為之力戰。
entries.en: The thousand men under his personal command were all Guanzhong natives and fought for him with desperate courage.
entries.literal: The thousand soldiers under his command were all men of Guanzhong and fought hard for him.

entries.zh: 孝寬等軍失利而卻。
entries.en: Wei Xiaokuan's army was beaten and fell back.
entries.literal: Wei Xiaokuan and the other armies lost the battle and withdrew.

entries.zh: 鄴中士女，觀者如堵。
entries.en: The men and women of Ye crowded the streets to watch, packed wall to wall.
entries.literal: Within Ye, men and women watching were thick as a wall.

entries.zh: 高熲與李詢整陣，先犯觀者，因其擾而乘之。
entries.en: Gao Jiong and Li Xun formed their lines, first charged the spectators, and then exploited the chaos to press the attack.
entries.literal: Gao Jiong and Li Xun ordered the ranks and first drove into the spectators, then taking advantage of the disturbance pressed the attack.

entries.zh: 迥大敗，遂入鄴。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong was routed and fled into Ye.
entries.literal: Jiong was greatly defeated and thereupon entered Ye.

entries.zh: 迥走保北城，孝寬縱兵圍之。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong withdrew into the north city; Wei Xiaokuan unleashed his troops to besiege it.
entries.literal: Jiong fled to hold the north city; Wei Xiaokuan released his troops to besiege it.

entries.zh: 李詢、賀樓子幹以其屬先登。
entries.en: Li Xun and Helou Zigan were first over the wall with their men.
entries.literal: Li Xun and Helou Zigan with their followers were first to ascend.

entries.zh: 迥上樓，射殺數人，乃自殺。
entries.en: Yuchi Jiong climbed the tower, shot down several men, and then took his own life.
entries.literal: Jiong ascended the tower, shot and killed several men, and then killed himself.

entries.zh: 勤、惇等東走，幷追獲之。
entries.en: Qin, Dun, and the others fled east and were run down and captured.
entries.literal: Qin, Dun, and the others fled east and were both pursued and captured.

entries.zh: 餘衆，月餘皆斬之。
entries.en: The remaining troops were hunted down and beheaded over the next month.
entries.literal: The remaining host, after more than a month, were all beheaded.

entries.zh: 時隋文帝秉政，謙令司錄賀若昂奉表詣闕。
entries.en: At that time, with Yang Jian directing the government, Qian ordered chief clerk He Ruo'ang to present a memorial at court.
entries.literal: At that time Yang Jian held government power, Qian ordered chief clerk He Ruo'ang to present a memorial at court.

entries.zh: 昂還，具陳京師事勢。
entries.en: When He Ruo'ang returned, he gave a full account of affairs in the capital.
entries.literal: When Ang returned, he fully reported the situation in the capital.

entries.zh: 謙以世受國恩，將圖匡復，遂舉兵，署官司。
entries.en: Qian, having received the state's grace for generations, intended to restore the dynasty, raised troops, and appointed officials.
entries.literal: Qian, having received the state's grace generation after generation, intended to restore the dynasty, and so raised troops and appointed offices.

entries.zh: 所管益、潼、新、始、龍、邛、青、瀘、戎、寧、汶、陵、遂、合、楚、資、眉、普十八州及嘉、渝、臨、渠、蓬、隆、通、興、武、庸十州之人多從之。
entries.en: The people of the eighteen provinces and ten additional prefectures under his jurisdiction—Yi, Tong, Xin, Shi, Long, Qiong, Qing, Lu, Rong, Ning, Wen, Ling, Sui, He, Chu, Zi, Mei, Pu, Jia, Yu, Lin, Qu, Peng, Long, Tong, Xing, Wu, and Yong—largely rallied to him.
entries.literal: The people of the eighteen provinces under his charge—Yi, Tong, Xin, Shi, Long, Qiong, Qing, Lu, Rong, Ning, Wen, Ling, Sui, He, Chu, Zi, Mei, and Pu—and the ten additional prefectures of Jia, Yu, Lin, Qu, Peng, Long, Tong, Xing, Wu, and Yong largely followed him.

entries.zh: 總管長史乙弗虔、益州刺史達奚惎勸謙據險觀變。
entries.en: Chief administrator Yifu Qian and Yi governor Daxi Ji urged Wang Qian to hold the difficult terrain and wait to see how events developed.
entries.literal: Chief administrator Yifu Qian and Yi Governor Daxi Ji urged Qian to hold the difficult terrain and watch how events unfolded.

entries.zh: 隆州刺史高阿
entries.en: Long Province governor Gao A
entries.literal: Governor of Long Province Gao A

entries.en: [variant: Shi]
entries.literal: (Shi)

entries.zh: 那瑰為謙畫三策曰：「公親率精銳，直指散關，蜀人知公有勤王之節，必當各思效命，此上策也；
entries.en: Na Gui proposed three plans to Qian: "If you personally lead picked troops straight for San Gate Pass, the people of Shu, knowing your loyalty in rushing to aid the throne, will surely each resolve to serve you—this is the best plan;
entries.literal: Na Gui drew up three plans for Qian, saying: "My lord, leading picked troops yourself and striking straight for San Gate Pass—the Shu people, knowing you have the loyalty of one who rushes to aid the sovereign, will surely each think to give their lives; this is the highest plan;

entries.zh: 出兵梁、漢，以顧天下，此中策也；
entries.en: to send troops from Liang and Han and thereby hold the realm's attention—this is the middle plan;
entries.literal: to send troops from Liang and Han and thereby command the realm's attention—this is the middle plan;

entries.zh: 坐守劍南，發兵自衞，此下策也。」
entries.en: to sit in Jiannan and raise troops only for self-defense—this is the worst plan."
entries.literal: to sit and hold Jiannan and raise troops only for self-defense—this is the lowest plan."

entries.zh: 謙參用其中下之策。
entries.en: Qian adopted parts of the middle and lower plans.
entries.literal: Qian partly adopted the middle and lower plans.

entries.zh: 梁睿未至大劔，謙遣兵鎮始州。
entries.en: Before Liang Rui reached Great Sword Pass, Qian sent troops to garrison Shi Province.
entries.literal: Before Liang Rui reached Great Sword Pass, Qian sent troops to garrison Shi Province.

entries.zh: 隋文即以睿為行軍元帥，便發利、鳳、文、秦、成諸州兵討之。
entries.en: Yang Jian immediately made Liang Rui campaign commander-in-chief and dispatched troops from Li, Feng, Wen, Qin, Cheng, and other provinces against him.
entries.literal: Yang Jian immediately made Rui campaign commander-in-chief and dispatched troops from Li, Feng, Wen, Qin, Cheng, and other provinces to suppress him.

entries.zh: 達奚惎、乙弗虔等衆十萬攻利州。
entries.en: Daxi Ji, Yifu Qian, and others with a host of one hundred thousand attacked Li Province.
entries.literal: Daxi Ji, Yifu Qian, and others with a host of one hundred thousand attacked Li Province.

entries.zh: 聞睿至，衆潰。
entries.en: When they heard Rui had arrived, the army broke apart.
entries.literal: When they heard Rui had arrived, the host broke up.

entries.zh: 睿乘其弊，縱兵深入。
entries.en: Rui seized their weakness and drove his troops deep into the country.
entries.literal: Rui seized their weakness and drove his troops in deep.

entries.zh: 惎、虔密使詣睿，請為內應以贖罪。
entries.en: Ji and Qian secretly sent envoys to Rui offering to serve as inside allies to atone for their guilt.
entries.literal: Ji and Qian secretly sent envoys to Rui asking to serve as inner allies to redeem their guilt.

entries.zh: 謙不知之，並令守成都。
entries.en: Qian knew nothing of this and still ordered them to hold Chengdu.
entries.literal: Qian knew nothing of this and still ordered them to hold Chengdu.

entries.zh: 謙先無籌略，承藉父勳，遂居重任。
entries.en: Qian had no strategy to begin with; relying on his father's merit, he had risen to a weighty post.
entries.literal: Qian had no strategy from the start; relying on his father's merit, he had risen to a weighty post.

entries.zh: 初謀舉兵，咸以地有江山之險，進可以立功，退可以自守。
entries.en: When they first planned rebellion, all held that the land was defended by rivers and mountains—one could win glory by advancing and hold out by retreating.
entries.literal: When they first planned to rebel, all held that the land had the defenses of rivers and mountains—advancing one could win merit, retreating one could hold oneself.

entries.zh: 且任用多非其才。
entries.en: Moreover, most of those he appointed were not men of real ability.
entries.literal: Moreover, those appointed were mostly not men of the right talent.

entries.zh: 及聞睿兵奄至，惶懼，乃自率衆迎戰。
entries.en: When he heard Rui's army had suddenly arrived, he was terrified and personally led his troops out to fight.
entries.literal: When he heard Rui's troops had suddenly arrived, he was afraid and personally led his host to meet them in battle.

entries.zh: 又以惎、虔之子為左右軍。
entries.en: He also made Ji's and Qian's sons command the left and right wings.
entries.literal: He also made Ji and Qian's sons command the left and right wings.

entries.zh: 行數十里，軍皆叛。
entries.en: After marching several tens of li, the whole army turned against him.
entries.literal: After marching several tens of li, the army all turned against him.

entries.zh: 謙以二十騎奔新都，縣令王寶斬之，傳首京師。
entries.en: Qian fled to Xindu with twenty horsemen; Magistrate Wang Bao beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
entries.literal: Qian fled to Xindu with twenty horsemen; Magistrate Wang Bao beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 惎、虔以成都降，隋文以其首謀，斬之。
entries.en: Ji and Qian surrendered Chengdu; Yang Jian, judging them the chief plotters, had them beheaded.
entries.literal: Ji and Qian surrendered Chengdu; Yang Jian, because they had been the chief plotters, beheaded them.

entries.zh: 高阿
entries.en: Gao A
entries.literal: Gao A

entries.en: [variant: Shi]
entries.literal: (Shi)

entries.zh: 那瓌亦誅。
entries.en: Na Gui was also executed.
entries.literal: Na Gui was also executed.

entries.zh: 隋文帝輔政，消難旣聞蜀公迥不受代，遂欲與迥合勢，亦舉兵應之。
entries.en: When Yang Jian directed the government, Xiaonan, hearing that Duke of Shu Jiong refused to be replaced, intended to join forces with him and also raised troops in response.
entries.literal: When Yang Jian directed the government, Xiaonan, having heard that Duke of Shu Jiong refused to be replaced, intended to join forces with Jiong and also raised troops in response.

entries.zh: 以開府田廣等為腹心，殺總管長史侯莫陳杲、鄖州刺史蔡澤等四十餘人。
entries.en: Taking opening-office commanders Tian Guang and others as his inner circle, he killed chief administrator Houmochen Gao, Yun governor Cai Ze, and more than forty others.
entries.literal: Taking opening-office commanders Tian Guang and others as his inner circle, he killed chief administrator Houmochen Gao, Yun Governor Cai Ze, and more than forty others.

entries.zh: 所管鄖、隨、溫、應
entries.en: The nine provinces under his charge—Yun, Sui, Wen, Ying
entries.literal: The nine provinces under his charge—Yun, Sui, Wen, Ying

entries.en: [variant: Shi]
entries.literal: (Shi)

entries.zh: 土、順、沔、環、岳九州，魯山、甑山、沌陽、應城、平靖、武陽、上明、
entries.en: Tu, Shun, Mian, Huan, and Yue, and the eight garrisons of Lushan, Zengshan, Chunyang, Yingcheng, Pingjing, Wuyang, Shaming, and
entries.literal: Tu, Shun, Mian, Huan, and Yue, and the eight garrisons of Lushan, Zengshan, Chunyang, Yingcheng, Pingjing, Wuyang, Shaming, and

entries.en: [variant: Xu]
entries.literal: (Xu)

entries.zh: 溳水八鎮，並從之。
entries.en: Yunshui—all followed him.
entries.literal: Yunshui—all followed him.

entries.zh: 使其子泳質於陳以求援。
entries.en: He sent his son Yong as a hostage to Chen to seek aid.
entries.literal: He sent his son Yong as a hostage to Chen to seek aid.

entries.zh: 隋文帝命襄州總管王誼為元帥，發荊襄兵以討之。
entries.en: Yang Jian ordered Wang Yi, inspector-general of Xiang, as commander-in-chief and dispatched Jing-Xiang troops to suppress him.
entries.literal: Yang Jian ordered Xiang Inspector-General Wang Yi as commander-in-chief and dispatched Jing-Xiang troops to suppress him.

entries.zh: 八月，消難聞誼軍將至，夜率其麾下，歸於陳。
entries.en: In the eighth month, hearing Wang Yi's army was about to arrive, Xiaonan led his personal followers by night and defected to Chen.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, hearing Yi's army was about to arrive, Xiaonan by night led his personal followers and went over to Chen.

entries.zh: 陳宣帝以為都督安
entries.en: Emperor Xuan of Chen made him commander of An
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen made him commander of An

entries.en: [variant: Zhao]
entries.literal: (Zhao)

entries.zh: 隨九州八鎮、車騎將軍、司空、隨公。
entries.en: Sui, the nine provinces and eight garrisons, plus general of chariots and cavalry, minister of works, and Duke of Sui.
entries.literal: Sui, the nine provinces and eight garrisons, plus general of chariots and cavalry, minister of works, and Duke of Sui.

entries.zh: 王謙字勑萬，太保雄之子也。
entries.en: Wang Qian, styled Timo, was the son of Grand Guardian Wang Xiong.
entries.literal: Wang Qian, styled Timo, was the son of Grand Guardian Xiong.

entries.zh: 性恭謹，無他才能。
entries.en: Respectful and cautious by nature, he had no other special talents.
entries.literal: By nature respectful and cautious, he had no other talents.

entries.zh: 以父功，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府。
entries.en: Through his father's merit he rose in stages to grand general of rapid cavalry and opening-office commander.
entries.literal: Through his father's merit, he was repeatedly promoted to grand general of rapid cavalry and opening-office commander.

entries.zh: 孝閔踐祚，治右小武伯。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he served as director of the right minor martial guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he served as director of the right minor martial guard.

entries.zh: 雄從晉公護東討，為齊人所斃。
