entries.en: Xiong followed Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu on an eastern campaign and was killed by Northern Qi troops.
entries.literal: Xiong followed Duke of Jin Hu on an eastern campaign and was killed by Qi men.

entries.zh: 朝議以謙父殞身行陣，特加殊寵，乃授謙柱國大將軍。
entries.en: The court held that Qian's father had fallen on the battlefield and, as a special honor, appointed Qian pillar-of-state grand general.
entries.literal: The court deliberated that Qian's father had died on the battlefield and, granting exceptional favor, appointed Qian pillar-of-state grand general.

entries.zh: 以情禮未終，固辭不拜。
entries.en: Because his mourning obligations were not yet complete, he firmly declined the appointment.
entries.literal: Because the period of mourning affection had not ended, he firmly declined the appointment.

entries.zh: 高祖手詔奪情，襲爵庸公，邑萬戶。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu issued a personal edict overriding mourning obligations, and Qian inherited the title Duke of Yong with a fief of ten thousand households.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu wrote a personal edict overriding mourning obligations; he inherited the title Duke of Yong with a fief of ten thousand households.

entries.en: [variant: later]
entries.literal: (Later)

entries.zh: 從皇太子討吐谷渾，力戰有功。
entries.en: He accompanied the crown prince against Tuyuhun, fought hard, and won distinction.
entries.literal: He accompanied the crown prince against Tuyuhun, fought hard, and had merit.

entries.zh: 是時高祖東征，謙又力戰，進上柱國、益州總管。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned east, Qian again fought hard and was promoted to upper pillar of state and inspector-general of Yi Province.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu campaigned east, and Qian again fought hard; he was promoted to upper pillar of state and inspector-general of Yi Province.

entries.zh: 齊文宣末年，昬虐滋甚。
entries.en: In the last years of Emperor Wenxuan of Qi, his cruelty and tyranny grew ever worse.
entries.literal: In the last years of Emperor Wenxuan of Qi, his cruelty and tyranny grew ever worse.

entries.zh: 消難旣懼禍及，常有自全之謀，曲意撫納，頗為百姓所附。
entries.en: Xiaonan, fearing disaster would reach him, constantly plotted to save himself; he courted favor, won over the people, and gained a strong local following.
entries.literal: Xiaonan, fearing calamity would reach him, constantly plotted to preserve himself; he courted favor and won over the people and was much attached to by the common folk.

entries.zh: 屬文宣在幷，驛召其弟上黨王渙，渙懼于屠害，遂斬使者東奔。
entries.en: When Wenxuan was at Bing, he summoned by courier his brother the Prince of Shangdang, Huan; Huan, fearing slaughter, killed the messenger and fled east.
entries.literal: When Wenxuan was at Bing, he summoned by post his brother the Prince of Shangdang, Huan; Huan, fearing slaughter, slew the messenger and fled east.

entries.zh: 數日間搜捕鄴中，鄴中大擾。
entries.en: Within a few days Ye was searched and hunted, and the city was thrown into turmoil.
entries.literal: Within several days Ye was searched and hunted; Ye was greatly disturbed.

entries.zh: 後竟獲於濟州。
entries.en: He was finally captured in Ji Province.
entries.literal: Later he was finally captured in Ji Province.

entries.zh: 渙之初走，朝士私相謂曰：「今上黨亡叛，似赴成皋。
entries.en: When Huan first fled, courtiers said privately among themselves: "The Prince of Shangdang has fled in rebellion, as if heading for Chenggao.
entries.literal: When Huan first fled, court gentlemen said privately to one another: "Now the Prince of Shangdang has fled in rebellion, as if heading for Chenggao.

entries.zh: 若與司馬北豫州連謀，必為國患。」
entries.en: If he joins in conspiracy with Sima Xiaonan of North Yu Province, he will surely become a threat to the state."
entries.literal: If he joins in conspiracy with Sima of North Yu Province, he will surely become a threat to the state."

entries.zh: 此言遂達於文宣，文宣頗疑之。
entries.en: This talk reached Wenxuan, and he grew deeply suspicious.
entries.literal: This talk reached Wenxuan, and he grew quite suspicious.

entries.zh: 消難懼，密令所親裴藻間行入關，請舉州來附。
entries.en: Xiaonan was afraid; he secretly ordered his close associate Pei Zao to slip into the Pass region and ask to surrender the entire province.
entries.literal: Xiaonan was afraid; he secretly ordered his close associate Pei Zao to slip across the border into the Pass region and ask to surrender the entire province.

entries.zh: 晉公護遣達奚武、楊忠迎之，消難遂與武俱入朝。
entries.en: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu sent Daxi Wu and Yang Zhong to welcome him; Xiaonan then entered court together with Wu.
entries.literal: Duke of Jin Hu dispatched Daxi Wu and Yang Zhong to welcome him; Xiaonan thereupon entered court together with Wu.

entries.zh: 授大將軍、滎陽公。
entries.en: He was appointed grand general and Duke of Xingyang.
entries.literal: He was appointed grand general and Duke of Xingyang.

entries.zh: 從高祖東伐，遷大後丞。
entries.en: He followed Emperor Gaozu on the eastern campaign and was transferred to grand rear chancellor.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor Gaozu on the eastern campaign and was transferred to grand rear chancellor.

entries.zh: 納女為靜帝后。
entries.en: He gave his daughter in marriage as empress to Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: He gave his daughter in marriage as empress to Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 尋出為
entries.en: He was soon sent out as
entries.literal: Soon he was sent out as

entries.en: [variant: Jiao]
entries.literal: (Jiao)

entries.zh: ［鄖］州總管。
entries.en: inspector-general of Yun Province.
entries.literal: [Yun] inspector-general.

entries.zh: 司馬消難字道融，河內溫人。
entries.en: Sima Xiaonan, styled Daorong, was a native of Wen in Henei.
entries.literal: Sima Xiaonan, styled Daorong, was a man of Wen in Henei.

entries.zh: 父子如，為齊神武佐命，位至尚書令。
entries.en: His father Sima Ziru had assisted Gao Huan at the founding of Northern Qi and rose to director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: His father Ziru assisted Gao Huan of Northern Qi at the founding and rose to director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 消難幼聰惠，微涉經史，好自矯飾，以求名譽。
entries.en: Xiaonan was clever from youth, had a light acquaintance with the classics and histories, liked to polish his appearance, and sought reputation.
entries.literal: Xiaonan was clever from youth, lightly touched on the classics and histories, liked to adorn himself, and sought reputation.

entries.zh: 起家著作郎。
entries.en: He began his career as a gentleman-attendant compiler.
entries.literal: He began his career as a gentleman-attendant compiler.

entries.zh: 子如旣當朝貴，消難亦愛賓客。
entries.en: Once Ziru held high court rank, Xiaonan also cultivated guests.
entries.literal: Once Ziru held court rank and power, Xiaonan also cultivated guests.

entries.zh: 邢子才、王元景、魏收、陸卬、崔贍等皆遊其門。
entries.en: Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, Wei Shou, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and others all frequented his house.
entries.literal: Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, Wei Shou, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and others all frequented his gate.

entries.zh: 尋拜駙馬都尉、光祿卿，出為北豫州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made commandant of the horse guard and director of imperial feasts, then sent out as governor of North Yu Province.
entries.literal: He was soon appointed commandant of the horse guard and director of imperial feasts, and sent out as governor of North Yu Province.

entries.zh: 大統三年，齊神武三道入寇，諸將咸欲分兵禦之，獨綽意與太祖同。
entries.en: In the third year of Datong, Gao Huan invaded on three fronts. The generals all wanted to split their forces to meet him, but only Su Chuo agreed with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.
entries.literal: In the third year of Datong, Gao Huan entered in invasion on three routes; all the generals wanted to divide troops to resist, only Su Chuo's view matched Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's.

entries.zh: 遂併力拒竇泰，擒之於潼關。
entries.en: They concentrated their strength against Dou Tai and captured him at Tong Pass.
entries.literal: They thereupon combined strength to resist Dou Tai and captured him at Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 四年，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫，封美陽縣子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was made Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Viscount of Meiyang with a fief of three hundred households.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was given the additional titles Guard General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Viscount of Meiyang with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 加通直散騎常侍，進爵為伯，增邑二百戶。
entries.en: He was given the additional title Honest and Direct Regular Palace Attendant, raised to earl, and granted two hundred more households.
entries.literal: Added Honest and Direct Regular Palace Attendant, advanced in rank to earl, fief increased by two hundred households.

entries.zh: 十年，授大行臺度支尚書，領著作，兼司農卿。
entries.en: In the tenth year he became Director of Revenue of the Grand Mobile Imperial Secretariat, head of the Palace Library, and Minister of Agriculture as well.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Director of Revenue of the Grand Mobile Imperial Secretariat, concurrently heading the Palace Library, and also Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 今刺史守令，悉有僚吏，皆佐治之人也。
entries.en: Today's inspectors, governors, and magistrates all have subordinate officials, and every one of them helps govern.
entries.literal: Today's inspectors, overseers, and magistrates all have staff officers—they are all people who assist in governance.

entries.zh: 刺史府官則命於天朝，其州吏以下，並牧守自置。
entries.en: An inspector's secretariat staff are appointed by the imperial court, but all other provincial officials are chosen by the governor himself.
entries.literal: Inspectors' bureau officials are appointed by the heavenly court; all state officials below them are appointed by the overseers themselves.

entries.zh: 自昔以來，州郡大吏，但取門資，多不擇賢良；
entries.en: From of old, major provincial and commandery posts have gone by family pedigree, with little regard for worth;
entries.literal: From old times, for major posts in provinces and commanderies they took only family pedigree, mostly not selecting the worthy and good;

entries.zh: 末曹小吏，唯試刀筆，並不問志行。
entries.en: petty clerks have been chosen by brush-and-knife tests alone, with no inquiry into character.
entries.literal: For petty bureau clerks they tested only brush and knife, and did not ask about intent and conduct at all.

entries.zh: 夫門資者，乃先世之爵祿，無妨子孫之愚瞽；
entries.en: Family pedigree is inherited rank and salary from past generations—it does not keep a descendant from being dull or blind;
entries.literal: Family pedigree is the rank and emolument of former generations—it does not prevent stupid blindness in descendants;

entries.zh: 刀筆者，乃身外之末材，不廢性行之澆偽。
entries.en: brush-and-knife skill is an outward, minor talent—it does not rule out deceit and corruption of character.
entries.literal: Brush and knife are external minor talents—they do not eliminate falsity and baseness in one's nature and conduct.

entries.zh: 若門資之中而得賢良，是則策騏驥而取千里也；
entries.en: If pedigree yields a worthy man, it is like spurring a thousand-li steed;
entries.literal: If among family pedigree one obtains the worthy and good, that is like spurring a qiji and taking a thousand li;

entries.zh: 若門資之中而得愚瞽，是則土牛木馬，形似而用非，不可以涉道也。
entries.en: if pedigree yields a fool, it is like an earthen ox or wooden horse—shaped like the real thing but useless on the road.
entries.literal: If among family pedigree one obtains stupid blindness, that is like an earthen ox or wooden horse—similar in form but useless in function, and cannot be used to travel the Way.

entries.zh: 若刀筆之中而得志行，是則金相玉質，內外俱美，實為人寶也；
entries.en: If clerical skill is joined to good character, it is gold outside and jade within—a true treasure among men;
entries.literal: If among brush and knife one obtains intent and conduct, that is like gold appearance and jade substance, beautiful inside and out—truly a treasure among men;

entries.zh: 若刀筆之中而得澆偽，是則飾畫朽木，悅目一時，不可以充榱椽之用也。
entries.en: if clerical skill hides baseness and deceit, it is painted rotten wood—pleasing for a moment but unfit to bear a roof beam.
entries.literal: If among brush and knife one obtains baseness and falsity, that is like painting rotten wood—pleasing to the eye for a moment, but cannot be used to fill rafters and beams.

entries.zh: 今之選舉者，當不限資蔭，唯在得人。
entries.en: Selection today should not be bound by pedigree and inherited privilege; what matters is getting the right man.
entries.literal: Today's selectors ought not to be limited by pedigree and inherited privilege—what matters is obtaining the right man.

entries.zh: 苟得其人，自可起塚養而為卿相，伊尹、傅說是也，而況州郡之職乎。
entries.en: Get the right man and he may rise from tending graves and feeding cattle to minister and chancellor, as with Yi Yin and Fu Yue—how much more so for provincial office!
entries.literal: If one obtains the right man, one can raise him from tending graves and rearing cattle to minister and chancellor—Yi Yin and Fu Yue were such; how much more for provincial and commandery posts!

entries.zh: 苟非其人，則丹朱、商均雖帝王之胤，不能守百里之封，而況於公卿之冑乎。
entries.en: Get the wrong man and even Dan Zhu and Shang Jun, though sons of kings, could not hold a hundred-li fief—much less the offspring of great ministers.
entries.literal: If he is not the right man, then Dan Zhu and Shang Jun, though heirs of emperors and kings, could not keep a fief of a hundred li—how much less the descendants of high ministers!

entries.zh: 由此而言，觀人之道可見矣。
entries.en: From this the way to judge men becomes clear.
entries.literal: From this speaking, the Way of observing men can be seen.

entries.zh: 夫良玉未剖，與瓦石相類；
entries.en: Uncut fine jade looks like ordinary tile and stone;
entries.literal: Fine jade uncut is like tile and stone;

entries.zh: 名驥未馳，與駑馬相雜。
entries.en: an unridden famous steed is indistinguishable from a nag.
entries.literal: A famous thoroughbred unrun mixes with nags.

entries.zh: 及其剖而瑩之，馳而試之，玉石駑驥，然後始分。
entries.en: Cut and polish the jade, run and test the horse—only then do jade and stone, thoroughbred and nag, stand apart.
entries.literal: When it is cut and polished, run and tested—then jade and stone, nag and thoroughbred, for the first time are distinguished.

entries.zh: 彼賢士之未用也，混於凡品，竟何以異。
entries.en: Before worthy men are employed, they mingle with the common run—how can anyone tell the difference?
entries.literal: When worthy scholars are not yet employed, they mix with ordinary ranks—how in the end are they different?

entries.zh: 要任之以事業，責之以成務，方與彼庸流較然不同。
entries.en: The point is to give them real work and hold them accountable for results—only then do they stand clearly apart from the mediocre crowd.
entries.literal: The essential is to entrust them with real tasks and hold them responsible for completed duties—only then are they clearly different from those mediocre streams.

entries.zh: 昔呂望之屠釣，百里奚之飯牛，甯生之扣角，管夷吾之三敗，當此之時，悠悠之徒，豈謂其賢。
entries.en: In ancient times Lü Wang butchered and fished, Baili Xi fed cattle, Ning Qi beat time on an ox horn, and Guan Yiwu suffered three defeats. At the time, would ordinary observers have recognized their worth?
entries.literal: In old times Lü Wang butchered and fished, Baili Xi fed cattle, Master Ning beat time on an ox horn, and Guan Yiwu suffered three defeats. At that time, how could the common crowd have called them worthy?

entries.zh: 及升王朝，登霸國，積數十年，功成事立，始識其奇士也。
entries.en: When they entered the royal court and rose in hegemonic states, and after decades of achievement people finally recognized them as extraordinary men.
entries.literal: When they ascended the royal court and entered hegemonic states, accumulated decades, achievement completed and affairs established—only then did they recognize them as extraordinary men.

entries.zh: 於是後世稱之，不容於口。
entries.en: Then later ages praised them without end.
entries.literal: Thereupon later ages praised them—could not contain it in the mouth.

entries.zh: 彼瑰偉之材，不世之傑，尚不能以未遇之時，自異於凡品，況降此者哉。
entries.en: Even such magnificent, once-in-an-age talents could not, before their chance came, distinguish themselves from ordinary men—how much less lesser men!
entries.literal: Those magnificent talents, unworldly heroes—even they could not, in times when they had not yet met opportunity, distinguish themselves from ordinary ranks; how much less those below them!

entries.zh: 若必待太公而後用，是千載無太公；
entries.en: If you must wait for a Taigong before appointing anyone, there will be no Taigong for a thousand years;
entries.literal: If one must wait for Grand Duke before employing anyone, then for a thousand years there would be no Grand Duke;

entries.zh: 必待夷吾而後任，是百世無夷吾。
entries.en: if you must wait for a Guan Yiwu before assigning anyone, there will be no Guan Yiwu for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: If one must wait for Yiwu before assigning anyone, then for a hundred generations there would be no Yiwu.

entries.zh: 所以然者，士必從微而至著，功必積小以至大，豈有未任而已成，不用而先達也。
entries.en: Talent rises from obscurity to fame, and achievement grows from small to great—how can there be finished achievement before office, or advancement before use?
entries.literal: The reason is this—a scholar must go from obscurity to prominence, achievement must accumulate from small to great; how could there be achievement already complete before office is held, or advancement before employment?

entries.zh: 若識此理，則賢可求，士可擇。
entries.en: Understand this, and worthy men can be found and talent can be chosen.
entries.literal: If one recognizes this principle, then worthies can be sought and scholars can be selected.

entries.zh: 得賢而任之，得士而使之，則天下之治，何向而不可成也。
entries.en: Find worthy men and appoint them, find talent and use it, and there is no direction in which good government cannot be achieved.
entries.literal: Obtain worthies and assign them, obtain scholars and employ them—then governing all under Heaven, what direction could not be accomplished?

entries.zh: 惟中興十有一年，仲夏，庶邦百辟，咸會於王庭。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Restoration, in midsummer, the myriad states and all ministers assembled at the royal court.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Restoration, in midsummer, the myriad states and hundred ministers all assembled at the royal court.

entries.zh: 柱國泰洎羣公列將，罔不來朝。
entries.en: Pillar-of-State Yuwen Tai and all the grandees and ranking generals came to court without exception.
entries.literal: Pillar-of-State Tai and all the grandees and ranking generals, none failed to come to court.

entries.zh: 時乃大稽百憲，敷於庶邦，用綏我王度。
entries.en: Then the hundred laws were reviewed in full, proclaimed to the myriad states, and royal order was secured.
entries.literal: Then a great review of the hundred laws was made, proclaimed to the myriad states, to stabilize our royal institutions.

entries.zh: 皇帝曰：「昔堯命羲和，允厘百工。
entries.en: The Emperor said: "In antiquity Yao charged Xi and He to regulate the hundred offices.
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "In antiquity Yao charged Xi and He, truly to regulate the hundred offices.

entries.zh: 舜命九官，庶績咸熙。
entries.en: Shun appointed the Nine Ministers, and every task flourished.
entries.literal: Shun appointed the Nine Ministers, and all achievements were glorious.

entries.zh: 武丁命說，克號高宗。
entries.en: Wu Ding charged Yue, and worthily earned the title High Ancestor.
entries.literal: Wu Ding charged Yue, and worthily was styled High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 時惟休哉，朕其欽若。
entries.en: Those were glorious ages; I shall reverently follow their example.
entries.literal: The time was truly splendid—I shall reverently follow their example.

entries.zh: 格爾有位，胥暨我太祖之庭，朕將丕命女以厥官。」
entries.en: You who hold office, having all come to our Grand Progenitor's court—I will grandly charge you with your posts."
entries.literal: To you who hold office, all having come to our Grand Progenitor's court, I will grandly charge you with your posts."

entries.zh: 皇帝若曰：「柱國，唯四海之不造，載繇二紀。
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Pillar of State, the realm has not yet been settled, for nearly two reign periods.
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Pillar of State, the realm has not yet been settled, for nearly two reign periods.

entries.zh: 天未絕我太祖列祖之命，用錫我以元輔。
entries.en: Heaven has not cut off the mandate of our Grand Progenitor and successive ancestors, and has granted me a chief minister.
entries.literal: Heaven has not cut off the mandate of our Grand Progenitor and successive ancestors, and has granted me a chief minister.

entries.zh: 國家將墜，公惟棟梁。
entries.en: The state was about to collapse—you alone were its pillar.
entries.literal: The state was about to collapse—you alone were its pillar.

entries.zh: 皇之弗極，公作相。
entries.en: The throne was not yet established—you served as chief minister.
entries.literal: The throne was not yet established—you served as chief minister.

entries.zh: 百揆諐度，公惟大錄。
entries.en: The hundred offices were in disorder—you alone were the great recorder.
entries.literal: The hundred offices were in disorder—you alone were the great recorder.

entries.zh: 公其允文允武，克明克乂，迪七德，敷九功，龕暴除亂，下綏我蒼生，旁施於九土。
entries.en: You have been both literary and martial, both discerning and governing, advancing the seven virtues and spreading the nine achievements, pacifying violence and removing disorder, soothing our people below and extending grace to the nine regions.
entries.literal: You have been both literary and martial, both discerning and governing, advancing the seven virtues and spreading the nine achievements, pacifying violence and removing disorder, soothing our black-haired people below and extending grace to the nine regions.

entries.zh: 若伊之在商，周之有呂，說之相丁，用保我無疆之祚。」
entries.en: Like Yi Yin in Shang, Lü Wang in Zhou, and Yue assisting Wu Ding—you preserve our boundless fortune."
entries.literal: Like Yi in Shang, Lü in Zhou, Yue assisting Ding—you preserve our boundless fortune."

entries.zh: 史臣曰：書云：「惟后非賢弗乂，惟賢非后罔食」。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: The Documents say: "If the sovereign is not worthy, he cannot govern; if the worthy man is not sovereign, he cannot find sustenance."
entries.literal: The historiographer says: The Book (Documents) says: "Only rulers who are not worthy cannot govern; only the worthy who are not rulers cannot eat."

entries.zh: 是以知人則哲，有國之所先；
entries.en: Therefore to know men is wisdom, and for one who holds a state it comes first;
entries.literal: Therefore knowing men makes one wise; it is the first priority for one who holds a state;

entries.zh: 用之則行，為下之常道。
entries.en: and to employ them is to put policy into action—the constant duty of ministers.
entries.literal: employing them then [policy] proceeds; it is the constant way for subordinates.

entries.zh: 若乃庖廚、胥靡、種德、微管之臣，罕聞於世；
entries.en: Men like the cook, the convict laborer, the planter of virtue, and Guan Zhong in humble obscurity are rarely celebrated in their own time;
entries.literal: As for ministers like cooks, convict laborers, planters of virtue, and Guan Zhong in obscurity, they are rarely heard of in the world;

entries.zh: 黜魯、逐荊、抱關、執戟之士，無乏於時。
entries.en: Yet men demoted from Lu, banished in Chu, gatekeepers, and halberd-bearers were never wanting in any age.
entries.literal: Those demoted from Lu, expelled in Jing, gatekeepers, and halberd-bearers—never lacking in their time.

entries.zh: 斯固《典慕》所以昭則，《風雅》所以興刺也。
entries.en: That is why the Documents set forth standards and the Odes stir rebuke.
entries.literal: This is precisely why the "Dian Mo" displays norms and the "Feng Ya" raises satire.

entries.zh: 誠能監前事之得喪，勞虛己於吐握，其知賢也必用，其授爵也勿疑，則舜禹湯武之德可連衡矣，稷契伊呂之流可比肩矣。
entries.en: If rulers could truly weigh past success and failure, humble themselves as Duke of Zhou did when he "spit out his food and released his hair grip" to receive men, employ the worthy without fail, and grant office without hesitation, then the virtue of Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wu would stand in one line and men like Hou Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, and Lü Shang could walk shoulder to shoulder.
entries.literal: If one can truly observe the gain and loss of prior affairs, exhaust oneself in emptying the self at spitting-and-gripping [receiving talents], when knowing the worthy must employ them, when granting titles must not doubt—then the virtue of Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wu can be joined in measure, and men like Ji, Xie, Yi, and Lü can be matched shoulder to shoulder.

entries.zh: 太祖痛惜之，哀動左右。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor grieved and cherished his memory; his sorrow moved those around him.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor grieved and cherished his memory; his sorrow moved those around him.

entries.zh: 及將葬，乃謂公卿等曰：「蘇尚書平生謙退，敦尚儉約。
entries.en: When the burial was at hand, he said to the chief ministers: "Master of Writing Su in his lifetime was humble and retiring, and honored thrift and restraint.
entries.literal: When the burial was at hand, he said to the chief ministers: "Master of Writing Su in his lifetime was humble and retiring, and honored thrift and restraint.

entries.zh: 吾欲全其素志，便恐悠悠之徒，有所未達；
entries.en: I wish to honor his lifelong intent, but fear that idle gossips may not understand;
entries.literal: I wish to honor his lifelong intent, but fear that idle gossips may not understand;

entries.zh: 如其厚加贈諡，又乖宿昔相知之道。
entries.en: Yet if I richly bestow posthumous honors and title, that too would go against the bond of long friendship.
entries.literal: Yet if I richly bestow posthumous honors and title, that too would go against the bond of long friendship.

entries.zh: 進退惟谷，孤有疑焉。」
entries.en: Advancing or holding back—I alone am undecided."
entries.literal: Advancing or holding back—I alone am undecided."

entries.zh: 尚書令史麻瑤越次而進曰：「昔晏子，齊之賢大夫，一狐裘三十年。
entries.en: Secretariat section chief Ma Yao overstepping rank advanced and said: "In olden days Yanzi, Qi state's worthy grandee, wore one fox-fur coat for thirty years.
entries.literal: Secretariat section chief Ma Yao overstepping rank advanced and said: "In olden days Yanzi, Qi state's worthy grandee, wore one fox-fur coat for thirty years.

entries.zh: 及其死也，遺車一乘。
entries.en: When he died, he left a single cart.
entries.literal: When he died, he left a single cart.

entries.zh: 齊侯不奪其志。
entries.en: The Marquis of Qi did not override his intent.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Qi did not override his intent.

entries.zh: 綽旣操履清白，謙挹自居，愚謂宜從儉約，以彰其美。」
entries.en: Su Chuo's conduct was pure and white, and he lived in humility and restraint—I hold that he should be buried with thrift to display his virtue."
entries.literal: Su Chuo's conduct was pure and white, and he lived in humility and restraint—I hold that he should be buried with thrift to display his virtue."

entries.zh: 太祖稱善，因薦瑤於朝廷。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor praised this, and on that account recommended Ma Yao to the court.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor praised this, and on that account recommended Ma Yao to the court.

entries.zh: 及綽歸葬武功，唯載以布車一乘。
entries.en: When Su Chuo was returned for burial at Wugong, he was carried on a single cloth-covered cart.
entries.literal: When Su Chuo was returned for burial at Wugong, he was carried on a single cloth-covered cart.

entries.zh: 太祖與羣公，皆步送出同州郭門外。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor with all the lords walked on foot to see him off outside Tong Province's outer gate.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor with all the lords walked on foot to see him off outside Tong Province's outer gate.

entries.zh: 太祖親于車後酹酒而言曰：「尚書平生為事，妻子兄弟不知者，吾皆知之。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor personally poured libation behind the carriage and said: "In his lifetime the Master of Writing did things his wife, children, and brothers did not know of—but I knew them all.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor personally poured libation behind the carriage and said: "In his lifetime the Master of Writing did things his wife, children, and brothers did not know of—but I knew them all.

entries.zh: 惟爾知吾心，吾知爾意。
entries.en: Only you know my heart, and I know your intent.
entries.literal: Only you know my heart, and I know your intent.

entries.zh: 方欲共定天下，不幸遂舍我去，奈何！」
entries.en: We were just about to settle all under Heaven together, when unfortunately he left me—what can be done!"
entries.literal: We were just about to settle all under Heaven together, when unfortunately he left me—what can be done!"

entries.zh: 因舉聲慟哭，不覺失卮於手。
entries.en: He then raised his voice and wept bitterly, unaware that he had dropped the cup from his hand.
entries.literal: He then raised his voice and wept bitterly, unaware that he had dropped the cup from his hand.

entries.zh: 至葬日，又遣使祭乙太牢，太祖自為其文。
entries.en: On the burial day he again sent an envoy to sacrifice a second-grade offering of ox, sheep, and pig, and Grand Progenitor wrote the sacrificial text himself.
entries.literal: On the burial day he again sent an envoy to sacrifice a second-grade offering of ox, sheep, and pig, and Grand Progenitor wrote the sacrificial text himself.

entries.zh: 蘇綽字令綽，武功人，魏侍中則之九世孫也。
entries.en: Su Chuo, styled Lingchuo, came from Wugong and was the ninth-generation descendant of Ze, Attendant-in-Chief of Wei.
entries.literal: Su Chuo, styled Lingchuo, was a man of Wugong, ninth-generation descendant of Wei Attendant-in-Chief Ze.

entries.zh: 累世二千石。
entries.en: For generations his family had held office at the two-thousand-bushel level.
entries.literal: For generations his family held posts at the two-thousand-bushel rank.

entries.zh: 父協，武功郡守。
entries.en: His father Xie served as administrator of Wugong commandery.
entries.literal: His father Xie was administrator of Wugong commandery.

entries.zh: 盧辯字景宣，范陽涿人。
entries.en: Lu Bian, styled Jingxuan, came from Zhuo in Fanyang commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Bian, styled Jingxuan, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.

entries.zh: 累世儒學。
entries.en: His family had produced Confucian scholars for generations.
entries.literal: For generations his family had pursued Confucian learning.

entries.zh: 父靖，太常丞。
entries.en: His father Jing served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: His father Jing was Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 及帝入關，事起倉卒，辯不及至家，單馬而從。
entries.en: When the emperor entered the Pass, events erupted in sudden confusion. Bian had no time to go home and rode out alone to follow him.
entries.literal: When the emperor entered the Pass, affairs arose in sudden haste; Bian had no time to reach home and followed on horseback alone.

entries.zh: 或問辯曰：「得辭家不？」
entries.en: Someone asked Bian: “Were you able to bid farewell to your household?”
entries.literal: Someone asked Bian: “Were you able to take leave of your family?”

entries.zh: 辯曰：「門外之治，以義斷恩，復何辭也。」
entries.en: Bian replied: “In public affairs beyond the household, righteousness cuts through private ties—what farewell could there be?”
entries.literal: Bian said: “In affairs outside the door, duty is decided by righteousness and severs private affection—what need is there to take leave?”

entries.zh: 孝武至長安，授給事黃門侍郎，領著作。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu arrived at Chang’an, Bian was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Overseer of Composition.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang’an, [Bian] was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Overseer of Composition.

entries.zh: 太祖以辯有儒術，甚禮之，朝廷大議，常召顧問。
entries.en: Because Bian was steeped in Confucian learning, the Grand Duke treated him with great respect and regularly called on him for counsel in weighty court debates.
entries.literal: The Grand Duke, seeing that Bian possessed Confucian learning, treated him with great courtesy; in major court deliberations he was regularly summoned for consultation.

entries.zh: 趙青雀之亂，魏太子出居渭北。
entries.en: During Zhao Qingque’s rebellion, the Wei crown prince withdrew to the north bank of the Wei River.
entries.literal: During the turmoil of Zhao Qingque, the Wei crown prince moved out to the north of the Wei River.

entries.zh: 辯時隨從，亦不告家人。
entries.en: Bian accompanied him on that occasion as well, and again told no one at home.
entries.literal: Bian followed at the time and likewise did not inform his family.

entries.zh: 其執志敢決，皆此類也。
entries.en: His steadfast resolve and decisive action were always of this kind.
entries.literal: His firmness of purpose and resolute decisions were all of this sort.

entries.zh: 尋除太常卿、太子少傅。
entries.en: He was soon made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 魏太子及諸王等，皆行束修之禮，受業於辯。
entries.en: The Wei crown prince and the other princes all presented the dried-meat gift of discipleship and studied under Bian.
entries.literal: The Wei crown prince and the various princes all performed the ceremony of dried-meat offering and received instruction from Bian.

entries.zh: 進爵范陽公，轉少師。
entries.en: He was ennobled as Duke of Fanyang and promoted to Junior Preceptor.
entries.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Fanyang and transferred to Junior Preceptor.

entries.zh: 自魏末離亂，孝武西遷，朝章禮度，湮墜咸盡。
entries.en: After the chaos of the Wei’s final years, when Emperor Xiaowu moved the court westward, statutes and ritual observance collapsed entirely.
entries.literal: From the disorders at the end of Wei, when Emperor Xiaowu moved west, court regulations and ritual forms were completely lost.

entries.zh: 辯因時制宜，皆合軌度。
entries.en: Bian shaped institutions to fit the times, and in every case they matched the proper norms.
entries.literal: Bian adapted measures to the times, and all accorded with proper standards.

entries.zh: 性彊記默契，能斷大事。
entries.en: He had an exceptionally retentive memory and an intuitive grasp of essentials, and could settle great matters of state.
entries.literal: By nature he had a powerful memory and silent understanding, and could decide great affairs.

entries.zh: 凡所創制，處之不疑。
entries.en: Whatever systems he devised, he carried through without second thoughts.
entries.literal: Whatever institutions he established, he handled without hesitation.

entries.zh: 累遷尚書右僕射。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 世宗卽位，進位大將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Bian was promoted to Grand General.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, he was advanced to Grand General.

entries.zh: 帝嘗與諸公幸其第，儒者榮之。
entries.en: The emperor once came with the chief ministers to Bian’s house—an honor few scholars ever received.
entries.literal: The emperor once visited his residence with the various nobles—a glory for a scholar.

entries.zh: 出為宜州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out to serve as Governor of Yizhou.
entries.literal: He went out as Governor of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 薨，配食太祖廟庭。
entries.en: After his death he was granted the honor of paired offerings in the Grand Duke’s ancestral temple.
entries.literal: When he died, he was granted paired sacrifice in the Grand Duke’s temple.

entries.zh: 子慎。
entries.en: He left a son named Shen.
entries.literal: His son was Shen.

entries.zh: 辯所述六官，太祖以魏恭帝三年始命行之。
entries.en: The Grand Duke first ordered Bian’s six-ministry system into effect in the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei.
entries.literal: The six ministries as set forth by Bian were first ordered implemented by the Grand Duke in the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei.

entries.zh: 自茲厥後，世有損益。
entries.en: After that, each reign revised the system with additions and cuts.
entries.literal: From that time onward, each generation made additions and reductions.

entries.zh: 宣帝嗣位，事不師古，官員班品，隨意變革。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he no longer looked to antiquity for guidance; ranks and titles were changed as he pleased.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he did not take antiquity as his teacher; official titles and grades were altered at will.

entries.zh: 至如初置四輔官，及六府諸司復置中大夫，幷御正、內史增置上大夫等，則載於外史。
entries.en: Matters such as the first creation of the four auxiliary posts, the reappointment of middle grandees in the six ministries, and the addition of upper grandees in the Office of the Imperial Clan and the Inner Scribe are recorded in the outer annals.
entries.literal: As for the initial establishment of the four auxiliary offices, and the restoration of middle grand masters in the six ministry offices together with additions of upper grand masters in the Office of the Imperial Clan and the Inner Scribe—these are recorded in the outer history.

entries.zh: 餘則朝出夕改，莫能詳錄。
entries.en: Everything else was altered from day to day, and cannot be chronicled in full.
entries.literal: The rest were changed morning and evening, and cannot be set down in detail.

entries.zh: 于時雖行《周禮》，其內外衆職，又兼用秦漢等官。
entries.en: Even while the Rites of Zhou were nominally in force, inner and outer offices still drew on Qin and Han titles side by side.
entries.literal: At that time although the Rites of Zhou were practiced, domestic and external offices also used Qin and Han titles concurrently.

entries.zh: 今略舉其名號及命數，附之于左。
entries.en: What follows is a brief list of titles and salary grades, set out on the left.
entries.literal: Now titles and salary grades are briefly listed and appended at left.

entries.zh: 其紀傳內更有餘官而於此不載者，亦史闕文也。
entries.en: Other offices mentioned in the biographies but omitted here likewise reflect gaps in the record.
entries.literal: If the biographies contain further offices not entered here, that too is where the history lacks text.

entries.zh: 東魏北豫州刺史高仲密請舉州來附。
entries.en: Gao Zhongmi, Eastern Wei's governor of North Yu Province, offered to surrender his province and defect.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei's governor of North Yu Province, Gao Zhongmi, requested to surrender the whole province and come over.

entries.zh: 時齊神武屯兵河陽。
entries.en: At that time Gao Huan had encamped at Heyang.
entries.literal: At that time Qi Divine Warrior Gao Huan had encamped his troops at Heyang.

entries.zh: 太祖以仲密所據遼遠，難為應接，諸將皆憚此行。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai thought Zhongmi's position too distant to support easily, and all the generals feared the mission.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because Zhongmi's position was distant and remote, found it hard to support him, and all the generals feared this expedition.

entries.zh: 遠曰：「北豫遠在賊境，高歡又屯兵河陽，常理而論，實難救援。
entries.en: Li Yuan said: "North Yu lies deep in enemy territory, and Gao Huan holds Hene; by ordinary reckoning rescue is nearly impossible.
entries.literal: Yuan said: "North Yu lies far in enemy territory, and Gao Huan again has troops encamped at Hene; by ordinary reasoning, rescue is truly hard.

entries.zh: 但兵務神速，事貴合機。
entries.en: But war demands speed, and success depends on timing.
entries.literal: But military affairs require speed, and affairs value seizing the moment.

entries.zh: 古人有言：『不入獸穴，安得獸子。』
entries.en: The ancients said: "If you do not enter the beast's den, how can you take the beast's cub?"
entries.literal: The ancients had a saying: 'If you do not enter the beast's den, how can you get the beast's cub?'

entries.zh: 若以奇兵出其不意，事或可濟。
entries.en: If we strike with a surprise force where they do not expect, the affair may yet succeed.
entries.literal: If with a surprise force one strikes where they do not expect, the affair may perhaps succeed.

entries.zh: 脫有利鈍，故是兵家之常。
entries.en: Gain or loss is the common lot of war.
entries.literal: If there should be gain or loss, that is the constant way of military men.

entries.zh: 如其顧望不行，便無克定之日。」
entries.en: If we hesitate and do not go, there will never be a day of victory."
entries.literal: If one hesitates and does not go, there will never be a day of pacification."

entries.zh: 太祖喜曰：「李萬歲所言，差強人意。」
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was pleased and said: "What Li Wansui has said is rather to my liking."
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said: "What Li Wansui has said is rather to one's liking."

entries.zh: 乃授行臺尚書，前驅東出。
entries.en: He thereupon made him director of the mobile secretariat and sent him east as vanguard.
entries.literal: He thereupon appointed him director of the mobile secretariat and sent him east as vanguard.

entries.zh: 太祖率大軍繼進。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai followed with the main army.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor led the great army in continued advance.

entries.zh: 遠乃潛師而往，拔仲密以歸。
entries.en: Li Yuan then marched secretly, extracted Zhongmi, and brought him back.
entries.literal: Yuan then moved his force secretly, went, and brought Zhongmi back after taking him.

entries.zh: 仍從太祖戰于邙山。
entries.en: He again followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in the battle at Mount Mang.
entries.literal: He again followed the Grand Progenitor in fighting at Mount Mang.

entries.zh: 時大軍不利，遠獨整所部為殿。
entries.en: When the main army was beaten, Li Yuan alone kept his command in order and covered the retreat.
entries.literal: At that time the great army fared badly; Yuan alone put his command in order and served as rearguard.

entries.zh: 尋授都督義州弘農等二十一防諸軍事。
entries.en: He was soon made area commander over the twenty-one garrisons of Yi Province, Hongnong, and the rest.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed area commander over the military affairs of the twenty-one garrisons of Yi Province, Hongnong, and the rest.

entries.zh: 太祖扶危定傾，威權震主，及魏廢帝卽位之後，猜隙彌深。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had supported the endangered realm and awed the throne; after the deposed Wei emperor succeeded, suspicion and rifts grew ever deeper.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor supported the endangered and settled the tottering; his authority and power awed the ruler; and after the deposed Wei emperor took the throne, suspicion and rifts grew ever deeper.

entries.zh: 時太祖諸子，年皆幼沖，章武公導、中山公護復東西作鎮，唯托意諸婿，以為心膂。
entries.en: At that time all Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's sons were still very young; Duke Dao of Zhangwu and Duke Hu of Zhongshan were posted on distant commands east and west; he relied only on his sons-in-law as his inner guard.
entries.literal: At that time all the Grand Progenitor's sons were still very young; Duke Dao of Zhangwu and Duke Hu of Zhongshan were again posted east and west on command; he relied only on his sons-in-law as his inner guard.

entries.zh: 基與義城公李暉、常山公于翼等俱為武衛將軍，分掌禁旅。
entries.en: Li Ji together with Li Hui, Duke of Yicheng, Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and the rest were all martial-guard generals, each commanding part of the palace guard.
entries.literal: Ji together with Li Hui, Duke of Yicheng, Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and the rest were all martial-guard generals, each commanding part of the forbidden troops.

entries.zh: 帝深憚之，故密謀遂泄。
entries.en: The emperor deeply feared them, and so the secret plot leaked out.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply feared them, and so the secret plot thereupon leaked out.

entries.zh: 李賢 弟遠
entries.en: Li Xian; Li Yuan (younger brother)
entries.literal: Li Xian; brother Yuan

entries.zh: 長孫儉 長孫紹遠 弟澄 兄子兕 斛斯徵
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian; Zhangsun Shaoyuan; Zhangsun Cheng (younger brother); Zhangsun Si (nephew); Hu Sizheng
entries.literal: Zhangsun Jian; Zhangsun Shaoyuan; younger brother Cheng; elder brother's son Si; Hu Sizheng

entries.zh: 長孫儉，河南洛陽人也。
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian came from Luoyang in Henan.
entries.literal: Zhangsun Jian was a man of Luoyang in Henan.

entries.zh: 本名慶明。
entries.en: He was originally named Qingming.
entries.literal: His original name was Qingming.

entries.zh: 其先，魏之枝族，姓托拔氏。
entries.en: His ancestors were a cadet line of Wei bearing the surname Tuoba.
entries.literal: His forebears were a branch clan of Wei, surnamed Tuoba.

entries.zh: 孝文遷洛，改為長孫。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, the family took the surname Zhangsun.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, [the surname] was changed to Zhangsun.

entries.zh: 五世祖嵩，魏太尉、北平王。
entries.en: His fifth-generation ancestor Song had been Grand Commandant of Wei and Prince of Beiping.
entries.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Song was Wei Grand Commandant and Prince of Beiping.

entries.zh: 徵授大行臺尚書，兼相府司馬。
entries.en: He was summoned to court and appointed minister of the Grand Executive Office, while also serving as major of the grand chancellor's office.
entries.literal: Summoned and appointed Grand Executive Office Minister, concurrently Grand Chancellor's Office Major.

entries.zh: 嘗與羣公侍坐于太祖，及退，太祖謂左右曰：「此公閒雅，孤每與語，嘗肅然畏敬，恐有所失。」
entries.en: Once, while sitting with the other lords in attendance on Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, he withdrew with them afterward; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told his attendants: "That man is refined and easy in manner. Whenever I talk with him I find myself sitting up straight in awe, afraid I may say something unworthy."
entries.literal: Once with the various lords he attended seated before Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; when they withdrew, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to those at his side: "This lord is leisurely and elegant; every time I speak with him, I am always solemnly awed and respectful, fearing I may fail in something."

entries.zh: 他日，太祖謂儉曰：「名實理須相稱，尚書旣志安貧素，可改名儉，以彰雅操。」
entries.en: Another day Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Zhangsun Jian: "Name and conduct ought to match. You, Minister, aspire to live plainly and without excess; you should take the name Jian to show that refinement."
entries.literal: Another day, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said to Jian: "Name and reality by principle must match each other; the Minister since his ambition is to settle in poverty and simplicity, may change his name to Jian, to display elegant conduct."

entries.zh: 及梁元帝嗣位於江陵，外敦鄰睦，內懷異計。
entries.en: When Liang Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiangling, he cultivated neighborly courtesy abroad while secretly nursing other designs.
entries.literal: When Liang Emperor Yuan succeeded to the throne at Jiangling, externally he was sincere in neighborly harmony, internally he harbored a different plan.

entries.zh: 儉密啟太祖，陳攻取之謀。
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian secretly reported to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and laid out a plan to seize Jiangling.
entries.literal: Jian secretly reported to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, stating a plan to attack and take [Jiangling].

entries.zh: 於是徵儉入朝，問其經略。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then summoned Zhangsun Jian to court and asked for his strategy.
entries.literal: Thereupon Jian was summoned to court to be asked his grand strategy.

entries.zh: 儉對曰：「今江陵旣在江北，去我不遠。
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian answered: "Jiangling now lies north of the Yangtze, close at hand.
entries.literal: Jian replied: "Now Jiangling is already north of the Yangtze, not far from us.

entries.zh: 湘東卽位，已涉三年。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan of Xiangdong has already reigned three years.
entries.literal: Xiangdong succeeded to the throne, already spanning three years.

entries.zh: 觀其形勢，不欲東下。
entries.en: Judging by the situation, he has no wish to march east.
entries.literal: Observing its situation and power, it does not wish to move east.

entries.zh: 骨肉相殘，民厭其毒。
entries.en: His own kin have torn one another apart, and the people are sick of the suffering.
entries.literal: Flesh and bone mutually slaughter; the people are weary of its poison.

entries.zh: 荊州軍資器械，儲積已久，若大軍西討，必無匱乏之慮。
entries.en: Jing Province has long hoarded arms and supplies; if a great army moves west, we need not fear want.
entries.literal: Jing Province's military stores and weapons have been accumulated long; if a great army westward punishes, there will surely be no fear of shortage.

entries.zh: 且兼弱攻昧，武之善經。
entries.en: Besides, to join against the weak and strike the blind is the finest rule of war.
entries.literal: Moreover "combining against the weak and attacking the dim"—this is warfare's excellent constant.

entries.zh: 國家旣有蜀土，若更平江漢，撫而安之，收其貢賦，以供軍國，天下不足定也。」
entries.en: The realm already holds Shu; if we also pacify the Jiang-Han region, soothe and settle it, and take its tribute and taxes for army and state, the rest of the empire will not be hard to secure."
entries.literal: The state already has Shu territory; if further pacifying Jiang-Han, comforting and settling it, collecting its tribute and levies to supply army and state, all under Heaven would not be difficult to settle."

entries.zh: 太祖深然之，乃謂儉曰：「如公之言，吾取之晚矣。」
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai strongly agreed and said to Zhangsun Jian: "As you say, I have moved too late."
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai deeply agreed, then said to Jian: "As you say, I have taken it too late."

entries.zh: 令儉還州，密為之備。
entries.en: He ordered Zhangsun Jian back to his province to make secret preparations.
entries.literal: He ordered Jian to return to the province and secretly prepare.

entries.zh: 尋令柱國、燕公于謹總戎衆伐江陵。
entries.en: Soon afterward he put Pillar of State Yu Jin, Duke of Yan, in command of the army for the assault on Jiangling.
entries.literal: Soon he ordered Pillar of State, Duke of Yan Yu Jin to command the army masses to attack Jiangling.

entries.zh: 平，以儉元謀，賞奴婢三百口。
entries.en: After the city fell, Zhangsun Jian was rewarded with three hundred slaves as the original architect of the campaign.
entries.literal: When pacified, because Jian was the original planner, rewarded with three hundred male and female slaves.

entries.zh: 太祖與儉書曰：「本圖江陵，由公畫計，今果如所言。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wrote to Zhangsun Jian: "The plan for Jiangling was yours from the start, and events have proved you right.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai wrote to Jian: "Originally planning Jiangling, it was by your drawing up the plan—now it indeed is as you spoke.

entries.zh: 智者見未萌，何其妙也。
entries.en: The wise foresee what has not yet budded—how subtle your insight was.
entries.literal: The wise see before sprouting—how wondrous.

entries.zh: 但吳民離散，事藉招懷，南服重鎮，非公莫可。」
entries.en: But the people of Wu are scattered and must be won back by kindness; no one but you can hold this great southern stronghold."
entries.literal: But Wu people's are scattered and dispersed; the affair relies on receiving and embracing; the southern domain's important fortress—none but you can [hold it]."

entries.zh: 遂令儉鎮江陵。
entries.en: He then put Zhangsun Jian in charge of Jiangling.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered Jian to garrison Jiangling.

entries.zh: 進爵昌寧公，遷大將軍，移鎮荊州，總管五十二州。
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian was raised to Duke of Changning and grand general, moved his headquarters to Jing Province, and took overall command of fifty-two provinces.
entries.literal: Advanced in rank to Duke of Changning, transferred to Grand General, moved garrison to Jing Province, overall administering fifty-two provinces.

entries.zh: 儉舊嘗詣闕奏事，時值大雪，遂立於雪中待報，自旦達暮，竟無惰容。
entries.en: Once, when Zhangsun Jian went to the palace to report on affairs, a heavy snow was falling; he stood in the snow from morning until night waiting for an answer, never once showing weariness.
entries.literal: Jian formerly once went to the palace gate to report affairs; at the time there fell great snow; he then stood in the snow awaiting reply, from dawn reaching dusk—throughout no lazy expression.

entries.zh: 其奉公勤至，皆此類也。
entries.en: His devotion to duty was always of this order.
entries.literal: His serving the public with diligence and utmost effort—all were of this kind.

entries.zh: 三年，以疾還京。
entries.en: In the third year he returned to the capital because of illness.
entries.literal: In the third year, because of illness returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 為夏州總管，薨，遺啟世宗，請葬于太祖陵側，並以官所賜之宅還官。
entries.en: He served as overall commander of Xia Province, then died; in his final memorial to Emperor Shizong he asked to be buried beside Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's tomb and to return to the state the house he had received as an official grant.
entries.literal: Served as Overall Commander of Xia Province; died; left memorial to Emperor Shizong requesting burial beside Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's tomb, and also returning to the state the residence granted by office.

entries.zh: 詔皆從之。
entries.en: The emperor granted both requests.
entries.literal: Edicts all followed him.

entries.zh: 追封鄶公。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Kuai.
entries.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Kuai.

entries.zh: 荊民儀同趙超等七百人，感儉遺愛，詣闕請為儉立廟樹碑，詔許之。
entries.en: Seven hundred men of Jing, led by honorary companion Zhao Chao, moved by Zhangsun Jian's lingering kindness, petitioned at court to build him a temple and stele; the emperor approved.
entries.literal: Jing people Honorary Companion Zhao Chao and others, seven hundred men, moved by Jian's legacy of love, went to the palace gate requesting to establish a temple and erect stele for Jian; edict granted it.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「昔叔敖辭沃壤之地，蕭何就窮僻之鄉，以古方今，無慚曩哲。
entries.en: An edict said: "Long ago Shu Ao refused rich land and Xiao He settled in a poor, remote place; measured against those ancients, Zhangsun Jian need not blush before the sages of old.
entries.literal: Edict said: "Formerly Shu Ao declined fertile lands, Xiao He took a poor and remote village—comparing ancient with present, one need not be shamed before past sages.

entries.zh: 言尋嘉尚，弗忘于懷。
entries.en: Such virtue deserves lasting remembrance.
entries.literal: Speaking of seeking worthy admiration, not forgetting in the heart.

entries.zh: 而有司未達大體，遽以其第卽便給外。
entries.en: Yet the officials failed to understand the larger meaning and had hastily turned his house over to others.
entries.literal: Yet the officials did not grasp the grand principle and hastily with his mansion immediately gave it to outsiders.

entries.zh: 今還其妻子。」
entries.en: Let his wife and children have it back."
entries.literal: Now return his wife and children."

entries.zh: 子隆。
entries.en: His son was Long.
entries.literal: His son Long.

entries.zh: 儉少方正，有操行，狀貌魁梧，神彩嚴肅，雖在私室，終日儼然。
entries.en: From boyhood Zhangsun Jian was upright and principled, with a imposing frame and a grave, commanding presence; even in private he sat all day with unbroken dignity.
entries.literal: Jian from youth was upright and proper, had moral conduct; his stature was imposing, his expression dignified and stern; even in private chambers, all day he remained solemnly composed.

entries.zh: 性不妄交，非其同志，雖貴遊造門，亦不與相見。
entries.en: He made no casual friendships; if a man was not of his mind, no matter how highborn the visitor at his gate, he would not receive him.
entries.literal: By nature he did not associate casually; those not of like mind, even if noble travelers came to his door, he would not meet with them.

entries.zh: 孝昌中，起家員外散騎侍郎，從爾朱天光破隴右。
entries.en: In the Xiaochang era he entered service as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and followed Erzhu Tianguang in the conquest of Longyou.
entries.literal: During Xiaochang, he first entered office as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and followed Erzhu Tianguang to defeat Longyou.

entries.zh: 太祖臨夏州，以儉為錄事，深器敬之。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai took up post at Xia Province, he appointed Zhangsun Jian recorder-in-chief and valued him deeply.
entries.literal: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai arrived at Xia Province, he made Jian recorder-in-chief and held him in deep esteem.

entries.zh: 賀拔岳被害，太祖赴平涼，凡有經綸謀策，儉皆參預。
entries.en: After Heba Yue was murdered, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched to Pingliang; Zhangsun Jian took part in every major plan and policy.
entries.literal: When He Ba Yue was murdered, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai went to Pingliang; for every grand strategy and plan, Jian participated.

entries.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，留儉為秦州長史。
entries.en: After Houmochen Yue was defeated, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai left Zhangsun Jian behind as chief clerk of Qin Province.
entries.literal: Following the pacification of Houmochen Yue, [Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai] left Jian as Chief Clerk of Qin Province.

entries.zh: 時西夏州仍未內屬，而東魏遣許和為刺史，儉以信義招之，和乃舉州歸附。
entries.en: Western Xia Province had not yet submitted, but Eastern Wei had sent Xu He as its governor; Zhangsun Jian won him over with good faith, and Xu He brought the whole province over.
entries.literal: At the time Western Xia Province still had not submitted internally, yet Eastern Wei sent Xu He as governor; Jian with faith and righteousness won him over, and He then raised the whole province in submission.

entries.zh: 卽以儉為西夏州刺史，總統三夏州。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then made Zhangsun Jian governor of Western Xia Province with overall authority over the three Xia provinces.
entries.literal: [Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai] immediately made Jian Governor of Western Xia Province, with overall command of the three Xia provinces.

entries.zh: 時荊襄初附，太祖表儉功績尤美，宜委東南之任，授荊州刺史、東南道行臺僕射。
entries.en: When Jing and Xiang had just submitted, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai memorialized that Zhangsun Jian's record was outstanding and that the southeast should be entrusted to him; he was made governor of Jing Province and vice director of the Southeastern Circuit Executive Office.
entries.literal: At the time Jing and Xiang had newly submitted; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai memorialized that Jian's achievements were especially excellent and he should be entrusted with the southeastern appointment, granting him Governor of Jing Province and Vice Director of the Southeastern Circuit Executive Office.

entries.zh: 所部鄭縣令泉璨為民所訟，推治獲實。
entries.en: Quan Can, magistrate of Zheng County in his jurisdiction, was denounced by the people, and an inquiry proved the charges true.
entries.literal: The Magistrate of Zheng County in his jurisdiction, Quan Can, was sued by the people; investigation established the facts.

entries.zh: 儉卽大集僚屬而謂之曰：「此由刺史教誨不明，信不被物，是我之愆，非泉璨之罪。」
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian then assembled his entire staff and said: "This happened because I failed to teach and lead clearly enough for trust to reach the people. The fault is mine, not Quan Can's."
entries.literal: Jian then greatly gathered his staff and said to them: "This is because the governor's instruction and guidance were not clear, and trust did not reach the people—it is my fault, not Quan Can's crime."

entries.zh: 遂於廳事前，肉袒自罰，舍璨不問。
entries.en: He then bared his back in the courtyard before the hall, flogged himself, and dismissed the case against Quan Can.
entries.literal: Thereupon before the hall gate he bared his torso and punished himself, and released Can from inquiry.

entries.zh: 於是屬城肅勵，莫敢犯法。
entries.en: From that day the subordinate districts stood in awe, and no one dared break the law.
entries.literal: Thereupon the subordinate cities became solemnly disciplined, and none dared violate the law.

entries.zh: 魏文帝璽書勞之。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Wei sent him an imperial letter of commendation.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei sent a sealed letter commending him.

entries.zh: 太祖又與儉書曰：「近行路傳公以部內縣令有罪，遂自杖三十，用肅羣下。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also wrote to Zhangsun Jian: "Travelers lately tell me that when a county magistrate under you was found guilty, you had yourself beaten thirty strokes to awe your staff.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai also wrote to Jian saying: "Recently travelers report that because a county magistrate within your department had guilt, you then self-cane thirty strokes to solemnize the subordinates.

entries.zh: 吾昔聞『王臣謇謇，匪躬之故』，蓋謂憂公忘私，知無不為而已。
entries.en: I have heard the saying that a king's minister must speak plainly and forget himself for the realm's sake—that is, to care for the public good and hold nothing back. Yet that is only the common measure.
entries.literal: I formerly heard "king's ministers are forthright, not for their own persons"—this broadly means worrying for the public and forgetting the private, and acting on all one knows—but only this.

entries.zh: 未有如公刻身罰己以訓羣僚者也。
entries.en: Never have I known a man who punished his own body to teach his colleagues, as you have done.
entries.literal: Never has there been like you, carving the body to punish the self to instruct the many officials.

entries.zh: 聞之嘉歎。」
entries.en: When I heard of it, I marveled and rejoiced."
entries.literal: Hearing this I rejoice and sigh [in admiration]."

entries.zh: 荊蠻舊俗，少不敬長。
entries.en: Among the Jing tribes the old custom held that the young owed little respect to their elders.
entries.literal: The old custom of the Jing barbarians: the young did not respect their elders.

entries.zh: 儉殷勤勸導，風俗大革。
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian worked patiently to guide them, and local customs changed profoundly.
entries.literal: Jian diligently counseled and guided, and customs greatly changed.

entries.zh: 務廣耕桑，兼習武事，故得邊境無虞，民安其業。
entries.en: He pushed farming and mulberry cultivation while keeping the people trained for war, so the frontier stayed quiet and the people could live by their trades in peace.
entries.literal: He devoted effort to expanding agriculture and sericulture, while also practicing military affairs; thus the border had no worry, and the people were secure in their occupations.

entries.zh: 吏民表請為儉構清德樓，樹碑刻頌，朝議許焉。
entries.en: Officials and commoners petitioned to build a Pure Virtue Tower for Zhangsun Jian and to raise a stele in his praise; the court approved.
entries.literal: Officials and people submitted a petition to build Pure Virtue Tower for Jian, erect a stele and inscribe praise; court deliberation granted it.

entries.zh: 在州遂歷
entries.en: He served in the province for
entries.literal: In the province he then served for

entries.en: [variant: two]
entries.literal: (two)

entries.zh: ［七］載。
entries.en: seven years.
entries.literal: [seven] years.

entries.zh: 又除行臺僕射、荊州刺史。
entries.en: He was again appointed vice director of the executive office and governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: Again appointed Executive Office Vice Director and Governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 時梁岳陽王蕭詧內附，初遣使入朝，至荊州。
entries.en: At that time the Liang Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, had submitted to the court and sent his first embassy through Jing Province.
entries.literal: At the time Liang's Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha internally submitted, first sent envoys to court, arriving at Jing Province.

entries.zh: 儉於廳事列軍儀，具戎服，與使人以賓主禮相見。
entries.en: In the reception hall Zhangsun Jian drew up a military guard, put on full martial dress, and received the envoys with formal host-and-guest ceremony.
entries.literal: Jian in the hall arranged military ceremony, fully equipped martial garb, and with the envoys met using host-and-guest rites.

entries.zh: 儉容貌魁偉，音聲如鐘，大為鮮卑語，遣人傳譯以問客。
entries.en: Zhangsun Jian was towering in build and spoke in a deep, bell-like voice; he addressed them at length in Xianbei and had interpreters relay his questions.
entries.literal: Jian's appearance was imposing and grand, his voice like a bell; he spoke much in Xianbei language, and sent men to translate and interpret to question the guests.

entries.zh: 客惶恐不敢仰視。
entries.en: The envoys were so awed that they did not dare raise their eyes.
entries.literal: The guests in fear and trepidation did not dare look up.

entries.zh: 日晚，儉乃著裙襦紗帽，引客宴於別齋。
entries.en: That evening he changed into civilian skirt-robe and gauze cap and entertained the guests at a separate banquet.
entries.literal: When evening came, Jian then wore skirt-robe and gauze cap, and led the guests to feast in a separate study.

entries.zh: 因序梁國喪亂，朝廷招攜之意，發言可觀。
entries.en: He then spoke of the Liang realm's ruin and of the court's wish to welcome and restore them; his remarks were eloquent and compelling.
entries.literal: Thereupon he narrated the Liang state's calamity and chaos, and the court's intent to receive and embrace; his words were worth viewing.

entries.zh: 使人大悅。
entries.en: The envoys were deeply pleased.
entries.literal: The envoys greatly rejoiced.

entries.zh: 出曰：「吾所不能測也。」
entries.en: When they departed they said, "He is beyond our power to measure."
entries.literal: On leaving they said: "What we could not fathom."

entries.zh: 初，紹遠為太常，廣召工人，創造樂器，土木絲竹，各得其宜。
entries.en: While serving as grand master of ceremonial, Zhangsun Shaoyuan gathered craftsmen from far and wide to make new instruments, fitting wood, clay, silk, and bamboo each to its proper use.
entries.literal: Initially, Shaoyuan as Grand Master of Ceremonial broadly summoned craftsmen, created musical instruments; wood, clay, silk, and bamboo—each obtained its proper place.

entries.zh: 為黃鐘不調，紹遠每以為意。
entries.en: The yellow bell pitch would not settle, and the problem weighed on him constantly.
entries.literal: Because the yellow bell was not in tune, Shaoyuan always took it to heart.

entries.zh: 嘗因退朝，經韓使君佛寺前過，浮圖三層之上，有鳴鐸焉。
entries.en: Once, leaving court, he passed Han Shijun's Buddhist temple and noticed a sounding bell on the three-tiered pagoda.
entries.literal: Once upon returning from court, passing before Han Shijun's Buddhist temple, atop the three-story pagoda there was a sounding bell-clapper.

entries.zh: 忽聞其音，雅合宮調，取而配奏，方始克諧。
entries.en: When he heard it strike, the tone matched the gong pitch perfectly; he took the bell, matched it in performance, and at last achieved harmony.
entries.literal: Suddenly hearing its sound, it elegantly matched the gong mode; taking it to pair and play, only then achieved harmony.

entries.zh: 紹遠乃啟世宗行之。
entries.en: Zhangsun Shaoyuan then memorialized Emperor Shizong to adopt it.
entries.literal: Shaoyuan thereupon reported to Emperor Shizong to implement it.

entries.zh: 紹遠所奏樂，以八為數。
entries.en: The music Zhangsun Shaoyuan submitted took eight as its governing number.
entries.literal: The music Shaoyuan presented used eight as the number.

entries.zh: 故梁黃門侍郎裴正上書，以為昔者大舜欲聞七始，下洎周武，爰創七音。
entries.en: Pei Zheng, former Attendant Secretary of the Yellow Gate of Liang, submitted a memorial arguing that in antiquity Great Shun had wished to hear the Seven Beginnings and that, down to King Wu of Zhou, the seven tones were first established.
entries.literal: Former Liang Attendant Secretary of the Yellow Gate Pei Zheng submitted a memorial, holding that in antiquity Great Shun wished to hear the Seven Beginnings, and down through King Wu of Zhou thereupon created the seven tones.

entries.zh: 持林鐘作黃鐘，以為正調之首。
entries.en: He treated Forest Bell as Yellow Bell and made it the head of the standard pitch sequence.
entries.literal: He took Forest Bell as Yellow Bell to serve as the head of the correct tuning.

entries.zh: 詔與紹遠詳議往復，於是遂定以八為數焉。
entries.en: An edict ordered Zhangsun Shaoyuan to debate the matter in detail; the court then fixed the number at eight.
entries.literal: An edict ordered detailed discussion back and forth with Shaoyuan; thereupon it was fixed to take eight as the number.

entries.zh: 授小司空。
entries.en: Zhangsun Shaoyuan was appointed Lesser Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was appointed Lesser Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 高祖讀史書，見武王克殷而作七始，又欲廢八而懸七，幷除黃鐘之正宮，用林鐘為調首。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu read the histories and, seeing that King Wu had created the Seven Beginnings after conquering Yin, again wished to abolish the eight-tone system and suspend seven sets, remove Yellow Bell as the principal palace pitch, and use Forest Bell as the leading tone.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu read the historical records and, seeing that King Wu, on conquering Yin, created the Seven Beginnings, again wished to abolish eight and suspend seven, also removing Yellow Bell as the correct palace tone and using Forest Bell as the head of the tuning.

entries.zh: 紹遠奏云：「天子懸八，肇自先民，百王共軌，萬世不易。
entries.en: Zhangsun Shaoyuan memorialized: "The Son of Heaven suspends eight sets of bells and chimes—a practice reaching back to antiquity, shared by a hundred kings and unchanging through the ages.
entries.literal: Shaoyuan memorialized, saying: "The Son of Heaven suspends eight—this began with the ancients; a hundred kings shared one standard, unchanging for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 下逮周武，甫修七始之音。
entries.en: Down to King Wu of Zhou, he merely restored the music of the Seven Beginnings.
entries.literal: Down to King Wu of Zhou, he only repaired the tones of the Seven Beginnings.

entries.zh: 詳諸經義，又無廢八之典。
entries.en: A careful reading of the canonical texts offers no precedent for abolishing the eight-tone system.
entries.literal: Examining all the canonical teachings, there is again no precedent for abolishing eight.

entries.zh: 且黃鐘為君，天子正位，今欲廢之，未見其可。」
entries.en: Moreover Yellow Bell is the sovereign pitch and the Son of Heaven's proper station; to abolish it now seems impossible to justify."
entries.literal: Moreover Yellow Bell is the ruler; it is the Son of Heaven's correct position—now to wish to abolish it, one does not see how this could be right."

entries.zh: 後高祖竟
entries.en: In the end Emperor Gaozu
entries.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu in the end

entries.en: (abolished) [deleted character]
entries.literal: (abolished)

entries.zh: 行七音。
entries.en: implemented the seven-tone system.
entries.literal: implemented the seven tones.

entries.zh: 屬紹遠遘疾，未獲面陳，慮有司遽損樂器，乃書與樂部齊樹之。
entries.en: Just then Zhangsun Shaoyuan fell ill. Unable to present his views in person and fearing that the relevant offices would hastily cut back the instruments, he wrote to Qi Shuzhi of the Music Bureau.
entries.literal: Just then Shaoyuan fell ill; unable to state his views in person, fearing the relevant offices would hastily reduce the musical instruments, he wrote to Qi Shuzhi of the Music Bureau.

entries.zh: 後從太祖援玉壁，又從戰邙山，進位驃騎大將軍、開府。
entries.en: Later he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to relieve Yubi and fought again at Mount Mang; he was raised to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.
entries.literal: Later he followed Grand Progenitor in relieving Yubi and again fought at Mount Mang; he was advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.

entries.zh: 孝閔踐阼，拜大將軍，封義門公，為玉壁總管。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, he was made Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Yimen, and appointed overall commander of Yubi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Yimen, and made overall commander of Yubi.

entries.zh: 卒，自喪初至及葬，世宗三臨之。
entries.en: After his death, from the start of mourning through the burial, Emperor Ming visited three times.
entries.literal: When he died, from the start of mourning to the burial, Emperor Ming visited three times.

entries.zh: 典祀中大夫宇文容諫曰：「君臨臣喪，自有節制。
entries.en: Palace Sacrifice Grand Master Yuwen Rong remonstrated: "When a sovereign attends a minister's mourning, ritual sets clear limits.
entries.literal: Palace Sacrifice Grand Master Yuwen Rong remonstrated, saying: "A lord visiting a minister's mourning has its own limits.

entries.zh: 今乘輿屢降，恐乖禮典。」
entries.en: For the imperial carriage to descend so often may violate ritual precedent."
entries.literal: Now the imperial carriage has repeatedly descended—this may violate ritual precedent."

entries.zh: 世宗不從。
entries.en: Emperor Ming did not listen.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming did not heed him.

entries.zh: 魏孝武初，累遷司徒右長史。
entries.en: Early in the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei he rose to chief clerk of the right under the Minister of Public Works.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, repeatedly promoted to Chief Clerk of the Right of the Minister of Public Works.

entries.zh: 及齊神武稱兵而帝西遷，紹遠隨稚奔赴。
entries.en: When Gao Huan took up arms and the emperor moved west, Zhangsun Shaoyuan went with his father to join him.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan raised troops and the Emperor migrated west, Shaoyuan followed Zhi in hurrying to join.

entries.zh: 又累遷殿中尚書、錄尚書事。
entries.en: He was promoted again to palace master of writing and recorder of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Again repeatedly promoted to Palace Master of Writing and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs.

entries.zh: 太祖每謂羣公曰：「長孫公任使之處，令人無反顧憂。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai often told the other ministers: "Wherever Lord Zhangsun is placed in office, men serve without looking back over their shoulders.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai often said to the various lords: "Where Lord Zhangsun is assigned and employed, it makes people have no worry of looking back.

entries.zh: 漢之蕭、寇，何足多也。
entries.en: The Xiao and Kou of Han were nothing beside him.
entries.literal: Han's Xiao and Kou—how could they be counted as much.

entries.zh: 然其容止堂堂，足為當今模楷。」
entries.en: And his bearing is so upright and commanding that he is a model for our own age."
entries.literal: Yet his bearing and deportment are dignified and imposing, sufficient to serve as today's model."

entries.zh: 六官建，拜大司樂。
entries.en: When the Six Offices were established, Zhangsun Shaoyuan was made grand master of music.
entries.literal: When the Six Offices were established, appointed Grand Master of Music.

entries.zh: 孝閔踐阼，封上黨公。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 澄字士亮。
entries.en: Cheng, styled Shiliang.
entries.literal: Cheng, styled Shiliang.

entries.zh: 年十歲，司徒李琰之見而奇之，遂以女妻焉。
entries.en: At ten he so impressed Minister over the Masses Li Yanzhi that Li gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: At age ten, Minister over the Masses Li Yanzhi saw him and was struck by him; he thereupon gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 十四，從征討，有策謀，勇冠諸將。
entries.en: At fourteen he joined campaigns, showed strategic talent, and outstripped the other generals in courage.
entries.literal: At fourteen, he followed on campaigns; he had strategy and counsel, and his bravery ranked above all the generals.

entries.zh: 及長，容貌魁岸，風儀溫雅。
entries.en: When grown he was tall and imposing, with a warm and refined bearing.
entries.literal: When grown, his appearance was imposing and his bearing warm and refined.

entries.zh: 魏孝武初，除征東將軍、渭州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he was made General Pacifying the East and Governor of Wei Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was appointed General Pacifying the East and Governor of Wei Province.

entries.zh: 兕字若汗，性機辯，強記博聞，雅重賓游，尤善談論。
entries.en: Si, styled Ruohan, was quick and eloquent by nature, with a strong memory and wide learning; he greatly valued guests and fellowship and was especially skilled at conversation.
entries.literal: Si, styled Ruohan, was by nature quick and eloquent, with a strong memory and wide learning; he greatly valued guests and fellowship and was especially skilled at discourse.

entries.zh: 從魏孝武西遷。
entries.en: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei on the westward migration.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei on the westward migration.

entries.zh: 天和初，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府，遷絳州刺史。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tianhe, after successive promotions he became Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office, then was transferred as Governor of Jiang Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, after successive promotions he became Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office, then was transferred as Governor of Jiang Province.

entries.zh: 自魏孝武西遷，雅樂廢缺，徵博采遺逸，稽諸典故，創新改舊，方始備焉。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's westward migration court music had fallen into ruin; Hu Sizheng gathered what survived, checked it against canonical precedent, and by creating anew and reforming the old at last restored it.
entries.literal: From Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's westward migration, court music had been lost and broken; Sizheng broadly gathered what survived, examined canonical precedent, created anew and reformed the old—and only then was it complete.

entries.zh: 又樂有錞于者，近代絕無此器，或有自蜀得之，皆莫之識。
entries.en: Music also includes the chunyu, an instrument long extinct in recent times; when one was brought from Shu, no one recognized it.
entries.literal: Moreover in music there is the chunyu—in recent times this instrument had completely ceased to exist; when some obtained one from Shu, none recognized it.

entries.zh: 徵見之曰：「此錞于也。」
entries.en: Hu Sizheng saw it and said: "This is a chunyu."
entries.literal: Sizheng saw it and said: "This is a chunyu."

entries.zh: 衆弗之信。
entries.en: No one believed him.
entries.literal: The crowd did not believe him.

entries.zh: 徵遂依干寶《周禮注》以芒筒捋之，其聲極振，衆乃歎服。
entries.en: Hu Sizheng then followed Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou and struck it with a bamboo tube; the sound rang out powerfully, and the onlookers marveled.
entries.literal: Sizheng thereupon, following Gan Bao's commentary on the Rites of Zhou, used a bamboo tube to strike it; the sound was extremely resonant, and the crowd then sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 徵乃取以合樂焉。
entries.en: He then incorporated it into the court music.
entries.literal: Sizheng then took it to combine with the music.

entries.zh: 六官建，拜司樂中大夫，進位驃騎大將軍、開府。
entries.en: When the Six Offices were established he was made Grand Master Director of Music and advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.
entries.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Master Director of Music, and advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office.

entries.zh: 後高祖以徵治經有師法，詔令教授皇太子。
entries.en: Later Emperor Gaozu, finding Hu Sizheng's teaching of the classics authoritative, ordered him to instruct the crown prince.
entries.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu, because Sizheng's handling of the classics had received-method orthodoxy, issued an edict ordering him to instruct the crown prince.

entries.zh: 宣帝時為魯公，與諸皇子等咸服青衿，行束修之禮，受業於徵，仍並呼徵為夫子。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan was Duke of Lu, he and the other princes all wore the scholar's blue collar, performed the ceremony of bundled dried meat, studied under Hu Sizheng, and all called him Master.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Duke of Lu, he and the other princes all wore the blue collar, performed the ceremony of bundled dried meat, received instruction from Sizheng, and all called Sizheng "Master."

entries.zh: 儒者榮之。
entries.en: Confucian scholars regarded it as an honor.
entries.literal: Confucian scholars took it as an honor.

entries.zh: 宣帝嗣位，遷上大將軍、大宗伯。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Hu Sizheng was transferred to Upper Grand General and Grand Director of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Upper Grand General and Grand Director of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 時高祖初崩，梓宮在殯，帝意欲速葬，令朝臣議之。
entries.en: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just died and the coffin was still in temporary burial; the emperor wished to bury him quickly and ordered the court to debate the matter.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu had just died and the coffin was still in temporary burial; the emperor wished a speedy burial and ordered the court ministers to deliberate.

entries.zh: 徵與內史宇文孝伯等固請依禮七月，帝竟不許。
entries.en: Hu Sizheng, Inner Scribe Yuwen Xiaobo, and others firmly asked that the seven-month mourning rite be observed, but the emperor refused.
entries.literal: Sizheng and Inner Scribe Yuwen Xiaobo and others firmly requested observing the seven-month rite, but the emperor did not permit it.

entries.zh: 帝之為太子也，宮尹鄭譯坐不能以正道調護，被謫除名。
entries.en: When the emperor had been crown prince, Palace Superintendent Zheng Yi had been demoted and dismissed for failing to guide him properly.
entries.literal: When the emperor had been crown prince, Palace Superintendent Zheng Yi had been demoted and removed from office for failing to guide and protect him by the correct way.

entries.zh: 而帝雅親愛譯，至是拜譯內史中大夫，甚委任之。
entries.en: But the emperor had long been fond of Zheng Yi; he now made him Inner Scribe Senior Grand Master and entrusted him heavily.
entries.literal: But the emperor had long been fond of Yi; at this point he appointed Yi Inner Scribe Senior Grand Master and entrusted him heavily.

entries.zh: 譯乃獻新樂，十二月各一笙，每一笙用十六管。
entries.en: Zheng Yi thereupon presented new music: one sheng for each month, each sheng using sixteen pipes.
entries.literal: Yi thereupon presented new music: each month had one sheng, and each sheng used sixteen pipes.

entries.zh: 帝令與徵議之，徵駁而奏，帝頗納焉。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Hu Sizheng to discuss it with him; Sizheng rebutted the proposal in a memorial, and the emperor largely accepted his view.
