entries.literal: The emperor ordered deliberation with Sizheng; Sizheng rebutted and submitted a memorial, and the emperor largely accepted it.

entries.zh: 及高祖山陵還，帝欲作樂，復令議其可不。
entries.en: When the procession returned from Emperor Gaozu's tomb, the emperor wished to perform music and again ordered the court to debate whether it was permissible.
entries.literal: When the procession returned from Emperor Gaozu's mount tomb, the emperor wished to perform music and again ordered discussion of whether it was permissible.

entries.zh: 徵曰：「《孝經》云『聞樂不樂』。
entries.en: Hu Sizheng said: "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'On hearing music, one is not joyful.'
entries.literal: Sizheng said: "The Classic of Filial Piety says, 'On hearing music, one is not joyful.'

entries.zh: 聞尚不樂，其況作乎。」
entries.en: If even hearing music brings no joy, how much less should one perform it?"
entries.literal: If even hearing music brings no joy, how much more making it?"

entries.zh: 鄭譯曰：「旣云聞樂，明卽非無。
entries.en: Zheng Yi said: "Since the text says 'hearing music,' music clearly exists.
entries.literal: Zheng Yi said: "Since it says 'hearing music,' that clearly means music is not absent.

entries.zh: 止可不樂，何容不奏。」
entries.en: One need only refrain from joy—how can one refuse to perform it altogether?"
entries.literal: Only one need not be joyful—how can one fail to perform it?"

entries.zh: 帝遂依譯議。
entries.en: The emperor then followed Zheng Yi's view.
entries.literal: The emperor then followed Yi's opinion.

entries.zh: 譯因此銜之。
entries.en: Zheng Yi thereby nursed a grudge against him.
entries.literal: Yi thereby harbored resentment against him.

entries.zh: 帝后肆行非度，昏虐日甚。
entries.en: Thereafter the emperor wantonly overstepped all bounds, and his folly and cruelty grew daily.
entries.literal: After this the emperor wantonly overstepped measure; his delusion and cruelty grew daily.

entries.zh: 徵以荷高祖重恩，嘗備位師傅，若生不能諫，死何以見高祖。
entries.en: Hu Sizheng, deeply indebted to Emperor Gaozu and having once served as tutor, thought: if he could not remonstrate while alive, how could he face Emperor Gaozu after death?
entries.literal: Sizheng, bearing the heavy grace of Emperor Gaozu and having once held the post of tutor, thought: if in life he could not remonstrate, how in death could he face Emperor Gaozu?

entries.zh: 乃上疏極諫，指陳帝失，帝不納。
entries.en: He then submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, listing the emperor's faults; the emperor would not listen.
entries.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance, pointing out the emperor's faults; the emperor did not accept it.

entries.zh: 譯因譖之，遂下徵獄。
entries.en: Zheng Yi thereupon slandered him, and Hu Sizheng was thrown into prison.
entries.literal: Yi thereupon slandered him, and Sizheng was thrown into prison.

entries.zh: 獄卒張元哀之，乃以佩刀穿獄牆，遂出之。
entries.en: The jailer Zhang Yuan took pity on him, used his girdle knife to break through the prison wall, and got him out.
entries.literal: The jailer Zhang Yuan pitied him; using his girdle knife he pierced the prison wall and thus got him out.

entries.zh: 元卒被拷而終無所言。
entries.en: Zhang Yuan was tortured in interrogation but never spoke.
entries.literal: Yuan was beaten in interrogation but to the end said nothing.

entries.zh: 徵遇赦得免。
entries.en: Hu Sizheng was spared when an amnesty was declared.
entries.literal: Sizheng met an amnesty and was spared.

entries.zh: 隋文踐極，例復官，除太子太傅，詔修撰樂書。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Hu Sizheng was restored to office by precedent, made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, and ordered to compile a book on music.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, by precedent his office was restored; he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and ordered to compile a book on music.

entries.zh: 開皇初，薨。
entries.en: At the beginning of Kaihuang he died.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he died.

entries.zh: 子諺。
entries.en: His son was Yan.
entries.literal: His son Yan.

entries.zh: 徵所撰《樂典》十卷。
entries.en: Hu Sizheng compiled the Music Canon in ten scrolls.
entries.literal: Sizheng compiled the Music Canon in ten scrolls.

entries.zh: 建德之後，武帝志在平齊。
entries.en: After the Jiande era Emperor Wu turned his mind to conquering Qi.
entries.literal: After the Jiande era, Emperor Wu set his mind on pacifying Qi.

entries.zh: 孝寬乃上疏陳三策。
entries.en: Xiaokuan submitted a memorial presenting three strategies.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan then submitted a memorial setting forth three strategies.

entries.zh: 其第一策曰：
entries.en: The first strategy read:
entries.literal: The first strategy said:

entries.zh: 書奏，武帝遣小司寇淮南西元
entries.en: When the memorial was in, Emperor Wu sent Junior Minister of Crime Yuan
entries.literal: The memorial was submitted; Emperor Wu sent Junior Minister of Crime Huainan Xi Yuan

entries.en: [Textual note: Wei]
entries.literal: (Wei) [emended variant]

entries.zh: 偉、開府伊婁謙等重幣聘齊。
entries.en: Wei, Kaifu Yilou Qian, and others with rich gifts to court Qi.
entries.literal: 〔Wei〕 emended: Xi Yuan → Yuan Wei, Kaifu Yilou Qian, and others with heavy gifts to visit Qi as envoys.

entries.zh: 爾後遂大舉，再駕而定山東，卒如孝寬之策。
entries.en: Later the court did launch a great campaign. The emperor marched twice and pacified the east of the mountains, just as Xiaokuan had foreseen.
entries.literal: After that a great campaign was launched; twice the emperor took the field and settled the lands east of the mountains; in the end it happened as Xiaokuan's strategy [had said].

entries.zh: 孝寬每以年迫懸車，屢請致仕。
entries.en: Xiaokuan, feeling his years advance, repeatedly asked to retire.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan repeatedly, because his years pressed toward hanging up his chariot, asked many times to retire from office.

entries.zh: 帝以海內未平，優詔弗許。
entries.en: The emperor, holding that the realm was not yet fully at peace, graciously refused each request.
entries.literal: The emperor, because within the seas was not yet pacified, with a gracious edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 至是復稱疾乞骸骨。
entries.en: At this point he again pleaded illness and asked to be allowed to retire.
entries.literal: At this point he again claimed illness and requested to retire.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「往已面申本懷，何煩重請也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "You already told me your mind face to face — why ask again?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "You have already stated your intent to me in person — why trouble yourself with repeated requests?"

entries.zh: 五年，帝東伐，過幸玉壁。
entries.en: In the fifth year Emperor Wu marched east and, passing through, visited Yubi.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the emperor marched east; passing through, he visited Yubi.

entries.zh: 觀禦敵之所，深嘆羨之，移時乃去。
entries.en: He inspected the enemy's old defenses, sighed in deep admiration, and lingered a long while before leaving.
entries.literal: He viewed the places where the enemy had been held at bay, sighed deeply in admiration, and only after a long while departed.

entries.zh: 孝寬自以習練齊人虛實，請為先驅。
entries.en: Xiaokuan, who knew the Qi armies well, asked to lead the van.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan, judging himself practiced in the strengths and weaknesses of the men of Qi, asked to serve as vanguard.

entries.zh: 帝以玉壁要衝，非孝寬無以鎮之，乃不許。
entries.en: The emperor held that Yubi was too vital to leave to anyone but Xiaokuan and refused.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Yubi was a vital choke point and none but Xiaokuan could hold it, would not allow it.

entries.zh: 及趙王招率兵出稽胡，與大軍掎角，乃敕孝寬為行軍總管，圍守華谷以應接之。
entries.en: When Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao marched against the Ji Hu in pincer with the main force, Xiaokuan was ordered to act as campaign commander, besiege Huagu, and keep the link open.
entries.literal: When Prince of Zhao Zhao led troops out against the Ji Hu in pincer coordination with the main army, he thereupon ordered Xiaokuan to be campaign commander, to besiege and hold Huagu in support.

entries.zh: 孝寬克其四城。
entries.en: Xiaokuan took four of their cities.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan captured four of their cities.

entries.zh: 武帝平晉州，復令孝寬還舊鎮。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu took Jin Province, Xiaokuan was sent back to his former post.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Jin Province, he again ordered Xiaokuan back to his old garrison.

entries.zh: 敻子瓘行隨州刺史，因疾物故，孝寬子總復於并州戰歿。
entries.en: Wei Xiong's son Guan, acting governor of Sui, died of illness, and Wei Xiaokuan's son Zong was killed in battle at Bing.
entries.literal: Xiong's son Guan was acting governor of Sui Prefecture and died of illness; Xiaokuan's son Zong also fell in battle at Bing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 一日之中，凶問俱至。
entries.en: Within a single day news of both deaths arrived.
entries.literal: Within a single day, tidings of both deaths arrived.

entries.zh: 家人相對悲慟，而敻神色自若。
entries.en: The household wept together, but Wei Xiong's face stayed unchanged.
entries.literal: The household faced one another in grief and lamentation, yet Xiong's expression remained as usual.

entries.zh: 謂之曰：「死生命也，去來常事，亦何足悲。」
entries.en: He told them, "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary things—what is there to mourn?"
entries.literal: He said to them: "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary affairs—what is there worth grieving over?"

entries.zh: 援琴撫之如舊。
entries.en: He took up his zither and played as before.
entries.literal: He took up the zither and played it as before.

entries.zh: 韋孝寬 韋敻 梁士彥
entries.en: Biographies of Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Xiong, and Liang Shiyan
entries.literal: Wei Xiaokuan; Wei Xiong; Liang Shiyan

entries.zh: 通少敦敏好學，有志節。
entries.en: From youth Tong was earnest, quick-witted, and devoted to learning, and he possessed strong moral resolve.
entries.literal: Tong from youth was sincere, quick, and fond of learning, with will and integrity.

entries.zh: 幼從在河西，遂逢寇難，與政相失。
entries.en: As a boy he followed his father west of the Yellow River; when bandits struck, he was separated from Zheng.
entries.literal: In youth he followed [his father] in Hexi; he then encountered bandit troubles and was separated from Zheng.

entries.zh: 通乃自拔東歸，從爾朱榮。
entries.en: Tong made his own escape back east and entered Erzhu Rong's service.
entries.literal: Tong then extricated himself and returned east, following Erzhu Rong.

entries.zh: 榮死，又從爾朱兆。
entries.en: After Rong died he followed Erzhu Zhao.
entries.literal: When Rong died, he followed Erzhu Zhao.

entries.zh: 及爾朱氏滅，乃入關。
entries.en: When the Erzhu clan fell, he entered Guanzhong.
entries.literal: When the Erzhu clan was destroyed, he then entered the Pass.

entries.zh: 文帝時在夏州，引為帳內督。
entries.en: While Yuwen Tai was stationed at Xia Province, he took Tong on as a supervisor in his personal staff.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was at Xia Province, he brought him in as supervisor within the headquarters.

entries.zh: 頃之，賀拔岳為侯莫陳悅所害，時有傳岳軍府已亡散者，文帝憂之，通以為不然。
entries.en: Soon afterward Heba Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue; word spread that Yue's headquarters had already fallen apart, and Yuwen Tai grew anxious, but Tong did not believe it.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter Heba Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue; at the time there were reports that Yue's army headquarters had already been scattered and lost, and Emperor Wen worried; Tong thought it was not so.

entries.zh: 居數日，問至，果如所策。
entries.en: Within days messengers came in, and events proved exactly as he had predicted.
entries.literal: After several days inquiries arrived, and it was exactly as he had judged.

entries.zh: 自是愈見親禮，遂晝夜陪侍，家人罕見其面。
entries.en: From then on he was treated with ever greater intimacy and favor; he attended Yuwen Tai day and night, and his family seldom saw him.
entries.literal: From then on he was ever more favored with intimate courtesy; he then attended day and night, and his family seldom saw his face.

entries.zh: 通雖處機密，愈自恭謹，文帝以此重之。
entries.en: Though he held confidential matters, he grew only more respectful and cautious, and Yuwen Tai esteemed him all the more for it.
entries.literal: Though Tong was privy to secrets, he became ever more deferential and careful, and Emperor Wen therefore valued him highly.

entries.zh: 後以迎孝武功，封都昌縣伯。
entries.en: Later, for service in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu, he was enfeoffed baron of Duchang county.
entries.literal: Later for merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed Baron of Duchang county.

entries.zh: 大統元年，進爵為侯。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he was raised to marquis.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong, his enfeoffment was advanced to marquis.

entries.zh: 從禽竇泰，復弘農。
entries.en: He took part in capturing Dou Tai and recovering Hongnong.
entries.literal: He followed [them] in capturing Dou Tai and recovering Hongnong.

entries.zh: 沙苑之役，力戰有功。
entries.en: At the battle of Shachuan he fought with great force and distinguished himself.
entries.literal: At the battle of Shachuan he fought fiercely and had merit.

entries.zh: 及魏孝武與齊神武有隙，詔賀拔勝出牧荊州，柔謂因此可著功績，遂從勝之荊州。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Gao Huan fell out, an edict sent Heba Sheng to take charge of Jing Province; Rou thought he could win distinction by it and followed Sheng there.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Gao Huan fell out, an edict sent Heba Sheng to administer Jing Province; Rou judged that he could thereby win merit and followed Sheng to Jing Province.

entries.zh: 以柔為大行臺郎中，掌書記。
entries.en: Rou was made gentleman of the grand mobile headquarters and put in charge of records.
entries.literal: Rou was made gentleman of the grand mobile headquarters in charge of records.

entries.zh: 軍中機務，柔多預之。
entries.en: He often took part in the army's critical business.
entries.literal: In important military affairs of the army, Rou often took part.

entries.zh: 及勝為太保，以柔為掾，加冠軍將軍。
entries.en: When Sheng was made grand guardian, Rou was made his staff officer and given the added rank of Champion General.
entries.literal: When Sheng became grand guardian, Rou was made his staff officer with the added rank of general of the victorious army.

entries.zh: 孝武后召勝引兵赴洛，勝以問柔。
entries.en: Later Emperor Xiaowu summoned Sheng to bring troops to Luoyang, and Sheng asked Rou's counsel.
entries.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu summoned Sheng to bring troops to Luoyang; Sheng asked Rou.

entries.zh: 曰：「高歡托晉陽之甲，意實難知。
entries.en: Rou said, "Gao Huan relies on the armies of Jinyang, and his intent is hard to read.
entries.literal: He said: "Gao Huan relies on the armies of Jinyang; his intent is truly hard to know.

entries.zh: 公宜席捲赴都，與決勝負，存沒以之，此忠之上策也。
entries.en: Your Grace should sweep to the capital, decide victory or defeat with him, and stake life on the outcome—that is the loyal upper plan.
entries.literal: My lord should sweep to the capital and decide victory or defeat with him, staking life upon it—that is the upper plan of loyalty.

entries.zh: 若北阻魯陽，南幷舊楚，東連兗、豫，西接關中，帶甲十萬，觀釁而動，亦中策也。
entries.en: If you hold Luyang in the north, join old Chu in the south, link Yan and Yu in the east, and tie to Guanzhong in the west, with one hundred thousand armored men watch for an opening and move—that is the middle plan.
entries.literal: If you block Luyang in the north, combine with old Chu in the south, link Yan and Yu in the east, and reach to Guanzhong in the west, with one hundred thousand armored men watch for openings and move—that too is a middle plan.

entries.zh: 舉三荊之地，通款梁國，可以身免，功名去矣。
entries.en: Raise the three Jing provinces and open friendly ties with Liang—you may save yourself, but fame and achievement are lost.
entries.literal: Raise the three Jing provinces, open friendly ties with Liang—you may save yourself, but fame and achievement are gone.

entries.zh: 策之下者。」
entries.en: That would be the least of the plans."
entries.literal: That is the lower plan."

entries.zh: 勝輕柔年少，笑而不應。
entries.en: Sheng looked down on Rou for his youth, smiled, and made no answer.
entries.literal: Sheng looked down on Rou for his youth, smiled, and did not reply.

entries.zh: 及孝武西遷，東魏遣侯景襲穰，勝敗，遂南奔梁。
entries.en: When Xiaowu moved westward, Eastern Wei dispatched Hou Jing against Xiang; Sheng was routed and fled south into Liang territory.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing to attack Xiang; Sheng was defeated and fled south to Liang.

entries.zh: 柔亦從之。
entries.en: Rou followed him.
entries.literal: Rou followed as well.

entries.zh: 勝頻表梁求歸，武帝覽表，嘉其辭彩。
entries.en: Sheng repeatedly memorialized Liang asking to return north; Emperor Wu of Liang read the memorials and praised their literary polish.
entries.literal: Sheng repeatedly memorialized Liang asking to return north; Emperor Wu of Liang, reading the memorials, praised their literary polish.

entries.zh: 既知柔所製，因遣舍人勞問，并遺縑錦。
entries.en: Learning that Rou had written them, he sent a palace attendant with greetings and also bestowed silk and brocade.
entries.literal: Learning they were Rou's composition, he sent a palace attendant with greetings and also bestowed silk and brocade.

entries.zh: 後與勝俱還，行至襄陽，齊神武懼勝西入，遣侯景以輕騎邀之。
entries.en: Later, returning north with Sheng, they reached Xiangyang; Gao Huan feared Sheng would go west and sent Hou Jing with light cavalry to cut them off.
entries.literal: Later, returning north with Sheng, when they reached Xiangyang, Gao Huan feared Sheng would enter the west and sent Hou Jing with light cavalry to intercept them.

entries.zh: 勝及柔懼，乃棄船山行，贏糧冒險，經數百里。
entries.en: Sheng and Rou, in fear, abandoned their boats and traveled by mountain paths, carrying grain on their backs through peril for several hundred li.
entries.literal: Sheng and Rou in fear abandoned their boats and traveled by mountain paths, carrying grain on their backs through danger for several hundred li.

entries.zh: 時屬秋霖，徒侶凍餒，死者太半。
entries.en: Autumn rains had set in; companions froze and starved, and more than half died on the road.
entries.literal: It was autumn rains; followers froze and starved, and more than half died.

entries.zh: 至豐陽界，柔迷失道，獨宿僵木之下，寒雨衣濕，殆至於死。
entries.en: At the border of Fengyang, Rou lost the road and slept alone beneath a dead tree, cold rain soaking his clothes until he was near death.
entries.literal: Reaching the border of Fengyang, Rou lost the road and slept alone beneath a dead tree, cold rain soaking his clothes, nearly to death.

entries.zh: 大統二年，至長安。
entries.en: In Datong year two he arrived at Chang'an.
entries.literal: In the second year of Datong he reached Chang'an.

entries.zh: 封容城縣男，邑二百戶。
entries.en: He received enfeoffment as baron of Rongcheng county, with a fief of two hundred households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed baron of Rongcheng county with a fief of two hundred households.

entries.zh: 太祖重其才，引為行臺郎中，加平東將軍，除從事中郎，與蘇綽對掌機密。
entries.en: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai valued his talent, brought him in as gentleman of the mobile headquarters, added general who pacifies the east, made him attendant gentleman, and paired him with Su Chuo to share confidential affairs.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor valued his talent, brought him in as gentleman of the mobile headquarters, added general who pacifies the east, made him attendant gentleman, and paired him with Su Chuo to share confidential affairs.

entries.zh: 時沙苑之後，大軍屢捷，汝、潁之間，多舉義來附。
entries.en: After Shayuan the great army won again and again; between the Ru and Ying rivers many districts rose in allegiance and submitted.
entries.literal: At that time after Shayuan, the great army repeatedly won; between Ru and Ying, many rose in allegiance and came to submit.

entries.zh: 書翰往反，日百餘牒。
entries.en: Letters went back and forth at a rate of more than a hundred dispatches a day.
entries.literal: Letters went back and forth—more than a hundred dispatches a day.

entries.zh: 柔隨機報答，皆合事宜。
entries.en: Rou answered as circumstances required, and every reply fit the occasion.
entries.literal: Rou answered as circumstances required, all fitting the matter.

entries.zh: 進爵為子，增邑三百戶，除中書舍人。
entries.en: His rank rose to viscount, his fief grew by three hundred households, and he was named palace secretary.
entries.literal: He was advanced to viscount, his fief increased by three hundred households, and he was made palace secretary.

entries.zh: 遷司農少卿，轉郎，兼著作，撰起居注。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice minister of the grand commissariat, then to gentleman, and concurrently compiled the imperial diary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the grand commissariat, then gentleman, concurrently compiling and writing the imperial diary.

entries.zh: 後拜黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He was later made attendant at the yellow gates.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed attendant at the yellow gates.

entries.zh: 文帝知其貧，解衣賜之。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai knew he was poor and gave him the coat off his own back.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen knew he was poor and gave him his own garment off his back.

entries.zh: 魏廢帝元年，加軍騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍、中書監。
entries.en: In the first year of the deposed emperor of Wei he was given the added ranks of grand general of the cavalry, equal in three departments, attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry, and supervisor of the palace secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of the deposed emperor of Wei, he was given the added ranks of grand general of the cavalry, equal in three departments, attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry, and supervisor of the palace secretariat.

entries.zh: 申徽 陸通 弟逞 柳敏 盧柔 唐瑾
entries.en: Biographies of Shen Hui, Lu Tong, Lu Cheng, Liu Min, Lu Rou, and Tang Jin
entries.literal: Shen Hui; Lu Tong; younger brother Cheng; Liu Min; Lu Rou; Tang Jin

entries.zh: 天和六年，出為汾州諸軍事、汾州刺史，進爵為公，增邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was sent out as area commander of military affairs for Fen Province and governor of Fen, raised to duke, and given an added fief of one thousand five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe, he went out as area commander of military affairs for Fen Province and Governor of Fen Province; he was advanced in rank to duke, and his fief was increased by one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 齊將段孝先率衆五萬來寇，梯沖地道，晝夜攻城。
entries.en: Northern Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led fifty thousand men against the city with siege towers, rams, and underground tunnels, attacking day and night.
entries.literal: Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led a host of fifty thousand to invade; with scaling ladders, rams, and underground tunnels, they assaulted the city day and night.

entries.zh: 敷親當矢石，隨事扞禦，拒守累旬。
entries.en: Fu met arrows and stones in person, met each assault as it came, and held out for many weeks.
entries.literal: Fu personally faced arrows and stones, resisted according to each circumstance, and held out for many tens of days.

entries.zh: 孝先攻之愈急。
entries.en: Duan Xiaoxian pressed the attack ever harder.
entries.literal: Xiaoxian attacked all the more urgently.

entries.zh: 時城中兵不滿二千，戰死者已十四五，糧儲又盡，公私窮蹙。
entries.en: The garrison held fewer than two thousand men; four or five men in ten had already fallen; grain was gone, and public stores and private households alike were desperate.
entries.literal: At the time the troops in the city numbered fewer than two thousand; those killed in battle already reached four or five tenths; grain stores were again exhausted, and public and private both were in desperate straits.

entries.zh: 齊公憲總兵赴救，憚孝先，不敢進軍。
entries.en: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian marched to the relief but feared Duan Xiaoxian and would not press forward.
entries.literal: Duke of Qi Xian mustered troops to go to the rescue, but feared Xiaoxian and did not dare advance.

entries.zh: 敷知必陷沒，乃召其衆謂之曰：「吾與卿等，俱在邊鎮，實願同心戮力，破賊全城。
entries.en: Knowing the city could not hold, Fu gathered his men and said, "You and I stand together on the frontier; I had hoped we might unite and break the enemy to save this city.
entries.literal: Fu knew the city must fall, so he summoned his men and said to them: "You and I together are stationed on the frontier; I truly wish to join hearts and combine strength to break the enemy and preserve the whole city.

entries.zh: 但強寇四面攻圍日久，吾等糧食已盡，救援斷絕。
entries.en: But a strong foe has besieged us from every side for days; our grain is spent and no relief will come.
entries.literal: But strong enemies have attacked from all sides for many days; our grain is already exhausted, and relief is cut off.

entries.zh: 守死窮城，非丈夫也。
entries.en: To die defending a doomed city is no true man's course.
entries.literal: To hold out and die in a hopeless city is not the act of a true man.

entries.zh: 今勝兵之士，猶數百人，欲突圍出戰，死生一決。
entries.en: We still have several hundred able fighters; I mean to break out and fight, staking life and death on a single charge.
entries.literal: Today the fit fighting men still number several hundred; I wish to break through the siege and go out to fight, settling life and death in one decision.

entries.zh: 儻或得免，猶冀生還，受罪闕庭，孰與死於寇乎！
entries.en: If we can break free, some of us may yet live, return home, and accept judgment at court—better that than dying at the enemy's hands!
entries.literal: If by chance we may escape, we may still hope to return alive, receive punishment before the imperial court — how is that not better than dying at the hands of the enemy!

entries.zh: 吾計決矣，於諸君意何如？」
entries.en: My mind is made up. What say you?"
entries.literal: My decision is made — what do you all think?"

entries.zh: 衆咸涕泣從命。
entries.en: All wept and agreed to follow him.
entries.literal: All wept and, weeping, obeyed.

entries.zh: 敷乃率見兵夜出，擊殺齊軍數十人。
entries.en: That night Fu led his remaining men out and killed several dozen Qi soldiers.
entries.literal: Fu then led the troops available and went out by night, killing several tens of Qi soldiers.

entries.zh: 齊軍衆稍卻。
entries.en: The Qi ranks fell back a little.
entries.literal: The Qi army masses withdrew slightly.

entries.zh: 俄而孝先率諸軍盡銳圍之，敷殊死戰，矢盡，為孝先所擒。
entries.en: Soon Duan Xiaoxian closed in with every available man; Fu fought to the last; when his arrows were spent he was taken.
entries.literal: Before long Xiaoxian led all the armies with full sharpness to surround them; Fu fought to the death; arrows exhausted, he was captured by Xiaoxian.

entries.zh: 齊人方欲任用之，敷不為之屈，遂以憂懼卒於鄴。
entries.en: The Qi meant to win him over, but Fu would not yield and died in Ye of grief and anguish.
entries.literal: The men of Qi were just then intending to employ him, but Fu would not submit to them; he thereupon died in Ye from grief and fear.

entries.zh: 高祖平齊，贈使持節、大將軍、淮廣復三州諸軍事、三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu pacified Qi, Fu was posthumously made bearer of the staff, grand general, area commander of military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu provinces, governor of those three provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified Qi, he was posthumously granted bearer of the staff, Grand General, military affairs for Huai, Guang, and Fu three provinces, Governor of three provinces, and the posthumous name Loyal and Robust.

entries.zh: 葬於華陰舊塋。
entries.en: He was buried in the family graveyard at Huayin.
entries.literal: He was buried at the old family graves at Huayin.

entries.zh: 趙善字僧慶，太傅、楚國公貴之從祖兄也。
entries.en: Zhao Shan, courtesy name Sengqing, was a senior cousin of Yuwen Gui, grand tutor and Duke of Chu.
entries.literal: Zhao Shan, styled Sengqing, was a paternal cousin once removed of the Grand Tutor and Duke of Chu, Gui.

entries.zh: 祖國，魏龍驤將軍、洛州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Guo had served Wei as general of dragon cavalry and inspector of Luo Province.
entries.literal: His grandfather Guo was Wei General of Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Luo Province.

entries.zh: 父更，安樂太守。
entries.en: His father Geng was administrator of Anle commandery.
entries.literal: His father Geng was Administrator of Anle commandery.

entries.zh: 太祖為丞相，加前將軍、太中大夫，封長安縣男，食邑三百戶。
entries.en: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became chancellor, Zhen was given the added ranks of former general and grand master of palace counsel and enfeoffed baron of Chang'an with a fief of three hundred households.
entries.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became chancellor, added Former General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel; enfeoffed Baron of Chang'an county with fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 轉行臺左丞，加撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫，遷使持節、都督南郢州諸軍事、南郢州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to left assistant director of the mobile headquarters, given the added titles of general who pacifies the army and silver-crown grand master of splendid happiness, and appointed bearer of the staff, area commander of Nan Ying, and governor of Nan Ying.
entries.literal: Transferred to left assistant director of the mobile headquarters; added General Who Pacifies the Army and Silver-Crown Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; moved to bearer of the staff, area commander of military affairs for Nan Ying Province, Governor of Nan Ying.

entries.zh: 復入為行臺左丞。
entries.en: He returned to the capital as left assistant director of the mobile headquarters.
entries.literal: Again entered service as left assistant director of the mobile headquarters.

entries.zh: 瑱明察有幹局，再居左轄，時論榮之。
entries.en: Clear-sighted and able, Zhen twice held the left assistant directorship and was widely praised for it.
entries.literal: Zhen was perceptive and capable; twice holding the left assistant post, contemporary opinion honored him.

entries.zh: 從復弘農，戰沙苑，加衛大將軍、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: He followed the campaign to recover Hongnong and fought at Shaye, for which he was given grand general of the guard and left grand master of splendid happiness.
entries.literal: Following recovery of Hongnong, battle at Shaye; added Grand General of the Guard and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 又從戰河橋，進爵為子，增邑二百戶。
entries.en: He fought again at Heqiao, was raised to viscount, and his fief was increased by two hundred households.
entries.literal: Again following battle at Heqiao; advanced enfeoffment to viscount, increased fief by two hundred households.

entries.zh: 大統八年，齊神武侵汾、絳，瑱從太祖禦之。
entries.en: In Datong year 8, when Gao Huan invaded Fen and Jiang, Zhen followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to meet him.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, Gao Huan invaded Fen and Jiang; Zhen followed the Grand Progenitor to resist.

entries.zh: 軍還，令瑱以本官鎮蒲津關，帶中潬城主。
entries.en: When the army returned, Zhen was ordered to hold Pujin Pass in his existing rank and also serve as lord of Zhongtan walled city.
entries.literal: Army returned; ordered Zhen with his existing rank to garrison Pujin Pass, concurrently city lord of Zhongtan.

entries.zh: 尋除蒲州總管府長史。
entries.en: Before long he was made chief administrator of the Puzhou headquarters command.
entries.literal: Soon appointed chief administrator of the Puzhou headquarters command.

entries.zh: 頃之，徵拜鴻臚卿。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was summoned and appointed minister of ceremonial.
entries.literal: Shortly after, summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 以望族，兼領鄉兵，加帥都督。
entries.en: As a man of a leading family, he also took charge of local militia and was given the added rank of area commander.
entries.literal: Because of eminent clan, concurrently commanded local militia; added area commander.

entries.zh: 遷大都督、通直散騎常侍，行京兆郡事，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。
entries.en: He rose to grand area commander and regular attendant of direct communication and scattered cavalry, acted for Jingzhao commandery, and was advanced to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in three departments, and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: Promoted to grand area commander, regular attendant of direct communication and scattered cavalry; acting Jingzhao commandery affairs; advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 韋瑱字世珍，京兆杜陵人也。
entries.en: Wei Zhen, courtesy name Shizhen, came from Duling in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Wei Zhen, styled Shizhen, was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 世為三輔著姓。
entries.en: His family had long been a leading house of the Three Metropolises.
entries.literal: For generations a prominent clan of the Three Metropolises.

entries.zh: 曾祖惠度，姚泓尚書郎。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Huidu had served Yao Hong as a gentleman of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Huidu was a masters of writing gentleman under Yao Hong.

entries.zh: 隨劉義真過江，仕宋為鎮西府司馬、順陽太守，行南雍州事。
entries.en: He crossed the Yangtze with Liu Yizhen and served the Song as marshal of the western garrison headquarters, administrator of Shunyang, and acting governor of southern Yong.
entries.literal: Following Liu Yizhen across the Yangtze, he served Song as western garrison headquarters marshal, Administrator of Shunyang, and acting southern Yong Province affairs.

entries.zh: 後於襄陽歸魏，拜中書侍郎，贈安西將軍、洛州刺史。
entries.en: Later, at Xiangyang, he went over to Wei and was made vice director of the palace secretariat; after death he was posthumously honored as general who pacifies the west and governor of Luo.
entries.literal: Later at Xiangyang he submitted to Wei, was appointed vice director of the Palace Secretariat, and posthumously given General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Luo Province.

entries.zh: 祖千雄，略陽郡守。
entries.en: His grandfather Qianxiong had been administrator of Lueyang commandery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Qianxiong was Administrator of Lueyang commandery.

entries.zh: 父英，代郡守，贈兗州刺史。
entries.en: His father Ying was administrator of Dai commandery and was posthumously made governor of Yan.
entries.literal: His father Ying was Administrator of Dai commandery, posthumously given Governor of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 李延孫，伊川人也。
entries.en: Li Yansun came from Yichuan.
entries.literal: Li Yansun was a native of Yichuan.

entries.zh: 祖伯扶，魏太和末，從征懸瓠有功，為汝南郡守。
entries.en: His grandfather Bofu distinguished himself in the late Taihe campaigns against Xuanhu and was appointed administrator of Runan commandery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Bofu, at the end of the Taihe era of Wei, followed the campaign against Xuanhu with merit and became Administrator of Runan Commandery.

entries.zh: 父長壽，性雄豪，有武藝。
entries.en: His father Changshou was a bold, formidable man skilled in arms.
entries.literal: His father Changshou was by nature bold and heroic and possessed martial skill.

entries.zh: 少與蠻酋結託，屢相招引，侵滅關南。
entries.en: In youth he allied with tribal chieftains and repeatedly led them in raids that ravaged the lands south of the passes.
entries.literal: In his youth he formed ties with barbarian chiefs, repeatedly leading each other in raids, encroaching upon and ravaging the region south of the passes.

entries.zh: 孝昌中，朝議恐其為亂，乃以長壽為防蠻都督，給其鼓節，以慰其意。
entries.en: During the Xiaochang era the court, fearing he would stir up rebellion, appointed Changshou commander for the defense against the tribes and bestowed on him drums and credentials of authority to win him over.
entries.literal: In the Xiaochang period the court deliberation feared he would cause disorder, and therefore appointed Changshou Commander for Barbarian Defense, granting him drums and credentials of office to appease his mind.

entries.zh: 長壽冀因此遂得任用，亦盡其智力，防遏群蠻。
entries.en: Changshou hoped this would lead to formal employment, and he threw all his wit and energy into holding the tribal peoples in check.
entries.literal: Changshou hoped that through this he would obtain employment, and also exerted all his intelligence and strength to defend against and restrain the various barbarians.

entries.zh: 伊川左右，寇盜為之稍息。
entries.en: Around Yichuan, raiding and banditry eased somewhat as a result.
entries.literal: On both sides of Yichuan, bandits and robbers for this reason gradually subsided.

entries.zh: 永安之後，盜賊蜂起，長壽乃招集叛亡，徒侶日盛。
entries.en: After the Yong'an period unrest spread like swarming bees; Changshou gathered deserters and fugitives until his following grew daily.
entries.literal: After the Yong'an era bandits rose like bees; Changshou then gathered deserters and fugitives, and his followers grew day by day.

entries.zh: 魏帝藉其力用，因而撫之。
entries.en: The Wei emperor valued his strength and made a point of keeping him on side.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor relied on his strength and usefulness and accordingly placated him.

entries.zh: 乃授持節、大都督，轉鎮張白塢。
entries.en: He received the insignia of a commissioner with plenipotentiary powers and the rank of grand commander-in-chief, and was posted to garrison Zhangbaiwu.
entries.literal: He was then granted bearing-the-staff credentials and the title of grand commander-in-chief and transferred to garrison Zhangbaiwu.

entries.zh: 後為河北郡守，轉河內郡守。
entries.en: He later served as administrator of Hebei commandery and then of Henei.
entries.literal: Later he became Administrator of Hebei Commandery, then transferred to Administrator of Henei Commandery.

entries.zh: 所歷之處，咸以猛烈聞。
entries.en: Wherever he served, he was known for his ruthless severity.
entries.literal: Every place he passed through was known for his fierceness.

entries.zh: 討捕諸賊，頻有功。
entries.en: His campaigns against bandits brought him repeated credit.
entries.literal: In pursuing and capturing various bandits he frequently had merit.

entries.zh: 授衛大將軍、北華州刺史，賜爵清河郡公。
entries.en: He was made General of the Guard and governor of Beihua province and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.
entries.literal: He was appointed General of the Guard and Governor of Beihua Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery.

entries.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，長壽率勵義士拒東魏。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Changshou rallied loyal volunteers to resist Eastern Wei.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Changshou led and encouraged loyal men to resist Eastern Wei.

entries.zh: 孝武嘉之，復授潁川郡守，遷廣州刺史。
entries.en: Xiaowu praised him, reappointed him administrator of Yingchuan, and promoted him to governor of Guang province.
entries.literal: Xiaowu commended him, again appointed him Administrator of Yingchuan Commandery, and promoted him to Governor of Guang Province.

entries.zh: 東魏遣行臺侯景率兵攻之，長壽衆少，城陷，遂遇害。
entries.en: Eastern Wei sent its executive commissioner Hou Jing against him with an army; Changshou had too few men, his city fell, and he was killed.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei sent the executive commissioner Hou Jing to lead troops to attack him; Changshou's forces were few, the city fell, and he was killed.

entries.zh: 大統元年，追贈太尉、使持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、冀定等十二州諸軍事、定州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander-in-chief over military affairs in twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and governor of Ding province.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously awarded Grand Commandant, commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander over the military affairs of the twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and Governor of Ding Province.

entries.zh: 自魏孝武西遷之後，朝士流亡。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, officials of the court fled into exile.
entries.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, court officials went into exile.

entries.zh: 廣陵王欣、錄尚書長孫稚、潁川王斌之、安昌王子均及建甯、江夏、隴東諸王幷百官等攜持妻子來投延孫者，延孫卽率衆衛送，並贈以珍玩，咸達關中。
entries.en: When Prince of Guangling Xin, Chief Clerk of the Records Office Changsun Zhi, Prince of Yingchuan Binzhi, Prince of Anchang Zijun, the princes of Jianning, Jiangxia, and Longdong, and many other officials fled east with their families to seek Yansun's protection, he led his men to escort them, gave them precious gifts, and saw them all safely through to Guanzhong.
entries.literal: Prince of Guangling Xin, Chief Clerk of the Records Office Changsun Zhi, Prince of Yingchuan Binzhi, Prince of Anchang Zijun, and the princes of Jianning, Jiangxia, and Longdong together with the hundred officials who came bringing wives and children to join Yansun—Yansun at once led his troops to guard and escort them, and also presented them with precious curios; all reached Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 齊神武深患之，遣行臺慕容紹宗等數道攻之。
entries.en: Gao Huan of Northern Qi took this as a grave threat and sent the executive commissioner Murong Shaozong and others to attack him along several routes.
entries.literal: Gao Huan of Qi was deeply troubled by this and sent the executive commissioner Murong Shaozong and others along several routes to attack him.

entries.zh: 延孫獎勵所部出戰，遂大破之，臨陣斬其揚州刺史薛喜。
entries.en: Yansun roused his troops to battle, routed the enemy completely, and on the field slew Xue Xi, their governor of Yang province.
entries.literal: Yansun encouraged and roused his subordinates to go out to battle, then utterly defeated them and on the field beheaded their Governor of Yang Province, Xue Xi.

entries.zh: 於是義軍更振。
entries.en: The loyalist cause rallied anew.
entries.literal: Thereupon the loyalist armies were revived once more.

entries.zh: 乃授延孫京南行臺、節度河南諸軍事、廣州刺史。
entries.en: Yansun was appointed executive commissioner for the capital south, given overall command of military affairs in Henan, and made governor of Guang province.
entries.literal: Yansun was then appointed Executive Commissioner of the Capital South, controller of military affairs in Henan, and Governor of Guang Province.

entries.zh: 尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督，賜爵華山郡公。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, given the privilege of ceremonial parity with the Three Dukes, made grand commander-in-chief, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huashan.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, made Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, appointed grand commander-in-chief, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huashan Commandery.

entries.zh: 延孫既荷重委，每以剋清伊、洛為己任。
entries.en: Entrusted with heavy responsibility, Yansun made it his personal mission to pacify the Yi and Luo region.
entries.literal: Yansun, having received this weighty commission, each time took clearing the Yi and Luo regions as his own responsibility.

entries.zh: 頻以少擊衆，威振敵境。
entries.en: Again and again he defeated larger forces with smaller ones, and his fame spread terror through enemy territory.
entries.literal: Repeatedly with few he struck many, and his prestige shook the enemy borders.

entries.zh: 法保少好遊俠，而質直少言。
entries.en: In youth Fabao loved the life of the wandering knight, yet he was plainspoken, upright, and sparing of words.
entries.literal: Fabao in youth loved roaming knights-errant, yet was plain and upright and spoke little.

entries.zh: 所與交遊，皆輕猾亡命。
entries.en: His companions were reckless outlaws and desperate men.
entries.literal: Those with whom he associated were all reckless, cunning fugitives.

entries.zh: 人有急難投之者，多保存之。
entries.en: Those who fled to him in desperate need usually found shelter with him.
entries.literal: When people in urgent distress came to him, he for the most part preserved them.

entries.zh: 雖屢被追捕，終不改其操，父沒，事母兄以孝敬聞。
entries.en: Though often hunted by the authorities, he never abandoned his ways; after his father's death he cared for his mother and elder brother with devoted filial piety and won renown for it.
entries.literal: Although repeatedly pursued and captured, he never changed his conduct; when his father died, he served his mother and elder brother with filial piety and was renowned for it.

entries.zh: 慕李長壽之為人，遂娶長壽女，因寓居關南。
entries.en: Admiring Li Changshou's character, he married Changshou's daughter and settled south of the passes.
entries.literal: He admired the character of Li Changshou, and therefore married Changshou's daughter and took up residence south of the passes.

entries.zh: 正光末，四方雲擾。
entries.en: At the end of the Zhenguang era the empire was in turmoil on every side.
entries.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era turmoil rose on all sides like clouds.

entries.zh: 王公被難者或依之，多得全濟，以此為貴遊所德。
entries.en: Princes and nobles in peril often found refuge with him and many were saved entirely; the great families were deeply grateful.
entries.literal: Princes and nobles who suffered calamity sometimes relied on him, and many were wholly saved; for this he was esteemed by the exalted wanderers.

entries.zh: 乃拜員外散騎侍郎，加輕車將軍。
entries.en: He was appointed supernumerary gentleman-attendant of the scattered cavalry and additionally made General of the Light Chariot.
entries.literal: He was then appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat and additionally made General of the Light Chariot.

entries.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，法保從山南赴行在所。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Fabao came from south of the mountains to join the imperial camp.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Fabao came from south of the mountains to the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 除右將軍、太中大夫，封固安縣男，邑二百戶。
entries.en: He was appointed Right General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an with a fief of two hundred households.
entries.literal: He was appointed Right General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an County with a fief of two hundred households.

entries.zh: 雄少敢勇，膂力絕人，工騎射，有將率材略。
entries.en: From youth Xiong was bold and fearless, with extraordinary strength; he excelled at mounted archery and showed the makings of a commander.
entries.literal: Xiong in youth was daring and brave, his physical strength surpassing other men; he was skilled in horseback archery and possessed the talent and strategy of a commander.

entries.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，雄便慷慨有立功之志。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Xiong was seized by a passionate desire to win distinction.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Xiong at once was ardent and had the will to achieve merit.

entries.zh: 大統初，遂與其屬六十餘人於洛西舉兵，數日間，衆至千人。
entries.en: At the opening of the Datong era he rose in arms west of the Luo with some sixty followers; within days his force grew to a thousand men.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Datong he then, with more than sixty of his followers, raised troops west of Luo; within several days his host reached a thousand men.

entries.zh: 與河南行臺楊琚共為掎角。
entries.en: He coordinated with Yang Ju, executive commissioner of Henan, in a pincer strategy.
entries.literal: Together with Yang Ju, Executive Commissioner of Henan, he formed pincers.

entries.zh: 每抄掠東魏，所向剋獲。
entries.en: His raids into Eastern Wei territory succeeded wherever he struck.
entries.literal: Each time he raided Eastern Wei, wherever he went he captured booty.

entries.zh: 徒眾日盛，州縣不能禦之。
entries.en: His following swelled daily until the local provinces and commanderies could no longer contain him.
entries.literal: His followers grew daily in strength, and the provinces and commanderies could not resist him.

entries.zh: 東魏洛州刺史韓賢以狀聞，鄴乃遣其軍司慕容紹宗率兵與賢合勢討雄。
entries.en: Han Xian, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province, reported the situation to the capital; Ye sent its army commander Murong Shaozong with troops to join Xian in suppressing Xiong.
entries.literal: Han Xian, Governor of Luo Province of Eastern Wei, reported the situation; Ye then sent its army commander Murong Shaozong to lead troops and join forces with Xian to attack Xiong.

entries.zh: 戰數十合，雄兵略盡，兄及妻子皆為賢所獲，將以為戮。
entries.en: After dozens of clashes Xiong's force was nearly spent; Xian captured his elder brother, wife, and children and prepared to execute them.
entries.literal: After several tens of engagements Xiong's troops were nearly exhausted; his elder brother and wife and children were all captured by Xian and were about to be executed.

entries.zh: 乃遣人告雄曰：「若雄至，皆免之。」
entries.en: He sent word to Xiong: "If you surrender, they will all be spared."
entries.literal: He then sent someone to tell Xiong: "If Xiong comes, all will be spared."

entries.zh: 雄與其所親謀曰：「奮不顧身以立功名者，本望上申忠義，下榮親戚。
entries.en: Xiong consulted his closest followers: "Men who risk everything for glory do so hoping to prove their loyalty above and bring honor to their families below.
entries.literal: Xiong consulted with his close associates, saying: "Those who exert themselves without regard for body to establish fame and merit originally hope above to display loyalty and righteousness and below to bring honor to kin.

entries.zh: 今若忍而不赴，人謂我何。
entries.en: If I hold back now, what will people say of me?
entries.literal: Now if I endure it and do not go, what will people say of me?

entries.zh: 既免之後，更思其計，未為晚也。」
entries.en: Once they are safe, I can still think of another plan—it will not be too late."
entries.literal: After they are spared, to think again of one's plans is not too late."

entries.zh: 於是，遂詣賢軍，卽隨賢還洛。
entries.en: With that he went to Xian's camp and returned with him to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went to Xian's army and at once followed Xian back to Luo.

entries.zh: 乃潛引賢黨，謀欲襲之。
entries.en: He secretly won over some of Xian's followers and plotted a surprise attack.
entries.literal: He then secretly won over Xian's partisans and plotted to strike him.

entries.zh: 事泄，遁免。
entries.en: The plot was discovered and he fled to safety.
entries.literal: The affair leaked out and he fled and escaped.

entries.zh: 陳忻字永怡，宜陽人也。
entries.en: Chen Xin, whose courtesy name was Yongyi, came from Yiyang.
entries.literal: Chen Xin, courtesy name Yongyi, was a native of Yiyang.

entries.zh: 少驍勇，有氣俠，姿貌魁岸，同類咸敬憚之。
entries.en: In youth he was fierce and brave, full of chivalrous spirit, and imposing in stature; his peers respected and feared him.
entries.literal: In youth he was valiant and brave, possessed chivalrous spirit, and had a towering stature; his peers all respected and feared him.

entries.zh: 魏孝武西遷之後，忻乃於辟惡山招集勇敢少年數十人，寇掠東魏，仍密遣使歸附。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew to the west, Xin gathered several dozen bold young men on Mount Pibie, raided Eastern Wei, and secretly sent envoys to declare allegiance to the west.
entries.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Xin then on Pibie Mountain gathered several tens of daring youths, raided Eastern Wei, and still secretly sent envoys to submit.

entries.zh: 大統元年，授持節、伏波將軍、羽林監、立義大都督，賜爵霸城縣男。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he received plenipotentiary credentials, was made General Who Subdues Waves, supervisor of the imperial guards, and commander of the righteous forces, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Bacheng.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong he was granted bearing-the-staff credentials, made General Who Subdues Waves, Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers, and Commander-in-Chief Who Raises Righteousness, and enfeoffed as Baron of Bacheng County.

entries.zh: 三年，太祖復弘農，東魏揚州刺史段琛拔城遁走。
entries.en: In the third year the Grand Ancestor recovered Hongnong; Duan Chen, Eastern Wei's governor of Yang province, abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: In the third year the Grand Ancestor recovered Hongnong; Duan Chen, Governor of Yang Province of Eastern Wei, abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 忻率義徒於九曲道邀之，殺傷甚衆，擒其新安令張祗。
entries.en: Xin ambushed them on the Jiuqu road with his volunteers, inflicting heavy casualties and capturing Zhang Di, magistrate of Xin'an.
entries.literal: Xin led his righteous followers to intercept them on the Jiuqu road, killing and wounding very many, and captured their magistrate of Xin'an, Zhang Di.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉其忠款，使行新安縣事。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor praised his loyalty and put him in charge of Xin'an county.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor commended his loyal sincerity and had him act as administrator of Xin'an County.

entries.zh: 及獨孤信入洛，忻舉李延孫為前鋒，仍從信守金墉城。
entries.en: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, Xin put Li Yansun at the head of the vanguard and joined Xin in holding Jinyong city.
entries.literal: When Dugu Xin entered Luo, Xin nominated Li Yansun as vanguard and still followed Xin in guarding Jinyong City.

entries.zh: 及河橋戰不利，隨軍西還，復行新安縣事。
entries.en: After the defeat at Heqiao he withdrew west with the army and again administered Xin'an county.
entries.literal: When the battle at Heqiao went badly, he followed the army west in retreat and again acted as administrator of Xin'an County.

entries.zh: 東魏遣土人牛道恆為
entries.en: Eastern Wei appointed the local leader Niu Daoheng as
entries.literal: Eastern Wei sent a local man, Niu Daoheng, to be

entries.en: (Yang [in the received text])
entries.literal: (Yang)

entries.zh: 陽州刺史，忻率兵擊破之，進爵為子。
entries.en: governor of Yang province; Xin attacked and defeated him and was promoted to viscount.
entries.literal: Yang Province governor; Xin led troops and defeated him, and his rank was advanced to viscount.

entries.zh: 常隨崤東諸將鎮遏伊、洛間，每有功效。
entries.en: He regularly served with the generals east of Xiao in holding the Yi–Luo corridor, and won credit in every campaign.
entries.literal: He constantly followed the generals east of Xiao in garrisoning and restraining the region between the Yi and Luo, and each time had merit.

entries.zh: 九年，與李遠迎高仲密，仍從戰邙山。
entries.en: In the ninth year he joined Li Yuan in receiving Gao Zhongmi's defection and fought at Mount Mang.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he joined Li Yuan in welcoming Gao Zhongmi and still followed in the battle at Mount Mang.

entries.zh: 及大軍西還，復與韓雄等依山合勢，破東魏三城，斬其金門郡守方臺洛。
entries.en: When the main army withdrew west, he joined Han Xiong and others in a mountain offensive, took three Eastern Wei cities, and slew Fang Tailuo, administrator of Jinmen commandery.
entries.literal: When the great army returned west, he again with Han Xiong and others combined their strength relying on the mountains, broke three Eastern Wei cities, and beheaded their Administrator of Jinmen Commandery, Fang Tailuo.

entries.zh: 增邑六百戶。
entries.en: His fief was increased by six hundred households.
entries.literal: His fief was increased by six hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋行宜陽郡事。
entries.en: He soon took charge of Yiyang commandery.
entries.literal: Soon he acted as administrator of Yiyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 東魏復遣劉盆生為金門郡守，忻又斬之。
entries.en: When Eastern Wei sent Liu Pensheng as administrator of Jinmen, Xin slew him as well.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei again sent Liu Pensheng as Administrator of Jinmen Commandery; Xin again beheaded him.

entries.zh: 除鎮遠將軍、魏郡守。
entries.en: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Wei commandery.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Wei Commandery.

entries.zh: 俄授使持節、平東將軍、顯州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, General Who Pacifies the East, and governor of Xian province.
entries.literal: Soon he was granted commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, made General Who Pacifies the East, and appointed Governor of Xian Province.

entries.zh: 太祖以忻威著敵境，仍留靜邊，弗令之任。
entries.en: Because Xin's reputation struck fear in enemy territory, the Grand Ancestor kept him on the frontier to hold the border and would not release him to take up his new post.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Xin's prestige was manifest in enemy territory, still kept him to pacify the frontier and did not let him take up his appointment.

entries.zh: 十年，侯景築九曲城，忻率衆邀之，擒其宜陽郡守趙嵩、金門郡守樂敬賓。
entries.en: In the tenth year Hou Jing built Jiuqu city; Xin intercepted him and captured Zhao Song, administrator of Yiyang, and Yue Jingbin, administrator of Jinmen.
entries.literal: In the tenth year Hou Jing built Jiuqu City; Xin led troops to intercept him and captured his Administrator of Yiyang Commandery Zhao Song and Administrator of Jinmen Commandery Yue Jingbin.

entries.zh: 十三年，從李遠平九曲城，授帥都督。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he joined Li Yuan in taking Jiuqu city and was made commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed Li Yuan in pacifying Jiuqu City and was appointed commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 東魏將爾朱渾願率精騎三千來向宜
entries.en: The Eastern Wei general Erzhu Hunyuan led three thousand elite horsemen toward Yi
entries.literal: The Eastern Wei general Erzhu Hunyuan led three thousand elite cavalry toward Yi

entries.en: (cheng [in the received text])
entries.literal: (cheng [city])

entries.zh: 陽，忻與諸將輕兵邀之，願遂退走。
entries.en: Yang; Xin and the other generals intercepted him with a light force, and Hunyuan withdrew.
entries.literal: yang; Xin with the various generals with light troops intercepted him, and Hunyuan then retreated and fled.

entries.zh: 十五年，除宜陽郡守，加大都督、撫軍將軍。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was made administrator of Yiyang commandery and additionally given the ranks of grand commander-in-chief and General Who Pacifies the Army.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Administrator of Yiyang Commandery and additionally made grand commander-in-chief and General Who Pacifies the Army.

entries.zh: 十六年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes and made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 與齊將東方老戰于石泉，破之，俘獲甚衆。
entries.en: He defeated the Qi general Dongfang Lao at Shiquan and took a great number of prisoners.
entries.literal: He fought with the Qi general Dongfang Lao at Shiquan, defeated him, and captured very many.

entries.zh: 時東魏每歲遣兵送米饋宜陽，忻輒與諸軍邀擊之，每多剋獲。
entries.en: Each year Eastern Wei sent grain convoys to Yiyang; Xin and the other commanders ambushed them again and again with rich spoils.
entries.literal: At that time each year Eastern Wei sent troops escorting grain to supply Yiyang; Xin then with the various armies intercepted and struck them, each time capturing much booty.

entries.zh: 玄少慷慨，有膽略。
entries.en: From youth Xuan was high-spirited and bold, with courage and resource.
entries.literal: Xuan in youth was ardent and generous and possessed courage and strategy.

entries.zh: 普泰中，除奉朝請。
entries.en: During the Putai era he was appointed court attendant.
entries.literal: In the Putai era he was appointed Attendant at Court.

entries.zh: 頻從軍與梁人交戰。
entries.en: He campaigned repeatedly against Liang.
entries.literal: He frequently followed the army in exchanges of battle with the men of Liang.

entries.zh: 永安初，以功授征虜將軍、中散大夫。
entries.en: At the opening of the Yong'an era he was rewarded with the ranks of General Who Captures Barbarians and palace attendant of the central scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, for merit he was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians and Palace Attendant of the Central Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，東魏北徙，人情騷動，各懷去就。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei withdrew west and Eastern Wei moved its capital north, the people were unsettled and everyone weighed whether to stay or go.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west and Eastern Wei shifted north, popular sentiment was agitated and each person harbored thoughts of staying or leaving.

entries.zh: 玄遂率募鄉曲，立義于關南，卽從韋法保與東魏司徒高敖曹戰於關口。
entries.en: Xuan raised a loyal militia south of the passes and fought with Wei Fabao against Gao Aocao, Eastern Wei's Minister of Works, at the pass.
entries.literal: Xuan then led recruited local militia and raised righteousness south of the passes, and at once followed Wei Fabao in battle against Gao Aocao, Minister of Works of Eastern Wei, at the pass.

entries.zh: 及獨孤信入洛陽，隸行臺楊琚防馬渚。
entries.en: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he served under the executive commissioner Yang Ju in defending Mazhu.
entries.literal: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, he was attached to Yang Ju, Executive Commissioner, in defending Mazhu.

entries.zh: 復與高敖曹接戰。
entries.en: He fought Gao Aocao again.
entries.literal: He again joined in battle with Gao Aocao.

entries.zh: 自是每率鄉兵，抗拒東魏。
entries.en: From then on he led local militia against Eastern Wei again and again.
entries.literal: From this time he each time led local militia to resist Eastern Wei.

entries.zh: 前後十餘戰，皆有功。
entries.en: In more than ten engagements he won credit every time.
entries.literal: Before and after, in more than ten battles, all had merit.

entries.zh: 及侯景以豫州來附，法保率兵赴景。
entries.en: When Hou Jing defected with Yuzhou, Fabao marched to join him.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing came over with Yuzhou to submit, Fabao led troops to go to Jing.

entries.zh: 景欲留之，法保疑其有貳心，乃固辭還所鎮。
entries.en: Hou Jing tried to keep him there, but Fabao suspected treachery and firmly refused, returning to his post.
entries.literal: Jing wished to detain him; Fabao suspected he had a divided heart and therefore firmly declined and returned to his garrison.

entries.zh: 十五年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，尋進爵為公。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and given a baron's establishment equal to the Three Dukes; soon afterward his title was raised to duke.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and Baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes; soon his rank was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 會東魏遣軍送糧饋宜陽，法保潛邀之。
entries.en: When Eastern Wei sent a convoy to supply Yiyang with grain, Fabao ambushed it.
entries.literal: It happened that Eastern Wei sent troops escorting grain rations to Yiyang; Fabao secretly intercepted them.

entries.zh: 轉戰數十里，兵少不敵，為流矢所中，卒於陣。
entries.en: After fighting for dozens of li his outnumbered force was overwhelmed; struck by a stray arrow, he died on the battlefield.
entries.literal: Fighting over several tens of li, his troops were few and could not match the enemy; he was struck by a stray arrow and died on the field.

entries.zh: 諡曰莊。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous name Zhuang.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuang.

entries.zh: 子初嗣。
entries.en: His son Chu succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Chu succeeded.

entries.zh: 建德末，位至開府儀同大將軍、閻韓防主。
entries.en: By the end of the Jiande era he had risen to a baron's establishment with the rank of great general and served as defender of Yanhan.
entries.literal: At the end of the Jiande era he reached the office of Baron with an establishment equal to the Great General and Defender of Yanhan.

entries.zh: 時太祖在弘農，雄至上謁。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor was then at Hongnong; Xiong went to present himself before him.
entries.literal: At that time the Grand Ancestor was at Hongnong; Xiong went up to pay his respects.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉之，封武陽縣侯，邑八百戶。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor praised him and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuyang with a fief of eight hundred households.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor commended him and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuyang County with a fief of eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 遣雄還鄉里，更圖進取。
entries.en: He sent Xiong home to plan the next advance.
entries.literal: He sent Xiong back to his home district to plan further advances.

entries.zh: 雄乃招集義衆，進逼洛州。
entries.en: Xiong rallied loyal volunteers and advanced on Luo province.
entries.literal: Xiong then gathered loyalist volunteers and pressed upon Luo Province.

entries.zh: 東魏洛州刺史元湛委州奔河陽，其長史孟彥舉城款附。
entries.en: Yuan Zhan, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province, abandoned his post and fled to Heyang; his chief clerk Meng Yan surrendered the city.
entries.literal: Yuan Zhan, Governor of Luo Province of Eastern Wei, abandoned the province and fled to Heyang; his chief clerk Meng Yan raised the city in surrender.

entries.zh: 俄而領軍獨孤信大軍繼至，雄遂從信入洛陽。
entries.en: Soon the army commander Dugu Xin arrived with the main force, and Xiong entered Luoyang with him.
entries.literal: Before long the army commander Dugu Xin arrived with a great host; Xiong then followed Xin into Luoyang.

entries.zh: 時東魏將侯景等圍蓼塢，雄擊走之。
entries.en: When Eastern Wei generals including Hou Jing besieged Liaowu, Xiong attacked and drove them away.
entries.literal: At that time the Eastern Wei generals Hou Jing and others besieged Liaowu; Xiong struck and drove them off.

entries.zh: 又從太祖戰於河橋。
entries.en: He also fought under the Grand Ancestor at Heqiao.
entries.literal: He again followed the Grand Ancestor in battle at Heqiao.

entries.zh: 軍還，仍鎮洛西。
entries.en: After the army withdrew, he continued to hold the west of the Luo.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he still garrisoned the region west of Luo.

entries.zh: 拜假平東將軍、東郡守，遷北中郎將。
entries.en: He was made acting General Who Pacifies the East and administrator of Dong commandery, then promoted to North Palace Gate General.
entries.literal: He was appointed acting General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Dong Commandery, then promoted to General of the North Palace Gate.

entries.zh: 邙山之役，太祖命雄率衆邀齊神武於隘道。
entries.en: At Mount Mang the Grand Ancestor ordered Xiong to ambush Gao Huan in a defile.
entries.literal: In the battle of Mount Mang, the Grand Ancestor ordered Xiong to lead troops to intercept Gao Huan of Qi in a narrow pass.

entries.zh: 神武怒，命三軍併力取雄。
entries.en: Enraged, Gao Huan ordered all three armies to concentrate on capturing Xiong.
entries.literal: Gao Huan was enraged and ordered the three armies to combine their strength to take Xiong.

entries.zh: 雄突圍得免。
entries.en: Xiong broke out of the encirclement and escaped.
entries.literal: Xiong broke through the encirclement and escaped.

entries.zh: 除東徐州刺史。
entries.en: He was appointed governor of East Xu province.
entries.literal: He was appointed Governor of East Xu Province.

entries.zh: 太祖以雄劬勞積年，乃徵入朝，屢加賞勞。
entries.en: Because Xiong had served strenuously on the frontier for many years, the Grand Ancestor summoned him to court and rewarded him again and again.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Xiong had toiled with merit for many years, then summoned him to court and repeatedly rewarded and comforted him.

entries.zh: 復遣還州。
entries.en: He was then sent back to his province.
entries.literal: He was again sent back to his province.

entries.zh: 韓雄字木蘭，河南東垣人也。
entries.en: Han Xiong, whose courtesy name was Mulan, came from Dongyuan in Henan.
entries.literal: Han Xiong, courtesy name Mulan, was a native of Dongyuan in Henan.

entries.zh: 祖景，魏孝文時為赭陽郡守。
entries.en: His grandfather Jing served under Emperor Xiaowen of Wei as administrator of Zheyang commandery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Jing, in the time of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, was Administrator of Zheyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 李延孫 韋祐 韓雄 陳忻 魏玄
entries.en: Biographies of Li Yansun, Wei You, Han Xiong, Chen Xin, and Wei Xuan
entries.literal: Li Yansun; Wei You; Han Xiong; Chen Xin; Wei Xuan

entries.zh: 李棠 柳檜 杜叔毗 荊可 秦族 皇甫遐 張元
entries.en: Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shubi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, and Zhang Yuan
entries.literal: Li Tang, Liu Gui, Du Shubi, Jing Ke, Qin Zu, Huangfu Xia, Zhang Yuan

entries.zh: 張元字孝始，河北芮城人也。
entries.en: Zhang Yuan, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshi, was a native of Ruicheng in Hebei.
entries.literal: Zhang Yuan, courtesy name Xiaoshi, was a native of Ruicheng in Hebei.

entries.zh: 祖成，假平陽郡守。
entries.en: His grandfather Cheng served as Acting Administrator of Pingyang commandery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Acting Administrator of Pingyang commandery.

entries.zh: 父延雋，仕州郡，累為功曹、主簿。
entries.en: His father Yanjuan served in provinces and commanderies, repeatedly as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk.
entries.literal: His father Yanjuan served in provinces and commanderies, repeatedly as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 竝以純至，為鄉里所推。
entries.en: Both were pure and upright and were commended throughout their neighborhoods.
entries.literal: Both were pure and utmost and were commended by lanes and alleys.

entries.zh: 元性謙謹，有孝行。
entries.en: Yuan by nature was modest and cautious and had a record of filial conduct.
entries.literal: Yuan by nature was modest and cautious and had a record of filial conduct.

entries.zh: 微涉經史，然精脩釋典。
entries.en: He had some acquaintance with the classics and histories, yet devoted himself chiefly to Buddhist sutras.
entries.literal: He slightly touched on the classics and histories, yet diligently cultivated Buddhist sutras.

entries.zh: 年六歲，其祖以夏中熱甚，欲將元就井浴。
entries.en: At age six his grandfather, because the midsummer heat was fierce, wished to take Yuan to bathe at the well.
entries.literal: At age six his grandfather, because the midsummer heat was extreme, wished to take Yuan to bathe at the well.

entries.zh: 元固不肯從。
entries.en: Yuan firmly refused to go.
entries.literal: Yuan firmly refused to follow.

entries.zh: 祖謂其貪戲，乃以杖擊其頭曰：「汝何為不肯洗浴？」
entries.en: His grandfather thought him greedy for play and struck his head with a staff, saying, "Why will you not bathe?"
entries.literal: His grandfather said he was greedy for play and thereupon struck his head with a staff, saying, "Why do you refuse to bathe?"

entries.zh: 元對曰：「衣以蓋形，為覆其褻。
entries.en: Yuan replied, "Clothing covers the body in order to veil what is private.
entries.literal: Yuan replied, "Clothing covers the form in order to veil what is private.

entries.zh: 元不能褻露其體于白日之下。」
entries.en: Yuan cannot expose his private body beneath the open sky."
entries.literal: Yuan cannot expose his private body beneath the bright sun."

entries.zh: 祖異而舍之。
entries.en: His grandfather marveled and desisted.
entries.literal: His grandfather marveled and desisted.

entries.zh: 南鄰有二杏樹，杏熟，多落元園中。
entries.en: South of the neighborhood stood two apricot trees; when the apricots ripened many fell into Yuan's garden.
entries.literal: South of the neighborhood were two apricot trees; when the apricots ripened many fell into Yuan's garden.

entries.zh: 諸小兒競取而食之；
entries.en: The village children vied to take and eat them;
entries.literal: The small children vied to take and eat them;

entries.zh: 元所得者，送還其主。
entries.en: what Yuan gathered he returned to the owner.
entries.literal: what Yuan obtained he returned to the owner.

entries.zh: 村陌有狗子為人所棄者，元見，卽收而養之。
entries.en: In the lanes was a pup someone had abandoned; when Yuan saw it he at once took it in and reared it.
entries.literal: In the lanes and fields was a pup the people had abandoned; when Yuan saw it he at once gathered and reared it.

entries.zh: 其叔父怒曰：「何用此為？」
entries.en: His uncle was angry and said, "What use is this?"
entries.literal: His uncle was angry and said, "What use is this?"

entries.zh: 將欲更棄之。
entries.en: He was about to abandon it again.
entries.literal: He was about to abandon it again.

entries.zh: 元對曰：「有生之類，莫不重其性命。
entries.en: Yuan replied, "Among living creatures none fails to value its life.
entries.literal: Yuan replied, "Among living kinds none does not value its life.

entries.zh: 若天生天殺，自然之理。
entries.en: If Heaven gives birth and Heaven takes life, that is nature's way.
entries.literal: If Heaven gives birth and Heaven kills, that is nature's principle.

entries.zh: 今為人所棄而死，非其道也。
entries.en: Now to die because people cast one away is not the proper Way.
entries.literal: Now to die because people abandon one is not its proper Way.

entries.zh: 若見而不收養，無仁心也。
entries.en: If one sees it yet does not take it in, one lacks a humane heart.
entries.literal: If one sees it yet does not gather and rear it, one has no humane heart.

entries.zh: 是以收而養之。」
entries.en: That is why I take it in and rear it."
entries.literal: Therefore I gather and rear it."

entries.zh: 叔父感其言，遂許焉。
entries.en: His uncle was moved by his words and thereupon permitted it.
entries.literal: His uncle was moved by his words and thereupon permitted it.

entries.zh: 未幾，乃有狗母銜一死兔，置元前而去。
entries.en: Before long the mother dog brought a dead hare in her mouth, laid it before Yuan, and departed.
entries.literal: Before long a mother dog brought a dead hare in her mouth, placed it before Yuan, and departed.

entries.zh: 及元年十六，其祖喪明三年，元恒憂泣，晝夜讀佛經，禮拜以祈福佑。
entries.en: When Yuan reached sixteen his grandfather had been blind for three years; Yuan constantly grieved and wept, reading Buddhist sutras day and night and performing obeisance to seek divine protection.
entries.literal: When Yuan reached sixteen his grandfather was blind for three years; Yuan constantly grieved and wept, day and night reading Buddhist sutras and performing obeisance to seek blessing and protection.

entries.zh: 後讀《藥師經》，見盲者得視之言，遂請七僧，然七燈，七日七夜，轉《藥師經》行道。
entries.en: Later, reading the Medicine Master Sutra, he saw the passage that the blind may regain sight; he thereupon invited seven monks, lit seven lamps, and for seven days and seven nights performed ritual procession with the Medicine Master Sutra.
entries.literal: Later reading the Medicine Master Sutra, he saw the passage that the blind may gain sight; he thereupon invited seven monks, lit seven lamps, and for seven days and seven nights turned the Medicine Master Sutra in ritual procession.

entries.zh: 每言：「天人師乎！
entries.en: Each time he said, "Teacher of gods and men!
entries.literal: Each time he said, "Teacher of gods and men!

entries.zh: 元為孫不孝，使祖喪明。
entries.en: Yuan as grandson was unfilial and caused his grandfather to lose his sight.
entries.literal: Yuan as grandson was unfilial and caused grandfather to lose his sight.

entries.zh: 今以燈光普施法界，願祖目見明，元求代闇。」
entries.en: Now with lamp-light spread through the dharma-realm, I pray my grandfather's eyes may see clearly; let Yuan take the darkness in his place."
entries.literal: Now with lamp-light broadly bestowed on the dharma-realm, I pray grandfather's eyes may see clearly; Yuan asks to replace the darkness."

entries.zh: 如此經七日。
entries.en: He did thus for seven days.
entries.literal: He did thus for seven days.

entries.zh: 其夜，夢見一老公，以金鎞治其祖目。
entries.en: That night he dreamed of an old man who with a golden lancet treated his grandfather's eyes.
entries.literal: That night he dreamed of an old man who with a golden lancet treated his grandfather's eyes.

entries.zh: 謂元曰：「勿憂悲也，三日之後，汝祖目必差。」
entries.en: He said to Yuan, "Do not grieve; after three days your grandfather's eyes will surely recover."
entries.literal: He said to Yuan, "Do not grieve; after three days your grandfather's eyes will surely recover."

entries.zh: 元於夢中喜躍，遂卽驚覺，乃遍告家人。
entries.en: Yuan in the dream leaped for joy, then startled awake, and told the whole family.
entries.literal: Yuan in the dream leaped for joy, thereupon startled awake, and then told all the family.

entries.zh: 居三日，祖果目明。
entries.en: After three days his grandfather's eyes indeed became clear.
entries.literal: After three days his grandfather's eyes indeed became clear.

entries.zh: 其後祖臥疾再周，元恆隨祖所食多少，衣冠不解，旦夕扶侍。
entries.en: Afterward his grandfather lay ill for two full years; Yuan matched his grandfather's meals, never removed his cap and belt, and morning and evening supported and served him.
entries.literal: Afterward his grandfather lay ill for two cycles of the year; Yuan constantly matched what his grandfather ate in amount, did not remove cap and belt, and morning and evening supported and served him.

entries.zh: 及祖歿，號踴，絕而復蘇。
entries.en: When his grandfather died he wailed and stamped; he fainted and revived.
entries.literal: When his grandfather died he wailed and stamped; he fainted and revived.

entries.zh: 復喪其父，水漿不入口三日。
entries.en: He again mourned his father and did not take water or broth into his mouth for three days.
entries.literal: He again mourned his father and did not take water or broth into his mouth for three days.

entries.zh: 鄉里咸歎異之。
entries.en: Lanes and alleys all sighed and marveled at him.
entries.literal: Lanes and alleys all sighed and marveled at him.

entries.zh: 縣博士楊軌等二百餘人上其狀，有詔表其門閭。
entries.en: District Scholar Yang Gui and more than two hundred others submitted his record; an edict was issued to mark his gate and lane.
entries.literal: District Scholar Yang Gui and more than two hundred others submitted his record; an edict was issued to mark his gate and lane.

entries.zh: 夫塞天地而橫四海者，其唯孝乎；
entries.en: What fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas—is it not filial piety alone?
entries.literal: As for what fills Heaven and Earth and spans the four seas—is it not filial piety alone?

entries.zh: 奉大功而立顯名者，其唯義乎。
entries.en: What sustains great merit and wins illustrious fame—is it not righteousness alone?
entries.literal: As for what upholds great merit and establishes illustrious fame—is it not righteousness alone?

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why is this so?
entries.literal: Why is this so?

entries.zh: 孝始事親，惟后資於致治；
entries.en: Filial piety begins with serving one's parents; only from that foundation can one contribute to good government.
entries.literal: Filial piety begins in serving one's parents; only thereafter does one draw on it to bring order to governance.

entries.zh: 義在合宜，惟人賴以成德。
entries.en: Righteousness lies in doing what is fitting; only through it do people complete their moral character.
entries.literal: Righteousness lies in doing what is fitting; only thereby do people rely on it to complete their virtue.

entries.zh: 上智稟自然之性，中庸有企及之美。
entries.en: The highest minds are born with nature's gifts; those of the middle path have virtues one may still aspire to attain.
entries.literal: Men of highest wisdom are endowed with nature's innate quality; men of the middle way have beauty one may strive to reach.

entries.zh: 其大也，則隆家光國，盛烈與河海爭流；
entries.en: At its greatest, it elevates the family and brings glory to the state, its splendid deeds flowing like rivers and seas;
entries.literal: In its grand scale, it exalts the family and glorifies the state, its splendid achievements contending in flow with rivers and seas;

entries.zh: 授命滅親，峻節與竹
entries.en: or accepting a charge that severs one's kin—integrity as unyielding as bamboo
entries.literal: accepting orders that destroy kin ties, stern integrity like bamboo

entries.en: Per the silk manuscript, cypress is read in place of bamboo
entries.literal: silk manuscript

entries.zh: 栢俱茂。
entries.en: and cypress—flourishing together without fail.
entries.literal: cypress flourishing together.

entries.zh: 其小也，則溫枕扇席，無替於晨昏；
entries.en: At its smallest, warming the pillow and fanning the mat, never slackening from dawn to dusk;
entries.literal: In its small scale, warming the pillow and fanning the mat, never failing from dawn to dusk;

entries.zh: 損己利物，有助於名教。
entries.en: sacrificing oneself to benefit others, strengthening the norms of moral teaching.
entries.literal: harming oneself to benefit others, aiding the norms of moral teaching.

entries.zh: 是以堯舜湯武居帝王之位，垂至德以敦其風；
entries.en: That is why Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu sat as emperors and kings, extending supreme virtue to deepen the customs of their age;
entries.literal: Therefore Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu occupied the throne of emperors and kings, extending supreme virtue to deepen their people's customs;

entries.zh: 孔墨荀孟稟聖賢之資，弘正道以勵其俗。
entries.en: while Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius bore the endowment of sages and spread the true Way to stir their contemporaries.
entries.literal: Confucius, Mozi, Xunzi, and Mencius received the endowment of sages, spreading the correct Way to encourage their age.

entries.zh: 觀其所由，在此而已矣。
entries.en: When one traces what they built upon, the source lies here and nowhere else.
entries.literal: Observing what they proceeded from, it is in this alone.

entries.zh: 李棠字長卿，勃海蓨人也。
entries.en: Li Tang, whose courtesy name was Changqing, came from Tiao in Bohai commandery.
entries.literal: Li Tang, courtesy name Changqing, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.

entries.zh: 祖伯貴，魏宣武時官至魯郡守。
entries.en: His grandfather Bo Gui had served in the reign of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei and risen to Administrator of Lu commandery.
entries.literal: His grandfather Bo Gui, in the time of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei, reached office as Administrator of Lu commandery.

entries.zh: 有孝行，居父喪，哀戚過禮，遂以毀卒。
entries.en: He was known for filial conduct; while mourning his father, his grief exceeded what the rites allowed, and he died from the damage to his health.
entries.literal: He had a record of filial conduct; while in mourning for his father, his grief exceeded the rites, and he therefore died from the damage to his person.

entries.zh: 宣武嘉之，贈勃海相。
