entries.en: Emperor Xuanwu commended him and posthumously enfeoffed him as Chancellor of Bohai.
entries.literal: Xuanwu commended him and posthumously enfeoffed him as Chancellor of Bohai.

entries.zh: 父元冑，員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: His father Yuan Zhou held the post of Outer Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: His father Yuan Zhou was an Outer Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 棠幼孤，好學，有志操。
entries.en: Tang lost his father while still young, loved learning, and possessed firm resolve and integrity.
entries.literal: Tang was orphaned young, loved learning, and had resolve and integrity.

entries.zh: 年十七，屬爾朱之亂，與司空高乾兄弟，舉兵信都。
entries.en: At seventeen, amid the turmoil of the Erzhu clan, he joined the Minister of Works Gao Gan and his brothers in raising troops at Xindu.
entries.literal: At age seventeen, during the turmoil of the Erzhu clan, together with the Minister of Works Gao Gan and his brothers, he raised troops at Xindu.

entries.zh: 魏中興初，辟衛軍府功曹參軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Wei's Zhongxing restoration, he was summoned to serve as Registrar in the Guard Army headquarters.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongxing restoration in Wei, he was summoned as Registrar in the Guard Army headquarters.

entries.zh: 太昌中，以軍功除征虜將軍，行東萊郡事。
entries.en: In the Taichang era, he was made General Who Punishes Barbarians on account of military merit and acted as Administrator of Donglai commandery.
entries.literal: In the Taichang era, by military merit he was made General Who Punishes Barbarians and acted as Administrator of Donglai commandery.

entries.zh: 魏孝武西遷，棠時在凹北，遂仕東魏。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved the court west, Tang was in the region north of Ye and therefore entered the service of Eastern Wei.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Tang was then in the north of Ye and therefore entered the service of Eastern Wei.

entries.zh: 及高仲密為北豫州刺史，請棠為掾。
entries.en: When Gao Zhongmi became Governor of North Yuzhou, he asked Tang to serve as his aide.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhongmi became Governor of North Yuzhou, he requested Tang as his aide.

entries.zh: 先是，仲密與吏部郎中崔暹有隙。
entries.en: Earlier, Zhongmi had fallen out with Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhongmi had a rift with Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 暹時被齊文襄委任，仲密恐其構己，每不自安，將圖來附。
entries.en: Xian was then entrusted with authority by Prince Wenxiang of Qi, and Zhongmi feared he would plot against him; uneasy at every turn, he planned to defect and surrender.
entries.literal: Xuan was then entrusted by Qi Prince Wenxiang, and Zhongmi feared he would frame him; he was constantly ill at ease and planned to come over in surrender.

entries.zh: 時東魏又遣鎮城奚壽興典兵事，仲密但知民務而已。
entries.en: Eastern Wei had also sent Xi Shouxing to garrison the city and oversee military affairs, while Zhongmi handled only civil administration.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei had also sent Xi Shouxing to garrison the city and oversee military affairs, while Zhongmi knew only civil administration.

entries.zh: 旣至州，遂與棠謀執壽興以成其計。
entries.en: Once he reached the province, he at once plotted with Tang to seize Shouxing and carry out his design.
entries.literal: Once he reached the province, he thereupon plotted with Tang to seize Shouxing and carry out his design.

entries.zh: 仲密乃置酒延壽興，陰伏壯士，欲因此執之。
entries.en: Zhongmi then set out wine to invite Shouxing, with stalwart men hidden nearby, intending to seize him at the feast.
entries.literal: Zhongmi then set out wine to invite Shouxing, with stalwart men hidden in secret, intending thereby to seize him.

entries.zh: 壽興辭而不赴。
entries.en: Shouxing declined and did not attend.
entries.literal: Shouxing declined and did not attend.

entries.zh: 棠遂往見之曰：「君與高公，義符昆季。
entries.en: Tang then went to see him and said, "You and Lord Gao are joined in righteousness like brothers.
entries.literal: Tang then went to see him and said, "You and Lord Gao are bound in righteousness like brothers.

entries.zh: 今日之席，以公為首。
entries.en: Today's banquet is held with you as the guest of honor.
entries.literal: Today's banquet takes you as its chief guest.

entries.zh: 豈有賓客總萃，而公無事不行？
entries.en: How can all the guests be assembled while you, the chief guest, stay away without cause?
entries.literal: How can all the guests be gathered while you, the chief, do nothing and stay away?

entries.zh: 將恐遠近聞之，竊有疑怪。」
entries.en: I fear that when word spreads far and near, people will privately wonder at it."
entries.literal: I fear that if distant and near hear of it, they will privately harbor doubts."

entries.zh: 壽興遂與俱赴，便發伏執之。
entries.en: Shouxing then went with him, and the hidden men at once seized him.
entries.literal: Shouxing then went together with him, and the hidden men at once seized him.

entries.zh: 乃帥其士衆據城，遣棠詣闕歸款。
entries.en: He then led his troops to hold the city and sent Tang to the capital to offer surrender.
entries.literal: He then led his troops to hold the city and sent Tang to the capital to offer surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉之，拜棠衛將軍、右光祿大夫，封廣宗縣公，邑一千戶。
entries.en: The Grand Progenitor commended him and appointed Tang General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffing him as Duke of Guangzong with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended him and appointed Tang General of the Guard, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Guangzong with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 棠固辭曰：「臣世荷朝恩，義當奉國。
entries.en: Tang firmly declined, saying, "My family has received the dynasty's grace for generations; in righteousness I ought to serve the state.
entries.literal: Tang firmly declined, saying, "Your servant's family has received the dynasty's grace for generations; in righteousness I ought to serve the state.

entries.zh: 而往者見拘逆命，不獲陪駕西巡。
entries.en: Yet formerly I was held back against my will and could not accompany the court on its move west.
entries.literal: Yet formerly I was detained against my will and could not accompany the imperial tour west.

entries.zh: 今日之來，免罪為幸，何敢以此微庸，冒受天爵。」
entries.en: To come today and be spared punishment is already my good fortune; how dare I, for this slight service, presumptuously accept a heavenly rank?"
entries.literal: To come today and be spared punishment is already good fortune; how dare I, for this slight merit, presumptuously receive a heavenly rank?"

entries.zh: 如此者再三，優詔不許。
entries.en: He spoke thus again and again, but gracious edicts would not allow it.
entries.literal: He spoke thus again and again, but gracious edicts would not permit it.

entries.zh: 俄遷給事黃門侍郎，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with the additional titles of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with additional titles of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 斌弟雄亮，字信誠。
entries.en: Bin's younger brother Xiongliang, whose courtesy name was Xincheng.
entries.literal: Bin's younger brother Xiongliang, courtesy name Xincheng.

entries.zh: 幼有志節，好學不倦。
entries.en: From youth he had resolve and integrity and loved learning without tiring.
entries.literal: From youth he had resolve and integrity and loved learning without tiring.

entries.zh: 年十二，遭父艱，幾至滅性。
entries.en: At twelve he encountered his father's mourning and nearly destroyed himself with grief.
entries.literal: At twelve he encountered his father's mourning and nearly destroyed his nature.

entries.zh: 終喪之後，志在復讎。
entries.en: After mourning ended, his purpose was set on taking revenge.
entries.literal: After mourning ended, his purpose was set on taking revenge.

entries.zh: 柱國、蔡國公廣欽其名行，引為記室參軍。
entries.en: Pillar of State and Duke of Cai Guang admired his reputation and conduct and brought him in as Recorder in the headquarters.
entries.literal: Pillar of State and Duke of Cai Guang admired his reputation and conduct and brought him in as Recorder in the headquarters.

entries.zh: 年始弱冠，府中文筆，頗亦委之。
entries.en: He had just reached the capping age; the literary work of the headquarters was also largely entrusted to him.
entries.literal: He had just reached the capping age; the literary work of the headquarters was also largely entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 後竟手刃衆寶於京城。
entries.en: Later he at last slew Zhongbao with his own hand in the capital.
entries.literal: Later he at last with his own hand slew Zhongbao in the capital.

entries.zh: 朝野咸重其志節，高祖特恕之。
entries.en: Court and countryside all respected his resolve and integrity; Emperor Gaozu especially pardoned him.
entries.literal: Court and countryside all respected his resolve and integrity; Emperor Gaozu especially pardoned him.

entries.zh: 由是知名。
entries.en: From this he became known.
entries.literal: From this he became known.

entries.zh: 大象末，位至賓部下大夫。
entries.en: At the end of the Daxiang era he reached the post of Attendant Grand Master of the Guests.
entries.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he reached the post of Attendant Grand Master of the Guests.

entries.zh: 尋拜都督、輔國將軍、中散大夫。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief, General Who Assists the State, and Palace Counsel Grand Master.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief, General Who Assists the State, and Palace Counsel Grand Master.

entries.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀骨立，殆不勝喪。
entries.en: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief wasted him until only bone remained standing, and he nearly could not survive the mourning.
entries.literal: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief wasted him until only bone remained standing, and he nearly could not survive the mourning.

entries.zh: 服闋，晉公護辟為中外府樂曹參軍，加授大都督，遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，行義歸郡守。
entries.en: When mourning ended, Duke of Jin Hu summoned him as Music Bureau Attendant in the Inner and Outer headquarters, with additional appointment as Commander-in-Chief; he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Acting Administrator of Yigui commandery.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, Duke of Jin Hu summoned him as Music Bureau Attendant in the Inner and Outer headquarters, with additional appointment as Commander-in-Chief; he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pillar of State of the Third Rank, and Acting Administrator of Yigui commandery.

entries.zh: 自君錫及宗室等為曹策所害，猶殯梁州，至是表請迎喪歸葬。
entries.en: Since Junxi and the clansmen had been harmed by Cao Ce, their coffins still lay in Liangzhou; at this time he memorialized requesting to bring the coffins home for burial.
entries.literal: Since Junxi and the clansmen had been harmed by Cao Ce, their coffins still lay in Liangzhou; at this time he memorialized requesting to bring the coffins home for burial.

entries.zh: 高祖許之，葬事所須，詔令官給。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu granted it; what the funeral required was ordered supplied by the officials.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu granted it; what the funeral required was ordered supplied by the officials.

entries.zh: 在梁舊田宅經外配者，竝追還之，仍賜田二百頃。
entries.en: Former fields and residences in Liang that had been allotted to others were all recovered and returned, and two hundred qing of fields were additionally granted.
entries.literal: Former fields and residences in Liang that had been allotted to others were all recovered and returned, and two hundred qing of fields were additionally granted.

entries.zh: 尋除硤州刺史。
entries.en: Before long he was made Governor of Xiazhou.
entries.literal: Before long he was made Governor of Xiazhou.

entries.zh: 杜叔毗字子弼。
entries.en: Du Shubi, whose courtesy name was Zibi.
entries.literal: Du Shubi, courtesy name Zibi.

entries.zh: 其先，京兆杜陵人也，徙居襄陽。
entries.en: His ancestors were natives of Duling in Jingzhao and had moved to settle in Xiangyang.
entries.literal: His ancestors were natives of Duling in Jingzhao and moved to settle in Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 祖乾光，齊司徒右長史。
entries.en: His grandfather Qian'guang was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Qi.
entries.literal: His grandfather Qian'guang was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Qi.

entries.zh: 父漸，梁邊城太守。
entries.en: His father Jian was Border City Administrator under Liang.
entries.literal: His father Jian was Border City Administrator under Liang.

entries.zh: 叔毗早歲而孤，事母以孝聞。
entries.en: Shubi lost his father while still young and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.
entries.literal: Shubi lost his father while still young and served his mother with a reputation for filial piety.

entries.zh: 性慷慨有志節。
entries.en: By nature he was generous and had resolve and integrity.
entries.literal: By nature he was generous and had resolve and integrity.

entries.zh: 勵精好學，尤善《左氏春秋》。
entries.en: He strove in spirit and loved learning, especially excelling in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
entries.literal: He strove in spirit and loved learning, especially excelling in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.

entries.zh: 仕梁，為宜豐侯蕭循府中直兵參軍。
entries.en: He served Liang as Direct Troops Attendant in the headquarters of Marquis Yifeng Xiao Xun.
entries.literal: He served Liang as Direct Troops Attendant in the headquarters of Marquis Yifeng Xiao Xun.

entries.zh: 大統十七年，太祖令大將軍達奚武經畧漢州。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year of Datong, the Grand Progenitor ordered Grand General Daxi Wu to campaign in Hanzhou.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year of Datong, the Grand Progenitor ordered Grand General Daxi Wu to campaign in Hanzhou.

entries.zh: 明年，武圍循於南鄭。
entries.en: The next year Wu besieged Xun at Nanzheng.
entries.literal: The next year Wu besieged Xun at Nanzheng.

entries.zh: 循令叔毗詣闕請和。
entries.en: Xun ordered Shubi to go to the capital to sue for peace.
entries.literal: Xun ordered Shubi to go to the capital to sue for peace.

entries.zh: 太祖見而禮之。
entries.en: The Grand Progenitor saw him and treated him with courtesy.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw him and treated him with courtesy.

entries.zh: 使未反，而循中直兵參軍曹策、參軍劉曉謀以城降武。
entries.en: The envoy had not yet returned when Xun's Direct Troops Attendant Cao Ce and Attendant Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.
entries.literal: The envoy had not yet returned when Xun's Direct Troops Attendant Cao Ce and Attendant Liu Xiao plotted to surrender the city to Wu.

entries.zh: 時叔毗兄君錫為循中記室參軍，從子映錄事參軍，映弟晰中直兵參軍，竝有文武材畧，各領部曲數百人。
entries.en: At the time Shubi's elder brother Junxi was Recorder in Xun's headquarters, his nephew Ying was Recording Attendant, and Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Attendant—all had civil and military talent, each leading several hundred men in their retinues.
entries.literal: At the time Shubi's elder brother Junxi was Recorder in Xun's headquarters, his nephew Ying was Recording Attendant, and Ying's younger brother Xi was Direct Troops Attendant—all had civil and military talent and strategy, each leading several hundred men in their retinues.

entries.zh: 策等忌之，懼不同己，遂誣以謀叛，擅加害焉。
entries.en: Ce and the rest envied them, fearing they would not join them, and therefore falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and killed them on their own authority.
entries.literal: Ce and the rest envied them, fearing they would not agree with themselves, and therefore falsely accused them of plotting rebellion and on their own authority harmed them.

entries.zh: 循尋討策等，擒之，斬曉而免策。
entries.en: Xun soon investigated Ce and the rest, seized them, executed Xiao and spared Ce.
entries.literal: Xun soon investigated Ce and the rest, seized them, executed Xiao and spared Ce.

entries.zh: 及循降，策至長安。
entries.en: When Xun surrendered, Ce came to Chang'an.
entries.literal: When Xun surrendered, Ce came to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 叔毗朝夕號泣，具申冤狀。
entries.en: Shubi wept morning and evening, fully stating the facts of the injustice.
entries.literal: Shubi wept morning and evening, fully stating the facts of the injustice.

entries.zh: 朝議以事在歸附之前，不可追罪。
entries.en: Court discussion held that the matter occurred before submission and surrender, and punishment could not be pursued.
entries.literal: Court discussion held that the matter occurred before submission and surrender, and punishment could not be pursued.

entries.zh: 叔毗內懷憤惋，志在復讎。
entries.en: Shubi harbored resentment within and set his purpose on revenge.
entries.literal: Shubi harbored resentment within and set his purpose on revenge.

entries.zh: 然恐違朝憲，坐及其母，遂沉吟積時。
entries.en: Yet he feared violating court law and implicating his mother, and therefore hesitated for a long time.
entries.literal: Yet he feared violating court law and implicating his mother, and therefore hesitated for a long time.

entries.zh: 母知其意，謂叔毗曰：「汝兄橫罹禍酷，痛切骨髓。
entries.en: His mother knew his intent and said to Shubi, "Your brother suffered cruel calamity by violence; the pain cuts to the marrow.
entries.literal: His mother knew his intent and said to Shubi, "Your brother suffered cruel calamity by violence; the pain cuts to the marrow.

entries.zh: 若曹策朝死，吾以夕歿，亦所甘心。
entries.en: If Cao Ce dies in the morning, I shall die in the evening—that too I would accept with a willing heart.
entries.literal: If Cao Ce dies in the morning, I shall die in the evening—that too I would accept with a willing heart.

entries.zh: 汝何疑焉。」
entries.en: What doubt do you have?"
entries.literal: What doubt do you have?"

entries.zh: 叔毗拜受母言，愈更感勵。
entries.en: Shubi bowed and received his mother's words and was all the more stirred and encouraged.
entries.literal: Shubi bowed and received his mother's words and was all the more stirred and encouraged.

entries.zh: 後遂白日手刃策於京城，斷首刳腹，解其肢體。
entries.en: Later he therefore in broad daylight slew Ce with his own hand in the capital, cut off his head, disemboweled him, and dismembered his limbs.
entries.literal: Later he therefore in broad daylight with his own hand slew Ce in the capital, cut off his head, disemboweled him, and dismembered his limbs.

entries.zh: 然後面縛，請就戮焉。
entries.en: He then bound himself and asked to undergo execution.
entries.literal: He then bound himself and asked to undergo execution.

entries.zh: 太祖嘉其志氣，特命赦之。
entries.en: The Grand Progenitor commended his spirit and resolve and specially ordered him pardoned.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor commended his spirit and resolve and specially ordered him pardoned.

entries.zh: 榮先亦至孝。
entries.en: Rongxian was also utmost in filial piety.
entries.literal: Rongxian was also utmost in filial piety.

entries.zh: 遭母喪，哀慕不已，遂以毀卒。
entries.en: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief and longing did not cease, and he therefore died from the damage to his person.
entries.literal: He encountered his mother's mourning; his grief and longing did not cease, and he therefore died from the damage to his person.

entries.zh: 邑裏化其孝行。
entries.en: The district was transformed by his filial conduct.
entries.literal: The district was transformed by his filial conduct.

entries.zh: 世宗嘉之，乃下詔曰：「孝為政本，德乃化先，旣表天經，又明地義。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong commended him and thereupon issued an edict saying, "Filial piety is the root of government; virtue is what transforms first—it displays the heavenly norm and clarifies earthly righteousness.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong commended him and thereupon issued an edict saying, "Filial piety is the root of government; virtue is what transforms first—it displays the heavenly norm and clarifies earthly righteousness.

entries.zh: 榮先居喪致疾，至感過人，窮號不反，迄乎滅性。
entries.en: Rongxian in mourning brought on illness; his utmost feeling surpassed other men; his exhausted wailing did not return until he destroyed his nature.
entries.literal: Rongxian in mourning brought on illness; his utmost feeling surpassed other men; his exhausted wailing did not return until he destroyed his nature.

entries.zh: 行標當世，理鏡幽明。
entries.en: His conduct marks the age; his principle mirrors the hidden and manifest.
entries.literal: His conduct marks the age; his principle mirrors the hidden and manifest.

entries.zh: 此而不顯，道將何述。
entries.en: If this is not displayed, by what means will the Way be transmitted?
entries.literal: If this is not displayed, by what means will the Way be transmitted?

entries.zh: 可贈滄州刺史，以旌厥異。」
entries.en: He may be posthumously made Governor of Cangzhou to signal this exceptional merit."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Governor of Cangzhou to signal this exceptional merit."

entries.zh: 史臣曰：李棠、柳檜竝臨危不撓，視死如歸，其壯志貞情可與青松白玉比質也。
entries.en: The historiographer says: Li Tang and Liu Gui alike faced peril without bending and viewed death as returning home; their stalwart will and steadfast feeling may be compared in quality to green pine and white jade.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Li Tang and Liu Gui alike, facing peril, did not bend and viewed death as returning home; their stalwart will and chaste feeling may be compared in quality to green pine and white jade.

entries.zh: 然檜恩隆加等，棠禮闕飾終，有周之政，於是乎偏矣。
entries.en: Yet Gui received favor raised a grade while Tang's rites lacked full adornment at the end—in Northern Zhou governance, partiality showed here.
entries.literal: Yet Gui received favor raised a grade while Tang's rites lacked adornment at the end—Northern Zhou government was thereby partial.

entries.zh: 雄亮銜戴天之痛，叔毗切同氣之悲，援白刃而不顧，雪家冤於輦轂。
entries.en: Xiongliang bore heaven's covering as a debt of vengeance; Shubi felt the grief of shared breath with kin; they drew white blades without flinching and cleared family wrongs at the imperial capital.
entries.literal: Xiongliang bore the pain of heaven's covering; Shubi felt the grief of shared breath; they drew white blades without regard and cleared family wrongs at the imperial carriage hub.

entries.zh: 觀其志節，處死固為易也。
entries.en: Observing their resolve and integrity, to face death was indeed the easier course.
entries.literal: Observing their resolve and integrity, to face death was indeed easy.

entries.zh: 荊可、秦族之徒，生自隴畝，曾無師資之訓，因心而成孝友，乘理而蹈禮節。
entries.en: Jing Ke, Qin Zu, and their kind were born from fields and furrows without formal instruction; following the heart they achieved filial piety and brotherhood, riding principle they walked the path of rites.
entries.literal: Jing Ke, Qin Zu, and their kind were born from fields and furrows, never having teachers' instruction; following the heart they completed filial piety and brotherhood, riding principle they trod rites and propriety.

entries.zh: 如使舉世若茲，則羲、農何遠之有。
entries.en: If all the world were thus, how distant would Fu Xi and Shen Nong seem?
entries.literal: If all the world were thus, how far could Fu Xi and Shen Nong be?

entries.zh: 若乃誠感天地，孝通神明，見之於張元矣。
entries.en: As for sincerity that moves Heaven and Earth and filial piety that reaches the spirits—this is seen in Zhang Yuan.
entries.literal: As for sincerity moving Heaven and Earth and filial piety penetrating the spirits—this is seen in Zhang Yuan.

entries.zh: 天和元年，詔開府陸騰督王亮、司馬裔等討之。
entries.en: In the first year of  Lu Teng was ordered to command Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others against them.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, an edict ordered Opening Office Lu Teng to supervise Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others in the campaign.

entries.zh: 騰水陸俱進，次于湯口，先遣喻之。
entries.en: Lu Teng advanced by land and water to Tangkou and first sent envoys to warn them.
entries.literal: Teng advanced by land and water together and halted at Tangkou, first sending envoys to admonish them.

entries.zh: 而令賢方增浚城池，嚴設扞禦。
entries.en: Meanwhile Lingxian deepened walls and strengthened defenses.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Lingxian was deepening moats and walls and setting stern defenses.

entries.zh: 遣其長子西黎、次子南王領其支屬，於江南險要之地置立十城，遠結涔陽蠻為其聲援。
entries.en: He sent sons Xili and the Southern King to ten strongpoints in the south, allying with the Cenyang Man.
entries.literal: He sent his eldest son Xili and second son the Southern King with their dependents to ten fortified places on the Jiang south's strategic heights, linking far with the Cenyang Man as their support.

entries.zh: 令賢率其精卒，固守水邏城。
entries.en: Lingxian held Shuilo with his elite troops.
entries.literal: Lingxian himself led his picked troops and held fast at Shuilo Fortress.

entries.zh: 騰乃總集將帥，謀其進趣。
entries.en: Lu Teng gathered his officers to plan the advance.
entries.literal: Teng then gathered the generals to plan the advance.

entries.zh: 咸欲先取水邏，然後經畧江南。
entries.en: All favored taking Shuilo first, then the south bank.
entries.literal: All wished first to take Shuilo and then deal with the Jiang south.

entries.zh: 騰言於衆曰：「令賢內恃水邏金湯之險，外托涔陽輔車之援，兼復資糧充實，器械精新。
entries.en: Lu Teng told them: "Lingxian trusts Shuilo's defenses and Cenyang's aid, with full stores and fresh arms.
entries.literal: Teng said to the assembly: "Lingxian relies within on Shuilo's golden moat and without on Cenyang's chariot-pole support, and moreover his provisions are full and weapons new and fine.

entries.zh: 以我懸軍攻其嚴壘，脫一戰不剋，更成其氣。
entries.en: If our isolated force assaults his fortress and fails once, his morale will rise.
entries.literal: If we as a suspended army attack his strong fortress and by chance one battle fails, his spirit will only grow.

entries.zh: 不如頓軍湯口，先取江南，剪其羽毛，然後進軍水邏。
entries.en: Better to hold at Tangkou, take the south bank first, clip his wings, then strike Shuilo.
entries.literal: Better to halt the army at Tangkou, first take the Jiang south, cut his feathers, and then advance on Shuilo.

entries.zh: 此制勝之計也。」
entries.en: That is how we win."
entries.literal: This is the plan for certain victory."

entries.zh: 衆皆然之。
entries.en: All agreed.
entries.literal: The multitude all approved.

entries.zh: 乃遣開府王亮率衆渡江，旬日攻拔其八城，凶黨奔散。
entries.en: Wang Liang crossed the river and in ten days took eight forts; the rebels fled.
entries.literal: He then sent Opening Office Wang Liang with troops across the river; in ten days they stormed eight fortresses and the rebels scattered.

entries.zh: 獲賊帥冉承公幷生口三千人，降其部衆一千戶。
entries.en: They took Ran Chenggong and three thousand captives and accepted a thousand households in surrender.
entries.literal: They captured the bandit leader Ran Chenggong together with three thousand captives and received the submission of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 遂簡募驍勇，數道入攻水邏。
entries.en: They then picked elite troops and assaulted Shuilo on several routes.
entries.literal: Then they selected fierce warriors and attacked Shuilo by several routes.

entries.zh: 路經石壁城。
entries.en: The march passed Shibi Fortress.
entries.literal: The route passed Shibi Fortress.

entries.zh: 此城峻嶮，四面壁立，故以名焉。
entries.en: The fortress was sheer, walled on every side, hence its name.
entries.literal: This fortress was steep and perilous, with walls standing on all four sides—hence the name.

entries.zh: 唯有一小路，緣梯而上。
entries.en: Only one path climbed by ladder.
entries.literal: There was only one narrow path, climbing by ladder.

entries.zh: 蠻蜑以為峭絕，非兵衆所行。
entries.en: The Man thought it impassable for an army.
entries.literal: The Man and boat peoples thought it too sheer for troops to pass.

entries.zh: 騰被甲先登，衆軍繼進，備經危阻，累月乃得舊路。
entries.en: Lu Teng armored himself and led the climb; the army followed through months of peril.
entries.literal: Teng donned armor and climbed first; the army followed, enduring repeated dangers, and only after months regained the old route.

entries.zh: 且騰先任隆州總管，雅知蠻帥冉伯犁、冉安西與令賢有隙。
entries.en: Lu Teng, former Longzhou commander, knew the Man chiefs Ran Boli and Ran Anxi hated Lingxian.
entries.literal: Moreover Teng had earlier served as Commander of Long Prefecture and knew well that the Man leaders Ran Boli and Ran Anxi were at odds with Lingxian.

entries.zh: 騰乃招誘伯犁等，結為父子，又多遺其金帛。
entries.en: He won over Boli with gifts and sworn brotherhood.
entries.literal: Teng then enticed Boli and others, binding them as sworn kin, and also sent them much gold and silk.

entries.zh: 伯犁等悅，遂為鄉導。
entries.en: Boli gladly guided the army.
entries.literal: Boli and the others were pleased and then served as local guides.

entries.zh: 水邏側又有石勝城者，亦是險要。
entries.en: Near Shuilo stood Shisheng Fortress, also a strongpoint.
entries.literal: Beside Shuilo there was also Shisheng Fortress, likewise strategic.

entries.zh: 令賢使兄子龍真據之。
entries.en: Lingxian put his nephew Long Zhen there.
entries.literal: Lingxian sent his elder brother's son Long Zhen to hold it.

entries.zh: 騰又密誘龍真云，若平水邏，使其代令賢處。
entries.en: Lu Teng secretly promised Long Zhen Lingxian's place if Shuilo fell.
entries.literal: Teng also secretly enticed Long Zhen, saying that if Shuilo were pacified he would place him in Lingxian's seat.

entries.zh: 龍真大悅，密遣其子詣騰。
entries.en: Long Zhen sent his son to Lu Teng in secret.
entries.literal: Long Zhen was greatly pleased and secretly sent his son to Teng.

entries.zh: 騰乃厚加禮接，賜以金帛。
entries.en: Lu Teng received him with honor and gifts of gold and silk.
entries.literal: Teng then treated him with generous courtesy and bestowed gold and silk.

entries.zh: 蠻貪利旣深，仍請立效。
entries.en: Greedy for the bounty, the Man asked to prove their loyalty in battle.
entries.literal: The Man, their greed for profit now deep, still asked to pledge achievement.

entries.zh: 乃謂騰曰：「欲翻所據城，恐人力寡少。」
entries.en: He told Lu Teng: "I want to turn the fortress I hold, but I lack men."
entries.literal: He then said to Teng: "I wish to turn the fortress I hold, but fear my manpower is too few."

entries.zh: 騰許以三百兵助之。
entries.en: Lu Teng promised three hundred men to help.
entries.literal: Teng promised three hundred troops to assist him.

entries.zh: 旣而遣二千人銜枚夜進。
entries.en: Then he sent two thousand men with gags in their mouths by night.
entries.literal: Presently he sent two thousand men with gags in their mouths advancing by night.

entries.zh: 龍真力不能禦，遂平石勝城。
entries.en: Long Zhen could not hold out and Shisheng fell.
entries.literal: Long Zhen's strength could not resist, and Shisheng Fortress was pacified.

entries.zh: 晨至水邏，蠻衆大潰，斬首萬餘級，虜獲一萬口。
entries.en: By dawn they reached Shuilo; the Man army collapsed with more than ten thousand killed and ten thousand taken.
entries.literal: At dawn they reached Shuilo; the Man masses broke in great rout, more than ten thousand heads cut off and ten thousand mouths captured.

entries.zh: 令賢遁走，追而獲之，幷其子弟等皆斬之。
entries.en: Lingxian fled, was caught, and was executed with his sons and kin.
entries.literal: Lingxian fled; pursued and captured, together with his sons and younger kin all were beheaded.

entries.zh: 司馬裔又別下其二十餘城，獲蠻帥冉三公等。
entries.en: Sima Yi took twenty-odd cities and captured the Man chief Ran Sangong.
entries.literal: Sima Yi separately reduced more than twenty of their cities and captured the Man leader Ran Sangong and others.

entries.zh: 騰乃積其骸骨於水邏城側，為京觀。
entries.en: Lu Teng piled their bones beside Shuilo as a victory mound.
entries.literal: Teng then heaped their bones beside Shuilo Fortress as a skull mound.

entries.zh: 後蠻蜑望見，輒大號哭。
entries.en: When the Man saw the mound they wailed aloud.
entries.literal: Later when the Man and boat peoples saw it, they would wail loudly.

entries.zh: 自此狼戾之心輟矣。
entries.en: After that their fierce spirit broke.
entries.literal: From this their fierce hearts were stilled.

entries.zh: 時向五子王據石默城，令其子寶勝據雙城。
entries.en: Xiang the Fifth Son King held Shimo and sent his son Baosheng to hold Shuang.
entries.literal: At that time Xiang the Fifth Son King held Shimo Fortress and ordered his son Baosheng to hold Shuang Fortress.

entries.zh: 水邏平後，頻遣喻之，而五子王猶不從命。
entries.en: After Shuilo fell Lu Teng warned them repeatedly, but the Fifth Son King refused.
entries.literal: After Shuilo was pacified he repeatedly sent envoys to admonish them, yet the Fifth Son King still did not obey.

entries.zh: 騰又遣王亮屯牢坪，司馬裔屯雙城以圖之。
entries.en: Lu Teng sent Wang Liang to Laoping and Sima Yi to Shuang to besiege them.
entries.literal: Teng again sent Wang Liang to encamp at Laoping and Sima Yi to encamp at Shuang to besiege them.

entries.zh: 騰慮雙城孤峭，攻未易拔。
entries.en: He feared Shuang was too steep to storm easily.
entries.literal: Teng worried that Shuang was isolated and steep and would not be easy to storm.

entries.zh: 賊若委城奔散，又難追討。
entries.en: If the rebels fled the city they would be hard to catch.
entries.literal: If the bandits abandoned the city and scattered, pursuit would again be hard.

entries.zh: 乃令諸軍周回立柵，遏其走路。
entries.en: He ringed the forts with palisades to block escape.
entries.literal: He then ordered the armies to encircle with palisades on all sides, blocking their escape routes.

entries.zh: 賊乃大駭。
entries.en: The rebels panicked.
entries.literal: The bandits were greatly terrified.

entries.zh: 於是縱兵擊破之，擒五子王于石默，獲寶勝於雙城，悉斬諸向首領，生擒萬餘口。
entries.en: His troops broke them, took the Fifth Son King at Shimo and Baosheng at Shuang, executed the Xiang chiefs, and captured ten thousand alive.
entries.literal: Thereupon he unleashed the troops to break them; the Fifth Son King was seized at Shimo and Baosheng captured at Shuang; all the Xiang chiefs were beheaded and more than ten thousand taken alive.

entries.zh: 信州舊治白帝。
entries.en: Xin Prefecture had formerly been at Baidi.
entries.literal: Xin Prefecture's old seat was Baidi.

entries.zh: 騰更于劉備故宮城南，八陣之北，臨江岸築城，移置信州。
entries.en: Lu Teng built a new city south of Liu Bei's old palace and north of the Eight Formations and moved Xin Prefecture there.
entries.literal: Teng then south of the former palace of Liu Bei and north of the Eight Formations, on the river bank built a city and moved Xin Prefecture there.

entries.zh: 又以巫縣、信陵、秭歸竝是硤中要險，於是築城置防，以為襟帶焉。
entries.en: He fortified Wu, Xinling, and Zigui in the gorges as strategic strongpoints.
entries.literal: He also took Wu, Xinling, and Zigui—all strategic points in the gorges—and built cities and defenses as strategic belts.

entries.zh: 異域上
entries.en: Other Regions, Part One
entries.literal: Other Regions, Part One

entries.zh: 張儀說魏襄王曰：「梁地方不至千里，卒不過三十萬，地四平，無名山大川之限，卒戍楚、韓、齊、趙之境，寧亭、障者不下十萬，梁之地勢固戰場也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi urged King Xiang of Wei: "Liang's territory is under a thousand li, its soldiers under three hundred thousand; the land is flat on every side, with no great mountains or rivers to defend it; troops garrison the borders of Chu, Han, Qi, and Zhao; men in forts and barrier posts are not fewer than one hundred thousand; Liang's terrain is in truth a battlefield.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi urged King Xiang of Wei, saying: "Liang's territory is less than a thousand li, its soldiers no more than three hundred thousand; the land is level on four sides, without famous mountains or great rivers to hem it in; soldiers garrison the borders of Chu, Han, Qi, and Zhao; those manning forts and barriers are not fewer than one hundred thousand; Liang's terrain is in truth a battlefield.

entries.zh: 夫諸侯之約從，盟洹水之上，結為兄弟以相堅也。
entries.en: When the lords ally vertically, they swear brotherhood above the Huan River to strengthen one another.
entries.literal: When the feudal lords covenant in vertical alliance, they ally above the Huan River and bind themselves as brothers to strengthen one another.

entries.zh: 今親兄弟同父母，尚有爭錢財相殺傷，而欲恃反覆蘇秦之餘謀，其不可成亦明矣。
entries.en: Even full brothers of the same parents fight over money and wound one another—yet you would rely on the leftover schemes of the fickle Su Qin; that this cannot succeed is obvious.
entries.literal: Now even full brothers of the same parents still fight over money and wound one another—yet you wish to rely on the leftover schemes of the fickle Su Qin; that it cannot succeed is clear.

entries.zh: 大王不事秦，秦下兵攻河外，據卷衍、酸棗，劫衛，取陽晉，則趙不南，趙不南而梁不北，梁不北則從道絕，從道絕則大王之國欲毋危，不可得也。
entries.en: If you do not serve Qin, Qin will march on Hewai, seize Juanyan and Suanzao, threaten Wei, and take Yangjin—Zhao cannot advance south; without Zhao in the south, Liang cannot advance north; without Liang in the north, the vertical alliance is severed; with that route cut, your state cannot hope to escape danger.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will send troops down to attack Hewai, hold Juanyan and Suanzao, threaten Wei, and take Yangjin—then Zhao cannot go south; if Zhao cannot go south, Liang cannot go north; if Liang cannot go north, the vertical route is cut; if the vertical route is cut, then Your Majesty's state wishing not to be in peril—it cannot be obtained.

entries.zh: 故願大王審定計議，且賜骸骨。」
entries.en: So I beg Your Majesty to weigh your plans carefully and let me take my leave."
entries.literal: Therefore I wish Your Majesty to examine and fix your plans, and grant me my bones."

entries.zh: 魏王乃倍從約，而因儀以請成於秦。
entries.en: King Xiang of Wei then broke the vertical alliance and, through Zhang Yi, sued for peace with Qin.
entries.literal: The king of Wei thereupon doubled back on the vertical covenant and, through Yi, sought peace with Qin.

entries.zh: 張儀歸，復相秦。
entries.en: Zhang Yi returned and again became chancellor of Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi returned and again became chancellor of Qin.

entries.zh: 巴、蜀相攻擊，俱告急於秦。
entries.en: Ba and Shu attacked each other; both urgently appealed to Qin.
entries.literal: Ba and Shu attacked each other; both urgently appealed to Qin.

entries.zh: 秦惠王欲伐蜀。
entries.en: King Hui of Qin wished to attack Shu.
entries.literal: King Hui of Qin wished to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 以為道險狹難至，而韓又來侵，猶豫未能決。
entries.en: He thought the road perilous, narrow, and hard to reach, while Han raided again; he hesitated and could not decide.
entries.literal: He thought the road perilous and narrow and hard to reach, while Han again came to raid; he hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 司馬錯請伐蜀。
entries.en: Sima Cuo urged an attack on Shu.
entries.literal: Sima Cuo requested to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 張儀曰：「不如伐韓。」
entries.en: Zhang Yi said: "Better to attack Han."
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said: "Better to attack Han."

entries.zh: 王曰：「請聞其說。」
entries.en: The king said: "Let me hear your reasoning."
entries.literal: The king said: "Please let me hear your reasoning."

entries.zh: 儀曰：「親魏，善楚，下兵三川，攻新城、宜陽，以臨二周之郊，據九鼎，按圖籍，挾天子以令於天下，天下莫敢不聽，此王業也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi said: "Befriend Wei, court Chu, march on the Three Rivers, attack Xincheng and Yiyang, threaten the Two Zhou, seize the Nine Cauldrons, hold the maps and registers, take the Son of Heaven hostage to command the realm—none under Heaven would dare disobey; that is true kingship.
entries.literal: Yi said: "Be close to Wei, be good to Chu, send troops down to the Three Rivers, attack Xincheng and Yiyang, to overlook the suburbs of the Two Zhou, hold the Nine Cauldrons, consult maps and registers, seize the Son of Heaven to command the realm—none under Heaven dares not obey; this is kingship.

entries.zh: 臣聞爭名者於朝，爭利者於市。
entries.en: I have heard that men contend for fame at court and for profit in the market.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that those who contend for fame do so at court, and those who contend for profit do so in the market.

entries.zh: 今三川、周室，天下之朝、市也，而王不爭焉，顧爭於戎翟，去王業遠矣！」
entries.en: The Three Rivers and the Zhou court are the realm's court and market—yet you do not fight for them, but turn to fight barbarians; you are far from kingship!"
entries.literal: Now the Three Rivers and the house of Zhou are the court and market of the realm—yet Your Majesty does not contend for them, but turns to contend with the Rong and Di; you are far from kingship!"

entries.zh: 司馬錯曰：「不然，臣聞之，欲富國者務廣其地，欲強兵者務富其民，欲王者務博其德，三資者備而王隨之矣。
entries.en: Sima Cuo said: "Not so. I have heard: to enrich the state, broaden its lands; to strengthen the army, enrich its people; to become king, spread your virtue—when these three are in place, kingship follows.
entries.literal: Sima Cuo said: "Not so. Your servant has heard: one who wishes to enrich the state must broaden its territory; one who wishes to strengthen the army must enrich its people; one who wishes to be king must spread his virtue—when these three resources are complete, kingship follows.

entries.zh: 今王地小民貧，故臣願先從事於易。
entries.en: Your territory is small and your people poor; so I wish to begin with what is easy.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty's territory is small and the people poor; therefore your servant wishes first to undertake what is easy.

entries.zh: 夫蜀，西僻之國而戎翟之長也，有桀、紂之亂，以秦攻之，譬如使豺狼逐群羊。
entries.en: Shu is a remote western state, chief among the barbarians; it has chaos like that of Jie and Zhou—if Qin attacks it, it is like setting wolves on a flock of sheep.
entries.literal: Shu is a remote western state and chief among the Rong and Di; it has the disorder of Jie and Zhou—if Qin attacks it, it is like setting wolves and jackals on a flock of sheep.

entries.zh: 得其地足以廣國，取其財足以富民，繕兵不傷眾而彼已服焉。
entries.en: Its land would widen your realm, its wealth would enrich your people; you could ready your army without heavy losses, and they would already submit.
entries.literal: Gaining its land suffices to broaden the state; taking its wealth suffices to enrich the people; drilling troops without harming the masses, and they already submit.

entries.zh: 拔一國而天下不以為暴，利盡西海而天下不以為貪，是我一舉而名實附也，而又有禁暴止亂之名。
entries.en: You would overthrow one state yet the realm would not call you violent; profits reaching the western seas yet the realm would not call you greedy—in one stroke we gain both fame and substance, and the name of ending violence and chaos.
entries.literal: Uprooting one state yet the realm does not deem you violent; profits extending to the western seas yet the realm does not deem you greedy—thus in one move fame and substance attach to us, and we also have the name of forbidding violence and stopping disorder.

entries.zh: 今攻韓，劫天子，惡名也，而未必利也，又有不義之名，而攻天下所不欲，危矣！
entries.en: To attack Han now, seize the Son of Heaven—that wins an evil name without sure profit, adds the name of injustice, and strikes where the realm does not wish—perilous!
entries.literal: Now to attack Han, seize the Son of Heaven—an evil name, and not necessarily profit; moreover an unrighteous name, attacking what the realm does not wish—perilous!

entries.zh: 臣請論其故。
entries.en: Let me explain why.
entries.literal: Your servant requests to discuss the reasons.

entries.zh: 周，天下之宗室也；
entries.en: Zhou is the ancestral house of the realm;
entries.literal: Zhou is the ancestral house of the realm;

entries.zh: 齊，韓之與國也。
entries.en: Qi is Han's ally.
entries.literal: Qi is Han's allied state.

entries.zh: 周自知失九鼎，韓自知亡三川，將二國並力合謀，以因乎齊、趙而求解乎楚、魏。
entries.en: Zhou knows it has lost the Nine Cauldrons; Han knows it has lost the Three Rivers; the two will join forces, lean on Qi and Zhao, and seek aid from Chu and Wei.
entries.literal: Zhou itself knows it has lost the Nine Cauldrons; Han itself knows it has lost the Three Rivers; the two states will combine strength and join plots, rely on Qi and Zhao, and seek rescue from Chu and Wei.

entries.zh: 以鼎與楚，以地與魏，王弗能止也。
entries.en: They will give the cauldrons to Chu and land to Wei—and you cannot stop it.
entries.literal: They will give the cauldrons to Chu and the lands to Wei—Your Majesty cannot stop it.

entries.zh: 此臣之所謂危也。
entries.en: That is what I call peril.
entries.literal: This is what your servant calls peril.

entries.zh: 不如伐蜀完。」
entries.en: Better to finish the conquest of Shu."
entries.literal: Better to attack Shu to completion."

entries.zh: 王從錯計，起兵伐蜀。
entries.en: The king followed Sima Cuo's plan and marched on Shu.
entries.literal: The king followed Cuo's plan and raised troops to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 十月取之。
entries.en: In the tenth month he conquered it.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he took it.

entries.zh: 貶蜀王，更號為侯，而使陳莊相蜀。
entries.en: He demoted the Shu king to marquis and sent Chen Zhuang to govern Shu.
entries.literal: He demoted the king of Shu, changed his title to marquis, and sent Chen Zhuang to govern Shu.

entries.zh: 蜀既屬秦，秦以益強，富厚，輕諸侯。
entries.en: Once Shu belonged to Qin, Qin grew stronger and richer and held the feudal lords in contempt.
entries.literal: Once Shu belonged to Qin, Qin thereby grew stronger, rich and substantial, and looked lightly on the feudal lords.

entries.zh: 秦王欲伐齊，患齊、楚之從親，乃使張儀至楚，說楚王曰：「大王誠能聽臣，閉關絕約於齊，臣請獻商於之地六百里，使秦女得為大王箕帚之妾，秦、楚娶婦嫁女，長為兄弟之國。」
entries.en: The king of Qin planned to attack Qi but feared the Qi–Chu alliance, so he sent Zhang Yi to Chu. Zhang Yi told the king: “If Your Majesty will heed me, close the passes and break with Qi—I will give you six hundred li in Shangyu, provide a Qin bride to serve in your household, and bind Qin and Chu in marriage so we remain brother states forever.”
entries.literal: The king of Qin wished to attack Qi and worried over the horizontal alliance of Qi and Chu; he therefore sent Zhang Yi to Chu to persuade the king of Chu, saying: “If Your Majesty will truly heed me, close the passes and break the treaty with Qi—I beg to present six hundred li of Shangyu land, let a Qin girl become Your Majesty’s wife who sweeps and serves, and Qin and Chu marry daughters and take wives, to be brother states forever.”

entries.zh: 楚王說而許之。
entries.en: The king of Chu was delighted and agreed.
entries.literal: The king of Chu was pleased and assented.

entries.zh: 君臣皆賀，陳軫獨吊。
entries.en: Court and king rejoiced; only Chen Zhen mourned.
entries.literal: Ministers and ruler all congratulated him; Chen Zhen alone offered condolences.

entries.zh: 王怒曰：「寡人不興師而得六百里地，何吊也？」
entries.en: The king said angrily: “I gain six hundred li without raising troops—why mourn?”
entries.literal: The king said angrily: “Without raising troops I gain six hundred li of land—why offer condolences?”

entries.zh: 對曰：「不然。
entries.en: He replied: “Not so.
entries.literal: He replied: “It is not so.

entries.zh: 以臣觀之，商於之地不可得而齊、秦合。
entries.en: In my view you will not get Shangyu, and Qi and Qin will join.
entries.literal: In your servant’s view, the land of Shangyu cannot be obtained, and Qi and Qin will unite.

entries.zh: 齊、秦合則患必至矣！」
entries.en: When Qi and Qin unite, disaster is certain!”
entries.literal: When Qi and Qin unite, calamity is sure to come!”

entries.zh: 王曰：「有說乎？」
entries.en: The king said: “Explain.”
entries.literal: The king said: “Have you an explanation?”

entries.zh: 對曰：「夫秦之所以重楚者，以其有齊也。
entries.en: He said: “Qin values Chu because you have Qi as ally.
entries.literal: He replied: “Qin values Chu because Chu has Qi.

entries.zh: 今閉關絕約於齊，則楚孤，秦奚貪夫孤國，而與之商於之地六百里？
entries.en: Close the passes and break with Qi, and Chu stands alone—why should Qin favor a lonely state with six hundred li of Shangyu?
entries.literal: Now if you close the passes and break the treaty with Qi, Chu is isolated—why should Qin covet such an isolated state as to give it six hundred li of Shangyu?

entries.zh: 張儀至秦，必負王。
entries.en: When Zhang Yi returns to Qin he will surely betray you.
entries.literal: When Zhang Yi reaches Qin, he is sure to betray Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 是王北絕齊交，西生患於秦也。
entries.en: You will cut off Qi in the north and breed trouble with Qin in the west.
entries.literal: Thus Your Majesty will cut off Qi in the north and breed trouble with Qin in the west.

entries.zh: 兩國之兵必俱至。
entries.en: Armies from both states will surely come against you.
entries.literal: The armies of both states are sure to come together.

entries.zh: 為王計者，不若陰合而陽絕於齊，使人隨張儀。
entries.en: Better secretly stay aligned with Qi while openly breaking off, and send someone to follow Zhang Yi.
entries.literal: For Your Majesty’s planning, it would be better to unite with Qi in secret while openly breaking with them, and send someone to follow Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 苟與吾地，絕齊未晚也。」
entries.en: If he gives the land, breaking with Qi will not be too late.”
entries.literal: If he truly gives us the land, breaking with Qi is not yet late.”

entries.zh: 王曰「願陳子閉口，毋復言，以待寡人得地！」
entries.en: The king said, “Counselor Chen, be silent until I have the land!”
entries.literal: The king said, “I wish Counselor Chen would close his mouth and speak no more, until I have gained the land!”

entries.zh: 乃以相印授張儀，厚賜之。
entries.en: He gave Zhang Yi the chancellor’s seal and rich gifts.
entries.literal: He thereupon gave Zhang Yi the seal of chancellor and richly rewarded him.

entries.zh: 遂閉關絕約於齊，使一將軍隨張儀至秦。
entries.en: He closed the passes, broke with Qi, and sent a general to accompany Zhang Yi to Qin.
entries.literal: He then closed the passes and broke the treaty with Qi, and sent a general to follow Zhang Yi to Qin.

entries.zh: 張儀佯墮車，不朝三月。
entries.en: Zhang Yi pretended to fall from his carriage and stayed away from court for three months.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi pretended to fall from his carriage and did not attend court for three months.

entries.zh: 楚王聞之，曰：「儀以寡人絕齊未甚邪？」
entries.en: The king of Chu heard this and said: “Does Zhang Yi think I have not broken with Qi thoroughly enough?”
entries.literal: The king of Chu heard of it and said: “Has Yi thought my break with Qi not thorough enough?”

entries.zh: 乃使勇士宋遺借宋之符，北罵齊王。
entries.en: He sent the warrior Song Yi, using Song’s credentials, north to insult the king of Qi.
entries.literal: He thereupon sent the warrior Song Yi, borrowing Song’s tally, to go north and revile the king of Qi.

entries.zh: 齊王大怒，折節而事秦，齊、秦之交合。
entries.en: The king of Qi was furious, humbled himself to court Qin, and Qi and Qin allied.
entries.literal: The king of Qi was greatly enraged, bent his dignity to serve Qin, and Qi and Qin’s alliance was joined.

entries.zh: 張儀乃朝，見楚使者曰：「子何不受地？
entries.en: Zhang Yi then appeared at court and asked the Chu envoy: “Why do you not take your land?
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then attended court and, seeing the Chu envoy, said: “Why do you not receive the land?

entries.zh: 從某至某，廣袤六里。」
entries.en: From here to here—six li square.”
entries.literal: From such-and-such a place to such-and-such a place—six li in length and breadth.”

entries.zh: 使者怒，還報楚王。
entries.en: The envoy was furious and returned to report to the king of Chu.
entries.literal: The envoy was enraged and returned to report to the king of Chu.

entries.zh: 楚王大怒，欲發兵而攻秦。
entries.en: The king of Chu was furious and wanted to march against Qin.
entries.literal: The king of Chu was greatly enraged and wished to raise troops to attack Qin.

entries.zh: 陳軫曰：「軫可發口言乎？
entries.en: Chen Zhen said: “May I speak?
entries.literal: Chen Zhen said: “May Zhen open his mouth to speak?

entries.zh: 攻之不如因賂以一名都，與之并兵而攻齊，是我亡地於秦，取償於齊也。
entries.en: Better than attacking: offer a great city in tribute and join forces to attack Qi—thus we lose land to Qin but gain compensation from Qi.
entries.literal: To attack is not as good as bribing them with a famous city and joining with them in troops to attack Qi—thus we lose land to Qin but take compensation from Qi.

entries.zh: 今王已絕於齊而責欺於秦，是吾合秦、齊之交而來天下之兵也，國必大傷矣！」
entries.en: You have already broken with Qi yet blame Qin for deceit—you unite Qin and Qi and invite every army under Heaven; the state will be gravely wounded!”
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty has broken with Qi yet holds Qin to account for deceit—this joins the alliances of Qin and Qi and brings the armies of the realm; the state is sure to suffer great harm!”

entries.zh: 楚王不聽，使屈匄帥師伐秦。
entries.en: The king would not listen and sent Qu Gai to command the attack on Qin.
entries.literal: The king of Chu would not heed him and sent Qu Gai to lead the army against Qin.

entries.zh: 秦亦發兵使庶長章擊之。
entries.en: Qin also mobilized and sent Chief Assistant Zhang against him.
entries.literal: Qin also raised troops and sent Chief Assistant Zhang to strike him.

entries.zh: 秦惠王使人告楚懷王，請以武關之外易黔中地。
entries.en: King Hui of Qin sent an envoy to King Huai of Chu, offering to trade the territory beyond Wu Pass for Qianzhong.
entries.literal: King Hui of Qin sent someone to inform King Huai of Chu, proposing to exchange the lands outside Wu Pass for Qianzhong.

entries.zh: 楚王曰：「不願易地，願得張儀而獻黔中地。」
entries.en: The king of Chu said, “I do not want a land swap. Give me Zhang Yi and I will yield Qianzhong.”
entries.literal: The king of Chu said, “I do not wish to exchange lands; I wish to have Zhang Yi and will offer Qianzhong.”

entries.zh: 張儀聞之，請行。
entries.en: Zhang Yi heard and asked leave to go.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi heard this and asked to go.

entries.zh: 王曰：「楚將甘心於子，奈何行？」
entries.en: The king said, “Chu will have your life—how can you go?”
entries.literal: The king said, “Chu will eagerly devour you—how can you go?”

entries.zh: 張儀曰：「秦強楚弱，大王在，楚不宜敢取臣。
entries.en: Zhang Yi said, “Qin is strong and Chu weak. While Your Majesty lives, Chu will not dare touch me.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said, “Qin is strong and Chu weak; while Your Majesty lives, Chu ought not dare take me.

entries.zh: 且臣善其嬖臣靳尚，靳尚得事幸姬鄭袖，袖之言，王無不聽者。」
entries.en: Besides, I am close to his favorite Jin Shang, who serves the favored consort Zheng Xiu. Whatever she says, the king hears.”
entries.literal: Moreover I am on good terms with his favorite Jin Shang; Jin Shang waits on the favored consort Zheng Xiu, and whatever Xiu says the king never fails to heed.”

entries.zh: 遂往。
entries.en: And he went.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went.

entries.zh: 楚王囚，將殺之。
entries.en: The king of Chu seized him and meant to kill him.
entries.literal: The king of Chu imprisoned him and was about to kill him.

entries.zh: 靳尚謂鄭袖曰：「秦王甚愛張儀，將以上庸六縣及美女贖之。
entries.en: Jin Shang told Zheng Xiu, “The king of Qin loves Zhang Yi and will ransom him with the six counties of Shangyong and fair women.
entries.literal: Jin Shang said to Zheng Xiu, “The king of Qin loves Zhang Yi dearly and will ransom him with the six counties of Shangyong and beautiful women.

entries.zh: 王重地尊秦，秦女必貴而夫人斥矣。」
entries.en: The king prizes land and defers to Qin. A Qin woman will rise high, and my lady will be cast aside.”
entries.literal: The king values territory and honors Qin; a woman of Qin will surely be exalted and my lady driven aside.”

entries.zh: 於是鄭袖日夜泣於楚王曰：「臣各為其主耳。
entries.en: Zheng Xiu wept before the king day and night: “Every minister serves his own lord.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zheng Xiu wept day and night before the king of Chu, saying, “Ministers each serve their own lord.

entries.zh: 今殺張儀，秦必大怒。
entries.en: Kill Zhang Yi now and Qin will rage.
entries.literal: Kill Zhang Yi now and Qin will surely rage.

entries.zh: 妾請子母俱遷江南，毋為秦所魚肉也！」
entries.en: Let me take our son and move south of the Yangtze, lest Qin cut us like fish on a board!”
entries.literal: I beg that you and I, mother and son, move together to the lands south of the Yangtze, lest we be carved up like fish on Qin’s board!”

entries.zh: 王乃赦張儀而厚禮之。
entries.en: The king pardoned Zhang Yi and treated him with great honor.
entries.literal: The king then pardoned Zhang Yi and entertained him generously.

entries.zh: 張儀因說楚王曰：「夫為從者無以異於驅群羊而攻猛虎，不格明矣。
entries.en: Zhang Yi then urged the king of Chu: “A horizontal alliance is no different from driving sheep against a tiger. The folly is plain.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then persuaded the king of Chu, saying, “For those in a horizontal alliance there is no difference from driving a flock of sheep to attack a fierce tiger—the inaptness is clear.

entries.zh: 今王不事秦，秦劫韓驅梁而攻楚，則楚危矣。
entries.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will seize Han, drive Liang, and strike Chu—and Chu will be lost.
entries.literal: Now if Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will seize Han and drive Liang to attack Chu—then Chu will be in peril.

entries.zh: 秦西有巴、蜀，治船積粟，浮岷江而下，一日行五百餘里，不至十日而拒扞關，扞關驚則從境以東盡城守矣，黔中、巫郡非王之有。
entries.en: West of Qin lie Ba and Shu. They build ships and hoard grain, float down the Min—five hundred li a day. In ten days they reach Hanguan. When Hanguan stirs, every city east of the border will shut its gates. Qianzhong and Wujun will no longer be yours.
entries.literal: Qin has Ba and Shu in the west; it builds boats and stocks grain, floats down the Min River—more than five hundred li in a day; in less than ten days it reaches Hanguan; when Hanguan is alarmed, from the border east all will garrison the cities—Qianzhong and Wujun will no longer be yours.

entries.zh: 秦舉甲出武關，則北地絕。
entries.en: Qin marches from Wu Pass and your northern lands are severed.
entries.literal: Qin raises armor and issues from Wu Pass, and the northern lands are cut off.

entries.zh: 秦兵之攻楚也，危難在三月之內，而楚待諸侯之救在半歲之外。
entries.en: Qin can bring Chu to ruin in three months, while Chu must wait half a year for the lords’ aid.
entries.literal: When Qin troops attack Chu, peril comes within three months, yet Chu waits for rescue from the feudal lords beyond half a year.

entries.zh: 夫待弱國之救，忘強秦之禍，此臣所為大王患也。
entries.en: To wait on weak allies and forget the threat of mighty Qin—that is what I fear for Your Majesty.
entries.literal: To await rescue from weak states while forgetting calamity from mighty Qin—this is what your servant fears for Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 大王誠能聽臣，臣請令秦、楚長為兄弟之國，無相攻伐。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty will hear me, I beg to make Qin and Chu brother states forever, never to attack each other.”
entries.literal: If Your Majesty will truly hear me, your servant begs to make Qin and Chu brother states forever, never attacking each other.”

entries.zh: 楚王已得張儀而重出黔中地，乃許之。
entries.en: The king of Chu, having Zhang Yi, still tried to keep Qianzhong, but at last agreed.
entries.literal: The king of Chu, having Zhang Yi in hand, still wished to withhold Qianzhong, yet in the end agreed.

entries.zh: 張儀遂之韓，說韓王曰：「韓地險惡山居，五穀所生，非菽而麥，國無二歲之食，見卒不過二十萬。
entries.en: Zhang Yi went on to Han and told the king: “Han is rugged and mountainous. Its fields yield little but beans and wheat. The state has less than two years’ grain. Its troops number at most two hundred thousand.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then went to Han and said to the king of Han, “Han’s lands are rugged and mountainous; of the grains they grow, none is not bean or wheat; the state has not two years’ food; visible troops number no more than two hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 秦被甲百餘萬。
entries.en: Qin fields more than a million armored men.
entries.literal: Qin has more than a million in armor.

entries.zh: 山東之士被甲蒙冑而會戰，秦人捐甲徒裼以趨敵，左挈人頭，右挾生虜。
entries.en: The lords east of the mountains arm and helm for battle; Qin’s men cast off mail and rush in bare skin, a head in the left hand, a captive in the right.
entries.literal: The warriors east of the mountains don armor and helms to meet in battle; the men of Qin cast off armor and rush bare to the foe, seizing heads in the left hand and living captives in the right.

entries.zh: 夫戰孟賁、烏獲之士以攻不服之弱國，無異垂千鈞之重於鳥卵之上，必無幸矣。
entries.en: To pit men like Meng Bo and Wu Huo against a weak state that will not yield is to hang a thousand jun on a bird’s egg—there is no hope.
entries.literal: To fight with men like Meng Bo and Wu Huo against a weak state that will not submit is no different from hanging a weight of a thousand jun on a bird’s egg—there can be no escape.

entries.zh: 大王不事秦，秦下甲據宜陽，塞成皋，則王之國分矣。
entries.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will march down, seize Yiyang, and choke Chenggao—and your realm will be cut in two.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will descend with armor, hold Yiyang, block Chenggao—and Your Majesty’s state will be split.

entries.zh: 鴻臺之宮，桑林之宛，非王之有也。
entries.en: The palace at Hongtai, the park at Sanglin—they will no longer be yours.
entries.literal: The palace of Hongtai, the parklands of Sanglin—will no longer be yours.

entries.zh: 為大王計，莫如事秦而攻楚，以轉禍而悅秦，計無便於此者。」
entries.en: For Your Majesty, nothing is wiser than to serve Qin and strike Chu—turn disaster to gain, please Qin. No plan is better.”
entries.literal: For Your Majesty’s counsel, nothing surpasses serving Qin and attacking Chu, turning calamity to favor with Qin—no plan is more expedient.”

entries.zh: 韓王許之。
entries.en: The king of Han agreed.
entries.literal: The king of Han agreed.

entries.zh: 張儀歸報，秦王封以六邑，號武信君。
entries.en: Zhang Yi returned and reported. The king of Qin gave him six towns and the title Lord Martial Faith.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi returned to report; the king of Qin enfeoffed him with six towns and titled him Lord Martial Faith.

entries.zh: 復使東說齊王曰：「從人說大王者必曰：『齊蔽於三晉，地廣民眾，兵強士勇，雖有百秦，將無奈齊何。』
entries.en: "He was sent east again to the king of Qi: The alliance men will tell Your Majesty, Qi is shielded by the Three Jin. Your lands are broad, your people many, your arms strong, your warriors brave. Even a hundred Qins cannot touch Qi.
entries.literal: "He was again sent east to persuade the king of Qi, saying, Those of the horizontal alliance who speak to Your Majesty will surely say, Qi is screened by the Three Jin; its lands are broad, its people many; its arms strong, its warriors brave—even a hundred Qins can do nothing to Qi.

entries.zh: 大王賢其說而不計其實。
entries.en: Your Majesty admires the words and ignores the fact.
entries.literal: Your Majesty admires their words and does not reckon the reality.

entries.zh: 今秦、楚嫁女娶婦，為昆弟之國；
entries.en: Now Qin and Chu exchange brides and are brother states;
entries.literal: Now Qin and Chu marry daughters and take wives, becoming brother states;

entries.zh: 韓獻宜陽；
entries.en: Han has yielded Yiyang;
entries.literal: Han has offered Yiyang;

entries.zh: 梁效河外；
entries.en: Liang has surrendered the lands beyond the River;
entries.literal: Liang has presented the lands beyond the River;

entries.zh: 趙王入朝，割河間以事秦。
entries.en: the king of Zhao has come to court and ceded Hejian to serve Qin.
entries.literal: the king of Zhao has come to court and ceded Hejian to serve Qin.

entries.zh: 大王不事秦，秦驅韓、梁攻齊之南地，悉趙兵，渡清河，指博關，臨菑、即墨非王之有也！
entries.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will drive Han and Liang against Qi’s south, muster Zhao, cross the Clear River, take Bomen—Linzi and Jimo will no longer be yours!
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will drive Han and Liang to attack Qi’s southern lands, muster Zhao’s troops, cross the Clear River, point at Bomen—Linzi and Jimo will no longer be yours!

entries.zh: 國一日見攻，雖欲事秦，不可得也！」
entries.en: Once your state is struck, you may wish to serve Qin—but it will be too late!”
entries.literal: Once the state is attacked in a day, even if you wish to serve Qin, it cannot be done!”

entries.zh: 齊王許張儀。
entries.en: The king of Qi agreed.
entries.literal: The king of Qi agreed to Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 張儀去，西說趙王曰：「大王收率天下以擯秦，秦兵不敢出函谷關十五年。
entries.en: Zhang Yi went west to the king of Zhao: “Your Majesty rallied the world against Qin. For fifteen years Qin’s armies did not pass Hangu Pass.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi departed and went west to persuade the king of Zhao, saying, “Your Majesty gathered and led the world to shut out Qin; Qin’s troops dared not leave Hangu Pass for fifteen years.

entries.zh: 大王之威行於山東，敝邑恐懼，繕甲厲兵，力田積粟，愁居懾處，不敢動搖，唯大王有意督過之也。
entries.en: Your Majesty’s power filled the east. Our poor state feared, repaired arms, tilled fields, hoarded grain, lived in dread, and dared not move—only hoping Your Majesty might yet reprove us.
entries.literal: Your Majesty’s might ran through the lands east of the mountains; our humble state feared, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, labored in the fields and stored grain, dwelt in worry and dread, dared not stir—only that Your Majesty might deign to reprove us.

entries.zh: 今以大王之力，舉巴、蜀，並漢中，包兩周，守白馬之津。
entries.en: Now, by Your Majesty’s power, we have taken Ba and Shu, joined Hanzhong, enclosed the Two Zhou, and hold the ford of White Horse.
entries.literal: Now by Your Majesty’s strength Qin has taken Ba and Shu, annexed Hanzhong, wrapped the Two Zhou, and holds the ford of White Horse.

entries.zh: 秦雖僻遠，然而心忿含怒之日久矣。
entries.en: Qin is far away, yet our hearts have nursed wrath a long time.
entries.literal: Though Qin is remote, hearts have long heaped wrath and held rage.

entries.zh: 今秦有敝甲凋兵軍於澠池，願渡河，逾漳，據番吾，會邯鄲之下，願以甲子合戰，正殷紂之事。
entries.en: Now we have battered armor and weary troops at Mianchi. We mean to cross the River, pass Zhang, hold Fanwu, and meet you below Handan. We ask battle on jiazi day—to settle what King Zhou of Yin left undone.
entries.literal: Now Qin has worn armor and withered troops encamped at Mianchi; we wish to cross the River, pass Zhang, hold Fanwu, meet below Handan—we wish to join battle on jiazi and set right the affair of King Zhou of Yin.

entries.zh: 謹使使臣先聞左右。
entries.en: I send this envoy first to inform Your Majesty.
entries.literal: I respectfully send an envoy first to inform those at your side.

entries.zh: 今楚與秦為昆弟之國，而韓、梁稱東籓之臣，齊獻魚鹽之地，此斷趙之右肩也。
entries.en: Chu and Qin are brothers. Han and Liang are your eastern vassals. Qi has yielded its coast. This cuts off Zhao’s right arm.
entries.literal: Now Chu and Qin are brother states, while Han and Liang call themselves eastern vassals and Qi has offered its fish-and-salt lands—this severs Zhao’s right shoulder.

entries.zh: 夫斷右肩而與人鬥，失其黨而孤居，求欲毋危，得乎？
entries.en: Cut off your right arm and fight—lose your allies and stand alone. Can you hope to be safe?
entries.literal: Sever the right shoulder and fight another—lose your party and stand alone; can you seek not to be imperiled and succeed?

entries.zh: 今秦發三將軍，其一軍塞午道，告齊使渡清河，軍於邯鄲之東；
entries.en: Qin now sends three generals. One blocks Wudao and tells Qi to cross the Clear River and camp east of Handan;
entries.literal: Now Qin sends three generals: one army blocks Wudao, tells Qi to cross the Clear River and encamp east of Handan;

entries.zh: 一軍軍成皋，驅韓、梁軍於河外；
entries.en: one camps at Chenggao and drives Han and Liang beyond the River;
entries.literal: one army encamps at Chenggao and drives Han and Liang’s troops beyond the River;

entries.zh: 一軍軍於澠池，約四國為一以攻趙，趙服必四分其地。
entries.en: one camps at Mianchi and binds four states to strike Zhao. When Zhao yields, its land will be carved four ways.
entries.literal: one army encamps at Mianchi, binds four states as one to attack Zhao—when Zhao submits, its lands will surely be quartered.

entries.zh: 臣竊為大王計，莫如與秦王面相約而口相結，常為兄弟之國也。」
entries.en: I urge Your Majesty: meet the king of Qin face to face, swear brotherhood, and stand as brothers forever.”
entries.literal: Your servant privately counsels Your Majesty: nothing surpasses meeting the king of Qin face to face, binding with spoken oath, ever to be brother states.”

entries.zh: 趙王許之。
entries.en: The king of Zhao agreed.
entries.literal: The king of Zhao agreed.

entries.zh: 張儀乃北之燕，說燕王曰：「今趙王已入朝，效河間以事秦。
entries.en: Zhang Yi went north to Yan and told the king: “The king of Zhao has come to court and yielded Hejian to serve Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi then went north to Yan and said to the king of Yan, “Now the king of Zhao has come to court and offered Hejian to serve Qin.

entries.zh: 大王不事秦，秦下甲雲中、九原，驅趙而攻燕，則易水、長城非大王之有也。
entries.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will march through Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, drive Zhao against Yan—and the Yi River and the Long Wall will no longer be yours.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will descend with armor through Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, drive Zhao to attack Yan—then the Yi River and the Long Wall will no longer be yours.

entries.zh: 且今時齊、趙之於秦，猶郡縣也，不敢妄舉師以攻伐。
entries.en: Qi and Zhao toward Qin are now like commanderies. They dare not raise armies against you.
entries.literal: Moreover, Qi and Zhao toward Qin now are like commanderies and counties—they dare not rashly raise armies to attack.

entries.zh: 今王事秦，長無齊、趙之患矣。」
entries.en: Serve Qin, and you will be free of Qi and Zhao forever.”
entries.literal: If Your Majesty serves Qin now, you will long be free of trouble from Qi and Zhao.”

entries.zh: 燕王請獻常山之尾五城以和。
entries.en: The king of Yan offered five towns at the foot of Mount Chang to make peace.
entries.literal: The king of Yan asked to offer the five towns at the tail of Mount Chang to make peace.

entries.zh: 張儀說秦武王曰：「為王計者，東方有變，然後王可以多割得地也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi told King Wu of Qin: “For Your Majesty’s sake, when the east is in turmoil, you may win more land.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said to King Wu of Qin, “For Your Majesty’s plan, when there is change in the east, then Your Majesty may take more land in cession.

entries.zh: 臣聞齊王甚憎臣，臣之所在，齊必伐之。
entries.en: I hear the king of Qi hates me. Wherever I am, Qi will attack.
entries.literal: I hear the king of Qi hates me deeply; wherever I am, Qi will surely attack.

entries.zh: 臣願乞其不肖之身以之梁，齊必伐梁，齊、梁交兵而不能相去，王以其間伐韓，入三川，挾天子，案圖籍，此王業也。」
entries.en: Let me take my worthless self to Liang. Qi will strike Liang. While Qi and Liang fight and cannot break off, Your Majesty may attack Han, enter the Three Rivers, hold the Son of Heaven, and read the maps and registers—that is the royal enterprise.”
entries.literal: I beg to offer my unworthy person to Liang; Qi will surely attack Liang. When Qi and Liang fight and cannot break away, Your Majesty may use the interval to attack Han, enter the Three Rivers, hold the Son of Heaven, examine maps and registers—this is the royal enterprise.”

entries.zh: 王許之。
entries.en: The king agreed.
entries.literal: The king agreed.

entries.zh: 齊王果伐梁，梁王恐。
entries.en: Qi did attack Liang, and the king of Liang was afraid.
entries.literal: The king of Qi did attack Liang; the king of Liang was afraid.

entries.zh: 張儀曰：「王勿患也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi said, “Do not fear.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi said, “Your Majesty, do not worry.

entries.zh: 請令齊罷兵。」
entries.en: I will make Qi withdraw.”
entries.literal: I beg to make Qi cease its troops.”

entries.zh: 乃使其舍人之楚，借使謂齊王曰：「甚矣，王之托儀於秦也！」
entries.en: He sent a retainer to Chu, borrowed an envoy, and told the king of Qi: “How deeply Your Majesty has trusted Yi to Qin!”
entries.literal: He then sent his retainer to Chu, borrowing an envoy to say to the king of Qi, “How far Your Majesty has entrusted Yi to Qin!”

entries.zh: 齊王曰：「何故？」
entries.en: The king of Qi asked, “Why?”
entries.literal: The king of Qi said, “Why?”

entries.zh: 楚使者曰：「張儀之去秦也，固與秦王謀矣，欲齊、梁相攻而令秦取三川也。
entries.en: The Chu envoy said, “When Zhang Yi left Qin he plotted with the king: he meant Qi and Liang to fight so Qin could take the Three Rivers.
entries.literal: The Chu envoy said, “When Zhang Yi left Qin he had surely plotted with the king of Qin: he wished Qi and Liang to fight each other so that Qin might take the Three Rivers.

entries.zh: 今王果伐梁，是王內罷國而外伐與國，以信儀於秦王也。」
entries.en: Now you have attacked Liang—you wear out your state within, strike an ally without, and prove Yi true to the king of Qin.”
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty has indeed attacked Liang—this is to exhaust your state within while attacking an allied state without, and to give credence to Yi before the king of Qin.”

entries.zh: 齊王乃解兵還。
entries.en: Qi withdrew its army.
entries.literal: The king of Qi then dismissed his troops and returned.

entries.zh: 張儀相魏一歲，夏，五月，儀卒。
entries.en: Zhang Yi served as chancellor of Wei one year; in summer, fifth month, Yi died.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi was chancellor of Wei one year; in summer, fifth month, Yi died.

entries.zh: 張儀歸報，未至咸陽，秦惠王薨，子武王立。
entries.en: Zhang Yi turned homeward to report. Before he reached Xianyang, King Hui of Qin died and his son King Wu succeeded.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi returned to report; before he reached Xianyang, King Hui of Qin died and his son King Wu succeeded.

entries.zh: 武王自為太子時，不悅張儀，及即位，群臣多毀短之。
entries.en: As crown prince, King Wu had disliked Zhang Yi. When he took the throne, many ministers slandered him.
entries.literal: King Wu, from the time he was heir, disliked Zhang Yi; when he took the throne, many among the ministers slandered him.

entries.zh: 諸侯聞儀與秦王有隙，皆畔衡，復合從。
entries.en: The lords heard that Yi and Qin were estranged. All left the vertical alliance and joined the horizontal again.
entries.literal: The feudal lords heard that Yi and the king of Qin were at odds; all turned from the vertical alliance and joined the horizontal again.

entries.zh: 儀與蘇秦皆以縱橫之術游諸侯，致位富貴，天下爭慕效之。
entries.en: Yi and Su Qin both won rank and riches by the arts of alliance and defiance among the lords; the world rushed to imitate them.
entries.literal: Yi and Su Qin both roamed the feudal lords with the arts of vertical and horizontal alliance, reaching rank and wealth; the world vied to admire and imitate them.

entries.zh: 又有魏人公孫衍者，號曰犀首，亦以談說顯名。
entries.en: There was also Gongsun Yan of Wei, called Rhino’s Head, who won fame by talk alone.
entries.literal: There was also Gongsun Yan of Wei, styled Rhino’s Head, who likewise won fame by persuasion.

entries.zh: 其餘蘇代、蘇厲、周最、樓緩之徒，紛紜遍於天下，務以辯詐相高，不可勝紀。
entries.en: Su Dai, Su Li, Zhou Zui, Lou Huan, and the rest swarmed the world, each trying to outtalk the other—too many to count.
entries.literal: The rest—Su Dai, Su Li, Zhou Zui, Lou Huan, and the like—swarmed across the world, striving to outdo one another in sophistry and deceit, beyond numbering.

entries.zh: 而儀、秦、衍最著。
entries.en: Yet Yi, Qin, and Yan stood foremost.
entries.literal: Yet Yi, Qin, and Yan were the most renowned.

entries.zh: 《孟子》論之曰：或謂：「張儀、公孫衍，豈不大丈夫哉！
entries.en: Mencius wrote: Some say, “Zhang Yi and Gongsun Yan—were they not true men!
entries.literal: Mencius discussed them, saying: Some say, “Zhang Yi and Gongsun Yan—were they not great men!

entries.zh: 一怒而諸侯懼，安居而天下熄。」
entries.en: One burst of wrath and the lords trembled; one year of peace and the world went still.”
entries.literal: In anger the feudal lords feared; at rest the world was stilled.”

entries.zh: 孟子曰：「是惡足以為大丈夫哉？
entries.en: Mencius said, “How could such men be called true men?
entries.literal: Mencius said, “How can such men suffice to be great men?

entries.zh: 君子立天下之正位，行天下之正道，得志則與民由之，不得志則獨行其道，富貴不能淫，貧賤不能移，威武不能詘，是之謂大丈夫。」
entries.en: A gentleman stands in the right place and walks the right path. When his will is done he shares it with the people; when it is not he walks alone. Wealth cannot seduce him, poverty cannot move him, power cannot bend him—that is a true man.”
entries.literal: The gentleman stands in the world’s right place, walks the world’s right path; when his will is fulfilled he shares it with the people, when it is not he walks his path alone—wealth and honor cannot dissolve him, poverty and low estate cannot shift him, force and might cannot bend him: this is called a great man."

entries.zh: 揚子《法言》曰：或問：「儀、秦學乎鬼谷術而習乎縱橫言，安中國者各十餘年，是夫？」
entries.en: Master Yang’s Fayan says: Someone asked, “Zhang Yi and Su Qin studied under Guiguzi and mastered coalition rhetoric; each held the Central States at peace for more than ten years—is that true?”
entries.literal: Master Yang’s Fayan says: Someone asked, “Zhang Yi and Su Qin studied the arts of Guiguzi and practiced coalition rhetoric; each kept the Central States secure for more than ten years—is that so?”

entries.zh: 曰：「詐人也。
entries.en: He answered, “Frauds.
entries.literal: He replied, “They were deceivers.

entries.zh: 聖人惡諸。」
entries.en: The sages despised men like that.”
entries.literal: The sages abhorred such men.”

entries.zh: 曰：「孔子讀而儀、秦行，何如也？」
entries.en: He said, “Suppose Confucius read the classics while Zhang Yi and Su Qin carried on as they did—what then?”
entries.literal: He said, “If Confucius read [the classics] but Zhang Yi and Su Qin acted [as they did]—what of that?”

entries.zh: 曰：「甚矣鳳鳴而鷙翰也！」
entries.en: He replied, “As absurd as a phoenix singing while a hawk strikes!”
entries.literal: He replied, “How far apart are the phoenix’s cry and the hawk’s strike!”

entries.zh: 「然則子貢不為歟？」
entries.en: “Then did not Zi Gong do likewise?”
entries.literal: “Then would Zi Gong not have done the same?”

entries.zh: 曰：「亂而不解，子貢恥諸。
entries.en: He said, “To stir disorder and not set it right—Zi Gong would be ashamed.
entries.literal: He said, “To create disorder and not resolve it—Zi Gong would be ashamed of that.

entries.zh: 說而不富貴，儀、秦恥諸。」
entries.en: To persuade without winning wealth and rank—Zhang Yi and Su Qin would be ashamed.”
entries.literal: To persuade without wealth and rank—Zhang Yi and Su Qin would be ashamed of that.”

entries.zh: 或曰：「儀、秦其才矣乎，跡不蹈已？」
entries.en: Someone asked, “Were Zhang Yi and Su Qin truly talented—walking where no one had walked?”
entries.literal: Someone asked, “Were Zhang Yi and Su Qin men of talent, treading paths none had walked before?”

entries.zh: 曰：「昔在任人，帝而難之，不以才矣。
entries.en: He said, “Long ago there was a man of ability; the Emperor found him hard to use and did not keep him for talent alone.
entries.literal: He said, “In antiquity there was a man of ability; the Emperor found him difficult and did not employ him for talent alone.

entries.zh: 才乎才，非吾徒之才也。」
entries.en: Talent? Talent—that is not the talent of our kind.”
entries.literal: Talent? Talent—that is not the talent of our fellowship.”

entries.zh: 周紀三
entries.en: Zhou Records 3
entries.literal: Zhou Records 3

entries.zh: 夏，益州夷二十四邑、三萬餘人皆反。
entries.en: In summer the Yi of Yizhou—twenty-four settlements and more than thirty thousand people—all rebelled.
entries.literal: In summer, the Yi of Yizhou—twenty-four settlements and more than thirty thousand people—all rebelled.

entries.zh: 遣水衡都尉呂辟胡募吏民及發犍為、蜀郡奔命往擊，大破之。
entries.en: Chief Steward for Water and Parks Lü Pihu was sent to recruit officials and commoners and raise emergency levies from Qianwei and Shu to attack them; he won a crushing victory.
entries.literal: The Chief Steward for Water and Parks Lü Pihu was sent to recruit officials and commoners and to raise emergency levies from Qianwei and Shu commanderies to attack them; he inflicted a great defeat.

entries.zh: 秋，七月，赦天下。
entries.en: In autumn, the seventh month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 大雨，至於十月，渭橋絕。
entries.en: Heavy rain lasted until the tenth month; the Wei River bridge was washed out.
entries.literal: Heavy rain lasted until the tenth month; the Wei River bridge was cut off.

entries.zh: 武帝初崩，賜諸侯王璽書。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu first died, imperial-seal letters of appointment were sent to the feudal kings.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu first died, imperial-seal letters of appointment were bestowed on the feudal kings.

entries.zh: 燕王旦得書不肯哭，曰：「璽書封小，京師疑有變。」
entries.en: Prince Dan of Yan received the letter and refused to mourn, saying, "The seal on the letter is small—the capital may suspect something has changed."
entries.literal: The Prince of Yan, Dan, received the letter and refused to mourn, saying: "The seal on the letter is small; the capital suspects there has been a change."

entries.zh: 遣幸臣壽西長、孫縱之、王孺等之長安，以問禮儀為名，陰刺候朝廷事。
entries.en: He sent favored retainers Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru, and others to Chang'an, ostensibly to inquire about ritual, but secretly to spy on affairs at court.
entries.literal: He sent favored retainers Shou Xichang, Sun Zongzhi, Wang Ru, and others to Chang'an, under the pretext of inquiring about ritual, to spy secretly on affairs at court.

entries.zh: 及有詔褒賜旦錢三十萬，益封萬三千戶，旦怒曰：「我當為帝，何賜也！」
entries.en: When an edict came praising and rewarding Dan with three hundred thousand cash and an additional enfeoffment of thirteen thousand households, Dan raged, "I ought to be emperor—what is this reward!"
entries.literal: When an edict came praising and rewarding Dan with three hundred thousand cash and an additional enfeoffment of thirteen thousand households, Dan angrily said: "I ought to be emperor—what is this reward!"

entries.zh: 遂與宗室中山哀王子長、齊孝王孫澤等結謀，詐言以武帝時受詔，得職吏事，修武備，備非常。
entries.en: He thereupon conspired with the imperial clansman Chang, son of King Ai of Zhongshan, Sun Ze, grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others, falsely claiming that in Emperor Wu's time he had received an edict empowering him to manage officials, repair armaments, and guard against the unexpected.
entries.literal: He thereupon joined in conspiracy with the imperial clansman Chang, son of King Ai of Zhongshan, Sun Ze, grandson of King Xiao of Qi, and others, falsely claiming that in Emperor Wu's time he had received an edict empowering him to manage officials and affairs, repair armaments, and guard against the unexpected.
