entries.zh: 郎中成軫謂旦曰：「大王失職，獨可起而索，不可坐而得也。
entries.en: Palace Gentleman Cheng Zhen told Dan, "Your Highness has lost your place; you can only rise and demand it—you cannot sit and obtain it.
entries.literal: Palace Gentleman Cheng Zhen said to Dan: "Your Highness has lost your post; you can only rise and demand it—you cannot sit and obtain it.

entries.zh: 大王壹起，國中雖女子皆奮臂隨大王。」
entries.en: If Your Highness rises once, throughout the state even women will take up arms and follow you."
entries.literal: If Your Highness rises once, throughout the state even women will swing their arms and follow Your Highness."

entries.zh: 旦即與澤謀，為奸書，言：「少帝非武帝子，大臣所共立；
entries.en: Dan at once plotted with Ze and forged a seditious letter, saying, "The young emperor is not Emperor Wu's son; the great ministers jointly established him;
entries.literal: Dan at once plotted with Ze and forged a wicked letter, saying: "The young emperor is not Emperor Wu's son; the great ministers jointly established him;

entries.zh: 天下宜共伐之！」
entries.en: all under Heaven ought jointly to attack him!"
entries.literal: all under Heaven ought jointly to attack him!"

entries.zh: 使人傳行郡國以搖動百姓。
entries.en: He sent men to circulate it through the commanderies and kingdoms to stir up the people.
entries.literal: He sent men to circulate it through the commanderies and kingdoms to stir up the people.

entries.zh: 澤謀歸發兵臨菑，殺青州刺史雋不疑。
entries.en: Ze plotted to return, raise troops, advance on Zi, and kill Qingzhou Inspector Juan Buyi.
entries.literal: Ze plotted to return, raise troops, advance on Zi, and kill Qingzhou Inspector Juan Buyi.

entries.zh: 旦招來郡國奸人，賦斂銅鐵作甲兵，數閱其車騎、材官卒，發民大獵以講士馬，須期日。
entries.en: Dan gathered wicked men from the commanderies and kingdoms, levied copper and iron for armor and weapons, repeatedly reviewed his chariots, cavalry, and skilled troops, and mobilized the people for great hunts to drill men and horses, awaiting the appointed day.
entries.literal: Dan gathered wicked men from the commanderies and kingdoms, levied copper and iron to make armor and weapons, repeatedly reviewed his chariots, cavalry, and skilled soldiers, and mobilized the people for great hunts to drill troops and horses, awaiting the appointed day.

entries.zh: 郎中韓義等數諫旦，旦殺義等凡十五人。
entries.en: Palace Gentlemen Han Yi and others repeatedly admonished Dan; Dan killed Yi and fourteen others—fifteen in all.
entries.literal: Palace Gentlemen Han Yi and others repeatedly admonished Dan; Dan killed Yi and the rest, fifteen in all.

entries.zh: 會缾侯成知澤等謀，以告雋不疑。
entries.en: Marquis of Ping Cheng learned of Ze's plot and reported it to Juan Buyi.
entries.literal: It happened that Marquis of Ping Cheng learned of Ze's plot and reported it to Juan Buyi.

entries.zh: 八月，不疑收捕澤等以聞。
entries.en: In the eighth month Buyi arrested Ze and the others and reported it.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Buyi arrested Ze and the others and reported it.

entries.zh: 天子遣大鴻臚丞治，連引燕王。
entries.en: The emperor sent the Grand Herald's assistant to investigate, implicating the Prince of Yan in succession.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the Grand Herald's assistant to investigate, implicating the Prince of Yan in succession.

entries.zh: 有詔，以燕王至親，勿治；
entries.en: An edict stated that because the Prince of Yan was a close kinsman, he was not to be prosecuted;
entries.literal: An edict stated that because the Prince of Yan was a close kinsman, he was not to be prosecuted;

entries.zh: 而澤等皆伏誅。
entries.en: but Ze and the others were all executed.
entries.literal: but Ze and the others were all executed.

entries.zh: 遷雋不疑為京兆尹。
entries.en: Juan Buyi was transferred to Metropolitan Commandant.
entries.literal: Juan Buyi was transferred to be Metropolitan Commandant.

entries.zh: 不疑為京兆尹，吏民敬其威信。
entries.en: As Metropolitan Commandant, Buyi won respect from officials and commoners for his authority and trustworthiness.
entries.literal: As Metropolitan Commandant, Buyi was respected by officials and commoners for his authority and trustworthiness.

entries.zh: 每行縣、錄囚徒還，其母輒問不疑：「有所平反？
entries.en: Whenever he toured the counties and returned from reviewing prisoners, his mother would ask Buyi, "Were any cases reversed?
entries.literal: Whenever he toured the counties and returned from recording prisoners, his mother would ask Buyi: "Were any cases reversed?

entries.zh: 活幾何人？」
entries.en: How many people were spared?"
entries.literal: How many people were spared?"

entries.zh: 即不疑多有所平反，母喜笑異於他時；
entries.en: If Buyi had reversed many cases, his mother would laugh with joy unlike at other times;
entries.literal: If Buyi had reversed many cases, his mother would laugh with joy unlike at other times;

entries.zh: 或無所出，母怒，為不食。
entries.en: if there were none, his mother grew angry and refused to eat.
entries.literal: if there were none, his mother grew angry and would not eat.

entries.zh: 故不疑為吏，嚴而不殘。
entries.en: For this reason Buyi as an official was stern but not cruel.
entries.literal: For this reason Buyi as an official was stern but not cruel.

entries.zh: 九月，丙子，秺敬侯金日磾薨。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Marquis Jing of Di Jin Midi died.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on bingzi, Marquis Jing of Di Jin Midi died.

entries.zh: 初，武帝病，有遺詔，封金日磾為秺侯，上官桀為安陽侯，霍光為博陸侯；
entries.en: At the outset, when Emperor Wu was ill, a testamentary edict enfeoffed Jin Midi as Marquis of Di, Shangguan Jie as Marquis of Anyang, and Huo Guang as Marquis of Bolu;
entries.literal: At the outset, when Emperor Wu was ill, there was a testamentary edict enfeoffing Jin Midi as Marquis of Di, Shangguan Jie as Marquis of Anyang, and Huo Guang as Marquis of Bolu;

entries.zh: 皆以前捕反者馬何羅等功封。
entries.en: all were enfeoffed for their former merit in capturing the rebel Ma Heluo and others.
entries.literal: all were enfeoffed for their former merit in capturing the rebel Ma Heluo and others.

entries.zh: 日磾以帝少，不受封，光等亦不敢受。
entries.en: Midi, because the emperor was young, did not accept the enfeoffment; Guang and the others also did not dare accept.
entries.literal: Midi, because the emperor was young, did not accept the enfeoffment; Guang and the others also did not dare accept.

entries.zh: 及日磾病困，光白封，日磾臥受印綬；
entries.en: When Midi's illness grew critical, Guang reported and enfeoffed him; Midi received the seal and ribbon while lying down;
entries.literal: When Midi's illness grew critical, Guang reported and enfeoffed him; Midi received the seal and ribbon while lying down;

entries.zh: 一日薨。
entries.en: and died the next day.
entries.literal: and died the next day.

entries.zh: 日磾兩子賞、建俱侍中，與帝略同年，共臥起。
entries.en: Midi's two sons Shang and Jian were both Palace Attendants, roughly the emperor's age, sharing bed and rising with him.
entries.literal: Midi's two sons Shang and Jian were both Palace Attendants, roughly the emperor's age, sharing bed and rising together.

entries.zh: 賞為奉車，建駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Shang was Director of the Imperial Carriage; Jian was Commandant of the Palace Steeds.
entries.literal: Shang was Director of the Imperial Carriage; Jian was Commandant of the Palace Steeds.

entries.zh: 及賞嗣侯，佩兩綬，上謂霍將軍曰：「金氏兄弟兩人，不可使俱兩綬邪？」
entries.en: When Shang succeeded to the marquisate and wore two ribbons, the emperor said to General Huo, "The two Jin brothers—could they not both wear two ribbons?"
entries.literal: When Shang succeeded to the marquisate and wore two ribbons, the emperor said to General Huo: "The two Jin brothers—could they not both wear two ribbons?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「賞自嗣父為侯耳。」
entries.en: He replied, "Shang has merely succeeded his father as marquis."
entries.literal: He replied: "Shang has merely succeeded his father as marquis."

entries.zh: 上笑曰：「侯不在我與將軍乎？」
entries.en: The emperor laughed and said, "Are marquisates not in my hands and yours?"
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Are marquisates not in my hands and the general's?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「先帝之約，有功乃得封侯。」
entries.en: He replied, "The former emperor's covenant: only with merit may one be enfeoffed as marquis."
entries.literal: He replied: "The former emperor's covenant: only with merit may one be enfeoffed as marquis."

entries.zh: 遂止。
entries.en: The matter thereupon ceased.
entries.literal: The matter thereupon ceased.

entries.zh: 閏月，遣故廷尉王平等五人持節行郡國，舉賢良，問民疾苦、冤、失職者。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, former Minister of Justice Wang Ping and five others were sent with credentials to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, recommend the worthy and good, and inquire into popular suffering, wrongs, and dereliction of duty.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, the former Minister of Justice Wang Ping and five others were sent with credentials to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, recommend the worthy and good, and inquire into the people's suffering, wrongs, and dereliction of duty.

entries.zh: 冬，無冰。
entries.en: In winter there was no ice.
entries.literal: In winter, there was no ice.

entries.zh: 春，正月，封大將軍光為博陸侯，左將軍桀為安陽侯。
entries.en: In spring, the first month, Grand General Guang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bolu and Left General Jie as Marquis of Anyang.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, Grand General Guang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Bolu and Left General Jie as Marquis of Anyang.

entries.zh: 或說霍光曰：「將軍不見諸呂之事乎？
entries.en: Someone said to Huo Guang, "General, have you not seen what befell the Lü clan?
entries.literal: Someone said to Huo Guang: "General, have you not seen what befell the Lü clan?

entries.zh: 處伊尹、周公之位，攝政擅權，而背宗室，不與共職，是以天下不信，卒至於滅亡。
entries.en: Occupying the positions of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, holding regency and monopolizing power, yet turning your back on the imperial clan and not sharing office with them—for this reason the realm did not trust them, and they ended in extinction.
entries.literal: Occupying the positions of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, holding regency and monopolizing power, yet turning your back on the imperial clan and not sharing office with them—for this reason all under Heaven did not trust them, and they ended in extinction.

entries.zh: 今將軍當盛位，帝春秋富，宜納宗室，又多與大臣共事，反諸呂道。
entries.en: Now you occupy a flourishing position and the emperor is still young; you ought to bring in the imperial clan and share many affairs with the great ministers—reversing the Lü path.
entries.literal: Now the general occupies a flourishing position and the emperor's years are still rich; you ought to bring in the imperial clan and share many affairs with the great ministers—reversing the way of the Lü.

entries.zh: 如是，則可以免患。」
entries.en: If so, you may escape calamity."
entries.literal: If so, you may escape calamity."

entries.zh: 光然之，乃擇宗室可用者，遂拜楚元王孫辟疆及宗室劉長樂皆為光祿大夫，辟疆守長樂衛尉。
entries.en: Guang assented; he selected usable members of the imperial clan and appointed King Yuan of Chu's grandson Pijiang and clansman Liu Changle both Palace Grandees, with Pijiang serving as Commandant of the Guards for Changle.
entries.literal: Guang assented; he thereupon selected usable members of the imperial clan and appointed the grandson of King Yuan of Chu, Pijiang, and the clansman Liu Changle both as Palace Grandees, with Pijiang holding office as Commandant of the Guards for Changle.

entries.zh: 三月，遣使者振貸貧民無種、食者。
entries.en: In the third month envoys were sent to relieve and lend to poor commoners without seed or food.
entries.literal: In the third month, envoys were sent to relieve and lend to poor commoners without seed or food.

entries.zh: 秋，八月，詔曰：「往年災害多，今年蠶、麥傷，所振貸種、食勿收責，毋令民出今年田租。」
entries.en: In autumn, the eighth month, an edict said, "Disasters were many in former years; this year silkworms and wheat were harmed. Do not collect repayment for the seed and food that were relieved and lent; do not make the people pay this year's field tax."
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, an edict said: "In former years disasters were many; this year silkworms and wheat were harmed. The seed and food that were relieved and lent—do not collect repayment; do not make the people pay this year's field tax."

entries.zh: 初，武帝征伐匈奴，深入窮追，二十餘年，匈奴馬畜孕重墮殰，罷極，苦之。
entries.en: At the outset Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu, driving deep in relentless pursuit for more than twenty years; Xiongnu horses and livestock, pregnant and heavy, miscarried and perished; exhausted to the limit, they suffered bitterly.
entries.literal: At the outset, Emperor Wu campaigned against the Xiongnu, driving deep in relentless pursuit for more than twenty years; the Xiongnu's horses and livestock, pregnant and heavy, miscarried and perished; exhausted to the limit, they suffered bitterly.

entries.zh: 常有欲和親意，未能得。
entries.en: They often wished for heqin peace but could not achieve it.
entries.literal: They often had the intent to seek heqin peace but could not achieve it.

entries.zh: 狐鹿孤單于有異母弟為左大都尉，賢，國人鄉之，母閼氏恐單于不立子而立左大都尉也，乃私使殺之。
entries.en: Chanyu Hulu Gu had a younger half-brother who was Left Grand Commandant and worthy; the people looked toward him. The chanyu's mother, the Yanzhi consort, feared the chanyu would not establish his son but would establish the Left Grand Commandant, and secretly had him killed.
entries.literal: The chanyu Hulu Gu had a younger half-brother who was Left Grand Commandant, worthy; the people of the state looked toward him. The chanyu's mother, the Yanzhi consort, feared the chanyu would not establish his son but would establish the Left Grand Commandant, and secretly had him killed.

entries.zh: 左大都尉同母兄怨，遂不肯復會單于庭。
entries.en: The Left Grand Commandant's elder brother by the same mother bore resentment and refused to attend the chanyu's court again.
entries.literal: The Left Grand Commandant's elder brother by the same mother bore resentment and thereupon refused to attend the chanyu's court again.

entries.zh: 是歲，單于病且死，謂諸貴人：「我子少，不能治國，立弟右谷蠡王。」
entries.en: That year the chanyu was ill and near death; he told the nobles, "My son is young and cannot govern the state; establish my younger brother, the Right Guli King."
entries.literal: That year the chanyu was ill and near death; he told the nobles: "My son is young and cannot govern the state; establish my younger brother, the Right Guli King."

entries.zh: 及單于死，衛律等與顓渠閼氏謀，匿其喪，矯單于令，更立子左谷蠡王為壺衍鞮單于。
entries.en: When the chanyu died, Wei Lü and others plotted with Zhuanqu Yanzhi, concealed his death, forged the chanyu's command, and instead established his son, the Left Guli King, as Chanyu Huyandi.
entries.literal: When the chanyu died, Wei Lü and others plotted with Zhuanqu Yanzhi, concealed his death, forged the chanyu's command, and instead established his son, the Left Guli King, as chanyu Huyandi.

entries.zh: 左賢王、右谷蠡王怨望，率其眾欲南歸漢，恐不能自致，即脅盧屠王，欲與西降烏孫。
entries.en: The Left Worthy King and the Right Guli King harbored resentment; they led their followers wishing to return south to Han, fearing they could not reach it on their own, and coerced the Lutu King, intending to surrender west to the Wusun.
entries.literal: The Left Worthy King and the Right Guli King harbored resentment; they led their followers wishing to return south to Han, fearing they could not reach it on their own, and thereupon coerced the Lutu King, intending to descend west and surrender to the Wusun.

entries.zh: 盧屠王告之單于，使人驗問，右谷蠡王不服，反以其罪罪盧屠王，國人皆冤之。
entries.en: The Lutu King reported it to the chanyu; investigators were sent. The Right Guli King would not submit and instead charged the Lutu King with that very crime; the people all considered it unjust.
entries.literal: The Lutu King reported it to the chanyu; men were sent to investigate and question. The Right Guli King would not submit and instead charged the Lutu King with that very crime; the people of the state all considered it unjust.

entries.zh: 於是二王去居其所，不復肯會龍城，匈奴始衰。
entries.en: Thereupon the two kings departed to their own territories and would no longer attend at Dragon City; the Xiongnu began to decline.
entries.literal: Thereupon the two kings departed to dwell in their own places and would no longer attend at Dragon City; the Xiongnu began to decline.

entries.zh: 春，正月，追尊帝外祖趙父為順成侯。
entries.en: In spring, the first month, the emperor's maternal grandfather, Father Zhao, was posthumously honored as Marquis of Shuncheng.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor's maternal grandfather, Father Zhao, was posthumously honored as Marquis of Shuncheng.

entries.zh: 順成侯有姊君姁，賜錢二百萬、奴婢、第宅以充實焉。
entries.en: Marquis of Shuncheng had an elder sister, Junxu; she was granted two million cash, slaves and maidservants, and a mansion to enrich her establishment.
entries.literal: Marquis of Shuncheng had an elder sister, Junxu; she was granted two million cash, slaves and maidservants, and a mansion to enrich her establishment.

entries.zh: 諸昆弟各以親疏受賞賜，無在位者。
entries.en: The various siblings each received rewards according to closeness of kin; none held office.
entries.literal: The various brothers and sisters each received rewards according to closeness of kin; none held office.

entries.zh: 有男子乘黃犢車詣北闕，自謂衛太子；
entries.en: A man riding a yellow calf-drawn carriage came to the Northern Gate Tower and declared himself Crown Prince Wei;
entries.literal: A man riding a yellow calf-drawn carriage came to the Northern Gate Tower and declared himself the Heir of Wei;

entries.zh: 公車以聞。
entries.en: the Imperial Carriage Office reported it.
entries.literal: the Imperial Carriage Office reported it.

entries.zh: 詔使公、卿、將軍、中二千石雜識視。
entries.en: An edict ordered dukes, ministers, generals, and officials at two thousand bushels and above jointly to identify and examine him.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the dukes, ministers, generals, and officials at two thousand bushels and above jointly to identify and examine him.

entries.zh: 長安中吏民聚觀者數萬人。
entries.en: Tens of thousands of Chang'an officials and commoners gathered to watch.
entries.literal: Officials and commoners of Chang'an gathered to watch—tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 右將軍勒兵闕下以備非常。
entries.en: The Right General arrayed troops below the gate tower to guard against the unexpected.
entries.literal: The Right General arrayed troops below the gate tower to guard against the unexpected.

entries.zh: 丞相、御史、中二千石至者並莫敢發言。
entries.en: The chancellor, censor, and officials at two thousand bushels and above who arrived all dared not speak.
entries.literal: The chancellor, censor, and officials at two thousand bushels and above who arrived all did not dare speak.

entries.zh: 京兆尹不疑後到，叱從吏收縛。
entries.en: Metropolitan Commandant Buyi arrived later and shouted at his clerks to seize and bind him.
entries.literal: Metropolitan Commandant Buyi arrived later and shouted at his attending clerks to seize and bind him.

entries.zh: 或曰：「是非未可知，且安之。」
entries.en: Someone said, "Whether this is true or false is not yet known; for now let him be."
entries.literal: Someone said: "Whether this is true or false is not yet known; for now let him be at ease."

entries.zh: 不疑曰：「諸君何患於衛太子！
entries.en: Buyi said, "Why do you gentlemen worry about Crown Prince Wei!
entries.literal: Buyi said: "Why do you gentlemen worry about the Heir of Wei!

entries.zh: 昔蒯聵違命出奔，輒距而不納，《春秋》是之。
entries.en: In former times Kuai Kui disobeyed orders and fled abroad; Ji Zhe barred him and would not admit him—the Spring and Autumn Annals approves this.
entries.literal: In former times Kuai Kui disobeyed orders and fled abroad; Ji Zhe barred him and would not admit him—the Spring and Autumn Annals approves this.

entries.zh: 衛太子得罪先帝，亡不即死，今來自詣，此罪人也！」
entries.en: Crown Prince Wei offended the former emperor, fled and did not die at once; now he has come of his own accord—this man is a criminal!"
entries.literal: The Heir of Wei offended the former emperor, fled and did not die at once; now he has come of his own accord—this man is a criminal!"

entries.zh: 遂送詔獄。
entries.en: He was thereupon sent to the imperial prison under edict.
entries.literal: He was thereupon sent to the imperial prison under edict.

entries.zh: 天子與大將軍霍光聞而嘉之曰：「公卿大臣當用有經術、明於大誼者。」
entries.en: The emperor and Grand General Huo Guang heard of it and praised him, saying, "Dukes, ministers, and great officials ought to employ those versed in the classics and clear on great principle."
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven and Grand General Huo Guang heard of it and praised him, saying: "Dukes, ministers, and great officials ought to employ those versed in the classics and clear on great principle."

entries.zh: 繇是不疑名聲重於朝廷，在位者皆自以不及也。
entries.en: From this Buyi's reputation weighed heavy at court; those in office all considered themselves his inferior.
entries.literal: From this Buyi's reputation weighed heavy in court; those in office all considered themselves his inferior.

entries.zh: 廷尉驗治何人，竟得奸詐，本夏陽人，姓成，名方遂，居湖，以卜筮為事。
entries.en: The Minister of Justice investigated: who was this man? At last the fraud was exposed. He was originally from Xiayang, surname Cheng, personal name Fang Sui, living at Hu, who made his living by divination.
entries.literal: The Minister of Justice investigated and tried: who was this man? At last the fraud was obtained. He was originally a man of Xiayang, surname Cheng, personal name Fang Sui, dwelling at Hu, who made divination by milfoil and tortoise his trade.

entries.zh: 有故太子舍人嘗從方遂卜，謂曰：「子狀貌甚似衛太子。」
entries.en: A former crown prince's palace attendant had once had Fang Sui divine for him and said, "Your appearance greatly resembles Crown Prince Wei."
entries.literal: A former Palace Attendant of the heir had once had Fang Sui divine for him and said to him: "Your appearance greatly resembles the Heir of Wei."

entries.zh: 方遂心利其言，冀得以富貴。
entries.en: Fang Sui's heart seized on his words and hoped thereby to gain wealth and rank.
entries.literal: Fang Sui's heart profited by his words and hoped thereby to gain wealth and rank.

entries.zh: 坐誣罔不道，要斬。
entries.en: Convicted of false accusation and impiety, he was beheaded at the waist.
entries.literal: Convicted of false accusation and impiety, he was beheaded at the waist.

entries.zh: 夏，六月，封上官安為桑樂侯。
entries.en: In summer, the sixth month, Shangguan An was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sangle.
entries.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Shangguan An was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sangle.

entries.zh: 安日以驕淫，受賜殿中，對賓客言：「與我婿飲，大樂！」
entries.en: An grew daily more arrogant and dissolute; receiving gifts in the palace hall, he said to guests, "Drink with my son-in-law—what joy!"
entries.literal: An daily grew arrogant and dissolute; receiving gifts in the palace hall, he said to guests: "Drink with my son-in-law—great joy!"

entries.zh: 見其服飾，使人歸，欲自燒物。
entries.en: Seeing their clothing and adornments, he had people go home, intending to burn their possessions.
entries.literal: Seeing their clothing and adornments, he had people return home, wishing to burn their possessions.

entries.zh: 子病死，仰而罵天。
entries.en: When his son died of illness, he looked up and cursed Heaven.
entries.literal: When his son died of illness, he looked up and cursed Heaven.

entries.zh: 其頑悖如此。
entries.en: His obstinate perversity was like this.
entries.literal: His obstinate perversity was like this.

entries.zh: 罷儋耳、真番郡。
entries.en: The Dan'er and Zhenfan commanderies were abolished.
entries.literal: The Dan'er and Zhenfan commanderies were abolished.

entries.zh: 秋，大鴻臚廣明、軍正王平擊益州，斬首、捕虜三萬餘人，獲畜產五萬餘頭。
entries.en: In autumn, Grand Herald Guangming and Army Rectifier Wang Ping attacked Yizhou, beheading and capturing more than thirty thousand men and taking more than fifty thousand head of livestock.
entries.literal: In autumn, Grand Herald Guangming and Army Rectifier Wang Ping attacked Yizhou; heads cut off and captives taken exceeded thirty thousand, and livestock obtained exceeded fifty thousand head.

entries.zh: 諫大夫杜延年見國家承武帝奢侈、師旅之後，數為大將軍光言：「年歲比不登，流民未盡還，宜修孝文時政，示以儉約、寬和，順天心，說民意，年歲宜應。」
entries.en: Remonstrance Grandee Du Yannian, seeing the state inherit Emperor Wu's extravagance and campaigns, repeatedly told Grand General Guang, "Harvests have failed year after year and displaced people have not all returned. It is fitting to restore Emperor Wen's policies, show frugality, restraint, lenience, and harmony, accord with Heaven's heart, please the people, and the years ought to respond."
entries.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Du Yannian, seeing the state inherit Emperor Wu's extravagance and campaigns, repeatedly spoke to Grand General Guang: "Years in succession have not had good harvests; displaced people have not all returned—it is fitting to restore Emperor Wen's policies, show frugality and restraint and lenience and harmony, accord with Heaven's heart, please the people's intent, and the years ought to respond."

entries.zh: 光納其言。
entries.en: Guang accepted his counsel.
entries.literal: Guang accepted his words.

entries.zh: 延年，故御史大夫周之子也。
entries.en: Yannian was a son of the former Censor-in-Chief Du Zhou.
entries.literal: Yannian was a son of the former Censor-in-Chief Zhou.

entries.zh: 春，二月，詔有司問郡國所舉賢良、文學，民所疾苦、教化之要，皆對：「願罷鹽、鐵、酒榷、均輸官，毋與天下爭利，示以儉節，然後教化可興。」
entries.en: In spring, the second month, an edict had the responsible offices question the worthy and learned men recommended by commanderies and kingdoms on the people's hardships and the essentials of moral instruction. All replied, "We wish to abolish the salt, iron, wine monopoly, and equalizing transport offices, stop contending with all under Heaven for profit, show frugality and restraint, and only then can moral instruction flourish."
entries.literal: In spring, the second month, an edict had the responsible offices question the worthy and learned men recommended by commanderies and kingdoms on the people's hardships and essentials of instruction and transformation; all replied: "We wish to abolish the salt, iron, wine monopoly, and equalizing transport offices, not contend with all under Heaven for profit, show frugality and restraint, and only then can instruction and transformation be raised."

entries.zh: 桑弘羊難，以為：「此國家大業，所以制四夷，安邊足用之本，不可廢也。」
entries.en: Sang Hongyang objected, saying, "This is the state's great enterprise, the foundation for controlling the four barbarians and securing the borders with sufficient resources—it cannot be abolished."
entries.literal: Sang Hongyang objected, holding: "This is the state's great enterprise, the foundation for controlling the four barbarians and securing the borders with sufficient resources—it cannot be abolished."

entries.zh: 於是鹽鐵之議起焉。
entries.en: Thereupon the salt-and-iron debate arose.
entries.literal: Thereupon the salt-and-iron debate arose.

entries.zh: 初，蘇武既徙北海上，稟食不至，掘野鼠、去草實而食之。
entries.en: At first, after Su Wu had been relocated to the North Sea coast, allotted food did not arrive; he dug up wild rats and stripped grass seeds to eat.
entries.literal: At first, after Su Wu had been relocated to the North Sea coast, allotted food did not arrive; he dug wild rats and removed grass seeds and ate them.

entries.zh: 杖漢節牧羊，臥起操持，節旄盡落。
entries.en: Leaning on the Han staff of office he herded sheep; whether lying down or rising he held it in hand, until the tassels on the staff had all fallen off.
entries.literal: Leaning on the Han staff of office he herded sheep; lying down and rising he held it in hand—the tassels on the staff all fell off.

entries.zh: 武在漢，與李陵俱為侍中；
entries.en: In Han, Wu and Li Ling had both served as Palace Attendants;
entries.literal: Wu in Han had together with Li Ling served as Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 陵降匈奴，不敢求武。
entries.en: Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu and did not dare seek out Wu.
entries.literal: Ling surrendered to the Xiongnu and did not dare seek Wu.

entries.zh: 久之，單于使陵至海上，為武置酒設樂，因謂武曰：「單于聞陵與子卿素厚，故使來說足下，虛心欲相待，終不得歸漢，空自苦；
entries.en: After a long time the Chanyu sent Ling to the sea coast, set out wine and music for Wu, and said to him, "The Chanyu heard that Ling and Ziqing were always close, and therefore sent me to persuade you, my lord. His heart is open and he wishes to treat you well, but in the end you cannot return to Han and only suffer in vain;
entries.literal: After long time the Chanyu sent Ling to the sea coast, set out wine and music for Wu, and thereby said to Wu: "The Chanyu heard Ling and Ziqing were always close, therefore sent me to persuade you, my lord—the heart is open and wishes to treat you well; in the end you cannot return to Han and vainly suffer yourself;

entries.zh: 亡人之地，信義安所見乎！
entries.en: in a land of lost men, where is faith and righteousness to be shown!
entries.literal: in a land of lost men, where is faith and righteousness to be shown!

entries.zh: 足下兄弟二人，前皆坐事自殺；
entries.en: Your lordship's two brothers were both earlier convicted of offenses and killed themselves;
entries.literal: Your lordship's two brothers before both sat convicted of offenses and killed themselves;

entries.zh: 來時，太夫人已不幸；
entries.en: when you came, your mother had already died;
entries.literal: when you came, the Grand Lady had already met misfortune;

entries.zh: 子卿婦年少，聞已更嫁矣；
entries.en: Ziqing's wife is young—I hear she has already remarried;
entries.literal: Ziqing's wife is young—I hear she has already remarried;

entries.zh: 獨有女弟二人、兩女、一男，今復十餘年，存亡不可知。
entries.en: only two younger sisters, two daughters, and one son remain; now more than ten years have passed again, and whether they live or die cannot be known.
entries.literal: only two younger sisters, two daughters, and one son remain; now again more than ten years—whether alive or dead cannot be known.

entries.zh: 人生如朝露，何久自苦如此！
entries.en: Human life is like morning dew—why long suffer yourself like this!
entries.literal: Human life is like morning dew—why long suffer yourself like this!

entries.zh: 陵始降時，忽忽如狂，自痛負漢，加以老母系保宮。
entries.en: When Ling first surrendered, he was restless as if mad, pained at having failed Han, and moreover his old mother was detained in the protection palace.
entries.literal: When Ling first surrendered, he was restless as if mad, himself pained at having failed Han, and moreover his old mother was detained in the protection palace.

entries.zh: 子卿不欲降，何以過陵！
entries.en: Ziqing does not wish to surrender—how are you better than Ling!
entries.literal: Ziqing does not wish to surrender—how does he surpass Ling!

entries.zh: 且陛下春秋高，法令無常，大臣無罪夷滅者數十家。
entries.en: Moreover the emperor is advanced in years, laws and orders are erratic, and several tens of families of guiltless great ministers have been exterminated root and branch.
entries.literal: Moreover the emperor's years are advanced, laws and orders are without constancy, and great ministers without guilt exterminated root and branch number several tens of families.

entries.zh: 安危不可知，子卿尚復誰為乎！」
entries.en: Safety and danger cannot be known—for whom do you still act, Ziqing!"
entries.literal: Safety and danger cannot be known—Ziqing, for whom do you still act!"

entries.zh: 武曰：「武父子無功德，皆為陛下所成就，位列將，爵通侯，兄弟親近，常願肝腦塗地。
entries.en: Wu said, "Wu father and son had no merit—all was accomplished by Your Majesty. We ranked as generals, were enfeoffed as full marquises, and as close brothers constantly wished to lay down our lives.
entries.literal: Wu said: "Wu father and son had no merit or virtue—all were accomplished by Your Majesty; we ranked as generals, enfeoffed as full marquises, brothers close and near, and constantly wished to smear liver and brain on the ground.

entries.zh: 今得殺身自效，雖斧鉞、湯鑊，誠甘樂之！
entries.en: Now to be able to give my life in service, though it be axe and halberd or boiling cauldron, I would truly and gladly accept it!
entries.literal: Now obtaining to kill the body and devote effect, though axe and halberd, boiling cauldron, truly I would gladly enjoy it!

entries.zh: 臣事君，猶子事父也。
entries.en: A subject serving his lord is like a son serving his father.
entries.literal: A subject serving his lord is like a son serving his father.

entries.zh: 子為父死，無所恨。
entries.en: A son dying for his father has nothing to regret.
entries.literal: A son dying for his father has nothing to regret.

entries.zh: 願勿復再言！」
entries.en: Please do not speak of this again!"
entries.literal: I wish you would not speak again!"

entries.zh: 陵與武飲數日，復曰：「子卿壹聽陵言！」
entries.en: Ling drank with Wu for several days, then again said, "Ziqing, please wholly heed my words!"
entries.literal: Ling drank with Wu for several days, then again said: "Ziqing, wholly listen to Ling's words!"

entries.zh: 武曰：「自分已死久矣，王必欲降武，請畢今日之歡，效死於前！」
entries.en: Wu said, "I have long considered myself dead. If you must have Wu surrender, please finish today's pleasure and I will die before you!"
entries.literal: Wu said: "I myself have judged myself dead long ago. If the king must have Wu surrender, please finish today's pleasure and I will devote death before you!"

entries.zh: 陵見其至誠，喟然歎曰：「嗟乎，義士！
entries.en: Ling saw his utmost sincerity and sighed with emotion, "Alas, a man of righteousness!
entries.literal: Ling saw his utmost sincerity and sighed with emotion: "Alas, a man of righteousness!

entries.zh: 陵與衛律之罪上通於天！」
entries.en: Ling's and Wei Lü's guilt reaches up to Heaven!"
entries.literal: Ling's and Wei Lü's guilt reaches up to Heaven!"

entries.zh: 因泣下沾衿，與武決去。
entries.en: Thereupon tears fell and soaked his collar; he took leave of Wu and departed.
entries.literal: Thereupon tears fell and soaked his collar; he took leave of Wu and departed.

entries.zh: 賜武牛羊數十頭。
entries.en: He bestowed on Wu several tens of cattle and sheep.
entries.literal: He bestowed on Wu several tens of cattle and sheep.

entries.zh: 後陵復至北海上，語武以武帝崩。
entries.en: Later Ling again came to the North Sea coast and told Wu that Emperor Wu had died.
entries.literal: Later Ling again came to the North Sea coast and told Wu that Emperor Wu had died.

entries.zh: 武南鄉號哭歐血，旦夕臨，數月。
entries.en: Wu faced south and wailed until he vomited blood; morning and evening he faced south in mourning for several months.
entries.literal: Wu faced south and wailed, vomiting blood; morning and evening he faced the direction in mourning for several months.

entries.zh: 及壺衍鞮單于立，母閼氏不正，國內乖離，常恐漢兵襲之，於是衛律為單于謀，與漢和親。
entries.en: When Chanyu Huyanshidi was established, the queen mother's position was irregular, the state was divided within, and they constantly feared Han troops would strike; thereupon Wei Lü schemed for the Chanyu and sought peace kinship with Han.
entries.literal: When Chanyu Huyanshidi was established, the mother's yanzhi was not correct, the state within was divided and estranged, and they constantly feared Han troops would strike them; thereupon Wei Lü schemed for the Chanyu and made peace kinship with Han.

entries.zh: 漢使至，求蘇武等，匈奴詭言武死。
entries.en: Han envoys arrived and sought Su Wu and the rest; the Xiongnu falsely claimed Wu was dead.
entries.literal: Han envoys arrived and sought Su Wu and the rest; the Xiongnu falsely said Wu was dead.

entries.zh: 後漢使復至匈奴，常惠私見漢使，教使者謂單于，言：「天子射上林中，得雁，足有系帛書，言武等在某澤中。」
entries.en: Later Han envoys again reached the Xiongnu; Chang Hui privately met the Han envoy and taught him to tell the Chanyu, saying, "The emperor shot in Shanglin Park and obtained a wild goose; on its foot was tied a silk message saying Wu and the rest are in a certain marsh."
entries.literal: Later Han envoys again reached the Xiongnu; Chang Hui privately saw the Han envoy and taught the envoy to tell the Chanyu, saying: "The Son of Heaven shot in Shanglin Park and obtained a wild goose; on its foot was tied a silk book saying Wu and the rest are in a certain marsh."

entries.zh: 使者大喜，如惠語以讓單于。
entries.en: The envoy was greatly pleased and, as Hui had said, reproached the Chanyu.
entries.literal: The envoy was greatly pleased and, as Hui's words directed, reproached the Chanyu.

entries.zh: 單于視左右而驚，謝漢使曰：「武等實在。」
entries.en: The Chanyu looked left and right in alarm and apologized to the Han envoy, "Wu and the rest truly still live."
entries.literal: The Chanyu looked left and right in alarm and apologized to the Han envoy: "Wu and the rest truly exist."

entries.zh: 乃歸武及馬宏等。
entries.en: Thereupon he returned Wu and Ma Hong and the rest.
entries.literal: Thereupon he returned Wu and Ma Hong and the rest.

entries.zh: 馬宏者，前副光祿大夫王忠使西國，為匈奴所遮；
entries.en: Ma Hong had formerly been deputy to Palace Illustrious Grandee Wang Zhong on a mission to western states and was intercepted by the Xiongnu;
entries.literal: Ma Hong was formerly deputy to Palace Illustrious Grandee Wang Zhong on a mission to western states and was intercepted by the Xiongnu;

entries.zh: 忠戰死，馬宏生得，亦不肯降。
entries.en: Zhong died in battle; Ma Hong was taken alive and also would not surrender.
entries.literal: Zhong died in battle; Ma Hong was taken alive and also would not surrender.

entries.zh: 故匈奴歸此二人，欲以通善意。
entries.en: Therefore the Xiongnu returned these two men, wishing thereby to signal good intent.
entries.literal: Therefore the Xiongnu returned these two men, wishing thereby to open good intent.

entries.zh: 於是李陵置酒賀武曰：「今足下還歸，揚名於匈奴，功顯於漢室，雖古竹帛所載，丹青所畫，何以過子卿！
entries.en: Thereupon Li Ling set out wine to congratulate Wu, saying, "Now your lordship returns home, your fame raised among the Xiongnu and your merit displayed in the Han house—even what ancient bamboo and silk record and paintings depict, how could they surpass Ziqing!
entries.literal: Thereupon Li Ling set out wine to congratulate Wu, saying: "Now your lordship returns home, fame raised among the Xiongnu, merit displayed in the Han house—even what ancient bamboo and silk record and red and green paint, how could they surpass Ziqing!

entries.zh: 陵雖駑怯，令漢貰陵罪，全其老母，使得奮大辱之積志，庶幾乎曹柯之盟，此陵宿昔之所不忘也。
entries.en: Ling is dull and timid, but if Han would pardon Ling's guilt, preserve his old mother, and let him exert the will long accumulated from great disgrace, perhaps like the covenant at Cao Ke—this Ling has never forgotten from of old.
entries.literal: Ling though dull and timid—if Han would pardon Ling's guilt, preserve his old mother, and let him be able to exert the long-accumulated will of great disgrace, perhaps like the Cao Ke covenant—this Ling from old nights has not forgotten.

entries.zh: 收族陵家，為世大戮，陵尚復何顧乎！
entries.en: His clan was gathered and exterminated—the age's great punishment—what does Ling still care for!
entries.literal: His clan was gathered and exterminated—an age's great punishment—what does Ling still care for!

entries.zh: 已矣，令子卿知吾心耳！」
entries.en: It is done—let Ziqing know my heart!"
entries.literal: It is done—let Ziqing know my heart!"

entries.zh: 陵泣下數行，因與武決。
entries.en: Ling wept several lines of tears and thereupon took leave of Wu.
entries.literal: Ling wept several lines of tears and thereupon took leave of Wu.

entries.zh: 單于召會武官屬，前已降及物故，凡隨武還者九人。
entries.en: The Chanyu summoned and assembled Wu's official subordinates; counting those who had earlier surrendered and those who had died, in all nine followed Wu back.
entries.literal: The Chanyu summoned and assembled Wu's official subordinates; those who had earlier surrendered and those who had died—in all nine followed Wu back.

entries.zh: 既至京師，詔武奉一太牢謁武帝園廟，拜為典屬國，秩中二千石，賜錢二百萬，公田二頃，宅一區。
entries.en: Once they reached the capital, an edict had Wu offer a grand sacrificial victim and visit Emperor Wu's park temple; he was appointed Director of Dependent States at rank of middle two thousand dan, bestowed two million cash, two qing of public fields, and one residence.
entries.literal: Once they reached the capital, an edict had Wu offer one grand sacrificial victim and visit Emperor Wu's park temple; he was appointed Director of Dependent States, rank middle two thousand dan, bestowed two million cash, two qing of public fields, and one residence.

entries.zh: 武留匈奴凡十九歲，始以強壯出，及還，鬚髮盡白。
entries.en: Wu remained among the Xiongnu nineteen years in all; he had gone forth in his prime, and on return his beard and hair were all white.
entries.literal: Wu remained among the Xiongnu in all nineteen years; he went forth in his prime strength, and on return his beard and hair were all white.

entries.zh: 霍光、上官桀與李陵素善，遣陵故人隴西任立政等三人俱至匈奴招之。
entries.en: Huo Guang, Shangguan Jie, and Li Ling had always been on good terms; they sent Ling's old acquaintance Ren Lizheng of Longxi and three others together to the Xiongnu to summon him.
entries.literal: Huo Guang, Shangguan Jie, and Li Ling had always been on good terms; they sent Ling's old acquaintance Ren Lizheng of Longxi and three others together to the Xiongnu to summon him.

entries.zh: 陵曰：「歸易耳，丈夫不能再辱！」
entries.en: Ling said, "Returning is easy, but a man cannot suffer disgrace twice!"
entries.literal: Ling said: "Returning is easy—but a man cannot suffer disgrace twice!"

entries.zh: 遂死於匈奴。
entries.en: Thereupon he died among the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Thereupon he died among the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 夏，旱。
entries.en: In summer, there was drought.
entries.literal: In summer, drought.

entries.zh: 秋，七月，罷榷酤官，從賢良、文學之議也。
entries.en: In autumn, the seventh month, the wine monopoly offices were abolished, following the counsel of the worthy and learned.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the wine monopoly offices were abolished, following the counsel of the worthy and learned.

entries.zh: 武帝之末，海內虛耗，戶口減半，霍光知時務之要，輕徭薄賦，與民休息。
entries.en: At the end of Emperor Wu's reign the realm was depleted and household registers were halved; Huo Guang knew the essentials of the times, lightened corvée and reduced levies, and gave the people rest.
entries.literal: At the end of Emperor Wu's reign, within the seas was empty and depleted and household registers were halved; Huo Guang knew the essentials of the times' affairs, lightened corvée and reduced levies, and gave the people rest.

entries.zh: 至是匈奴和親，百姓充實，稍復文、景之業焉。
entries.en: By this time the Xiongnu made peace kinship, the common people were prosperous, and the realm slightly restored the achievements of Emperors Wen and Jing.
entries.literal: By this time the Xiongnu made peace kinship, the common people were full and solid, and they slightly restored the enterprises of Emperors Wen and Jing.

entries.zh: 詔以鉤町侯毋波率其邑君長、人民擊反者有功，立以為鉤町王。
entries.en: An edict, because Marquis of Goujing Wubo had led his town chiefs, elders, and people to strike rebels with merit, established him as King of Goujing.
entries.literal: An edict because Marquis of Goujing Wubo led his town chiefs and elders and people to strike rebels with merit established him as King of Goujing.

entries.zh: 賜田廣明爵關內侯。
entries.en: Tian Guangming was bestowed the noble rank of Marquis within the Passes.
entries.literal: Tian Guangming was bestowed the noble rank of Marquis within the Passes.

entries.zh: 春，正月，泰山有大石自起立；
entries.en: In spring, the first month, on Mount Tai a great stone by itself stood up;
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on Mount Tai a great stone by itself stood up;

entries.zh: 上林有柳樹枯僵自起生；
entries.en: in Shanglin a willow tree, dead and stiff, by itself rose and lived;
entries.literal: in Shanglin a willow tree, dead and stiff, by itself rose and lived;

entries.zh: 有蟲食其葉成文，曰「公孫病已立」。
entries.en: insects ate its leaves forming characters saying "Gongsun Bingyi established."
entries.literal: insects ate its leaves forming characters saying "Gongsun Bingyi established."

entries.zh: 符節令魯國眭弘上書，言：「大石自立，僵柳復起，當有匹庶為天子者。
entries.en: Staff-and-tally Director Sui Hong of Lu submitted a memorial, saying, "The great stone stood by itself, the stiff willow revived—there ought to be a commoner who becomes Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Staff-and-tally Director Sui Hong of Lu submitted a memorial, saying: "The great stone stood by itself, the stiff willow revived—there ought to be a commoner who becomes Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 枯樹復生，故廢之家公孫氏當復興乎？
entries.en: A dead tree revives—perhaps the Gongsun clan of the abolished house should revive?
entries.literal: A dead tree revives—perhaps the Gongsun clan of the abolished house should revive?

entries.zh: 漢家承堯之後，有傳國之運，當求賢人禪帝位，退自封百里，以順天命。」
entries.en: The House of Han succeeds after Yao and has the fortune to transmit the state—one should seek a worthy man and yield the imperial throne, retire and enfeoff oneself with a hundred li, to accord with Heaven's mandate."
entries.literal: The House of Han succeeds after Yao and has the fortune to transmit the state—one should seek a worthy man and yield the imperial throne, retire and enfeoff oneself with a hundred li, to accord with Heaven's mandate."

entries.zh: 弘坐設妖言惑眾伏誅。
entries.en: Hong was punished for setting up freakish words to delude the masses and was executed.
entries.literal: Hong was punished for setting up freakish words to delude the masses and was executed.

entries.zh: 匈奴單于使犁汙王窺邊，言酒泉、張掖兵益弱，出兵試擊，冀可復得其地。
entries.en: The Xiongnu Chanyu sent King Liwu to spy on the border, saying Jiuquan and Zhangye troops were growing weaker—send troops to try striking, hoping to recover their territory.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu Chanyu sent King Liwu to spy on the border, saying Jiuquan and Zhangye troops were growing weaker—send troops to try striking, hoping to recover their territory.

entries.zh: 時漢先得降者，聞其計，天子詔邊警備。
entries.en: At this time Han first obtained surrenderers and heard their plan; the Son of Heaven issued an edict the border to warn and prepare.
entries.literal: At this time Han first obtained surrenderers and heard their plan; the Son of Heaven issued an edict the border to warn and prepare.

entries.zh: 後無幾，右賢王、犁汙王四千騎分三隊，入日勒、屋蘭、番和。
entries.en: Not long after, the Wise King of the Right and King Liwu with four thousand horsemen divided into three columns and entered Rile, Wulan, and Fanhe.
entries.literal: Not long after, the Wise King of the Right and King Liwu with four thousand horsemen divided into three columns and entered Rile, Wulan, and Fanhe.

entries.zh: 張掖太守、屬國都尉發兵擊，大破之，得脫者數百人。
entries.en: The Administrator of Zhangye and Commandant of the Dependent State raised troops and struck, greatly defeated them; those who escaped were several hundred.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Zhangye and Commandant of the Dependent State raised troops and struck, greatly defeated them; those who escaped were several hundred.

entries.zh: 屬國義渠王射殺犁汙王，賜黃金二百斤，馬二百匹，因封為犁汙王。
entries.en: King Yiqu of the Dependent State shot and killed King Liwu; he was granted two hundred jin of gold and two hundred horses, and thereby enfeoffed as King Liwu.
entries.literal: King Yiqu of the Dependent State shot and killed King Liwu; he was granted two hundred jin of gold and two hundred horses, and thereby enfeoffed as King Liwu.

entries.zh: 自是後，匈奴不敢入張掖。
entries.en: From this afterward the Xiongnu did not dare enter Zhangye.
entries.literal: From this afterward the Xiongnu did not dare enter Zhangye.

entries.zh: 燕、蓋之亂，桑弘羊子遷亡，過父故吏侯史吳，後遷捕得，伏法。
entries.en: In the Yan and Gaishan disorder, Sang Hongyang's son Qian fled, passed his father's old clerk Marquis-History Wu; later Qian was captured and punished by law.
entries.literal: In the Yan and Gaishan disorder, Sang Hongyang's son Qian fled, passed his father's old clerk Marquis-History Wu; later Qian was captured and punished by law.

entries.zh: 會赦，侯史吳自出繫獄。
entries.en: An amnesty occurred; Marquis-History Wu of himself came out of imprisonment.
entries.literal: An amnesty occurred; Marquis-History Wu of himself came out of imprisonment.

entries.zh: 廷尉王平、少府徐仁雜治反事，皆以為「桑遷坐父謀反而侯史吳臧之，非匿反者，乃匿為隨者也」，即以赦令除吳罪。
entries.en: Director of Justice Wang Ping and Privy Treasurer Xu Ren jointly tried the rebellion affair; all thought "Qian sat under his father's plotting rebellion and Marquis-History Wu hid him—not hiding a rebel but hiding a follower"—and thereby by the amnesty edict removed Wu's crime.
entries.literal: Director of Justice Wang Ping and Privy Treasurer Xu Ren jointly tried the rebellion affair; all thought "Qian sat under his father's plotting rebellion and Marquis-History Wu hid him—not hiding a rebel but hiding a follower"—and thereby by the amnesty edict removed Wu's crime.

entries.zh: 後侍御史治實，以「桑遷通經術，知父謀反而不諫爭，與反者身無異。
entries.en: Later the attendant censor investigated the facts and held that "Qian mastered the classics, knew his father plotted rebellion yet did not remonstrate and contend—in person no different from rebels.
entries.literal: Later the attendant censor investigated the facts and held that "Qian mastered the classics, knew his father plotted rebellion yet did not remonstrate and contend—in person no different from rebels.

entries.zh: 侯史吳故三百石吏，首匿遷，不與庶人匿隨從者等，吳不得赦。」
entries.en: Marquis-History Wu was formerly an official of three hundred bushels who first hid Qian—not equal to commoners hiding followers—Wu could not receive amnesty."
entries.literal: Marquis-History Wu was formerly an official of three hundred bushels who first hid Qian—not equal to commoners hiding followers—Wu could not receive amnesty."

entries.zh: 奏請覆治，劾廷尉、少府縱反者。
entries.en: The memorial requested renewed trial and impeached the Director of Justice and Privy Treasurer for indulging rebels.
entries.literal: The memorial requested renewed trial and impeached the Director of Justice and Privy Treasurer for indulging rebels.

entries.zh: 少府徐仁，即丞相車千秋女婿也，故千秋數為侯史吳言；
entries.en: Privy Treasurer Xu Ren was Chancellor Che Qianqiu's son-in-law; therefore Qianqiu repeatedly spoke for Marquis-History Wu;
entries.literal: Privy Treasurer Xu Ren was Chancellor Che Qianqiu's son-in-law; therefore Qianqiu repeatedly spoke for Marquis-History Wu;

entries.zh: 恐大將軍光不聽，千秋即召中二千石、博士會公車門，議問吳法。
entries.en: fearing Grand General Guang would not listen, Qianqiu then summoned officials of the middle two thousand bushels and erudites to meet at the Public Carriage Gate and discuss and question Wu's law.
entries.literal: fearing Grand General Guang would not listen, Qianqiu then summoned officials of the middle two thousand bushels and erudites to meet at the Public Carriage Gate and discuss and question Wu's law.

entries.zh: 議者知大將軍指，皆執吳為不道。
entries.en: The discussants knew the Grand General's intent and all held Wu as lawless.
entries.literal: The discussants knew the Grand General's intent and all held Wu as lawless.

entries.zh: 明日，千秋封上眾議。
entries.en: The next day Qianqiu sealed and sent up the collective discussion.
entries.literal: The next day Qianqiu sealed and sent up the collective discussion.

entries.zh: 光於是以千秋擅召中二千石以下，外內異言，遂下廷尉平、少府仁獄。
entries.en: Guang thereupon because Qianqiu on his own authority summoned middle two thousand bushels and below, with outer and inner differing words, sent down Director of Justice Ping and Privy Treasurer Ren to prison.
entries.literal: Guang thereupon because Qianqiu on his own authority summoned middle two thousand bushels and below, with outer and inner differing words, sent down Director of Justice Ping and Privy Treasurer Ren to prison.

entries.zh: 朝廷皆恐丞相坐之。
entries.en: The court all feared the Chancellor would be implicated.
entries.literal: The court all feared the Chancellor would be implicated.

entries.zh: 太僕杜延年奏記光曰：「吏縱罪人，有常法。
entries.en: Grand Coachman Du Yanian submitted a note to Guang, saying, "Officials who indulge criminals have a regular law.
entries.literal: Grand Coachman Du Yanian submitted a note to Guang, saying: "Officials who indulge criminals have a regular law.

entries.zh: 今更詆吳為不道，恐於法深。
entries.en: Now again denouncing Wu as lawless—I fear it is deep in the law.
entries.literal: Now again denouncing Wu as lawless—your subject fears it is deep in the law.

entries.zh: 又，丞相素無所守持而為好言於下，盡其素行也。
entries.en: Moreover, the Chancellor by nature has nothing he holds to and speaks kindly to those below—that is fully his usual conduct.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Chancellor by nature has nothing he holds to and speaks kindly to those below—that is fully his usual conduct.

entries.zh: 至擅召中二千石，甚無狀。
entries.en: As for on his own authority summoning middle two thousand bushels—that is very lawless.
entries.literal: As for on his own authority summoning middle two thousand bushels—that is very lawless.

entries.zh: 延年愚以為丞相久故及先帝用事，非有大故，不可棄也。
entries.en: Yanian foolishly thinks the Chancellor is long in office and served the late emperor—without a great cause he cannot be abandoned.
entries.literal: Yanian foolishly thinks the Chancellor is long in office and served the late emperor—without a great cause he cannot be abandoned.

entries.zh: 間者民頗言獄深，吏為峻詆；
entries.en: Of late the people have often said the prisons are harsh and officials make severe accusations;
entries.literal: Of late the people have often said the prisons are deep and harsh, and the officials make severe slander;

entries.zh: 今丞相所議，又獄事也，如是以及丞相，恐不合眾心，群下讙嘩，庶人私議，流言四布。
entries.en: now what the Chancellor discusses is again a prison matter; if it extends to the Chancellor in this fashion, I fear it will not accord with popular sentiment—the officials will clamor, commoners will gossip privately, and rumors will spread everywhere.
entries.literal: now what the Chancellor discusses is again a prison matter; if in this fashion it extends to the Chancellor, I fear it will not accord with the hearts of the multitude—the ranks below will clamor, commoners will privately discuss, and floating slander will spread in all directions.

entries.zh: 延年竊重將軍失此名於天下也。」
entries.en: Yannian privately fears the General will lose this reputation throughout the realm."
entries.literal: Yannian privately fears the General will lose this reputation under Heaven."

entries.zh: 光以廷尉、少府弄法輕重，卒下之獄。
entries.en: Guang, because the Director of Justice and the Minister Steward had manipulated the law regarding severity, finally sent them to prison.
entries.literal: Guang, because the Director of Justice and the Minister Steward manipulated the law regarding severity, finally sent them to prison.

entries.zh: 夏，四月，仁自殺，平與左馮翊賈勝胡皆要斬。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, Ren committed suicide; Ping and Left Governor of Anding Jia Shenghu were all executed by waist chop.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Ren committed suicide; Ping and the Left Governor of Anding Jia Shenghu were all executed by waist chop.

entries.zh: 而不以及丞相，終與相竟。
entries.en: Yet he did not extend the matter to the Chancellor; in the end he still came to a final contest with the Chancellor.
entries.literal: Yet he did not extend it to the Chancellor; in the end he still contended with the Chancellor to the finish.

entries.zh: 延年論議持平，合和朝廷，皆此類也。
entries.en: Yannian's discussions were even-handed and harmonized the court—all were of this sort.
entries.literal: Yannian's discussions and judgments were even-handed and harmonized the court—all were of this sort.

entries.zh: 冬，遼東烏桓反。
entries.en: In winter, the Wuhuan of Liaodong rebelled.
entries.literal: In winter, the Wuhuan of Liaodong rebelled.

entries.zh: 初，冒頓破東胡，東胡餘眾散保烏桓及鮮卑山為二族，世役屬匈奴。
entries.en: Initially Modun defeated the Eastern Hu; the Eastern Hu remnant peoples scattered and took refuge on the Wuhuan and Xianbei mountains as two peoples, for generations subject to corvée and allegiance to the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Initially Modun broke the Eastern Hu; the Eastern Hu's remaining masses scattered and took refuge on Wuhuan and Xianbei mountains as two peoples, generation after generation subject to corvée and allegiance to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 武帝出破匈奴左地，因徙烏桓於上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼東塞外，為漢偵察匈奴動靜。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu campaigned and broke the Xiongnu's left territory, he moved the Wuhuan beyond the passes of Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, and Liaodong to spy on Xiongnu movements for Han.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu went out and broke the Xiongnu's left territory; he thereupon moved the Wuhuan to beyond the passes of Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, and Liaodong, to spy on the Xiongnu's movements for Han.

entries.zh: 置護烏桓校尉監領之，使不得與匈奴交通。
entries.en: He appointed a Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan to oversee them, so they could not communicate with the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: He set a Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan to oversee and lead them, so they could not communicate with the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 至是，部眾漸強，遂反。
entries.en: By this time their tribes had gradually grown strong, and they rebelled.
entries.literal: At this time their tribal masses gradually grew strong, and they thereupon rebelled.

entries.zh: 起旃蒙協洽，盡柔兆敦牂，凡十二年。
entries.en: From Zhanmeng Xiehe through Rouzhao Dunjiang—twelve years in all.
entries.literal: From Zhanmeng Xiehe through Rouzhao Dunjiang; twelve years in all.

entries.zh: 春，正月，上始行幸甘泉，郊泰畤，三月，行幸河東，祠后土。
entries.en: In spring, the first month, the emperor first traveled to Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar; in the third month he traveled to Hedong and sacrificed to the Queen of Earth.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor first undertook the journey to favor Sweet Springs and sacrificed at the Great Altar; in the third month he undertook the journey to favor Hedong and sacrificed to the Queen of Earth.

entries.zh: 上頗修武帝故事，謹齋祀之禮，以方士言增置神祠；
entries.en: The emperor largely revived Emperor Wu's ways, carefully observing fasting and sacrifice; on fangshi advice he added shrines;
entries.literal: The emperor largely restored Emperor Wu's practices, carefully observing fasting and sacrificial rites; on the word of fangshi he added divine shrines;

entries.zh: 聞益州有金馬、碧雞之神，可醮祭而致，於是遣諫大夫蜀郡王褒使持節而求之。
entries.en: hearing that Yizhou held the spirits of the Golden Horse and Green Cock, whom libation could summon, he dispatched Remonstrance Grandee Wang Bao of Shu as envoy bearing credentials to seek them.
entries.literal: hearing that in Yizhou were the spirits of the Golden Horse and Green Cock, whom libation-sacrifice could summon, he thereupon dispatched Remonstrance Grandee Wang Bao of Shu commandery as envoy bearing credentials to seek them.

entries.zh: 起上章涒灘，盡玄黓閹茂，凡三年。
entries.en: From Shangzhang Tuntan through Xuanji Yanmao—three years in all.
entries.literal: From Shangzhang Tuntan through Xuanji Yanmao; three years in all.

entries.zh: :班固贊曰：古之制名，必由象類，遠取諸物，近取諸身。
entries.en: Ban Gu writes in praise: In antiquity names were fashioned from images and categories—drawing from distant things and from the body itself.
entries.literal: Ban Gu's praise says: In antiquity naming was made necessarily from images and categories—taking from distant things, taking from the near body.

entries.zh: 故《經》謂君為元首，臣為股肱，明其一體，相待而成也。
entries.en: Therefore the Classic calls the ruler the head and limbs and ministers the thighs and arms—making clear they are one body that rely on each other to be whole.
entries.literal: Therefore the Classic calls the ruler the head and limbs, ministers the thighs and arms—making clear they are one body, mutually relying to be completed.

entries.zh: 是故君臣相配，古今常道，自然之勢也。
entries.en: Therefore ruler and ministers match each other—the constant way of past and present and the natural order.
entries.literal: Therefore ruler and ministers match each other—the constant way of past and present, the natural tendency.

entries.zh: 近觀漢相，高祖開基，蕭、曹為冠；
entries.en: Observing Han chancellors at hand: Gaozu laid the foundation, and Xiao and Cao were foremost;
entries.literal: Observing Han chancellors near at hand: Gaozu opened the foundation, Xiao and Cao were foremost;

entries.zh: 孝宣中興，丙、魏有聲。
entries.en: In Emperor Xuan's restoration, Bing and Wei won renown.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiao's restoration, Bing and Wei had renown.

entries.zh: 是時黜陟有序，眾職修理，公卿多稱其位，海內興於禮讓。
entries.en: At that time promotion and demotion were orderly, offices well maintained, ministers and grandees mostly filled their posts, and courtesy and yielding flourished throughout the realm.
entries.literal: At that time promotion and demotion were orderly, the multitude of offices well maintained, ministers and grandees mostly filled their posts, and within the seas courtesy and yielding flourished.

entries.zh: 覽其行事，豈虛虖哉！
entries.en: Review their conduct—was it empty indeed!
entries.literal: Reviewing their conduct—was it empty indeed!

entries.zh: 二月，壬辰，黃霸為丞相。
entries.en: In the second month, on day renchen, Huang Ba became chancellor.
entries.literal: Second month, day renchen: Huang Ba became chancellor.

entries.zh: 霸材長於治民，及為丞相，功名損於治郡。
entries.en: Ba excelled at governing the people; as chancellor his fame and achievement fell short of his record as commandery governor.
entries.literal: Ba's talent lay in governing the people; when he became chancellor, his fame and achievement fell short of governing a commandery.

entries.zh: 時京兆尹張敞捨鶡雀飛集丞相府，霸以為神雀，議欲以聞。
entries.en: At that time Metropolitan Governor Zhang Chang had a magpie from his lodging fly to the chancellor's residence; Ba took it for a divine bird and considered reporting it.
entries.literal: At that time Metropolitan Governor Zhang Chang's lodging had a magpie fly and gather at the chancellor's residence; Ba took it for a divine bird and deliberated wishing to report it.

entries.zh: 敞奏霸曰：「竊見丞相請與中二千石、博士雜問郡、國上計長史、守丞為民興利除害，成大化，條其對。
entries.en: Chang memorialized to Ba, "Your servant has seen the chancellor request to join ranked officials at two thousand shi and academicians in questioning the commandery and state annual-report chief clerks and administrators on benefiting the people and removing harm, accomplishing great transformation, and itemizing their replies.
entries.literal: Chang memorialized to Ba, saying: "Your servant has seen the chancellor request to join with ranked officials at two thousand shi and academicians in mixed questioning of the commandery and state annual-report chief clerks and administrators on benefiting the people and removing harm, accomplishing great transformation, and itemizing their replies.

entries.zh: 有耕者讓畔，男女異路，道不拾遺。
entries.en: There were farmers yielding field boundaries, men and women on separate roads, and no picking up lost things on the road.
entries.literal: There were farmers yielding field boundaries, men and women on separate roads, and no picking up lost things on the road.

entries.zh: 及舉孝子、貞婦者為一輩，先上殿；
entries.en: Those who presented filial sons and chaste wives formed one class and entered the hall first;
entries.literal: Those who presented filial sons and chaste wives formed one class and entered the hall first;

entries.zh: 舉而不知其人數者，次之；
entries.en: those who presented them without knowing the persons' names came next;
entries.literal: those who presented them without knowing the persons' names came next;

entries.zh: 不為條教者在後。
entries.en: those who did not make regulations and teachings came last.
entries.literal: those who did not make regulations and teachings came last.

entries.zh: 叩頭謝丞相，雖口不言，而心欲其為之也。
entries.en: They kowtowed and thanked the chancellor; though they did not speak aloud, they wished in their hearts to do it.
entries.literal: They kowtowed and thanked the chancellor; though the mouth did not speak, the heart wished them to do it.

entries.zh: 長史、守丞對時，臣敞舍有鶡雀飛止丞相府屋上，丞相以下見者數百人。
entries.en: When the chief clerks and administrators replied, a magpie from your servant Chang's lodging flew and perched on the chancellor's roof; from the chancellor down, several hundred people saw it.
entries.literal: When the chief clerks and administrators replied, your servant Chang's lodging had a magpie fly and perch on the chancellor's residence roof; from the chancellor down, those who saw it numbered several hundred.

entries.zh: 邊吏多知鶡雀者，問之，皆陽不知。
entries.en: Many frontier officials knew magpies; when asked, all pretended ignorance.
entries.literal: Many frontier officials knew magpies; when asked, all pretended not to know.

entries.zh: 丞相圖議上奏曰：『臣問上計長史、守丞以興化條，皇天報下神爵。』
entries.en: The chancellor drafted a memorial saying, 'Your servant questioned the annual-report chief clerks and administrators on items for promoting transformation—August Heaven responded by sending down the divine bird.'
entries.literal: The chancellor drafted deliberation to memorialize upward, saying: 'Your servant questioned the annual-report chief clerks and administrators on items for promoting transformation—August Heaven responded by sending down the divine bird.'

entries.zh: 後知從臣敞舍來，乃止。
entries.en: Learning later it came from your servant Chang's lodging, he stopped.
entries.literal: Later learning it came from your servant Chang's lodging, he stopped.

entries.zh: 郡國吏竊笑丞相仁厚有知略，微信奇怪也。
entries.en: Commandery and state officials privately laughed that the chancellor, though benevolent and wise, still slightly believed in the strange.
entries.literal: Commandery and state officials privately laughed that the chancellor, though benevolent and thick and possessed of knowledge and strategy, still slightly believed in the strange.

entries.zh: 臣敞非敢毀丞相也，誠恐群臣莫白，而長史、守丞畏丞相指，歸捨法令，各為私教，務相增加，澆淳散樸，並行偽貌，有名亡實，傾搖解怠，甚者為妖。
entries.en: Your servant Chang does not dare slander the chancellor—he truly fears the ministers will not speak plainly, while chief clerks and administrators, fearing the chancellor's intent, set aside laws and ordinances, each making private teachings and striving to outdo one another, watering down purity and scattering simplicity, all practicing false appearances with name but no substance, growing lax and negligent, and in extreme cases becoming demonic.
entries.literal: Your servant Chang does not dare destroy the chancellor—he truly fears the ministers will not speak plainly, while chief clerks and administrators, fearing the chancellor's intent, return and set aside laws and ordinances, each making private teachings, striving to outdo one another, watering down purity and scattering simplicity, all practicing false appearances, having name without substance, leaning and wavering in slackness, and in extreme cases becoming demonic.

entries.zh: 假令京師先行讓畔、異路、道不拾遺，其實亡益廉貪、貞淫之行，而以偽先天下，固未可也。
entries.en: Suppose the capital region first practiced yielding boundaries, separate roads, and not picking up lost things—in truth it would not improve honest or greedy conduct or chaste or licentious behavior, yet with falsity leading the empire, that truly could not be approved.
entries.literal: Suppose the capital region first practiced yielding boundaries, separate roads, and not picking up lost things on the road—in truth it would not benefit honest and greedy conduct or chaste and licentious behavior, yet with falsity leading all under Heaven, it truly could not be approved.

entries.zh: 即諸侯先行之，偽聲軼於京師，非細事也。
entries.en: If the feudal lords practiced it first, false reputation would outrun the capital—not a small matter.
entries.literal: If the feudal lords practiced it first, false reputation would outrun the capital region—not a small matter.

entries.zh: 漢家承敝通變，造起律令，所以勸善禁奸，條貫詳備，不可復加。
entries.en: The House of Han inherited decline and adapted through change, creating laws and ordinances to encourage good and forbid wickedness—provisions thorough and complete, not to be added to again.
entries.literal: The House of Han inherited decline and adapted through change, creating laws and ordinances to encourage good and forbid wickedness—articles thorough and complete, not to be added to again.

entries.zh: 宜令貴臣明飭長史、守丞，歸告二千石，舉三老、孝弟、力田、孝廉、廉吏，務得其人，郡事皆以法令為檢式，毋得擅為條教；
entries.en: Noble ministers ought clearly to instruct chief clerks and administrators to tell the two-thousand-shi officials to present the three elders, filial and brotherly men, strength-in-farming men, filial and incorrupt candidates, and honest officials, striving to obtain the right men; commandery affairs should all take laws and ordinances as the standard, and none may on their own authority make regulations and teachings;
entries.literal: One ought to order noble ministers clearly to instruct chief clerks and administrators, return and tell the two-thousand-shi officials, present the three elders, filial and brotherly, strength-in-farming, filial and incorrupt, and honest officials, striving to obtain the right men; commandery affairs should all take laws and ordinances as models and measures, and none may on their own authority make regulations and teachings;

entries.zh: 敢挾詐偽以干名譽者，必先受戮，以正明好惡。」
entries.en: whoever dares to rely on fraud and falsity to seek fame and reputation should first be punished, to rectify likes and dislikes."
entries.literal: whoever dares to rely on fraud and falsity to seek fame and reputation should first receive punishment, to rectify and clarify likes and dislikes."

entries.zh: 天子嘉納敞言，召上計吏，使侍中臨飭，如敞指意。
entries.en: The emperor praised and accepted Chang's words, summoned the annual-report clerks, and had a palace attendant oversee and instruct them according to Chang's intent.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven praised and accepted Chang's words, summoned the annual-report clerks, and had a palace attendant oversee and instruct them according to Chang's intent.

entries.zh: 霸甚慚。
entries.en: Ba was deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: Ba was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: :臣光曰：以孝宣之明，魏相、丙吉為丞相，于定國為廷尉，而趙、蓋、韓、楊之死皆不厭眾心，惜哉，其為善政之累大矣！
entries.en: Your servant Guang says: With Emperor Xuan's clarity, Wei Xiang and Bing Ji as chancellors, and Yu Dingguo as Minister of Justice, yet the deaths of Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang all failed to satisfy popular sentiment-alas, how great the burden on good government!
entries.literal: Your servant Guang says: With Emperor Xiao Xuan's clarity, Wei Xiang and Bing Ji as chancellors, and Yu Dingguo as Minister of Justice, yet the deaths of Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang all failed to satisfy the people's hearts-alas, how great the burden on good government!

entries.zh: 《周官》司寇之法，有議賢、議能。
entries.en: In the Zhou Offices, the Minister of Crime's law provides deliberation for the worthy and deliberation for the capable.
entries.literal: In the Zhou Offices, the Minister of Crime's law has deliberation for the worthy and deliberation for the capable.

entries.zh: 若廣漢、延壽之治民，可不謂能乎！
entries.en: If Guanghan and Yanshou's governing of the people—can they not be called capable!
entries.literal: If Guanghan and Yanshou's governing of the people—can they not be called capable!

entries.zh: 寬饒、惲之剛直，可不謂賢乎！
entries.en: Kuanrao and Yun's firm uprightness—can they not be called worthy!
entries.literal: Kuanrao and Yun's firm uprightness—can they not be called worthy!

entries.zh: 然則雖有死罪，猶將宥之，況罪不足以死乎！
entries.en: If so, though there were a death offense, one would still pardon them—how much more when the offense did not warrant death!
entries.literal: If so, though there were a death offense, one would still pardon them—how much more when the offense was not enough to die!

entries.zh: 揚子以韓馮翊之愬蕭為臣之自失。
entries.en: Master Yang held that Governor of Han, Fengyi's suing Xiao was a minister losing himself.
entries.literal: Master Yang held that Governor of Han, Fengyi's suing Xiao was a minister's losing himself.

entries.zh: 夫所以使延壽犯上者，望之激之也。
entries.en: What made Yanshou offend his superior was Wang Zhi provoking him.
entries.literal: What made Yanshou offend his superior was Wang Zhi's provoking him.

entries.zh: 上不之察，而延壽獨蒙其辜，不亦甚哉！
entries.en: The emperor did not examine it, yet Yanshou alone bore the guilt—is it not extreme!
entries.literal: The emperor did not examine it, yet Yanshou alone bore the guilt—is it not extreme!

entries.zh: 匈奴閏振單于率其眾東擊郅支單于。
entries.en: Chanyu Runzhen of the Xiongnu led his forces east to attack Chanyu Zhizhi.
entries.literal: Chanyu Runzhen of the Xiongnu led his masses east to attack Chanyu Zhizhi.

entries.zh: 郅支與戰，殺之，併其兵；
entries.en: Zhizhi fought him, killed him, and absorbed his troops;
entries.literal: Zhizhi fought with him, killed him, and merged his troops;

entries.zh: 遂進攻呼韓邪。
entries.en: then he advanced to attack Huhanye.
entries.literal: thereupon he advanced to attack Huhanye.

entries.zh: 呼韓邪兵敗走，郅支都單于庭。
entries.en: Huhanye was defeated and fled; Zhizhi occupied the Chanyu's court.
entries.literal: Huhanye's army was defeated and fled; Zhizhi occupied the Chanyu's court.

entries.zh: :臣光曰：王霸無異道。
entries.en: Minister Guang said: The ways of king and hegemon are not different paths.
entries.literal: Minister Guang said: The ways of king and hegemon are not different paths.

entries.zh: 昔三代之隆，禮樂、征伐自天子出，則謂之王。
entries.en: In antiquity at the height of the Three Dynasties, when rites, music, and campaigns issued from the Son of Heaven, it was called kingship.
entries.literal: In antiquity at the height of the Three Dynasties, when rites and music and campaigns and punishments issued from the Son of Heaven, it was called kingship.

entries.zh: 天子微弱不能治諸侯，諸侯有能率其與國同討不庭以尊王室者，則謂之霸。
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven was weak and could not govern the feudal lords, and a lord was able to lead allied states to punish the disobedient and honor the royal house, it was called hegemony.
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven was weak and could not govern the feudal lords, and a feudal lord was able to lead the states allied with him jointly to punish the disobedient and honor the royal house, it was called hegemony.

entries.zh: 其所以行之也，皆本仁祖義，任賢使能，賞善罰惡，禁暴誅亂。
entries.en: The means by which both were carried out all took benevolence as root and righteousness as model, employed the worthy, rewarded good and punished evil, and forbade violence.
entries.literal: The means by which they were carried out all took benevolence as root and righteousness as model, employed the worthy and used the able, rewarded good and punished evil, forbade violence and executed disorder.

entries.zh: 顧名位有尊卑，德澤有深淺，功業有鉅細，政令有廣狹耳，非若白黑、甘苦之相反也。
entries.en: Only that rank had high and low, favor had depth, achievements had scale, and orders had scope—that is all; it is not like black and white or sweet and bitter in opposition.
entries.literal: Only that name and position had high and low, virtue's favor had deep and shallow, achievements had large and small, and government orders had broad and narrow—that is all; it is not like black and white or sweet and bitter in mutual opposition.

entries.zh: 漢之所以不能復三代之治者，由人主之不為，非先王之道不可復行於後世也。
entries.en: The reason Han could not restore Three Dynasties governance was that rulers did not do it—not that the former kings' Way could not be practiced again.
entries.literal: The reason Han could not restore the governance of the Three Dynasties was that the human ruler did not do it—not that the former kings' Way could not again be practiced in later generations.

entries.zh: 夫儒有君子，有小人。
entries.en: Among Confucians there are gentlemen and petty men.
entries.literal: Among Confucians there are gentlemen and there are petty men.

entries.zh: 彼俗儒者，誠不足與為治也，獨不可求真儒而用之乎？
entries.en: Those vulgar Confucians truly are not fit to govern with—but cannot one seek true Confucians and employ them?
entries.literal: Those vulgar Confucians truly are not fit to govern with—but can one alone not seek true Confucians and employ them?

entries.zh: 稷、契、皋陶、伯益、伊尹、周公、孔子，皆大儒也，使漢得而用之，功烈豈若是而止邪！
entries.en: Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius were all great Confucians; had Han obtained and employed them, would achievements have stopped at this!
entries.literal: Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius were all great Confucians; had Han obtained and employed them, would achievements and glory have stopped like this!

entries.zh: 孝宣謂太子懦而不立，闇於治體，必亂我家，則可矣；
entries.en: Emperor Xuan's saying the heir apparent was weak, unfit to stand, ignorant of governance, and would disorder his house—that could pass;
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan's saying the heir apparent was weak and could not stand, dark to the body of governance, and would surely disorder his house—that could pass;

entries.zh: 乃曰王道不可行，儒者不可用，豈不過甚矣哉！
entries.en: yet to say the kingly Way could not be practiced and Confucians could not be employed—was that not going too far!
entries.literal: yet to say the kingly Way could not be practiced and Confucians could not be employed—was that not going too far!

entries.zh: 殆非所以訓示子孫，垂法將來者也。
entries.en: It was hardly the way to instruct posterity or hand down law for the future.
entries.literal: It was nearly not the means to instruct and show sons and grandsons or to hand down law for the future.

entries.zh: 淮陽憲王好法律，聰達有材；
entries.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was fond of law, clever and talented;
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was fond of law, clever and penetrating with talent;

entries.zh: 王母張婕妤尤幸。
entries.en: his queen mother, Lady Zhang the Beautiful Companion, was especially favored.
entries.literal: his queen mother, Lady Zhang the Beautiful Companion, was especially favored.

entries.zh: 上由是疏太子而愛淮陽憲王，數嗟歎憲王曰：「真我子也！」
entries.en: The emperor thereby grew distant from the heir apparent and loved Prince Xian of Huaiyang, repeatedly sighing and saying, "Truly my son!"
entries.literal: The emperor thereby grew distant from the heir apparent and loved Prince Xian of Huaiyang, repeatedly sighing in admiration of the prince and saying: "Truly my son!"

entries.zh: 常有意欲立憲王，然用太子起於微細，上少依倚許氏，及即位而許后以殺死，故弗忍也。
entries.en: He constantly intended to establish Prince Xian, yet because the heir apparent had risen from humble origins, the emperor in youth had relied on the Xu clan, and after accession Empress Xu died by execution, he could not bear to do it.
entries.literal: He constantly had intent to establish Prince Xian, yet because the heir apparent had risen from minute origins and the emperor in youth had relied on the Xu clan, and after accession the Empress Xu died by killing, he therefore could not bear it.

entries.zh: 久之，上拜韋玄成為淮陽中尉，以玄成嘗讓爵于兄，欲以感諭憲王。
entries.en: After a long time, the emperor appointed Wei Xuancheng Commandant of Huaiyang, because Xuancheng had once yielded his noble rank to his elder brother, wishing thereby to instruct Prince Xian by example.
entries.literal: After a long time, the emperor appointed Wei Xuancheng as Commandant of Huaiyang, because Xuancheng had once yielded his noble rank to his elder brother, wishing thereby to move and instruct Prince Xian.

entries.zh: 由是太子遂安。
entries.en: Thereby the heir apparent was at last secure.
entries.literal: Thereby the heir apparent was at last secure.

entries.zh: 匈奴呼韓邪單于之敗也，左伊秩訾王為呼韓邪計，勸令稱臣入朝事漢，從漢求助，如此，匈奴乃定。
entries.en: When Chanyu Huhanye of the Xiongnu was defeated, the Left Yizhi Zhi King advised him to declare himself a subject, attend court, and serve Han, seeking Han's aid—thus the Xiongnu would be settled.
entries.literal: When the Xiongnu Chanyu Huhanye was defeated, the Left Yizhi Zhi King made a plan for Huhanye, urging him to declare himself a subject, enter court, and serve Han, follow Han to seek aid—thus the Xiongnu would be settled.

entries.zh: 呼韓邪問諸大臣，皆曰：「不可。
entries.en: Huhanye asked the great ministers; all said, "It cannot be done.
entries.literal: Huhanye asked the various great ministers; all said: "It cannot be done.

entries.zh: 匈奴之俗，本上氣力而下服役，以馬上戰鬥為國，故有威名於百蠻。
entries.en: Xiongnu custom esteems strength above and servitude below; taking battle on horseback as the foundation of state, they have prestige among the hundred barbarians.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu custom esteems above physical strength and below servitude; taking battle on horseback as the state, therefore they have a prestigious name among the hundred barbarians.

entries.zh: 戰死，壯士所有也。
entries.en: To die in battle is a stalwart man's portion.
entries.literal: To die in battle is what a stalwart man possesses.

entries.zh: 今兄弟爭國，不在兄則在弟，雖死猶有威名，子孫常長諸國。
entries.en: Now brothers contend for the state—if not the elder then the younger; though one dies he still wins prestige, and sons and grandsons will long lead the various states.
entries.literal: Now brothers contend for the state—if not the elder brother then the younger; though one dies he still has a prestigious name, and sons and grandsons constantly lead the various states.

entries.zh: 漢雖強，猶不能兼併匈奴。
entries.en: Though Han is strong, it still cannot annex the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: Though Han is strong, it still cannot annex and merge the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 奈何亂先古之制，臣事於漢，卑辱先單于，為諸國所笑！
entries.en: How can we overturn ancient institutions, serve Han as subjects, humiliate the former Chanyu, and become a laughingstock to the various states!
