entries.literal: How can we disorder the institutions of former antiquity, serve Han as subjects, and humiliate the former Chanyu, becoming what the various states laugh at!

entries.zh: 雖如是而安，何以復長百蠻！」
entries.en: Even if we were secure thus, how could we again lead the hundred barbarians!"
entries.literal: Even if we were secure thus, how could we again lead the hundred barbarians!"

entries.zh: 左伊秩訾曰：「不然，強弱有時。
entries.en: The Left Yizhi Zhi said, "It is not so—strength and weakness have their seasons.
entries.literal: The Left Yizhi Zhi said: "It is not so—strength and weakness have their seasons.

entries.zh: 今漢方盛，烏孫城郭諸國皆為臣妾。
entries.en: Now Han is flourishing; the walled states of Wusun and all the rest have become Han subjects.
entries.literal: Now Han is flourishing; the walled states of Wusun and all the rest have become subjects and concubines.

entries.zh: 自且鞮侯單于以來，匈奴日削，不能取復，雖屈強於此，未嘗一日安也。
entries.en: Since Chanyu Qiedihou, the Xiongnu have daily dwindled and could not recover; though they bent their strength here, they never had a day of peace.
entries.literal: From the time of Chanyu Qiedihou onward, the Xiongnu daily dwindled and could not recover; though they bent their strength here, they never had a single day of peace.

entries.zh: 今事漢則安存，不事則危亡，計何以過此！」
entries.en: Now to serve Han is security; not to serve is extinction—what plan surpasses this!"
entries.literal: Now to serve Han is security and survival; not to serve is peril and extinction—what plan surpasses this!"

entries.zh: 諸大人相難久之，呼韓邪從其計，引眾南近塞，遣子右賢王銖婁渠堂入侍。
entries.en: The great men disputed for a long time; Huhanye followed his plan, led his people south near the border, and sent his son the Right Wise King Zhu Louqu Tang to attend court.
entries.literal: The various great men disputed one another for a long time; Huhanye followed his plan, led his masses south near the passes, and sent his son the Right Wise King Zhu Louqu Tang to enter and attend court.

entries.zh: 郅支單于亦遣子右大將駒于利受入侍。
entries.en: Chanyu Zhizhi also sent his son the Right Grand General Juyu Lishou to attend court.
entries.literal: Chanyu Zhizhi also sent his son the Right Grand General Juyu Lishou to enter and attend court.

entries.zh: 二月，丁巳，樂成敬侯許延壽薨。
entries.en: In the second month, on day dingsi, Marquis Jing of Lecheng Xu Yanshou died.
entries.literal: In the second month, on day dingsi, Marquis Jing of Lecheng Xu Yanshou died.

entries.zh: 夏，四月，黃龍見新豐。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, a yellow dragon appeared at Xinfeng.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, a yellow dragon appeared at Xinfeng.

entries.zh: 丙申，太上皇廟火；
entries.en: On day bingshen, the Grand Supreme Emperor's temple caught fire;
entries.literal: On day bingshen, the Grand Supreme Emperor's temple caught fire;

entries.zh: 甲辰，孝文廟火；
entries.en: on day jiachen, Emperor Wen's temple caught fire;
entries.literal: on day jiachen, Emperor Wen's temple caught fire;

entries.zh: 上素服五日。
entries.en: the emperor wore plain mourning garments for five days.
entries.literal: the emperor wore plain white garments for five days.

entries.zh: 烏孫狂王復尚楚主解憂，生一男鴟靡，不與主和，又暴惡失眾。
entries.en: The Mad King of Wusun again married the Chu princess Jieyou and begot a son, Nimi; he was not harmonious with her and was violent and wicked, losing popular support.
entries.literal: The Mad King of Wusun again took in marriage the Chu princess Jieyou and begot a son, Nimi; he was not harmonious with the princess and again was violent and wicked, losing the masses.

entries.zh: 漢使衛司馬魏和意、副侯任昌至烏孫。
entries.en: Han sent Guard Major Wei Heyi and Deputy Marquis Ren Chang to Wusun.
entries.literal: Han sent Guard Major Wei Heyi and Deputy Marquis Ren Chang to Wusun.

entries.zh: 公主言：「狂王為烏孫所患苦，易誅也。」
entries.en: The princess said, "The Mad King is what Wusun suffers from; he is easy to kill."
entries.literal: The princess said: "The Mad King is what Wusun suffers from; he is easy to execute."

entries.zh: 遂謀置酒，使士拔劍擊之。
entries.en: They plotted a banquet and had soldiers draw swords and strike him.
entries.literal: They thereupon plotted to set out wine and had soldiers draw swords and strike him.

entries.zh: 劍旁下，狂王傷，上馬馳去。
entries.en: The sword struck beside him; the Mad King was wounded, mounted his horse, and fled.
entries.literal: The sword struck beside him; the Mad King was wounded, mounted his horse, and galloped away.

entries.zh: 其子細沈瘦會兵圍和意、昌及公主於赤谷城。
entries.en: His son Xishen Sou gathered troops and besieged Heyi, Chang, and the princess at Red Valley City.
entries.literal: His son Xishen Sou gathered troops and besieged Heyi, Chang, and the princess at Red Valley City.

entries.zh: 數月，都護鄭吉發諸國兵救之，乃解去。
entries.en: Several months later, Protector-General Zheng Ji mobilized troops from the various states to rescue them, and the siege was lifted.
entries.literal: Several months later, Protector-General Zheng Ji mobilized the various states' troops to rescue them, and the siege was then lifted.

entries.zh: 漢遣中郎將張遵持醫藥治狂王，賜金帛。
entries.en: Han sent Palace Gentleman Zhang Zun with medicine to treat the Mad King and bestowed gold and silks.
entries.literal: Han sent Palace Gentleman Zhang Zun bearing medicine to treat the Mad King and bestowed gold and silks.

entries.zh: 因收和意、昌系瑣，從尉犁檻車至長安，斬之。
entries.en: Thereupon Heyi and Chang were seized in fetters, sent in a caged cart from Weili to Chang'an, and beheaded.
entries.literal: Thereupon Heyi and Chang were seized in fetters, sent in a caged cart from Weili to Chang'an, and beheaded.

entries.zh: :班固贊曰：孝宣之治，信賞必罰，綜核名實。
entries.en: Ban Gu's praise says: The governance of Emperor Xiaoxuan—rewards and punishments were sure, names and realities were comprehensively verified.
entries.literal: Ban Gu's praise says: The governance of Emperor Xiaoxuan—rewards and punishments were sure, names and realities were comprehensively verified.

entries.zh: 政事、文學、法理之士，鹹精其能。
entries.en: Men of government affairs, letters, and legal principle all refined their abilities.
entries.literal: Men of government affairs, letters, and legal principle all refined their abilities.

entries.zh: 至於技巧、工匠、器械，自元、成間鮮能及之。
entries.en: As for skill, craftsmen, and instruments—from the Yuan and Cheng reigns few could match it.
entries.literal: As for skill, craftsmen, and instruments—from the Yuan and Cheng reigns few could match it.

entries.zh: 亦足以知吏稱其職，民安其業也。
entries.en: This too is enough to know that officials claimed their posts and the people were secure in their livelihoods.
entries.literal: This too is enough to know that officials claimed their posts and the people were secure in their livelihoods.

entries.zh: 遭值匈奴乖亂，推亡固存，信威北夷，單于慕義，稽首稱籓。
entries.en: He encountered the Xiongnu in disorder, pushed the perishing and secured what remained, his trust and might reached the northern Yi; the chanyu admired his righteousness and bowed, calling himself vassal.
entries.literal: He encountered the Xiongnu in disorder, pushed the perishing and secured what remained, his trust and might reached the northern Yi; the chanyu admired his righteousness and bowed, calling himself vassal.

entries.zh: 功光祖宗，業垂後嗣，可謂中興，侔德殷宗、周宣矣！
entries.en: His merit illumined the ancestors and his enterprise hangs for posterity; it can be called a restoration, equal in virtue to the Yin Ancestor and King Xuan of Zhou!
entries.literal: His merit illumined the ancestors and his enterprise hangs for posterity; it can be called a restoration, equal in virtue to the Yin Ancestor and King Xuan of Zhou!

entries.zh: 癸巳，太子即皇帝位，謁高廟，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: On guisi, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, visited Gaozu's temple, and honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: On guisi, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, visited Gaozu's temple, and honored the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 起昭陽太淵獻，盡玄黓涒灘，凡十年。
entries.en: From Zhaoyang Taiyuanxian through Xuanqi Tunshan—ten years in all.
entries.literal: From Zhaoyang Taiyuanxian through Xuanqi Tunshan; ten years in all.

entries.zh: 初，紅陽侯立不得輔政，疑為長毀譖，常怨毒長；
entries.en: Earlier, Marquis Li of Hongyang, denied a role in government, suspected Chang of slandering him and constantly hated him;
entries.literal: Earlier, Marquis Li of Hongyang, not obtaining a role in government, suspected Chang of slandering him and constantly bore bitter hatred toward Chang;

entries.zh: 上知之。
entries.en: the emperor knew this.
entries.literal: the emperor knew this.

entries.zh: 及長當就國，立嗣子融從長請車騎，長以珍寶因融重遺立。
entries.en: When Chang was about to depart for his fief, Li's heir Rong followed Chang to request chariots and escort; Chang sent a heavy gift of treasures to Li through Rong.
entries.literal: When Chang was about to go to his state, Li's heir Rong followed Chang to request chariots and horsemen; Chang used treasures through Rong to send a heavy gift again to Li.

entries.zh: 立因上封事，為長求留，曰：「陛下既托文以皇太后故，誠不可更有它計。」
entries.en: Li thereupon submitted a sealed memorial seeking to retain Chang, saying, "Your Majesty has already committed in writing on account of the Empress Dowager—there truly must not be another plan."
entries.literal: Li thereupon submitted a sealed memorial seeking to retain Chang, saying: "Your Majesty has already entrusted the matter to writing on account of the Empress Dowager—truly there must not be another plan."

entries.zh: 於是天子疑焉，下有司按驗。
entries.en: Thereupon the emperor grew suspicious and ordered the responsible offices to investigate.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven grew suspicious and sent it down to the responsible offices for investigation and verification.

entries.zh: 吏捕融，立令融自殺以滅口。
entries.en: Officials arrested Rong; Li ordered Rong to kill himself to silence him.
entries.literal: Officials arrested Rong; Li ordered Rong to kill himself to silence him.

entries.zh: 上愈疑其有大奸，遂逮長系洛陽詔獄，窮治。
entries.en: The emperor grew still more suspicious of great treachery and arrested Chang, imprisoning him in the Luoyang imperial prison for a full investigation.
entries.literal: The emperor grew still more suspicious of great treachery and thereupon arrested Chang and imprisoned him in the Luoyang imperial prison, investigating to the end.

entries.zh: 長具服戲侮長定宮，謀立左皇后，罪至大逆，死獄中。
entries.en: Chang fully confessed to mocking Changding Palace and plotting to install a Left Empress—crime reaching great treason; he died in prison.
entries.literal: Chang fully confessed to mocking Changding Palace and plotting to install a Left Empress—crime reaching great treason; he died in prison.

entries.zh: 妻子當坐者徙合浦；
entries.en: Wife and children who shared punishment were exiled to Hepu;
entries.literal: Wife and children who should share punishment were exiled to Hepu;

entries.zh: 母若歸故郡。
entries.en: his mother Ru returned to her native commandery.
entries.literal: his mother Ru returned to her native commandery.

entries.zh: 上使廷尉孔光持節賜廢後藥，自殺。
entries.en: The emperor sent Commandant of Justice Kong Guang with credentials to bestow poison on the deposed empress for suicide.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Commandant of Justice Kong Guang with credentials to bestow poison on the deposed empress for self-destruction.

entries.zh: 丞相方進復劾奏「紅陽侯立，狡猾不閫，請下獄。」
entries.en: Chancellor Fangjin again impeached, saying, "Marquis Li of Hongyang is crafty and unbounded—please send him to prison."
entries.literal: Chancellor Fangjin again impeached and memorialized: "Marquis Li of Hongyang is crafty and does not keep to bounds—please send him to prison."

entries.zh: 上曰：「紅陽侯，朕之舅，不忍致法；
entries.en: The emperor said, "Marquis Li of Hongyang is Our maternal uncle—we cannot bear to apply the law;
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Marquis Li of Hongyang is Our maternal uncle—we cannot bear to apply the law;

entries.zh: 遣就國。」
entries.en: send him to his fief."
entries.literal: send him to his state."

entries.zh: 於是方進復奏立黨友後將軍朱博、巨鹿太守孫閎，皆免官，與故光祿大夫陳鹹皆歸故郡。
entries.en: Thereupon Fangjin again memorialized that Li's associates Rear General Zhu Bo and Administrator of Julu Sun Hong were all removed from office, and together with former Grand Master of Splendor Chen Xian returned to their native commanderies.
entries.literal: Thereupon Fangjin again memorialized that Li's partisan associates Rear General Zhu Bo and Administrator of Julu Sun Hong were all removed from office, and together with former Grand Master of Splendor Chen Xian all returned to their native commanderies.

entries.zh: 鹹自知廢錮，以憂死。
entries.en: Xian, knowing himself disgraced and barred from office, died from grief.
entries.literal: Xian, knowing himself disgraced and barred, died from grief.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑第032卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 32.
entries.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 32.

entries.zh: 初，董仲舒說武帝，以「秦用商鞅之法，除井田，民得賣買，富者田連阡陌，貧者亡立錐之地，邑有人君之尊，裡有公侯之富，小民安得不困！
entries.en: Earlier, Dong Zhongsun persuaded Emperor Wu: "Qin used Lord Shang's laws, abolished the well-field system, and allowed land to be bought and sold—the rich held fields stretching across paths and moors, the poor had no place to stand an awl; townships held men with a ruler's honor, lanes men with a duke's wealth—how could common people not be distressed!
entries.literal: Initially, Dong Zhongsun persuaded Emperor Wu, saying: "Qin used Lord Shang's laws, abolished the well-field system, and allowed the people to sell and buy land—the rich had fields stretching across paths and moors, the poor had no place to stand an awl; in the townships were men with a ruler's honor, in the lanes were men with a duke or marquis's wealth—how could the little people not be distressed!

entries.zh: 古井田法雖難卒行，宜少近古，限民名田以贍不足，塞並兼之路；
entries.en: Though the ancient well-field law cannot be restored at once, one ought to draw near antiquity, limit registered land to support the needy, and block the path of merger;
entries.literal: Though the ancient well-field law is hard to carry out at once, one ought to draw somewhat near antiquity, limit the people's registered land to support the insufficient, and block the path of merger and absorption;

entries.zh: 去奴婢，除專殺之威；
entries.en: abolish slaveholding and the power of arbitrary killing;
entries.literal: remove slave servants and abolish the authority of arbitrary killing;

entries.zh: 薄賦斂，省繇役，以寬民力，然後可善治也！」
entries.en: lighten taxes, reduce corvée labor, ease the people's burden—only then can there be good governance!"
entries.literal: lighten taxes and levies, reduce corvée labor, thereby easing the people's strength—only then can there be good governance!"

entries.zh: 及上即位，師丹復建言：「今累世承平，豪富吏民訾數巨萬，而貧弱愈困，宜略為限。」
entries.en: When this emperor took the throne, Shi Dan again proposed: "After generations of peace, the powerful and wealthy count their wealth in tens of millions while the poor grow ever weaker—it is fitting to set limits."
entries.literal: When this emperor took the throne, Shi Dan again proposed: "Now, after generations of enduring peace, powerful and wealthy officials and people number their wealth in tens of millions, while the poor and weak grow ever more distressed—it is fitting to set some limit."

entries.zh: 天子下其議，丞相光、大司空武奏請：「自諸侯王、列侯、公主名田各有限；
entries.en: The emperor referred the matter; Chancellor Guang and Grand Minister of Works Wu memorialized: "From feudal kings and princes, ranked marquises, and princesses, registered land should each have a limit;
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven sent down their deliberation; Chancellor Guang and Grand Minister of Works Wu memorialized requesting: "From feudal kings and princes, ranked marquises, and princesses, registered land each should have a limit;

entries.zh: 關內侯、吏、民名田皆毋過三十頃；
entries.en: for marquises within the passes, officials, and common people, registered land must not exceed thirty qing;
entries.literal: for marquises within the passes, officials, and common people, registered land must not exceed thirty qing;

entries.zh: 奴婢毋過三十人。
entries.en: slaves must not exceed thirty persons.
entries.literal: slave servants must not exceed thirty persons.

entries.zh: 期盡三年。
entries.en: A deadline of three years was set.
entries.literal: A deadline of three years was set for full compliance.

entries.zh: 犯者沒入宮。」
entries.en: Violators would have excess property confiscated by the palace."
entries.literal: Violators would have their property confiscated into the palace."

entries.zh: 時田宅、奴婢賈為減賤，貴戚近習皆不便也，詔書：「且須後。」
entries.en: Land, houses, and slaves fell in price; the noble kin and court favorites were all discommoded; an edict said, "For now, wait."
entries.literal: At the time the prices of fields, dwellings, and slave servants fell in reduction, and the noble kin and those near the emperor were all discommoded; an edict said: "For now, wait."

entries.zh: 遂寢不行。
entries.en: Thereupon the measure was shelved and never carried out.
entries.literal: Thereupon the measure was shelved and not carried out.

entries.zh: 又詔齊三服官：「諸官織綺繡，難成、害女紅之物，皆止，無作輸。
entries.en: Another edict to the Three Garment Offices of Qi: "All offices weaving patterned silks and brocades—things hard to finish and harmful to women's work—must stop; produce nothing for delivery.
entries.literal: Another edict to the Three Garment Offices of Qi: "All offices weaving patterned silks and brocades—things hard to finish and harmful to women's needlework—are all to stop; do not produce them for delivery.

entries.zh: 除任子令及誹謗詆欺法。
entries.en: The emperor abolished the statute on gratifying heirs and the statutes on slander, defamation, and fraud.
entries.literal: They abolished the statute on gratifying heirs and the statutes on slander, defamation, and fraud.

entries.zh: 掖廷宮人年三十以下，出嫁之；
entries.en: Palace women of the Palace Domestic Service aged thirty and below were released to marry;
entries.literal: Palace women of the Palace Domestic Service aged thirty and below were given in marriage;

entries.zh: 官奴婢五十以上，免為庶人，益吏三百石以下俸。」
entries.en: official bondmen and bondwomen aged fifty and above were freed as commoners, and salaries for officials ranked at three hundred piculs and below were raised."
entries.literal: official male and female slaves fifty and above were freed as commoners, and salaries for officials of three hundred piculs and below were increased."

entries.zh: 孔光、何武奏：「迭毀之次當以時定，請與群臣雜議。」
entries.en: Kong Guang and He Wu memorialized, "The sequence for successive removal from the temple should be fixed according to the times—we request to deliberate with the ministers."
entries.literal: Kong Guang and He Wu memorialized: "The sequence for successive removal from the temple should be fixed according to the times—we request to deliberate mixed with the ministers."

entries.zh: 於是光祿勳彭宣等五十三人皆以為：「孝武皇帝雖有功烈，親盡宜毀。」
entries.en: Thereupon Director of the Secretariat Peng Xuan and fifty-three others all held, "Although Emperor Xiaowu had meritorious achievements, when his line of descent is exhausted he should be removed from the temple."
entries.literal: Thereupon Director of the Secretariat Peng Xuan and fifty-three others all held: "Although Emperor Xiaowu had meritorious achievements, when kin is exhausted he should be removed from the temple."

entries.zh: 太僕王舜、中壘校尉劉歆議曰：「《禮》，天子七廟。
entries.en: Grand Master of Equipage Wang Shun and Commandant of the Inner Ramparts Liu Xin argued, "In the Rites, the Son of Heaven has seven temples.
entries.literal: Grand Master of Equipage Wang Shun and Commandant of the Inner Ramparts Liu Xin deliberated, saying: "In the Rites, the Son of Heaven has seven temples.

entries.zh: 七者其正法數，可常數者也。
entries.en: Seven is the correct standard number—the number that may remain constant.
entries.literal: Seven is the correct standard number—the number that may be constant.

entries.zh: 宗不在此數中，宗變也。
entries.en: An honored ancestor is not within this number—honored ancestor is an exception.
entries.literal: An 'honored ancestor' is not within this number—'honored ancestor' is a change.

entries.zh: 苟有功德則宗之，不可預為設數。
entries.en: If there are merit and achievement, then one honors him as an ancestor—the number cannot be set in advance.
entries.literal: If there are merit and achievement, then one honors him as an ancestor—it cannot be predetermined and a number set in advance.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為孝武皇帝功烈如彼，孝宣皇帝崇立之如此，不宜毀。」
entries.en: Your servant foolishly considers that Emperor Xiaowu's achievements were as great as they were, and Emperor Xiaoxuan exalted him as he did—he should not be removed from the temple."
entries.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that Emperor Xiaowu's achievements and merit were as they were, and Emperor Xiaoxuan exalted and established him as he did—he should not be removed."

entries.zh: 上覽其議，制曰：「太僕舜、中壘校尉歆議可。」
entries.en: The emperor reviewed their deliberation and decreed, "The argument of Grand Master of Equipage Shun and Commandant of the Inner Ramparts Xin is accepted."
entries.literal: The emperor reviewed their deliberation and decreed: "The deliberation of Grand Master of Equipage Shun and Commandant of the Inner Ramparts Xin is acceptable."

entries.zh: 議郎耿育上書冤訟陳湯曰：「甘延壽、陳湯，為聖漢揚鉤深致遠之威，雪國家累年之恥，討絕域不羈之君，系萬里難制之虜，豈有比哉！
entries.en: Remonstrance Officer Geng Yu submitted a memorial pleading Chen Tang's case, saying, "Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang displayed holy Han's power to strike deep and reach far, wiped away years of national shame, punished a lord of the distant realm who would not submit, and bound a captive hard to control across ten thousand li—has anything compared!
entries.literal: Remonstrance Officer Geng Yu submitted a memorial pleading Chen Tang's wrong, saying: "Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang for holy Han displayed the authority of hooking deep and reaching far, wiped away the state's shame accumulated over years, punished the lord of the distant realm who would not submit, and bound the captive hard to control across ten thousand li—has anything compared!

entries.zh: 先帝嘉之，仍下明詔，宣著其功，改年垂歷，傳之無窮。
entries.en: The former emperor praised them and issued a bright edict proclaiming their merit; the reign era was changed and handed down through the calendar to be transmitted without end.
entries.literal: The former emperor praised them and again issued a bright edict, proclaiming and making manifest their merit; the reign year was changed and handed down through the calendar, transmitted without end.

entries.zh: 應是，南郡獻白虎，邊垂無警備。
entries.en: In response, Nanyang presented a white tiger and the border marches needed no alarm.
entries.literal: In response to this, Nanyang presented a white tiger; the border marches had no alarms or guards needed.

entries.zh: 會先帝寢疾，然猶垂竟不忘，數使尚書責問丞相，趣立其功；
entries.en: When the former emperor fell gravely ill, even at the end he did not forget, repeatedly sending the Master of Documents to reproach the Chancellor and urge that their merit be established;
entries.literal: It happened that the former emperor fell gravely ill, yet even at the end he did not forget, repeatedly sending the Master of Documents to reproach and question the Chancellor, urging that their merit be established;

entries.zh: 獨丞相匡衡排而不予，封延壽、湯數百戶，此功臣戰士所以失望也。
entries.en: only Chancellor Kuang Heng blocked it and would not grant proper reward, enfeoffing Yanshou and Tang with only several hundred households—this is why meritorious soldiers were disappointed.
entries.literal: only Chancellor Kuang Heng blocked and would not grant it, enfeoffing Yanshou and Tang with several hundred households—this is why meritorious ministers and fighting soldiers were disappointed.

entries.zh: 孝成皇帝承建業之基，乘征伐之威，兵革不動，國家無事，而大臣傾邪，欲專主威，排妒有功，使湯塊然被冤拘囚，不能自明，卒以無罪老棄。
entries.en: Emperor Cheng inherited an established foundation and the prestige of conquest—arms were not moved and the state was at peace, yet great ministers were crooked, wishing to monopolize authority, excluding and envying the meritorious, leaving Tang alone wronged, imprisoned, unable to clear himself, and in the end cast off in old age though guiltless.
entries.literal: Emperor Cheng inherited the foundation of established enterprise and rode the authority of campaigns and punishments—arms were not moved, the state had no troubles, yet great ministers were crooked, wishing to monopolize authority, excluding and envying the meritorious, making Tang stand alone wronged, bound and imprisoned, unable to clear himself, and in the end, though guiltless, cast off in old age.

entries.zh: 敦煌正當西域通道，令威名折衝之臣，旋踵及身，復為郅支遺虜所笑，誠可悲也！
entries.en: Dunhuang lies on the Western Regions route—when a minister whose renown once turned enemies at the frontier suffers within a turning of the heel and is laughed at again by Zhizhi's surviving captives, it is truly pitiable!
entries.literal: Dunhuang lies right on the Western Regions route—making a minister whose renown turned enemies at the frontier, within a turning of the heel suffer upon his person, again laughed at by Zhizhi's surviving captives—is truly pitiable!

entries.zh: 至今奉使外蠻者，未嘗不陳郅支之誅以揚漢國之盛。
entries.en: Down to the present, envoys to outer barbarians never fail to cite the execution of Zhizhi to display Han magnificence.
entries.literal: Down to the present, envoys sent to outer barbarians have never failed to cite the execution of Zhizhi to display the Han state's magnificence.

entries.zh: 夫援人之功以懼敵，棄人之身以快讒，豈不痛哉！
entries.en: To use another man's merit to frighten enemies yet abandon his person to please slanderers—how is it not painful!
entries.literal: To use another man's merit to frighten enemies yet abandon another man's person to please slanderers—how is it not painful!

entries.zh: 且安不忘危，盛必慮衰，今國家素無文帝累年節儉富饒之畜，又無武帝薦延梟俊禽敵之臣，獨有一陳湯耳！
entries.en: Moreover, in security do not forget peril; in flourishing one must consider decline—the state lacks the stores from Emperor Wen's years of thrift and abundance and lacks Emperor Wu's fierce ministers who captured enemies; there is only Chen Tang!
entries.literal: Moreover, in security do not forget peril; in flourishing one must consider decline—now the state has never had the stores from Emperor Wen's years of thrift and abundance, nor Emperor Wu's recommending and extending fierce and outstanding ministers who captured enemies—there is only one Chen Tang!

entries.zh: 假使異世不及陛下，尚望國家追錄其功，封表其墓，以勸後進也。
entries.en: Suppose he had not lived to serve Your Majesty—still one would hope the state would record his merit posthumously and mark his tomb to encourage those who come after.
entries.literal: Suppose in another age he did not reach Your Majesty—still one would hope the state would trace back and record his merit, enfeoff and mark his tomb, to encourage those who come after.

entries.zh: 湯幸得身當聖世，功曾未久，反聽邪臣鞭逐斥遠，使亡逃分竄，死無處所。
entries.en: Tang was fortunate to serve a sagely age; his merit had not long stood, yet wicked ministers whipped, drove, and expelled him, making him flee and scatter, dying with no place to rest.
entries.literal: Tang was fortunate to have his person meet the sagely age; his merit had not long stood, yet on the contrary he listened to wicked ministers who whipped, drove, expelled, and distanced him, making him flee and scatter in hiding, dying with no place to rest.

entries.zh: 遠覽之士，莫不計度，以為湯功累世不可及，而湯過人情所有，湯尚如此，雖復破絕筋骨，暴露形骸，猶複製於脣舌，為嫉妒之臣所繫虜耳。
entries.en: Men of far vision all reckoned that Tang's merit over generations was unmatched, yet his faults were what any man might have—if even Tang was so treated, though one broke bones and exposed one's body one would still be made captive to envious ministers' tongues.
entries.literal: Men of far vision all reckoned and measured, holding that Tang's merit over generations could not be reached, yet Tang's faults were what any man might have—if even Tang was so treated, though one again broke bones and sinews and exposed one's body, one would still be made subject to tongues and bound captive by envious ministers.

entries.zh: 此臣所以為國家尤戚戚也。」
entries.en: This is why your subject grieves especially for the state."
entries.literal: This is why your subject is especially grieved for the state."

entries.zh: 書奏，天子還湯，卒於長安。
entries.en: The memorial was submitted; the emperor recalled Chen Tang, and he died in Chang'an.
entries.literal: The memorial was submitted; the Son of Heaven recalled Tang, and he died in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑第033卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 33.
entries.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 33.

entries.zh: 尚兵既至，諸將皆以為：「此歸師，人自為戰，不如避之。」
entries.en: When Shang's army arrived, his commanders argued: "These are men hurrying home to save their city. They will fight as if each man alone mattered. We ought to avoid them."
entries.literal: When Shang's army had arrived, the generals all considered: "This is a returning army; each man will fight for himself — better to avoid it."

entries.zh: 操曰：「尚從大道來，當避之；
entries.en: Cao Cao said, "If Shang comes by the main road, we should avoid him;
entries.literal: Cao Cao said: "If Shang comes by the great road, we ought to avoid him;

entries.zh: 若循西山來者，此成禽耳。」
entries.en: but if he comes by the western hills, he will be easy prey."
entries.literal: If he comes along the western hills, this will be catching prey."

entries.zh: 尚果循西山來，東至陽平亭，去鄴十七里，臨滏水為營。
entries.en: Shang did come by the western hills, reached Yangping Pavilion seventeen li from Ye, and made camp on the Fu River.
entries.literal: Shang indeed came along the western hills, proceeding east to Yangping Pavilion, seventeen li from Ye, and encamped on the Fu River.

entries.zh: 夜，舉火以示城中，城中亦舉火相應。
entries.en: At night he lit signal fires for the city, and the city answered with fires of its own.
entries.literal: At night he raised fires to signal the city; the city also raised fires in answer.

entries.zh: 配出兵城北，欲與尚對決圍。
entries.en: Shen Pei led troops out from the north gate, intending to link up with Shang and break the siege.
entries.literal: Pei led troops out from the north of the city, wishing to meet Shang and break the encirclement face to face.

entries.zh: 操逆擊之，敗還，尚亦破走，依曲漳為營，操遂圍之。
entries.en: Cao Cao counterattacked and drove Shen Pei back. Shang was also routed and withdrew to the Qu Zhang to make camp, where Cao Cao besieged him.
entries.literal: Cao Cao struck them in reverse, defeated them and they retreated; Shang was also routed and fled, relying on the Qu Zhang for an encampment — Cao Cao then encircled him.

entries.zh: 未合，尚懼，遣使求降；
entries.en: Before the ring closed, Shang, alarmed, sent envoys to sue for peace;
entries.literal: Before the encirclement closed, Shang was afraid and sent envoys to beg surrender;

entries.zh: 操不聽，圍之益急。
entries.en: Cao Cao refused and tightened the siege.
entries.literal: Cao Cao would not listen and pressed the encirclement the more urgently.

entries.zh: 尚夜遁，保祁山，操復進圍之。
entries.en: Shang fled by night to Qishan. Cao Cao pursued and besieged him again.
entries.literal: Shang fled by night, took refuge at Qishan — Cao Cao again advanced and encircled him.

entries.zh: 尚將馬延、張顗等臨陳降，眾大潰，尚奔中山。
entries.en: Shang's generals Ma Yan and Zhang Yi surrendered on the field. His army collapsed, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Shang's generals Ma Yan, Zhang Yi, and others surrendered before the battle line; the masses greatly collapsed, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 盡收其輜重，得尚印綬、節鉞及衣物，以示城中，城中崩沮。
entries.en: Cao Cao captured all his supplies, along with Shang's seals, credentials, and regalia, and displayed them before Ye. The city's morale shattered.
entries.literal: [Cao Cao] took all his baggage train, obtained Shang's seal ribbon, tally and axe of authority, and clothing, and displayed them to the city — within the city spirits collapsed in dismay.

entries.zh: 審配令士卒曰：「堅守死戰！
entries.en: Shen Pei told the troops: "Hold the walls and fight to the death!
entries.literal: Shen Pei ordered the soldiers: "Hold fast and fight to the death!

entries.zh: 操軍疲矣，幽州方至，何憂無主！」
entries.en: Cao Cao's army is spent, and reinforcements from You Province are on the way. Why fear that we are leaderless?"
entries.literal: Cao Cao's army is exhausted; forces from You Province are just arriving — why worry that there will be no lord!"

entries.zh: 操出行圍，配伏弩射之，幾中。
entries.en: When Cao Cao rode out to inspect the siege lines, Shen Pei had crossbowmen hidden to shoot at him. The bolts nearly found their mark.
entries.literal: When Cao Cao went out on an inspection of the encirclement, Pei hid crossbowmen who shot at him — he was nearly hit.

entries.zh: 配兄子榮為東門校尉，八月，戊寅，榮夜開門內操兵。
entries.en: Shen Pei's nephew Rong commanded the east gate. On wuyin in the eighth month, Rong opened the gate by night and let Cao Cao's men in.
entries.literal: Pei's elder brother's son Rong was Commandant of the East Gate; on the day wuyin in the eighth month, Rong opened the gate by night and admitted Cao Cao's troops.

entries.zh: 配拒戰城中，操兵生獲之。
entries.en: Shen Pei fought on inside the city until Cao Cao's men captured him alive.
entries.literal: Pei resisted in battle within the city, and Cao Cao's troops took him alive.

entries.zh: 辛評家系鄴獄，辛毘馳往，欲解之，已悉為配所殺。
entries.en: Xin Ping's family was held in the Ye jail. Xin Pi rushed to free them, but Shen Pei had already had them all executed.
entries.literal: Xin Ping's family was imprisoned in Ye; Xin Pi galloped there wishing to release them, but they had already all been killed by Pei.

entries.zh: 操兵縛配詣帳下，毘逆以馬鞭擊其頭，罵之曰：「奴，汝今日真死矣！」
entries.en: Cao Cao's men bound Shen Pei and brought him to headquarters. Xin Pi met him and whipped him across the head, shouting, "You slave — this time you are truly dead!"
entries.literal: Cao Cao's troops bound Pei and brought him beneath the tent; Pi went up to him and struck his head with a riding crop, cursing him: "Slave — today you truly die!"

entries.zh: 配顧曰：「狗輩，正由汝曹破我冀州，恨不得殺汝也！
entries.en: Shen Pei turned and said, "You curs — it was your kind who ruined Ji Province. I only regret I could not kill you!
entries.literal: Pei turned and said: "Dog pack — it was precisely you lot who ruined my Ji Province; I only regret I could not kill you!

entries.zh: 且汝今日能殺生我邪？」
entries.en: And as I still live, can you kill me now?"
entries.literal: And can you today kill me while I yet live?"

entries.zh: 有頃，操引見，謂配曰：「曩日孤之行圍，何弩之多也！」
entries.en: After a time Cao Cao had him brought before him and said, "When I rode the lines the other day, your crossbow bolts came thick as rain."
entries.literal: After a while Cao Cao had him brought in and said to Pei: "The other day when I inspected the encirclement, how many crossbow bolts there were!"

entries.zh: 配曰：「猶恨其少！」
entries.en: Shen Pei said, "I only regret there were not more."
entries.literal: Pei said: "I still regret there were too few!"

entries.zh: 操曰：「卿忠於袁氏，亦自不得不爾。」
entries.en: Cao Cao said, "You were loyal to the Yuan house. You could not have done otherwise."
entries.literal: Cao Cao said: "You were loyal to the Yuans — you could not have acted otherwise."

entries.zh: 意欲活之。
entries.en: He meant to spare him.
entries.literal: He intended to spare his life.

entries.zh: 配意氣壯烈，終於橈辭，而辛毘等號哭不已，遂斬之。
entries.en: Shen Pei remained fierce and unyielding to the end, but Xin Pi and the others kept wailing until Cao Cao ordered his execution.
entries.literal: Pei's spirit and bearing were fierce and bold; to the end he would not soften his words — but Xin Pi and the others wept and wailed without cease, and so he was beheaded.

entries.zh: 冀州人張子謙先降，素與配不善，笑謂配曰：「正南，卿竟何如我？」
entries.en: Zhang Ziqian of Ji Province, who had surrendered earlier and had never been on good terms with Shen Pei, mocked him: "Zhengnan — see how much better I fare than you?"
entries.literal: The Ji Province native Zhang Ziqian had surrendered earlier; he had always been on bad terms with Pei and, laughing, said to Pei: "Zhengnan — in the end how do you compare with me?"

entries.zh: 配厲聲曰：「汝為降虜，審配為忠臣。
entries.en: Shen Pei shouted back, "You are a turncoat. I am a loyal minister.
entries.literal: Pei said in a harsh voice: "You are a surrendered captive; Shen Pei is a loyal minister.

entries.zh: 雖死，豈羨汝生邪！」
entries.en: Even in death, why should I envy your life?"
entries.literal: Though I die, why should I envy your living?"

entries.zh: 臨行刑，叱持兵者令北向，曰：「我君在北也。」
entries.en: At the moment of execution he ordered the executioners to turn him north, saying, "My lord is in the north."
entries.literal: Facing execution, he shouted at those holding the weapons to make him face north, saying: "My lord is in the north."

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第064卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 64
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 64

entries.zh: 秋，七月，魏公操擊孫權，留少子臨菑侯植守鄴。
entries.en: In autumn, during the seventh month, Duke Cao attacked Sun Quan and left his youngest son, Marquis of Linzi Cao Zhi, to guard Ye.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Duke Cao attacked Sun Quan, leaving his youngest son Marquis of Linzi Zhi to guard Ye.

entries.zh: 操為諸子高選官屬，以刑顒為植家丞。
entries.en: Cao carefully chose staff for his sons and made Xing Yong household aide to Zhi.
entries.literal: Cao for his sons carefully selected staff, making Xing Yong Zhi's household aide.

entries.zh: 顒防閒以禮，無所屈撓，由是不合。
entries.en: Yong kept him in check with strict ritual propriety and would not bend, and for that reason they did not get along.
entries.literal: Yong guarded and restrained him with ritual propriety, yielding in nothing, and for this reason they did not get along.

entries.zh: 庶子劉楨美文辭，植親愛之。
entries.en: Liu Zhen, a junior associate, wrote fine prose, and Zhi was fond of him.
entries.literal: Associate Liu Zhen had fine literary style; Zhi was fond of him.

entries.zh: 楨以書諫植曰：「君侯采庶子之春華，忘家丞之秋實，為上招謗，其罪不小，愚實懼焉。」
entries.en: Zhen wrote to admonish Zhi, "You gather the spring blossoms your junior offers but forget the autumn fruit your household aide provides. You invite your father's reproach, and the fault is no small one. I am truly afraid for you."
entries.literal: Zhen admonished Zhi in a letter: "Your Lordship gathers the associate's spring flowers but forgets the household aide's autumn fruit—this invites slander from above, and the fault is no small one; I truly fear it."

entries.zh: 丞相主簿司馬懿言於操曰：「劉備以詐力虜劉璋，蜀人未附，而遠爭江陵，此機不可失也。
entries.en: Chief Clerk Sima Yi said to Cao, "Liu Bei seized Liu Zhang by fraud and force; the people of Shu are not yet loyal to him, yet he is fighting far away at Jiangling—this is an opportunity we must not miss.
entries.literal: Chief Clerk of the Chancellor Sima Yi spoke to Cao, saying: "Liu Bei by deceit and force captured Liu Zhang; the people of Shu are not yet attached, yet he contends far away at Jiangling—this opportunity must not be lost.

entries.zh: 今克漢中，益州震動，進兵臨之，勢必瓦解。
entries.en: With Hanzhong in our hands, Yizhou will be shaken; if we march against it at once, it will surely fall apart.
entries.literal: Now that Hanzhong is taken, Yizhou will be shaken; if we advance and press upon it, the momentum will surely collapse.

entries.zh: 聖人不能違時，亦不可失時也。」
entries.en: Even a sage cannot defy the season, and one must not miss the moment."
entries.literal: A sage cannot go against the times, nor can one miss the times."

entries.zh: 操曰：「人苦無足，既得隴，復望蜀邪！」
entries.en: Cao said, "Men are never satisfied—having taken Long, you would look to Shu as well!"
entries.literal: Cao said: "Men suffer from lack of contentment—having already gained Long, yet still look to Shu!"

entries.zh: 劉曄曰：「劉備，人傑也，有度而遲；
entries.en: Liu Ye said, "Liu Bei is a man of heroic stature—far-sighted but deliberate;
entries.literal: Liu Ye said: "Liu Bei is a hero among men—he has measure yet is slow;

entries.zh: 得蜀日淺，蜀人未恃也。
entries.en: he has held Shu only briefly, and the people there do not yet trust him.
entries.literal: he has held Shu for only a short time, and the people of Shu do not yet rely on him.

entries.zh: 今破漢中，蜀人震恐，其勢自傾。
entries.en: With Hanzhong lost, the people of Shu are terrified and his position is already crumbling.
entries.literal: Now that Hanzhong is broken, the people of Shu will be shaken in terror and their momentum will collapse of itself.

entries.zh: 以公之神明，因其傾而壓之，無不克也。
entries.en: With your brilliance, if you press him while he is faltering, you cannot fail.
entries.literal: With your brilliance, if you press upon them as they collapse, there is nothing you cannot overcome.

entries.zh: 若小緩之，諸葛亮明於治國而為相，關羽、張飛勇冠三軍而為將，蜀民既定，據險守要，則不可犯矣。
entries.en: Wait even a little, and with Zhuge Liang as a brilliant administrator and chancellor and Guan Yu and Zhang Fei as the bravest generals in the land, once the people of Shu settle in and hold the mountain passes, he will become untouchable.
entries.literal: If you relax slightly, Zhuge Liang is clear in governing the state and serves as chancellor; Guan Yu and Zhang Fei are bravest in the three armies and serve as generals; once the people of Shu are settled and hold difficult passes and guard strategic points, they cannot be violated.

entries.zh: 今不取，必為後憂。」
entries.en: If you do not strike now, you will regret it later."
entries.literal: If you do not take it now, it will surely become a later worry."

entries.zh: 操不從。
entries.en: Cao would not listen.
entries.literal: Cao did not follow his advice.

entries.zh: 居七日，蜀降者說「蜀中一日數十驚，守將雖斬之而不能安也。」
entries.en: Seven days later a defector from Shu reported, "In Shu there are dozens of alarms in a single day; though the garrison commanders execute people, they cannot restore order."
entries.literal: After seven days, a Shu surrenderer said: "In Shu there are several tens of alarms in a single day; though the defending generals execute men, they cannot restore calm."

entries.zh: 操問曄曰：「今尚可擊不？」
entries.en: Cao asked Liu Ye, "Can we still attack?"
entries.literal: Cao asked Ye: "Can we still attack now?"

entries.zh: 曄曰：「今已小定，未可擊也。」
entries.en: Liu Ye said, "It has already stabilized somewhat—we cannot attack now."
entries.literal: Ye said: "It has now settled somewhat; it cannot be attacked."

entries.zh: 乃還。
entries.en: So Cao withdrew.
entries.literal: He then returned.

entries.zh: 以夏侯淵為都護將軍，督張郃、徐晃等守漢中；
entries.en: He appointed Xiahou Yuan Protector General to command Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others in holding Hanzhong;
entries.literal: He made Xiahou Yuan Protector General and had him supervise Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others in guarding Hanzhong;

entries.zh: 以丞相長史杜襲為駙馬都尉，留督漢中事。
entries.en: He left Chancellor Chief Clerk Du Xi as Commandant of Equipage to oversee civil affairs in Hanzhong.
entries.literal: he made Chancellor Chief Clerk Du Xi Commandant of Equipage and left him to supervise Hanzhong affairs.

entries.zh: 襲綏懷開導，百姓自樂出徙洛、鄴者八萬餘口。
entries.en: Du Xi soothed and settled the people with gentle guidance, and more than eighty thousand families willingly migrated to Luoyang and Ye.
entries.literal: Xi soothed and guided with kindness; more than eighty thousand common people willingly moved out to settle in Luoyang and Ye.

entries.zh: 漢紀五十九起閼逢敦牂，盡柔兆涒灘，凡三年。
entries.en: Han Records 59 Spanning from the year Yanfeng Dunxiang through Rouzhao Toushan—a period of three years.
entries.literal: Han Records 59 Beginning with Yanfeng Dunxiang, ending with Rouzhao Toushan, three years in all.

entries.zh: 是時太子在鄴，軍中騷動。
entries.en: The Crown Prince was then at Ye, and the army was in uproar.
entries.literal: At this time the Heir Apparent was at Ye, and the army was in turmoil.

entries.zh: 群僚欲秘不發喪，諫議大夫賈逵以為事不可秘，乃發喪。
entries.en: The ministers wished to conceal the death and not announce mourning, but Remonstrance Counselor Jia Kui argued that the affair could not be hidden, and mourning was proclaimed.
entries.literal: The officials wished to keep secret and not announce the mourning. Remonstrance Counselor Jia Kui held that the matter could not be kept secret, and so the mourning was announced.

entries.zh: 或言宜諸城守，悉用譙、沛人。
entries.en: Some proposed that every city garrison should be staffed entirely with men from Qiao and Pei.
entries.literal: Some said that city garrisons should all employ men from Qiao and Pei.

entries.zh: 魏郡太守廣陵徐宣厲聲曰：「今者遠近一統，人懷效節，何必專任譙、沛以沮宿衛者之心！」
entries.en: Xu Xuan of Guangling, prefect of Wei Commandery, said sharply: "Now that the realm is united from near and far, and all are eager to serve, why should we rely solely on men from Qiao and Pei and thus discourage the hearts of the palace guards!"
entries.literal: Administrator of Wei Commandery Xu Xuan of Guangling said sternly: "Now near and far are united, and men are ready to serve faithfully—why must we exclusively employ those from Qiao and Pei to dampen the hearts of the long-serving guards!"

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: The proposal was dropped.
entries.literal: And so it was stopped.

entries.zh: 青州兵擅擊鼓相引去，眾人以為宜禁止之，不從者討之。
entries.en: Qingzhou troops began beating drums on their own and marched off together. Many thought they should be stopped by force and that anyone who refused should be attacked.
entries.literal: Qingzhou soldiers on their own beat drums and led one another away. The crowd thought they should be stopped, and those who did not obey should be punished.

entries.zh: 賈逵曰：「不可。」
entries.en: Jia Kui said, "That must not be done."
entries.literal: Jia Kui said: "It cannot be done."

entries.zh: 為作長檄，令所在給其稟食。
entries.en: He drafted a long proclamation ordering every locality along their route to furnish them rations.
entries.literal: He wrote a long dispatch ordering that wherever they passed, provisions be supplied to them.

entries.zh: 鄢陵侯彰從長安來赴，問逵先王璽綬所在，逵正色曰：「國有儲副，先王璽綬非君侯所宜問也。」
entries.en: Marquis Zhang of Yanling had come from Chang'an to attend the funeral and asked Kui where the late king's seal and ribbon were. Kui said sternly, "The state already has an heir designate; the seal and ribbon of the late king are not a matter Your Lordship should raise."
entries.literal: Marquis Zhang of Yanling came from Chang'an to attend and asked Kui where the late king's seal and cord were. Kui said with stern face: "The state has a designated heir; the late king's seal and cord are not what Your Lordship should inquire about."

entries.zh: 凶問至鄴，太子號哭不已。
entries.en: When word of the death reached Ye, the Crown Prince wailed ceaselessly.
entries.literal: When news of the death reached Ye, the Heir Apparent wailed without cease.

entries.zh: 中庶子司馬孚諫曰：「君王晏駕，天下恃殿下為命。
entries.en: Palace Attendant Sima Fu admonished him: "Our lord is gone, and the empire looks to Your Highness for its very life.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Sima Fu remonstrated: "Our lord has passed away; the empire relies on Your Highness for its fate.

entries.zh: 當上為宗廟，下為萬國，奈何效匹夫孝也！」
entries.en: You must tend the ancestral shrines above and govern the myriad realms below—why imitate the mourning of a private commoner!"
entries.literal: You should above serve the ancestral temple and below rule ten thousand states—why act the private filial piety of a common man!"

entries.zh: 太子良久乃止，曰：「卿言是也。」
entries.en: Only after a long while did the Crown Prince cease and say, "You speak rightly."
entries.literal: After a long while the Heir Apparent stopped and said: "Your words are correct."

entries.zh: 時群臣初聞王薨，相聚哭，無復行列。
entries.en: When the ministers had first heard that the King was dead, they had clustered together in tears with no regard for order.
entries.literal: At this time when the officials first heard the King had died, they gathered to weep and there was no longer any formation of ranks.

entries.zh: 孚厲聲於朝曰：「今君王違世，天下震動，當早拜嗣君，以鎮萬國，而但哭邪！」
entries.en: Fu cried out sternly in court: "Our lord has departed and the realm is shaken. You ought to bow to the successor at once to steady the empire—yet all you do is weep!"
entries.literal: Fu said sternly in court: "Now our lord has left the world and the empire trembles—we should early pay homage to the successor to settle ten thousand states—yet only weep?"

entries.zh: 乃罷群臣，備禁衛，治喪事。
entries.en: He then dismissed the assembly, posted the guards, and set the mourning in order.
entries.literal: Then he dismissed the officials, prepared the guard, and arranged mourning affairs.

entries.zh: 孚，懿之弟也。
entries.en: Fu was the younger brother of Sima Yi.
entries.literal: Fu was Sima Yi's younger brother.

entries.zh: 群臣以為太子即位，當須詔命。
entries.en: The ministers held that the Crown Prince could not take the throne without an imperial edict.
entries.literal: The officials thought that for the Heir Apparent to ascend, an imperial edict was required.

entries.zh: 尚書陳矯曰：「王薨於外，天下惶懼。
entries.en: Minister of Works Chen Qiao said, "The King died away from the capital, and the realm is filled with fear.
entries.literal: Minister Chen Qiao said: "The King died abroad; the empire is fearful and alarmed.

entries.zh: 太子宜割哀即位，以系遠近之望。
entries.en: The Crown Prince ought to set grief aside and take the throne at once, to hold the hopes of men near and far together.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent should cut short mourning and ascend, to tie the hopes of near and far.

entries.zh: 且又愛子在側，彼此生變，則社稷危也。」
entries.en: Moreover, with a favored son close at hand, any friction between them could put the altars of state in danger."
entries.literal: Moreover there is a favored son at hand—if each side bred change, the altars of state would be in peril."

entries.zh: 即具官備禮，一日皆辦。
entries.en: The requisite officials and ceremonies were prepared that same day.
entries.literal: Immediately the officials and rituals were all provided, completed in one day.

entries.zh: 明旦，以王后令，策太子即王位，大赦。
entries.en: The next morning, by order of the Queen, the Crown Prince was installed as King and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: Next dawn, by the Queen's order, the Heir Apparent was enthroned as King with an edict of investiture, and a general amnesty was declared.

entries.zh: 漢帝尋遣御史大夫華歆奉策詔，授太子丞相印、綬，魏王璽、綬，領冀州牧。
entries.en: Before long the Han emperor dispatched Imperial Counselor Hua Xin with the formal investiture, granting the Crown Prince the seals and ribbons of Chancellor and King of Wei and appointing him Governor of Ji Province.
entries.literal: Soon the Han Emperor sent Imperial Counselor Hua Xin bearing the edict of investiture, conferring on the Heir Apparent the seal and cord of Chancellor, the seal and cord of King of Wei, and appointment as Governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 於是尊王后曰王太后。
entries.en: The Queen was then honored as Queen Dowager.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Queen was honored as Queen Dowager.

entries.zh: 吳王以其子登為太子，妙選師友，以南郡太守諸葛瑾之子恪、綏遠將軍張昭之子休、大理吳郡顧雍之子譚、偏將軍廬江陳武之子表皆為中庶子，入講詩書，出從騎射，謂之四友。
entries.en: The King of Wu made his son Deng crown prince and finely selected teachers and companions—making Zhuge Ke, son of Grand Administrator of Nanjun Zhuge Jin; Sun Xiu, son of General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao; Gu Tan, son of Grand Judge of Wujun Gu Yong; and Chen Biao, son of Adjunct General of Lujiang Chen Wu all Supernumerary Palace Attendants. They entered to lecture on the Poetry and Documents and went out to follow in horsemanship and archery—he called them the Four Friends.
entries.literal: The King of Wu made his son Deng crown prince, finely selected teachers and companions—making Zhuge Ke son of Grand Administrator of Nanjun Zhuge Jin, Sun Xiu son of General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao, Gu Tan son of Grand Judge of Wujun Gu Yong, and Chen Biao son of Adjunct General of Lujiang Chen Wu all Supernumerary Palace Attendants, entering to lecture on Poetry and Documents, going out to follow in horsemanship and archery—calling them the Four Friends.

entries.zh: 登接待僚屬，略用布衣之禮。
entries.en: In receiving and attending to subordinates, Deng generally used the courtesies of a plain-clothed gentleman.
entries.literal: Deng in receiving and attending to subordinates generally used the courtesies of the plain-clothed.

entries.zh: 魏紀一
entries.en: Wei Records 1
entries.literal: Wei Records 1

entries.zh: 春，正月，司馬懿攻新城，旬有六日，拔之，斬孟達。
entries.en: In spring, during the first month, Sima Yi besieged Xincheng; within sixteen days he captured it and executed Meng Da.
entries.literal: Spring, first month, Sima Yi attacked Xincheng; in sixteen days he took it and beheaded Meng Da.

entries.zh: 申儀久在魏興，擅承製刻印，多所假授；
entries.en: Shen Yi had long served in Weixing, where he had taken it upon himself to cut seals and issue credentials on his own authority, handing out many illicit commissions.
entries.literal: Shen Yi had long been in Weixing, usurping authority to engrave seals on imperial orders and granting many unauthorized appointments.

entries.zh: 懿召而執之，歸于洛陽。
entries.en: Sima Yi summoned him, placed him under arrest, and sent him back to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Yi summoned and arrested him, then sent him back to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 吳王使鄱陽太守周魴密求山中舊族名帥為北方所聞知者，令譎挑揚州牧曹休。
entries.en: The King of Wu had Poyang Administrator Zhou Fang secretly recruit mountain clan leaders whose names were known in the north, to lure and provoke Yang Province Governor Cao Xiu.
entries.literal: The King of Wu had Poyang Administrator Zhou Fang secretly seek out old clan leaders of renown in the mountains known to the north, and had them deceive and provoke Yang Province Governor Cao Xiu.

entries.zh: 魴曰：「民帥小丑，不足杖任，事或漏洩，不能致休。
entries.en: Fang said, "These local chiefs are small fry—not fit for the task; word might leak and we would fail to draw Xiu out.
entries.literal: Fang said: "These civilian chieftains are petty figures, not fit to be relied upon; the affair might leak and fail to draw Xiu.

entries.zh: 乞遣親人繼箋以誘休，言被譴懼誅，欲以郡降北，求兵應接。」
entries.en: Send my kinsman Ji Jian to bait Xiu—say I have been censured and fear death, wish to surrender the commandery to Wei, and need troops to receive me."
entries.literal: I beg to send a close kinsman, Ji Jian, to entice Xiu, saying that having been reprimanded and fearing execution, he wishes to surrender the commandery to the north and seeks troops to support him."

entries.zh: 吳王許之。
entries.en: The King of Wu agreed.
entries.literal: The King of Wu consented.

entries.zh: 時頻有郎官詣魴詰問諸事，魴因詣郡門下，下發謝。
entries.en: Court envoys kept coming to question Fang; he went to the commandery gate and issued a letter of apology.
entries.literal: At the time palace attendants frequently came to Fang to question him on various matters; Fang therefore went to the commandery gate, sent down a letter of apology.

entries.zh: 休聞之，率步騎十萬向皖以應魴；
entries.en: When Xiu heard, he led one hundred thousand foot and horse toward Wan to answer Fang.
entries.literal: When Xiu heard of it, he led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry toward Wan to answer Fang.

entries.zh: 帝又使司馬懿向江陵，賈逵向東關，三道俱進。
entries.en: The emperor also sent Sima Yi toward Jiangling and Jia Kui toward Dong Pass—the three columns advanced together.
entries.literal: The Emperor also sent Sima Yi toward Jiangling and Jia Kui toward Dong Pass; all three columns advanced together.

entries.zh: 大司馬曹真以「漢(蜀)人數入寇，請由斜谷伐之。
entries.en: Grand Minister of War Cao Zhen said, "Han troops have repeatedly raided. I request to attack by way of Xiegu.
entries.literal: Grand Minister of War Cao Zhen said, "Han troops have repeatedly raided; I request to attack them by way of Xiegu.

entries.zh: 諸將數道並進，可以大克。」
entries.en: With several generals advancing on parallel routes, a crushing victory could be won."
entries.literal: If the generals advance on several routes together, a great victory can be achieved."

entries.zh: 帝從之，詔大將軍司馬懿溯漢水由西城入，與真會漢中，諸將或由子午谷、或由建(
entries.en: The Emperor agreed and ordered Grand General Sima Yi to ascend the Han River and enter by Xicheng, to rendezvous with Zhen at Hanzhong, while other generals were to move either through Ziwu Valley or through Jian (
entries.literal: The Emperor followed this and ordered Grand General Sima Yi to go upstream on the Han River and enter by Xicheng, to meet Zhen at Hanzhong; the generals were either to go by Ziwu Valley or by Jian (

entries.zh: 武)
entries.en: Wu)
entries.literal: Wu)

entries.zh: 威入 武)
entries.en: Wu)
entries.literal: Wu)

entries.zh: 威入據胡注改。。
entries.en: Wei) to enter—the reading Jianwei is emended according to Hu Zan's commentary. End of editorial note.
entries.literal: Wei) to enter—emended according to Hu's commentary. .

entries.zh: 司空陳群諫曰：「太祖昔到陽平攻張魯，多收豆麥以益軍糧，魯未下而食猶乏。
entries.en: Director of Works Chen Qun remonstrated: "When the Grand Ancestor marched on Yangping to attack Zhang Lu, he requisitioned beans and wheat to fill the army's granaries—yet before Lu fell, provisions were already running short.
entries.literal: Director of Works Chen Qun remonstrated, saying: "When the Grand Ancestor once came to Yangping to attack Zhang Lu, he gathered much beans and wheat to augment the army's grain; before Lu was taken, food was still scarce.

entries.zh: 今既無所因，且斜谷阻險，難以進退，轉運必見鈔截，多留兵守要，則損戰士，不可不熟慮也。」
entries.en: Now we have no such base to draw on, and Xiegu is steep and treacherous—hard to advance and harder to retreat. Convoys will be cut off; garrison too many choke points and you strip the fighting line. This cannot be weighed too carefully."
entries.literal: Now there is nothing to rely on, and moreover Xiegu is rugged and perilous, hard to advance or withdraw; transport will surely be intercepted by raiders; if many troops are left to guard key points, fighting strength is diminished—you cannot fail to consider this carefully."

entries.zh: 帝從群議。
entries.en: The Emperor accepted Qun's counsel.
entries.literal: The Emperor followed Qun's advice.

entries.zh: 真復表從子午道；
entries.en: Zhen memorialized again, insisting on the Ziwu route;
entries.literal: Zhen again memorialized to go by the Ziwu route;

entries.zh: 群又陳其不便，並言軍事用度之計。
entries.en: Qun again laid out the route's drawbacks and spelled out the cost of the campaign.
entries.literal: Qun again set forth its drawbacks and also spoke of military expenditure calculations.

entries.zh: 詔以群議下真，真據之遂行。
entries.en: The court forwarded Qun's objections to Zhen; Zhen held to his plan and marched anyway.
entries.literal: An edict sent Qun's arguments down to Zhen; Zhen resisted and proceeded anyway.

entries.zh: 魏紀三
entries.en: Wei Records 3
entries.literal: Wei Records 3

entries.zh: 乙未，峻逼遷帝於石頭。
entries.en: On day Yiwei, Su Jun forced the emperor to move to Stone City.
entries.literal: On day Yiwei, Jun compelled the relocation of the emperor to Stone City.

entries.zh: 司徒導固爭，不從。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Wang Dao protested fiercely but was overruled.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Dao remonstrated firmly but was not heeded.

entries.zh: 帝哀泣升車，宮中慟哭。
entries.en: The emperor wept as he boarded the carriage; the palace echoed with mourning.
entries.literal: The emperor wept in grief as he mounted the carriage; within the palace there was wailing.

entries.zh: 時天大雨，道路泥濘，劉超、鐘雅步侍左右。
entries.en: It rained heavily; the roads were mud; Liu Chao and Zhong Ya walked at his side through it all.
entries.literal: At the time Heaven sent great rain; the roads were mire; Liu Chao and Zhong Ya walked in attendance at left and right.

entries.zh: 峻給馬，不肯乘，而悲哀慷慨。
entries.en: Su Jun offered horses; they refused to ride, grieving yet defiant.
entries.literal: Jun provided horses; they refused to mount, yet were mournful and resolute.

entries.zh: 峻聞而惡之，然未敢殺也。
entries.en: Su Jun hated this but dared not kill them.
entries.literal: Jun heard and hated this, yet did not dare kill them.

entries.zh: 以其親信許方等補司馬督、殿中監，外托宿衛，內實防禦超等。
entries.en: He made his confidant Xu Fang Commander of the Army and Palace Director—nominally for palace guard, in truth to watch Liu Chao and the others.
entries.literal: He appointed his trusted follower Xu Fang and others as Commander of the Army and Palace Director—outwardly entrusted with night guard, inwardly really to guard against Chao and the rest.

entries.zh: 峻以倉屋為帝宮，日來帝前肆丑言。
entries.en: Su Jun housed the emperor in granary buildings and came each day to hurl insults at him.
entries.literal: Jun made granary buildings the emperor's palace and daily came before the emperor to vent foul speech.

entries.zh: 劉超、鐘雅與右光祿大夫荀崧、金紫光祿大夫華恆、尚書荀邃、侍中丁潭侍從，不離帝側。
entries.en: Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Right Grand Master of the Bright Xu Song, Grand Master of the Golden Purple Hua Heng, Secretary Xun Sui, and Palace Attendant Ding Tan never left the emperor's side.
entries.literal: Liu Chao, Zhong Ya, Right Grand Master of the Bright Xu Song, Grand Master of the Golden Purple Hua Heng, Secretary Xun Sui, and Palace Attendant Ding Tan attended in service and did not leave the emperor's side.

entries.zh: 時饑饉，米貴，峻問遺，超一無所受，繾綣朝夕，臣節愈恭；
entries.en: Famine had driven rice prices high; when Su Jun sent gifts, Liu Chao refused every one; day and night he tended the emperor, his loyalty growing ever more reverent;
entries.literal: At the time there was famine; rice was costly; Jun sent gifts; Chao accepted none; day and night he was devoted; his ministerial conduct grew ever more respectful;

entries.zh: 雖居幽厄之中，超猶啟帝，授《孝經》、《論語》。
entries.en: though held captive, Liu Chao still taught the emperor the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
entries.literal: though dwelling in dire straits, Chao still instructed the emperor, teaching him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

entries.zh: 曜見勒，曰：「石王，頗憶重門之盟否？」
entries.en: When Liu Yao was brought before Shi Le, he said: "King Shi, do you still remember our pact at Chongmen?"
entries.literal: When Yao saw Le he said: "King Shi, do you still recall the covenant at Chongmen?"

entries.zh: 勒使徐光謂之曰：「今日之事，天使其然，復雲何邪！」
entries.en: Shi Le had Xu Guang reply: "What has happened today Heaven itself ordained—what more is there to say!"
entries.literal: Le had Xu Guang tell him: "Today's matter Heaven has made so—what further can one say!"

entries.zh: 乙酉，勒班師。
entries.en: On yiyou, Shi Le withdrew his army.
entries.literal: On yiyou, Le withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 使征東將軍石邃將兵衛送曜。
entries.en: He sent Eastern Campaign General Shi Sui with troops to guard and escort Liu Yao.
entries.literal: He sent Eastern Campaign General Shi Sui to lead troops guarding and escorting Yao.

entries.zh: 邃，虎之子也。
entries.en: Shi Sui was Shi Hu's son.
entries.literal: Sui was Hu's son.

entries.zh: 曜瘡甚，載以馬輿，使醫李永與同載。
entries.en: Liu Yao's wounds were grave. He was carried in a horse-drawn litter, with the physician Li Yong riding beside him.
entries.literal: Yao's wounds were severe; he was carried in a horse litter with the physician Li Yong riding with him.

entries.zh: 己亥，至襄國，捨曜於永豐小城，給其妓妾，嚴兵圍守。
entries.en: On jihai they reached Xiangguo. Liu Yao was housed in the small town of Yongfeng, given singing girls and concubines, and kept under heavy guard.
entries.literal: On jihai they reached Xiangguo; they lodged Yao in Yongfeng small town, supplied him with courtesans, and surrounded him with strict troops.

entries.zh: 遣劉岳、劉震等從男女盛服以見之，曜曰：「吾謂卿等久為灰土，石王仁厚，乃全宥至今邪！
entries.en: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen, and others, followed by men and women in fine dress, to visit him. Liu Yao said: "I thought you had long since turned to dust. King Shi is generous indeed—to have spared you all until now!
entries.literal: He sent Liu Yue, Liu Zhen, and others followed by men and women in splendid dress to see him; Yao said: "I thought you had long been ashes; King Shi's kindness and generosity—yet he fully spared you till now!

entries.zh: 我殺石佗，愧之多矣。
entries.en: When I killed Shi Tuo, I already owed him more shame than I can count.
entries.literal: I killed Shi Tuo—a weight of shame.

entries.zh: 今日之禍，自其分耳。」
entries.en: The disaster that has befallen me today is simply my allotted fate."
entries.literal: Today's calamity is simply what was fated."

entries.zh: 留宴終日而去。
entries.en: They remained and feasted with him all day before departing.
entries.literal: They stayed feasting all day then left.

entries.zh: 勒使曜與其太子熙書，諭令速降；
entries.en: Shi Le had Liu Yao write to his crown prince Liu Xi, urging him to surrender quickly;
entries.literal: Le had Yao write to his crown prince Xi, instructing swift surrender;

entries.zh: 曜但敕熙與諸大臣「匡維社稷，勿以吾易意也。」
entries.en: but Liu Yao merely instructed Xi and the chief ministers: "Hold firm to the altars of state. Do not alter your purpose because of me."
entries.literal: But Yao only ordered Xi and the ministers "Uphold the altars of state; do not change your resolve on my account."

entries.zh: 勒見而惡之，久之，乃殺曜。
entries.en: When Shi Le read the letter he was disgusted, and after some time he had Liu Yao executed.
entries.literal: Le saw it and loathed it; after some time he killed Yao.

entries.zh: 右衛將軍齊超、侍中鐘雅與建康令管旆等謀奉帝出赴西軍；
entries.en: Right Guard General Qi Chao, Palace Attendant Zhong Ya, and Jiankang Prefect Guan Pei and others plotted to take the emperor out to the western armies;
entries.literal: Right Guard General Qi Chao, Palace Attendant Zhong Ya, and Jiankang Prefect Guan Pei and others plotted to escort the emperor out to join the western armies;

entries.zh: 事洩，蘇逸使其將平原任讓將兵入宮收超、雅。
entries.en: when the plot leaked, Su Yi sent his general Ren Rang of Pingyuan with troops into the palace to seize Chao and Ya.
entries.literal: The plot leaked; Su Yi sent his general Pingyuan Ren Rang with troops into the palace to seize Chao and Ya.

entries.zh: 帝抱持悲泣曰：「還我侍中、右衛！」
entries.en: The emperor clung to them, weeping: "Give me back my palace attendant and my right guard!"
entries.literal: The emperor clung to them weeping: "Give me back my palace attendant and right guard!"

entries.zh: 讓奪而殺之。
entries.en: Ren Rang tore them from his arms and killed them.
entries.literal: Rang snatched them away and killed them.

entries.zh: 初，讓少無行，太常華恆為本州大中正，黜其品。
entries.en: Ren Rang had been dissolute in his youth. Hua Heng, Grand Master of Ceremonies and chief provincial arbiter of ranks, had lowered his standing.
entries.literal: Earlier, Rang in youth had no proper conduct; Grand Master of Ceremonies Hua Heng as provincial chief arbiter of ranks demoted his grade.

entries.zh: 及讓為蘇峻將，乘勢多所誅殺，見恆輒恭敬，不敢縱暴。
entries.en: After he became one of Su Jun's generals and rode the tide of power, he killed many—but whenever he saw Hua Heng he behaved with deference and did not dare abuse his authority.
entries.literal: When Rang became Su Jun's general, riding the momentum he killed many; when he saw Heng he always showed respect and did not dare act violently.

entries.zh: 及鐘、劉之死，蘇逸欲並殺恆，讓盡心救衛，恆乃得免。
entries.en: When Zhong Ya and Liu Chao died, Su Yi wanted to kill Hua Heng as well. Ren Rang threw himself into protecting him, and Heng was spared.
entries.literal: At the deaths of Zhong and Liu, Su Yi wished to kill Heng as well; Rang exerted himself to save and protect him, and Heng thus escaped.

entries.zh: 二月，後趙群臣請後趙王勒即皇帝位；
entries.en: In the second month, the ministers of Later Zhao asked King Le to take the imperial throne;
entries.literal: Second month, the ministers of Later Zhao requested that Later Zhao King Le assume the imperial throne;

entries.zh: 勒乃稱大趙天王，行皇帝事。
entries.en: Le then styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao and ruled as emperor in all but name.
entries.literal: Le then styled himself Heavenly King of Great Zhao and exercised imperial affairs.

entries.zh: 立妃劉氏為王后，世子弘為太子。
entries.en: He made Consort Liu queen and his heir Hong crown prince.
entries.literal: He established Consort Liu as queen and heir-apparent Hong as crown prince.

entries.zh: 以其子宏為驃騎大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、大單于，封秦王；
entries.en: He appointed his son Hong General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Commander of all military affairs, and Grand Chanyu, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Qin;
entries.literal: He made his son Hong General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Commander of all military affairs within and without, and Grand Chanyu, enfeoffing him as Prince of Qin;

entries.zh: 斌為左衛將軍，封太原王；
entries.en: Bin was made General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan;
entries.literal: Bin was made General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan;

entries.zh: 恢為輔國將軍，封南陽王。
entries.en: Hui was made General Who Assists the State and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.
entries.literal: Hui was made General Who Assists the State and enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 以中山公虎為太尉、尚書令，進爵為王；
entries.en: Hu, Duke of Zhongshan, was made Grand Commandant and Director of the Masters of Writing and raised to princely rank;
entries.literal: Duke of Zhongshan Hu was made Grand Commandant and Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced in rank to king;

entries.zh: 虎子邃為冀州刺史，封齊王；
entries.en: Hu's son Sui was appointed Governor of Jizhou and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi;
entries.literal: Hu's son Sui was made Governor of Jizhou and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi;

entries.zh: 宣為左將軍；
entries.en: Xuan was made General of the Left;
entries.literal: Xuan was made General of the Left;

entries.zh: 挺為侍中，封梁王。
entries.en: Ting was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: Ting was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 又封石生為河東王，石堪為彭城王。
entries.en: Shi Sheng was also enfeoffed as Prince of Hedong and Shi Kan as Prince of Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Also enfeoffed Shi Sheng as Prince of Hedong and Shi Kan as Prince of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 以左長史郭敖為尚書左僕射，右長史程遐為右僕射、領吏部尚書，左司馬夔安、右司馬郭殷、從事中郎李鳳、前郎中令裴憲，皆為尚書，參軍事徐光為中書令、領秘書監。
entries.en: Left Chief Clerk Guo Ao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Chief Clerk Cheng Xia was made Right Vice Director and concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Left Major Kui An, Right Major Guo Yin, Attendant Cadet Li Feng, and former Director of Palace Attendants Pei Xian were all appointed Masters of Writing; and Staff Officer Xu Guang was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Supervisor of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: Left Chief Clerk Guo Ao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Chief Clerk Cheng Xia was made Right Vice Director and concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Left Major Kui An, Right Major Guo Yin, Attendant Cadet Li Feng, and former Director of Palace Attendants Pei Xian were all made Masters of Writing; Staff Officer Xu Guang was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent Supervisor of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 自餘文武，封拜各有差。
entries.en: The remaining civil and military officials received promotions and appointments according to their rank.
entries.literal: The remaining civil and military officials received enfeoffments and appointments each according to rank.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第094卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 94
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 94

entries.zh: 夏，五月，乙卯，帝不豫；
entries.en: In summer, in the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell gravely ill;
entries.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell ill;

entries.zh: 六月，庚寅，疾篤。
entries.en: and in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his condition turned critical.
entries.literal: in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his illness became critical.

entries.zh: 或詐為尚書符，敕宮門無得內宰相；
entries.en: Someone forged a Secretariat order barring chief ministers from entering the palace gates;
entries.literal: Someone forged an order in the name of the Secretariat forbidding the palace gates to admit the chief ministers;

entries.zh: 眾皆失色。
entries.en: and everyone turned pale with alarm.
entries.literal: all turned pale.

entries.zh: 庾冰曰：「此必詐也。」
entries.en: Yu Bing said, "This must be a forgery."
entries.literal: Yu Bing said, "This must be a fraud."

entries.zh: 推問，果然。
entries.en: Investigation proved that it was.
entries.literal: On investigation, it proved so.

entries.zh: 帝二子丕、弈，皆在襁褓。
entries.en: The emperor's two sons, Pi and Yi, were both still infants.
entries.literal: The emperor's two sons Pi and Yi were both still in swaddling clothes.

entries.zh: 庾冰自以兄弟秉權日久，恐易世之後，親屬愈疏，為它人所間，每說帝以國有強敵，宜立長君；
entries.en: Yu Bing, knowing that he and his brothers had held power for years, feared that after a change of reign their kin would be pushed aside and others would come between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful foes abroad the throne should pass to a mature heir.
entries.literal: Yu Bing, considering that he and his brothers had held power long, feared that after a change of reign kinsmen would grow more distant and others would drive wedges between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful enemies abroad the state should install an elder sovereign;

entries.zh: 請以母親弟琅邪王岳為嗣，帝許之。
entries.en: He proposed the emperor's younger uterine half-brother, Prince Yue of Langye, as successor, and the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: he asked that the emperor's younger maternal half-brother, Prince of Langye Yue, be made heir, and the emperor assented.

entries.zh: 中書令何充曰：「父子相傳，先王舊典，易之者鮮不致亂。
entries.en: He Chong, Director of the Secretariat, said, "Passing the throne from father to son is the ancient royal norm; those who alter it seldom avoid turmoil.
entries.literal: Zhongshu Ling He Chong said, "Father-to-son succession is the ancient royal norm; those who change it rarely escape disorder.

entries.zh: 故武王不授聖弟，非不愛也。
entries.en: King Wu did not enthrone his gifted younger brother—not because he loved him less.
entries.literal: Therefore King Wu did not give the throne to his sage younger brother—not from lack of love.

entries.zh: 今琅邪踐阼，將如孺子何！」
entries.en: If Prince Langye takes the throne, what will become of these infant princes!"
entries.literal: If Langye now ascends the throne, what is to become of the infant sons!"

entries.zh: 冰不聽。
entries.en: Bing would not heed him.
entries.literal: Bing would not listen.

entries.zh: 下詔，以岳為嗣，並以弈繼琅邪哀王。
entries.en: An edict named Yue as heir and assigned Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.
entries.literal: An edict was issued making Yue the heir and also assigning Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.

entries.zh: 壬辰，冰、充及武陵王晞、會稽王昱、尚書令諸葛恢並受顧命。
entries.en: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Zhuge Hui, Director of the Secretariat, all received the emperor's deathbed commission.
entries.literal: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Shangshu Ling Zhuge Hui all received the dying emperor's charge.

entries.zh: 癸巳，帝崩。
entries.en: On guǐsì the emperor died.
entries.literal: On guǐsì, the emperor died.

entries.zh: 帝幼沖嗣位，不親庶政；
entries.en: He had come to the throne as a child and had not personally directed routine affairs;
entries.literal: The emperor had succeeded young and did not personally handle routine government;

entries.zh: 及長，頗有勤儉之德。
entries.en: but as he matured he showed real virtue in diligence and frugality.
entries.literal: when he grew up he showed considerable virtue in diligence and frugality.

entries.zh: 十一月，皝自將勁兵四萬出南道，以慕容翰、慕容霸為前鋒，別遣長史王寓等將兵萬五千出北道，以伐高句麗。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Huang led forty thousand picked troops in person along the southern route, with Murong Han and Murong Ba as vanguard, while Chief Clerk Wang Yu and others took fifteen thousand men along the northern route against Koguryŏ.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Huang personally led forty thousand crack troops out the southern road, with Murong Han and Murong Ba as vanguard, and separately sent Chief Clerk Wang Yu and others with fifteen thousand men out the northern road to attack Koguryŏ.

entries.zh: 高句麗王釗果遣弟武帥精兵五萬拒北道，自帥羸兵以備南道。
entries.en: King Chao of Koguryŏ duly sent his brother Wu with fifty thousand elite troops to block the northern road, while he himself led weaker forces to face the south.
entries.literal: King Chao of Koguryŏ indeed sent his brother Wu at the head of fifty thousand elite troops to block the northern road, while he himself led weak troops to guard the southern road.

entries.zh: 慕容翰等先至，與釗合戰，皝以大眾繼之。
entries.en: Murong Han's vanguard arrived first and engaged Chao; Huang came up with the main army.
entries.literal: Murong Han and the others arrived first and joined battle with Chao; Huang followed with the main host.

entries.zh: 左常侍鮮于亮曰：「臣以俘虜蒙王國士之恩，不可以不報；
entries.en: Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xianyu Liang said, "I was once a captive, yet Your Majesty treated me as a pillar of the state; I cannot fail to repay that debt;
entries.literal: Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xianyu Liang said, "Your servant, though once a captive, received the grace of the state's favor and cannot fail to repay it;

entries.zh: 今日，臣死日也！」
entries.en: today is the day I die!"
entries.literal: today is the day your servant dies!"

entries.zh: 獨與數騎先犯高句麗陣，所向摧陷。
entries.en: He charged the Koguryŏ line at the head of only a few horsemen and broke through wherever he struck.
entries.literal: He alone with a few horsemen was first to charge the Koguryŏ line, breaking through wherever he turned.

entries.zh: 高句麗陣動，大眾因而乘之，高句麗兵大敗。
entries.en: The Koguryŏ line buckled; the main army pressed the advantage and routed them completely.
entries.literal: The Koguryŏ formation wavered; the great host pressed the advantage and the Koguryŏ army was utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 左長史韓壽斬高句麗將阿佛和度加，諸軍乘勝追之，遂入丸都。
entries.en: Left Chief Clerk Han Shou slew the Koguryŏ general Afohedujia; the armies pursued the victory and entered Wandu.
entries.literal: Left Chief Clerk Han Shou slew the Koguryŏ general Afohedujia; the armies pursued in victory and entered Wandu.

entries.zh: 釗單騎走，輕車將軍慕輿泥追獲其母周氏及妻而還。
entries.en: Chao fled alone; Light-Carriage General Murong Ni pursued and captured his mother, Lady Zhou, and his wife before returning.
entries.literal: Chao fled alone on horseback; Light-Carriage General Murong Ni pursued and captured his mother Lady Zhou and his wife before returning.

entries.zh: 會王寓等戰於北道，皆敗沒，由是皝不復窮追。
entries.en: Meanwhile Wang Yu's force on the northern road was destroyed; for that reason Huang did not press the pursuit further.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Wang Yu and the others fought on the northern road and were all defeated and lost; for this reason Huang did not press the pursuit to the end.

entries.zh: 遣使招釗，釗不出。
entries.en: He sent envoys to summon Chao, but Chao would not submit.
entries.literal: He sent envoys to summon Chao; Chao did not come forth.

entries.zh: 皝將還，韓壽曰：「高句麗之地，不可戍守。
entries.en: As Huang prepared to withdraw, Han Shou said, "Koguryŏ cannot be held by garrisons.
entries.literal: As Huang was about to withdraw, Han Shou said, "The land of Koguryŏ cannot be garrisoned.

entries.zh: 今其主亡民散，潛伏山谷；
entries.en: Their king has fled and the people are scattered in the hills;
entries.literal: Now their ruler is fled and the people scattered, hiding in mountain valleys;

entries.zh: 大軍既去，必復鳩聚，收其餘燼，猶足為患。
entries.en: once our army leaves they will rally again, and even the embers they gather will be enough to trouble us.
entries.literal: once the great army departs they will surely gather again; gathering the embers that remain, they will still be enough to cause trouble.

entries.zh: 請載其父屍、囚其生母而歸，俟其束身自歸，然後返之，撫以恩信，策之上也。」
entries.en: Carry off his father's corpse and take his mother prisoner; when he comes to surrender in person, return them and win him with kindness and trust—that is the best policy."
entries.literal: I ask that we carry off his father's corpse and take his living mother prisoner; wait until he binds himself and comes to surrender, then return them and treat him with favor and trust—this is the supreme stratagem."

entries.zh: 皝從之。
entries.en: Huang agreed.
entries.literal: Huang followed this advice.

entries.zh: 發釗父乙弗利墓。
entries.en: They opened the tomb of Chao's father Yifuli.
entries.literal: They opened the tomb of Chao's father Yifuli.

entries.zh: 載其屍，收其府庫累世之寶，虜男女五萬餘口，燒其宮室，毀丸都城而還。
entries.en: They carried off the corpse, seized the hoarded treasures of generations, took more than fifty thousand captives, burned the palaces, razed the walls of Wandu, and withdrew.
entries.literal: They carried off the corpse, seized the treasures accumulated in the royal storehouses for generations, captured more than fifty thousand men and women, burned the palaces, destroyed the walls of Wandu, and returned.

entries.zh: 帝疾篤，庾冰、庾翼欲立會稽王昱為嗣；
entries.en: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;
