entries.literal: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;

entries.zh: 中書監何充建議立皇子聃，帝從之。
entries.en: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.
entries.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.

entries.zh: 九月，丙申，立聃為皇太子。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 戊戌，帝崩於式乾殿。
entries.en: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.
entries.literal: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.

entries.zh: 己亥，何充以遺旨奉太子即位，大赦。
entries.en: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 由是冰、翼深恨充。
entries.en: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.
entries.literal: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.

entries.zh: 尊皇后褚氏為皇太后。
entries.en: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 時穆帝方二歲，太后臨朝稱制。
entries.en: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.

entries.zh: 何充加中書監，錄尚書事。
entries.en: He Chong was additionally made director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.
entries.literal: He Chong was additionally made Director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.

entries.zh: 充自陳既錄尚書，不宜復監中書；
entries.en: Chong himself stated that having authority to record Masters of Writing affairs, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;
entries.literal: Chong himself stated that having authority to record the Masters of Writing, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;

entries.zh: 許之，復加侍中。
entries.en: this was granted, and he was additionally made palace attendant.
entries.literal: this was granted, and he was additionally made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 詔征衛將軍褚裒，欲以為揚州刺史、錄尚書事。
entries.en: An edict summoned Defender-General Chu Pou, intending to appoint him Governor of Yangzhou and Recorder of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: An edict summoned Defender-General Chu Pou, intending to make him Governor of Yangzhou and Recorder of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書劉遐、長史王胡之說裒曰：「會稽王令德雅望，國之周公也，足下宜以大政授之。」
entries.en: Minister of the Civil Service Liu Xia and chief clerk Wang Huzhi urged Pou: "The Prince of Kuaiji's virtue and reputation make him the state's Duke of Zhou; you ought to entrust supreme authority to him."
entries.literal: Minister of the Civil Service Liu Xia and Chief Clerk Wang Huzhi urged Pou, saying: "The Prince of Kuaiji's virtue and elegant reputation make him the Duke of Zhou of the state; you ought to entrust great affairs to him."

entries.zh: 裒乃固辭，歸籓。
entries.en: Pou then firmly declined and returned to his fief.
entries.literal: Pou then firmly declined and returned to his fief.

entries.zh: 壬戌，以會稽王昱為撫軍大將軍，錄尚書六條事。
entries.en: On renxu the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, was made General of Agitating the Army and Recorder of the Six Secretariat Articles.
entries.literal: On renxu, the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, was made General of Agitating the Army and Recorder of Six Articles of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 昱清虛寡慾，尤善玄言，常以劉惔、王濛及穎川韓伯為談客，又辟郗超為撫軍掾，謝萬為從事中郎。
entries.en: Yu was pure and sparing of desire, especially skilled in Dark Learning; he often took Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Han Bo of Yingchuan as conversationalists, and also appointed Xi Chao as staff officer of the Agitating Army and Xie Wan as Secretariat Attendant.
entries.literal: Yu was pure and sparing of desires, especially skilled in Dark Learning; he often took Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Yingchuan's Han Bo as conversation guests; he also appointed Xi Chao as staff officer of the Agitating Army and Xie Wan as Secretariat Attendant.

entries.zh: 超，鑒之孫也，少卓犖不羈。
entries.en: Chao was Xi Jian's grandson; in youth he was outstanding and unrestrained.
entries.literal: Chao was the grandson of Xi Jian; in youth he was outstanding and unrestrained.

entries.zh: 父愔，簡默沖退而嗇於財，積錢至數千萬，嘗開庫任超所取；
entries.en: His father Xi Yin was plain, silent, retiring, and miserly, amassing cash to tens of millions; he once opened the treasury and let Chao take as he wished;
entries.literal: His father Xi Yin was plain, silent, retiring, and stingy with wealth, amassing cash to tens of millions; he once opened the treasury and let Chao take as he wished;

entries.zh: 超散施親故，一日都盡。
entries.en: Chao distributed it to kin and friends and in a single day spent it all.
entries.literal: Chao distributed it to kin and friends and in one day spent it all.

entries.zh: 萬，安之弟也，清曠秀邁，亦有時名。
entries.en: Wan was Xie An's younger brother—pure, open, and elegantly lofty—and he too enjoyed a reputation of the day.
entries.literal: Wan was the younger brother of Xie An; pure, open, and elegantly lofty, he too had a name of the age.

entries.zh: 翼部將干瓚等作亂，殺冠軍將軍曹據。
entries.en: Yi's subordinate generals Gan Zan and others rebelled and killed General of the Champions Cao Ju.
entries.literal: Yi's subordinate generals Gan Zan and others rebelled and killed General of the Champions Cao Ju.

entries.zh: 朱燾與安西長史江虨，建武司馬毛穆之、將軍袁真等共誅之。
entries.en: Zhu Dan, with Western Pacification chief clerk Jiang Bin, Jianwu marshal Mao Muzhi, and general Yuan Zhen and others, jointly executed them.
entries.literal: Zhu Dan with Western Pacification Chief Clerk Jiang Bin, Jianwu Marshal Mao Muzhi, and General Yuan Zhen and others jointly executed them.

entries.zh: 虨，統之子也。
entries.en: Bin was Jiang Tong's son.
entries.literal: Bin was the son of Jiang Tong.

entries.zh: 丹楊尹劉惔每奇溫才，然知其有不臣之志，謂會稽王昱曰：「溫不可使居形勝之地，其位號常宜抑之。」
entries.en: Governor of Danyang Liu Tan often marveled at Wen's talent, yet knew he harbored disloyal ambitions; he told the Prince of Kuaiji: "Wen must not be placed in a strategically decisive post; his rank and title should constantly be held down."
entries.literal: Governor of Danyang Liu Tan often marveled at Wen's talent, yet knew he harbored unruly ambitions; he told the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu: "Wen must not be placed in a strategically decisive region; his rank and title should constantly be kept down."

entries.zh: 勸昱自鎮上流，以己為軍司，昱不聽；
entries.en: He urged Yu personally to guard the upper reaches, with Tan himself as army marshal; Yu would not listen;
entries.literal: He urged Yu personally to guard the upper reaches, with Tan himself as army marshal; Yu would not listen;

entries.zh: 又請自行，亦不聽。
entries.en: He asked again to go himself—again Yu would not listen.
entries.literal: he asked again to go himself—again Yu would not listen.

entries.zh: 二月，癸丑，以左光祿大夫蔡謨領司徒，與會稽王昱同輔政。
entries.en: In the second month, on guichou, Left Household Grandee Cai Mo was made acting Minister of Education, to assist government jointly with the Prince of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Second month, on guichou, Left Household Grandee Cai Mo was made acting Minister of Education, jointly assisting government with the Prince of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 褚裒薦前光祿大夫顧和、前司徒左長史殷浩；
entries.en: Chu Pou recommended former Household Grandee Gu He and former left chief clerk of the Minister of Education Yin Hao;
entries.literal: Chu Pou recommended former Household Grandee Gu He and former Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Yin Hao;

entries.zh: 三月，丙子，以和為尚書令，浩為建武將軍、揚州刺史。
entries.en: In the third month, on bingzi, He was made Director of the Secretariat and Hao General of Establishing Martial Prowess and Governor of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Third month, on bingzi, He was made Director of the Secretariat and Hao made General of Establishing Martial Prowess and Governor of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 和有母喪，固辭不起，謂所親曰：「古人有釋衰絰從王者，以其才足干時故也。
entries.en: He was in mourning for his mother and firmly declined office; he told those close to him: "In antiquity some cast off mourning bands to follow kings because their talent sufficed to sustain the age.
entries.literal: He was in mourning for his mother and firmly declined to take office; he told those close to him: "In antiquity some cast off mourning bands to follow kings because their talent sufficed to sustain the age.

entries.zh: 如和者，正足以虧孝道、傷風俗耳。」
entries.en: One like me would only impair filial duty and harm custom."
entries.literal: One like He would only enough to impair filial duty and harm custom."

entries.zh: 識者美之。
entries.en: Those of insight praised him.
entries.literal: Those of insight praised him.

entries.zh: 浩亦固辭。
entries.en: Hao also firmly declined.
entries.literal: Hao also firmly declined.

entries.zh: 會稽王昱與浩書曰：「屬當厄運，危弊理極，足下沈識淹長，足以經濟。
entries.en: The Prince of Kuaiji wrote to Hao: "We face ill fortune; peril and decay have reached their limit. Your profound knowledge and long experience are enough to sustain the state.
entries.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, wrote to Hao: "We face ill fortune; peril and decay have reached their limit. You have profound knowledge and long experience, enough to sustain the state.

entries.zh: 若復深存挹退，苟遂本懷，吾恐天下之事於此去矣。
entries.en: If you again deeply preserve modest withdrawal and simply follow your original wish, I fear the realm's affairs will slip away at this very moment.
entries.literal: If you again deeply preserve modest withdrawal and simply follow your original wish, I fear the affairs of the realm at this point will pass away.

entries.zh: 足下去就，即時之廢興，則家國不異，足下宜深思之。」
entries.en: Your going or staying at this moment is the rise or fall of the age; family and state are one—you should ponder this deeply."
entries.literal: Your going or staying at this moment is the rise or fall of the age; then family and state are not different—you should ponder this deeply."

entries.zh: 浩乃就職。
entries.en: Hao then took office.
entries.literal: Hao then took office.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第097卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.
entries.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.

entries.zh: 義康僚屬及諸附麗湛者，潛相約勒，無敢歷殷氏之門。
entries.en: Yikang's staff and all who clung to Zhan secretly agreed among themselves that none would dare pass through the Yin family's gate.
entries.literal: Yikang's staff and all who clung to Zhan secretly agreed among themselves that none would dare pass through the Yin family's gate.

entries.zh: 彭城王主簿沛郡劉敬文父成，未悟其機，詣景仁求郡。
entries.en: Liu Jingwen of Pei, chief clerk to Prince Pengcheng—his father Liu Cheng, not grasping the situation, went to Jingren to request a prefecture.
entries.literal: Liu Jingwen of Pei, chief clerk to the Prince of Pengcheng—his father Liu Cheng, not grasping the situation, went to Jingren to request a prefecture.

entries.zh: 敬文遽往謝湛曰：「老父悖耄，遂就殷鐵干祿。
entries.en: Jingwen hastened to apologize to Zhan, saying, "My old father, in his senile folly, went to Yin Tie to seek an office.
entries.literal: Jingwen hastened to go apologize to Zhan, saying: "My old father, in his senile folly, went to Yin Tie to seek an office.

entries.zh: 由敬文暗淺，上負生成，闔門慚懼，無地自處。」
entries.en: Through my own blindness and shallowness, I have failed the parents who gave me life; our whole household is ashamed and fearful, with nowhere to hide our faces."
entries.literal: Through Jingwen's own blindness and shallowness, I have failed my parents who gave me life; our whole household is ashamed and fearful, with nowhere to hide our faces."

entries.zh: 唯後將軍司馬庾炳之遊二人之間，皆得其歡心，而密輸忠於朝廷。
entries.en: Only the major of the rear general Yu Bingzhi moved between the two men's circles, winning the goodwill of both while secretly reporting loyally to the court.
entries.literal: Only the major of the rear general Yu Bingzhi moved between the two men's circles, winning the goodwill of both while secretly reporting loyally to the court.

entries.zh: 景仁臥家不朝謁，帝常使炳之銜命往來，湛不疑也。
entries.en: Jingren lay ill at home and did not attend court. The Emperor often sent Bingzhi back and forth bearing orders, and Zhan suspected nothing.
entries.literal: Jingren lay ill at home and did not attend court; the Emperor often sent Bingzhi back and forth bearing orders, and Zhan suspected nothing.

entries.zh: 炳之，登之之弟也。
entries.en: Bingzhi was a younger brother of Dengzhi.
entries.literal: Bingzhi was a younger brother of Dengzhi.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第122卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 122.
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 122.

entries.zh: 寧朔將軍何邁，瑀之子也，尚帝姑新蔡長公主。
entries.en: He Mai, General Who Pacifies the North, was the son of He Yu and had married the emperor's paternal aunt, the Princess of Xincai.
entries.literal: He Mai, General Who Pacifies the North, was the son of Yu and had married the emperor's paternal aunt, the Princess of Xincai.

entries.zh: 帝納公主於後宮，謂之謝貴嬪；
entries.en: The emperor took the princess into the rear palace and called her Honored Consort Xie;
entries.literal: The emperor took the princess into the rear palace and called her Honored Consort Xie;

entries.zh: 詐言公主薨，殺宮婢，送邁等殯葬，行喪禮。
entries.en: he falsely announced that the princess had died, killed a palace maid, and sent Mai and others to conduct the funeral and perform mourning rites.
entries.literal: he falsely announced that the princess had died, killed a palace maid, and sent Mai and others to conduct the funeral and perform mourning rites.

entries.zh: 庚辰，拜貴嬪為夫人。
entries.en: On gengchen, the Honored Consort was invested as Lady.
entries.literal: On gengchen, the Honored Consort was invested as Lady.

entries.zh: 加鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕。
entries.en: She was given the imperial carriage with dragon banners and escorts clearing the road on her exits and entries.
entries.literal: She was given the imperial carriage with dragon banners and escorts clearing the road on her exits and entries.

entries.zh: 邁素豪俠，多養死士。
entries.en: Mai had always been bold and chivalrous and kept many men willing to die for him.
entries.literal: Mai had always been bold and chivalrous and kept many men willing to die for him.

entries.zh: 謀因帝出遊，廢之，立晉安王子勳。
entries.en: He plotted that when the emperor went out on excursion, they would depose him and set up Prince of Jin'an Zixun.
entries.literal: He plotted that when the emperor went out on excursion, they would depose him and set up the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun.

entries.zh: 事洩，十一月，壬辰，帝自將兵誅邁。
entries.en: The affair leaked out. In the eleventh month, on renchen, the emperor himself led troops to execute Mai.
entries.literal: The affair leaked out. In the eleventh month, on renchen, the emperor himself led troops to execute Mai.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第130卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 130
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 130

entries.zh: 丁卯，吳喜至錢唐，孔璪、王曇生奔浙東。
entries.en: On dingmao, Wu Xi reached Qiantang; Kong Zuan and Wang Tansheng fled into eastern Zhe.
entries.literal: On dingmao, Wu Xi reached Qiantang; Kong Zuan and Wang Tansheng fled to eastern Zhe.

entries.zh: 喜遣強弩將軍任農夫等引兵向黃山浦；
entries.en: Xi sent Strong Crossbow general Ren Nongfu and others toward Huangshan Ford;
entries.literal: Xi sent Strong Crossbow General Ren Nongfu and others to lead troops toward Huangshan Ford;

entries.zh: 東軍據岸結寨，農夫等擊破之。
entries.en: the eastern army held the bank and built stockades; Nongfu and his men attacked and broke them.
entries.literal: the eastern army held the bank and built stockades; Nongfu and the others attacked and broke them.

entries.zh: 喜自柳浦渡，取西陵，擊斬庚業。
entries.en: Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.
entries.literal: Xi crossed from Liupu, took Xiling, and attacked and beheaded Geng Ye.

entries.zh: 會稽人大懼，將士多奔亡，孔凱不能制。
entries.en: The people of Kuaiji were terrified; officers and soldiers fled in droves; Kong Kai could not control them.
entries.literal: The people of Kuaiji were greatly afraid; officers and soldiers mostly fled; Kong Kai could not control them.

entries.zh: 戊寅，上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，凱逃奔脊山；
entries.en: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the commandery; Kong Kai fled to Jishan;
entries.literal: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops to attack the commandery; Kai fled to Jishan;

entries.zh: 車騎從事中郎張綏封府庫以待吳喜。
entries.en: Chief clerk to the general of chariots and cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.
entries.literal: Chief Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.

entries.zh: 己卯，王晏入城，殺綏，執尋陽王子房於別署。
entries.en: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Zhang Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang at a separate residence.
entries.literal: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Zifang at a separate residence.

entries.zh: 縱兵大掠，府庫皆空；
entries.en: He let his troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;
entries.literal: He let the troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;

entries.zh: 獲孔璪，殺之。
entries.en: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.
entries.literal: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.

entries.zh: 庚辰，脊山民縛孔凱送晏，晏謂之曰：「此事孔璪所為，無預卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」
entries.en: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Wang Yan; Yan said to him: "This was Kong Zuan's doing and does not involve you; draft a confession and I will present it for you at court."
entries.literal: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This affair was Kong Zuan's doing; it does not involve you; you may compose a memorial of confession and I shall present it on your behalf to the throne."

entries.zh: 凱曰：「江東處分，莫不由身；
entries.en: Kong Kai said: "Every decision in the Jiangdong region was mine alone;
entries.literal: Kai said: "Every disposition in Jiangdong was none other than my own;

entries.zh: 委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」
entries.en: to shift blame to save my skin—that is exactly your sort's way."
entries.literal: to shift blame to seek life—that is precisely your sort's intent."

entries.zh: 晏乃斬之。
entries.en: Yan then beheaded him.
entries.literal: Yan then beheaded him.

entries.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等詣吳喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。
entries.en: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender; Xi pardoned them all.
entries.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender blame; Xi pardoned them all.

entries.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陳斬十七人，其餘皆原宥。
entries.en: Of seventy-six eastern army commanders in all, seventeen were beheaded in battle; the rest were all pardoned.
entries.literal: Eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded in the array; the rest were all pardoned.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第131卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 131
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 131

entries.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，以後將軍柳世隆為尚書右僕射；
entries.en: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Rear General Liu Shilong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Rear General Liu Shilong was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良為護軍將軍兼司徒，領兵置佐，鎮西州。
entries.en: Prince Jingling Xiao Ziliang was made Protector-General of the Army and concurrently Minister over the Masses; he took on military aides and garrisoned West Province.
entries.literal: Prince Jingling of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, was made Protector-General of the Army and concurrently Minister over the Masses, with military staff appointed, garrisoning West Province.

entries.zh: 子良少有清尚，傾意賓客，才俊之士，皆游集其門。
entries.en: From youth Ziliang had refined tastes and lavished attention on his guests; talented men of every sort flocked to his house.
entries.literal: Ziliang from youth had pure and lofty tastes, devoted himself to guests, and men of talent all gathered at his gate.

entries.zh: 開西邸，多聚古人器服以充之。
entries.en: He opened the Western Lodge and filled it with antiquities—vessels and vestments from former ages.
entries.literal: He opened the Western Lodge and gathered many ancient vessels and vestments to fill it.

entries.zh: 記室參軍范雲、蕭琛、樂安任昉、法曹參軍王融、衛軍東閣祭酒蕭衍、鎮西功曹謝朓、步兵校尉沈約、揚州秀才吳郡陸倕，並以文學，尤見親待，號曰八友。
entries.en: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Ren Fang of Le'an, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer Xiao Yan, West Garrison merit officer Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and presented scholar Lu Chun of Wu—all celebrated for literature and especially cherished—were known as the Eight Friends.
entries.literal: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Le'an Ren Fang, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer of the Guards Army Xiao Yan, Merit Officer of the West Garrison Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and Yangzhou Presented Scholar Lu Chun of Wu Commandery—all famed for letters and especially favored—were called the Eight Friends.

entries.zh: 法曹參軍柳惲、太學博士王僧孺、南徐州秀才濟陽江革、尚書殿中郎范縝、會稽孔休源亦預焉。
entries.en: Liu Yun, Wang Sengru, Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji were among them as well.
entries.literal: Legal Affairs Officer Liu Yun, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Sengru, South Xuzhou Presented Scholar Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji also took part.

entries.zh: 琛，惠開之從子；
entries.en: Chen was a nephew of Hui Kai;
entries.literal: Chen was the son of a younger brother of Hui Kai;

entries.zh: 惲，元景之從孫；
entries.en: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;
entries.literal: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;

entries.zh: 融，僧達之孫；
entries.en: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;
entries.literal: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;

entries.zh: 衍，順之之子；
entries.en: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;
entries.literal: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;

entries.zh: 朓，述之孫；
entries.en: Tiao was a grandson of Shu;
entries.literal: Tiao was a grandson of Shu;

entries.zh: 約，璞之子；
entries.en: Yue was a son of Pu;
entries.literal: Yue was a son of Pu;

entries.zh: 僧孺，雅之曾孫；
entries.en: Sengru was a great-grandson of Yazhi;
entries.literal: Sengru was a great-grandson of Yazhi;

entries.zh: 縝，雲之從兄也。
entries.en: Zhen was Yun's elder cousin.
entries.literal: Zhen was Yun's elder cousin.

entries.zh: 范縝盛稱無佛。
entries.en: Fan Zhen loudly maintained that there is no Buddha.
entries.literal: Fan Zhen loudly proclaimed that there is no Buddha.

entries.zh: 子良曰：「君不信因果，何得有富貴、貧賤？」
entries.en: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in karma, how can there be rich and poor?"
entries.literal: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how can there be wealth and honor, poverty and low estate?"

entries.zh: 縝曰：「人生如樹花同發，隨風而散：或拂簾幌墜茵席之上，或關籬牆落糞溷之中。
entries.en: Zhen replied, "Human life is like flowers on a tree blooming at once and scattering in the wind—some brush the curtain and land on cushions, others hit the fence and fall into the dung pit.
entries.literal: Zhen said, "Human life is like blossoms on a tree blooming together and scattering with the wind: some brush the curtain and fall on cushions and mats, some strike the fence and fall into the privy.

entries.zh: 墜茵席者，殿下是也；
entries.en: Those who land on cushions—that is you, my lord;
entries.literal: Those who fall on cushions and mats—that is Your Highness;

entries.zh: 落糞溷者，下官是也。
entries.en: those who fall into the dung pit—that is this humble official.
entries.literal: those who fall into the privy—that is this humble official.

entries.zh: 貴賤雖復殊途，因果竟在何處！」
entries.en: Noble and base may take different paths—where then is karma!"
entries.literal: Noble and base may take different paths, but where after all is cause and effect!"

entries.zh: 子良無以難。
entries.en: Ziliang had no answer.
entries.literal: Ziliang had nothing with which to refute him.

entries.zh: 縝又著《神滅論》，以為：「形者神之質，神者形之用也。
entries.en: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," arguing that "the body is the substance of the spirit, and the spirit is the function of the body.
entries.literal: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," holding that "the body is the substance of the spirit; the spirit is the function of the body.

entries.zh: 神之於形，猶利之於刀；
entries.en: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness to a blade;
entries.literal: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness in relation to a knife;

entries.zh: 未聞刀沒而利存，豈容形亡而神在哉！」
entries.en: no one has heard of the blade vanishing while sharpness remains—how then could the body perish while the spirit endures!"
entries.literal: one has never heard of the knife perishing while sharpness remains—how could the body perish while the spirit endures!"

entries.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩，難之，終不能屈。
entries.en: When the treatise appeared, court and country were in an uproar; critics assailed it, but none could refute him in the end.
entries.literal: When this treatise appeared, court and countryside clamored; many challenged it, but in the end none could overcome him.

entries.zh: 太原王琰著論譏縝曰：「嗚呼范子！
entries.en: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise mocking Zhen: "Alas, Master Fan!
entries.literal: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise to mock Zhen, saying, "Alas, Master Fan!

entries.zh: 曾不知其先祖神靈所在！」
entries.en: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"
entries.literal: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"

entries.zh: 欲以杜縝後對。
entries.en: He meant to silence any reply from Zhen.
entries.literal: He wished thereby to block Zhen from replying.

entries.zh: 縝對曰：「嗚呼王子！
entries.en: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!
entries.literal: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!

entries.zh: 知其先祖神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之！」
entries.en: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide, yet you cannot kill yourself to join them!"
entries.literal: You know where the spirits of your ancestors abide, yet cannot kill yourself to follow them!"

entries.zh: 子良使王融謂之曰：「以卿才美，何患不至中書郎；
entries.en: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent, why should you fail to reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;
entries.literal: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent and beauty, why worry that you will not reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;

entries.zh: 而故乖剌為此論，甚可惜也！
entries.en: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how regrettable!
entries.literal: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how very regrettable!

entries.zh: 宜急毀棄之。」
entries.en: You should destroy it at once."
entries.literal: You should hurry to destroy and abandon it."

entries.zh: 縝大笑曰：「使范縝賣論取官，已至令、僕矣，何但中書郎邪！」
entries.en: Zhen laughed and said, "If Fan Zhen sold his thesis for office, he would already be Minister or Vice Minister—why settle for mere Director of the Palace Secretariat!"
entries.literal: Zhen laughed loudly and said, "If Fan Zhen were to sell his thesis for office, he would already have reached Minister and Vice Minister—why only Director of the Palace Secretariat!"

entries.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明二年（
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 2 (
entries.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 2 (

entries.zh: 甲子，公元四八四年）
entries.en: jiazi, corresponding to 484 CE)
entries.literal: jiazi, the year 484 CE)

entries.zh: 初，上為鎮西長史，主簿王晏以傾諂為上所親，自是常在上府。
entries.en: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won his favor through sycophantic flattery and thereafter remained constantly at his headquarters.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Chief Clerk of the Army of the West, Registrar Wang Yan won the emperor's favor through fawning flattery; from then on he was constantly at the prince's headquarters.

entries.zh: 上為太子，晏為中庶子。
entries.en: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan was made Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When the emperor became heir apparent, Yan became Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 上之得罪於太祖也，晏稱疾自疏。
entries.en: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan feigned illness and distanced himself.
entries.literal: When the emperor fell from favor with the Founding Emperor, Yan pleaded illness and kept his distance.

entries.zh: 及即位，為丹陽尹，意任如舊，朝夕進見，議論朝事；
entries.en: After the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor trusted him as before and received him morning and evening to discuss affairs of state;
entries.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Yan was made Governor of Danyang; the emperor's trust in him was as before, and he was received morning and evening to discuss court affairs;

entries.zh: 自豫章王嶷及王儉皆降意接之。
entries.en: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all showed deference in receiving him.
entries.literal: From Prince Liao of Yuzhang down to Wang Jian, all lowered themselves to receive him graciously.

entries.zh: 二月，壬寅，出為江州刺史；
entries.en: In the second month, on renyin, he was appointed Inspector of Jiang Province;
entries.literal: In the second month, on renyin, he was sent out as Inspector of Jiang Province;

entries.zh: 晏不願外出，復留為吏部尚書。
entries.en: Yan did not wish to leave the capital and was kept on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: Yan did not wish to go out on assignment and was again retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 三月，甲寅，立皇子子岳為臨賀王，子峻為廣漢王，子琳為宣城王，子鈱為義安王。
entries.en: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.
entries.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, the emperor enfeoffed his sons Ziyue as Prince of Linhe, Zijun as Prince of Guanghan, Zilin as Prince of Xuancheng, and Zimin as Prince of Yi'an.

entries.zh: 五月，乙巳，儉卒。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on yisi, Wang Jian died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, Jian died.

entries.zh: 王晏既領選，權行台閣，與儉頗不平。
entries.en: Wang Yan, now in charge of personnel selection, exercised the powers of the Secretariat and was on bad terms with Jian.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, having taken charge of selection, wielded the authority of the Secretariat and was on rather poor terms with Jian.

entries.zh: 禮官欲依王導，謚儉為文獻。
entries.en: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and posthumously name Jian Literary Paragon.
entries.literal: The ritual officials wished to follow the precedent of Wang Dao and give Jian the posthumous title Literary Paragon.

entries.zh: 晏啟上曰：「導乃得此謚；
entries.en: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Wang Dao deserved that posthumous title;
entries.literal: Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Only Dao deserved this posthumous title;

entries.zh: 但宋氏以來，不加異姓。」
entries.en: since the Song, such titles have not been granted to men of a different surname;"
entries.literal: since the Song dynasty, such titles have not been granted to those of a different surname;"

entries.zh: 出，謂親人曰：「『平頭憲』事已行矣。」
entries.en: After leaving, he told his intimates, "The affair of the 'Flat-Xian' title is already settled."
entries.literal: After leaving, he told his intimates, "The affair of the 'truncated Xian' has already been settled."

entries.zh: 上欲用領軍王奐為尚書令，以問王晏。
entries.en: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Wang Yan.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Commandant of the Guards Wang Huan as Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Wang Yan about it.

entries.zh: 晏與奐不相能，對曰：「柳世隆有勳望，恐不宜在奐後。」
entries.en: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has both merit and prestige; it would hardly be fitting to rank him below Huan."
entries.literal: Yan was on bad terms with Huan and replied, "Liu Shilong has merit and prestige; I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."

entries.zh: 甲子，以尚書左僕射柳世隆為尚書令，王奐為左僕射。
entries.en: On jiazi, Left Vice Director Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: On jiazi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shilong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明七年（
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 7 (
entries.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 7 (

entries.zh: 己巳，公元四八九年）
entries.en: jisi, corresponding to 489 CE)
entries.literal: jisi, the year 489 CE)

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第136卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 136
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Government, Volume 136

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第138卷 卷第一百三十八 。
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 138.
entries.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 138, Volume 138.

entries.zh: 【齊紀四】 昭陽作噩，一年。。
entries.en: [Qi Annals 4] The year Zhaoyang Zuoe—one year in all.
entries.literal: [Qi Annals 4] Zhaoyang Zuoe; one year.

entries.zh: 世祖武皇帝下永明十一年（癸酉，公元四九三年） 。
entries.en: Yongming year 11 of Emperor Wu of Qi (Guiyou, 493 CE).
entries.literal: Under the Shizu, Emperor Wu, Yongming year 11 (Guiyou, 493 CE).

entries.zh: 春，正月，以驃騎大將軍王敬則為司空，鎮軍大將軍陳顯達為江州刺史。
entries.en: In spring, the first month, Emperor Wu appointed Grand Cavalry General Wang Jingze Minister of Works and General Who Pacifies the Army Chen Xianda governor of Jiang Province.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, Grand Cavalry General Wang Jingze was made Minister of Works; General Who Pacifies the Army Chen Xianda was made Governor of Jiang Province.

entries.zh: 顯達自以門寒位重，每遷官，常有愧懼之色，戒其子勿以富貴陵人；
entries.en: Chen Xianda felt keenly that he had risen far from humble origins; each promotion brought him shame and anxiety, and he warned his sons never to flaunt wealth or rank over others;
entries.literal: Xianda, considering his humble birth and heavy rank, whenever he was promoted often showed a look of shame and fear, and admonished his sons not to lord wealth and rank over others;

entries.zh: 而諸子多事豪侈，顯達聞之，不悅。
entries.en: His sons, however, mostly lived lavishly; when Xianda learned of it, he was unhappy.
entries.literal: But his sons mostly indulged in luxury; when Xianda heard of it, he was displeased.

entries.zh: 子休尚為郢府主簿，過九江。
entries.en: His son Chen Xiushang, serving as chief clerk on the staff at Ying, traveled through Jiujiang.
entries.literal: His son Xiushang served as chief clerk of the Ying prefecture staff and passed through Jiujiang.

entries.zh: 顯達曰：「麈尾蠅拂是王、謝家物，汝不須捉此！」
entries.en: Xianda said, "Deer's-tail and fly-whisk fans belong to the great clans Wang and Xie—you have no business handling such things!"
entries.literal: Xianda said: "Deer's-tail and fly-whisk fans are objects of the Wang and Xie families—you need not hold these!"

entries.zh: 即取於前燒之。。
entries.en: He snatched them from his son's hands and burned them on the spot.
entries.literal: He immediately took them before him and burned them.

entries.zh: 初，上於石頭造露車三千乘，欲步道取彭城。
entries.en: Earlier the emperor had had three thousand uncovered wagons built at Shitou, planning to take Pengcheng on foot.
entries.literal: Initially, the emperor had constructed three thousand open wagons at Shitou, intending to march on foot and take Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 魏人知之，劉昶數泣訴於魏主，乞處邊戍，招集遺民，以雪私恥。
entries.en: When the Northern Wei learned of this, Liu Chang pleaded tearfully before the Wei emperor to serve on the frontier, rally dispersed loyalists, and redeem his disgrace.
entries.literal: When the Wei learned of it, Liu Chang wept repeatedly before the Wei emperor, begging to be posted on the frontier, to gather scattered populations, and to wipe away his private shame.

entries.zh: 魏主大會公卿於經武殿，以議南伐，於淮、泗間大積馬芻。
entries.en: The Wei emperor convened dukes and officials in the Hall of Military Classics to debate invading south, while stockpiling fodder on a vast scale between the Huai and Si.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor convened the nobles and officials at the Jingwu Hall to discuss a southern campaign, and amassed great stores of fodder along the Huai and Si rivers.

entries.zh: 上聞之，以右衛將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史以備之。。
entries.en: Emperor Wu heard of this and appointed Right Guards General Cui Huijing governor of Yu Province to prepare defenses.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he appointed Right Guards General Cui Huijing Governor of Yu Province to guard against it.

entries.zh: 魏遣員外散騎侍郎邢巒等來聘。
entries.en: Northern Wei sent Xing Luan, an extraordinary attendant, and others as envoys.
entries.literal: Wei sent Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary Xing Luan and others on a diplomatic mission.

entries.zh: 巒，穎之孫也。。
entries.en: Xing Luan was a grandson of Xing Ying.
entries.literal: Luan was the grandson of Xing Ying.

entries.zh: 丙子，文惠太子長懋卒。
entries.en: On the day bingzi, Crown Prince Changmao died.
entries.literal: On bingzi, Crown Prince Wenhui Changmao died.

entries.zh: 太子風韻甚和，上晚年好游宴，尚書曹事分送太子省之，由是威加內外。。
entries.en: The crown prince was gentle and even-tempered; as the emperor in his later years grew fond of feasting and travel, memorials from the secretariat were routed to the crown prince for review, and his authority reached throughout the court.
entries.literal: The crown prince's bearing was very harmonious; in the emperor's later years he delighted in banquets and excursions, and matters of the Masters of Writing were forwarded to the crown prince for review, whereby his authority extended inside and outside.

entries.zh: 太子性奢靡，治堂殿、園囿過於上宮，費以千萬計，恐上望見之，乃傍門列修竹；
entries.en: The crown prince was extravagant by nature; the halls and gardens he built outdid the imperial palace and cost tens of millions; lest the emperor glimpse them from afar, he lined the gates with tall bamboo;
entries.literal: The crown prince was by nature extravagant; the halls and gardens he built exceeded the upper palace, costing tens of millions; fearing the emperor might see them, he planted tall bamboo beside the gates;

entries.zh: 凡諸服玩，率多僭侈。
entries.en: Nearly everything he wore or collected smacked of presumptuous luxury.
entries.literal: Of all his garments and curios, most were presumptuously lavish.

entries.zh: 啟於東田起小苑，使東宮將吏更番築役，營城包巷，彌亙華遠。
entries.en: He laid out a private park on the Eastern Fields and set Eastern Palace officers to build in rotating shifts, walling off whole blocks until the complex sprawled in lavish grandeur.
entries.literal: He opened a small park on the Eastern Fields, set the Eastern Palace officers and clerks to rotate in construction duty, walled streets and lanes, and the splendor stretched far.

entries.zh: 上性雖嚴，多布耳目，太子所為，人莫敢以聞。
entries.en: Though the emperor was strict by nature, he had informants everywhere, and no one dared report the crown prince's doings.
entries.literal: Although the emperor's nature was strict, he placed many informants; no one dared report what the crown prince did.

entries.zh: 上嘗過太子東田，見其壯麗，大怒，收監作主帥；
entries.en: Once, passing the crown prince's Eastern Fields, the emperor saw how grand they were, flew into a rage, and had the supervising officers arrested;
entries.literal: The emperor once passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields, saw how grand they were, flew into a rage, and imprisoned the supervising commanders;

entries.zh: 太子皆藏之，由是大被誚責。。
entries.en: The crown prince concealed them all and was sharply rebuked for it.
entries.literal: The crown prince hid them all, and for this was severely rebuked.

entries.zh: 又使嬖人徐文景造輦及乘輿御物；
entries.en: He also had his favorite Xu Wenjing build imperial carriages and regalia;
entries.literal: He also had his favorite Xu Wenjing make imperial carriages and regalia;

entries.zh: 上嘗幸東宮，匆匆不暇藏輦，文景乃以佛像內輦中，故上不疑。
entries.en: When the emperor once visited the Eastern Palace, there was no time to hide the carriage; Wenjing stuffed a Buddha image inside it, and the emperor suspected nothing.
entries.literal: The emperor once visited the Eastern Palace; in the hurry there was no time to hide the carriage, so Wenjing placed a Buddha image inside it, and the emperor did not suspect.

entries.zh: 文景父陶仁謂文景曰：「我正當掃墓待喪耳！」
entries.en: Wenjing's father Tao Ren told him, "All I should do now is tend graves and wait for the funeral!"
entries.literal: Wenjing's father Tao Ren said to Wenjing: "I ought simply to sweep graves and await the mourning!"

entries.zh: 仍移家避之。
entries.en: He moved his household away to distance himself from his son.
entries.literal: He then moved his household to avoid him.

entries.zh: 後文景竟賜死，陶仁遂不哭。。
entries.en: When Wenjing was eventually ordered to die, Tao Ren did not weep.
entries.literal: Later Wenjing was indeed ordered to die; Tao Ren then did not weep.

entries.zh: 及太子卒，上履行東宮，見其服玩，大怒，敕有司隨事毀除。
entries.en: After the crown prince's death, the emperor toured the Eastern Palace, saw his lavish belongings, flew into a rage, and ordered officials to destroy them one by one.
entries.literal: When the crown prince died, the emperor walked through the Eastern Palace, saw his garments and curios, flew into a rage, and ordered the authorities to destroy them item by item.

entries.zh: 以竟陵王子良與太子善，而不啟聞，並責之。。
entries.en: Prince Ziliang of Jingling, who had been close to the crown prince yet had not reported his excesses, was rebuked as well.
entries.literal: Because Prince of Jingling Ziliang was on good terms with the crown prince yet had not reported it, he was rebuked as well.

entries.zh: 太子素惡西昌侯鸞，嘗謂子良曰：「我意中殊不喜此人，不解其故，當由其福薄故也。」
entries.en: The crown prince had long disliked Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang; he once told Ziliang, "I have always disliked that man and cannot say why—perhaps his fate is simply too slight."
entries.literal: The crown prince had long disliked Marquis of Xichang Luan; he once told Ziliang: "In my heart I especially dislike this man; I do not understand why—it must be because his fortune is thin."

entries.zh: 子良為之救解。
entries.en: Ziliang pleaded on Luan's behalf.
entries.literal: Ziliang spoke in his defense.

entries.zh: 及鸞得政，太子子孫無遺焉。。
entries.en: When Luan seized power, he left none of the crown prince's descendants alive.
entries.literal: When Luan seized power, none of the crown prince's descendants survived.

entries.zh: 二月，魏主始耕藉田於平城南。。
entries.en: In the second month, the Wei emperor plowed the sacred field for the first time south of Pingcheng.
entries.literal: In the second month, the Wei emperor for the first time plowed the sacred field south of Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 雍州刺史王奐惡寧蠻長史劉興祖，收繫獄，誣其構扇山蠻，欲為亂，敕送興祖下建康；
entries.en: Wang Huan, governor of Yong Province, hated Liu Xingzu, chief clerk for pacifying the barbarians; he jailed him on false charges of inciting mountain tribes to revolt and ordered him sent to Jiankang;
entries.literal: Governor of Yong Province Wang Huan hated Chief Clerk of Pacifying the Barbarians Liu Xingzu, imprisoned him, and falsely accused him of inciting the mountain barbarians to rebel; he ordered Xingzu sent down to Jiankang;

entries.zh: 奐於獄中殺之，詐雲自經。
entries.en: Huan killed him in prison and claimed he had hanged himself.
entries.literal: Huan killed him in prison and falsely claimed he had hanged himself.

entries.zh: 上大怒，遣中書舍人呂文顯、直閣將軍曹道剛將齋仗五百人收奐，敕鎮西司馬曹虎從江陵步道會襄陽。。
entries.en: The emperor was furious and sent Palace Attendant Lü Wenxian and Direct-Palace General Cao Daogang with five hundred armed guards to arrest Wang Huan, while ordering Pacifying-the-West chief of staff Cao Hu to march overland from Jiangling and rendezvous at Xiangyang.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent Palace Attendant Lü Wenxian and Direct-Palace General Cao Daogang with five hundred armed guards to arrest Huan, ordering Pacifying-the-West Chief of Staff Cao Hu to march overland from Jiangling and join at Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 奐子彪，素凶險，奐不能制。
entries.en: Huan's son Wang Biao was violent and reckless by nature, and Huan could not control him.
entries.literal: Huan's son Biao was by nature fierce and dangerous; Huan could not control him.

entries.zh: 長史殷睿，奐之婿也。
entries.en: Chief clerk Yin Rui was Huan's son-in-law.
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Yin Rui was Huan's son-in-law.

entries.zh: 謂奐曰：「曹、呂來，既不見真敕，恐為奸變，正宜錄取，馳啟聞耳。」
entries.en: He told Huan, "Cao and Lü are coming without a verifiable edict—we may be facing a coup. We should seize them and send an urgent report to the throne."
entries.literal: He said to Huan: "When Cao and Lü come, since we have not seen the true edict, we fear a treacherous turn; we ought to seize them and send a swift report."

entries.zh: 奐納之。
entries.en: Huan agreed.
entries.literal: Huan accepted this.

entries.zh: 彪輒發州兵千餘人，開庫配甲仗，出南堂，陳兵，閉門拒守。
entries.en: Biao at once mobilized over a thousand provincial troops, opened the armory to issue arms, deployed men in the Southern Hall, shut the gates, and prepared to resist.
entries.literal: Biao immediately mobilized more than a thousand provincial troops, opened the armory to issue armor and weapons, went out to the Southern Hall, arrayed troops, closed the gates, and resisted.

entries.zh: 奐門生鄭羽叩頭啟奐，乞出城迎台使，奐曰：「我不作賊，欲先遣啟自申；
entries.en: Huan's protégé Zheng Yu kowtowed and begged him to go out and welcome the imperial envoys; Huan said, "I am no rebel—I mean first to send a memorial explaining myself;
entries.literal: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and urged Huan to go out and welcome the imperial envoys; Huan said: "I am not making rebellion; I wish first to send a report to explain myself;

entries.zh: 正恐曹、呂輩小人相陵藉，故且閉門自守耳。」
entries.en: I only fear petty men like Cao and Lü will abuse us, so for now I am merely holding the gates closed."
entries.literal: I only fear that petty men like Cao and Lü will bully and insult us, so for now I close the gates and hold myself."

entries.zh: 彪遂出，與虎軍戰，兵敗，走歸。
entries.en: Biao then sallied out, fought Cao Hu's troops, was beaten, and fled back inside.
entries.literal: Biao then went out, fought Cao Hu's army, was defeated, and fled back.

entries.zh: 三月，乙亥，司馬黃瑤起、寧蠻長史河東裴叔業於城內起兵，攻奐，斬之，執彪及弟爽、弼、殷睿，皆伏誅。
entries.en: In the third month, on yihai, chief of staff Huang Yaoqi and pacifying-the-barbarians chief clerk Pei Shuye of Hedong mutinied inside the city, attacked Wang Huan, and killed him; they seized Biao, his brothers Shuang and Bi, and Yin Rui, and all were put to death.
entries.literal: In the third month, on yihai, Chief of Staff Huang Yaoqi and Chief Clerk of Pacifying the Barbarians Pei Shuye of Hedong rose in arms within the city, attacked Huan, beheaded him, seized Biao and his brothers Shuang, Bi, and Yin Rui, and all were executed.

entries.zh: 彪兄融、琛死於建康，琛弟秘書丞肅獨得脫，奔魏。。
entries.en: Biao's elder brothers Rong and Chen were killed at Jiankang; Chen's younger brother Su, a director in the secretariat, alone escaped and fled to Northern Wei.
entries.literal: Biao's elder brothers Rong and Chen died at Jiankang; Chen's younger brother, Secretariat Director Su, alone escaped and fled to Wei.

entries.zh: 夏，四月，甲午，立南郡王昭業為皇太孫，東宮文武悉改為太孫官屬，以太子妃琅邪王氏為皇太孫太妃，南郡王妃何氏為皇太孫妃。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince Zhaoye of Nan Commandery was named imperial grandson; Eastern Palace officials were retitled as imperial-grandson staff; the late crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, became grand consort to the imperial grandson; and Prince Zhaoye's consort, Lady He, became consort of the imperial grandson.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince of Nanjun Zhaoye was established as imperial grandson; all Eastern Palace civil and military offices were changed to imperial-grandson staff; the crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, was made grand consort to the imperial grandson; the Prince of Nanjun's consort, Lady He, was made consort of the imperial grandson.

entries.zh: 妃戢，之女也。。
entries.en: Lady He was a daughter of Ji.
entries.literal: The consort was the daughter of Ji.

entries.zh: 魏太尉丕等請建中宮，戊戌，立皇后馮氏。
entries.en: Northern Wei's Grand Commandant Yuan Pi and others petitioned to establish an empress; on wuxu, Lady Feng was made empress.
entries.literal: Wei Grand Commandant Pi and others requested establishing the central palace; on wuxu, Empress Feng was established.

entries.zh: 後，熙之女也。
entries.en: She was a daughter of Feng Xi.
entries.literal: The empress was the daughter of Xi.

entries.zh: 魏主以《白虎通》云：「王者不臣妻之父母」，下詔令太師上書不稱臣，入朝不拜；
entries.en: Citing the Baihu tong—"A king does not treat his wife's parents as subjects"—the Wei emperor decreed that Grand Preceptor Feng Xi need not style himself a subject in memorials or bow when entering court;
entries.literal: The Wei emperor, citing the Baihu tong: "A king does not treat his wife's parents as subjects," issued an edict that the Grand Preceptor in memorials should not call himself subject and in court should not bow;

entries.zh: 熙固辭。。
entries.en: Feng Xi firmly declined the privilege.
entries.literal: Xi firmly declined.

entries.zh: 光城蠻帥征虜將軍田益宗帥部落四千餘戶叛，降於魏。。
entries.en: Tian Yizong, a Guangcheng tribal chief holding the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians, led more than four thousand households in revolt and surrendered to Northern Wei.
entries.literal: Tian Yizong, barbarian chief of Guangcheng and General Who Punishes the Barbarians, led more than four thousand households of his tribe in rebellion and surrendered to Wei.

entries.zh: 五月，壬戌，魏主宴四廟子孫於宣文堂，親與之齒，用家人禮。。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on renxu, the Wei emperor entertained imperial clansmen from all four ancestral temples in the Hall of Promoting Culture, seating himself by their ages and treating them with family courtesy.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, the Wei emperor feasted the descendants of the four temples in the Xuwen Hall, personally matching their ages and using family ritual.

entries.zh: 甲子，魏主臨朝堂，引公卿以下決疑政，錄囚徒。
entries.en: On jiazi, the Wei emperor held court, called dukes and officials to settle doubtful matters of policy, and reviewed prisoners.
entries.literal: On jiazi, the Wei emperor attended the court hall, summoned the nobles and officials and below to decide doubtful policies, and reviewed prisoners.

entries.zh: 帝謂司空穆亮曰：「自今朝廷政事，日中以前，卿等先自論議；
entries.en: The emperor told Minister of Works Mu Liang, "From now on, on court business before noon you are to deliberate among yourselves first;
entries.literal: The emperor said to Minister of Works Mu Liang: "From now on, on court affairs, before noon you shall first deliberate among yourselves;

entries.zh: 日中以後，朕與卿等共決之。」。
entries.en: after noon I shall decide them together with you."
entries.literal: After noon, I together with you shall jointly decide them."

entries.zh: 丙子，以宜都王鏗為南豫州刺史。
entries.en: On bingzi, Prince Keng of Yidu was appointed governor of Southern Yu Province.
entries.literal: On bingzi, Prince of Yidu Keng was appointed Governor of Southern Yu Province.

entries.zh: 先是廬陵王子卿為南豫州刺史，之鎮，道中戲部伍為水軍；
entries.en: Earlier Prince Ziqing of Luling had been governor of Southern Yu Province; on the road to his post he playfully drilled his escort as a naval force;
entries.literal: Earlier Prince of Luling Ziqing had been Governor of Southern Yu Province; on the way to his post he playfully drilled his retinue as a naval force;

entries.zh: 上聞之，大怒，殺其典簽，以鏗代之。
entries.en: When the emperor heard of this, he flew into a rage, executed Ziqing's chief clerk, and replaced him with Keng.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was greatly angered, executed his chief clerk, and replaced him with Keng.

entries.zh: 子卿還第，上終身不與相見。
entries.en: Ziqing returned home; the emperor never saw him again for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: Ziqing returned to his residence; the emperor never met with him again for the rest of his life.

entries.zh: 襄陽蠻首雷婆思等帥戶千餘求內徙於魏，魏人處之沔北。。
entries.en: Lei Posi and other Xiangyang tribal chiefs led more than a thousand households seeking resettlement within Wei territory; the Wei placed them north of the Han.
entries.literal: Lei Posi and other Xiangyang barbarian chiefs led more than a thousand households seeking inward migration to Wei; the Wei settled them north of the Mian.

entries.zh: 魏主以平城地寒，六月雨雪，風沙常起，將遷都洛陽；
entries.en: The Wei emperor found Pingcheng too cold—rain and snow even in the sixth month, wind and sand constant—and planned to move the capital to Luoyang;
entries.literal: The Wei emperor, considering Pingcheng's land cold, with rain and snow in the sixth month and wind and sand constantly rising, intended to move the capital to Luoyang;

entries.zh: 恐群臣不從，乃議大舉伐齊，欲以脅眾。
entries.en: fearing his ministers would resist, he proposed a major campaign against Qi to bring them into line.
entries.literal: fearing the nobles and officials would not follow, he then discussed a great campaign against Qi, intending to coerce the multitude.

entries.zh: 齋於明堂左個，使太常卿王諶筮之，遇「革」，帝曰：「『湯、武革命，順乎天而應乎人。』
entries.en: He fasted in the left bay of the Bright Hall and had Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen cast the oracle, which yielded the hexagram Revolution; the emperor said, "'Tang and Wu carried out revolution, accordant with Heaven and responsive to the people.
entries.literal: He fasted in the left bay of the Bright Hall, had Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen divine, and obtained "Revolution"; the emperor said: "'Tang and Wu carried out revolution, accordant with Heaven and responsive to men.

entries.zh: 吉孰大焉！」
entries.en: What omen could be more auspicious!'"
entries.literal: What auspice could be greater!"

entries.zh: 群臣莫敢言。
entries.en: None of the assembled ministers dared object.
entries.literal: None of the nobles and officials dared speak.

entries.zh: 尚書任城王澄曰：「陛下弈葉重光，帝有中土；
entries.en: Minister of the Masters of Writing Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, said, "Your Majesty's house has renewed its radiance generation after generation and already rules the central lands;
entries.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, said: "Your Majesty's line has renewed its radiance generation after generation and rules the central land;

entries.zh: 今出師以征未服，而得湯、武革命之象，未為全吉也。」
entries.en: to march out now against unsubdued foes yet draw the image of Tang and Wu's revolution is not wholly auspicious."
entries.literal: now to march out and campaign against those not yet submitted, yet obtain the image of Tang and Wu's revolution—is not wholly auspicious."

entries.zh: 帝厲聲曰：「繇云：『大人虎變』，何言不吉！」
entries.en: The emperor snapped, "The commentary says, 'The great man transforms like a tiger'—how can you call that inauspicious!"
entries.literal: The emperor said sharply: "The commentary says: 'The great man transforms like a tiger'—how can you say it is not auspicious!"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「陛下龍興已久，何得今乃虎變！」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's dragon rise was long ago—how can you be transforming like a tiger only now!"
entries.literal: Cheng said: "Your Majesty's dragon rise was long ago—how can you now be tiger-transforming!"

entries.zh: 帝作色曰：「社稷我之社稷，任城欲沮眾邪！」
entries.en: The emperor flushed and said, "The realm is mine—does Prince of Rencheng mean to discourage the army!"
entries.literal: The emperor changed color and said: "The altars of soil and grain are my altars of soil and grain—does Rencheng wish to discourage the multitude!"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「社稷雖為陛下之有，臣為社稷之臣，安可知危而不言！」
entries.en: Cheng said, "Though the realm belongs to Your Majesty, I am its subject—how can I see peril and stay silent!"
entries.literal: Cheng said: "Although the altars of soil and grain belong to Your Majesty, I am a subject of the altars of soil and grain—how can I know danger and not speak!"

entries.zh: 帝久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，夫亦何傷！」。
entries.en: After a long while the emperor relented. "Speak your minds," he said—"what harm is there in that?"
entries.literal: After a long while the emperor relented and said: "Each speak his mind—what harm is there!"

entries.zh: 既還宮，召澄入見，逆謂之曰：「向者《革卦》，今當更與卿論之。
entries.en: Back at the palace he summoned Cheng and, going out to meet him, said, "About the Revolution hexagram just now—I should discuss it further with you.
entries.literal: When he had returned to the palace, he summoned Cheng to an audience and, going to meet him, said: "As to the Revolution hexagram just now, I ought to discuss it further with you.

entries.zh: 明堂之忿，恐人人競言，沮我大計，故以聲色怖文武耳。
entries.en: My anger in the Bright Hall was feigned—I feared everyone would speak up and block my great plan, so I used harsh words to frighten the court, nothing more.
entries.literal: My anger in the Bright Hall—I feared everyone would compete in speech and discourage my great plan, so I used voice and countenance to frighten the civil and military officials, that is all.

entries.zh: 想識朕意。」
entries.en: I trust you understand my intent."
entries.literal: I trust you understand my intent."

entries.zh: 因屏人，謂澄曰：「今日之舉，誠為不易。
entries.en: He dismissed everyone else and told Cheng, "What I mean to do today is truly no small matter.
entries.literal: He then dismissed attendants and said to Cheng: "Today's undertaking is truly not easy.

entries.zh: 但國家興自朔土，徙居平城；
entries.en: Our state arose in the northern frontier and moved its seat to Pingcheng;
entries.literal: But the state rose from the northern lands and moved to dwell at Pingcheng;

entries.zh: 此乃用武之地，非可文治。
entries.en: that is a land for wielding arms, not for civil rule.
entries.literal: this is a land for wielding arms, not for civil governance.

entries.zh: 今將移風易俗，其道誠難，朕欲因此遷宅中原，卿以為何如？」
entries.en: Changing customs and habits is truly hard. I mean to seize this moment and move our capital to the Central Plains—what do you think?"
entries.literal: Now we are to change customs and transform habits—the path is truly difficult. I wish to take this opportunity to move our seat to the Central Plains. What do you think?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「陛下欲卜宅中土，以經略四海，此周、漢之所以興隆也。」
entries.en: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty means to establish the capital in the heartland and extend rule over the four seas—that is how Zhou and Han achieved their greatness."
entries.literal: Cheng said: "Your Majesty wishes to choose a seat in the Central Land and strategize over the four seas—this is how Zhou and Han rose to greatness."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「北人習常戀故，必將驚擾，奈何？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Northerners cling to custom and old homes—they will panic and resist. What can be done?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Northerners are accustomed to the old ways and attached to their homes—they will surely be alarmed and disturbed. What is to be done?"

entries.zh: 澄曰：「非常之事，故非常人之所及。
entries.en: Cheng said, "An extraordinary task lies beyond ordinary men.
entries.literal: Cheng said: "An extraordinary undertaking is therefore beyond ordinary men.

entries.zh: 陛下斷自聖心，彼亦何所能為！」
entries.en: Once Your Majesty decides from your own sage judgment, what can they do?"
entries.literal: If Your Majesty decides from your sage heart, what can they possibly do!"

entries.zh: 帝曰；
entries.en: The emperor said;
entries.literal: The emperor said;

entries.zh: 「任城，吾之子房也！」。
entries.en: "Rencheng, you are my Zhang Liang!"
entries.literal: "Rencheng—you are my Zifang!"

entries.zh: 六月，丙戌，命作河橋，欲以濟師。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the day bingxu, he ordered a bridge built over the river to move his army across.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on bingxu, he ordered a river bridge built to ferry troops across.

entries.zh: 秘書監盧淵上表，以為：「前世承平之主，未嘗親御六軍，決勝行陳之間；
entries.en: Secretary Supervisor Lu Yuan submitted a memorial arguing that "emperors of earlier peaceful ages never personally led the Six Armies or decided battles in the field;
entries.literal: Secretary Supervisor Lu Yuan submitted a memorial stating: "Emperors of past ages in times of peace never personally commanded the Six Armies or decided victory amid the battle lines;

entries.zh: 豈非勝之不足為武，不勝有虧威望乎！
entries.en: for victory would scarcely enhance martial glory, while defeat would tarnish imperial prestige.
entries.literal: is it not that victory would add little to martial renown, while defeat would damage imperial prestige?

entries.zh: 昔魏武以弊卒一萬破袁紹，謝玄以步兵三千摧苻秦，勝負之變，決於須臾，不在眾寡也。」
entries.en: In the past Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao with ten thousand exhausted troops, and Xie Xuan crushed the army of Former Qin with three thousand infantry—the outcome turns in a moment, not on numbers alone."
entries.literal: In former days Cao Cao broke Yuan Shao with ten thousand worn troops; Xie Xuan shattered Fu Qin's forces with three thousand foot soldiers—the turn of victory and defeat is decided in an instant, not by numbers."

entries.zh: 詔報曰：「承平之主，所以不親戎事者，或以同軌無敵，或以懦劣偷安。
entries.en: The imperial reply said, "Peaceful emperors stayed away from war either because the realm was united and they had no foe, or because they were timid and sought ease.
entries.literal: The edict replied: "Emperors in peaceful times did not personally take to arms either because all lands submitted and there were no enemies, or because they were weak and sought idle comfort.

entries.zh: 今謂之同軌則未然，比之懦劣則可恥，必若王者不當親戎，則先王制革輅，何所施也？
entries.en: Neither description fits us today—the first is not yet true, and the second would be shameful. If a true king should never take the field, why did the ancient kings establish the leather war chariot?
entries.literal: To call our case the former is not yet so; to compare us to the latter is shameful. If a true king ought not to take the field personally, then to what purpose did the former kings ordain the leather war chariot?

entries.zh: 魏武之勝，蓋由仗順，苻氏之敗，亦由失政；
entries.en: Cao Cao won because he had justice on his side, and the Fu clan fell because it lost the way of governance;
entries.literal: Cao Cao's victory was largely because he had righteousness on his side; the Fu clan's defeat was also due to misgovernment;

entries.zh: 豈寡必能勝眾，弱必能制強邪！」
entries.en: surely the few do not always defeat the many, nor the weak always master the strong!"
entries.literal: how could the few necessarily overcome the many, or the weak necessarily control the strong!"

entries.zh: 丁未，魏主講武，命尚書李沖典武選。。
entries.en: On the day dingwei the Wei emperor held a military review and put Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong in charge of selecting troops.
entries.literal: On dingwei the Wei sovereign held a military review and ordered Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong to oversee selection for martial service.

entries.zh: 建康僧法智與徐州民周盤龍等作亂，夜，攻徐州城，入之；
entries.en: The monk Fazhi of Jiankang and Zhou Panlong, a commoner of Xuzhou, and others rose in rebellion; by night they attacked Xuzhou city and took it;
entries.literal: The monk Fazhi of Jiankang and Zhou Panlong of Xuzhou and others rebelled; by night they attacked Xuzhou city and entered it;

entries.zh: 刺史王玄邈討誅之。。
entries.en: Governor Wang Xuanmiao put down the revolt and executed the ringleaders.
entries.literal: Governor Wang Xuanmiao suppressed and executed them.

entries.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，魏立皇子恂為太子。。
entries.en: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guichou, Wei enthroned Prince Xun as crown prince.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, Wei installed the prince Xun as crown prince.

entries.zh: 戊午，魏中外戒嚴，發露布及移書，稱當南伐。
entries.en: On the day wuwu Wei put the court and realm on alert, issued public proclamations and diplomatic letters, and announced a coming southern invasion.
entries.literal: On wuwu Wei declared martial law throughout court and realm, issued open proclamations and diplomatic letters announcing a southern campaign.

entries.zh: 詔發揚、徐州民丁，廣設召募以備之。。
entries.en: An edict mobilized laborers from Yang and Xu provinces and opened wide recruitment to prepare defenses.
entries.literal: An edict mobilized labor from Yang and Xu provinces and widely opened recruitment to prepare against it.

entries.zh: 中書郎王融，自恃人地，三十內望為公輔。
entries.en: Wang Rong, an attendant gentleman of the Secretariat, counted on his family and status and expected to reach the highest offices before he turned thirty.
entries.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Wang Rong, relying on his birth and standing, expected to reach the highest ministerial posts before thirty.

entries.zh: 嘗夜直省中，撫案歎曰：「為爾寂寂，鄧禹笑人！」
entries.en: Once, on night duty in the secretariat, he leaned on his desk and sighed, "To live so obscurely—Deng Yu would laugh at me!"
entries.literal: Once while on night duty in the secretariat, he leaned on his desk and sighed: "To end up so obscure—Deng Yu would laugh at me!"

entries.zh: 行逢朱雀桁開，喧湫不得進，捶車壁歎曰：「車前無八騶，何得稱丈夫！」
entries.en: On his way out he found the Vermilion Bird Bridge raised and the throng so thick he could not pass; he pounded the carriage wall and sighed, "No eight outriders before my carriage—how can I call myself a man!"
entries.literal: As he went out he met the Vermilion Bird Bridge raised and the crowd so dense he could not pass; he beat the carriage wall and sighed: "No eight outriders before my carriage—how can I call myself a true man!"

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良愛其文學，特親厚之。。
entries.en: Prince Ziliang of Jingling admired his literary gifts and treated him with exceptional warmth.
entries.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling admired his literary talent and treated him with special intimacy.

entries.zh: 融見上有北伐之志，數上書獎勸，因大習騎射。
entries.en: Seeing that the emperor wished to campaign north, Rong repeatedly submitted memorials urging him on and trained hard in horsemanship and archery.
entries.literal: Rong saw that the emperor had a mind to campaign north and repeatedly submitted memorials urging it on; he therefore trained intensively in horsemanship and archery.

entries.zh: 及魏將入寇，子良於東府募兵，版融寧朔將軍，使典其事。
entries.en: When Wei was about to invade, Ziliang raised troops at the Eastern Headquarters, commissioned Rong as General Who Calms the North, and put him in charge of recruitment.
entries.literal: When Wei was about to invade, Ziliang recruited troops at the Eastern Headquarters and appointed Rong General Who Calms the North, putting him in charge of the effort.

entries.zh: 融傾意招納，得江西傖楚數百人，並有干用。。
entries.en: Rong recruited with all his energy and gathered several hundred hardy men from Jiangxi, all of them capable and useful.
entries.literal: Rong recruited wholeheartedly and gathered several hundred Jiangxi migrants, all capable and useful.

entries.zh: 會上不豫，詔子良甲仗入延昌殿侍醫藥；
entries.en: Just then the emperor fell ill, and an edict permitted Ziliang to enter the Hall of Extended Splendor in armor to attend him and oversee his medicine;
entries.literal: Just then the emperor fell ill; an edict allowed Ziliang to enter the Hall of Extended Splendor armed to attend and administer medicine;

entries.zh: 子良以蕭衍、范雲等皆為帳內軍主。
entries.en: Ziliang made Xiao Yan, Fan Yun, and others commanders of the guard within his headquarters.
entries.literal: Ziliang appointed Xiao Yan, Fan Yun, and others as military commanders within his tent guard.

entries.zh: 戊辰，遣江州刺史陳顯達鎮樊城。
entries.en: On the day wuchen he sent Jiang Province Governor Chen Xianda to hold Fancheng.
entries.literal: On wuchen he sent Jiang Province Governor Chen Xianda to garrison Fancheng.

entries.zh: 上慮朝野憂遑，力疾召木府奏正聲伎。
entries.en: Fearing panic in court and country, the emperor forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox music.
entries.literal: The emperor, fearing anxiety in court and country, forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox pieces.

entries.zh: 子良日夜在內，太孫間日參承。。
entries.en: Ziliang remained inside day and night, while the crown prince came every other day to pay his respects.
entries.literal: Ziliang stayed within day and night; the crown prince visited at intervals to pay respects.

entries.zh: 戊寅，上疾亟，暫絕；
entries.en: On the day wuyin the emperor's illness turned grave and he briefly lost consciousness;
entries.literal: On wuyin the emperor's illness turned critical and he briefly lost consciousness;

entries.zh: 太孫未入，內外惶懼，百僚皆已變服。
entries.en: The crown prince had not yet arrived; court and palace were seized with fear, and all the officials had already changed into mourning dress.
entries.literal: The crown prince had not yet entered; inside and outside were filled with fear, and all officials had already changed into mourning dress.

entries.zh: 王融欲矯詔立子良，詔草已立。
entries.en: Wang Rong wanted to forge an edict enthroning Ziliang, and the draft was already written.
entries.literal: Wang Rong wished to forge an edict making Ziliang emperor; the draft was already prepared.

entries.zh: 蕭衍謂范雲曰：「道路籍籍，皆雲將有非常之舉。
entries.en: Xiao Yan said to Fan Yun, "The streets are full of rumor—everyone says something extraordinary is coming.
entries.literal: Xiao Yan said to Fan Yun: "The roads are buzzing—all say something extraordinary is about to happen.

entries.zh: 王元長非濟世才，視其敗也。」
entries.en: Wang Yuanzhang is no statesman—watch him fail."
entries.literal: Wang Yuanzhang is no talent to save the age—we shall see his ruin."

entries.zh: 雲曰：「憂國家者，唯有王中書耳。」
entries.en: Fan Yun said, "The only one who cares for the state is Secretary Wang."
entries.literal: Yun said: "The one who cares for the state is none but Secretary Wang."

entries.zh: 衍曰：「憂國，欲為周、召，欲為豎刁邪？」
entries.en: Xiao Yan said, "Caring for the state—is he trying to be the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, or Duke Huan's eunuch?"
entries.literal: Yan said: "Caring for the state—does he mean to be like the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, or like Duke Huan's eunuch?"

entries.zh: 雲不敢答。
entries.en: Fan Yun did not dare answer.
entries.literal: Yun did not dare reply.

entries.zh: 及太孫來，王融戎服絳衫，於中書省閣口斷東宮仗不得進。
entries.en: When the crown prince arrived, Wang Rong, dressed for battle in a scarlet shirt, blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate and would not let them pass.
entries.literal: When the crown prince arrived, Wang Rong in martial dress and a scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the gate of the Secretariat, barring them from entering.

entries.zh: 頃之，上復甦，問太孫所在，因召東宮器甲皆入，以朝事委尚書左僕射西昌侯鸞。
entries.en: Before long the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guard, weapons and all, and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.
entries.literal: Shortly after, the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guards with their weapons inside and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.

entries.zh: 俄而上殂，融處分以子良兵禁諸門。
entries.en: Soon the emperor died, and Rong used Ziliang's troops to seal every gate.
entries.literal: Soon the emperor died; Rong deployed Ziliang's troops to seal every gate.

entries.zh: 鸞聞之，急馳至雲龍門，不得進，鸞曰：「有敕召我！」
entries.en: When Luan heard this he galloped to the Cloud Dragon Gate but could not get through; he cried, "I have been summoned by imperial order!"
entries.literal: Luan heard and galloped to the Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter; Luan said: "There is an imperial order summoning me!"

entries.zh: 排之而入，奉太孫登殿，命左右扶出子良；
entries.en: He forced his way in, escorted the crown prince to the throne, and ordered attendants to lead Ziliang away;
entries.literal: He pushed through and entered, escorted the crown prince to the throne, and ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out;

entries.zh: 指麾部署，音響如鐘，殿中無不從命。
entries.en: His orders rang out like a bell, and everyone in the hall obeyed.
entries.literal: His commands rang out like a bell; everyone in the hall obeyed without exception.

entries.zh: 融知不遂，釋服還省，歎曰：「公誤我！」
entries.en: Rong saw that his plan had failed, changed out of martial dress, returned to the Secretariat, and sighed, "My lord, you have led me astray!"
entries.literal: Rong knew his plan had failed; he changed back from martial dress and returned to the Secretariat, sighing: "My lord—you have ruined me!"

entries.zh: 由是鬱林王深怨之。。
entries.en: From that time on Emperor Yulin deeply resented him.
entries.literal: From this Emperor Yulin deeply resented him.

entries.zh: 遺詔曰：「太孫進德日茂，社稷有寄。
entries.en: The testamentary edict said, "The crown prince's virtue grows daily, and the altars of state have one to rely on.
entries.literal: The testamentary edict said: "The crown prince's virtue grows daily; the altars of state have one to rely on.

entries.zh: 子良善相毘輔，思弘治道，內外眾事，無大小悉與鸞參懷，共下意！
entries.en: Ziliang is well suited to assist and support—let him strive to broaden good governance; on all matters within and without, great and small alike, consult with Luan and share your intentions!
entries.literal: Ziliang excels at assisting and supporting—let him strive to expand good governance; all affairs within and without, great and small alike, consult with Luan and share your intentions!

entries.zh: 尚書中事，職務根本，悉委右僕射王晏、吏部尚書徐孝嗣；
entries.en: Affairs of the Secretariat, the root of government, entrust wholly to Right Vice Minister Wang Yan and Minister of Civil Appointments Xu Xiaosi;
entries.literal: Affairs within the Secretariat, the root of office, entrust entirely to Right Vice Minister Wang Yan and Minister of Civil Appointments Xu Xiaosi;

entries.zh: 軍旅之略，委王敬則、陳顯達、王廣之、王玄邈、沈文季、張瑰、薛淵等。」。
entries.en: Military affairs entrust to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanyao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest."
entries.literal: Military strategy entrust to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanyao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest."

entries.zh: 世祖留心政事，務總大體，嚴明有斷，郡縣久於其職，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。
entries.en: Emperor Wu attended closely to governance, keeping to the broad essentials with strict and decisive judgment; prefectures and counties kept their officials in office for long terms, and when local leaders broke the law he had them executed on the spot.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu attended closely to governance, keeping to the broad essentials, strict and clear in judgment; prefectures and counties held their posts for long terms, and when chief officials broke the law he ordered immediate execution.

entries.zh: 故永明之世，百姓豐樂，賊盜屏息。
entries.en: Thus in the Yongming era the people were prosperous and content, and bandits and thieves disappeared.
entries.literal: Therefore in the Yongming era the people were prosperous and content, and bandits and thieves vanished.

entries.zh: 然頗好游宴，華靡之事，常言恨之，未能頓遣。。
entries.en: Yet he was rather fond of feasting and touring and of lavish display; he often said he regretted it but could not give it up all at once.
entries.literal: Yet he was rather fond of feasting and touring, and of luxuriant extravagance; he often spoke of regretting it but could not abandon it all at once.

entries.zh: 鬱林王之未立也，眾皆疑立子良，口語喧騰。
entries.en: Before Emperor Yulin was enthroned, everyone suspected that Ziliang would be made emperor, and rumors swirled.
entries.literal: Before Emperor Yulin was enthroned, everyone suspected Ziliang would be made emperor, and rumors ran wild.

entries.zh: 武陵王曄於眾中大言曰：「若立民，則應在我；
entries.en: Before the assembly Prince Ye of Wuling declared loudly, "If a lesser prince is to be enthroned, it should be me;
entries.literal: Prince of Wuling Ye declared loudly before the assembly: "If a lesser prince is to be enthroned, it ought to be me;

entries.zh: 立嫡，則應在太孫。」
entries.en: if the rightful heir is enthroned, it should be the crown prince."
entries.literal: if the legitimate heir is enthroned, it ought to be the crown prince."

entries.zh: 由是帝深憑賴之。
entries.en: From this the emperor came to rely on him deeply.
entries.literal: From this the emperor relied on him deeply.

entries.zh: 直閣周奉叔、曹道剛素為帝心膂，並使監殿中直衛；
entries.en: Chamber Attendants Zhou Fengshu and Cao Daogang had long been the emperor's trusted confidants; both were put in charge of the palace guard;
entries.literal: Chamberlain Attendant Zhou Fengshu and Cao Daogang had long been the emperor's trusted right hands; both were made to oversee the direct palace guard;

entries.zh: 少日，復以道剛為黃門郎。。
entries.en: A few days later Daogang was again made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: A few days later Daogang was again appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 初，西昌侯鸞為太祖所愛，鸞性儉素，車服儀從，同於素士，所居官名為嚴能，故世祖亦重之。
entries.en: Earlier Marquis Luan of Xichang had been favored by Emperor Gao; Luan was frugal and plain, his carriage, dress, and retinue no different from an ordinary scholar's, and in every office he held he was known for strict competence—so Emperor Wu also valued him.
entries.literal: Earlier, Marquis of Xichang Luan had been beloved by Emperor Gao; Luan was frugal and plain—carriages, robes, and retinue matched those of common scholars—and wherever he served his reputation was for strict capability; therefore Emperor Wu also valued him highly.

entries.zh: 世祖遺詔，使竟陵王子良輔政，鸞知尚書事。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's testamentary edict had Prince Ziliang of Jingling assist in governance and Luan oversee Secretariat affairs.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu's testamentary edict had Prince Ziliang of Jingling assist in governance and Luan oversee Secretariat affairs.

entries.zh: 子良素仁厚，不樂世務，乃更推鸞，故遺詔云「事無大小，悉與鸞參懷」，子良之志也。。
entries.en: Ziliang was naturally kind and generous and took no pleasure in worldly affairs, so he pushed authority toward Luan; hence the testament's words, "on all matters great and small alike consult with Luan," reflected Ziliang's own wish.
entries.literal: Ziliang was naturally kind and generous and took no joy in worldly affairs; he therefore pushed authority further toward Luan—hence the testamentary lines "all affairs great and small alike consult with Luan" reflected Ziliang's own wish.

entries.zh: 帝少養於子良妃袁氏，慈愛甚著。
entries.en: The emperor had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan, and their mutual affection was well known.
entries.literal: The emperor had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan, and their affection was well known.

entries.zh: 及王融有謀，遂深忌子良。
entries.en: After Wang Rong's plot, he came to deeply mistrust Ziliang.
entries.literal: After Wang Rong's plot, he came to deeply mistrust Ziliang.

entries.zh: 大行出太極殿，子良居中書省，帝使虎賁中郎將潘敞領二百人仗屯太極西階以防之。
entries.en: When the imperial coffin was borne out of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, Ziliang remained in the Secretariat; the emperor sent Captain of the Tiger Guard Pan Chang with two hundred armed men to hold the western steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and guard against him.
entries.literal: When the imperial coffin was borne out of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, Ziliang remained in the Secretariat; the emperor sent Captain of the Tiger Guard Pan Chang with two hundred armed men to station on the western steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to guard against him.

entries.zh: 既成服，諸王皆出，子良乞停至山陵，不許。。
entries.en: After the mourning period was complete, all the princes were to leave the capital; Ziliang asked to remain until the imperial tomb was finished, but permission was denied.
entries.literal: After mourning dress was completed, all princes were to leave the capital; Ziliang asked to stay until the imperial tomb was completed but was refused.

entries.zh: 壬午，稱遺詔，以武陵王曄為衛將軍，與征南大將軍陳顯達並開府儀同三司；
entries.en: On the day renwu, by testamentary edict Prince Ye of Wuling was made Defender-General and, together with General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda, granted an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies;
entries.literal: On renwu, by testamentary edict Prince of Wuling Ye was made Defender-General, and together with General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda received the honors of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies;

entries.zh: 尚書左僕射、西昌侯鸞為尚書令；
entries.en: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis Luan of Xichang, was made Director of the Secretariat;
entries.literal: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Marquis of Xichang Luan, became Director of the Secretariat;

entries.zh: 太孫詹事沈文季為護軍。
entries.en: Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Shen Wenji was made Guardian-General.
entries.literal: Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Shen Wenji became Guardian-General.

entries.zh: 癸未，以竟陵王子良為太傅；
