entries.en: On the day guiwei Prince Ziliang of Jingling was made Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: On guiwei Prince Ziliang of Jingling was made Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 蠲除三調及眾逋，省御府及無用池田、邸治。
entries.en: Taxes of three categories and all arrears were remitted; imperial storehouses and unused ponds, fields, and lodges were cut back;
entries.literal: Taxes of three categories and all arrears were remitted; imperial storehouses and unused ponds, fields, and lodges were reduced;

entries.zh: 減關市徵稅。。
entries.en: Levies at passes and markets were reduced.
entries.literal: Levies at passes and markets were lowered.

entries.zh: 先是，蠲原之詔，多無事實，督責如故。
entries.en: Before this, edicts remitting taxes and land often amounted to nothing; collection and enforcement continued as before.
entries.literal: Before this, edicts remitting taxes and land often had no real effect; collection and enforcement continued as before.

entries.zh: 是時西昌侯鸞知政，恩信兩行，眾皆悅之。。
entries.en: Now Marquis Luan of Xichang held the reins of government; favor and trust went hand in hand, and everyone was pleased.
entries.literal: Now Marquis of Xichang Luan held the reins of government; favor and trust both flowed, and everyone was pleased.

entries.zh: 魏山陽景桓公尉元卒。。
entries.en: In Wei, Yu Yuan, Marquis Jinghuan of Shanyang, died.
entries.literal: In Wei, Marquis Jinghuan of Shanyang, Yu Yuan, died.

entries.zh: 魏主使錄尚書事廣陵王羽持節安撫六鎮，發其突騎。
entries.en: The Wei emperor sent Grand Secretary Prince Yu of Guangling with credentials to reassure the Six Garrisons and levy their elite cavalry.
entries.literal: The Wei sovereign sent Grand Secretary Guangling Wang Yu with credentials to pacify and reassure the Six Garrisons and levy their elite cavalry.

entries.zh: 丁亥，魏主辭永固陵；
entries.en: On the day dinghai the Wei emperor took leave of Yonggu Mausoleum;
entries.literal: On dinghai the Wei sovereign took leave of Yonggu Mausoleum;

entries.zh: 己丑，發平城，南伐，步騎三十餘萬；
entries.en: On the day jichou he set out from Pingcheng on a southern campaign with more than three hundred thousand infantry and cavalry;
entries.literal: On jichou he departed Pingcheng on a southern campaign with more than three hundred thousand infantry and cavalry;

entries.zh: 使太尉丕與廣陵王羽留守平城，並加使持節。
entries.en: He left Grand Commandant Pi and Prince Yu of Guangling to hold Pingcheng, both granted extraordinary credentials.
entries.literal: He left Grand Commandant Pi and Guangling Wang Yu to hold Pingcheng, both with extraordinary credentials.

entries.zh: 羽曰：「太尉宜專節度，臣正可為副。」
entries.en: Yu said, "The Grand Commandant should hold sole command; I can serve only as his deputy."
entries.literal: Yu said: "The Grand Commandant ought to hold sole command; I can serve only as his deputy."

entries.zh: 魏主曰：「老者之智，少者之決，汝無辭也。」
entries.en: The Wei emperor said, "The old have wisdom, the young have resolve—you need make no excuses."
entries.literal: The Wei sovereign said: "The old have wisdom, the young have resolve—you need make no excuses."

entries.zh: 以河南王干為車騎大將軍、都督關右諸軍事，又以司空穆亮、安南將軍盧淵、平南將軍薛胤皆為干副，眾合七萬出子午谷。
entries.en: He then appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and commander of all forces west of the Pass, with Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Calms the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Xue Yin all serving as Gan's deputies; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.
entries.literal: He appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs west of the Pass, and further made Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Calms the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Xue Yin all deputies to Gan; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.

entries.zh: 胤，辯之曾孫也。。
entries.en: Yin was the great-grandson of Bian.
entries.literal: Yin was the great-grandson of Bian.

entries.zh: 鬱林王性辯慧，美容止，善應對，哀樂過人；
entries.en: Prince Yulin was quick-witted and eloquent by nature, handsome in bearing, skilled in repartee, and more expressive in joy and sorrow than others;
entries.literal: Prince Yulin was quick-witted and eloquent by nature, handsome in bearing, skilled in repartee, and more expressive in joy and sorrow than others;

entries.zh: 世祖由是愛之。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu therefore favored him.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu therefore loved him.

entries.zh: 而矯情飾詐，陰懷鄙慝，與左右群小共衣食，同臥起。。
entries.en: Yet he put on false feeling and practiced deceit, secretly nursing base resentments; he shared food and clothing with the low companions around him and slept and rose together with them.
entries.literal: Yet he feigned emotion and practiced deception, secretly harboring base malice; he shared food and clothing with his favored low companions and slept and rose with them.

entries.zh: 始為南郡王，從竟陵王子良在西州，文惠太子每禁其起居，節其用度。
entries.en: When he was first Prince of Nanjun, he followed Prince Ziliang of Jingling at Xizhou; Crown Prince Wenhui often restricted his daily conduct and curtailed his expenditures.
entries.literal: When he was first Prince of Nanjun, he followed Prince Ziliang of Jingling at Xizhou; Crown Prince Wenhui often restricted his daily conduct and curtailed his expenditures.

entries.zh: 王密就富人求錢，無敢不與。
entries.en: The prince secretly approached wealthy men to borrow money, and none dared refuse him.
entries.literal: The prince secretly approached wealthy men to borrow money, and none dared refuse him.

entries.zh: 別作鑰鉤，夜開西州後閣，與左右至諸營署中淫宴。
entries.en: He had a separate key-hook made and at night opened the rear gate of Xizhou, going with his companions to various camp offices for licentious feasting.
entries.literal: He had a separate key-hook made and at night opened the rear gate of Xizhou, going with his companions to various camp offices for licentious feasting.

entries.zh: 師史仁祖、侍書胡天翼相謂曰：「若言之二宮，則其事未易；
entries.en: His tutor Shi Renzu and the attendant-scribe Hu Tianyi said to each other, "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;
entries.literal: Tutor Shi Renzu and attendant-scribe Hu Tianyi said to each other: "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;

entries.zh: 若於營署為異人所毆及犬物所傷，豈直罪止一身，亦當盡室及禍。
entries.en: if in the camp offices we are beaten by strangers or injured by dogs or the like, would the guilt stop with us alone? Our whole households would also be ruined.
entries.literal: if in the camp offices we are beaten by strangers or injured by dogs or such things, would the guilt stop with us alone? Our whole households would also suffer disaster.

entries.zh: 年各七十，餘生豈足吝邪！」
entries.en: Each of us is seventy years old—why begrudge what little life remains!"
entries.literal: Each of us is seventy years old—why begrudge what remains of our lives!"

entries.zh: 數日間，二人相繼自殺，二宮不知也。
entries.en: Within a few days the two men killed themselves in succession, and the two palaces knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: Within a few days the two men killed themselves in succession, and the two palaces knew nothing of it.

entries.zh: 所愛左右，皆逆加官爵，疏於黃紙，使囊盛帶之，許南面之日，依此施行。。
entries.en: Those he favored among his attendants he all in advance conferred rank and titles upon, writing the appointments on yellow paper and having them stored in pouches and carried on their persons, with a promise that when he faced south as emperor these would be put into effect.
entries.literal: Those he favored among his attendants he all in advance conferred rank and titles upon, writing the appointments on yellow paper and having them stored in pouches and carried on their persons, with a promise that when he faced south as emperor these would be put into effect.

entries.zh: 侍太子疾及居喪，憂容號毀，見者嗚咽；
entries.en: When attending the crown prince in illness and during mourning, his face wore grief and he wailed and emaciated himself; those who saw him sobbed;
entries.literal: When attending the crown prince in illness and during mourning, his face wore grief and he wailed and emaciated himself; those who saw him sobbed;

entries.zh: 裁還私室，即歡笑酣飲。
entries.en: but as soon as he returned to his private quarters he laughed merrily and drank deeply.
entries.literal: but as soon as he returned to his private quarters he laughed merrily and drank deeply.

entries.zh: 常令女巫楊氏禱祀，速求天位。
entries.en: He constantly had the shamaness Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices, urgently seeking the imperial throne.
entries.literal: He constantly had the shamaness Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices, urgently seeking the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 及太子卒，謂由楊氏之力，倍加敬倍。
entries.en: When the crown prince died, he believed it was through Lady Yang's power and redoubled his reverence for her.
entries.literal: When the crown prince died, he believed it was through Lady Yang's power and redoubled his reverence for her.

entries.zh: 既為太孫，世祖有疾，又令楊氏禱祀。
entries.en: Once he became grand heir apparent, when Emperor Shizu fell ill he again had Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices.
entries.literal: Once he became grand heir apparent, when Emperor Shizu fell ill he again had Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices.

entries.zh: 時何妃猶在西州，世祖疾稍危，太孫與何妃書，紙中央作一大喜字，而作三十六小喜字繞之。。
entries.en: At that time Consort He was still at Xizhou. When Emperor Shizu's illness grew critical, the grand heir wrote to Consort He; in the center of the paper he drew one large character for joy, surrounded by thirty-six smaller joy characters.
entries.literal: At that time Consort He was still at Xizhou. When Emperor Shizu's illness grew critical, the grand heir wrote to Consort He; in the center of the paper he drew one large character xi for joy, surrounded by thirty-six smaller xi characters.

entries.zh: 侍世祖疾，言發淚下。
entries.en: When attending Emperor Shizu in his illness, he spoke and tears fell.
entries.literal: When attending Emperor Shizu in his illness, he spoke and tears fell.

entries.zh: 世祖以為必能負荷大業，謂曰：「五年中一委宰相，汝勿措意；
entries.en: Emperor Shizu thought he would surely be able to bear the great enterprise and said to him, "For five years leave everything entirely to the chief minister; do not concern yourself;
entries.literal: Emperor Shizu thought he would surely be able to bear the great enterprise and said to him: "For five years leave everything entirely to the chief minister; do not concern yourself;

entries.zh: 五年外勿復委人。
entries.en: After five years do not entrust matters to others again.
entries.literal: After five years do not entrust matters to others again.

entries.zh: 若自作無成，無所多恨。」
entries.en: If you act on your own and achieve nothing, you will have little cause for regret."
entries.literal: If you act on your own and achieve nothing, you will have little cause for regret."

entries.zh: 臨終，執其手曰：「若憶翁，當好作！」
entries.en: At the end of his life he took his hand and said, "If you remember your old grandfather, you must do well!"
entries.literal: At the end of his life he took his hand and said: "If you remember your old grandfather, you must do well!"

entries.zh: 遂殂。
entries.en: Then he died.
entries.literal: Then he died.

entries.zh: 大斂始畢，悉呼世祖諸伎，備奏眾樂。。
entries.en: As soon as the grand dressing of the corpse was finished, he summoned all of Emperor Shizu's performers and had every sort of music played.
entries.literal: As soon as the grand dressing of the corpse was finished, he summoned all of Emperor Shizu's performers and had every sort of music played.

entries.zh: 即位十餘日，即收王融下廷尉，使中丞孔稚珪奏融險躁輕狡，招納不逞，誹謗朝政。
entries.en: Within little more than ten days of taking the throne he had Wang Rong arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice; he had Censor-in-Chief Kong Zhigui memorialize that Rong was reckless, volatile, and cunning, that he gathered malcontents, and that he slandered the court and government.
entries.literal: Within little more than ten days of taking the throne he had Wang Rong arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice; he had Censor-in-Chief Kong Zhigui memorialize that Rong was reckless, volatile, and cunning, that he gathered malcontents, and that he slandered the court and government.

entries.zh: 融求援於竟陵王子良，子良憂懼，不敢救。
entries.en: Rong sought help from Prince Ziliang of Jingling; Ziliang was anxious and afraid and did not dare save him.
entries.literal: Rong sought help from Prince Ziliang of Jingling; Ziliang was anxious and afraid and did not dare save him.

entries.zh: 遂於獄賜死，時年二十七。。
entries.en: He was therefore granted death in prison; he was twenty-seven years old at the time.
entries.literal: He was therefore granted death in prison; he was twenty-seven years old at the time.

entries.zh: 初，融欲與東海徐勉相識，每托人召之。
entries.en: Earlier, Rong had wished to become acquainted with Xu Mian of Donghai and repeatedly sent people to summon him.
entries.literal: Earlier, Rong had wished to become acquainted with Xu Mian of Donghai and repeatedly sent people to summon him.

entries.zh: 勉謂人曰：「王君名高望促，難可輕{敝衣}衣裾。」
entries.en: Mian said to others, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly grasp his robe."
entries.literal: Mian said to others: "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly grasp his robe."

entries.zh: 俄而融及禍。
entries.en: Before long Rong met with disaster.
entries.literal: Before long Rong met with disaster.

entries.zh: 勉由是知名。
entries.en: Mian became famous on this account.
entries.literal: Mian became famous on this account.

entries.zh: 太學生會稽魏准，以才學為融所賞；
entries.en: Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, an Imperial University student, was admired by Rong for his talent and learning;
entries.literal: Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, an Imperial University student, was admired by Rong for his talent and learning;

entries.zh: 融欲立子良，准鼓成其事。
entries.en: Rong wished to establish Ziliang as emperor, and Zhun urged the matter on to success.
entries.literal: Rong wished to establish Ziliang as emperor, and Zhun urged the matter on to success.

entries.zh: 太學生虞羲、丘國賓竊相謂曰：「竟陵才弱，王中書無斷，敗在眼中矣。」
entries.en: University students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin secretly said to each other, "Jingling lacks talent, and Wang the Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary has no resolve—defeat is plain to see."
entries.literal: University students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin secretly said to each other: "Jingling lacks talent, and Wang the Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary has no resolve—defeat is plain to see."

entries.zh: 及融誅，召准入舍人省詰問，惶懼而死，舉體皆青，時人以為膽破。。
entries.en: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Secretariat of Palace Attendants for questioning; in terror and dread he died, his whole body turning blue-green, and people of the time thought his gall had burst.
entries.literal: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Secretariat of Palace Attendants for questioning; in terror and dread he died, his whole body turning blue-green, and people of the time thought his gall had burst.

entries.zh: 壬寅，魏主至肆州，見道路民有跛、眇者，停駕慰勞，給衣食終身。。
entries.en: On the day renyin the Wei emperor reached Sizhou; seeing common people along the road who were lame or blind, he halted his carriage to comfort and reassure them and granted them food and clothing for life.
entries.literal: On renyin the Wei sovereign reached Sizhou; seeing common people along the road who were lame or blind, he halted his carriage to comfort and reassure them and granted them food and clothing for life.

entries.zh: 大司馬安定王休執軍士為盜者三人，以徇於軍，將斬之。
entries.en: Grand Marshal Prince Xiu of Anding had seized three soldiers who had been thieves, displayed them before the army, and was about to execute them.
entries.literal: Grand Marshal Prince Xiu of Anding had seized three soldiers who had been thieves, displayed them before the army, and was about to execute them.

entries.zh: 魏主行軍遇之，命赦之，休不可，曰：「陛下親御六師，將遠清江表，今始行至此，而小人已為攘盜，不斬之，何以禁奸！」
entries.en: The Wei emperor encountered this on march and ordered them pardoned; Xiu would not consent and said, "Your Majesty personally leads the six armies and intends soon to clear the lands south of the Yangtze. We have only just set out and arrived here, yet petty men are already plundering—if we do not execute them, how can we check wrongdoing!"
entries.literal: The Wei sovereign encountered this on march and ordered them pardoned; Xiu would not consent and said: "Your Majesty personally leads the six armies and intends soon to clear the lands south of the Yangtze. We have only just set out and arrived here, yet petty men are already plundering—if we do not execute them, how can we check wrongdoing!"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「誠如卿言。
entries.en: The emperor said, "What you say is indeed true.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is indeed true.

entries.zh: 然王者之體，時有非常之澤。
entries.en: Yet the bearing of a true king sometimes includes extraordinary grace.
entries.literal: Yet the bearing of a true king sometimes includes extraordinary grace.

entries.zh: 三人罪雖應死，而因緣遇朕，雖違軍法，可特赦之。」
entries.en: Though these three men's crime deserves death, by chance they encountered me; though this violates military law, they may be specially pardoned."
entries.literal: Though these three men's crime deserves death, by chance they encountered me; though this violates military law, they may be specially pardoned."

entries.zh: 既而謂司徒馮誕曰：「大司馬執法嚴，諸君不可不慎。」
entries.en: Then he said to Minister of Education Feng Yan, "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."
entries.literal: Then he said to Minister of Education Feng Yan: "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."

entries.zh: 於是軍中肅然。。
entries.en: Thereupon the army became orderly and solemn.
entries.literal: Thereupon the army became orderly and solemn.

entries.zh: 臣光曰：「人主之於其國，譬猶一身，視遠如視邇，在境如在庭。
entries.en: Minister Guang said, "A ruler toward his state is like a body toward itself—he should regard the distant as he regards the near, and regard what is beyond the borders as though it were in his court hall.
entries.literal: Minister Guang said: "A ruler toward his state is like a body toward itself—he should regard the distant as he regards the near, and regard what is beyond the borders as though it were in his court hall.

entries.zh: 舉賢才以任百官，修政事以利百姓，則封域之內無不得其所矣。
entries.en: If he raises the worthy and talented to appoint the hundred officers, and rectifies government to benefit the common people, then within his domain none will fail to find their proper place.
entries.literal: If he raises the worthy and talented to appoint the hundred officers, and rectifies government to benefit the common people, then within his domain none will fail to find their proper place.

entries.zh: 是以先王黈纊塞耳，前旒蔽明，欲其廢耳目之近用，推聰明於四遠也。
entries.en: Therefore the former kings blocked their ears with cotton and covered their vision with the front pendants, wishing to set aside the immediate use of eyes and ears and extend their clarity and wisdom to the four quarters.
entries.literal: Therefore the former kings blocked their ears with cotton and covered their vision with the front pendants, wishing to set aside the immediate use of eyes and ears and extend their clarity and wisdom to the four quarters.

entries.zh: 彼廢疾者宜養，當命有司均之於境內，今獨施於道路之所遇，則所遺者多矣。
entries.en: Those maimed and disabled ought to be supported—the government offices should distribute care evenly throughout the realm. To grant it only to those encountered on the road means that many are left out.
entries.literal: Those maimed and disabled ought to be supported—the government offices should distribute care evenly throughout the realm. To grant it only to those encountered on the road means that many are left out.

entries.zh: 其為仁也，不亦微乎！
entries.en: Is this not petty as an act of benevolence!
entries.literal: Is this not petty as an act of benevolence!

entries.zh: 況赦罪人以橈有司之法，尤非人君之體也。
entries.en: Moreover, pardoning criminals and bending the law of the responsible officials is especially unworthy of a ruler's bearing.
entries.literal: Moreover, pardoning criminals and bending the law of the responsible officials is especially unworthy of a ruler's bearing.

entries.zh: 惜也！
entries.en: What a pity!
entries.literal: What a pity!

entries.zh: 孝文，魏之賢君，而猶有是乎！。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen was Wei's worthy sovereign, and yet he still did such things!
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Wei's worthy sovereign, and yet he still did such things!

entries.zh: 戊申，魏主至并州。
entries.en: On the day wushen the Wei emperor reached Bingzhou.
entries.literal: On wushen the Wei sovereign reached Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 并州刺史王襲，治有聲跡，境內安靜，帝嘉之。
entries.en: Bingzhou Inspector Wang Xi had a reputation for good governance and kept the region quiet; the emperor commended him.
entries.literal: Bingzhou Inspector Wang Xi had a reputation for good governance and kept the region quiet; the emperor commended him.

entries.zh: 襲教民多立銘置道側，虛稱其美；
entries.en: Xi instructed the people to erect many steles placed beside the roads, falsely praising his merits;
entries.literal: Xi instructed the people to erect many steles placed beside the roads, falsely praising his merits;

entries.zh: 帝聞而問之，襲對不以實。
entries.en: When the emperor heard and questioned him, Xi answered not according to the truth.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard and questioned him, Xi answered not according to the truth.

entries.zh: 帝怒，降襲號二等。。
entries.en: The emperor was angry and reduced Xi's noble rank by two grades.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and reduced Xi's noble rank by two grades.

entries.zh: 九月，壬子，魏遣兼員外散騎常侍勃海高聰等來聘。。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the day renzi, Wei sent Acting Supernumerary Palace Attendant Gao Cong of Bohai and others on a diplomatic mission.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on renzi, Wei sent Acting Supernumerary Palace Attendant Gao Cong of Bohai and others on a diplomatic mission.

entries.zh: 丁巳，魏主詔車駕所經，傷民秋稼者，畝給谷五斛。。
entries.en: On the day dingsi the Wei emperor decreed that wherever the imperial procession passed and damaged the people's autumn crops, five hu of grain would be given per mu.
entries.literal: On dingsi the Wei sovereign decreed that wherever the imperial procession passed and damaged the people's autumn crops, five hu of grain would be given per mu.

entries.zh: 辛酉，追尊文惠太子為文皇帝，廟號世宗。。
entries.en: On the day xinyou they posthumously honored Crown Prince Wenhui as Emperor Wen, with temple name Shizong.
entries.literal: On xinyou they posthumously honored Crown Prince Wenhui as Emperor Wen, with temple name Shizong.

entries.zh: 世祖梓宮下渚，帝於端門內奉辭，轀輬車未出端門，亟稱疾還內。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu's coffin was lowered to the ferry, the emperor took farewell inside the Duan Gate; before the hearses had even passed out of the Duan Gate he urgently claimed illness and returned inside.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu's coffin was lowered to the ferry, the emperor took farewell inside the Duan Gate; before the hearses had even passed out of the Duan Gate he urgently claimed illness and returned inside.

entries.zh: 裁入閣，即於內奏胡伎，鞞鐸之聲，響震內外。
entries.en: Hardly had he entered the inner quarters when he had barbarian performers play inside; the sound of drums and bells shook inside and out.
entries.literal: Hardly had he entered the inner quarters when he had barbarian performers play inside; the sound of drums and bells shook inside and out.

entries.zh: 丙寅，葬武皇帝於景安陵，廟號世祖。。
entries.en: On the day bingyin they buried Emperor Wu at Jing'an Mausoleum, with temple name Shizu.
entries.literal: On bingyin they buried Emperor Wu at Jing'an Mausoleum, with temple name Shizu.

entries.zh: 戊辰，魏主濟河；
entries.en: On the day wuchen the Wei emperor crossed the river;
entries.literal: On wuchen the Wei sovereign crossed the river;

entries.zh: 庚午，至洛陽；
entries.en: On the day gengwu he reached Luoyang;
entries.literal: On gengwu he reached Luoyang;

entries.zh: 壬申，詣故太學觀《石經》。。
entries.en: On the day renshen he went to the former Imperial Academy to view the Stone Classics.
entries.literal: On renshen he went to the former Imperial Academy to view the Stone Classics.

entries.zh: 乙亥，鄧至王像舒彭遣其子舊朝於魏，且請傳位於舊；
entries.en: On the day yihai King Xiangshu Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;
entries.literal: On yihai King Xiangshu Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;

entries.zh: 魏主許之。。
entries.en: The Wei emperor granted it.
entries.literal: The Wei sovereign granted it.

entries.zh: 魏主自發平城至洛陽，霖雨不止。
entries.en: From the time the Wei emperor set out from Pingcheng until he reached Luoyang, the rains did not cease.
entries.literal: From the time the Wei sovereign set out from Pingcheng until he reached Luoyang, the rains did not cease.

entries.zh: 丙子，詔諸軍前發。
entries.en: On the day bingzi he decreed that all armies advance.
entries.literal: On bingzi he decreed that all armies advance.

entries.zh: 丁丑，帝戎服，執鞭乘馬而出。
entries.en: On the day dingchou the emperor donned military garb, took the whip, mounted a horse, and rode out.
entries.literal: On dingchou the emperor donned military garb, took the whip, mounted a horse, and rode out.

entries.zh: 群臣稽顙於馬前。
entries.en: The ministers prostrated themselves kowtowing before his horse.
entries.literal: The ministers prostrated themselves kowtowing before his horse.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「廟算已定，大軍將進，諸公更欲何雲？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "The plans made in the temple are settled and the great army is about to advance—what more do you gentlemen wish to say?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "The plans made in the temple are settled and the great army is about to advance—what more do you gentlemen wish to say?"

entries.zh: 尚書李沖等曰：「今者之舉，天下所不願，唯陛下欲之。
entries.en: Chief Secretary Li Chong and others said, "This campaign we now undertake is what all under Heaven does not wish for—only Your Majesty desires it.
entries.literal: Chief Secretary Li Chong and others said: "This campaign we now undertake is what all under Heaven does not wish for—only Your Majesty desires it.

entries.zh: 臣不知陛下獨行，竟何之也！
entries.en: Your servants do not know where Your Majesty intends to go if you advance alone!
entries.literal: Your servants do not know where Your Majesty intends to go if you advance alone!

entries.zh: 臣等有其意而無其辭，敢以死請！」
entries.en: We have the intent but not the words—we dare beg with our lives!"
entries.literal: We have the intent but not the words—we dare beg with our lives!"

entries.zh: 帝大怒曰：「吾方經營天下，期於混壹，而卿等儒生，屢疑大計；
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage and said, "I am now setting the empire in order, aiming at unification, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great design;
entries.literal: The emperor flew into a rage and said: "I am now setting the empire in order, aiming at unification, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great design;

entries.zh: 斧鉞有常，卿勿復言！」
entries.en: The axe and halberd have their fixed law—speak no more!"
entries.literal: The axe and halberd have their fixed law—speak no more!"

entries.zh: 策馬將出，於是安定王休等並殷勤泣諫。
entries.en: He spurred his horse and was about to depart; then Prince Xiu of Anding and the others all earnestly wept and remonstrated.
entries.literal: He spurred his horse and was about to depart; then Prince Xiu of Anding and the others all earnestly wept and remonstrated.

entries.zh: 帝乃諭群臣曰：「今者興發不小，動而無成，何以示後！
entries.en: The emperor then addressed the ministers, "The undertaking we launch today is no small matter—if we act and achieve nothing, how can we show ourselves to posterity!
entries.literal: The emperor then addressed the ministers: "The undertaking we launch today is no small matter—if we act and achieve nothing, how can we show ourselves to posterity!

entries.zh: 朕世居幽朔，欲南遷中土；
entries.en: My house has for generations dwelt in the northern wilds, and I wish to move south to the central lands;
entries.literal: I have long dwelt in the northern wilds and wish to move south to the central lands;

entries.zh: 苟不南伐，當遷都於此，王公以為何如？
entries.en: If we do not campaign south, we should move the capital here—what do the princes and dukes think?
entries.literal: If we do not campaign south, we should move the capital here—what do the princes and dukes think?

entries.zh: 欲遷者左，不欲者右。」
entries.en: Those who wish to move, stand to the left; those who do not, to the right."
entries.literal: Those who wish to move, stand to the left; those who do not, to the right."

entries.zh: 安定王休等相帥如右。
entries.en: Prince Xiu of Anding and the others led one another to the right.
entries.literal: Prince Xiu of Anding and the others led one another to the right.

entries.zh: 南安王楨進曰：「『成大功者不謀於眾。』
entries.en: Prince Zhen of Nan'an stepped forward and said, "'He who would achieve great things does not consult the multitude.
entries.literal: Prince Zhen of Nan'an stepped forward and said: "'He who would achieve great things does not consult the multitude.

entries.zh: 今陛下苟輟南伐之謀，遷都洛邑，此臣等之願，蒼生之幸也。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty would now abandon the plan for a southern campaign and move the capital to Luoyang, that is the wish of your servants—and the fortune of the people.'"
entries.literal: If Your Majesty would now abandon the plan for a southern campaign and move the capital to Luoyang, that is the wish of your servants—and the fortune of the people."

entries.zh: 群臣皆呼萬歲。
entries.en: All the ministers cried, "Long live the emperor!"
entries.literal: All the ministers cried "Long live the emperor!"

entries.zh: 時舊人雖不願內徙，而憚於南伐，無敢言者；
entries.en: At the time the northerners, though unwilling to move south, feared the southern campaign and none dared object;
entries.literal: At the time the old guard, though unwilling to move inward, feared the southern campaign and none dared speak;

entries.zh: 遂定遷都之計。。
entries.en: and so the plan to move the capital was settled.
entries.literal: and so the plan to move the capital was settled.

entries.zh: 李沖言於上曰：「陛下將定鼎洛邑，宗廟宮室，非可馬上行遊以待之。
entries.en: Li Chong said to the emperor, "Your Majesty intends to establish the capital at Luoyang; the ancestral temples and palaces cannot be readied while you travel on horseback.
entries.literal: Li Chong said to the emperor: "Your Majesty intends to establish the capital at Luoyang; the ancestral temples and palaces cannot be awaited while touring on horseback.

entries.zh: 願陛下暫還代都，俟群臣經營畢功，然後備文物、鳴和鸞而臨之。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to return for the time being to the capital at Dai, wait until the ministers have finished their preparations, and then enter Luoyang with full ceremonial regalia and the imperial bells ringing."
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to return for the time being to the capital at Dai, wait until the ministers have finished their preparations, and then, with full regalia and the harmon and phoenix bells sounding, take up residence there."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「朕將巡省州郡，至鄴小停，春首即還，未宜歸北。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I shall tour and inspect the provinces and commanderies, pause briefly at Ye, and return at the beginning of spring—it is not yet fitting to go back north."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I shall tour and inspect the provinces and commanderies, pause briefly at Ye, and return at the beginning of spring—it is not yet fitting to go back north."

entries.zh: 乃遣任城王澄還平城，諭留司百官以遷都之事，曰：「今日真所謂革也。
entries.en: He then sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng back to Pingcheng to instruct the officials left behind in the Northern Capital concerning the move of the capital, saying, "Today this is truly revolution itself.
entries.literal: He then sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng back to Pingcheng to instruct the officials left behind in the Northern Capital concerning the move of the capital, saying: "Today this is truly what is called revolution.

entries.zh: 王其勉之！」
entries.en: Prince, exert yourself!"
entries.literal: Prince, exert yourself!"

entries.zh: 帝以群臣意多異同，謂衛尉卿、鎮南將軍於烈曰：「卿意如何？」
entries.en: Since the ministers' views differed greatly, the emperor asked Commander of the Guard and General Who Guards the South Yu Lie, "What is your view?"
entries.literal: Since the ministers' views differed greatly, the emperor asked Commander of the Guard and General Who Guards the South Yu Lie: "What is your view?"

entries.zh: 烈曰：「陛下聖略淵遠，非愚淺所測。
entries.en: Lie said, "Your Majesty's sacred design is profound and far-reaching—beyond what the dull and shallow can fathom.
entries.literal: Lie said: "Your Majesty's sacred design is profound and far-reaching—beyond what the dull and shallow can fathom.

entries.zh: 若隱心而言，樂遷之與戀舊，適中半耳。」
entries.en: If I speak from the heart, those who welcome the move and those who cling to the old are about evenly divided."
entries.literal: If I speak from the heart, those who rejoice in the move and those who cling to the old are about evenly divided."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿既不唱異，即是肯同，深感不言之益。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Since you do not lead the opposition, that is support enough. I am grateful for your restraint."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Since you do not lead the dissent, that is agreement; I deeply feel the benefit of your not speaking out."

entries.zh: 使還鎮平城，曰：「留台庶政，一以相委。」
entries.en: He sent him back to garrison Pingcheng, saying, "All routine affairs of the Northern Capital—I entrust them entirely to you."
entries.literal: He sent him back to garrison Pingcheng, saying: "All routine affairs of the Northern Capital—I entrust them entirely to you."

entries.zh: 烈，栗磾之孫也。。
entries.en: Lie was the grandson of Yu Lidi.
entries.literal: Lie was the grandson of Yu Lidi.

entries.zh: 先是，北地民支酉聚眾數千，起兵於長安城北石山，遣使告梁州刺史陰智伯，秦州民王廣亦起兵應之，攻執魏刺史劉藻，秦、雍間七州民皆響震，眾至十萬，各守堡壁以待齊救。
entries.en: Earlier, Zhi You of the Northern Lands gathered several thousand men and raised troops at Stone Mountain north of Chang'an, sending envoys to inform Governor of Liang Province Yin Zhibo; Wang Guang of Qin Province also rose in response, attacked and seized the Wei governor Liu Zao, and the people of the seven provinces between Qin and Yong all echoed the uprising until the force reached one hundred thousand; each held fortified walls and awaited relief from Qi.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhi You of the Northern Lands gathered several thousand men and raised troops at Stone Mountain north of Chang'an, sending envoys to inform Governor of Liang Province Yin Zhibo; Wang Guang of Qin Province also raised troops in response, attacked and seized Wei Governor Liu Zao, and the people of the seven provinces between Qin and Yong all echoed the uprising until the force reached one hundred thousand; each held fortified walls and awaited Qi relief.

entries.zh: 魏河南王干引兵擊之，干兵大敗；
entries.en: Prince Gan of Henan of Wei led troops to attack them, and Gan's army was utterly defeated;
entries.literal: Prince Gan of Henan of Wei led troops to attack them, and Gan's army was utterly defeated;

entries.zh: 支酉進至咸陽北濁谷，穆亮與戰，又敗；
entries.en: Zhi You advanced to Turbid Valley north of Xianyang; Mu Liang fought him and was again defeated;
entries.literal: Zhi You advanced to Turbid Valley north of Xianyang; Mu Liang fought him and was again defeated;

entries.zh: 陰智伯遣軍主席德仁等將兵數千與相應接。
entries.en: Yin Zhibo sent the army commander Xi Deren and others to lead several thousand troops to join and support them.
entries.literal: Yin Zhibo sent the army commander Xi Deren and others to lead several thousand troops to join and support them.

entries.zh: 酉等進向長安，盧淵、薛胤等拒擊，大破之，降者數萬口。
entries.en: You and the others advanced toward Chang'an; Lu Yuan, Xue Yin, and others repulsed and attacked them, inflicting a great defeat, and tens of thousands surrendered.
entries.literal: You and the others advanced toward Chang'an; Lu Yuan, Xue Yin, and others repulsed and attacked them, inflicting a great defeat, and those who surrendered numbered tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 淵唯誅首惡，餘悉不問，獲酉、廣，並斬之。。
entries.en: Lu Yuan executed only the ringleaders and questioned none of the rest; capturing You and Guang, he beheaded them both.
entries.literal: Lu Yuan executed only the ringleaders and questioned none of the rest; capturing You and Guang, he beheaded them both.

entries.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅朔，魏主如金墉城，征穆亮，使與尚書李沖、將作大匠董爾經營洛都。
entries.en: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day wuyin, the Wei emperor went to Jinyong City, recalled Mu Liang, and had him together with Chief Secretary Li Chong and Master of Works Dong Er oversee the construction of the Luoyang capital.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of the month wuyin, the Wei emperor went to Jinyong City, recalled Mu Liang, and had him together with Chief Secretary Li Chong and Master of Works Dong Er oversee the construction of the Luoyang capital.

entries.zh: 己卯，如河南城；
entries.en: On the day jimao he went to Henan City;
entries.literal: On jimao he went to Henan City;

entries.zh: 乙酉，如豫州；
entries.en: On the day yiyou he went to Yu Province;
entries.literal: On yiyou he went to Yu Province;

entries.zh: 癸巳，捨於石濟。
entries.en: On the day guisi he lodged at Shiji.
entries.literal: On guisi he lodged at Shiji.

entries.zh: 乙未，魏解嚴，設壇於滑台城東，告行廟以遷都之意。
entries.en: On the day yiwei Wei lifted martial law, set up an altar east of Huatai City, and informed the traveling temple of the intent to move the capital.
entries.literal: On yiwei Wei lifted martial law, set up an altar east of Huatai City, and informed the traveling temple of the intent to move the capital.

entries.zh: 大赦。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 起滑台宮。
entries.en: The Huatai Palace was built.
entries.literal: The Huatai Palace was built.

entries.zh: 任城王澄至平城，眾始聞遷都，莫不驚駭。
entries.en: When Prince Cheng of Rencheng reached Pingcheng, the people first heard of the move of the capital and all were startled and dismayed.
entries.literal: When Prince Cheng of Rencheng reached Pingcheng, the people first heard of the move of the capital and all were startled and dismayed.

entries.zh: 澄援引古今，徐以曉之，眾乃開伏。
entries.en: Cheng cited examples from past and present and gradually explained to them; the crowd then opened up and submitted.
entries.literal: Cheng cited examples from past and present and gradually explained to them; the crowd then opened up and submitted.

entries.zh: 澄還報於滑台，魏主喜曰：「非任城，朕事不成。」。
entries.en: Cheng returned and reported at Huatai; the Wei emperor said with delight, "Without Rencheng, my undertaking would not have succeeded."
entries.literal: Cheng returned and reported at Huatai; the Wei emperor said with delight: "Without Rencheng, my undertaking would not have succeeded."

entries.zh: 壬寅，尊皇太孫太妃為皇太后；
entries.en: On the day renyin the imperial great-grandson's grand consort was honored as empress dowager;
entries.literal: On renyin the imperial great-grandson's grand consort was honored as empress dowager;

entries.zh: 立妃為皇后。。
entries.en: and the consort was established as empress.
entries.literal: the consort was established as empress.

entries.zh: 癸卯，魏主如鄴城。
entries.en: On the day guimao the Wei emperor went to Ye City.
entries.literal: On guimao the Wei emperor went to Ye City.

entries.zh: 王肅見魏主於鄴，陳伐齊之策。
entries.en: Wang Su met the Wei emperor at Ye and set forth a strategy for campaigning against Qi.
entries.literal: Wang Su met the Wei emperor at Ye and set forth a strategy for campaigning against Qi.

entries.zh: 魏主與之言，不覺促席移晷。
entries.en: The Wei emperor spoke with him and, without noticing, drew his seat close and hours slipped by.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor spoke with him and, without noticing, drew his seat close and hours slipped by.

entries.zh: 自是器遇日隆，親舊貴臣莫能間也。
entries.en: From then on his honors and favor daily increased, and none among the emperor's kin and great ministers could come between them.
entries.literal: From then on his honors and favor daily increased, and none among the emperor's kin and great ministers could come between them.

entries.zh: 魏主或屏左右與肅語，至夜分不罷，自謂君臣相得之晚。
entries.en: The Wei emperor would sometimes dismiss his attendants and speak with Su until deep into the night, saying to himself that monarch and minister had found each other late.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor would sometimes dismiss his attendants and speak with Su until deep into the night, saying to himself that monarch and minister had found each other late.

entries.zh: 尋除輔國將軍、大將軍長史。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to the Grand General.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to the Grand General.

entries.zh: 時魏主方議興禮樂，變華風，凡威儀文物，多肅所定。。
entries.en: At the time the Wei emperor was discussing reviving ritual and music and changing to civilized customs; nearly all ceremonial regalia and institutions were determined by Su.
entries.literal: At the time the Wei emperor was just then discussing reviving ritual and music and changing to civilized customs; nearly all ceremonial regalia and institutions were determined by Su.

entries.zh: 乙巳，魏主遣安定王休帥從官迎家於平城。。
entries.en: On the day yisi the Wei emperor sent Prince Xiu of Anding to lead the accompanying officials to bring the imperial household from Pingcheng.
entries.literal: On yisi the Wei emperor sent Prince Xiu of Anding to lead the accompanying officials to bring the imperial household from Pingcheng.

entries.zh: 辛亥，封皇弟昭文為新安王，昭秀為臨海王，昭粲為永嘉王。。
entries.en: On the day xinhai the emperor's younger brothers Zhaowen, Zhaoxiu, and Zhaocan were enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, Prince of Linhai, and Prince of Yongjia respectively.
entries.literal: On xinhai the emperor's younger brothers Zhaowen, Zhaoxiu, and Zhaocan were enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an, Prince of Linhai, and Prince of Yongjia respectively.

entries.zh: 魏主築宮於鄴西，十一月，癸亥，徙居之。。
entries.en: The Wei emperor built a palace west of Ye; in the eleventh month, on the day guihai, he moved into it.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor built a palace west of Ye; in the eleventh month, on guihai, he moved into it.

entries.zh: 御史中丞江淹劾奏前益州刺史劉悛、梁州刺史陰智伯贓貨巨萬，皆抵罪。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Jiang Yan impeached the former Governor of Yi Province Liu Quan and Governor of Liang Province Yin Zhibo for accepting bribes worth tens of thousands; both were punished according to law.
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Jiang Yan impeached the former Governor of Yi Province Liu Quan and Governor of Liang Province Yin Zhibo for accepting bribes worth tens of thousands; both were punished according to law.

entries.zh: 初，悛罷廣、司二州，傾貲以獻世祖，家無留儲。
entries.en: Earlier, when Quan left his posts in Guang and Si provinces, he poured out his wealth as tribute to Emperor Shizu and left nothing in store at home.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Quan left his posts in Guang and Si provinces, he poured out his wealth as tribute to Emperor Shizu and left nothing in store at home.

entries.zh: 在益州，作金浴盆，餘物稱是。
entries.en: While in Yi Province he had a golden bathtub made, and his other possessions matched this in extravagance.
entries.literal: While in Yi Province he had a golden bathtub made, and his other possessions matched this in extravagance.

entries.zh: 及鬱林王即位，悛所獻減少。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, the tribute Quan offered diminished.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, the tribute Quan offered diminished.

entries.zh: 帝怒，收悛付廷尉，欲殺之；
entries.en: The emperor was enraged, seized Quan and handed him over to the Court of Justice, intending to execute him;
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged, seized Quan and handed him over to the Court of Justice, intending to execute him;

entries.zh: 西昌侯鸞救之，得免，猶禁錮終身。
entries.en: Marquis of Xichang Luan rescued him, and he was spared, though still confined for life.
entries.literal: Marquis of Xichang Luan rescued him, and he was spared, though still confined for life.

entries.zh: 悛，勉之子也。。」
entries.en: Quan was the son of Mian.”
entries.literal: Quan was the son of Mian.”

entries.zh: 臣光曰：孔子稱「鄙夫不可與事君，未得之，患得之；
entries.en: Sima Guang comments: Confucius said, "A vulgar man is unfit to serve his sovereign; before he gains office, he fears he will not gain it;
entries.literal: Minister Guang says: Confucius said, "The base fellow cannot be entrusted with serving a ruler; before obtaining it, he worries he will not obtain it;

entries.zh: 既得之，患失之。
entries.en: Once he holds it, he fears he will lose it.
entries.literal: Once he has obtained it, he worries he will lose it.

entries.zh: 苟患失之，無所不至。」
entries.en: If he dreads losing what he has, there is no limit to what he will do."
entries.literal: If he worries about losing it, there is nothing to which he will not go."

entries.zh: 王融乘危徼幸，謀易嗣君。
entries.en: Wang Rong seized a moment of crisis to gamble for advantage and schemed to replace the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Wang Rong, riding peril to seek fortune, plotted to change the heir.

entries.zh: 子良當時賢王，雖素以忠慎自居，不免憂死。
entries.en: Ziliang was the most admired prince of his day; though he had always prided himself on loyalty and prudence, he still died of anxiety.
entries.literal: Ziliang was the worthy prince of the time; though he had always taken loyalty and caution as his stand, he could not escape dying of worry.

entries.zh: 跡其所以然，正由融速求富貴而已。
entries.en: Trace the cause to its root, and it was nothing more than Rong's rush to seize wealth and status.
entries.literal: Tracing why this came about, it was simply because Rong was hastening to seek wealth and rank.

entries.zh: 輕躁之士，烏可近哉！
entries.en: How can anyone keep company with a man so rash and unstable!
entries.literal: A frivolous and impetuous fellow— how can one draw near to him!

entries.zh: 二月，乙丑，魏主如河陰，規方澤。
entries.en: In the second month, on the yichou day, the Wei emperor went to Heyin to plan the square altar to Earth.
entries.literal: In the second month, on day yichou, the Wei sovereign went to Heyin to plan the square altar to Earth.

entries.zh: 是時，蕭諶、蕭坦之握兵權，左僕射王晏總尚書事。
entries.en: At this time Chen and Tanzhi controlled the army, while Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, oversaw the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: At this time Chen and Tanzhi held military authority; Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat Wang Yan oversaw Masters of Writing affairs.

entries.zh: 諶密召諸王典簽，約語之，不許諸王外接人物。
entries.en: Chen secretly summoned each prince's chief clerk, bound them by agreement, and forbade the princes to receive outsiders.
entries.literal: Chen secretly summoned the palace stewards of the princes, made agreements with them, not permitting the princes to receive people from outside.

entries.zh: 諶親要日久，眾皆憚而從之。
entries.en: Chen had long been close to power, and everyone feared him and complied.
entries.literal: Chen had been intimate and influential for many days; all feared him and obeyed.

entries.zh: 鸞以其謀告王晏，晏聞之，響應；
entries.en: Luan disclosed his plan to Wang Yan, who at once assented;
entries.literal: Luan reported his plot to Wang Yan; Yan on hearing it responded in agreement;

entries.zh: 又告丹陽尹徐孝嗣，孝嗣亦從之。
entries.en: He also informed Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang, and Xiaosi went along as well.
entries.literal: He also told Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang; Xiaosi also followed.

entries.zh: 驃騎錄事南陽樂豫謂孝嗣曰：「外傳籍籍，似有伊、周之事。
entries.en: Leyu of Nanyang, recorder on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General, told Xiaosi: "Rumors are everywhere, as though someone were playing Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou to the throne.
entries.literal: Recorder of Affairs under the Rapid Cavalry General Leyu of Nanyang said to Xiaosi: "Outside the talk is widespread, as if there were an Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou affair.

entries.zh: 君蒙武帝殊常之恩，荷托附之重，恐不得同人此舉。
entries.en: You received extraordinary favor from Emperor Wu and bore a heavy trust; I fear you cannot join them in this.
entries.literal: You received Emperor Wu's exceptional grace, bore the weight of entrustment— I fear you cannot go along with this action in common with them.

entries.zh: 人笑褚公，至今齒冷。」
entries.en: Men still mock Lord Chu, and the mockery has not grown stale."
entries.literal: People still laugh at Lord Chu; to this day teeth are cold."

entries.zh: 孝嗣心然之，而不能從。
entries.en: Xiaosi agreed in his heart but could not bring himself to refuse.
entries.literal: Xiaosi inwardly agreed but could not refuse to follow.

entries.zh: 西昌侯鸞既誅徐龍駒、周奉叔，而尼媼外入者，頗傳異語。
entries.en: After Luan, Marquis of Xichang, had killed Xu Longju and Zhou Fengshu, nuns and old women coming in from outside spread all manner of alarming rumors.
entries.literal: After Luan, Marquis of Xichang, had executed Xu Longju and Zhou Fengshu, nuns and old women entering from outside rather widely spread strange talk.

entries.zh: 中書令何胤，以後之從叔，為帝所親，使直殿省。
entries.en: He Yin, Director of the Secretariat, was a maternal uncle of the empress and a favorite of the emperor, who had him serve in the Hall Directorate.
entries.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Yin, being a paternal uncle on the empress's side, was intimate with the emperor and was made to attend the Hall Directorate.

entries.zh: 帝與胤謀誅鸞，令胤受事；
entries.en: The emperor plotted with Yin to kill Luan and told Yin to take charge;
entries.literal: The emperor with Yin plotted to kill Luan and ordered Yin to take charge of the matter;

entries.zh: 胤不敢當，依違諫說，帝意復止。
entries.en: Yin did not dare accept the role; he hedged and urged caution, and the emperor's resolve faded again.
entries.literal: Yin did not dare undertake it, vacillating with admonitory persuasion, and the emperor's intent again ceased.

entries.zh: 乃謀出鸞於西州，中敕用事，不復關咨於鸞。
entries.en: They then planned to post Luan away to Western Province so that central orders would govern affairs without consulting him.
entries.literal: Then they plotted to send Luan out to Western Province; central edicts would govern affairs, no longer consulting Luan.

entries.zh: 八月，甲辰，以司空王敬則為太尉。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the jiachen day, Wang Jingze, Minister of Works, was appointed Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Eighth month, jiachen, Wang Jingze, Minister of Works, was made Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 鄱陽王鏘為司徒，車騎大將軍陳顯達為司空，尚書左僕射王晏為尚書令。
entries.en: Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, became Minister of Education; Chen Xianda, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, became Minister of Works; and Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, became Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, was made Minister of Education; Chen Xianda, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, was made Minister of Works; Wang Yan, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 魏主至陰山。
entries.en: The Wei emperor reached Yin Mountain.
entries.literal: The Wei emperor reached Yin Mountain.

entries.zh: 帝謂蕭坦之曰：「人言鎮軍與王晏、蕭諶欲共廢我，似非虛傳。
entries.en: The emperor said to Tanzhi: "People say the General Who Guards the Army, Wang Yan, and Chen are plotting to depose me together. That does not sound like idle talk.
entries.literal: The emperor said to Tanzhi: "People say the General Who Guards the Army with Wang Yan and Xiao Chen together wish to depose me— it does not seem a false rumor.

entries.zh: 卿所聞雲何？」
entries.en: What have you heard on your side?"
entries.literal: What have you heard?"

entries.zh: 坦之曰：「天下寧當有此，誰樂無事廢天子邪！
entries.en: Tanzhi replied: "Could such a thing truly happen in the world? Who would want to depose the Son of Heaven when nothing is amiss!
entries.literal: Tanzhi said: "Would such a thing really exist under Heaven— who would delight in deposing the Son of Heaven when there is nothing wrong!

entries.zh: 朝貴不容造此論，當是諸尼姥言耳，豈有信邪！
entries.en: The great officials of court would never invent such talk; it must be those nuns and old women. How could anyone believe it!
entries.literal: Court nobles would not allow such talk to be made; it must be the words of those nuns and old women— how could there be belief!

entries.zh: 官若無事除此二人，誰敢自保！」
entries.en: If Your Majesty removed these two men without cause, who would dare think himself safe!"
entries.literal: If Your Majesty without cause removed these two men, who would dare protect himself!"

entries.zh: 直閣將軍曹道剛疑外間有異，密有處分，謀未能發。
entries.en: Cao Daogang, Director of the Palace Gate, suspected trouble outside and made secret arrangements, but the plot never came off.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Gate Cao Daogang suspected something unusual outside, had secret dispositions, but the plot could not be launched.

entries.zh: 壬辰，鸞使蕭諶先入宮，遇曹道剛及中書舍人朱隆之，皆殺之。
entries.en: On the renchen day, Luan sent Chen into the palace ahead of him; Chen met Cao Daogang and Zhu Longzhi, Master of Writing Attendant, and killed them both.
entries.literal: On day renchen, Luan sent Chen to enter the palace first; encountering Cao Daogang and Master of Writing Attendant Zhu Longzhi, he killed them both.

entries.zh: 直後徐僧亮盛怒，大言於眾曰：「吾等荷恩，今日應死報！」
entries.en: Xu Sengliang, palace attendant, flew into a rage and cried out to those around him: "We owe the emperor our lives; today we must repay him with death!"
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Xu Sengliang was greatly enraged and spoke loudly before the crowd: "We have received grace; today we should repay with death!"

entries.zh: 又殺之。
entries.en: He too was killed.
entries.literal: He was killed as well.

entries.zh: 鸞引兵自尚書入雲龍門，戎服加朱衣於上，比入門，三失履。
entries.en: Luan led his troops from the Masters of Writing compound through the Cloud Dragon Gate, wearing armor with a vermilion robe over it; before he crossed the threshold he lost his shoes three times.
entries.literal: Luan led troops from the Masters of Writing into the Cloud Dragon Gate, military dress with vermilion robe over it; by the time he entered the gate he had lost his shoes three times.

entries.zh: 王晏、徐孝嗣、蕭坦之、陳顯達、王廣之、沈文季皆隨其後。
entries.en: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji all followed in his train.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji all followed behind him.

entries.zh: 帝在壽昌殿。
entries.en: The emperor was in the Hall of Longevity and Prosperity.
entries.literal: The emperor was in the Shouchang Hall.

entries.zh: 聞外有變，猶密為手敕呼蕭諶，又使閉內殿諸房閣。
entries.en: When he heard trouble outside, he still secretly drafted a personal order summoning Chen and had the inner chambers and side halls barred.
entries.literal: Hearing there was disturbance outside, he still secretly made a hand edict summoning Chen, and also ordered the inner hall rooms and pavilions closed.

entries.zh: 俄而諶引兵入壽昌閣，帝走趨徐姬房，拔劍自刺，不入，以帛纏頸，輿接出延德殿。
entries.en: Soon Chen marched into the Shouchang Pavilion. The emperor fled to Lady Xu's rooms, tried to stab himself but failed, bound his neck in silk, and was carried out on a litter to the Hall of Extended Virtue.
entries.literal: Before long Chen led troops into the Shouchang Pavilion; the emperor ran to Lady Xu's quarters, drew his sword to stab himself but did not penetrate, wrapped his neck in silk, and was carried out by litter to the Yande Hall.

entries.zh: 諶初入殿，宿衛將士皆操弓楯欲拒戰。
entries.en: When Chen first entered the hall, the palace guards seized bows and shields, ready to fight.
entries.literal: When Chen first entered the hall, the palace guards all grasped bows and shields wishing to resist and fight.

entries.zh: 諶謂之曰：「所取自有人，卿等不須動！」
entries.en: Chen told them: "We are only taking the man we came for; none of you need stir!"
entries.literal: Chen said to them: "The one taken has his own person; you need not move!"

entries.zh: 宿衛素隸服於諶，皆信之，及見帝出，各欲自奮，帝竟無一言。
entries.en: The guards had long served under Chen and trusted him. When they saw the emperor led away, several wanted to fight, but the emperor never spoke a word.
entries.literal: The palace guards had long been subordinate to Chen and all believed him; when they saw the emperor brought out, each wished to exert himself, but the emperor in the end said not a word.

entries.zh: 行至西弄，弒之。
entries.en: At the western passage they murdered him.
entries.literal: When they reached the western lane, they assassinated him.

entries.zh: 輿屍出殯徐龍駒宅，葬以王禮。
entries.en: They carried his body out and laid it in state at Xu Longju's house, then buried him with the honors due a prince.
entries.literal: They carried the corpse out and encoffined it at Xu Longju's residence, burying him with princely rites.

entries.zh: 徐姬及諸嬖倖皆伏誅。
entries.en: Lady Xu and all the emperor's favorites were put to death.
entries.literal: Lady Xu and all the favored minions were executed.

entries.zh: 鸞既執帝，欲作太后令；
entries.en: Once Luan held the emperor captive, he wanted to issue an order in the empress dowager's name;
entries.literal: After Luan had seized the emperor, he wished to draft an empress dowager order;

entries.zh: 徐孝嗣於袖中出而進之，鸞大悅。
entries.en: Xu Xiaosi drew the draft from his sleeve and submitted it, and Luan was delighted.
entries.literal: Xu Xiaosi produced it from his sleeve and presented it; Luan was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以太后令追廢帝為鬱林王，又廢何後為王妃，迎立新安王昭文。
entries.en: On the guisi day, by order of the empress dowager the emperor was posthumously demoted to Prince of Yulin, Empress He was reduced to princess consort, and Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was installed on the throne.
entries.literal: On day guisi, by empress dowager order the emperor was posthumously deposed as Prince of Yulin, Empress He was also deposed as princess consort, and Zhaowen, Prince of Xin'an, was welcomed and established.

entries.zh: 海陵王在位，起居飲食，皆咨宣城王而後行。
entries.en: While Prince Hailing sat on the throne, every act of daily life—rising, resting, eating, drinking—required the Prince of Xuancheng's approval.
entries.literal: The Prince of Hailing, on the throne, in rising, resting, eating, and drinking—all consulted the Prince of Xuancheng before acting.

entries.zh: 嘗思食蒸魚菜，太官令答無錄公命，竟不與。
entries.en: Once he craved steamed fish and greens; the palace provisioner answered that without the Chief Recorder's command nothing could be served, and he went without.
entries.literal: He once wished to eat steamed fish and vegetables; the Grand Provisioner replied that without the Chief Recorder's order, in the end it was not given.

entries.zh: 辛亥，皇太后令曰：「嗣主沖幼，庶政多昧；
entries.en: On xinhai the Empress Dowager issued an edict: "The heir to the throne is young, and public affairs are beyond him;
entries.literal: On day xinhai, the Empress Dowager's order said: "The successor ruler is young and tender, and the many affairs of government are obscure;

entries.zh: 且早嬰尪疾，弗克負荷。
entries.en: moreover he has been frail from childhood and cannot bear the burden of rule.
entries.literal: moreover, from early youth he has been afflicted with wasting illness and cannot bear the burden.

entries.zh: 太傅宣城王，胤體宣皇，鐘慈太祖，宜入承寶命。
entries.en: Grand Tutor the Prince of Xuancheng, born of the imperial line and cherished by the founding emperor, should ascend and receive the Mandate.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor the Prince of Xuancheng, by blood-line the body of the Proclaimed Emperor, concentrating kindness from the Grand Ancestor, ought to enter and receive the precious mandate.

entries.zh: 帝可降封海陵王，吾當歸老別館。」
entries.en: Let the emperor be demoted to Prince Hailing; I shall retire to a separate palace."
entries.literal: The emperor may be demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing; I shall return to age in a separate lodge."

entries.zh: 且以宣城王為太祖第三子。
entries.en: The court also declared the Prince of Xuancheng to be the founding emperor's third son.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Xuancheng was treated as the Grand Ancestor's third son.

entries.zh: 癸亥，高宗即皇帝位，大赦，改元。
entries.en: On guihai Emperor Ming took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
entries.literal: On day guihai, the High Ancestor assumed the imperial position, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

entries.zh: 以太尉王敬則為大司馬，司空陳顯達為太尉，尚書令王晏加驃騎大將軍，左僕射徐孝嗣加中軍大將軍，中領軍蕭諶為領軍將軍。
entries.en: Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal, Chen Xianda Grand Commandant, Wang Yan Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Xu Xiaosi General of the Central Army, and Xiao Zhen Commander of the Palace Guards.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal; Minister of Works Chen Xianda was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was added as Rapid Cavalry Grand General; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Xiaosi was added as General of the Central Army; Central Palace Guard Commander Xiao Zhen was made Commander of the Palace Guards.

entries.zh: 度支尚書虞悰稱疾不陪位。
entries.en: Yu Song, Minister of Revenue, pleaded illness and did not attend the enthronement.
entries.literal: Minister of Revenue Yu Song claimed illness and did not attend the enthronement.

entries.zh: 帝以悰舊人，欲引參佐命，使王晏繼廢立事示悰。
entries.en: The emperor, knowing Song as an old associate, wished to enlist him in the new order and had Wang Yan recount the deposition and enthronement for his benefit.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Song was an old acquaintance, wished to draw him in to assist the mandate; he had Wang Yan continue the account of deposition and enthronement to show Song.

entries.zh: 悰曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以贊惟新乎！
entries.en: Song said: "Your Majesty is sage and brilliant, and the ministers serve with one accord—why borrow a worn-out old man for the renewal of the state!
entries.literal: Song said: "The ruler above is sagely and bright, the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—how could one borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal!

entries.zh: 不敢聞命！」
entries.en: I dare not accept such a command!"
entries.literal: dare not hear command!"

entries.zh: 因慟哭。
entries.en: And thereupon he broke into bitter weeping.
entries.literal: thereupon wailed in grief.

entries.zh: 朝議欲糾之，徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」
entries.en: The court debated punishing him; Xu Xiaosi said, "This, too, is a remnant of the ancient type who spoke straight to power."
entries.literal: court deliberation wished to impeach him, Xu Xiaosi said: "this also is antiquity's surviving straightness."

entries.zh: 乃止。
entries.en: And they desisted.
entries.literal: then stopped.

entries.zh: 帝與群臣宴會，詔功臣上酒。
entries.en: The emperor feasted with his ministers and ordered meritorious officials to offer toasts.
entries.literal: emperor with ministers banquet, ordered meritorious ministers offer wine.

entries.zh: 王晏等興席，謝瀹獨不起，曰：「陛下受命，應天順人；
entries.en: Wang Yan and the others rose from their seats; Xie Yue alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the Mandate, harmonizing with Heaven and following the people;
entries.literal: Wang Yan and others rose from seats, Xie Yue alone did not rise, said: "Your Majesty received Mandate, responded to Heaven followed people;

entries.zh: 王晏妄叨天功以為己力！」
entries.en: Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement!"
entries.literal: Wang Yan presumptuously usurps Heaven's merit as his own strength!"

entries.zh: 帝大笑，解之。
entries.en: The emperor laughed heartily and let the matter pass.
entries.literal: emperor great laugh, excused him.

entries.zh: 座罷，晏呼瀹共載還令省，欲相撫悅。
entries.en: When the banquet ended, Yan summoned Yue to ride back with him to the Ministry of Justice, hoping to win him over.
entries.literal: seats ended, Yan called Yue share carriage return to Ministry office, wished mutually to soothe and please.

entries.zh: 瀹正色曰：「君巢窟在何處！」
entries.en: Yue said with a stern face, "Where is your nest and den!"
entries.literal: Yue stern countenance said: "my lord's nest den at what place!"

entries.zh: 晏甚憚之。
entries.en: Yan was deeply intimidated by him.
entries.literal: Yan greatly feared him.

entries.zh: 通直散騎常侍劉芳，纘之族弟也，與給事黃門侍郎太原郭祚，皆以文學為帝所親禮，多引與講論及密議政事；
entries.en: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Fang, a clansman of Liu Zuan, and Supervisor of the Secretariat Guo Zuo of Taiyuan were both treated with intimate favor by the emperor for their literary learning; he often drew them into discussions and private deliberations on state affairs;
entries.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Fang, Zuan's clansman younger brother, with Supervisor of Secretariat Taiyuan Guo Zuo, all by literary learning by emperor intimately honored, often drawn into discussions and secret deliberations state affairs;

entries.zh: 大臣貴戚皆以為疏己，怏怏有不平之色。
entries.en: Great ministers and noble kin all felt themselves estranged and showed discontent on their faces.
entries.literal: great ministers noble kin all considered estranged themselves, resentful had discontented expressions.

entries.zh: 帝使給事黃門侍郎陸覬私諭之曰：「至尊但欲廣知古事，詢訪前世法式耳，終不親彼而相疏也。」
entries.en: The emperor had Supervisor Lu Guan privately instruct them, saying, "His Majesty only wishes to broaden his knowledge of antiquity and inquire into institutions of former ages—that is all; he will never favor them and distance you."
entries.literal: emperor made Supervisor Lu Guan privately instruct them said: "Sovereign only wishes broaden knowledge ancient matters, inquire former ages institutions, that is all, ultimately will not favor them and estrange you."

entries.zh: 眾意乃稍解。
entries.en: The crowd's resentment gradually eased.
entries.literal: crowd's resentment then slightly eased.

entries.zh: 覬，□之子也。
entries.en: Guan was the son of [name lost in the source].
entries.literal: Guan, □'s son.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第139卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 139
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 139

entries.zh: 魏陳留公主寡居，僕射高肇、秦州刺史張彝皆欲尚之，公主許彝而不許肇。
entries.en: The Chenliu princess of Wei was a widow. Grand chancellor Gao Zhao and Zhang Yi, governor of Qin province, both sought to marry her. She favored Zhang Yi and rejected Gao Zhao.
entries.literal: The Princess of Chenliu of Wei lived as a widow; Vice Director Gao Zhao and Governor of Qin Province Zhang Yi both wished to marry her; the Princess agreed to Yi but not to Zhao.

entries.zh: 肇怒，譖彝於魏主，彝坐沉廢累年。
entries.en: Gao Zhao, furious, denounced Zhang Yi to the Wei emperor, and Yi languished in disgrace for years.
entries.literal: Zhao was angry, slandered Yi before the Wei ruler; Yi on account of this was demoted and idle for many years.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第145卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 145
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 145

entries.zh: 二月，甲午，魏主尊彭城武宣王為文穆皇帝，廟號肅祖；
entries.en: In the second month, on jiawu, the Wei emperor posthumously elevated Prince Wuxuan of Pengcheng as Emperor Wenmu, with the temple name Suzu;
entries.literal: In the second month, on day jiawu, the Wei ruler honored the Prince of Pengcheng, posthumous name Wuxuan, as Emperor Wenmu, with temple name Suzu;

entries.zh: 母李妃為文穆皇后。
entries.en: His mother, Lady Li, was honored as Empress Wenmu.
entries.literal: his mother, Consort Li, as Empress Wenmu.

entries.zh: 將遷神主於太廟，以高祖為伯考，大司馬兼錄尚書臨淮王彧表諫，以為：「漢高祖立太上皇廟於香街，光武祀南頓君於舂陵。
entries.en: As the court prepared to install their spirit tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and rank Emperor Gaozu as a collateral forebear, the Grand Marshal and acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, submitted a memorial of protest: "Emperor Gaozu of Han raised a temple to the Supreme Emperor on Fragrant Street, and Emperor Guangwu worshipped his father at Chunling.
entries.literal: When they were about to move the spirit tablets to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and treat Emperor Gaozu as an uncle in the patriline, the Grand Marshal and Acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, memorialized in protest, saying: "Emperor Gaozu of Han established the temple of the Supreme Emperor at Xiang Street, and Emperor Guangwu enshrined his father at Chunling.

entries.zh: 元帝之於光武，已疏絕服，猶身奉子道，入繼大宗。
entries.en: Between Emperor Yuan and Emperor Guangwu the mourning tie was already distant, yet Guangwu still personally kept a son's duty and entered the succession of the great lineage.
entries.literal: Between Emperor Yuan and Emperor Guangwu the bond of mourning was already severed, yet Guangwu still personally observed the son's rites and entered to succeed the great lineage.

entries.zh: 高祖德洽寰中，道超無外，肅祖雖勳格宇宙，猶北面為臣。
entries.en: Our Gaozu's virtue filled the realm and his Way surpassed all within the four seas; though Suzu's achievements spanned the cosmos, he still stood facing north as a subject.
entries.literal: Our Gaozu's virtue filled the realm and his Way surpassed all bounds; though Suzu's merit reached to heaven and earth, he still faced north as a subject.

entries.zh: 又，二後皆將配享，乃是君臣並筵，嫂叔同室，竊謂不可。」
entries.en: Moreover, both empresses are to share the altar—lord and minister would sit at one feast, sister-in-law and brother-in-law under one roof; this, I submit, cannot be allowed."
entries.literal: Moreover, both empresses are to receive joint sacrifice—this would set lord and minister at one mat and sister-in-law with brother-in-law in one chamber; I venture that it cannot be done."

entries.zh: 吏部尚書李神俊亦諫，不聽，彧又請去「帝」著「皇」，亦不聽。
entries.en: The Minister of Personnel, Li Shenjun, remonstrated as well, but the throne would not listen; Yuan Yu then asked that the title drop "emperor" and read only "august," and that too was refused.
entries.literal: The Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun also remonstrated, but they were not heeded; Yuan Yu again asked to drop the character "emperor" and use only "august," and this too was refused.

entries.zh: 辛丑，魏上黨王天穆及爾朱兆破邢杲於濟南，杲降，送洛陽，斬之。
entries.en: On xinchou, the Wei Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and Erzhu Zhao routed Xing Gao at Ji'nan; Gao surrendered, was sent to Luoyang, and beheaded.
entries.literal: On day xinchou, the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and Erzhu Zhao of Wei defeated Xing Gao at Ji'nan; Gao surrendered, was sent to Luoyang, and executed.

entries.zh: 兆，榮之從子也。
entries.en: Zhao was a nephew of Erzhu Rong.
entries.literal: Zhao was a nephew of Rong.

entries.zh: 顥使黃門郎祖瑩作書遺魏主曰：「朕泣請梁朝，誓在復恥，正欲問罪於爾朱，出卿於桎梏。
entries.en: Hao had the Yellow Gate Gentleman Zu Ying draft a letter to the Wei emperor: "I wept and begged the Liang court, swearing to wipe away disgrace, meaning only to call Erzhu to account and free you from bonds.
entries.literal: Hao had the Yellow Gate Gentleman Zu Ying draft a letter to the Wei ruler, saying: "I wept and begged the Liang court, swearing to wipe away shame, intending only to call Erzhu to account and release you from fetters.

entries.zh: 卿托命豺狼，委身虎口，假獲民地，本是榮物，固非卿有。
entries.en: You entrusted your life to wolves and cast your body into a tiger's maw; the people's land you hold was always Rong's prize and was never truly yours.
entries.literal: You entrusted your life to wolves and tigers and cast your body into the tiger's maw; the people's land you seized in name was originally Rong's spoil and was never yours.

entries.zh: 今國家隆替，在卿與我。
entries.en: Now whether the state rises or falls lies between you and me.
entries.literal: Now the state's rise or fall lies between you and me.

entries.zh: 若天道助順，則皇魏再興；
entries.en: If Heaven aids the righteous, great Wei will rise again;
entries.literal: If Heaven's Way aids the righteous, the great Wei will rise again;

entries.zh: 脫或不然，在榮為福，於卿為禍。
entries.en: if not, fortune for Rong, disaster for you.
entries.literal: if not, for Rong it is fortune, for you disaster.

entries.zh: 卿宜三復，富貴可保。」
entries.en: Think thrice, and wealth and rank may yet be kept."
entries.literal: Consider thrice, and wealth and rank may be preserved."

entries.zh: 魏以侍中、車騎將軍、尚書右僕射爾朱世隆為使持節、行台僕射、大將軍、相州刺史，鎮鄴城。
entries.en: Wei appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Erzhu Shilong bearer of the staff, acting mobile-staff vice director, grand general, and inspector of Xiangzhou, to hold Ye city.
entries.literal: Wei made the Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Erzhu Shilong Bearer of the Staff, Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the mobile staff, Grand General, and regional inspector of Xiang, to garrison Ye city.

entries.zh: 魏主之出也，單騎而去，侍衛後宮皆案堵如故。
entries.en: When the Wei emperor fled, he rode off alone; the palace guard and inner quarters remained undisturbed.
entries.literal: When the Wei ruler departed, he went off with a single horse; the palace guard and inner quarters all remained undisturbed as before.

entries.zh: 顥一旦得之，號令己出，四方人情想其風政。
entries.en: Once Hao held power, his orders went forth and people everywhere looked to his rule.
entries.literal: Once Hao had it in a day, his orders issued forth, and popular sentiment everywhere looked to his governance.

entries.zh: 而顥自謂天授，遽有驕怠之志。
entries.en: But Hao, believing Heaven had handed him the throne, soon grew arrogant and careless.
entries.literal: But Hao, thinking Heaven had granted it to him, abruptly took on an arrogant, negligent will.

entries.zh: 宿昔賓客近習，鹹見寵待，干擾政事，日夜縱酒，不恤軍國，所從南兵，陵暴市裡，朝野失望。
entries.en: Old clients and close attendants were showered with favor and meddled in government; he drank day and night and neglected army and state; the southern soldiers who followed him bullied the markets, and court and countryside lost heart.
entries.literal: His old guests and close attendants were all favored and pampered, meddling in government affairs; he drank day and night without caring for army or state; the southern troops who followed him bullied the markets—court and countryside lost hope.

entries.zh: 高道穆兄子儒自洛陽出從魏主，魏主問洛中事，子儒曰：「顥敗在旦夕，不足憂也。」
entries.en: Gao Daomu's nephew Ru left Luoyang to join the Wei emperor; asked about Luo, Ru said, "Hao will fall within days—there is nothing to fear."
entries.literal: Gao Daomu's nephew Ru came out from Luoyang to join the Wei ruler; the Wei ruler asked about affairs in Luo, and Ru said: "Hao's defeat is a matter of days—nothing to worry about."

entries.zh: 爾朱榮聞魏主北出，即時馳傳見魏主於長子，行，且部分。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong, hearing the emperor had fled north, galloped by post to meet him at Changzi, marching and deploying as he went.
entries.literal: Erzhu Rong, hearing the Wei ruler had gone north, at once galloped by post to see the Wei ruler at Changzi, marching and deploying as he went.

entries.zh: 魏主即日南還，榮為前驅。
entries.en: That same day the Wei emperor turned south, with Rong in the vanguard.
entries.literal: That same day the Wei ruler turned south; Rong served as vanguard.

entries.zh: 旬日之間，兵眾大集，資糧器仗，相繼而至。
entries.en: Within ten days hosts massed, and grain, supplies, and arms arrived in steady streams.
entries.literal: Within ten days or so, troops massed in great numbers, and provisions, grain, and weapons arrived in succession.

entries.zh: 六月，壬午，魏大赦。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on renwu, Wei proclaimed a great amnesty.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on day renwu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 己丑，費穆至洛陽，顥引入，責以河陰之事而殺之。
entries.en: On jichou, Fei Mu reached Luoyang; Hao received him, blamed him for the massacre at Heyin, and executed him.
entries.literal: On day jichou, Fei Mu reached Luoyang; Hao brought him in, blamed him for the affair at Heyin, and killed him.

entries.zh: 顥使都督宗正珍孫與河內太守元襲據河內；
entries.en: Hao sent the commander Zongzheng Zhensun and the administrator of Henei, Yuan Xi, to hold Henei;
entries.literal: Hao sent the commander Zongzheng Zhensun and the Administrator of Henei, Yuan Xi, to hold Henei;

entries.zh: 爾朱榮攻之，上黨王天穆引兵會之，壬寅，拔其城，斬珍孫及襲。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong attacked them; the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, joined him; on renyin they stormed the city and beheaded Zhensun and Xi.
entries.literal: Erzhu Rong attacked them; the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, led troops to join him; on day renyin they took the city and beheaded Zhensun and Xi.

entries.zh: 榮既南下，並、肆不安，乃以爾朱天光為並、肆等九州行台，仍行并州事。
entries.en: After Rong marched south, Bing and Xi grew restless; he made Erzhu Tianguang mobile-staff director over nine provinces including Bing and Xi while still governing Bing.
entries.literal: Once Rong had marched south, Bing and Xi were unsettled; he therefore made Erzhu Tianguang mobile-staff director for nine provinces including Bing and Xi, while still conducting affairs of Bing province.

entries.zh: 天光至晉陽，部分約勒，所部皆安。
entries.en: Tianguang reached Jinyang, organized and disciplined his command, and all under him were pacified.
entries.literal: Tianguang reached Jinyang, deployed and restrained his command, and all under him were pacified.

entries.zh: 魏北海王顥既得志，密與臨淮王彧、安豐王延明謀叛梁；
entries.en: Once the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, had achieved his aim, he secretly plotted to turn against Liang with the Prince of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and the Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming;
entries.literal: Once the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, had achieved his aim, he secretly plotted rebellion against Liang with Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming;

entries.zh: 以事難未平，藉陳慶之兵力，故外同內異，言多猜忌。
entries.en: because the realm was not yet settled he still needed Chen Qingzhi's troops; outwardly they agreed, inwardly they doubted one another.
entries.literal: because affairs were not yet settled, he relied on Chen Qingzhi's military strength; outwardly they agreed, inwardly they differed, and their words were full of suspicion.

entries.zh: 慶之亦密為之備，說顥曰：「今遠來至此，未服者尚多，彼若知吾虛實，連兵四合，將何以御之！
entries.en: Qingzhi also quietly prepared and told Hao, "We have marched far, and many here are still unsubmissive; if they learn how few we are and link armies on every side, how will we hold them off?
entries.literal: Qingzhi also secretly made preparations and said to Hao: "Having come far to this place, many are still unsubmissive; if they learn our true strength and link armies on four sides, how will we defend against them!

entries.zh: 宜啟天子，更請精兵，並敕諸州，有南人沒此者悉須部送。」
entries.en: You should inform the Son of Heaven and ask for more picked troops, and order every province to send here all southerners it holds under arms."
entries.literal: You should inform the Son of Heaven and request more picked troops, and also order the provinces that any southerners captured here must all be sent under command."

entries.zh: 顥欲從之，延明曰：「慶之兵不出數千，已自難制；
entries.en: Hao meant to agree; Yanming said, "Qingzhi commands only a few thousand men and is already hard to control;
entries.literal: Hao wished to follow this; Yanming said: "Qingzhi's troops number only a few thousand and are already hard to control;

entries.zh: 今更增其眾，寧肯復為人用乎！
entries.en: if you swell his host now, will he still let others command him?
entries.literal: if you now increase his host, will he consent to be used by others again!

entries.zh: 大權一去，動息由人，魏之宗廟，於斯墜矣。」
entries.en: Once great power passes from your hands, every move depends on others—the Wei ancestral temple will topple with it."
entries.literal: Once great power is gone, every move depends on others—the ancestral temple of Wei will fall at this stroke."

entries.zh: 顥乃不用慶之言。
entries.en: Hao therefore ignored Qingzhi's advice.
entries.literal: Hao therefore did not adopt Qingzhi's words.

entries.zh: 又慮慶之密啟，乃表於上曰：「今河北、河南一時克定，唯爾朱榮尚敢跋扈，臣與慶之自能擒討。
entries.en: Fearing Qingzhi might report him in secret, he memorialized the throne: "Hebei and Henan are for the moment pacified; only Erzhu Rong still dares to swagger—your servant and Qingzhi can seize him ourselves.
entries.literal: He also feared Qingzhi would secretly report him, and therefore memorialized the throne: "Now Hebei and Henan are for the moment pacified; only Erzhu Rong still dares to be overbearing—your servant and Qingzhi can capture and punish him ourselves.

entries.zh: 州郡新服，正須綏撫，不宜更復加兵，搖動百姓。」
entries.en: The provinces have only just submitted and need soothing rule; we must not add more troops and unsettle the people."
entries.literal: The provinces and commanderies have newly submitted and need soothing governance; we should not add more troops and shake the people."

entries.zh: 上乃詔諸軍繼進者皆停於境上。
entries.en: The Liang emperor therefore ordered every army meant to follow up to halt at the borders.
entries.literal: The Emperor therefore ordered all armies that were to follow up to halt at the borders.

entries.zh: 爾朱榮與顥相持於河上。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong and Hao faced each other along the river.
