entries.literal: Erzhu Rong and Hao faced each other along the river.

entries.zh: 慶之守北中城，顥自據南岸；
entries.en: Qingzhi held North Central Fort while Hao held the south bank;
entries.literal: Qingzhi held North Central Fort; Hao himself held the south bank;

entries.zh: 慶之三日十一戰，殺傷甚眾。
entries.en: in three days Qingzhi fought eleven battles, with heavy casualties on both sides.
entries.literal: in three days Qingzhi fought eleven battles, with many killed and wounded.

entries.zh: 有夏州義士為顥守河中渚，陰與榮通謀，求破橋立效，榮引兵赴之。
entries.en: A loyalist from Xia province held a mid-river islet for Hao, secretly treated with Rong, and offered to break the bridge; Rong marched to support him.
entries.literal: A righteous man of Xia province held an islet in mid-river for Hao, secretly communicated with Rong, and asked to break the bridge and show merit; Rong led troops to go to him.

entries.zh: 及橋破，榮應接不逮，顥悉屠之，榮悵然失望。
entries.en: When the bridge fell, Rong could not arrive in time; Hao slaughtered the loyalists, and Rong was bitterly disappointed.
entries.literal: When the bridge was broken, Rong could not come up in time; Hao slaughtered them all, and Rong was deeply disappointed.

entries.zh: 又以安豐王延明緣河固守，而北軍無船可渡，議欲還北，更圖後舉。
entries.en: Prince of Anfeng Yanming held the river line, and the northern army had no boats; they debated retreating north to try again later.
entries.literal: Moreover Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, held the line along the river, while the northern army had no boats to cross; they discussed returning north and planning again later.

entries.zh: 黃門郎楊侃曰：「大王發并州之日，已知夏州義士之謀指來應之邪？
entries.en: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Yang Kan said, "When you marched from Bing province, did you already know the Xia loyalists meant to answer you?
entries.literal: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Yang Kan said: "When the Great King set out from Bing province, did you already know the Xia loyalists' plan was to come answer you?

entries.zh: 為欲廣施經略匡復帝室乎？
entries.en: Or did you mean to deploy your hosts and restore the imperial house?
entries.literal: Or did you mean broadly to deploy strategy and restore the imperial house?

entries.zh: 夫用兵者，何嘗不散而更合，瘡愈更戰；
entries.en: In war, armies scatter and gather again, wounds heal and men fight again;
entries.literal: In warfare, has there ever been an army that did not scatter and reunite, or a wound that healed and then fought again;

entries.zh: 況今未有所損，豈可以一事不諧而眾謀頓廢乎！
entries.en: and we have not yet suffered real loss—how can one setback scrap the whole design?
entries.literal: moreover we have not yet suffered loss—how can one setback make you abandon the whole plan!

entries.zh: 今四方顒顒，視公此舉；
entries.en: Now the four quarters watch eagerly what you will do;
entries.literal: Now the four quarters watch eagerly what you do;

entries.zh: 若未有所成，遽復引歸，民情失望，各懷去就，勝負所在，未可知也。
entries.en: if you achieve nothing and pull back, hearts will fail, men will think of leaving, and victory is anyone's guess.
entries.literal: if you achieve nothing and hastily withdraw, popular hearts will lose hope, each will think of leaving, and where victory lies is unknown.

entries.zh: 不若征發民材，多為桴筏，間以舟楫，緣河布列，數百里中，皆為渡勢，首尾既遠，使顥不知所防，一旦得渡，必立大功。」
entries.en: Better to levy timber, build rafts and boats, and array crossings for hundreds of li—head and tail far apart so Hao cannot guess where we will strike; cross once, and merit is certain."
entries.literal: Better to levy civilian timber, make many rafts, add boats here and there, array along the river for hundreds of li, all as crossing positions; with head and tail far apart, Hao will not know where to guard—once we cross in a day, great merit is certain."

entries.zh: 高道穆曰：「今乘輿飄蕩，主憂臣辱。
entries.en: Gao Daomu said, "The imperial carriage drifts in peril—the ruler grieves and ministers are shamed.
entries.literal: Gao Daomu said: "Now the imperial carriage drifts in peril—the ruler grieves and ministers are shamed.

entries.zh: 大王擁百萬之眾，輔天子而令諸侯，若分兵造筏，所在散渡，指掌可克；
entries.en: You command a million men, assisting the Son of Heaven to command the lords—divide troops, build rafts, and cross piecemeal, and victory is at hand;
entries.literal: Great King, you hold a host of a million, assisting the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords—if you divide troops to build rafts and cross here and there, it can be taken in a gesture;

entries.zh: 奈何捨之北歸，使顥復得完聚，徵兵天下！
entries.en: why turn north and let Hao gather strength and levy the realm again!
entries.literal: why abandon this and return north, letting Hao gather his strength again and levy troops throughout the realm!

entries.zh: 此所謂養虺成蛇，悔無及矣。」
entries.en: That is to nurture a viper you will regret forever."
entries.literal: This is what they call nurturing a viper to your sorrow, with regret too late."

entries.zh: 榮曰：「楊黃門已陳此策，當相與議之。」
entries.en: Rong said, "Yellow Gate Yang has already offered this plan; we shall discuss it together."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Yellow Gate Yang has already set forth this plan; we should deliberate it together."

entries.zh: 劉靈助言於榮曰：「不出十日，河南必平。」
entries.en: Liu Lingzhu told Rong, "Within ten days Henan will be pacified."
entries.literal: Liu Lingzhu said to Rong: "Within ten days Henan will surely be pacified."

entries.zh: 伏波將軍正平楊心剽與其族居馬渚，自言有小船數艘，求為鄉導。
entries.en: The General Who Subdues Waves, Yang Xin of Zhengping, lived with his clan at Horse Ford and offered several small boats as guide.
entries.literal: The General Who Subdues Waves, Yang Xin of Zhengping, lived with his clan at Ma islet and said he had several small boats, asking to serve as guide.

entries.zh: 戊辰，榮命車騎將軍爾朱兆與大都督賀拔勝縛材為筏，自馬渚西硤石夜渡，襲擊顥子領軍將軍冠受，擒之；
entries.en: On wuchen, Rong ordered Erzhu Zhao and the grand commander Heba Sheng to bind rafts; from Horse Ford they crossed by night at Xiashi, struck Hao's son and commander-in-chief Guan Shou, and captured him;
entries.literal: On day wuchen, Rong ordered the Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Erzhu Zhao and the Grand Commander Heba Sheng to bind timber as rafts; from Ma Ford they crossed west at Xiashi by night, struck Hao's son and commander-in-chief Guan Shou, and captured him;

entries.zh: 安豐王延明之眾聞之，大潰。
entries.en: when Prince of Anfeng Yanming's host heard this, it broke in rout.
entries.literal: when the host of Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, heard this, it collapsed in great rout.

entries.zh: 顥失據，帥麾下數百騎南走，陳慶之收步騎數千，結陳東還，顥所得諸城，一時復降於魏。
entries.en: Hao lost his footing and fled south with a few hundred horsemen; Qingzhi gathered several thousand foot and horse, formed ranks, and marched east; the cities Hao had taken at once submitted again to Wei.
entries.literal: Hao lost his footing, led several hundred horsemen south in flight; Chen Qingzhi gathered several thousand foot and horse, formed battle lines, and marched east; the cities Hao had taken all at once submitted again to Wei.

entries.zh: 爾朱榮自追陳慶之，會嵩高水漲，慶之軍士死散略盡，乃削鬚髮為沙門，間行出汝陰，還建康，猶以功除右衛將軍，封永興縣侯。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong himself pursued Qingzhi; the Songgao River flooded, and Qingzhi's men died or scattered almost to the last; he shaved his head as a monk, slipped out through Ruyin, returned to Jiankang, and was still made Defender-General of the Right and Marquis of Yongxing for his merit.
entries.literal: Erzhu Rong himself pursued Chen Qingzhi; the Songgao River rose in flood, and Qingzhi's soldiers died or scattered until almost none remained; he shaved his beard and hair to become a monk, slipped out by hidden paths through Ruyin, returned to Jiankang, and was still made Defender-General of the Right and Marquis of Yongxing county for his merit.

entries.zh: 中軍大都督兼領軍大將軍楊津入宿殿中，掃灑宮庭，封閉府庫，出迎魏主於北邙，流涕謝罪，帝慰勞之。
entries.en: Grand Commander of the Central Army and concurrent Defender-General Yang Jin lodged in the palace, swept the courts, sealed the treasuries, went out to welcome the Wei emperor at Northern Mang, wept, and apologized; the emperor comforted him.
entries.literal: The Grand Commander of the Central Army and concurrent Defender-General Yang Jin entered to lodge in the palace hall, swept the palace courts, sealed the treasuries and storehouses, went out to welcome the Wei ruler at Northern Mang, wept and apologized for his fault; the Emperor comforted and encouraged him.

entries.zh: 庚午，帝入居華林園，大赦。
entries.en: On gengwu, the emperor entered the Hualin Garden and proclaimed a great amnesty.
entries.literal: On day gengwu, the Emperor entered and dwelt in the Hualin Garden and proclaimed a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 以爾朱兆為車騎大將軍、儀同三司，北來軍士及隨賀文武諸立義者加五級，河北報事之官及河南立義者加二級。
entries.en: Erzhu Zhao was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and bearer of the Three Similitudes; northern soldiers and all who had joined the righteous rising gained five ranks; reporters from Hebei and risers in Henan gained two.
entries.literal: Erzhu Zhao was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Bearer of the Three Similitudes; northern soldiers and all civil and military who had joined the righteous cause received five grades of promotion; officials who reported from Hebei and those who rose in Henan received two grades.

entries.zh: 壬申，加大丞相榮天柱大將軍，增封通前二十萬戶。
entries.en: On renshen, Grand Chancellor Rong was further made Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar, his fief increased by two hundred thousand households counting prior grants.
entries.literal: On day renshen, the Grand Chancellor Rong was further made Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar, with fief increased by two hundred thousand households including previous grants.

entries.zh: 甲戌，魏以上黨王天穆為太宰，城陽王徽為大司馬兼太尉。
entries.en: On jiaxu, Wei made the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Grand Preceptor, and the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Grand Marshal and concurrent Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: On day jiaxu, Wei made the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Grand Preceptor, and the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Grand Marshal concurrent Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 乙亥，魏主宴勞爾朱榮、上黨王天穆及北來督將於都亭，出宮人三百，繒錦雜彩數萬匹，班賜有差，凡受元顥爵賞階復者，悉追奪之。
entries.en: On yihai, the Wei emperor feasted Erzhu Rong, Yuan Tianmu, and the northern commanders at the Capital Pavilion; three hundred palace women attended, and tens of thousands of rolls of silk were given in graded gifts; everyone who had taken rank or reward from Yuan Hao had it stripped away.
entries.literal: On day yihai, the Wei ruler feasted and rewarded Erzhu Rong, the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and the northern commanders at the Capital Pavilion; three hundred palace women came forth, and tens of thousands of rolls of silk and brocade of mixed colors were distributed in graded gifts; all who had received ranks, rewards, and promotions from Yuan Hao had them seized back.

entries.zh: 魏爾朱榮使大都督尖山侯淵討韓樓於薊，配卒甚少，騎止七百。
entries.en: Erzhu Rong sent Grand Commander Hou Yuan, Marquis of Jianshan, to campaign against Han Lou at Ji with very few men—only seven hundred horsemen.
entries.literal: Erzhu Rong of Wei sent the Grand Commander, Hou Yuan, Marquis of Jianshan, to campaign against Han Lou at Ji, with very few assigned troops—only seven hundred horsemen.

entries.zh: 或以為言，榮曰：「侯淵臨機設變，是其所長；
entries.en: Some objected; Rong said, "Hou Yuan adapts at the moment—that is his strength;
entries.literal: Some spoke of this; Rong said: "Hou Yuan adapts to the moment at hand—that is his strength;

entries.zh: 若總大眾，未必能用。
entries.en: give him a great host and he may not use it well.
entries.literal: if he commanded a great host, he might not be able to use it.

entries.zh: 今以此眾擊此賊，必能取之。」
entries.en: With this force against that bandit, he will surely take him."
entries.literal: Now with this force to strike this bandit, he will surely take him."

entries.zh: 淵遂廣張軍聲，多設供具，親帥數百騎深入樓境。
entries.en: Yuan spread word of a great army, set out lavish supplies, and personally led several hundred horsemen deep into Lou's territory.
entries.literal: Yuan therefore greatly spread word of his army's strength, set out many supplies, and personally led several hundred horsemen deep into Lou's territory.

entries.zh: 去薊百餘里，值賊帥陳周馬步萬餘，淵潛伏以乘其背，大破之，虜其卒五千餘人。
entries.en: A hundred li from Ji he met the bandit commander Chen Zhou with more than ten thousand foot and horse; Yuan ambushed his rear, routed him, and captured more than five thousand men.
entries.literal: More than a hundred li from Ji, he met the bandit commander Chen Zhou with more than ten thousand foot and horse; Yuan lay in ambush and struck his rear, routing him greatly and capturing more than five thousand of his soldiers.

entries.zh: 尋還其馬仗，縱令入城，左右諫曰：「既獲賊眾，何為復資遣之？」
entries.en: He then returned their horses and arms and let them enter the city; his officers protested, "You have captured these men—why send them back?"
entries.literal: Soon he returned their horses and weapons and let them enter the city; those at his side remonstrated: "Having captured the bandit host, why release them again?"

entries.zh: 淵曰：「我兵既少，不可力戰，須為奇計以離間之，乃可克也。」
entries.en: Yuan said, "Our troops are too few for a straight fight; we need a stratagem to divide them—that is how we win."
entries.literal: Yuan said: "Our troops are few and cannot fight by force; we must use a stratagem to divide them—only then can we conquer."

entries.zh: 淵度其已至，遂帥騎夜進，昧旦，叩其城門。
entries.en: When he judged they had entered the city, he led his horsemen forward by night and at dawn knocked on the gates.
entries.literal: When Yuan judged they had arrived, he led his horsemen forward by night; at dawn he knocked on the city gates.

entries.zh: 韓樓果疑降卒為淵內應，遂走；
entries.en: Han Lou suspected the returned prisoners were Yuan's agents inside the walls and fled;
entries.literal: Han Lou indeed suspected the surrendered soldiers were Yuan's inner response and fled;

entries.zh: 追擒之，幽州平。
entries.en: they pursued, captured him, and You province was pacified.
entries.literal: they pursued and captured him, and You province was pacified.

entries.zh: 以淵為平州刺史，鎮范陽。
entries.en: Yuan was made inspector of Ping and garrisoned Fanyang.
entries.literal: Yuan was made regional inspector of Ping and garrisoned Fanyang.

entries.zh: 先是，魏使征東將軍劉靈助兼尚書僕射，慰勞幽州流民於濮陽頓丘，因帥流民北還，與侯淵共滅韓樓；
entries.en: Earlier Wei had sent General Who Conquers the East Liu Lingzhu, concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, to comfort You refugees at Dunqiu in Puyang; he led them north, joined Yuan, and destroyed Han Lou;
entries.literal: Earlier, Wei had sent the General Who Conquers the East, Liu Lingzhu, concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, to comfort and encourage the displaced people of You province at Dunqiu in Puyang; he therefore led the displaced north, joined Yuan in destroying Han Lou;

entries.zh: 仍以靈助行幽州事，加車騎將軍，又為幽、平、營、安四州行台。
entries.en: then made Lingzhu govern You, added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and made him mobile-staff director over You, Ping, Ying, and An.
entries.literal: and further made Lingzhu conduct affairs of You province, added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and also made him mobile-staff director of You, Ping, Ying, and An provinces.

entries.zh: 万俟丑奴攻魏東秦州，拔之，殺刺史高子朗。
entries.en: Moqi Chounu attacked Wei's Eastern Qin province, took it, and killed the inspector Gao Zilang.
entries.literal: Moqi Chounu attacked Eastern Qin province in Wei, took it, and killed the regional inspector Gao Zilang.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第153卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 153
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 153

entries.zh: 爾朱仲遠攻西兗州，丁丑，拔之，擒刺史王衍。
entries.en: Erzhu Zhongyuan attacked Western Yanzhou. On dingchou he captured it and seized Inspector Wang Yan.
entries.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan attacked Western Yanzhou. On dingchou he took it and captured the inspector Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 衍，蕭之兄子也。
entries.en: Yan was the son of Xiao's elder brother.
entries.literal: Yan was a nephew of Xiao by his elder brother.

entries.zh: 癸未，敬宗以右衛將軍賀拔勝為東征都督。
entries.en: On guiwei Emperor Xiaozhuang made Right Guard General Heba Sheng commander of the eastern campaign.
entries.literal: On guiwei Jingzong appointed Right Guard General Heba Sheng eastern campaign commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 壬辰，又以鄭先護兼尚書左僕射為行台，與勝共討仲遠。
entries.en: On renchen he also named Zheng Xianhu, who concurrently served as left vice director of the secretariat, mobile headquarters commissioner, to join Sheng against Zhongyuan.
entries.literal: On renchen he also made Zheng Xianhu, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, mobile headquarters commissioner, to join Sheng in attacking Zhongyuan.

entries.zh: 戊戌，詔罷魏蘭根行台，以定州刺史薛曇尚兼尚書，為北道行台。
entries.en: On wuxu an edict dissolved Wei Langen's mobile headquarters and made Dingzhou inspector Xue Tanshang, concurrently a secretariat director, northern-route mobile headquarters commissioner.
entries.literal: On wuxu an edict abolished Wei Langen's mobile headquarters and made Dingzhou Inspector Xue Tanshang, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, northern-route mobile headquarters commissioner.

entries.zh: 鄭先護疑賀拔勝，置之營外。
entries.en: Zheng Xianhu distrusted Heba Sheng and posted him outside the camp.
entries.literal: Zheng Xianhu distrusted Heba Sheng and kept him outside the camp.

entries.zh: 庚子，勝與仲遠戰於滑台東，兵敗，降於仲遠。
entries.en: On gengzi Sheng met Zhongyuan east of Huatai, lost, and surrendered to him.
entries.literal: On gengzi Sheng fought Zhongyuan east of Huatai, was defeated, and surrendered to Zhongyuan.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第154卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 154
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 154

entries.zh: 高祖武皇帝十五大同十一年（
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang, fifteenth year of Datong (
entries.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, fifteenth year of the Datong era (

entries.zh: 乙丑，公元五四五年）
entries.en: yichou, AD 545)
entries.literal: yichou, 545 CE)

entries.zh: 臣光曰：梁高祖之不終也，宜哉！
entries.en: Sima Guang comments: That Liang Gaozu did not finish his course was fitting!
entries.literal: Subject Guang says: Liang High Ancestor's not finishing his course—was it not fitting!

entries.zh: 夫人主聽納之失，在於叢脞；
entries.en: A ruler's fault in listening lies in clutter;
entries.literal: The fault of a ruler in listening and accepting lies in clutter;

entries.zh: 人臣獻替之病，在於煩碎。
entries.en: ministers' fault in remonstrance lies in fineness.
entries.literal: the illness of ministers in offering and replacing lies in fineness.

entries.zh: 是以明主守要道以御萬機之本，忠臣陳大體以格君心之非。
entries.en: The enlightened ruler keeps the essential way to master affairs; the loyal minister states the great body to correct the ruler's heart.
entries.literal: Therefore the enlightened ruler keeps the essential way to master the root of ten thousand affairs; the loyal minister states the great body to correct what is wrong in the ruler's heart.

entries.zh: 故身不勞而收功遠，言至約而為益大也。
entries.en: The body does not toil yet harvests far; words stay essential yet benefit is great.
entries.literal: Thus the body does not toil yet harvests achievement afar; words reach only the essential yet the benefit is great.

entries.zh: 觀夫賀琛之諫亦未至於切直，而高祖已赫然震怒，護其所短，矜其所長；
entries.en: He Chen's remonstrance was not even cutting, yet Gaozu was already enraged, guarding his faults and boasting his strengths;
entries.literal: Considering He Chen's remonstrance—it had not reached cutting directness—yet High Ancestor was already wrathfully shaken, guarding his shortcomings and boasting his strengths;

entries.zh: 詰貪暴之主名，問勞費之條目，困以難對之狀，責以必窮之辭。
entries.en: he demanded names of greedy lords, lists of waste, trapped him with unanswerable conditions, and blamed him into a corner.
entries.literal: he interrogated the names of greedy and violent lords, asked the items of labor and expense, trapped him with hard-to-answer conditions, and blamed him with words that must corner him.

entries.zh: 自以蔬食之儉為盛德，日昃之勤為至治，君道已備，無復可加，群臣箴規，舉不足聽。
entries.en: He took plain food for supreme virtue and sundown labor for perfect rule; in his mind the Way was complete and remonstrance worthless.
entries.literal: He took vegetable eating as supreme virtue and working until sundown as utmost governance; ruler's way was already complete, nothing more could be added; ministers' admonitions were altogether not worth hearing.

entries.zh: 如此，則自餘切直之言過於琛者，誰敢進哉！
entries.en: Who then would dare speak blunter words than Chen!
entries.literal: Thus—who would dare advance blunt words sharper than Chen!

entries.zh: 由是奸佞居前而不見，大謀顛錯而不知，名辱身危，覆邦絕祀，為千古所閔笑，豈不哀哉！
entries.en: Treacherous men stood before him unseen; great plans failed unknown; disgraced, endangered, state lost, sacrifices ended—mocked for ages: pitiful!
entries.literal: Hence treacherous flatterers stood before him unseen, great plans toppled and erred unknown; name disgraced, body endangered, state overturned, sacrifices cut off—mocked for a thousand years: is it not pitiful!

entries.zh: 上年高，諸子心不相下，互相猜忌。
entries.en: The Liang emperor was old; his sons would not yield to one another and suspected one another.
entries.literal: The emperor was advanced in years; his sons' hearts would not yield to one another, and they suspected one another.

entries.zh: 邵陵王綸為丹楊尹，湘東王繹在江州，武陵王紀在益州，皆權侔人主；
entries.en: Prince Lun of Shaoling held Danyang, Prince Yi of Xiangdong Jiangzhou, Prince Ji of Wuling Yizhou—each with power like a sovereign;
entries.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling was governor of Danyang, Prince Yi of Xiangdong was in Jiangzhou, Prince Ji of Wuling in Yizhou—all with power equal to a sovereign;

entries.zh: 太子綱惡之，常選精兵以衛東宮。
entries.en: Crown Prince Gang hated this and kept picked troops to guard the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: the Crown Prince Gang hated this and constantly chose picked troops to guard the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 八月，以綸為南徐州刺史。
entries.en: In the eighth month, Lun was made inspector of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Lun was made inspector of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 上為孝教慈恭儉，博學能文，陰陽、卜筮、騎射、聲律、草隸、圍棋，無不精妙。
entries.en: The emperor was filial, kind, respectful, and frugal, broadly learned and skilled in writing; yin-yang, divination, riding, archery, music, chess, clerical script, and go—none beyond him.
entries.literal: The emperor was filial, taught kindness, respectful and frugal, broadly learned and able in writing; yin-yang, divination, riding, archery, pitch, chess, clerical script, and go—none not exquisitely skilled.

entries.zh: 勤於政務，冬月四更竟，即起視事，執筆觸寒，手為皴裂。
entries.en: He was diligent: in winter he worked until the fourth watch and rose again; in the cold his hands cracked on the brush.
entries.literal: Diligent in government: in winter he finished at the fourth watch and rose to handle affairs; holding the brush in the cold, his hands cracked.

entries.zh: 自天監中用釋氏法，長齋斷魚肉，日止一食，惟菜羹，糲飯而已，或遇事繁，日移中則嗽口以過。
entries.en: From Tianjian he used Buddhist practice—long fasts without meat, one meal of vegetable broth and coarse rice; busy days he rinsed his mouth past noon and passed.
entries.literal: From the Tianjian era he used Buddhist methods, long fasts without fish or meat, one meal a day of only vegetable broth and coarse rice; when affairs were numerous, past midday he rinsed his mouth and passed.

entries.zh: 身衣布衣，木綿皁帳，一冠三載，一衾二年，後宮貴妃以下，衣不曳地。
entries.en: He wore cloth, cotton bedding, black curtains; one cap three years, one quilt two years; consorts and below wore hems that did not touch the ground.
entries.literal: He wore cloth himself, cotton and black curtains; one cap three years, one quilt two years; consorts and below did not trail the ground in dress.

entries.zh: 性不飲酒，非宗廟祭祀、大饗宴及諸法事，未嘗作樂。
entries.en: He did not drink; except for temple sacrifice, great feasts, and rites, he never had music.
entries.literal: By nature he did not drink; except for ancestral temple sacrifice, great feasts, and legal rites, he never made music.

entries.zh: 雖居暗室，恆理衣冠，小坐盛暑，未嘗褰袒。
entries.en: Even in a dark room he dressed properly; in summer heat he never bared his shoulders.
entries.literal: Even in a dark room he always arranged cap and robes; in small sessions even in great heat he never bared his shoulders.

entries.zh: 對內豎小臣，如遇大賓。
entries.en: Toward eunuchs and minor servants he was as toward great guests.
entries.literal: Toward inner attendants and minor servants he was as toward great guests.

entries.zh: 然優假士人太過，牧守多浸漁百姓，使者干擾郡縣。
entries.en: Yet he favored scholars too much; governors often preyed on the people; envoys harassed the districts.
entries.literal: Yet he favored scholars too much; governors and magistrates often soaked the people; envoys harassed commanderies and counties.

entries.zh: 又好親任小人，頗復苛察。
entries.en: He also liked to trust petty men and was harsh in scrutiny.
entries.literal: He also liked to trust petty men personally and was rather harsh in scrutiny.

entries.zh: 多造塔廟，公私費損。
entries.en: He built many pagodas and temples at great public and private cost.
entries.literal: He built many pagodas and temples; public and private expenses were harmed.

entries.zh: 江南久安，風俗奢靡。
entries.en: The south had long been at peace; customs had grown extravagant.
entries.literal: The south had been long at peace; customs were extravagant.

entries.zh: 故琛啟及之。
entries.en: Therefore Chen's memorial touched on it.
entries.literal: Therefore Chen's memorial touched on it.

entries.zh: 上惡其觸實，故怒。
entries.en: The emperor hated that it struck truth, and was angry.
entries.literal: The emperor hated that it struck truth, and so was angry.

entries.zh: 上敦尚文雅，疏簡刑法，自公卿大臣，鹹不以鞫獄為意。
entries.en: He honored letters and was light on penal law; from ministers down, none cared about judging crime.
entries.literal: The emperor honored literature and was sparing with penal law; from dukes and ministers down, none took criminal judgment as their concern.

entries.zh: 奸吏招權弄法，貨賂成市，枉濫者多。
entries.en: Crafty clerks twisted law; bribes were a market; the wrongly punished were many.
entries.literal: Crafty clerks wielded power and twisted law; bribes formed a market; the wrongly punished were many.

entries.zh: 大率二歲刑已上歲至五千人；
entries.en: Roughly five thousand a year were sentenced to two years or more and sent to the works;
entries.literal: Roughly, of punishments two years and up, five thousand a year reached the works;

entries.zh: 徙居作者具五任，其無任者著升械；
entries.en: those with full corvée went to labor; those without wore foot shackles;
entries.literal: those sent to labor had full corvée; those without corvée wore foot shackles;

entries.zh: 若疾病，權解之，是後囚徒或有優、劇。
entries.en: if ill, shackles were briefly removed—after that sentences could be light or heavy.
entries.literal: if ill, shackles were temporarily removed—after that prisoners might have light or heavy.

entries.zh: 時王侯子弟，多驕淫不法。
entries.en: Princes' and marquises' sons were mostly arrogant and lawless.
entries.literal: At the time princes and marquises' sons were mostly arrogant and lawless.

entries.zh: 上年老，厭於萬幾。
entries.en: The emperor was old and weary of government.
entries.literal: The emperor was old and weary of the ten thousand affairs.

entries.zh: 又專精佛戒，每斷重罪，則終日不懌；
entries.en: He devoted himself to Buddhist precepts; a heavy sentence displeased him all day;
entries.literal: He also devoted himself to Buddhist precepts; whenever he cut a heavy sentence he was displeased all day;

entries.zh: 或謀反逆，事覺，亦泣而宥之。
entries.en: even discovered rebellion he wept and pardoned.
entries.literal: even when rebellion was discovered, he wept and pardoned.

entries.zh: 由是王侯益橫，或白晝殺人於都街，或暮夜公行剽掠，有罪亡命者，匿於王家，有司不敢搜捕。
entries.en: Princes grew bolder; some killed in daylight on capital streets, plundered by night; fugitives hid in princes' houses and officials dared not search.
entries.literal: Thus princes and marquises grew more overbearing; some killed men in broad daylight on the capital streets, or at night openly plundered; criminals who fled hid in princes' houses and officials dared not search.

entries.zh: 上深知其弊，而溺於慈愛，不能禁也。
entries.en: He knew the evil yet drowned in kindness and could not forbid it.
entries.literal: The emperor knew the evil deeply yet drowned in kindness and could not forbid it.

entries.zh: 魏東陽王榮為瓜州刺史，與其婿鄧彥偕行。
entries.en: Western Wei's Prince of Dongyang, Rong, was governor of Guazhou and traveled with his son-in-law Deng Yan.
entries.literal: Western Wei Prince of Dongyang Rong was governor of Guazhou and traveled with his son-in-law Deng Yan.

entries.zh: 榮卒，瓜州首望表榮子康為刺史，彥殺康而奪其位。
entries.en: Rong died; Guazhou's leading clans nominated his son Kang as governor; Yan killed Kang and seized his post.
entries.literal: Rong died; the leading clans of Guazhou nominated Rong's son Kang as governor; Yan killed Kang and seized his place.

entries.zh: 魏不能討，因以彥為刺史，屢征不至，又南通吐谷渾。
entries.en: Western Wei could not punish him and made him governor; repeatedly summoned, he did not come, and also allied south with Tuyuhun.
entries.literal: Wei could not punish him and therefore made Yan governor; he was repeatedly summoned and did not come, and also opened south to Tuyuhun.

entries.zh: 丞相泰以道遠難於動眾，欲以計取之，以給事黃門侍郎申徽為河西大使，密令圖彥。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai, finding the road too far for an army, wished to take him by stratagem and made Shen Hui, Attendant of the Yellow Gate, western-route ambassador to plot against Yan in secret.
entries.literal: Chancellor Tai, because the road was far and hard to move the host, wished to take him by stratagem and made Attendant of the Yellow Gate Shen Hui western-route ambassador to plot against Yan secretly.

entries.zh: 徽以五十騎行，既至，止於賓館；
entries.en: Hui rode with fifty men; on arrival he lodged at the guest house;
entries.literal: Hui traveled with fifty riders; when he arrived he stopped at the guest lodge;

entries.zh: 彥見徽單使，不以為疑。
entries.en: Yan saw a lone envoy and did not suspect him.
entries.literal: Yan saw Hui as a lone envoy and did not suspect him.

entries.zh: 徽遣人微勸彥歸朝，彥不從；
entries.en: Hui secretly urged Yan to return to court; Yan refused;
entries.literal: Hui sent men secretly to urge Yan to return to court; Yan did not follow;

entries.zh: 徽又使贊成其留計，彥信之，遂來至館。
entries.en: Hui again had men support his plan to remain; Yan believed them and came to the lodge.
entries.literal: Hui again had men support his plan to stay; Yan believed them and came to the lodge.

entries.zh: 徽先與州主簿敦煌令狐整等密謀，執彥於坐，責而縛之；
entries.en: Hui had secretly plotted with the commandery recorder Linghu Zheng of Dunhuang and others; they seized Yan at the seat, reproached and bound him;
entries.literal: Hui had already secretly plotted with the commandery recorder Dunhuang Linghu Zheng and others; they seized Yan at the seat, reproached and bound him;

entries.zh: 因宣詔慰諭吏民，且云「大軍續至」，城中無敢動者，遂送彥於長安。
entries.en: then proclaimed the edict to comfort officials and people and said "the great army follows at once"; the city dared not move, and they sent Yan to Chang'an.
entries.literal: then proclaimed the edict to comfort officials and people, and said "the great army follows immediately"; none in the city dared move, and they sent Yan to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 泰以徽為都官尚書。
entries.en: Yuwen Tai made Hui Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Tai made Hui Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 啟奏，上大怒，召主書於前，口授敕書以責琛。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was furious; he summoned the chief clerks and dictated an edict reproaching Chen.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly angered; he summoned the chief clerks before him and dictated an edict in person to reproach Chen.

entries.zh: 大指以為：「朕有天下四十餘年，公車讜言，日關聽覽，所陳之事，與卿不異，每苦倥傯，更增惛惑。
entries.en: The gist was: "I have held the realm forty years; remonstrance reaches me daily. What you say I already hear—I am only vexed and grow more confused.
entries.literal: The main points held that: "I have held the realm more than forty years; public and private remonstrance daily reaches my ears. What you state is no different from what I hear; I am only vexed by hurry and only grow more confused.

entries.zh: 卿不宜自同闒茸，止取名字，宣之行路，言『我能上事，恨朝廷之不用』。
entries.en: Do not act the vulgar partisan, make a name for yourself, and proclaim in the streets, 'I can memorialize to the throne—pity the court will not employ me.'
entries.literal: You should not make yourself like the vulgar, take only a name, proclaim it on the road, and say, 'I can memorialize to the throne and regret that the court does not use me.'

entries.zh: 何不分別顯言：某刺史橫暴，某太守貪殘，尚書、蘭台某人奸猾，使者漁獵，並何姓名？
entries.en: Why not name them plainly: which governor is violent, which prefect greedy, which minister or Secretariat man crafty, which envoy plunders—what are their names?
entries.literal: Why not plainly name them: such-and-such governor is violent, such-and-such prefect greedy, such-and-such Master of Writing or such-and-such Secretariat man crafty, such-and-such envoy plunders—what are their names?

entries.zh: 取與者誰？
entries.en: Who gives and who takes?
entries.literal: Who gives and who takes?

entries.zh: 明言其事，得以誅黜，更擇材良。
entries.en: State it plainly so they can be punished and better men chosen.
entries.literal: State the affair plainly so they can be executed and removed, and choose new talent.

entries.zh: 又，士民飲食過差，若加嚴禁，密房曲屋，雲何可知？
entries.en: If gentry and people exceed in food and drink—strict prohibition in hidden rooms, how would you know?
entries.literal: Again, when gentry and people exceed in food and drink—if you add strict prohibition, in hidden rooms and inner chambers, how can you know?

entries.zh: 倘家家搜檢，恐益增苛擾。
entries.en: Search every house and you only add harassment.
entries.literal: If you search every house, I fear you will only add harsh harassment.

entries.zh: 若指朝廷，我無此事。
entries.en: If you mean the court—I have no such thing.
entries.literal: If you mean the court— I have no such thing.

entries.zh: 昔之牲牢，久不宰殺，朝中會同，菜蔬而已；
entries.en: Long ago we stopped slaughtering sacrificial beasts; court gatherings use only vegetables;
entries.literal: Long ago the sacrificial oxen were not slaughtered for a long time; court gatherings used only vegetables;

entries.zh: 若復減此，必有《蟋蟀》之譏。
entries.en: reduce that further and you invite the reproach of the "Crickets."
entries.literal: if this is reduced further, there will surely be the reproach of the "Crickets."

entries.zh: 若以為功德事者，皆是園中之物，變一瓜為數十種，治一菜為數十味；
entries.en: If you think merit feasts are only garden stuff—one melon into dozens of dishes, one vegetable into dozens of flavors—
entries.literal: If you think merit and virtue affairs are all garden produce—one melon made into dozens of kinds, one dish into dozens of flavors—

entries.zh: 以變故多，何損於事！
entries.en: with so many changes, what harm is done!
entries.literal: with so many changes, what harm to affairs!

entries.zh: 「我自非公宴，不食國家之食，多歷年所；
entries.en: Unless it is a public feast, I do not eat the state's food—many years now;
entries.literal: I myself, unless it is a public feast, do not eat the state's food—many years now;

entries.zh: 乃至宮人，亦不食國家之食。
entries.en: even palace women do not eat the state's food.
entries.literal: down to the palace women, they too do not eat the state's food.

entries.zh: 凡所營造，不關材官及以國匠，皆資雇藉以成其事。
entries.en: All my building uses hired labor, not the materials office or state craftsmen.
entries.literal: All construction does not involve the materials office or state craftsmen; all is hired labor to complete the work.

entries.zh: 勇怯不同，貪廉各用，亦非朝廷為之傅翼。
entries.en: Brave and timid differ; greedy and honest each have their place—the court does not give them wings for that.
entries.literal: Brave and timid differ; greedy and clean each have their use—this too is not the court giving them wings.

entries.zh: 卿以朝廷為悖，乃自甘之，當思致悖所以！
entries.en: You call the court perverse yet take your ease—you should ask what makes perverseness!
entries.literal: You take the court as perverse yet gladly accept it yourself—you should think what makes perverseness!

entries.zh: 卿云『宜導之以節儉』，朕絕房室三十餘年，至於居處不過一床之地，雕飾之物不入於宮；
entries.en: You say guide by frugality—I have closed the inner quarters thirty years; my dwelling is one bed's space; carved ornament does not enter the palace;
entries.literal: You say 'they should be guided by frugality'—I have closed off the inner quarters more than thirty years; my dwelling is no more than one bed's space; carved ornament does not enter the palace;

entries.zh: 受生不飲酒，不好音聲，所以朝中曲宴，未嘗奏樂，此群賢之所見也。
entries.en: I do not drink, I do not love music; at court feasts there is no music—the worthies have seen it.
entries.literal: from birth I do not drink wine, I do not love sounds; therefore at court feasts music is never played—the assembled worthies have seen this.

entries.zh: 朕三更出治事，隨事多少，事少午前得竟，事多日昃方食，日常一食，若晝若夜；
entries.en: I rise at the third watch; few affairs I finish before noon, many I eat at sundown—one meal, day or night;
entries.literal: I rise at the third watch to handle affairs; as affairs are many or few, when few I finish before noon, when many I eat only at sundown; ordinarily one meal, day or night;

entries.zh: 昔要腹過於十圍，今之瘦削裁二尺餘，舊帶猶存，非為妄說。
entries.en: once my waist was ten spans; now I am barely two feet round—the old belt still proves it.
entries.literal: once my belly was more than ten spans around; now my leanness is barely two feet and more; the old belt still remains—this is no empty claim.

entries.zh: 為誰為之？
entries.en: For whom?
entries.literal: For whom did I do it?

entries.zh: 救物故也。
entries.en: To save living things.
entries.literal: To save living things.

entries.zh: 「卿又曰『百司莫不奏事，詭競求進』，今不使外人呈事，誰屍其任！
entries.en: You say every office memorializes and competes by tricks—if outsiders may not present affairs, who bears the burden!
entries.literal: You also say 'the hundred offices all memorialize and compete by trickery'—if outsiders are not allowed to present affairs, who bears the burden!

entries.zh: 專委之人，雲何可得？
entries.en: Entrust all to one man—how can you have him?
entries.literal: To entrust it wholly to one man—how can he be obtained?

entries.zh: 古人云：『專聽生奸，獨任成亂。』
entries.en: The ancients said: "Sole hearing breeds treachery; sole trust breeds chaos."
entries.literal: The ancients said: 'Sole hearing breeds treachery; sole trust breeds chaos.'

entries.zh: 二世之委趙高，元後之付王莽，呼鹿為馬，又可法歟？
entries.en: The Second Emperor entrusted Zhao Gao; Empress Yuan entrusted Wang Mang—calling a deer a horse—is that law?
entries.literal: The Second Emperor entrusted Zhao Gao; Empress Yuan entrusted Wang Mang; calling a deer a horse—can that be taken as law?

entries.zh: 卿云『吹毛求疵』，復是何人？
entries.en: You say "splitting hairs"—who?
entries.literal: You say 'splitting hairs'—who is it?

entries.zh: 『擘肌分理』，復是何事？
entries.en: "Dividing fibers"—what affair?
entries.literal: 'Dividing fibers'—what affair is it?

entries.zh: 治、署、邸、肆等，何者宜除？
entries.en: Which offices, lodges, and markets should go?
entries.literal: Administration, offices, lodges, markets, and the like—which should be abolished?

entries.zh: 何者宜減？
entries.en: Which should be cut?
entries.literal: Which should be reduced?

entries.zh: 何處興造非急？
entries.en: Where is construction not urgent?
entries.literal: Where is construction not urgent?

entries.zh: 何處徵求可緩？
entries.en: Where may levies wait?
entries.literal: Where may levies be delayed?

entries.zh: 各出其事，具以奏聞！
entries.en: Set out each and memorialize in full!
entries.literal: Set out each matter and memorialize in full!

entries.zh: 富國強兵之術，息民省役之宜，並宜具列！
entries.en: List every method to enrich the state, strengthen the army, and rest the people!
entries.literal: Methods to enrich the state and strengthen the army, and measures to rest the people and reduce corvée—all should be listed in full!

entries.zh: 若不具列，則是欺罔朝廷。
entries.en: If you do not list them, you deceive the court.
entries.literal: If you do not list them in full, you are deceiving the court.

entries.zh: 佇聞重奏，當復省覽，付之尚書，班下海內，庶惟新之美，復見今日。」
entries.en: I await your renewed memorial, will examine it, send it to the Masters of Writing, and promulgate it—may renewal appear again today."
entries.literal: I await your renewed memorial; I shall examine it again, deliver it to the Masters of Writing, and promulgate it throughout the realm—may the beauty of renewal appear again today."

entries.zh: 琛但謝過而已，不敢復言。
entries.en: Chen only apologized and dared not speak again.
entries.literal: Chen only apologized and did not dare speak again.

entries.zh: 甲子，詔：「犯罪非大逆，父母、祖父母不坐。」
entries.en: On jiazi came an edict: "For crimes short of great treason, parents and grandparents shall not be punished."
entries.literal: On jiazi, an edict: "For crimes short of great treason, parents and grandparents shall not be punished."

entries.zh: 先是，江東唯建康及三吳、荊、郢、江、湘、梁、益用錢，其餘州郡雜以谷帛，交、廣專以金銀為貨。
entries.en: Before this, only Jiankang, the Three Wus, and Jing, Ying, Jiang, Xiang, Liang, and Yi used coin; elsewhere grain and cloth mixed, and Jiao and Guang traded in gold and silver alone.
entries.literal: Before this, east of the river only Jiankang and the Three Wus, Jing, Ying, Jiang, Xiang, Liang, and Yi used coin; other provinces mixed grain and cloth, and Jiao and Guang used only gold and silver as currency.

entries.zh: 上自鑄五銖及女錢，二品並行，禁諸古錢。
entries.en: The Liang emperor cast wuzhu and "female" coins, let both circulate, and forbade ancient coin.
entries.literal: The emperor himself cast wuzhu and "female" coins; both kinds circulated and ancient coins were forbidden.

entries.zh: 普通中，更鑄鐵錢。
entries.en: In the Putong era he cast iron coin anew.
entries.literal: In the Putong era iron coin was cast anew.

entries.zh: 由是民私鑄者多，物價騰踴，交易者至以車載錢，不復計數。
entries.en: Private casting flourished, prices soared, and traders hauled coin by the cartload without counting.
entries.literal: Hence private casting flourished, prices soared, and traders loaded coin by the cart and no longer counted.

entries.zh: 又自破嶺以東，八十為百，名曰「東錢」；
entries.en: East of Poling, eighty passed for a hundred—"eastern coin";
entries.literal: Again, east of Poling, eighty counted as a hundred—called "eastern coin";

entries.zh: 江、郢以上，七十為百，名曰：「西錢」；
entries.en: above Jiang and Ying, seventy for a hundred—"western coin";
entries.literal: above Jiang and Ying, seventy for a hundred—called "western coin";

entries.zh: 建康以九十為百，名曰「長錢」。
entries.en: Jiankang used ninety for a hundred—"long coin."
entries.literal: Jiankang used ninety for a hundred—called "long coin."

entries.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「朝四暮三，眾狙皆喜，名實未虧而喜怒為用。
entries.en: On bingyin an edict said, "Morning four, evening three—the monkeys are pleased; the sum is unchanged, yet joy and anger rule.
entries.literal: On bingyin, an edict said, "Morning four, evening three—the monkeys are all pleased; name and substance are not diminished, yet joy and anger are wielded.

entries.zh: 頃聞外間多用九陌錢，陌減則物貴，陌足則物賤，非物有貴賤，乃心有顛倒。
entries.en: Lately the outer regions use short tenths: a short tenth makes goods dear, a full tenth cheap—not goods that shift, but hearts turned upside down.
entries.literal: Lately we hear the outer regions use much nine-tenths coin: when the tenth is short, goods seem dear; when the tenth is full, goods seem cheap—not that goods have high and low, but hearts are turned upside down.

entries.zh: 至於遠方，日更滋甚，徒亂王制，無益民財。
entries.en: In distant places it worsens daily, disordering royal rule without helping the people's wealth.
entries.literal: In distant places it grows worse day by day, vainly disordering royal rule and helping the people's wealth not at all.

entries.zh: 自今可通用足陌錢！
entries.en: From now let full-tenth coin circulate everywhere!
entries.literal: From now let full-tenth coin circulate everywhere!

entries.zh: 令書行後，百日為期，若猶有犯，男子謫運，女子質作，並同三年。」
entries.en: A hundred days after the order; offenders—men to transport labor, women pledged to service—for three years alike."
entries.literal: After the order goes forth, a hundred days are allowed; if any still offend, men shall be sent to transport labor, women pledged to service—all for three years alike."

entries.zh: 詔下而人不從，錢陌益少；
entries.en: The edict descended and the people did not obey; tenths grew ever shorter;
entries.literal: When the edict descended the people did not obey, and coin tenths grew ever shorter;

entries.zh: 至於季年，遂以三十五為百雲。
entries.en: by the late years thirty-five passed for a hundred.
entries.literal: by the late years thirty-five passed for a hundred, it was said.

entries.zh: 庚戌，上幸同泰寺，遂停寺省，講《三慧經》。
entries.en: On gengxu the emperor visited Tongtai Temple, then lodged in the temple compound and lectured on the "Sutra of Three Wisdoms."
entries.literal: On gengxu the emperor visited Tongtai Temple, then stopped at the temple compound and lectured on the "Sutra of Three Wisdoms."

entries.zh: 夏，四月，丙戌，解講，大赦，改元。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the lecture ended; general amnesty; the era name was changed.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the lecture ended; general amnesty; era name changed.

entries.zh: 是夜，同泰寺浮圖災，上曰：「此魔也，宜廣為法事。」
entries.en: That night Tongtai Temple's pagoda burned; the emperor said: "This is a demon—we should perform the dharma on a great scale."
entries.literal: That night the Tongtai Temple pagoda burned; the emperor said: "This is a demon; we should widely perform the dharma."

entries.zh: 群臣皆稱善。
entries.en: The ministers all approved.
entries.literal: The ministers all called it good.

entries.zh: 乃下詔曰：「道高魔盛，行善鄣生。
entries.en: An edict followed: "The Way is high and demons flourish; doing good meets obstruction.
entries.literal: An edict was then issued: "The Way is high and demons flourish; doing good meets obstruction.

entries.zh: 當窮茲土木，倍增往日。」
entries.en: Let us exhaust timber and earth, doubling what went before."
entries.literal: We should exhaust ourselves in timber and earth, doubling what went before."

entries.zh: 遂起十二層浮圖；
entries.en: A twelve-story pagoda was raised;
entries.literal: Thereupon a twelve-story pagoda was raised;

entries.zh: 將成，值侯景亂而止。
entries.en: and when it was nearly done, Hou Jing's rebellion stopped the work.
entries.literal: when it was nearly finished, Hou Jing's rebellion came and the work stopped.

entries.zh: 上遣交州刺史楊瞟討李賁，以陳霸先為司馬；
entries.en: The Liang emperor sent Jiaozhou Inspector Yang Biao against Li Ben and made Chen Baxian marshal;
entries.literal: The emperor sent Jiaozhou Inspector Yang Biao against Li Ben and made Chen Baxian marshal;

entries.zh: 命定州刺史蕭勃會瞟於西江。
entries.en: He ordered Dingzhou Inspector Xiao Bo to join Biao at Xijiang.
entries.literal: He ordered Dingzhou Inspector Xiao Bo to join Biao at Xijiang.

entries.zh: 勃知軍士憚遠役，因詭說留瞟。
entries.en: Bo knew the troops dreaded a distant campaign and used deceit to hold Biao back.
entries.literal: Bo knew the troops feared a long campaign and used deceit to detain Biao.

entries.zh: 瞟集諸將問計，霸先曰：「交趾叛換，罪由宗室，遂使溷亂數州，逋誅累歲。
entries.en: Biao gathered the generals for counsel. Baxian said: "Jiaozhi rebels; the fault lies with the imperial clan, and several provinces have been in turmoil while the court has failed to punish for years.
entries.literal: Biao gathered the generals to ask counsel; Baxian said: "Jiaozhi rebels and shifts allegiance; the fault lies with the imperial clan, and several provinces have been thrown into turmoil while punishment has been evaded for years.

entries.zh: 定州欲偷安目前，不顧大計。
entries.en: Dingzhou wants comfort for the moment and ignores the larger plan.
entries.literal: Dingzhou wishes ease for the moment and does not care for the great plan.

entries.zh: 節下奉辭伐罪，當死生以之。
entries.en: Your command bears the mandate to punish crime—we should stake our lives on it.
entries.literal: Your command bears the mandate to punish crime—we should stake life and death on it.

entries.zh: 豈可逗撓不進，長寇沮眾也！」
entries.en: How can we hang back and not advance, feeding the rebel and breaking the army's heart!"
entries.literal: How can we hesitate and not advance, nourishing the bandit and discouraging the host!"

entries.zh: 遂勒兵先發。
entries.en: He then led the troops out first.
entries.literal: He then led the troops out first.

entries.zh: 瞟以霸先為前鋒。
entries.en: Biao made Baxian his vanguard.
entries.literal: Biao made Baxian vanguard.

entries.zh: 至交州，賁帥眾三萬拒之，敗於朱鳶，又敗於蘇歷江口。
entries.en: At Jiaozhou, Ben led thirty thousand to resist; he was beaten at Zhuyuan and again at the mouth of the Suli River.
entries.literal: When they reached Jiaozhou, Ben commanded thirty thousand men to resist; he was defeated at Zhuyuan and again at the mouth of the Suli River.

entries.zh: 賁奔嘉寧城，諸軍進圍之。
entries.en: Ben fled to Jianing; the armies advanced to besiege it.
entries.literal: Ben fled to Jianing city; the armies advanced to besiege it.

entries.zh: 勃，昺之子也。
entries.en: Bo was the son of Bing.
entries.literal: Bo was the son of Bing.

entries.zh: 散騎常侍賀琛啟陳四事：其一以為「今北邊稽服，正是生聚教議之時，而天下戶口減落，關外彌甚。
entries.en: Palace Attendant He Chen submitted four memorials. The first argued that "with the north now subdued, this should be a time to gather people and teach—but registers are shrinking everywhere, and beyond the passes the loss is worse.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant He Chen memorialized on four matters. The first held that "now the north has submitted—it is exactly the time to gather the people and teach and deliberate—yet household registers throughout the land are falling, and beyond the passes the loss is worse still.

entries.zh: 郡不堪州之控總，縣不堪郡之裒削，更相呼擾，惟事征斂。
entries.en: Commanderies cannot bear provincial control; counties cannot bear commandery exactions; they harass one another and do nothing but levy.
entries.literal: Commanderies cannot bear the provinces' control; counties cannot bear the commanderies' stripping; they call on one another in turmoil and do nothing but levy.

entries.zh: 民不堪命，各務流移，此豈非牧守之過歟！
entries.en: The people cannot bear their lot and flee—is this not the fault of local officials!
entries.literal: The people cannot bear their lot; each seeks to flee—are these not the faults of the shepherds of the people!

entries.zh: 東境戶口空虛，皆由使命繁數，窮幽極遠，無不皆至，每有一使，所屬搔擾，駑困邑宰，則拱手聽其漁獵，桀黠長吏，又因之重為貪殘，縱有廉平，郡猶掣肘。
entries.en: The east is hollowed out because envoys are too many—no corner too remote. Every envoy ravages his route; worn magistrates fold their hands while he plunders; crafty chiefs use him to plunder again. Even an honest man finds the commandery tugging his sleeve.
entries.literal: The eastern marches are empty of households, all because missions are numerous: to the farthest corners, none are left unreached. With every envoy, the districts he touches are harassed; when the magistrate is worn down, he folds his hands and lets them plunder; when the chief is crafty, he uses them to be doubly greedy. Even if one is honest, the commandery still pulls his elbow.

entries.zh: 如此，雖年降復業之詔，屢下蠲賦之恩，而民不得反其居也。」
entries.en: So though edicts year after year call people home and tax relief is granted again and again, they cannot return."
entries.literal: Thus, though year after year edicts recall people to their trades and amnesties on levies are issued again and again, the people cannot return home."

entries.zh: 其二以為「今天下守宰所以貪殘，良由風俗侈靡使之然也。
entries.en: The second held that "today's greedy magistrates are made so by extravagant custom.
entries.literal: The second held that "today the reason governors and magistrates are greedy and cruel is truly that extravagant custom makes them so.

entries.zh: 今之燕喜，相競誇豪，積果如丘陵，列餚同綺繡，露台之產，不週一燕之資，而賓主之間，裁取滿腹，未及下堂，已同臭腐。
entries.en: At feasts they vie in display: fruit heaped like hills, dishes like brocade; a terrace garden's yield will not pay for one banquet, yet host and guest eat only their fill—before they leave the hall it is rot.
entries.literal: At today's feasts they vie in boasting wealth: fruit piled like hills, dishes set out like brocade; the yield of a terrace garden does not suffice for one banquet's cost, yet between host and guest they take only a full belly—before leaving the hall it is all rot.

entries.zh: 又，畜妓之夫，無有等秩，為吏牧民者，致貲巨億，罷歸之日，不支數年，率皆盡於燕飲之物、歌謠之具。
entries.en: Men who keep courtesans know no rank; officials who rule the people amass fortunes, and within years of leaving office it is all gone on feasts and music.
entries.literal: Again, men who keep courtesans have no rank limit; those who govern the people amass hundreds of millions, and the day they leave office they cannot last a few years—all is spent on feasting and on songs and music.

entries.zh: 所費事等丘山，為歡止在俄頃，乃更追恨向所取之少；
entries.en: They spend like mountains; the joy lasts a moment—then they regret they took too little before;
entries.literal: What is spent equals mountains; the pleasure lasts only a moment—then they regret having taken too little before;

entries.zh: 如復傅翼，增其搏噬，一何悖哉！
entries.en: give them wings and they bite harder—how perverse!
entries.literal: give them wings again and they bite all the harder—how perverse!

entries.zh: 其餘淫侈，著之凡百，習以成俗，日見滋甚。
entries.en: The rest of debauchery, in a hundred forms, has become custom and worsens daily.
entries.literal: The rest of debauchery, set out in a hundred ways, has become custom and grows worse daily.

entries.zh: 欲使人守廉白，安可得邪！
entries.en: To expect integrity—how can you have it!
entries.literal: To wish men to keep integrity—how can it be obtained!

entries.zh: 誠宜嚴為禁制，導以節儉，糾奏浮華，變其耳目。
entries.en: Forbid it strictly, guide by frugality, impeach display, and change what they see.
entries.literal: It is truly fitting to forbid this strictly, guide them by frugality, impeach florid display, and change what meets their eyes.

entries.zh: 夫失節之嗟，亦民所自患，正恥不能及群，故勉強而為之；
entries.en: People suffer from lost restraint too—they are ashamed not to keep up and force themselves;
entries.literal: The sigh at lost restraint is also what the people themselves suffer from—they are ashamed not to keep up with the crowd and so force themselves to it;

entries.zh: 苟以淳素為先，足正雕流之弊矣。」
entries.en: put simplicity first and you can correct carved display."
entries.literal: if simplicity comes first, it is enough to correct the evil of carved display."

entries.zh: 其三以為「陛下憂念四海，不憚勤勞，至於百司，莫不奏事。
entries.en: The third held that "Your Majesty cares for all under heaven and toils without shrinking; every office memorializes.
entries.literal: The third held that "Your Majesty cares for the four seas and does not shrink from toil; down to the hundred offices, none fails to memorialize.

entries.zh: 但斗筲之人，既得伏奏帷扆，便欲詭競求進，不論國之大體，心存明恕；
entries.en: But petty men, once they can speak before the curtain, compete by tricks; they ignore the state's great body and forget magnanimity;
entries.literal: But petty men, once they can memorialize before the curtain, wish to compete by trickery for advancement; they do not discuss the great body of the state or keep magnanimity in mind;

entries.zh: 惟務吹毛求疵，擘肌分理，以深刻為能，以繩逐為務。
entries.en: they split hairs and divide fibers, take harshness for talent, and drive people with the rope.
entries.literal: they only pursue splitting hairs and dividing fibers, taking harshness as ability and driving people with the rope.

entries.zh: 跡雖似於奉公，事更成其威福，犯罪者多，巧避滋甚，長弊增奸，實由於此。
entries.en: It looks like public service but only swells their power; crime multiplies and evasion grows—long abuse and added treachery come from this.
entries.literal: The trace seems to serve the public, but the affair only increases their power and profit; criminals multiply and clever evasions grow—long abuses and added treachery truly come from this.

entries.zh: 誠願責其公平之效，黜其讒慝之心，則下安上謐，無徼幸之患矣。」
entries.en: Demand fairness, dismiss malice—then below is secure and above tranquil, without lucky gambles."
entries.literal: I truly wish to demand their effect in fairness and dismiss their hearts of slander and malice; then below will be secure and above tranquil, with no hope of luck."

entries.zh: 其四以為「今天下無事，而猶日不暇給，宜省事、息費，事省則民養，費息則財聚。
entries.en: The fourth held that "the realm is at peace yet there is no leisure; reduce affairs and still expenses—reduce affairs and the people are fed; still expenses and wealth gathers.
entries.literal: The fourth held that "today the realm is at peace, yet there is still no leisure from day to day; affairs should be reduced and expenses stilled—when affairs are reduced the people are nourished; when expenses are stilled wealth gathers.

entries.zh: 應內省職掌各檢所部：凡京師治、署、邸、肆及國容、戎備，四方屯、傳、邸治，有所宜除，除之，有所宜減，減之；
entries.en: Each office should inspect its charge: capital offices, lodges, markets, regalia, armaments; frontier posts and stations—abolish what should go, reduce what should shrink;
entries.literal: Within, each office should inspect its charge: all capital administration, offices, lodges, markets, state regalia, and military readiness; all frontier stations, posts, and lodge administration—what should be abolished, abolish; what should be reduced, reduce;

entries.zh: 興造有非急者，徵求有可緩者，皆宜停省，以息費休民。
entries.en: halt non-urgent construction and delayable levies to still expense and rest the people.
entries.literal: construction that is not urgent and levies that can be delayed should all be halted to still expense and rest the people.

entries.zh: 故畜其財者，所以大用之也；
entries.en: Store wealth to use it greatly;
entries.literal: Thus to store wealth is to use it greatly;

entries.zh: 養其民者，所以大役之也。
entries.en: nourish the people to employ them greatly.
entries.literal: to nourish the people is to employ them greatly.

entries.zh: 若言小事不足害財，則終年不息矣；
entries.en: If you say small matters cannot harm wealth, there is no ceasing all year;
entries.literal: If one says small matters cannot harm wealth, then there is no ceasing year round;

entries.zh: 以小役不足妨民，則終年不止矣。
entries.en: if small corvée cannot harm the people, there is no stopping all year.
entries.literal: if small corvée cannot harm the people, then there is no stopping year round.

entries.zh: 如此，則難可以語富強而圖遠大矣。」
entries.en: Then you cannot speak of enriching the state, strong armies, or far-reaching plans."
entries.literal: Thus it is hard to speak of enriching the state and strong armies or plan for the far and great."

entries.zh: 高祖武皇帝十五中大同元年（
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang, fifteenth year, first year of Zhongdatong (
entries.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, fifteenth year, Zhongdatong first year (

entries.zh: 丙寅，公元五四六年）
entries.en: bingyin, AD 546)
entries.literal: bingyin, 546 CE)

entries.zh: 東魏儀同爾朱文暢與丞相司馬任冑、都督鄭仲禮等，謀因正月望夜觀打簇戲作亂，殺丞相歡，奉文暢為主。
entries.en: Eastern Wei's Erzhu Wenchang, Chancellor Gao Huan's marshal Ren Zhou, Commissioner Zheng Zhongli, and others plotted a Lantern-night rising during the fireworks show: kill Gao Huan and make Wenchang ruler.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei Yitong Erzhu Wenchang, the chancellor's marshal Ren Zhou, and Commissioner Zheng Zhongli and others plotted to use the first-month full-moon night, while watching fireworks, to rebel—kill Chancellor Huan and set Wenchang up as ruler.

entries.zh: 事洩，皆死。
entries.en: The plot leaked; all were executed.
entries.literal: The plot leaked; all were executed.

entries.zh: 文暢，榮之子也；
entries.en: Wenchang was Erzhu Rong's son.
entries.literal: Wenchang was Erzhu Rong's son.

entries.zh: 其姊，敬宗之後，及仲禮姊大車，皆為歡妾，有寵，故其兄弟皆不坐。
entries.en: His sister, Jingzong's empress, and Zhongli's elder sister Dache were all Gao Huan's favored concubines, so their brothers went unpunished.
entries.literal: His sister, Jingzong's empress, and Zhongli's elder sister Dache were all Huan's favored concubines, so their brothers were not punished.

entries.zh: 三月，乙未，東魏丞相歡入朝於鄴，百官迎於紫陌。
entries.en: In the third month, on yiwei, Gao Huan entered court at Ye; the officials welcomed him at Zimo.
entries.literal: In the third month, on yiwei, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan entered court at Ye; the hundred officials welcomed him at Zimo.

entries.zh: 歡握崔暹手而勞之曰：「往日朝廷豈無法官，莫肯糾劾。
entries.en: Gao Huan took Cui Xian's hand and praised him: "The court always had law officers—none would impeach.
entries.literal: Huan took Cui Xian's hand and praised him: "In the past the court certainly had law officers—none would impeach.

entries.zh: 中尉盡心徇國，不避豪強，遂使遠邇肅清。
entries.en: The Commandant gave his heart to the state and did not spare the powerful, until far and near were clean.
entries.literal: The Commandant gave his heart to the state and did not avoid the powerful, so far and near were purified.

entries.zh: 衝鋒陷陣，大有其人；
entries.en: Men who charge breaches and break arrays—there are many;
entries.literal: Men who charge breaches and break arrays—there are many such;

entries.zh: 當官正色，今始見之。
entries.en: but to hold office with an upright countenance—only now do I see it.
entries.literal: to hold office with an upright countenance—only now do I see it.

entries.zh: 富貴乃中尉自取，高歡父子無以相報。」
entries.en: Wealth and rank the Commandant earns himself; Gao Huan and his sons have no way to repay him."
entries.literal: Wealth and rank the Commandant takes for himself; Gao Huan father and son have nothing with which to repay him."

entries.zh: 賜暹良馬。
entries.en: He gave Xian a fine horse.
entries.literal: He gave Xian a fine horse.

entries.zh: 暹拜，馬驚走，歡親擁之，授以轡。
entries.en: Xian bowed; the horse bolted; Gao Huan himself caught him and gave him the reins.
entries.literal: Xian bowed; the horse startled and bolted; Huan personally steadied him and handed him the reins.

entries.zh: 東魏主宴於華林園，使歡擇朝廷公直者勸之酒；
entries.en: The Eastern Wei emperor feasted at Hualin Garden and had Gao Huan choose upright courtiers to toast him;
entries.literal: The Eastern Wei ruler feasted at Hualin Garden and had Huan choose upright men of the court to toast him;

entries.zh: 歡降階跪曰：「唯暹一人可勸，並請以臣所射賜物千段賜之。」
entries.en: Gao Huan came down the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Xian is fit to toast; I also ask that the thousand lengths of my archery prizes be given him."
entries.literal: Huan descended the steps, knelt, and said: "Only Xian can toast; I also ask that the thousand lengths of my archery prizes be given him."

entries.zh: 高澄退，謂暹曰：「我尚畏羨，何況餘人！」
entries.en: Gao Cheng withdrew and told Xian: "Even I still fear envy—how much more the rest!"
entries.literal: Gao Cheng withdrew and said to Xian: "I still fear envy—how much more the rest!"

entries.zh: 然暹中懷頗挾巧詐。
entries.en: Yet Xian inwardly carried a good deal of crafty deceit.
entries.literal: Yet Xian inwardly harbored much crafty deceit.

entries.zh: 初，魏高陽王斌有庶妹玉儀，不為其家所齒，為孫騰妓，騰又棄之；
entries.en: Earlier, Eastern Wei's Prince of Gaoyang, Bin, had a concubine-born sister Yuyi whom the family disdained; she became Sun Teng's courtesan, and Teng cast her off;
entries.literal: Earlier, Eastern Wei Prince of Gaoyang Bin had a concubine-born sister Yuyi; her family disdained her; she became Sun Teng's courtesan, and Teng abandoned her;

entries.zh: 高澄遇諸塗，悅而納之，遂有殊寵，封琅邪公主。
entries.en: Gao Cheng met her on the road, was taken with her, and took her in; she won special favor and was made Princess of Langye.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng met her on the road, was delighted, and took her in; she won special favor and was made Princess of Langye.

entries.zh: 澄謂崔季舒曰：「崔暹必造直諫，我亦有以待之。」
entries.en: Cheng told Cui Jishu: "Cui Xian is sure to remonstrate bluntly; I have a way to wait for him too."
entries.literal: Cheng told Cui Jishu: "Cui Xian is sure to offer blunt remonstrance; I too have a way to wait for him."

entries.zh: 及暹咨事，澄不復假以顏色。
entries.en: When Xian came to consult, Cheng no longer gave him a pleasant face.
entries.literal: When Xian came to consult on affairs, Cheng no longer showed him a pleasant face.

entries.zh: 居三日，暹懷刺墜之於前。
entries.en: After three days Xian let a visiting card fall before him.
entries.literal: After three days Xian dropped a visiting card before him.

entries.zh: 澄問：「何用此為？」
entries.en: Cheng asked: "What is this for?"
entries.literal: Cheng asked: "What is this for?"

entries.zh: 暹悚然曰：「未得通公主。」
entries.en: Xian said fearfully: "I have not yet been presented to the Princess."
entries.literal: Xian said fearfully: "I have not yet gained access to the Princess."

entries.zh: 澄大悅，把暹臂，入見之。
entries.en: Cheng was delighted, took Xian's arm, and led him in to see her.
entries.literal: Cheng was greatly pleased, took Xian's arm, and led him in to see her.

entries.zh: 季舒語人曰：「崔暹常忿吾佞，在大將軍前，每言叔父可殺；
entries.en: Jishu told others: "Cui Xian always hated my flattery; before the Great General he often said my uncle deserved death;
entries.literal: Jishu told people: "Cui Xian always resented my flattery; before the Great General he often said my uncle should be killed;

entries.zh: 及其自作，乃過於吾。」
entries.en: when he did it himself, he outdid me."
entries.literal: when he did it himself, he surpassed me."

entries.zh: 歡上書言：「并州，軍器所聚，動須女功，請置宮以處配沒之口；
entries.en: Gao Huan memorialized: "Bingzhou is where the arsenals gather and women's labor is always needed. I ask that a palace be established for persons taken in confiscations;
entries.literal: Huan memorialized: "Bingzhou is where military stores gather; work constantly needs women's labor. I ask that a palace be set up to house persons assigned from confiscations;

entries.zh: 又納吐谷渾之女以招懷之。」
entries.en: and that a Tuyuhun woman be taken in marriage to win them over."
entries.literal: Also take a Tuyuhun woman in marriage to win them over."

entries.zh: 丁未，置晉陽宮。
entries.en: On dingwei the Jinyang Palace was established.
entries.literal: On dingwei the Jinyang Palace was established.

entries.zh: 二月，庚申，東魏主納吐谷渾可汗從妹為容華。
entries.en: In the second month, on gengshen, the Eastern Wei emperor took a cousin of the Tuyuhun khan as Ronghua.
entries.literal: In the second month, on gengshen, the Eastern Wei ruler took a cousin of the Tuyuhun khan as Ronghua.

entries.zh: 魏徙并州刺史王思政為荊州刺史，使之舉諸將可代鎮玉壁者。
entries.en: Western Wei moved Wang Sizheng from Bingzhou to Jingzhou and had him name a general to hold Yubi in his stead.
entries.literal: Wei transferred Bingzhou inspector Wang Sizheng to Jingzhou and had him name generals fit to replace him in holding Yubi.

entries.zh: 思政舉晉州刺史韋孝寬，丞相泰從之。
entries.en: Sizheng named Wei Xiaokuan of Jinzhou; Yuwen Tai agreed.
entries.literal: Sizheng named Jinzhou inspector Wei Xiaokuan; Chancellor Tai agreed.

entries.zh: 東魏丞相歡悉舉山東之眾，將伐魏；
entries.en: Gao Huan mustered all Shandong to attack Western Wei;
entries.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan mustered all the hosts of Shandong to attack Wei;

entries.zh: 癸巳，自鄴會兵於晉陽；
entries.en: on guisi he gathered troops at Jinyang from Ye;
entries.literal: on guisi he gathered troops at Jinyang from Ye;

entries.zh: 九月，至玉壁，圍之。
entries.en: in the ninth month he reached Yubi and besieged it.
entries.literal: in the ninth month he reached Yubi and besieged it.

entries.zh: 以挑西師，西師不出。
entries.en: He meant to draw the western army out; it did not come.
entries.literal: He meant to provoke the western army; the western army did not come out.

entries.zh: 魏與柔然頭兵可汗謀連兵伐東魏，丞相歡患之，遣行台郎中杜弼使於柔然，為世子澄求婚。
entries.en: Western Wei and the Rouran khan Toubing plotted a joint attack on Eastern Wei. Gao Huan, alarmed, sent Secretariat Lang Du Bi to the Rouran to seek a bride for heir Cheng.
entries.literal: Western Wei and Rouran Khan Toubing plotted a joint attack on Eastern Wei; Chancellor Huan was troubled and sent Secretariat Lang Du Bi to the Rouran to seek a bride for heir Cheng.

entries.zh: 頭兵曰：「高王自娶則可。」
entries.en: Toubing said: "If King Gao takes her himself, very well."
entries.literal: Toubing said: "If King Gao takes her himself, that will do."

entries.zh: 歡猶豫未決。
entries.en: Gao Huan hesitated.
entries.literal: Huan hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 婁妃曰：「國家大計，願勿疑也。」
entries.en: Consort Lou said: "This is the state's great plan—do not doubt."
entries.literal: Consort Lou said: "This is the great plan of the state—pray do not doubt."

entries.zh: 世子澄、尉景亦勸之。
entries.en: Heir Cheng and Wei Jing also urged him.
entries.literal: Heir Cheng and Wei Jing also urged him.

entries.zh: 歡乃遣鎮南將軍慕容儼聘之，號曰蠕蠕公主。
entries.en: Gao Huan then sent Murong Yan, Suppressing-the-South General, to betroth her as the Rouran Princess.
entries.literal: Huan then sent Suppressing-the-South General Murong Yan to betroth her, titled Rouran Princess.

entries.zh: 秋，八月，歡親迎於下館。
entries.en: In autumn, the eighth month, Gao Huan personally welcomed her at Xiaguan.
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Huan personally welcomed her at Xiaguan.

entries.zh: 公主至，婁妃避正室以處之；
entries.en: When the princess arrived, Consort Lou vacated the main chamber for her;
entries.literal: When the princess arrived, Consort Lou vacated the main chamber to house her;

entries.zh: 歡跪而拜謝，妃曰：「彼將覺之，願絕勿顧。」
entries.en: Gao Huan knelt to thank her; the consort said: "She will notice—cut off all attention."
entries.literal: Huan knelt and thanked her; the consort said: "She will notice—pray cut off all attention."

entries.zh: 頭兵使其弟禿突佳來送女，且報聘；
entries.en: Toubing sent his brother Tutujia to escort his daughter and return the visit;
entries.literal: Toubing sent his brother Tutujia to escort his daughter and return the visit;

entries.zh: 仍戒曰：「待見外孫乃歸。」
entries.en: He also warned: "Do not return until you have seen your grandson."
entries.literal: He also warned: "Wait until you see the grandson before returning."

entries.zh: 公主性嚴毅，終身不肯華言。
entries.en: The princess was stern by nature and all her life refused to speak Chinese.
entries.literal: The princess was stern by nature and all her life refused to speak Chinese.

entries.zh: 歡嘗病，不得往，禿突佳怨恚，歡輿疾就之。
entries.en: Gao Huan once fell ill and could not visit; Tutujia was resentful; Gao Huan rode out while ill to see him.
entries.literal: Huan once fell ill and could not visit; Tutujia resented it; Huan rode in a carriage while ill to see him.

entries.zh: 東魏遣中書舍人尉瑾來聘。
entries.en: Eastern Wei sent Secretariat Attendant Yu Jin on a friendly mission.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei sent Secretariat Attendant Yu Jin as envoy.

entries.zh: 乙未，東魏丞相歡請釋邙山俘囚桎梏，配以民間寡婦。
entries.en: On yiwei, Gao Huan asked to free the Mangshan prisoners from shackles and give them widows from among the people.
entries.literal: On yiwei, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan asked to release the Mangshan prisoners from shackles and match them with widows from among the people.

entries.zh: 東魏丞相歡如鄴。
entries.en: Gao Huan went to Ye.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan went to Ye.

entries.zh: 高澄遷洛陽《石經》五十二碑於鄴。
entries.en: Gao Cheng moved fifty-two steles of the Luoyang Stone Classics to Ye.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng moved fifty-two steles of the Luoyang Stone Classics to Ye.

entries.zh: 十二月，東魏以侯景為司徒，中書令韓軌為司空；
entries.en: In the twelfth month, Eastern Wei made Hou Jing Minister over the Masses and Han Gui Minister of Works;
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Eastern Wei made Hou Jing Minister over the Masses and Han Gui Minister of Works;

entries.zh: 戊子，以孫騰錄尚書事。
entries.en: On wuzi, Sun Teng was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: On wuzi, Sun Teng was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 六月，庚子，東魏以司徒侯景為河南大將軍、大行台。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Eastern Wei made Hou Jing Grand General of Henan and Grand Mobile Headquarters.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Eastern Wei made Minister over the Masses Hou Jing Grand General of Henan and Grand Mobile Headquarters.

entries.zh: 李賁復帥眾二萬自獠中出屯典澈湖，大造船艦，充塞湖中。
entries.en: Li Ben again led twenty thousand from the Liao to Dianche Lake, built a fleet, and filled the lake.
entries.literal: Li Ben again led twenty thousand men out from among the Liao to camp at Dianche Lake, built many ships, and filled the lake.

entries.zh: 眾軍憚之，頓湖口，不敢進。
entries.en: The allied armies feared him, halted at the lake mouth, and dared not advance.
entries.literal: The allied armies feared him, halted at the lake mouth, and dared not advance.

entries.zh: 陳霸先謂諸將曰：「我師已老，將士疲勞；
entries.en: Chen Baxian told the generals, "Our army is worn, the men weary;
entries.literal: Chen Baxian told the generals, "Our army is worn, officers and soldiers weary;

entries.zh: 且孤軍無援，入人心腹，若一戰不捷，豈望生全！
entries.en: we stand alone without relief, deep in the enemy belly—lose one battle and who lives!
entries.literal: moreover we are a lone force without relief, deep in the enemy's belly—if one battle fails, who hopes to live!

entries.zh: 今藉其屢奔，人情未固，夷、獠烏合，易為摧殄。
entries.en: They have fled again and again; hearts are not firm; Yi and Liao are a crow flock—easy to break.
entries.literal: Now they rely on repeated flight; hearts are not firm; Yi and Liao are a crow flock—easy to shatter.

entries.zh: 正當共出百死，決力取之；
entries.en: We should stake our lives together and strike with all our force;
entries.literal: We should together stake a hundred deaths and strike with all our force;

entries.zh: 無故停留，時事去矣！」
entries.en: to halt for no reason is to let the moment pass!"
entries.literal: to halt for no reason is to let the moment pass!"

entries.zh: 諸將皆默然莫應。
entries.en: The generals were silent.
entries.literal: The generals were all silent and answered not.

entries.zh: 是夜，江水暴起七丈，注湖中。
entries.en: That night the river rose seven zhang and poured into the lake.
entries.literal: That night the river rose seven zhang in flood and poured into the lake.

entries.zh: 霸先勒所部兵乘流先進，眾軍鼓噪俱前；
entries.en: Baxian drove his men forward on the flood; the armies drummed and shouted and advanced;
entries.literal: Baxian drove his own troops forward on the current; the armies drummed and shouted and advanced together;

entries.zh: 賁眾大潰，竄入屈獠洞中。
entries.en: Ben's host broke and fled into the Qu-Liao caves.
entries.literal: Ben's host broke in great rout and fled into the Qu-Liao caves.

entries.zh: 東魏司徒、河南大將軍、大行台侯景，右足偏短，弓馬非其長，而多謀算。
entries.en: Hou Jing of Eastern Wei—Minister of Works, Grand General of Henan, Grand Mobile Headquarters—had a shortened right foot; bow and horse were not his gifts, but stratagem was.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei's Minister of Works, Grand General of Henan, and Grand Mobile Headquarters Hou Jing had a right foot somewhat short; bow and horse were not his strength, but he had much stratagem.

entries.zh: 諸將高敖曹、彭樂等皆勇冠一時，景常輕之，曰：「此屬皆如豕突，勢何所至！」
entries.en: Gao Aocao, Peng Le, and the rest were bravest of their age; Jing often held them light and said, "These are pigs charging—how far can they go!"
entries.literal: The generals Gao Aocao, Peng Le, and others were bravest of their age; Jing often held them light and said, "These sorts are like pigs charging—how far can their momentum go!"

entries.zh: 景嘗言於丞相歡：「願得兵三萬，橫行天下，要須濟江縛取蕭衍老公、以為太平寺主。」
entries.en: Jing once told Gao Huan, "Give me thirty thousand men and I will sweep the realm—cross the river, bind the old man Xiao Yan, and make him abbot of Taiping Temple."
entries.literal: Jing once said to Chancellor Huan, "Give me thirty thousand troops and I will sweep the realm—I need only cross the river, bind the old man Xiao Yan, and make him abbot of Taiping Temple."

entries.zh: 歡使將兵十萬，專制河南，杖任若己之半體。
entries.en: Huan gave him a hundred thousand men and sole rule of Henan, staff and trust like half his body.
entries.literal: Huan had him lead a hundred thousand troops with sole rule of Henan, staff and trust like half his own body.

entries.zh: 冬，十月，乙亥，以前東揚州刺史岳陽王察為雍州刺史。
entries.en: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, Prince Cha of Yueyang, former inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, was made inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yihai, the former Eastern Yangzhou inspector, Prince Cha of Yueyang, was made inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 上捨察兄弟而立太子綱，內常愧之，寵亞諸子。
entries.en: The Liang emperor had passed over Cha and his brothers for Crown Prince Gang and inwardly felt shame, favoring them next to his own sons.
entries.literal: The emperor had set aside Cha and his brothers to establish Crown Prince Gang and inwardly always felt shame toward them, favoring them next only to his sons.

entries.zh: 以會稽人物殷阜，故用察兄弟迭為東揚州以慰其心。
entries.en: Because Kuaiji was rich in men and goods, he rotated Cha and his brothers through Eastern Yangzhou to comfort them.
entries.literal: Because Kuaiji was rich in men and goods, he used Cha and his brothers in turn as Eastern Yangzhou to comfort their hearts.

entries.zh: 察兄弟亦內懷不平。
entries.en: Cha and his brothers also nursed inward discontent.
entries.literal: Cha and his brothers also nursed inward discontent.

entries.zh: 察以上衰老，朝多秕政，遂蓄聚貨財，折節下士，招募勇敢，左右至數千人。
entries.en: Cha, seeing the emperor aged and the court rotten, hoarded wealth, humbled himself to scholars, recruited the bold, and kept several thousand at his side.
entries.literal: Cha, seeing the emperor aged and the court full of rotten policy, then hoarded wealth, humbled himself to scholars, recruited the bold, and had several thousand at his side.

entries.zh: 以襄陽形勝之地，梁業所基，遇亂可以圖大功。
entries.en: Xiangyang was strong ground, the foundation of Liang—when disorder came, great deeds could be plotted.
entries.literal: Xiangyang was a place of strategic strength, the foundation of Liang's enterprise—when disorder came, great deeds could be plotted.

entries.zh: 乃克己為政，撫循士民，數施恩惠，延納規諫，所部稱治。
entries.en: He governed with restraint, comforted scholars and people, showed kindness, welcomed remonstrance, and his district was called well ruled.
entries.literal: He then restrained himself in government, comforted scholars and people, often showed kindness, welcomed remonstrance, and his district was called well ruled.

entries.zh: 東魏丞相歡攻玉壁，晝夜不息，魏韋孝寬隨機拒之。
entries.en: Gao Huan attacked Yubi day and night; Wei Xiaokuan of Western Wei met him as occasion demanded.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan attacked Yubi day and night without cease; Wei's Wei Xiaokuan met him as occasion demanded.

entries.zh: 城中無水，汲於汾，歡使移汾，一夕而畢。
entries.en: The city had no water and drew from the Fen; Huan diverted the Fen, and in one night it was done.
entries.literal: The city had no water and drew from the Fen; Huan had the Fen diverted, and in one night it was done.

entries.zh: 歡於城南起土山，欲乘之以入。
entries.en: Huan raised an earthen hill south of the city to ride over the wall.
entries.literal: Huan raised an earthen hill south of the city, intending to ride it in.

entries.zh: 城上先有二樓，孝寬縛木接之，令常高於土山以御之。
entries.en: Two towers already stood on the wall; Xiaokuan bound timbers to extend them, always keeping them higher than the hill.
entries.literal: On the wall were already two towers; Xiaokuan bound timbers to extend them, keeping them always higher than the earthen hill to defend against it.

entries.zh: 歡使告之曰：「雖爾縛樓至天，我當穿地取爾。」
entries.en: Huan sent word: "Though you raise your towers to the sky, I will tunnel under and take you."
entries.literal: Huan sent word: "Though you bind your towers to the sky, I shall tunnel under and take you."

entries.zh: 乃鑿地為十道，又用術士李業興「孤虛法」，聚攻其北。
entries.en: He dug ten tunnels and used Li Yexing's "solitary and void" method, massing attack on the north.
entries.literal: He then dug ten tunnels and also used the adept Li Yexing's "solitary and void" method, massing attack on the north.

entries.zh: 北，天險也。
entries.en: The north was heaven's barrier.
entries.literal: The north was heaven's barrier.

entries.zh: 孝寬掘長塹，邀其地道，選戰士屯塹上。
entries.en: Xiaokuan dug a long moat to intercept the tunnels and posted warriors on its rim.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan dug a long moat to intercept the tunnels and chose warriors to camp on the moat.

entries.zh: 每穿至塹，戰士輒擒殺之。
entries.en: Whenever a tunnel reached the moat, the warriors seized and killed the diggers.
entries.literal: Whenever a tunnel reached the moat, the warriors seized and killed the diggers.

entries.zh: 又於塹外積柴貯火，敵有在地道內者，塞柴投火，以皮排吹之，一鼓皆焦爛。
entries.en: He piled firewood outside the moat; when enemies were in the tunnels, they blocked the mouths, cast fire, and blew with leather bellows—at one blast all were charred.
entries.literal: He also piled firewood and stored fire outside the moat; when enemies were in the tunnels, they blocked with wood, cast fire, and blew with leather bellows—at one blast all were charred.

entries.zh: 敵以攻車撞城，車之所及，莫不摧毀，無能御者。
entries.en: The enemy used battering chariots; wherever they reached, the wall gave way—none could stop them.
entries.literal: The enemy used battering chariots against the wall; wherever the chariots reached, nothing stood—they could not be stopped.

entries.zh: 孝寬縫布為幔，隨其所向張之，布既懸空，車不能壞。
