entries.en: Xiaokuan sewed cloth curtains and spread them where the chariots aimed; the cloth hung slack and the chariots could not break through.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan sewed cloth into curtains and spread them wherever the chariots aimed; the cloth hung slack in air and the chariots could not destroy.

entries.zh: 敵又縛松、麻於竿，灌油加火以燒布，並欲焚樓。
entries.en: The enemy bound pine and hemp on poles, poured oil, set fire to burn the cloth and the towers.
entries.literal: The enemy bound pine and hemp on poles, poured oil and added fire to burn the cloth, and meant also to burn the towers.

entries.zh: 孝寬作長鉤，利其刃，火竿將至，以鉤遙割之，松、麻俱落。
entries.en: Xiaokuan made long hooks with sharp blades; as the fire poles neared, he cut them from afar—pine and hemp fell together.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan made long hooks with sharp blades; as the fire poles neared, he cut them from afar with hooks—pine and hemp both fell.

entries.zh: 敵又於城四面穿地為二十道，其中施樑柱，縱火燒之。
entries.en: The enemy dug twenty tunnels on all four sides, set beams within, and burned them.
entries.literal: The enemy also dug twenty tunnels on all four sides of the city, set beams and pillars within, and set them afire.

entries.zh: 柱折，城崩。
entries.en: The pillars broke and the wall collapsed.
entries.literal: The pillars broke and the wall collapsed.

entries.zh: 孝寬隨崩處豎木柵以扞之，敵不得入。
entries.en: Xiaokuan raised wooden palisades wherever it fell; the enemy could not enter.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan raised wooden palisades wherever it fell and held them off; the enemy could not enter.

entries.zh: 城外盡攻擊之術，而城中守禦有餘。
entries.en: Every art of attack was spent outside; inside, defense still had surplus.
entries.literal: Outside the city every art of attack was spent; inside, defense still had surplus.

entries.zh: 孝寬又奪據其土山。
entries.en: Xiaokuan also seized their earthen hill.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan also seized and held their earthen hill.

entries.zh: 歡無如之何，乃使倉曹參軍祖珽說之曰：「君獨守孤城，而西方無救，恐終不能全，何不降也？」
entries.en: Huan could do nothing and sent Zu Ting of the granary registry to say, "You hold a lone city and the west sends no rescue—you cannot hold out; why not surrender?"
entries.literal: Huan could do nothing and sent Registrar of the Granary Zu Ting to persuade him, saying, "You alone hold a lone city while the west sends no rescue—you fear you cannot hold out in the end; why not surrender?"

entries.zh: 孝寬報曰：「我城池嚴固，兵食有餘。
entries.en: Xiaokuan replied, "My walls are strong, troops and grain abundant.
entries.literal: Xiaokuan replied, "My walls are strong and firm, troops and grain abundant.

entries.zh: 攻者自勞，守者常逸，豈有旬朔之間已須救援！
entries.en: Attackers weary themselves; defenders rest—how would I need rescue within a month!
entries.literal: Attackers weary themselves; defenders always rest—how could aid be needed within a ten-day month!

entries.zh: 適憂爾眾有不返之危。
entries.en: I only fear your host may not return.
entries.literal: I only fear your host may not return.

entries.zh: 孝寬關西男子，必不為降將軍也！」
entries.en: Xiaokuan is a Guanxi man—I shall never be a surrendering general!"
entries.literal: Xiaokuan is a Guanxi man—I shall never be a surrendering general!"

entries.zh: 珽復謂城中人曰：「韋城主受彼榮祿，或復可爾；
entries.en: Ting told the city, "Commandant Wei takes their pay—perhaps that can be forgiven;
entries.literal: Ting again told the people in the city, "Commandant Wei receives their honors and salary—perhaps that can be forgiven;

entries.zh: 自外軍民，何事相隨入湯火中！」
entries.en: but you soldiers and civilians—why follow him into fire and boiling water!"
entries.literal: but you soldiers and civilians—why follow him into boiling water and fire!"

entries.zh: 乃射募格於城中云：「能斬城主降者，拜太尉，封開國郡公，賞帛萬匹。」
entries.en: He shot a notice into the city: "Behead the commander and surrender—Grand Commandant, Duke of a founding state, ten thousand bolts of silk."
entries.literal: He then shot a recruitment notice into the city, saying, "Who can behead the city commander and surrender shall be made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed Duke of a founding state, and given ten thousand bolts of silk."

entries.zh: 孝寬手題書背，返射城外云：「能斬高歡者准此。」
entries.en: Xiaokuan wrote on the back and shot it back: "Behead Gao Huan—same reward."
entries.literal: Xiaokuan wrote on the back in his own hand and shot it back outside, saying, "Who can behead Gao Huan—same reward."

entries.zh: 珽，瑩之子也。
entries.en: Ting was Ying's son.
entries.literal: Ting was Ying's son.

entries.zh: 東魏苦攻凡五十日，士卒戰及病死者七萬人，共為一塚。
entries.en: Eastern Wei attacked for fifty days; seventy thousand fell in battle and sickness and were buried in one mound.
entries.literal: Eastern Wei attacked bitterly for fifty days in all; soldiers killed in battle and by sickness numbered seventy thousand, buried in one mound.

entries.zh: 歡智力皆困，因而發疾。
entries.en: Huan's wit and strength were exhausted, and he fell ill.
entries.literal: Huan's wit and strength were both exhausted, and he fell ill thereby.

entries.zh: 有星墜歡營中，士卒驚懼。
entries.en: A star fell in Huan's camp; the soldiers were alarmed.
entries.literal: A star fell in Huan's camp; soldiers were alarmed and afraid.

entries.zh: 十一月，庚子，解圍去。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on gengzi, he lifted the siege and left.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengzi, he lifted the siege and departed.

entries.zh: 十二月，己卯，歡以無功，表解都督中外諸軍，東魏主許之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on jimao, Gao Huan, having achieved nothing, resigned command of all armies; the Eastern Wei emperor permitted it.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on jimao, Huan, having achieved nothing, memorialized to resign as commander-in-chief of all armies within and without; the Eastern Wei ruler permitted it.

entries.zh: 歡之自玉壁歸也，軍中訛言韋孝寬以定功弩射殺丞相；
entries.en: When Gao Huan returned from Yubi, the army rumored that Wei Xiaokuan had killed the chancellor with a crossbow;
entries.literal: When Huan returned from Yubi, a rumor in the army said Wei Xiaokuan had killed the chancellor with a merit-fixed crossbow;

entries.zh: 魏人聞之，因下令曰：「勁弩一發，凶身自隕。」
entries.en: Western Wei heard and ordered, "One shot of a strong crossbow—the evil body falls."
entries.literal: the people of Wei heard it and thereupon ordered, "One shot of a strong crossbow—the evil body falls of itself."

entries.zh: 歡聞之，勉坐見諸貴，使斛律金作《敕勒歌》，歡自和之，哀感流涕。
entries.en: When Gao Huan heard it, he forced himself to receive the nobles, had Hulu Jin compose the "Song of the Tiele," sang with him, and wept.
entries.literal: When Huan heard it, he forced himself to sit and see the nobles, had Hulu Jin compose the "Song of the Tiele," joined in himself, and wept with grief moved.

entries.zh: 景素輕高澄，嘗謂司馬子如曰：「高王在，吾不敢有異；
entries.en: Jing had long held Gao Cheng light and once told Sima Ziru, "While the King of Gao lives I dare not differ;
entries.literal: Jing had long held Gao Cheng light and once told Sima Ziru, "While the King of Gao lives I dare not differ;

entries.zh: 王沒，吾不能與鮮卑小兒共事！」
entries.en: when he is gone I cannot serve a Xianbei stripling!"
entries.literal: when the King is gone I cannot serve with a Xianbei stripling!"

entries.zh: 子如掩其口。
entries.en: Ziru covered his mouth.
entries.literal: Ziru covered his mouth.

entries.zh: 及歡疾篤，澄詐為歡書以召景。
entries.en: When Gao Huan's illness grew grave, Gao Cheng forged his hand to summon Jing.
entries.literal: When Huan's illness grew grave, Cheng forged Huan's hand to summon Jing.

entries.zh: 先是，景與歡約曰：「今握兵在遠，人易為詐，所賜書皆請加微點。」
entries.en: Before this, Jing and Huan had agreed, "Holding troops afar, men easily deceive—mark every letter with a small dot."
entries.literal: Before this, Jing and Huan had agreed, "Now holding troops afar, men easily deceive—every letter granted, please add a small mark."

entries.zh: 歡從之。
entries.en: Huan agreed.
entries.literal: Huan agreed.

entries.zh: 景得書無點，辭不至；
entries.en: Jing received a letter without the mark and would not come;
entries.literal: Jing received a letter without the mark and declined to come;

entries.zh: 又聞歡疾篤，用其行台郎穎川王偉計，遂擁兵自固。
entries.en: hearing Huan was grave, he took counsel from Wang Wei of Yingchuan and held his troops.
entries.literal: hearing also that Huan's illness was grave, he used the counsel of his mobile headquarters gentleman Wang Wei of Yingchuan and then held his troops and fortified himself.

entries.zh: 先是，歡別使侯景將兵趣齊子嶺，魏建州刺史楊檦鎮車箱，恐其寇邵郡，帥騎御之。
entries.en: Before this, Gao Huan had sent Hou Jing toward Qizi Ridge; Yang Biao of Western Wei held Chexiang, feared a raid on Shao, and led cavalry to meet him.
entries.literal: Before this, Huan had separately sent Hou Jing with troops toward Qizi Ridge; Wei's Jianzhou inspector Yang Biao held Chexiang, feared he would raid Shao commandery, and led cavalry to meet him.

entries.zh: 景聞檦至，斫木斷路六十餘里，猶驚而不安，遂還河陽。
entries.en: Jing heard Biao was coming, felled trees and blocked the road for sixty li, yet remained uneasy and returned to Heyang.
entries.literal: Jing heard Biao had come, felled trees and blocked the road for more than sixty li, yet was still alarmed and uneasy, and returned to Heyang.

entries.zh: 庚戌，歡使段韶從太原公洋鎮鄴。
entries.en: On gengxu, Gao Huan sent Duan Shao with Duke Yang of Taiyuan to guard Ye.
entries.literal: On gengxu, Huan sent Duan Shao with Duke Yang of Taiyuan to guard Ye.

entries.zh: 辛亥，征世子澄會晉陽。
entries.en: On xinhai he summoned the heir apparent Gao Cheng to Jinyang.
entries.literal: On xinhai, he summoned the heir apparent Cheng to meet at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 歡謂澄曰：「我雖病，汝面更有餘憂，何也？」
entries.en: Gao Huan said to Gao Cheng, "Though I am ill, your face holds more worry—why?"
entries.literal: Huan said to Cheng, "Though I am ill, your face has still more worry—why?"

entries.zh: 澄未及對，歡曰：「豈非憂侯景叛邪？」
entries.en: Before Cheng could answer, Huan said, "You fear Hou Jing will rebel, do you not?"
entries.literal: Before Cheng could answer, Huan said, "Is it not fear that Hou Jing will rebel?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「然。」
entries.en: He answered, "It is so."
entries.literal: He answered, "It is so."

entries.zh: 歡曰：「景專制河南，十四年矣，常有飛揚跋扈之志，顧我能畜養，非汝所能駕御也。
entries.en: Huan said, "Jing has ruled Henan fourteen years with a soaring will; I could keep him—not you.
entries.literal: Huan said, "Jing has ruled Henan alone fourteen years; he has always had a soaring, overbearing will, but seeing that I could keep and nourish him—not you, who can drive him.

entries.zh: 今四方未定，勿遽發哀。
entries.en: The four quarters are not settled—do not hasten to announce mourning.
entries.literal: The four quarters are not yet settled—do not hasten to announce mourning.

entries.zh: 庫狄干鮮卑老公，斛律金敕勒老公，並性遒直，終不負汝。
entries.en: Kudi Gan, the Xianbei old man, and Hulu Jin, the Tiele old man—both are forthright and will never fail you.
entries.literal: Kudi Gan, the Xianbei old man, and Hulu Jin, the Tiele old man—both are forthright in nature and will never fail you.

entries.zh: 可朱渾道元、劉豐生，遠來投我，必無異心。
entries.en: Kezhuhun Daoyuan and Liu Fengsheng came from afar—they have no other heart.
entries.literal: Kezhuhun Daoyuan and Liu Fengsheng came from afar to join me—they surely have no other heart.

entries.zh: 潘相樂本作道人，心和厚，汝兄弟當得其力。
entries.en: Pan Xiangle was once a Taoist, mild and thick—you brothers should gain his strength.
entries.literal: Pan Xiangle was originally a Taoist; his heart is mild and thick—you brothers should gain his strength.

entries.zh: 韓軌少戇，宜寬借之。
entries.en: Han Gui is somewhat dull—treat him generously.
entries.literal: Han Gui is somewhat dull in youth—you should treat him generously.

entries.zh: 彭樂心腹難得，宜防護之。
entries.en: Peng Le's heart is hard to win—guard him.
entries.literal: Peng Le's inner heart is hard to win—you should guard and protect him.

entries.zh: 堪敵侯景者，唯有慕容紹宗，我故不貴之，留以遺汝。」
entries.en: Only Murong Shaozong can match Hou Jing; I did not honor him, but left him for you."
entries.literal: The one who can match Hou Jing is only Murong Shaozong; I therefore did not honor him highly, but left him for you."

entries.zh: 又曰：「段孝先忠亮仁厚，智勇兼備，親戚之中，唯有此子，軍旅大事，宜共籌之。」
entries.en: He also said, "Duan Xiaoxian is loyal, humane, wise, and brave—in kin, only this son; on great military affairs, plan together."
entries.literal: He also said, "Duan Xiaoxian is loyal, bright, humane, and thick, with wisdom and courage together—in kin, only this son; great military affairs, you should plan together."

entries.zh: 又曰：「邙山之戰，吾不用陳元康之言，留患遺汝，死不瞑目！」
entries.en: He also said, "At Mount Mang I ignored Chen Yuankang and left trouble for you—I cannot close my eyes in death!"
entries.literal: He also said, "At the battle of Mount Mang I did not use Chen Yuankang's counsel and left trouble for you—I cannot close my eyes in death!"

entries.zh: 相樂，廣寧人也。
entries.en: Xiangle was a man of Guangning.
entries.literal: Xiangle was a man of Guangning.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第159卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 159
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 159

entries.zh: 是時，唯荊、益所部尚完實，太尉、益州刺史武陵王紀移告征、鎮，使世子圓照帥兵三萬受湘東王節度。
entries.en: At this time only the domains of Jing and Yi remained intact. Grand commandant and Yizhou inspector Prince Ji of Wuling sent notice to the campaign armies and garrisons, ordering his heir Yuanzhao to lead thirty thousand men under Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: At this time only the parts held by Jing and Yi remained intact; Grand Commandant and Yizhou Inspector Prince Ji of Wuling sent notice to the campaign armies and garrisons, making his heir Yuanzhao lead thirty thousand men to accept Prince of Xiangdong Yi's command.

entries.zh: 圓照軍至巴水，繹授以信州刺史，令屯白帝，未許東下。
entries.en: Yuanzhao's army reached the Bashui. Yi made him Xinzhou inspector, ordered him to camp at Baidi, and would not let him march east.
entries.literal: Yuanzhao's army reached Bashui; Yi made him Xinzhou Inspector and ordered him to camp at Baidi, not permitting him to go east.

entries.zh: 益州沙門孫天英帥徒數千人夜攻州城，武陵王紀與戰，斬之。
entries.en: The monk Sun Tianying of Yizhou led several thousand followers in a night attack on the provincial city; Prince Ji of Wuling fought him and beheaded him.
entries.literal: The monk Sun Tianying of Yizhou led several thousand followers in a night attack on the provincial city; Prince Ji of Wuling fought him and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 黎州民攻刺史張賁，賁棄城走。
entries.en: The people of Lizhou attacked inspector Zhang Ben; Ben abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: The people of Lizhou attacked Inspector Zhang Ben; Ben abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 州民引氐酋北益州刺史楊法琛據黎州，命王、賈二姓詣武陵王紀請法琛為刺史。
entries.en: The provincials brought in Di chieftain Yang Fachen, Northern Yi inspector, to hold Lizhou, and sent the Wang and Jia clans to Prince Ji of Wuling to ask that Fachen be made inspector.
entries.literal: The provincials brought in the Di chieftain Yang Fachen, Northern Yi Inspector, to hold Lizhou, and ordered the Wang and Jia clans to go to Prince Ji of Wuling and ask that Fachen be made inspector.

entries.zh: 紀深責之，囚法琛質子崇顒、崇虎。
entries.en: Ji rebuked them severely and imprisoned Fachen's hostage sons Chongyan and Chonghu.
entries.literal: Ji rebuked them severely and imprisoned Fachen's hostage sons Chongyan and Chonghu.

entries.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑朔，法琛遣使附魏。
entries.en: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, Fachen sent envoys to submit to Wei.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day dingchou, Fachen sent envoys to submit to Wei.

entries.zh: 武陵王紀帥諸軍發成都，湘東王繹遣使以書止之曰：「蜀人勇悍，易動難安，弟可鎮之，吾自當滅賊。」
entries.en: Prince Ji of Wuling led the armies out from Chengdu; Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong sent envoys with a letter stopping him: "The men of Shu are fierce and hard to settle once stirred; younger brother, hold them—I myself will destroy the rebels."
entries.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling led the armies out from Chengdu; Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent envoys with a letter stopping him, saying, "The men of Shu are fierce and hard to settle once stirred; younger brother, you can hold them—I myself will destroy the rebels."

entries.zh: 又別紙云：「地擬孫、劉，各安境界；
entries.en: On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our lands may be compared to Sun and Liu—each keeps his border.
entries.literal: On a separate sheet he wrote, "Our lands may be compared to Sun and Liu—each keeps his border.

entries.zh: 情深魯、衛，書信恆通。」
entries.en: Our bond is deep as Lu and Wei—letters should always pass."
entries.literal: Our bond is deep as Lu and Wei—letters should always pass."

entries.zh: 武陵王紀遣潼州刺史楊乾運、南梁州刺史譙淹合兵二萬討楊法琛，法琛發兵據劍閣以拒之。
entries.en: Prince Ji of Wuling sent Tongzhou inspector Yang Qianyun and Nanliangzhou inspector Qiao Yan with twenty thousand men to attack Yang Fachen; Fachen raised troops and held Jiange Pass to resist.
entries.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling sent Tongzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun and Nanliangzhou Inspector Qiao Yan with a combined force of twenty thousand to attack Yang Fachen; Fachen raised troops and held Jiange Pass to resist.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第163卷卷第一百六十三
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 163
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 163, Roll 163

entries.zh: 周信州蠻冉令賢、向五子王等據巴峽反，攻陷白帝，黨與連結二千餘里。
entries.en: In Zhou's Xinzhou, the chieftains Ran Lingxian and Xiang Wuzi Wang seized the Ba Gorge and rebelled, capturing Baidi; their allies stretched along more than two thousand li.
entries.literal: Zhou's Xinzhou barbarians Ran Lingxian, Xiang Wuzi Wang, and others held the Ba Gorge and rebelled, storming and taking Baidi; their partisans linked for more than two thousand li.

entries.zh: 周遣開府儀同三司元契、趙剛等前後討之，終不克。
entries.en: Zhou dispatched Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and other commissioners of equal protocol in successive campaigns, but could not subdue them.
entries.literal: Zhou sent commissioners with equal protocol Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and others, in successive campaigns to attack them, but in the end could not overcome them.

entries.zh: 九月，詔開府儀同三司陸騰督開府儀同三司王亮、司馬裔討之。
entries.en: In the ninth month, an edict put Commissioner Lu Teng in overall command of Wang Liang and Sima Yi to suppress the rebels.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered Commissioner Lu Teng to supervise Commissioners Wang Liang and Sima Yi in attacking them.

entries.zh: 信州舊治白帝，騰徙之於八陳灘北，以司馬裔為信州刺史。
entries.en: Teng moved the Xinzhou seat from Baidi to north of the Eight Formations Shoals and appointed Sima Yi governor.
entries.literal: Xinzhou's old seat was at Baidi; Teng moved it north of Bachan Beach and made Sima Yi Governor of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 癸酉，上殂。
entries.en: On the day guiyou, the emperor died.
entries.literal: On guiyou, the emperor died.

entries.zh: 臣光曰：夫臣之事君，宜將順其美，正救其惡。
entries.en: Sima Guang comments: A minister serving his sovereign should nurture what is good in him and correct what is evil.
entries.literal: Chen Guang remarks: In a subject's service to his ruler, he ought to nurture and follow the ruler's virtues and straightly remedy his faults.

entries.zh: 孔奐在陳，處腹心之重任，決禮義之大計，苟以世祖之言為不誠，則當如竇嬰面辯，袁盎廷爭，防微杜漸以絕覬覦之心。
entries.en: Kong Huan in Chen occupied a position of deepest trust and weighed the gravest questions of ritual and right. If he believed Emperor Wendi's intent was false, he should have remonstrated as Dou Ying did in open debate, or as Yuan Ang did at court—stopping the rot early and cutting off all who would plot usurpation.
entries.literal: Kong Huan in Chen held a trusted post at the ruler's heart and decided great questions of ritual and righteousness; if he took Shizu's words as insincere, then he ought, like Dou Ying, to argue face to face, or like Yuan Ang, to contend in court—to stop evil at the sprout and cut off covetous designs.

entries.zh: 以為誠邪，則當請明下詔書，宣告中外，使世祖有宋宣之美，高宗無楚靈之惡。
entries.en: If he took the emperor at his word, he should have asked for a clear edict proclaimed at home and abroad, so that Wendi would gain the praise owed Duke Xuan of Song and the court would not repeat the evil of King Ling of Chu.
entries.literal: If he thought them sincere, then he ought to request a clear proclamation, announcing it within and without, so that Shizu might have the beauty of Duke Xuan of Song, and Gaozong would lack the evil of King Ling of Chu.

entries.zh: 不然，謂太子嫡嗣，不可動搖，欲保附而安全之，則當盡忠竭節，以死繼之，如晉之荀息，趙之肥義。
entries.en: Or, if he held the heir's position inviolable and wished only to cling to power in safety, he should have given his utmost loyalty unto death, as Xun Xi of Jin or Fei Yi of Zhao did.
entries.literal: Otherwise, holding that the crown prince as legitimate heir could not be shaken, wishing to preserve and attach himself and win safety, then he ought to exhaust loyalty and drain his integrity, following in death, like Xun Xi of Jin or Fei Yi of Zhao.

entries.zh: 奈何於君之存，則逆探其情而求合焉；
entries.en: Yet while the emperor still lived, he probed obliquely for the ruler's hidden wishes and strove to conform to them.
entries.literal: Yet how was it that while the ruler still lived, he inversely probed his feelings to seek accord?

entries.zh: 及其既沒，則權臣移國而不能救，嗣主失位而不能死！
entries.en: When the emperor was gone, powerful ministers seized the state and he could not save it; the rightful heir was dethroned and he would not die in his defense!
entries.literal: When he had already died, powerful ministers shifted the realm yet he could not rescue it; the heir lost his place yet he could not die for it!

entries.zh: 斯乃奸諛之尤者，而世祖謂之遺直，以托六尺之孤，豈不悖哉！
entries.en: Here was flattery at its worst—yet Emperor Wendi called him a minister straight as those of old and entrusted to him his young son: how perverse!
entries.literal: This is the extreme of flattery and deceit—yet Shizu called him a straight remnant of antiquity and entrusted to him a six-foot orphan: is this not perverse!

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第169卷卷第一百六十九
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 169.
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 169, the one hundred sixty-ninth fascicle.

entries.zh: 世民既行，元吉與妃嬪更迭為建成請，封德彝復為之營解於外，上意遂變，復遣建成還京師居守。
entries.en: After Shimin had set out, Yuanji and the consorts took turns pleading for Jiancheng; Feng Deyi again worked to clear matters for him from outside, and the emperor's mind changed; he sent Jiancheng back to the capital to remain as regent.
entries.literal: After Shimin had set out, Yuanji and the consorts took turns pleading for Jiancheng; Feng Deyi again worked to clear matters for him from outside, and the emperor's mind thereupon changed; he again sent Jiancheng back to the capital to remain and hold it.

entries.zh: 惟責以兄弟不睦，歸罪於太子中允王珪、左衛率韋挺、天策兵曹參軍杜淹，並流於巂州。
entries.en: He blamed only the brothers' discord, laid the guilt on Crown Prince Zhongyun Wang Gui, Left Weilü Wei Ting, and Heavenly Stratagem Army Caocan Du Yan, and exiled them all to Xizhou.
entries.literal: He only blamed them for discord among the brothers, laid the guilt on the crown prince's zhongyun Wang Gui, the Left Weilü Wei Ting, and the Heavenly Stratagem army caocan Du Yan, and exiled them all to Xizhou.

entries.zh: 挺，沖之子也。
entries.en: Wei Ting was the son of Wei Chong.
entries.literal: Ting was the son of Chong.

entries.zh: 初，洛陽既平，杜淹久不得調，欲求事建成。
entries.en: Earlier, after Luoyang had been pacified, Du Yan had long gone without an appointment and wished to attach himself to Jiancheng.
entries.literal: Earlier, after Luoyang had been pacified, Du Yan long went without an appointment and wished to attach himself to Jiancheng.

entries.zh: 房玄齡以淹多狡數，恐其教導建成，益為世民不利，乃言於世民，引入天策府。
entries.en: Fang Xuanling, knowing Yan's crafty ways, feared he would counsel Jiancheng to Shimin's further disadvantage and spoke to Shimin, who brought Yan into the Heavenly Stratagem headquarters.
entries.literal: Fang Xuanling, because Yan was full of crafty schemes, feared that he would instruct Jiancheng to Shimin's further disadvantage, and therefore spoke to Shimin and had him brought into the Heavenly Stratagem headquarters.

entries.zh: 初，洗馬魏徵常勸太子建成早除秦王，及建成敗，世民召徵謂曰：「汝何為離間我兄弟！」
entries.en: Earlier, Study Horse Wei Zheng had often urged Crown Prince Jiancheng to eliminate the Prince of Qin early; when Jiancheng fell, Shimin summoned him and said, "Why did you set my brothers against each other!"
entries.literal: Earlier, study horse Wei Zheng often urged crown prince Jiancheng early to eliminate the Prince of Qin; when Jiancheng was defeated, Shimin summoned Zheng and said: "Why did you divide and estrange my brothers!"

entries.zh: 眾為之危懼，徵舉止自若，對曰：「先太子早從徵言，必無今日之禍。」
entries.en: The courtiers feared for him, but Wei Zheng was perfectly composed and replied, "Had the late crown prince heeded my counsel in time, he would not have met today's fate."
entries.literal: The crowd for him was in peril and fear; Zheng's bearing and conduct were as if calm, and he replied: "Had the former crown prince early followed Zheng's words, there would necessarily be none of today's calamity."

entries.zh: 世民素重其才，改容禮之，引為詹事主簿。
entries.en: Shimin had long valued his talent; his manner changed and he treated Wei Zheng with honor, appointing him chief clerk to the household steward.
entries.literal: Shimin from of old valued his talent, changed countenance and honored him, and brought him in as household steward chief clerk.

entries.zh: 亦召王珪、韋挺於巂州，皆以為諫議大夫。
entries.en: He also recalled Wang Gui and Wei Ting from Xizhou and made them both Remonstrance and Discussion Grandees.
entries.literal: He also summoned Wang Gui and Wei Ting from Xizhou, and all were made admonishing and discussing grandees.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第191卷卷第一百九十一
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 191.
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 191, the one hundred ninety-first scroll.

entries.zh: 藝之初入朝也，恃功驕倨，秦王左右至其營，藝無故毆之。
entries.en: When Li Yi first came to court, he was arrogant and overbearing on account of his merit; when attendants of the Prince of Qin came to his camp, he beat them without cause.
entries.literal: When Yi first entered the capital for audience, relying on his merit he was arrogant and insolent; when attendants of the Prince of Qin came to his camp, Yi beat them for no cause.

entries.zh: 上皇怒，收藝繫獄，既而釋之。
entries.en: The Retired Emperor was enraged, had Yi arrested and imprisoned, but later released him.
entries.literal: The Retired Emperor was angry, seized Yi, and imprisoned him, but afterward released him.

entries.zh: 上即位，藝內不自安。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, Li Yi grew uneasy within.
entries.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, Yi inwardly could not feel secure.

entries.zh: 曹州妖巫李五戒謂藝曰：「王貴色已發！」
entries.en: Li Wujie, a sorcerer of Caozhou, told Li Yi: "Your noble aura has already appeared!"
entries.literal: Li Wujie, a sorcerer of Caozhou, said to Yi: "Your noble aura has already appeared!"

entries.zh: 勸之反。
entries.en: He urged Li Yi to rebel.
entries.literal: He urged him to rebel.

entries.zh: 藝乃詐稱奉密敕，勒兵入朝。
entries.en: Li Yi then falsely claimed to be acting on a secret edict and mustered his troops to march on the capital.
entries.literal: Yi then falsely claimed he was acting on a secret edict and mustered troops to enter the capital.

entries.zh: 遂引兵至幽州，幽州治中趙慈皓馳出謁之，藝入據幽州。
entries.en: He then marched on You Prefecture. Zhao Cihao, acting prefect of You Prefecture, rode out to meet him, and Li Yi entered and seized the prefecture.
entries.literal: He then led his troops to You Prefecture. Zhao Cihao, acting prefect of You Prefecture, galloped out to meet him, and Yi entered and seized You Prefecture.

entries.zh: 詔吏部尚書長孫無忌等為行軍總管以討之。
entries.en: An edict appointed Zhangsun Wuji, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and others as campaign commanders to suppress the rebellion.
entries.literal: An edict appointed Zhangsun Wuji, minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and others as campaign commanders to suppress him.

entries.zh: 趙慈皓聞官軍將至，密與統軍楊岌圖之，事洩，藝囚慈皓。
entries.en: When Zhao Cihao heard that the imperial army was approaching, he secretly plotted with Yang Ji, commander of the garrison, but the plot was discovered and Li Yi imprisoned Zhao.
entries.literal: Zhao Cihao, hearing that the imperial army was about to arrive, secretly plotted with Yang Ji, commander of the garrison, but the affair leaked out and Yi imprisoned Cihao.

entries.zh: 岌在城外覺變，勒兵攻之，藝眾潰，棄妻子，將奔突厥。
entries.en: Yang Ji, outside the city, realized what had happened, mustered troops, and attacked. Li Yi's forces collapsed; he abandoned his wife and children and fled toward the Türks.
entries.literal: Ji, outside the city, perceived the change, mustered troops and attacked; Yi's forces collapsed, and he abandoned his wife and children, intending to flee to the Türks.

entries.zh: 至烏氏，左右斬之，傳首長安。
entries.en: At Wushi, his attendants beheaded him and sent his head to Chang'an.
entries.literal: When he reached Wushi, his attendants beheaded him and sent his head to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 弟壽，為利州都督，亦坐誅。
entries.en: His younger brother Shou, military governor of Lizhou, was also executed in connection with the rebellion.
entries.literal: His younger brother Shou, who was military governor of Lizhou, was also executed on account of the affair.

entries.zh: 初，隋末喪亂，豪傑並起，擁眾據地，自相雄長；
entries.en: Earlier, amid the chaos at the end of the Sui, local strongmen rose everywhere, gathering followers, seizing territory, and ruling as rival chieftains;
entries.literal: Earlier, amid the ruin and disorder at the end of Sui, heroes rose together, gathering followers and seizing territory, each making himself a local strongman;

entries.zh: 唐興，相帥來歸，上皇為之割置州縣以寵祿之，由是州縣之數，倍於開皇、大業之間。
entries.en: when the Tang rose, they submitted in succession, and the Retired Emperor carved out new prefectures and counties to honor and reward them. As a result, the number of prefectures and counties doubled what it had been under the Kaihuang and Daye reigns.
entries.literal: when Tang arose, they came in succession to submit; the Retired Emperor carved out and established prefectures and counties to honor and reward them, and thereby the number of prefectures and counties doubled what it had been between the Kaihuang and Daye reigns.

entries.zh: 上以民少吏多，思革其弊；
entries.en: Because the people were too few and officials too many, the emperor sought to reform the abuse;
entries.literal: The Emperor, because the people were few and officials many, wished to reform this abuse;

entries.zh: 二月，命大加並省，因山川形便，分為十道：一曰關內，二曰河南，三曰河東，四曰河北，五曰山南，六曰隴右，七曰淮南，八曰江南，九曰劍南，十曰嶺南。
entries.en: in the second month he ordered a major consolidation of administrative units. Following natural geography, the realm was divided into ten circuits: Guannei, Henan, Hedong, Hebei, Shannan, Longyou, Huainan, Jiangnan, Jiannan, and Lingnan.
entries.literal: in the second month he ordered a great consolidation and reduction of offices; following the convenience of mountains and rivers, the realm was divided into ten circuits: first, Guannei; second, Henan; third, Hedong; fourth, Hebei; fifth, Shannan; sixth, Longyou; seventh, Huainan; eighth, Jiangnan; ninth, Jiannan; tenth, Lingnan.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第192卷卷第一百九十二
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 192
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 192, the one hundred ninety-second juan.

entries.zh: 突厥既亡，其部落或北附薛延陀，或西奔西域，其降唐者尚十萬口，詔群臣議區處之宜。
entries.en: Once the Turks had perished, some tribes submitted north to Xueyantuo, others fled west to the Western Regions; those who surrendered to Tang still numbered one hundred thousand people. An edict ordered the assembled ministers to debate how best to settle them.
entries.literal: Once the Turks had perished, some tribes submitted north to Xueyantuo, others fled west to the Western Regions; those who surrendered to Tang still numbered one hundred thousand people. An edict ordered the assembled ministers to debate how best to settle them.

entries.zh: 朝士多言：「北狄自古為中國患，今幸而破亡，宜悉徙之河南兗、豫之間，分其種落，散居州縣，教之耕織，可以化胡虜為農民，永空塞北之地。」
entries.en: Many court officials said, "The northern barbarians have been China's scourge since antiquity. Now that they are fortunately destroyed, all should be moved between the Yellow River south and Yan and Yu, their tribes divided and dispersed among prefectures and counties, taught to farm and weave—thus barbarian invaders can be turned into farmers and the northern frontier forever emptied."
entries.literal: Many court officials said: "The northern barbarians have been China's scourge since antiquity. Now that they are fortunately destroyed, all should be moved between the Yellow River south and Yan and Yu, their tribes divided and dispersed among prefectures and counties, taught to farm and weave—thus barbarian invaders can be turned into farmers and the northern frontier forever emptied."

entries.zh: 中書侍郎顏師古以為：「突厥、鐵勒皆上古所不能臣，陛下既得而臣之，請皆置之河北。
entries.en: Zhongshu Shilang Yan Shigu held, "Both Turks and Tiele were peoples that antiquity could not subjugate. Your Majesty has already made them subjects—please settle them all north of the Yellow River.
entries.literal: Zhongshu Shilang Yan Shigu held: "Both Turks and Tiele were peoples that antiquity could not subjugate. Your Majesty has already made them subjects—please settle them all north of the Yellow River.

entries.zh: 分立酋長，領其部落，則永永無患矣。」
entries.en: Appoint separate chiefs to lead their tribes, and there will never again be trouble."
entries.literal: Appoint separate chiefs to lead their tribes, and there will never again be trouble."

entries.zh: 禮部侍郎李百藥以為：「突厥雖雲一國，然其種類區分，各有酋帥。
entries.en: Libu Shilang Li Baiyao held, "Though the Turks are called one nation, their peoples are divided and each has its own chieftain.
entries.literal: Libu Shilang Li Baiyao held: "Though the Turks are called one nation, their peoples are divided and each has its own chieftain.

entries.zh: 今宜因其離散，各即本部署為君長，不相臣屬；
entries.en: Now we should take advantage of their dispersal and set up each original division as a separate chief, not subject to one another;
entries.literal: Now we should take advantage of their dispersal and set up each original division as a separate chief, not subject to one another;

entries.zh: 縱欲存立阿史那氏，唯可使臣其本族而已。
entries.en: even if we wish to preserve the Ashina clan, we can only make them rulers over their own tribe alone.
entries.literal: even if we wish to preserve the Ashina clan, we can only make them rulers over their own tribe alone.

entries.zh: 國分則弱而易制，勢敵則難相吞滅，各自保全，必不能抗衡中國。
entries.en: Split the state and it grows weak and easy to control; with rival powers equal, mutual destruction is hard—each will preserve itself and surely cannot stand against China.
entries.literal: Split the state and it grows weak and easy to control; with rival powers equal, mutual destruction is hard—each will preserve itself and surely cannot stand against China.

entries.zh: 仍請於定襄置都護府，為其節度，此安邊之長策也。」
entries.en: He further requested establishing a Protectorate at Dingxiang to command them—this is the long-term policy for securing the frontier."
entries.literal: He further requested establishing a Protectorate at Dingxiang to command them—this is the long-term policy for securing the frontier."

entries.zh: 夏州都督竇靜以為：「戎狄之性，有如禽獸，不可以刑法威，不可以仁義教，況彼首丘之情，未易忘也。
entries.en: Area Commander of Xia Prefecture Dou Jing held, "The nature of barbarians is like that of birds and beasts—they cannot be awed by penal law or instructed by benevolence and righteousness; moreover, their longing for their native hills is not easily forgotten.
entries.literal: Area Commander of Xia Prefecture Dou Jing held: "The nature of barbarians is like that of birds and beasts—they cannot be awed by penal law or instructed by benevolence and righteousness; moreover, their longing for their native hills is not easily forgotten.

entries.zh: 置之中國，有損無益，恐一旦變生，犯我王略。
entries.en: Settled within China, there is harm and no benefit—I fear that if rebellion arises suddenly, they will violate our royal domain.
entries.literal: Settled within China, there is harm and no benefit—I fear that if rebellion arises suddenly, they will violate our royal domain.

entries.zh: 莫若因其破亡之餘，施以望外之恩，假之王侯之號，妻以宗室之女，分其土地，析其部落，使其權弱勢分，易為羈制，可使常為籓臣，永保邊塞。」
entries.en: Better to take advantage of their ruin, bestow unexpected grace, grant them nominal titles of king and marquis, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their land and split their tribes, weaken their authority and scatter their strength so they are easy to tether and control—thus they can forever serve as frontier vassals and guard the border forever."
entries.literal: Better to take advantage of their ruin, bestow unexpected grace, grant them nominal titles of king and marquis, marry them to daughters of the imperial clan, divide their land and split their tribes, weaken their authority and scatter their strength so they are easy to tether and control—thus they can forever serve as frontier vassals and guard the border forever."

entries.zh: 溫彥博以為：「徙於兗、豫之間，則乖違物性，非所以存養之也。
entries.en: Wen Yanbo held, "Moving them to Yan and Yu would violate their nature—it is not the way to preserve and nurture them.
entries.literal: Wen Yanbo held: "Moving them to Yan and Yu would violate their nature—it is not the way to preserve and nurture them.

entries.zh: 請准漢建武故事，置降匈奴於塞下，全其部落，順其土俗，以實空虛之地，使為中國扞蔽，策之善者也。」
entries.en: I request following the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han, settling surrendered Xiongnu below the frontier, keeping their tribes intact and honoring their local customs, to fill empty lands and make them a shield for China—this is the wise policy."
entries.literal: I request following the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han, settling surrendered Xiongnu below the frontier, keeping their tribes intact and honoring their local customs, to fill empty lands and make them a shield for China—this is the wise policy."

entries.zh: 魏徵以為：「突厥世為寇盜，百姓之仇也；
entries.en: Wei Zheng held, "The Turks for generations have been raiders and plunderers—the enemies of the people;
entries.literal: Wei Zheng held: "The Turks for generations have been raiders and plunderers—the enemies of the people;

entries.zh: 今幸而破亡，陛下以其降附，不忍盡殺，宜縱之使還故土，不可留之中國。
entries.en: now that they are fortunately destroyed, Your Majesty, because they have surrendered, cannot bear to kill them all—you should release them to return to their homeland and not keep them within China.
entries.literal: now that they are fortunately destroyed, Your Majesty, because they have surrendered, cannot bear to kill them all—you should release them to return to their homeland and not keep them within China.

entries.zh: 夫戎狄人面獸心，弱則請服，強則叛亂，固其常性。
entries.en: Barbarians have human faces but beastly hearts—when weak they beg submission, when strong they rebel; such is their constant nature.
entries.literal: Barbarians have human faces but beastly hearts—when weak they beg submission, when strong they rebel; such is their constant nature.

entries.zh: 今降者眾近十萬，數年之後，蕃息倍多，必為腹心之疾，不可悔也。
entries.en: Now the surrendered number nearly one hundred thousand; in several years they will multiply severalfold—they will surely become a malady in the heartland, and there will be no undoing it.
entries.literal: Now the surrendered number nearly one hundred thousand; in several years they will multiply severalfold—they will surely become a malady in the heartland, and there will be no undoing it.

entries.zh: 晉初諸胡與民雜居中國，郭欽、江統，皆勸武帝驅出塞外以絕亂階，武帝不從。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jin, various barbarians were mixed among the people within China; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier to cut off the seeds of disorder, but Emperor Wu did not listen.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jin, various barbarians were mixed among the people within China; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier to cut off the seeds of disorder, but Emperor Wu did not listen.

entries.zh: 後二十餘年，伊、洛之間，遂為氈裘之域，此前事之明鑒也！」
entries.en: More than twenty years later, the lands between Yi and Luo became a domain of felt and fur—that is the clear mirror of events past!"
entries.literal: More than twenty years later, the lands between Yi and Luo became a domain of felt and fur—that is the clear mirror of events past!"

entries.zh: 彥博曰：「王者之於萬物。
entries.en: Yanbo said, "A true king toward all things—
entries.literal: Yanbo said: "A true king toward all things—

entries.zh: 天覆地載，靡有所遺。
entries.en: heaven covers and earth bears up; nothing is left out.
entries.literal: heaven covers and earth bears up; nothing is left out.

entries.zh: 今突厥窮來歸我，奈何棄之而不受乎！
entries.en: Now the Turks, in their extremity, come to submit—how can we cast them away and not receive them!
entries.literal: Now the Turks, in their extremity, come to submit—how can we cast them away and not receive them!

entries.zh: 孔子曰：『有教無類。』
entries.en: Confucius said, 'In teaching, there is no distinction of classes.'
entries.literal: Confucius said: 'In teaching, there is no distinction of classes.'

entries.zh: 若救其死亡，授以生業，教之禮義，數年之後，悉為吾民。
entries.en: If we save them from death, grant them livelihoods, and teach them ritual and righteousness, in several years they will all become our people.
entries.literal: If we save them from death, grant them livelihoods, and teach them ritual and righteousness, in several years they will all become our people.

entries.zh: 選其酋長，使入宿衛，畏威懷德，何後患之有！」
entries.en: Select their chiefs to enter palace guard service—awed by our might and cherishing our virtue, what afterward trouble could there be!"
entries.literal: Select their chiefs to enter palace guard service—awed by our might and cherishing our virtue, what afterward trouble could there be!"

entries.zh: 上卒用彥博策，處突厥降眾，東自幽州，西至靈州；
entries.en: The emperor finally adopted Yanbo's plan and settled the surrendered Turks from You Prefecture in the east to Ling Prefecture in the west;
entries.literal: The emperor finally adopted Yanbo's plan and settled the surrendered Turks from You Prefecture in the east to Ling Prefecture in the west;

entries.zh: 分突利故所統之地，置順、祐、化、長四州都督府；
entries.en: he divided the territory formerly under Tuli's command and established four area command offices: Shun, You, Hua, and Chang;
entries.literal: he divided the territory formerly under Tuli's command and established four area command offices: Shun, You, Hua, and Chang;

entries.zh: 又分頡利之地為六州，左置定襄都督府，右置雲中都督府，以統其眾。
entries.en: he also divided Jiali's territory into six prefectures, establishing the Dingxiang Area Command on the left and the Yunzhong Area Command on the right to govern the masses.
entries.literal: he also divided Jiali's territory into six prefectures, establishing the Dingxiang Area Command on the left and the Yunzhong Area Command on the right to govern the masses.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第193卷卷第一百九十三
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 193.
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, fascicle 193, the one hundred ninety-third volume.

entries.zh: 張守珪使平盧討撃使、左驍衞將軍安祿山討奚、契丹叛者，祿山恃勇輕進，爲虜所敗。
entries.en: Zhang Shougui sent Pinglu Strike Commissioner and Left Brave Guard General An Lushan against Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, overconfident, advanced rashly and was defeated.
entries.literal: Zhang Shougui sent Pinglu Strike Commissioner and Left Brave Guard General An Lushan to attack Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, relying on his courage, advanced rashly and was defeated by the enemy.

entries.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，守珪奏請斬之。
entries.en: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Shougui memorialized asking that he be executed.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Shougui memorialized requesting his execution.

entries.zh: 祿山臨刑呼曰：「大夫不欲滅奚、契丹邪！
entries.en: Facing execution, Lushan cried: "Commissioner, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!
entries.literal: As Lushan faced execution he cried: "Commissioner, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan!

entries.zh: 奈何殺祿山！」
entries.en: Why kill Lushan!"
entries.literal: Why kill Lushan!"

entries.zh: 守珪亦惜其驍勇，欲活之，乃更執送京師。
entries.en: Shougui, valuing his fighting skill, wished to spare him and sent him to the capital under guard instead.
entries.literal: Shougui also prized his fierce valor and wished to spare him, and so bound him and sent him to the capital.

entries.zh: 張九齡批曰：「昔穰苴誅莊賈，孫武斬宮嬪。
entries.en: Zhang Jiuling wrote in the margin: "Long ago Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.
entries.literal: Zhang Jiuling annotated: "In the past Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia and Sun Wu beheaded palace women.

entries.zh: 守珪軍令若行，祿山不宜免死。」
entries.en: If Shougui enforced military law, Lushan should not have been spared."
entries.literal: If Shougui's military law were enforced, Lushan ought not to escape death."

entries.zh: 上惜其才，敕令免官，以白衣將領。
entries.en: The Emperor prized his talent, pardoned him from office, and let him lead troops in plain clothes.
entries.literal: The Emperor prized his talent and ordered him pardoned from office, to lead troops as a commoner.

entries.zh: 九齡固爭曰：「祿山失律喪師，於法不可不誅。
entries.en: Jiuling insisted: "Lushan broke discipline and lost his army; by law he must die.
entries.literal: Jiuling firmly remonstrated: "Lushan violated discipline and lost the army; by law he cannot go unpunished.

entries.zh: 且臣觀其貌有反相，不殺必爲後患。」
entries.en: Moreover I see rebel features in his face; if he is not killed he will become a future scourge."
entries.literal: Moreover I observe that his appearance has the look of a rebel; if he is not killed he will surely become a later trouble."

entries.zh: 上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫識石勒，枉害忠良。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu mistaking Shi Le, wrongly destroy a loyal man."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le, wrongly harm a loyal man."

entries.zh: 竟赦之。
entries.en: In the end he was pardoned.
entries.literal: In the end he was pardoned.

entries.zh: 上之爲臨淄王也，趙麗妃、皇甫德儀、劉才人皆有寵，麗妃生太子瑛，德儀生鄂王瑤，才人生光王琚。
entries.en: As Prince of Linzi he had favored Consort Zhao Lifi, Consort Huangfu Deyi, and Lady Liu; Lifi bore Crown Prince Ying, Deyi bore Prince E Yao, and Lady Liu bore Prince Guang Ju.
entries.literal: When the Emperor had been Prince of Linzi, Consort Zhao Lifi, Consort Huangfu Deyi, and Lady Liu the Talented were all favored; Lifi bore Crown Prince Ying, Deyi bore Prince E Yao, and the Talented Lady bore Prince Guang Ju.

entries.zh: 及即位，幸武惠妃，麗妃等愛皆馳；
entries.en: After enthronement he favored Consort Wu Huifei, and the others waned in favor;
entries.literal: After his accession he favored Consort Wu Huifei, and affection for Lifi and the others slackened;

entries.zh: 惠妃生壽王瑁，寵冠諸子。
entries.en: Huifei bore Prince Shou Li Mao, favored above all other sons.
entries.literal: Huifei bore Prince Shou Mao, whose favor surpassed all other sons.

entries.zh: 太子與瑤、琚會於内第，各以母失職有怨望語。
entries.en: The Crown Prince met Yao and Ju privately, each venting resentment over his mother's fall from favor.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince met with Yao and Ju in the inner quarters, each speaking resentfully of his mother's loss of favor.

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉楊洄尚咸宜公主，常伺三子過失以告惠妃。
entries.en: Commandant of Cavaliers Yang Hui, married to Princess Xianyi, constantly watched the three princes' missteps and reported them to Consort Wu Huifei.
entries.literal: Commandant of Cavaliers Yang Hui, who had married Princess Xianyi, constantly watched the three sons' faults and reported them to Huifei.

entries.zh: 惠妃泣訴於上曰：「太子陰結黨與，將害妾母子，亦指斥至尊。」
entries.en: Consort Wu Huifei tearfully told the Emperor: "The Crown Prince is secretly building a faction and plotting to destroy me and my son—and he even rails against Your Majesty himself."
entries.literal: Consort Wu Huifei, weeping, complained to the Emperor, saying: "The Crown Prince has secretly formed a faction and will harm me and my son; he also insults Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 上大怒，以語宰相，欲皆廢之。
entries.en: The Emperor flew into a rage, told his chief ministers what she said, and declared he would remove all three princes.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered; he told the chief ministers and wished to depose them all.

entries.zh: 九齡曰：「陛下踐祚垂三十年，太子諸王不離深宮，日受聖訓，天下之人皆慶陛下享國久長，子孫蕃昌。
entries.en: Zhang Jiuling replied: "Your Majesty has ruled for nearly thirty years. The Crown Prince and the royal princes have never left the inner palace; day after day they receive your instruction. All the realm rejoices that your reign will be long and your line will flourish.
entries.literal: Zhang Jiuling said: "Your Majesty has occupied the throne for nearly thirty years; the Crown Prince and the princes have not left the inner palace, receiving the sage's instruction daily—all under Heaven rejoice that Your Majesty will long hold the state and that descendants will flourish in abundance.

entries.zh: 今三子皆已成人，不聞大過，陛下奈何一旦以無根之語，喜怒之際，盡廢之乎！
entries.en: All three are grown men now, and no serious wrongdoing has been reported. How can you, on the spur of anger, act on unsubstantiated gossip and disinherit them all at once!
entries.literal: Now all three sons have already become adults, and no great faults are heard—how can Your Majesty, in a moment of passion over baseless words, depose them all!

entries.zh: 且太子天下本，不可輕搖。
entries.en: Besides, the Crown Prince is the very foundation of the realm. That foundation must not be casually undermined.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Crown Prince is the root of all under Heaven—it must not be lightly shaken.

entries.zh: 昔晉獻公聽驪姬之讒殺申生，三世大亂。
entries.en: Long ago, Duke Xian of Jin heeded Li Ji's calumny and executed Crown Prince Shensheng—and three generations of chaos followed.
entries.literal: Of old, Duke Xian of Jin listened to Li Ji's slander and killed Shensheng; three generations suffered great disorder.

entries.zh: 漢武帝信江充之誣罪戾太子，京城流血。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han trusted Jiang Chong's fabricated charges against Crown Prince Li, and the capital ran with blood.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's false accusation against the Crown Prince Li, and the capital ran with blood.

entries.zh: 晉惠帝用賈後之譖廢愍懷太子，中原塗炭。
entries.en: Emperor Hui of Jin acted on Empress Jia's accusations and deposed Crown Prince Minhuai—and the heartland was laid waste.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin took Empress Jia's slander and deposed the Crown Prince Minhuai; the Central Plain was scorched to ruin.

entries.zh: 隋文帝納獨孤後之言黜太子勇，立煬帝，遂失天下。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to Empress Dugu, set aside Crown Prince Yong, and raised Yang Guang to the throne—and in the end lost the empire.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Empress Dugu's words, removed Crown Prince Yong, and installed Emperor Yang—thereby losing all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 由此觀之，不可不愼。
entries.en: The lesson of history is plain: such a step demands the utmost caution.
entries.literal: Viewed from this, one must be cautious.

entries.zh: 陛下必欲爲此，臣不敢奉詔。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty insists on this course, I cannot in conscience obey such an order."
entries.literal: If Your Majesty must do this, your servant dare not receive the command."

entries.zh: 上不悅。
entries.en: The Emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: The Emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 林甫初無所言，退而私謂宦官之貴幸者曰：「此主上家事，何必問外人！」
entries.en: Li Linfu said nothing at first. Afterward he took aside a favored eunuch and murmured: "This is a matter for the Son of Heaven's own household. Why consult outsiders at all?"
entries.literal: Li Linfu at first said nothing; on retiring he privately told a favored eunuch: "This is the sovereign's household affair—why must outsiders be consulted!"

entries.zh: 上猶豫未決。
entries.en: The Emperor wavered, unable to settle on a decision.
entries.literal: The Emperor hesitated and had not yet decided.

entries.zh: 惠妃密使官奴牛貴兒謂九齡曰：「有廢必有興，公爲之援，宰相可長處。」
entries.en: Consort Wu Huifei secretly sent her palace attendant Niu Guier to Zhang Jiuling with this offer: "One prince deposed means another raised. Back us, and you can keep your post as chief minister indefinitely."
entries.literal: Consort Wu Huifei secretly sent the office slave Niu Guier to tell Zhang Jiuling: "Where there is removal there must be elevation—if you lend support, you may long remain chief minister."

entries.zh: 九齡叱之，以其語白上；
entries.en: Zhang Jiuling rebuked the messenger and reported the overture to the Emperor;
entries.literal: Zhang Jiuling berated him and reported his words to the Emperor;

entries.zh: 上爲之動色，故訖九齡罷相，太子得無動。
entries.en: the Emperor's expression changed at the news. From that point until Zhang Jiuling was removed from office, the Crown Prince was left unshaken.
entries.literal: the Emperor was moved in countenance on account of this; therefore up until Zhang Jiuling's dismissal from the chief ministership, the Crown Prince remained unmoved.

entries.zh: 林甫日夜短九齡於上，上浸疎之。
entries.en: Li Linfu daily poisoned the Emperor's mind against Zhang Jiuling, and the Emperor steadily turned away from him.
entries.literal: Li Linfu day and night spoke ill of Zhang Jiuling before the Emperor; the Emperor gradually grew distant toward him.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑巻第二百一十四
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214

entries.zh: 李林甫領吏部尚書，日在政府，選事悉委侍郎宋遙、苗晉卿。
entries.en: Li Linfu held the ministry of personnel and was at the secretariat every day; he entrusted all selections entirely to Vice Ministers Song Yao and Miao Jinqing.
entries.literal: Li Linfu held the post of Minister of Personnel and was daily at the Secretariat; all matters of selection he entirely entrusted to Vice Ministers Song Yao and Miao Jinqing.

entries.zh: 御史中丞張倚新得幸於上，遙、晉卿欲附之。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi had recently won the emperor's favor, and Yao and Jinqing sought his patronage.
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi had recently won the emperor's favor, and Yao and Jinqing wished to attach themselves to him.

entries.zh: 時選人集者以萬計，入等者六十四人。
entries.en: Tens of thousands of candidates had assembled; only sixty-four passed the selection.
entries.literal: At the time candidates assembled in numbers of tens of thousands; those who passed into the selected ranks were sixty-four.

entries.zh: 倚子奭為之首，群議沸騰。
entries.en: Yi's son Shi ranked first, and public outrage erupted.
entries.literal: Yi's son Shi ranked first, and public talk seethed.

entries.zh: 前薊令蘇孝韞以告安祿山，祿山入言於上，上悉召入等人面試之，奭手持試紙，終日不成一字，時人謂之「曳白」。
entries.en: Former prefect of Ji Su Xiaoyun reported the affair to An Lushan, who brought it to the emperor. The emperor summoned all sixty-four passers for a personal examination. Shi held his paper all day and could not write a single character. People called it "dragging a blank sheet."
entries.literal: Former Ji Prefect Su Xiaoyun reported it to An Lushan; Lushan entered and spoke of it to the emperor. The emperor summoned all who had passed for a face-to-face examination. Shi held the examination paper in hand and throughout the day could not complete a single character. People of the time called this "dragging a blank."

entries.zh: 癸亥，遙貶武當太守，晉卿貶安康太守，倚貶淮陽太守，同考判官禮部郎中裴朏等皆貶嶺南官。
entries.en: On guihai day, Yao was demoted to prefect of Wudang, Jinqing to prefect of Ankang, and Yi to prefect of Huaiyang; the co-examiners, including Ministry of Rites section chief Pei Fei, were all sent to posts in Lingnan.
entries.literal: On the day guihai, Yao was demoted to Prefect of Wudang, Jinqing to Prefect of Ankang, Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang, and the co-examiners including Ministry of Rites Section Chief Pei Fei were all demoted to posts in Lingnan.

entries.zh: 晉卿，壺關人也。
entries.en: Jinqing came from Huguan.
entries.literal: Jinqing was a native of Huguan.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第215卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 215
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 215

entries.zh: 己亥，命大理少卿楊濟修好於吐蕃。
entries.en: On jihai, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yang Ji was ordered to restore friendly relations with Tibet.
entries.literal: On jihai, Yang Ji, vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was ordered to restore friendly relations with the Tibetans.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑 第224卷卷第二百二十四
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 224.
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 224.

entries.zh: 九月，丙辰，加昭義節度使劉悟同平章事。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the bingchen day, Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu was made Associate Chief Minister.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingchen, Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu was given the additional title of Associate Chief Minister.

entries.zh: 昭義節度使劉悟方去鄆州也，以鄆兵二千自隨為親兵。
entries.en: When Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu had left Yun Prefecture earlier, he kept two thousand Yun soldiers as a personal guard.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Zhaoyi Military Governor Liu Wu left Yun Prefecture, he took two thousand Yun troops with him as personal guards.

entries.zh: 八月，庚戌，悟暴疾薨，子將作監主簿從諫匿其喪，與大將劉武德及親兵謀，以悟遺表求知留後。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the gengxu day, Liu Wu died suddenly; his son Congjian, a chief secretary in the palace workshops, hid the corpse and, with General Liu Wude and the guard, planned to use Wu's deathbed memorial to secure Congjian's succession.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the gengxu day, Wu died suddenly of illness; his son, Chief Secretary of the Directorate of Palace Buildings Congjian, concealed the death and, with Grand General Liu Wude and the personal guard, plotted to use Wu's final memorial to request that Congjian be made acting military governor.

entries.zh: 司馬賈直言入責從諫曰：「爾父提十二州地歸朝廷，其功非細，只以張汶之故，自謂不潔淋頭，竟至羞死。
entries.en: Assistant Military Governor Jia Zhiyan burst in and upbraided Congjian: "Your father surrendered twelve prefectures to the throne—no small deed; yet over Zhang Wen he felt himself stained through and shamed unto death.
entries.literal: Assistant Military Governor Jia Zhiyan entered and rebuked Congjian, saying: "Your father brought the lands of twelve prefectures back to the court—his merit was not slight; only because of Zhang Wen did he deem himself defiled from head to foot and in the end died of shame.

entries.zh: 爾孺子，何敢如此！
entries.en: You reckless boy—how dare you behave thus!
entries.literal: You rash youth—how dare you act like this!

entries.zh: 父死不哭，何以為人！」
entries.en: Your father is dead and you will not mourn—what kind of man are you!"
entries.literal: Father dead yet no mourning—how can you be called human!"

entries.zh: 從諫恐悚不能對，乃發喪。
entries.en: Congjian, terrified and speechless, at last proclaimed the funeral.
entries.literal: Congjian, fearful and unable to reply, then announced the mourning.

entries.zh: 朝廷得劉悟遺表，議者多言上黨內鎮，與河朔異，不可許。
entries.en: When the court received Liu Wu's final memorial, many argued that Shangdang was an interior commandery, unlike the Hebei frontier, and that the request could not be granted.
entries.literal: The court received Liu Wu's final memorial. Many in the debate said that Shangdang is an interior commandery, different from the Hebei north, and could not be granted.

entries.zh: 左僕射李絳上疏，以為：「兵機尚速，威斷貴定，人情未一，乃可伐謀。
entries.en: The Left Vice Director Li Jiang submitted a memorial arguing: "Military opportunity demands speed, and decisive authority must be settled quickly. When hearts are divided, that is when you can overturn their plots.
entries.literal: The Left Vice Director Li Jiang submitted a memorial, holding: "Military opportunity favors speed; authority and decision value firmness; when men's hearts are not yet one, then one may attack their schemes.

entries.zh: 劉悟死已數月，朝廷尚未處分，中外人意，共惜事機。
entries.en: Liu Wu has been dead for months, yet the court still has not decided the matter. At court and in the provinces alike, everyone laments the missed chance.
entries.literal: Liu Wu has been dead for several months, yet the court has still not acted; inside and outside, all alike regret the lost opportunity.

entries.zh: 今昭義兵眾，必不盡與從諫同謀，縱使其半葉同，尚有其半效順。
entries.en: The Zhaoyi troops surely do not all stand with Congjian. Even if half join him, the other half will still submit to the throne.
entries.literal: Now the Zhaoyi army masses will certainly not all plot with Congjian; even if half side with him, still half will submit in loyalty.

entries.zh: 從諫未嘗久典兵馬，威惠未加於人。
entries.en: Congjian has never held military command for long, and neither authority nor kindness has yet won over the soldiers.
entries.literal: Congjian has never long commanded troops; authority and grace have not yet been imposed on the men.

entries.zh: 又此道素貧，非時必無優賞。
entries.en: The circuit has always been poor, and in ordinary times there are no lavish rewards to offer.
entries.literal: Moreover this circuit has always been poor; except at the right moment there will certainly be no generous rewards.

entries.zh: 今朝廷但速除近澤潞一將充昭義節度使，令兼程赴鎮，從諫未及佈置，新使已至潞州，所謂『先人奪人之心』也。
entries.en: The court should promptly appoint a general from the Ze-Lu region as Zhaoyi military commissioner and order him to rush to the post by forced marches. Before Congjian can organize anything, the new commissioner will already be at Luzhou—the classic case of seizing the initiative.
entries.literal: Now the court need only quickly appoint a general near Ze-Lu as Zhaoyi military commissioner, order him to travel night and day to his post; before Congjian can arrange matters, the new envoy will already be at Luzhou—what is called 'one who arrives first seizes men's hearts.'

entries.zh: 新使既至，軍心自有所繫。
entries.en: Once the new commissioner arrives, the troops will naturally have someone else to follow.
entries.literal: Once the new envoy arrives, the army's hearts will naturally have something to attach to.

entries.zh: 從諫無位，何名主張，設使謀撓朝命，其將士必不肯從。
entries.en: Without an appointment, what standing would Congjian have to press his claims? Even if he tried to block the court's decision, his officers and men would not follow him.
entries.literal: Congjian, without position—by what name would he assert himself? Even if he schemes to thwart the court's order, his officers and men will certainly not follow.

entries.zh: 今朝廷久無處分，彼軍不曉朝廷之意，欲效順則恐忽授從諫，欲同軍惡則恐別更除人，猶豫之間，若有奸人為之畫策，虛張賞設錢數，軍士覬望，尤難指揮。
entries.en: The court's long delay has left the army unsure of its intent. Men who want to submit fear Congjian will suddenly be confirmed; men who want to join in rebellion fear someone else will be appointed instead. In that uncertainty, schemers can inflate promised rewards, the soldiers' greed will be stirred, and command will become all the harder.
entries.literal: Now the court has long been without a disposition; that army does not understand the court's intent. Those wishing to submit fear that Congjian may suddenly be appointed; those wishing to join the army's wickedness fear that another man may be appointed instead. In their hesitation, if a villain plots for them and falsely inflates the sums for rewards and distributions, the soldiers will covet them and will be especially hard to command.

entries.zh: 伏望速賜裁斷，仍先下明敕，宣示軍眾，獎其從來忠節，賜新使繒五十萬匹，使之賞設。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to decide at once: issue a clear edict praising the troops' long loyalty, and grant the new commissioner five hundred thousand bolts of silk for rewards and distributions.
entries.literal: I humbly hope for a speedy decision, and also that a clear edict be issued first to show the army masses, praising their constant loyalty, and that five hundred thousand bolts of silk be granted the new envoy for distribution and rewards.

entries.zh: 續除劉從諫一剌史。
entries.en: Then appoint Liu Congjian to a prefectural post.
entries.literal: Then appoint Liu Congjian to a prefecture.

entries.zh: 從諫既粗有所得，必且擇利而行，萬無違拒。
entries.en: Once Congjian has gained something tangible, he is sure to take what benefits him and comply—he will not resist.
entries.literal: Congjian, having roughly gained something, will certainly choose what profits him and act; there is no chance he will defy.

entries.zh: 設不從命，臣亦以為不假攻討，何則？
entries.en: If he still refuses, I believe there is no need for military action either. Why?
entries.literal: If he does not obey the order, I also think there is no need to borrow an attack—why?

entries.zh: 臣聞從諫已禁山東三州軍士不許自畜兵刀，足明群心殊未得一，帳下之事亦在不疑。
entries.en: I have heard that Congjian has already forbidden soldiers in the three eastern prefectures from keeping weapons privately—proof enough that the ranks are far from united and that his own hold on them is shaky.
entries.literal: I hear that Congjian has already forbidden soldiers of the three Shandong prefectures from keeping arms and blades privately—enough to show that group hearts are especially not united; matters under his tent are also beyond doubt.

entries.zh: 熟計利害，決無即授從諫之理。」
entries.en: Weigh the gains and losses carefully, and there is simply no case for confirming Congjian at once."
entries.literal: On mature consideration of benefit and harm, there is certainly no principle of immediately appointing Congjian."

entries.zh: 時李逢吉、王守澄計議已定，竟不用絳等謀。
entries.en: By then Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng had already made up their minds, and Li Jiang's plan was never adopted.
entries.literal: At that time Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng's plans were already settled; in the end they did not use Jiang's stratagem.

entries.zh: 十二月，辛丑，以從諫為昭義留後。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on the xinchou day, Congjian was appointed acting military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, Congjian was made acting regent of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 劉悟煩苛，從諫濟以寬厚，眾頗附之。
entries.en: Liu Wu had been harsh and finicky; Congjian tempered that with lenience and generosity, and the troops came to favor him.
entries.literal: Liu Wu had been vexatious and exacting; Congjian supplemented this with lenience and generosity, and the masses quite attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 自元和之末，宦官益橫，建置天子在其掌握，威權出人主之右，人莫敢言。
entries.en: Since the close of the Yuanhe era the eunuchs had grown ever bolder, enthroning and deposing emperors at will. Their power eclipsed the throne itself, and no one dared protest.
entries.literal: From the end of the Yuanhe era the eunuchs grew ever more overbearing; they installed and removed emperors at their grasp, and their authority and power stood to the right of the sovereign—no one dared speak.

entries.zh: 辛已，上親策制舉人，賢良方正，昌平劉蕡對策極言其禍，其略曰：「陛下宜先憂者：宮闈將變，社稷將危，天下將傾，海內將亂。」
entries.en: On the xinsi day the emperor held the special civil examination for "upright and good" candidates. Liu Zhen of Changping answered with a memorial that laid bare the peril in the plainest terms: "Your Majesty's first concerns ought to be these: the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval, the altars of state are in danger, the realm is tottering, and turmoil is about to engulf the empire."
entries.literal: On the day xinsi the emperor personally examined the civil-service candidates of the special decree examination for "upright and good," and Liu Zhen of Changping answered the policy question by speaking bluntly of the disaster; in summary he said: "What Your Majesty should worry about first: the inner palace is about to change, the altars of state are about to be endangered, the realm is about to topple, and within the seas disorder is about to break out."

entries.zh: 又曰：「陛下將杜篡弒之漸，則居正位而近正人，遠刀鋸之賤，親骨鯁之直，輔相得以專其任，庶職得以守其官，奈何以褻近五六人總天下大政！
entries.en: He went on: "To choke off the drift toward regicide, hold the throne in dignity and keep honest men close. Banish the butcher's minions; cherish the blunt counselors who speak truth. Let your chief ministers govern, and let every office do its work—how can five or six favored eunuchs run the empire?
entries.literal: He also said: "If Your Majesty wishes to cut off the gradual growth of usurpation and regicide, then occupy the correct position and keep upright men near, keep far from the base of the knife and saw, be close to blunt, loyal remonstrators, let the chief ministers fully carry out their duties, and let the hundred offices keep to their posts—how can you let five or six lewd intimates hold all great government of the realm!

entries.zh: 禍稔蕭牆，奸生帷幄，臣恐曹節、侯覽復生於今日。」
entries.en: Disaster is ripening behind the palace walls; treachery is breeding within the curtained hall. I fear that Cao Jie and Hou Lan live again in our time."
entries.literal: Disaster ripens within the palace walls; treachery is born inside the curtain. I fear Cao Jie and Hou Lan are being reborn in our own day."

entries.zh: 又曰：「忠賢無腹心之寄，閫寺恃廢立之權，陷先君不得正其終，致陛下不得正其始。」
entries.en: He also wrote: "Loyal ministers have nowhere to place their trust. The eunuch commanders rest on the power to make and unmake emperors. They prevented your predecessor from ending his reign in peace, and they have kept you from beginning yours in legitimacy."
entries.literal: He also said: "Loyal ministers have no place to lodge their hearts; the eunuch commanders rely on the power to depose and establish [emperors]. They trapped the late emperor so that he could not end his reign properly, and they have caused Your Majesty not to begin yours properly."

entries.zh: 又曰：「威柄陵夷，籓臣跋扈。
entries.en: He also said: "Sovereign power erodes daily, while the military commissioners grow insolent on their borders.
entries.literal: He also said: "Imperial authority declines day by day; the frontier lords are arrogant and domineering.

entries.zh: 或有不達人臣之節，首亂者以安君為名；
entries.en: Some who lack a subject's restraint raise rebellion in the name of saving the throne;
entries.literal: Some who do not understand a subject's propriety take the lead in disorder in the name of securing the ruler;

entries.zh: 不究《春秋》之微，稱兵者以逐惡為義。
entries.en: without grasping the Spring and Autumn Annals' deeper lesson, men who march armies call it righteous to expel the wicked.
entries.literal: without probing the subtle meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, those who take up arms claim the righteousness of driving out evil.

entries.zh: 則政刑不由乎天子，征伐必自於諸侯。」
entries.en: Then law and punishment no longer flow from the Son of Heaven, and war is waged only at the command of the regional lords."
entries.literal: Then government and punishments no longer proceed from the Son of Heaven, and campaigns and punishments necessarily originate with the feudal lords."

entries.zh: 又曰：「陛下何不塞陰邪之路，屏褻狎之臣，制侵陵迫脅之心，復門戶掃除之役，戒其所宜戒，憂其所宜憂！
entries.en: He urged: "Block the road of secret malice. Cast out the emperor's coarse intimates. Curb the impulse to bully and threaten. Restore the old duties of gatekeeping and court order. Warn yourself where warning is needed; fear what ought to be feared.
entries.literal: He also said: "Why does Your Majesty not block the path of hidden evil, dismiss lewd and familiar ministers, restrain hearts that encroach and coerce, restore the work of guarding the gates and sweeping the court—warn where warning is due, and worry where worry is due!

entries.zh: 既不能治於前，當治於後，既不能正其始，當正其終；
entries.en: If you could not set things right at the start, set them right at the finish; if you could not cure what came before, cure what comes after.
entries.literal: If you could not govern what came before, govern what comes after; if you could not set right the beginning, set right the end;

entries.zh: 則可以虔奉典謨，克承丕構矣。
entries.en: Then you may reverently uphold the classics and inherit the great enterprise of your house.
entries.literal: then you may reverently follow the canonical models and succeed to the great foundation.

entries.zh: 昔秦之亡也失於強暴，漢之亡也失於微弱。
entries.en: Qin fell because its rule was too brutal; Han fell because its rule was too feeble.
entries.literal: In antiquity Qin perished through excess violence; Han perished through excess weakness.

entries.zh: 強暴則賊臣畏死而害上，微弱則奸臣竊權而震主。
entries.en: Under brutal rule, treacherous ministers, fearing for their lives, murder their lord; under feeble rule, crafty ministers seize power and terrify the throne.
entries.literal: When violent, treacherous ministers fear death and harm their sovereign; when weak, crafty ministers steal power and shake the throne.

entries.zh: 伏見敬宗皇帝不虞亡秦之禍，不翦其萌。
entries.en: I see that Emperor Jingzong never foresaw Qin's fate and never cut the evil in its bud.
entries.literal: I observe that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's manner of perishing and did not cut off the evil at its sprout.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下深軫亡漢之憂，以杜其漸，則祖宗之鴻業可紹，三、五之遐軌可追矣。」
entries.en: I pray that Your Majesty will take Han's fall deeply to heart and stop the rot while it is still slight. Then the ancestral legacy may be renewed and the distant example of the sage kings pursued once more."
entries.literal: I pray that Your Majesty will deeply take to heart Han's manner of perishing and cut off the gradual growth of evil; then the magnificent enterprise of the ancestors may be continued, and the distant model of the Three Dynasties may be pursued."

entries.zh: 又曰：「臣聞昔漢元帝即位之初，更制七十餘事，其心甚誠，其稱甚美，然而紀綱日紊，國祚日衰，奸宄日強，黎元日困者，以其不能擇賢明而任之，失其操柄也。」
entries.en: He also wrote: "When Emperor Yuan of Han first reigned he reformed more than seventy institutions. His intent was sincere and his praise resounded—yet order unraveled daily, the dynasty weakened daily, villains grew bolder daily, and the people suffered daily, because he could not choose wise men and give them real authority. He lost the tiller of state."
entries.literal: He also said: "I have heard that when Emperor Yuan of Han first took the throne he changed more than seventy institutions; his heart was very sincere and his reputation very fine—yet day by day the statutes grew disorderly, day by day the fortune of the state declined, day by day treachery grew strong, and day by day the common people were distressed, because he could not choose the worthy and enlightened and employ them, and lost hold of the helm."

entries.zh: 又曰：「陛下誠能揭國權以歸相，持兵柄以歸將，則心無不達，行無不孚矣。」
entries.en: He said further: "If Your Majesty will truly restore civil authority to the chief ministers and military authority to the generals, nothing you intend will go unheard and nothing you do will lack credibility."
entries.literal: He also said: "If Your Majesty can truly raise the authority of the state and return it to the chief ministers, and hold the military power and return it to the generals, then no thought will go unheeded and no act will fail to win trust."

entries.zh: 又曰：「法宜畫一，官宜正名。
entries.en: He also said: "Law should be one; offices should bear their proper names.
entries.literal: He also said: "The law ought to be uniform; offices ought to have correct names.

entries.zh: 今分外官、中官之員，立南司、北司之局，或犯禁於南則亡命於北，或正刑於外則破律於中，法出多門，人無所措，實由兵農勢異而中外法殊也。」
entries.en: Today outer and inner officials multiply without limit; southern and northern bureaus stand side by side. Break the law in one jurisdiction and flee to the other; punish a crime in the open court and see it voided within the palace. When law has many mouths, the people do not know where to stand. This comes of treating army and empire as separate worlds, with one law for the court and another for the realm."
entries.literal: Now the posts of outer officials and inner officials are set up separately, and the bureaus of the southern and northern administrations are established; if one violates prohibition in the south he flees to the north, if one is punished by regular law outside he breaks the statutes within—law issues from many gates and people have nowhere to turn; this truly comes from the differing power of soldiers and farmers and the differing law inside and outside."

entries.zh: 又曰：「今夏官不知兵籍，止於奉朝請；
entries.en: "He went on: Today the Ministry of War no longer knows the rolls of the armies and exists only to attend morning audience;
entries.literal: "He also said: "This summer the Ministry of War does not know the military registers and is limited to attendance at court;"

entries.zh: 六軍不主兵事，止於養勳階。
entries.en: The Six Armies no longer commanded military affairs but only cultivated ranks of merit.
entries.literal: The Six Armies do not command military affairs but only cultivate ranks of merit.

entries.zh: 軍容合中官之政，戎律附內臣之職。
entries.en: Military prestige merged with eunuch policy, and martial law became an inner-court function.
entries.literal: Military prestige merged with the policies of inner officials; martial law attached to the duties of palace servants.

entries.zh: 首一戴武弁，疾文吏如仇讎。
entries.en: Once they donned the warrior's cap, they hated civil officials like mortal enemies.
entries.literal: Once they donned the warrior's cap, they hated civil officials like mortal enemies.

entries.zh: 足一蹈軍門，視農夫如草芥。
entries.en: Once they entered the army gate, they treated farmers as worthless weeds.
entries.literal: Once they set foot in the army gate, they regarded farmers as worthless weeds.

entries.zh: 謀不足以翦除凶逆，而詐足以抑揚威福；
entries.en: They lacked the wit to destroy traitors, yet their cunning sufficed to raise and lower power and favor;
entries.literal: Their plotting was insufficient to cut down the vicious and rebellious, yet their deceit was enough to raise and lower power and favor;

entries.zh: 勇不足以鎮衛社稷，而暴足以侵軼里閭。
entries.en: their courage could not guard the realm, yet their violence could trample villages and lanes.
entries.literal: their courage was insufficient to guard the altars of state, yet their violence was enough to trample villages and lanes.

entries.zh: 羈紲籓臣，干陵宰舖，隳裂王度，汩亂朝經。
entries.en: They bound frontier ministers, overawed chief ministers, shattered royal standards, and muddied court regulations.
entries.literal: They bound frontier ministers, overawed chief ministers, shattered royal standards, and muddied court regulations.

entries.zh: 張武夫之威，上以制君父；
entries.en: They stretched warriors' might upward to control emperor and father;
entries.literal: They stretched the might of warriors upward to control father and sovereign;

entries.zh: 假天子之命，下以御英豪。
entries.en: they borrowed the Son of Heaven's mandate downward to command heroes and champions.
entries.literal: they borrowed the Son of Heaven's mandate downward to command heroes and champions.

entries.zh: 有藏奸觀釁之父，無伏節死難之義。
entries.en: There were fathers who hid treachery and watched for openings, but none who died loyal deaths for the throne.
entries.literal: There were fathers who hid treachery and watched for openings, but no righteousness of laying down one's life in loyal death.

entries.zh: 豈先王經文緯武之旨邪！」
entries.en: How could this be what the former kings intended when they wove culture and arms together!"
entries.literal: How could this be the intent of the former kings who wove culture and martial power together!"

entries.zh: 又曰：「臣非不知言發而禍應，計行而身戮，蓋痛社稷之危，哀生人之困，豈忍姑息時忌，竊陛下一命之寵哉！」
entries.en: He also wrote, 'I know that words bring calamity and action brings death — yet I grieve the realm's peril and pity the people's distress. How could I indulge the taboos of the age and steal Your Majesty's favor!'
entries.literal: He also said: 'Your servant is not unaware that words once spoken bring calamity in answer, and plans once carried out bring the body to execution — yet I grieve the altars of state in peril and pity the people's distress; how could I bear to indulge the taboos of the time and steal Your Majesty's single favor of office!'

entries.zh: 資治通鑑第241卷
entries.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 241
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 241

entries.zh: 劉稹腹心將高文端降，言賊中乏食，令婦人挼穗舂之以給軍。
entries.en: Gao Wenduan, a trusted Liu Zhen commander, defected and reported that the rebels were short of food and had women thresh grain by hand to feed the troops.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen's trusted general Gao Wenduan surrendered, saying that within the rebel ranks food was scarce and they had women rub ears of grain and pound them to supply the army.

entries.zh: 德裕訪文端破賊之策，文端以為：「官軍今真攻澤州，恐多殺士卒，城未易得。
entries.en: Deyu asked Wenduan how to break the rebels. Wenduan said: "If our army assaults Ze Prefecture head-on, we will lose many men and still may not take the city.
entries.literal: Deyu asked Wenduan for a strategy to defeat the rebels; Wenduan held that: "If government troops now truly attack Ze Prefecture, I fear many soldiers will be killed and the city will not be easily taken.

entries.zh: 澤州兵約萬五千人，賊常分兵太半，潛伏山谷，伺官軍攻城疲弊，則四集救之，官軍必失利。
