entries.en: Ze holds about fifteen thousand men. The rebels habitually keep more than half their force hidden in the hills, waiting until our siege troops are exhausted, then converge from every direction—the assault will fail.
entries.literal: Ze Prefecture has about fifteen thousand troops; the rebels often divide more than half their forces, lie hidden in valleys, wait until government troops are worn out from attacking the city, then gather from four sides to rescue it, and government troops will certainly suffer defeat.

entries.zh: 今請令陳許軍過乾河立寨，自寨城連延築為夾城，環繞澤州，日遣大軍布陳於外以扞救兵。
entries.en: Instead, have the Chenxu army cross the Gan River and build a camp, then extend linked walls in a double enclosure all around Ze. Each day station a large force outside to block relief columns.
entries.literal: Now I ask that the Chenxu army be ordered to cross the Gan River and establish a camp, and from the camp city continuously build a twin-walled encirclement ringing Ze Prefecture, daily sending large forces to deploy formations outside to ward off relief troops.

entries.zh: 賊見圍城將合，必出大戰；
entries.en: Seeing the ring about to close, the rebels will surely sally out for a decisive fight;
entries.literal: When the rebels see the siege walls about to close, they will certainly come out for a great battle;

entries.zh: 待其敗北，然後乘勢可取。」
entries.en: once they are beaten and retreating, we can take the city at a stroke."
entries.literal: wait until they are defeated and flee north, then ride the momentum and they can be taken."

entries.zh: 德裕奏請詔示王宰。
entries.en: Deyu memorialized that this plan be sent to Wang Zai by imperial order.
entries.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict be issued to inform Wang Zai.

entries.zh: 文端又言：「固鎮寨四崖懸絕，勢不可攻。
entries.en: Wenduan added: "The Guzhen stockade sits on sheer cliffs on all four sides and cannot be stormed.
entries.literal: Wenduan also said: "The Guzhen camp's four cliffs hang sheer; by its terrain it cannot be attacked.

entries.zh: 然寨中無水，皆飲澗水，在寨東南約一里許。
entries.en: But the camp has no water of its own; everyone drinks from a stream about a li to the southeast.
entries.literal: Yet within the camp there is no water; all drink stream water about one li southeast of the camp.

entries.zh: 宜令王逢進兵逼之，絕其水道，不過三日，賊必棄寨遁去，官軍即可追躡。
entries.en: Have Wang Feng advance and seize the stream. Within three days the rebels will abandon the camp; our troops can then run them down.
entries.literal: It is fitting to order Wang Feng to advance troops and press them, cut off their water route—in no more than three days the rebels will surely abandon the camp and flee, and government troops can immediately pursue.

entries.zh: 前十五里至青龍寨，亦四崖懸絕，水在寨外，可以前法取也。
entries.en: Fifteen li farther on lies Qinglong Camp, equally cliff-bound with its water outside—the same method will work there.
entries.literal: Fifteen li ahead is Qinglong Camp, likewise with four sheer cliffs; water is outside the camp, and the previous method can be used to take it.

entries.zh: 其東十五里則沁州城。」
entries.en: Fifteen li east of that stands Qin Prefecture city."
entries.literal: Fifteen li east of that is Qin Prefecture city."

entries.zh: 德裕奏請詔示王逢。
entries.en: Deyu memorialized that these instructions be sent to Wang Feng by imperial order.
entries.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict be issued to inform Wang Feng.

entries.zh: 文端又言：「都頭王釗將萬兵戍洺州，劉稹既族薛茂卿，又誅刑洺救援兵馬使談朝義兄弟三人，釗自是疑懼。
entries.en: Wenduan also said: "Commander Wang Zhao holds Ming Prefecture with ten thousand men. Liu Zhen had already wiped out the Xue Maqing clan and executed Tan Chaoyi, the Ming relief commander, together with his three brothers. Zhao has been fearful and suspicious ever since.
entries.literal: Wenduan also said: "Commander Wang Zhao leads ten thousand troops garrisoning Ming Prefecture. After Liu Zhen had the Xue Maqing clan executed and also put to death the Ming relief army commander Tan Chaoyi and his three brothers, Zhao from that time was suspicious and afraid.

entries.zh: 稹遣使召之，釗不肯入，士卒皆嘩噪，釗必不為稹用。
entries.en: Zhen sent to summon him, but Zhao would not come in; his troops are in an uproar. He will not fight for Zhen.
entries.literal: Zhen sent envoys to summon him; Zhao refused to enter, the soldiers all clamored, and Zhao will certainly not serve Zhen.

entries.zh: 但釗及士卒家屬皆在潞州，又士卒恐己降為官軍所殺，招之必不肯來。
entries.en: Yet Zhao's and his men's families are all in Lu Prefecture, and the troops fear that surrender means execution. They will not come if we merely call.
entries.literal: But Zhao and the soldiers' families are all in Lu Prefecture, and moreover the soldiers fear that if they surrender they will be killed by government troops; if summoned they will certainly not come.

entries.zh: 惟有諭意於釗，使引兵入潞州取稹。
entries.en: We should instead make our terms clear to Zhao: lead your men into Lu Prefecture and seize Liu Zhen.
entries.literal: Only by conveying our intent to Zhao, making him lead troops into Lu Prefecture to seize Zhen.

entries.zh: 事成之日，許除別道節度使，仍厚有賜與，庶幾肯從。」
entries.en: Promise him a military governorship on another circuit and rich rewards when he succeeds—then he may agree."
entries.literal: On the day the affair succeeds, promise to appoint him military governor of another circuit and still give generous rewards—then perhaps he will consent."

entries.zh: 德裕奏請詔何弘潛遣人諭以此意。
entries.en: Deyu memorialized that He Hongjing be ordered by edict to send an envoy with this proposal.
entries.literal: Deyu memorialized asking that an edict order He Hongjing to send someone to explain this intent.

entries.zh: 劉稹年少懦弱，押牙王協、宅內兵馬使李士貴用事，專聚貨財，府庫充溢，而將士有功無賞，由是人心離怨。
entries.en: Liu Zhen was young and timid. Wang Xie, his yamen guard, and Li Shigui, commander of the household troops, ran affairs, hoarding wealth until the vaults brimmed while meritorious officers went unrewarded. Disaffection spread through the ranks.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen was young and weak; the yamen guard Wang Xie and the household army commander Li Shigui held power, devoted solely to amassing wealth until the treasuries overflowed, while officers and soldiers who had merit received no reward—thereby hearts turned away in resentment.

entries.zh: 劉從諫妻裴氏，冕之支孫也，憂稹將敗，其弟問典兵在山東，欲召之使掌軍政。
entries.en: Lady Pei, Liu Congjian's widow and a collateral descendant of Pei Mian, feared Zhen's fall. Her younger brother Wen commanded troops in Shandong; she wanted to recall him to take charge of the army.
entries.literal: Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was a collateral descendant of Pei Mian; fearing Zhen would be defeated, she wished to summon her younger brother Wen, who commanded troops in Shandong, to make him manage military affairs.

entries.zh: 士貴恐問至奪己權，且洩其奸狀，乃曰：「山東之事仰成於五舅，若召之，是無三州也。」
entries.en: Shigui feared Wen would displace him and expose his corruption. He said: "Shandong has been entrusted to the Fifth Uncle; recall him and we lose the three prefectures."
entries.literal: Shigui feared that if Wen arrived he would seize his authority and also expose his wicked conduct, so he said: "Shandong affairs rely on completion by the Fifth Uncle; if he is summoned, that means losing the three prefectures."

entries.zh: 乃上。
entries.en: He then withdrew.
entries.literal: He then went up.

entries.zh: 八月，辛卯，鎮、魏奏邢、洺、磁三州降，宰相入賀。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, the Zhen and Wei armies reported the surrender of Xing, Ming, and Ci. The chief ministers came in to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, Zhen and Wei reported that Xing, Ming, and Ci—the three prefectures—had surrendered; the chief ministers entered to congratulate.

entries.zh: 李德裕曰：「昭義根本盡在山東，三州降，則上黨不日有變矣。」
entries.en: Li Deyu said: "Zhaoyi's strength lay entirely in Shandong. With those three prefectures gone, Shangdang will collapse before long."
entries.literal: Li Deyu said: "Zhaoyi's foundation is entirely in Shandong; with the three prefectures surrendered, Shangdang will before long have change."

entries.zh: 上曰：「郭誼必梟劉稹以自贖。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Guo Yi is sure to deliver Liu Zhen's head to save his own skin."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Guo Yi will certainly present Liu Zhen's head to redeem himself."

entries.zh: 德裕曰：「誠如聖料。」
entries.en: Deyu said: "Your Majesty reads the situation exactly right."
entries.literal: Deyu said: "It is truly as Your Sagely foresight judged."

entries.zh: 上曰：「於今所宜先處者何事？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked: "What should we settle first, now?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Of what should be handled first at present?"

entries.zh: 德裕請以給事中盧弘止為三州留後，曰：「萬一鎮、魏請占三州，朝廷難於可否。」
entries.en: Deyu proposed appointing Supervising Secretary Lu Hongzhi regent of the three prefectures. "If Zhen and Wei ask to keep them," he said, "the court will be hard pressed to refuse yet should not concede."
entries.literal: Deyu requested that Supervising Secretary Lu Hongzhi be made regent of the three prefectures, saying: "In the event Zhen and Wei request to occupy the three prefectures, the court will find it hard to grant or refuse."

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The Emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Emperor followed this.

entries.zh: 詔山南東道兼昭義節度使盧鈞乘驛赴鎮。
entries.en: An edict ordered Lu Jun—governor of Shannan East who also held Zhaoyi—to hurry to his command by post relay.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Lu Jun, military governor of Shannan East Circuit who also held Zhaoyi, to ride post-horses and proceed to his post.

entries.zh: 王協薦王釗為洺州都知兵馬使。
entries.en: Wang Xie recommended Wang Zhao as overall commander of Ming Prefecture's forces.
entries.literal: Wang Xie recommended Wang Zhao as Ming Prefecture commander of military affairs.

entries.zh: 釗得眾心，而多不遵使府約束，同列高元武、安玉言其有貳心。
entries.en: Zhao won the soldiers' loyalty but often ignored headquarters orders. His peers Gao Yuanwu and An Yu accused him of disloyalty.
entries.literal: Zhao won the troops' hearts, yet often did not follow the headquarters' regulations; his colleagues Gao Yuanwu and An Yu said he had a divided heart.

entries.zh: 稹召之，釗辭以「到洺州未立少功，實所慚恨，乞留數月，然後詣府。」
entries.en: Zhen summoned him. Zhao pleaded: "I have done little since reaching Ming and am ashamed to face headquarters. Grant me a few more months, then I will come in."
entries.literal: Zhen summoned him; Zhao declined on the grounds that "since arriving at Ming Prefecture I have achieved little merit—this is truly my shame and regret; I beg to remain several months and then come to headquarters."

entries.zh: 許之，王協請稅商人，每州遣軍將一人主之，名為稅商，實籍編戶家貲，至於什器無所遺，皆估為絹匹，十分取其二，率高其估。
entries.en: Zhen agreed. Wang Xie proposed a merchant tax: each prefecture would send an officer to levy it. In practice they inventoried every registered household's assets down to household goods, appraised everything in silk bolts, and took two-tenths—always at inflated valuations.
entries.literal: Permission was granted. Wang Xie requested to tax merchants: each prefecture would send one army officer to supervise it, called "merchant tax," but in fact they registered registered households' property; even utensils were not omitted—all were appraised as silk bolts, two-tenths taken, and the appraisals were usually set high.

entries.zh: 民竭浮財及糗糧輸之，不能充，皆璟璟不安。
entries.en: People drained their movable property and grain stores and still could not meet the demand; everywhere there was unrest and fear.
entries.literal: The people exhausted floating wealth and dry provisions to pay it yet could not fill the quota; all were anxious and uneasy.

entries.zh: 軍將劉溪尤貪殘，劉從諫棄不用。
entries.en: The officer Liu Xi was notoriously rapacious; Liu Congjian had long refused to employ him.
entries.literal: The army officer Liu Xi was especially greedy and cruel; Liu Congjian had cast him aside and not used him.

entries.zh: 溪厚賂王協，協以刑州富商最多，命溪主之。
entries.en: Xi bribed Wang Xie heavily. Xie assigned him Xing Prefecture, where the richest merchants were concentrated.
entries.literal: Xi gave Wang Xie heavy bribes; Xie, because Xing Prefecture had the most wealthy merchants, ordered Xi to supervise it.

entries.zh: 裴問所將兵號「夜飛」，多富商子弟，溪至，悉拘其父兄。
entries.en: Pei Wen's unit, the "Night Flight," was largely drawn from merchant families. When Xi arrived he seized their fathers and elder brothers.
entries.literal: The troops Pei Wen commanded were called "Night Flight," mostly sons of wealthy merchants; when Xi arrived he detained all their fathers and elder brothers.

entries.zh: 軍士訴於問，問為之請，溪不許，以不遜語答之。
entries.en: The soldiers appealed to Wen, who interceded for them. Xi refused and answered with insults.
entries.literal: The soldiers appealed to Wen; Wen pleaded for them, but Xi would not agree and answered with insolent words.

entries.zh: 問怒，密與麾下謀殺溪歸國，並告刺史崔嘏，嘏從之。
entries.en: Wen, furious, secretly plotted with his men to kill Xi and submit to the court. He told Prefect Cui Gu, who agreed.
entries.literal: Wen was enraged, secretly plotted with his subordinates to kill Xi and return to allegiance with the state, and also informed Prefect Cui Gu, who agreed.

entries.zh: 丙子，嘏、問閉城，斬城中大將四人，請降於王元逵。
entries.en: On the day bingzi, Gu and Wen shut the gates, executed four senior officers in the city, and offered surrender to Wang Yuankui.
entries.literal: On the day bingzi, Gu and Wen closed the city, beheaded four great generals in the city, and requested surrender to Wang Yuankui.

entries.zh: 時高元武在黨山，聞之，亦降。
entries.en: Gao Yuanwu, then at Dang Mountain, heard the news and surrendered as well.
entries.literal: At that time Gao Yuanwu was at Dang Mountain; on hearing this, he also surrendered.

entries.zh: 先是使府賜洺州軍士布，人一端，尋有帖以折冬賜。
entries.en: Headquarters had earlier given each Ming soldier a bolt of cloth, and a notice soon followed promising a mid-winter bonus.
entries.literal: Earlier the headquarters had granted Ming Prefecture soldiers cloth, one bolt per man; soon there was a notice for a mid-winter grant.

entries.zh: 會稅商軍將至洺州，王釗因人不安，謂軍士曰：「留後年少，政非己出。
entries.en: As the tax officer was about to reach Ming, Zhao, sensing the troops' unrest, told them: "The young commissioner does not truly rule.
entries.literal: Just as the merchant-tax army officer was about to reach Ming Prefecture, Wang Zhao, because the people were uneasy, said to the soldiers: "The acting commissioner is young; government is not his own.

entries.zh: 今倉庫充實，足支十年，豈可不少散之以慰勞苦之士！
entries.en: The warehouses are full enough for ten years. Should we not open them a little to reward men who have suffered?
entries.literal: Now the storehouses are full, enough to last ten years—how can we not distribute a little to comfort the toiling soldiers!

entries.zh: 使貼不可用也。」
entries.en: Ignore headquarters' notice."
entries.literal: The headquarters notice cannot be used."

entries.zh: 乃擅開倉庫，給士卒人絹一匹，谷十二石，士卒大喜。
entries.en: He opened the stores on his own authority and gave each man a bolt of silk and twelve piculs of grain. The troops were overjoyed.
entries.literal: He then on his own authority opened the storehouses and gave each soldier one bolt of silk and twelve piculs of grain; the soldiers were greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 釗遂閉城請降於何弘敬。
entries.en: Zhao then shut the gates and offered surrender to He Hongjing.
entries.literal: Zhao then closed the city and requested surrender to He Hongjing.

entries.zh: 安玉在磁州，聞二州降，亦降於弘敬。
entries.en: An Yu at Ci Prefecture, hearing that both prefectures had submitted, surrendered to Hongjing as well.
entries.literal: An Yu was at Ci Prefecture; on hearing that the two prefectures had surrendered, he also surrendered to Hongjing.

entries.zh: 堯山都知失馬使魏元談等降於王元逵，元逵以其久不下，皆殺之。
entries.en: Wei Yuantan, commander at Yaoshan, and others surrendered to Wang Yuankui, who executed them all for having held out so long.
entries.literal: The Yaoshan commander Wei Yuantan and others surrendered to Wang Yuankui; Yuankui, because they had long not submitted, killed them all.

entries.zh: 潞人聞三州降，大懼。
entries.en: When Lu Prefecture heard that the three prefectures had fallen, panic spread.
entries.literal: The people of Lu heard the three prefectures had surrendered and were greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 郭誼、王協謀殺劉稹以自贖，稹再從兄中軍使匡周兼押牙，誼患之，言於稹曰：「十三郎在牙院，諸將皆莫敢言事，恐為十三郎所疑而獲罪，以此失山東。
entries.en: Guo Yi and Wang Xie plotted to kill Liu Zhen and save themselves. Zhen's cousin Kuang Zhou commanded the central army and also held the yamen guard; Yi feared him. He told Zhen: "With the Thirteenth Son in the headquarters courtyard, no general dares speak freely—we lost Shandong because of it.
entries.literal: Guo Yi and Wang Xie plotted to kill Liu Zhen to redeem themselves; Zhen's second cousin once removed, the central army commander Kuang Zhou who also held the yamen guard, was a worry to Yi, who said to Zhen: "The Thirteenth Son is in the yamen courtyard; the generals all dare not speak on affairs, fearing the Thirteenth Son's suspicion and punishment—thereby we lost Shandong.

entries.zh: 今誠得十三郎不入，則諸將始敢盡言，采於眾人，必獲長策。」
entries.en: Keep him out, and the officers will finally speak plainly. Take counsel from all sides and we are sure to find a way forward."
entries.literal: Now if we can truly keep the Thirteenth Son from entering, then the generals will begin to dare speak fully; gathering from the multitude, we will certainly obtain a long-term plan."

entries.zh: 稹召匡周諭之，使稱疾不入。
entries.en: Zhen summoned Kuang Zhou and told him to stay away on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: Zhen summoned Kuang Zhou and instructed him to plead illness and not enter.

entries.zh: 匡周怒曰：「我在院中，故諸將不敢有異圖；
entries.en: Kuang Zhou flared up: "While I am here, the generals dare not plot;
entries.literal: Kuang Zhou angrily said: "While I am in the courtyard, therefore the generals dare not have divergent designs;

entries.zh: 我出院，家必滅矣！」
entries.en: if I leave, our house is finished!"
entries.literal: if I leave the courtyard, the family will certainly be destroyed!"

entries.zh: 稹固請之，匡周不得已，彈指而出。
entries.en: Zhen insisted. Kuang Zhou had no choice: he snapped his fingers and walked out.
entries.literal: Zhen firmly pressed him; Kuang Zhou had no choice, snapped his fingers, and went out.

entries.zh: 誼令稹所親董可武說稹曰：「山東之叛，事由五舅，城中人人誰敢相保！
entries.en: Yi had Zhen's confidant Dong Kewu tell him: "The Fifth Uncle caused the Shandong revolt. In this city, who can feel safe?
entries.literal: Yi ordered Zhen's intimate Dong Kewu to persuade Zhen, saying: "The Shandong rebellion was caused by the Fifth Uncle; within the city, who dares guarantee anyone's safety!

entries.zh: 留後今欲何如？」
entries.en: What does the commissioner intend to do now?"
entries.literal: What does the acting commissioner wish to do now?"

entries.zh: 稹曰：「今城中尚有五萬人，且當閉門堅守耳。」
entries.en: Zhen said: "We still have fifty thousand men in the city. We should shut the gates and hold on."
entries.literal: Zhen said: "Now within the city there are still fifty thousand men; for the time being we should shut the gates and hold firm."

entries.zh: 可武曰：「非良策也。
entries.en: Kewu said: "That is no good plan.
entries.literal: Kewu said: "That is not a good plan.

entries.zh: 留後不若束身歸朝，如張元益，不失作刺史。
entries.en: Better surrender yourself to the court, as Zhang Yuanyi did—you would still receive a prefecture.
entries.literal: The acting commissioner would do better to bind himself and return to the court, like Zhang Yuanyi, and not fail to become a prefect.

entries.zh: 且以郭誼為留後，俟得節之日，徐奉太夫人及室家金帛歸之東都，不亦善乎！」
entries.en: Make Guo Yi acting commissioner for now. Once he receives the commission, your mother and family can take their wealth back to Luoyang in good time. Would that not be best?"
entries.literal: Moreover appoint Guo Yi acting commissioner; when the day of receiving the commission arrives, slowly escort the Dowager Lady and the household's gold and silk back to the Eastern Capital—is that not also good!"

entries.zh: 稹曰：「誼安肯如是？」
entries.en: Zhen said: "Would Yi truly do that?"
entries.literal: Zhen said: "How would Yi be willing to act thus?"

entries.zh: 可武曰：「可武已與之重誓，必不負也。」
entries.en: Kewu said: "I have sworn a solemn oath with him. He will not betray you."
entries.literal: Kewu said: "Kewu has already sworn a heavy oath with him; he will certainly not betray you."

entries.zh: 及引誼入。
entries.en: Then he brought Yi in.
entries.literal: Thereupon he led Yi in.

entries.zh: 稹與之密約既定，乃白其母。
entries.en: Once Zhen and Yi had sealed their secret pact, Zhen told his mother.
entries.literal: After Zhen and he had set their secret agreement, he then informed his mother.

entries.zh: 母曰：「歸朝誠為佳事，但恨已晚。
entries.en: His mother said: "Surrender would indeed be wise, but I fear it is too late.
entries.literal: His mother said: "Returning to the court is truly a fine matter, but I regret it is already late.

entries.zh: 吾有弟不能保，安能保郭誼！
entries.en: I could not even save my own brother—how can I trust Guo Yi!
entries.literal: I could not even protect my own younger brother—how can I protect Guo Yi!

entries.zh: 汝自圖之！」
entries.en: You must decide for yourself!"
entries.literal: You must plot for yourself!"

entries.zh: 稹乃素服出門，以母命署誼都知兵馬使。
entries.en: Zhen put on plain clothes, went out, and by his mother's authority appointed Yi commander of the army.
entries.literal: Zhen then in plain dress went out the gate and, by his mother's order, appointed Yi commander of military affairs.

entries.zh: 王協已戒諸將列於外廳，誼拜謝稹已，出見諸將，稹治裝於內廳。
entries.en: Wang Xie had already assembled the generals in the outer hall. Yi bowed to Zhen, went out to face the officers, while Zhen packed in the inner hall.
entries.literal: Wang Xie had already warned the generals to line up in the outer hall; after Yi bowed in thanks to Zhen, he went out to see the generals while Zhen packed in the inner hall.

entries.zh: 李士貴聞之，帥後院兵數千攻誼。
entries.en: Li Shigui heard of it and led several thousand household guards against Yi.
entries.literal: Li Shigui heard this and led several thousand rear-courtyard troops to attack Yi.

entries.zh: 誼叱之曰：「何不自取賞物，乃欲與李士貴同死乎！」
entries.en: Yi shouted: "Why not seize your share of the loot instead of dying with Li Shigui!"
entries.literal: Yi shouted at them: "Why not take reward goods for yourselves—do you wish to die together with Li Shigui!"

entries.zh: 軍士乃退，共殺士貴。
entries.en: The troops fell back and together killed Shigui.
entries.literal: The soldiers then withdrew and together killed Shigui.

entries.zh: 誼易置將吏，部署軍士，一夕俱定。
entries.en: Yi replaced officers, redeployed the troops, and within a single night had everything under control.
entries.literal: Yi replaced generals and officials, deployed the soldiers, and in one night all was settled.

entries.zh: 明日，使董可武入謁稹曰：「請議公事。」
entries.en: The next day he sent Dong Kewu to see Zhen: "We must discuss state business."
entries.literal: The next day he sent Dong Kewu in to visit Zhen, saying: "I request to discuss official business."

entries.zh: 稹曰：「何不言之！」
entries.en: Zhen said: "Speak here, then!"
entries.literal: Zhen said: "Why not speak of it!"

entries.zh: 可武曰：「恐驚太夫人。」
entries.en: Kewu said: "I fear distressing your mother."
entries.literal: Kewu said: "I fear alarming the Dowager Lady."

entries.zh: 乃引稹步出牙門，至北宅，置酒作樂。
entries.en: He led Zhen on foot out through the headquarters gate to the North Residence, where wine and music were prepared.
entries.literal: He then led Zhen on foot out the yamen gate to the North Residence, set out wine, and made music.

entries.zh: 酒酣，乃言：「今日之事欲全太尉一家，須留後自圖去就，則朝廷必垂矜閔。」
entries.en: When the wine had gone deep, he said: "To save your whole house, Commissioner, you must decide your own course. The court will surely show mercy."
entries.literal: When the wine was deep, he then said: "Today's affair wishes to preserve the Grand Marshal's whole household; the acting commissioner must himself plot his going or staying—then the court will certainly extend pity."

entries.zh: 稹曰：「如所言，稹之心也。」
entries.en: Zhen said: "What you say is exactly what I wish."
entries.literal: Zhen said: "As you have said—that is Zhen's own heart."

entries.zh: 可武遂前執其手，，崔率度自後斬之，因收稹宗族，匡周以下至襁褓中子皆殺之。
entries.en: Kewu seized his hands from the front while Cui Shualv struck from behind and cut off his head. They then seized Zhen's entire clan and killed everyone from Kuang Zhou down to babes in arms.
entries.literal: Kewu then stepped forward and seized his hand; Cui Shualv from behind beheaded him, then rounded up Zhen's clan—from Kuang Zhou down to infants still in swaddling clothes, all were killed.

entries.zh: 又殺劉從諫父子所厚善者張谷、陳揚庭、李仲京、郭台、王羽、韓茂章、茂實、王渥、賈庠等凡十二家，並其子侄甥婿無遺。
entries.en: They also slaughtered twelve households whom Liu Congjian and his son had favored—Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Guo Tai, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang and Maoshi, Wang Wo, Jia Xiang, and others—sparing not a son, nephew, son-in-law, or grandson.
entries.literal: They also killed those whom Liu Congjian and his son had deeply favored—Zhang Gu, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Guo Tai, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang, Maoshi, Wang Wo, Jia Xiang, and twelve households in all—together with their sons, nephews, sons-in-law, and sons of daughters, leaving none.

entries.zh: 仲京，訓之兄；
entries.en: Zhongjing was the elder brother of Li Xun;
entries.literal: Zhongjing was Xun's elder brother;

entries.zh: 台，行餘之子。
entries.en: Guo Tai was the son of Guo Xingyu.
entries.literal: Tai was Xingyu's son.

entries.zh: 羽，涯之從孫；
entries.en: Wang Yu was a collateral descendant of Wang Ya;
entries.literal: Yu was Ya's collateral grandson;

entries.zh: 茂章、茂實，約之子；
entries.en: Han Maozhang and Maoshi were sons of Han Yue;
entries.literal: Maozhang and Maoshi were Yue's sons;

entries.zh: 渥，璠之子。
entries.en: Wang Wo was the son of Wang Fan.
entries.literal: Wo was Fan's son.

entries.zh: 庠，餗之子也。
entries.en: Jia Xiang was the son of Jia Su.
entries.literal: Xiang was Su's son.

entries.zh: 甘露之亂，仲京等亡歸從諫，從諫撫養之。
entries.en: After the Sweet Dew Affair, Zhongjing and the others had fled to Liu Congjian, who sheltered and raised them.
entries.literal: In the Sweet Dew turmoil, Zhongjing and the others fled and returned to Congjian, who nurtured them.

entries.zh: 凡軍中有小嫌者，誼日有所誅，流血成泥。
entries.en: Anyone in the army who bore the slightest grudge was put to death day after day until blood ran like mud.
entries.literal: For anyone in the army with the slightest grudge, Yi daily executed some; blood flowed like mud.

entries.zh: 乃函稹首，遣使奉表及書，降於王宰。
entries.en: He placed Zhen's head in a box, sent envoys with a memorial and letter of surrender, and submitted to Wang Zai.
entries.literal: He then boxed Zhen's head, sent envoys bearing a memorial and letter, and surrendered to Wang Zai.

entries.zh: 首過澤州，劉公直舉營慟哭，亦降於宰。
entries.en: As the head passed through Ze Prefecture, Liu Gongzhi led his entire camp in mourning and surrendered to Zai as well.
entries.literal: When the head passed Ze Prefecture, Liu Gongzhi raised the whole camp in wailing lament and also surrendered to Zai.

entries.zh: 乙未，宰以狀聞。
entries.en: On the day yiwei, Zai reported the victory to the court.
entries.literal: On the day yiwei, Zai reported the situation.

entries.zh: 丙申，宰相入賀。
entries.en: On the day bingshen, the chief ministers came in to offer congratulations.
entries.literal: On the day bingshen, the chief ministers entered to congratulate.

entries.zh: 李德裕奏：「今不須復置邢、洺、磁留後，但遣盧弘止宣慰三州及成德、魏博兩道。」
entries.en: Li Deyu memorialized: "We need no longer appoint regents for Xing, Ming, and Ci. Send Lu Hongzhi to proclaim comfort to those three prefectures and to the Chengde and Weibo circuits."
entries.literal: Li Deyu memorialized: "Now there is no need again to appoint regents for Xing, Ming, and Ci; only send Lu Hongzhi to proclaim comfort to the three prefectures and the two circuits of Chengde and Weibo."

entries.zh: 上曰：「郭誼宜如何處之？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked: "What should be done with Guo Yi?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "How should Guo Yi be dealt with?"

entries.zh: 德裕對曰：「劉稹騃孺子耳，阻兵拒命，皆誼為之謀主。
entries.en: Deyu answered: "Liu Zhen was a witless boy. Yi was the mastermind who armed the rebellion and defied the throne.
entries.literal: Deyu replied: "Liu Zhen was but a foolish child; blocking troops and defying orders—all were plotted by Yi as chief strategist.

entries.zh: 及勢孤力屈，又賣稹以求賞。
entries.en: When his power collapsed, he sold out Zhen for a reward.
entries.literal: When his position was isolated and strength exhausted, he again sold Zhen to seek reward.

entries.zh: 此而不誅，何以懲惡！
entries.en: If we spare him, how will we punish treachery!
entries.literal: If this man is not executed, how can evil be punished!

entries.zh: 宜及諸軍在境，並誼等誅之！」
entries.en: Execute Yi and his accomplices while our armies are still on the ground!"
entries.literal: It is fitting, while the various armies are still in the territory, to execute Yi and the rest together!"

entries.zh: 上曰：「朕意亦以為然。」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "I agree."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "My mind also holds it so."

entries.zh: 乃詔石雄將七千人入潞州，以應謠言。
entries.en: An edict ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand men into Lu Prefecture—fulfilling a popular prophecy.
entries.literal: An edict then ordered Shi Xiong to lead seven thousand men into Lu Prefecture, in accord with a popular saying.

entries.zh: 杜悰以饋運不給，謂誼等可赦，上熟視不應。
entries.en: Du Cong, citing supply shortages, argued that Yi and the others should be pardoned. The Emperor fixed him with a long stare and said nothing.
entries.literal: Du Cong, because supply transport was insufficient, said Yi and the others could be pardoned; the Emperor stared at him intently and did not reply.

entries.zh: 德裕曰：「今春澤潞未平，太原復擾，自非聖斷堅定，二寇何由可平！
entries.en: Deyu said: "This spring Ze and Lu were still in revolt and Taiyuan was in turmoil again. Without Your Majesty's firm resolve, how could both rebellions have been crushed!
entries.literal: Deyu said: "This spring Ze and Lu were not yet pacified, and Taiyuan was disturbed again—if not for Your Sagely resolve being firm, how could the two rebels have been subdued!

entries.zh: 外議以為若在先朝，赦之久矣。」
entries.en: Outsiders say that under the previous reign they would have been pardoned long ago."
entries.literal: Outside opinion holds that under the previous reign they would long ago have been pardoned."

entries.zh: 上曰：「卿不知文宗心地不與卿合，安能議乎！」
entries.en: The Emperor said: "You forget that Emperor Wenzong's mind was not yours. How could he have acted as you would!"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "You do not know that Emperor Wenzong's mind was not in accord with yours—how could he have deliberated thus!"

entries.zh: 罷盧鈞山南東道，專為昭義節度使。
entries.en: Lu Jun was relieved of Shannan East and appointed solely military governor of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: Lu Jun was removed from Shannan East Circuit and made solely military governor of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 戊戌，劉稹傳首至京師。
entries.en: On the day wuxu, Liu Zhen's head arrived at the capital.
entries.literal: On the day wuxu, Liu Zhen's transmitted head reached the capital.

entries.zh: 詔：「昭義五州給復一年，軍行所過州縣免今年秋稅。
entries.en: An edict declared: "The five Zhaoyi prefectures shall receive a year's tax relief, and every county and prefecture the army passed through is exempt from this autumn's levy.
entries.literal: An edict: "The five prefectures of Zhaoyi shall receive tax relief for one year; prefectures and counties through which the army passed are exempted from this year's autumn tax.

entries.zh: 昭義自劉從諫以來，橫增賦斂，悉從蠲免。
entries.en: All arbitrary levies imposed since Liu Congjian's day were abolished.
entries.literal: Since Liu Congjian's time Zhaoyi had arbitrarily increased levies—all are remitted from exemption.

entries.zh: 所藉土團並縱遣歸農。
entries.en: Conscripted local militia were disbanded and sent home to farm.
entries.literal: Local militia that had been conscripted were all released and sent back to farming.

entries.zh: 諸道將士有功者，等級加賞。」
entries.en: Meritorious officers and soldiers from every circuit were rewarded according to rank."
entries.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various circuits who had merit received graded additional rewards."

entries.zh: 郭誼既殺劉稹，日望旌節，既久不聞問，乃曰：「必移它鎮。」
entries.en: After killing Liu Zhen, Guo Yi waited daily for his commission as military governor. When no word came for a long time, he said: "They must be transferring me to another circuit."
entries.literal: After Guo Yi had killed Liu Zhen, he daily looked for the commission of office; having long heard nothing, he then said: "I must surely be transferred to another post."

entries.zh: 於是閱鞍馬，治行裝。
entries.en: He inspected his horses and packed for the journey.
entries.literal: He then inspected saddles and horses and prepared traveling gear.

entries.zh: 及聞石雄將至，懼失色。
entries.en: When he learned that Shi Xiong was coming, he turned pale with fear.
entries.literal: When he heard Shi Xiong was about to arrive, he turned pale with fear.

entries.zh: 雄至，誼等參賀畢，敕使張仲清曰：「郭都知告身來日當至，諸高班告身在此，晚牙來受之！」
entries.en: When Xiong arrived, Yi and the others paid their respects. The imperial envoy Zhang Zhongqing announced: "Commander Guo's commission will arrive tomorrow. The senior officers' commissions are here—come to the evening assembly to receive them!"
entries.literal: When Xiong arrived, after Yi and the others had paid their respects, the edict envoy Zhang Zhongqing said: "Commander Guo's commission of appointment will arrive tomorrow; the senior officers' commissions are here—come receive them at the evening roll call!"

entries.zh: 乃以河中兵環球場，晚牙，誼等至，唱名引入，凡諸將桀黠拒官軍者，悉執送京師。
entries.en: Hezhong troops ringed the parade ground. At the evening assembly, as Yi and the others arrived, their names were called and they were led in. Every fierce commander who had resisted the imperial army was seized and sent to the capital.
entries.literal: He then had Hezhong troops surround the ball ground; at evening roll call, when Yi and the others arrived, names were called and they were led in—all fierce and cunning generals who had resisted government troops were seized and sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 加何弘敬同平章事。
entries.en: He Hongjing was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
entries.literal: He Hongjing was promoted to Associate Director of the Chancellery.

entries.zh: 丁未，詔發劉從諫屍，暴於潞州市三日，石雄取其屍置球場斬坐刀之。
entries.en: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered Liu Congjian's corpse exhumed and displayed in Lu Prefecture for three days. Shi Xiong then had the body brought to the parade ground and executed by waist-slicing in the seated position.
entries.literal: On the day dingwei, an edict ordered Liu Congjian's corpse exhumed and exposed in Lu Prefecture city for three days; Shi Xiong took the corpse, placed it on the ball ground, and executed it by seated waist-slicing.

entries.zh: 丁巳，盧鈞入潞州。
entries.en: On the day dingsi, Lu Jun entered Lu Prefecture.
entries.literal: On the day dingsi, Lu Jun entered Lu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 鈞素寬厚愛人，劉稹未平，鈞已領昭義節度，襄州士卒在行營者，與潞人戰，常對陳揚鈞之美。
entries.en: Jun was known for his generosity and kindness. Even before Liu Zhen fell, he had been appointed military governor of Zhaoyi, and Xiang soldiers in the field camp often praised his virtues to the Lu troops across the battle lines.
entries.literal: Jun was by nature generous and loving toward people; before Liu Zhen was pacified, Jun already held the Zhaoyi military governorship, and Xiang Prefecture soldiers in the field camp, when fighting Lu men, often praised Jun's virtues across the battle lines.

entries.zh: 及赴鎮，入天井關，昭義散卒歸之道，鈞皆厚撫之，人情大洽，昭議遂安。
entries.en: When he went to take up his post and entered Tianjing Pass, he generously treated every scattered Zhaoyi soldier he met on the road. Hearts warmed to him, and Zhaoyi was soon at peace.
entries.literal: When he went to his post and entered Tianjing Pass, Zhaoyi scattered soldiers returning on the road were all generously comforted by Jun; popular sentiment was greatly harmonious, and Zhaoyi was thereby settled.

entries.zh: 劉稹將郭誼、王協、劉公直、安全慶、李道德、劉佐堯、劉開德、董可武等至京師，皆斬之。
entries.en: Liu Zhen's generals Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Quanqing, Li Daode, Liu Zuoyao, Liu Kaide, Dong Kewu, and others were brought to the capital and all beheaded.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen's generals Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Quanqing, Li Daode, Liu Zuoyao, Liu Kaide, Dong Kewu, and others reached the capital—all were beheaded.

entries.zh: 臣光曰：董重質之在淮西，郭誼之在昭義，吳元濟、劉稹，如木偶人在伎兒之手耳。
entries.en: Sima Guang comments: With Dong Chongzhi in Huaixi and Guo Yi in Zhaoyi, Wu Yuanji and Liu Zhen were no more than wooden puppets in the hands of puppeteers.
entries.literal: Your subject Guang says: With Dong Chongzhi in Huaixi and Guo Yi in Zhaoyi, Wu Yuanji and Liu Zhen were like wooden puppets in the hands of showmen.

entries.zh: 彼二人者，始則勸人為亂，終則賣主規利，其死固有餘罪。
entries.en: Those two men first incited rebellion and then betrayed their masters for gain. Their deaths were richly deserved.
entries.literal: Those two men at first urged others to rebel, and in the end sold their masters to seek profit; their deaths indeed left guilt to spare.

entries.zh: 然憲宗用之於前，武宗誅之於後，臣愚以為皆失之。
entries.en: Yet Emperor Xianzong used them before, and Emperor Wuzong executed them after. In my humble view, both rulers were wrong.
entries.literal: Yet Emperor Xianzong employed them before, and Emperor Wuzong executed them after—I, your foolish subject, hold that both were in error.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why so?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 賞奸，非義也；
entries.en: To reward traitors is unjust;
entries.literal: Rewarding the wicked is not righteous;

entries.zh: 殺降，非信也。
entries.en: to kill men who have surrendered is faithless.
entries.literal: killing those who surrender is not faithful.

entries.zh: 失義與信，何以為國！
entries.en: Without righteousness and faith, how can a state endure!
entries.literal: Losing righteousness and faith—how can one be a state!

entries.zh: 昔漢光武待王郎、劉盆子止於不死，知其非力竭則不降故也。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu of Han spared Wang Lang and Liu Penzi only their lives, knowing that rebels surrender only when their strength is spent.
entries.literal: Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han treated Wang Lang and Liu Penzi only to the point of not killing them, knowing that unless strength was exhausted they would not surrender.

entries.zh: 樊崇、徐宣、王元、牛邯之徒，豈非助亂之人乎？
entries.en: Were Fan Chong, Xu Xuan, Wang Yuan, Niu Han, and their like not agents of rebellion?
entries.literal: Fan Chong, Xu Xuan, Wang Yuan, Niu Han, and their kind—were they not men who aided rebellion?

entries.zh: 而光武弗殺。
entries.en: Yet Guangwu did not execute them.
entries.literal: Yet Guangwu did not kill them.

entries.zh: 蓋以既受其降，則不可復誅故也。
entries.en: Once he had accepted their surrender, he could not put them to death.
entries.literal: This was because once their surrender had been accepted, they could not again be executed.

entries.zh: 若既赦而復逃亡叛亂，則其死固無辭矣！
entries.en: If, after pardon, they fled and rebelled again, execution would be fully justified!
entries.literal: If after pardon they again fled, rebelled, and made turmoil, then their death would indeed admit no excuse!

entries.zh: 如誼等，免死流之遠方，沒齒不還，可矣；
entries.en: Men like Yi should have been spared and exiled to distant lands, never to return—that would have been enough;
entries.literal: Men like Yi could have been spared death and exiled to distant regions, never to return within their lives—that would have sufficed;

entries.zh: 殺之，非也！
entries.en: to kill them was wrong!
entries.literal: to kill them was wrong!

entries.zh: 王羽、賈庠等已為誼所殺，李德裕復下詔稱「逆賊王涯、賈餗等已就昭義誅其子孫」，宣告中外，識者非之。
entries.en: Wang Yu, Jia Xiang, and the others had already been killed by Yi. Li Deyu then issued an edict proclaiming to all within and without that "the rebel criminals Wang Ya, Jia Su, and others have had their descendants executed in Zhaoyi." Thoughtful men condemned this.
entries.literal: Wang Yu, Jia Xiang, and the others had already been killed by Yi; Li Deyu again issued an edict stating "the rebel criminals Wang Ya, Jia Su, and others have already had their descendants executed at Zhaoyi," proclaiming it within and without—men of judgment disapproved.

entries.zh: 劉從諫妻裴氏亦賜死。
entries.en: Liu Congjian's widow Lady Pei was also ordered to take her own life.
entries.literal: Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was also ordered to die.

entries.zh: 又令昭義降將李丕、高文端、王釗等疏昭義將士與劉稹同惡者，悉誅之，死者甚眾。
entries.en: He also had Zhaoyi defectors Li Pi, Gao Wenduan, Wang Zhao, and others denounce every officer and soldier who had sided with Liu Zhen. All were executed, and the dead were very numerous.
entries.literal: He also ordered Zhaoyi surrendering generals Li Pi, Gao Wenduan, Wang Zhao, and others to denounce Zhaoyi officers and soldiers who shared Liu Zhen's evil—all were executed, and the dead were very many.

entries.zh: 盧鈞疑其枉濫，奏請寬之，不從。
entries.en: Lu Jun suspected wholesale injustice and memorialized for clemency, but the court refused.
entries.literal: Lu Jun suspected this was excessive and indiscriminate, memorialized asking leniency, and was not followed.

entries.zh: 昭義屬城有嘗無禮於王元逵者，元逵推求得二十餘人，斬之。
entries.en: In one Zhaoyi subordinate city, men who had once insulted Wang Yuankui were hunted down; he beheaded more than twenty of them.
entries.literal: In a subordinate city of Zhaoyi there were those who had once been disrespectful to Wang Yuankui; Yuankui tracked them down and got more than twenty men, whom he beheaded.

entries.zh: 餘眾懼，復閉城自守。
entries.en: The rest of the populace, terrified, shut the gates and held the city again.
entries.literal: The remaining multitude were afraid and again closed the city to hold it themselves.

entries.zh: 戊辰，李德裕等奏：「寇孽既平，盡為國家城鎮，豈可令元逵窮兵攻討！
entries.en: On the day wuchen, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The rebels are crushed and these are imperial towns. How can we let Yuankui press the attack to the bitter end!
entries.literal: On the day wuchen, Li Deyu and others memorialized: "The rebel brood being already pacified, all are the state's towns and cities—how can Yuankui be allowed to exhaust troops in attack!

entries.zh: 望遣中使賜城內將士敕，招安之，仍詔元逵引兵歸鎮，並詔盧鈞自遣使安撫。」
entries.en: Send a palace envoy with an edict to reassure the garrison, order Yuankui to withdraw to his post, and let Lu Jun send his own envoys to pacify them."
entries.literal: We hope to send a palace envoy to grant an edict to the city's officers and soldiers and win them by reassurance, and also order Yuankui to lead troops back to his post, and order Lu Jun on his own to send envoys to pacify."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court agreed.
entries.literal: This was followed.

entries.zh: 李德裕怨太子太傅、東都留守牛僧孺、湖州刺史李宗閔，言於上曰：「劉從諫據上黨十年，太和中入朝，僧孺、宗閔執政，不留之，加宰相縱去，以成今日之患，竭天下力乃能取之，皆二人之罪也。」
entries.en: Li Deyu bore a grudge against Niu Sengru, Grand Mentor and regent of the Eastern Capital, and Li Zongmin, prefect of Huzhou. He told the Emperor: "Liu Congjian held Shangdang for ten years. During the Taihe era he came to court while Sengru and Zongmin were in power. They did not detain him but made him chief minister and let him return—creating today's disaster. Only by exhausting the empire's strength could we recover the region. The fault lies with those two men."
entries.literal: Li Deyu resented Grand Mentor and Eastern Capital regent Niu Sengru and Huzhou Prefect Li Zongmin, and said to the Emperor: "Liu Congjian held Shangdang for ten years; in the Taihe era he entered court—Sengru and Zongmin held government, did not detain him, added him as chief minister and let him go, thereby creating today's calamity; exhausting the empire's strength was needed to take it—all is the crime of those two men."

entries.zh: 德裕又使人於潞州求僧孺、宗閔與從諫交通書疏，無所得，乃令孔目官鄭慶言從諫每得僧孺、宗閔書疏，皆自焚毀。
entries.en: Deyu also sent men to Lu Prefecture to search for correspondence between Sengru, Zongmin, and Congjian. Finding none, he had a clerk named Zheng Qing claim that Congjian had burned every letter he received from Sengru and Zongmin.
entries.literal: Deyu also sent men to Lu Prefecture to seek correspondence between Sengru, Zongmin, and Congjian; obtaining none, he then had clerical officer Zheng Qing say that whenever Congjian received letters from Sengru and Zongmin he burned them himself.

entries.zh: 詔追慶下御史台近問，中丞李回、知雜鄭亞以為信然。
entries.en: An edict ordered Qing brought before the Censorate for interrogation. Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Supervisory Censor Zheng Ya found his testimony credible.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Qing pursued to the Censorate for close interrogation; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Supervisory Censor Zheng Ya held it credible.

entries.zh: 河南少尹呂述與德裕書，言稹破報至，僧孺出聲歎恨。
entries.en: Lü Shu, vice prefect of Henan, wrote to Deyu that when news of Liu Zhen's defeat arrived, Niu Sengru sighed aloud in regret.
entries.literal: Henan Vice Prefect Lü Shu wrote to Deyu, saying that when the report of Zhen's defeat arrived, Sengru gave voice to sighs of regret.

entries.zh: 德裕奏述書，上大怒，以僧孺為太子少保、分司，宗閔為漳州刺史。
entries.en: Deyu submitted a memorial recounting Lü Shu's letter. The emperor flew into a rage and made Niu Sengru Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal court post, and Li Zongmin prefect of Zhang Prefecture.
entries.literal: Deyu memorialized describing Shu's letter; the emperor was greatly angered and made Sengru Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal post, and Zongmin Prefect of Zhang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 戊子，再貶僧孺汀州刺史，宗閔漳州長史。
entries.en: On wuzi, Sengru was demoted again to prefect of Ting Prefecture, and Zongmin to chief secretary of Zhang Prefecture.
entries.literal: On wuzi, Sengru was demoted again to Prefect of Ting Prefecture, Zongmin to Chief Secretary of Zhang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 資治通鑑第248卷
entries.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 248
entries.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 248

entries.zh: 韶性行溫裕，以高氏婿，頗膺時寵。
entries.en: Shao was mild and generous by nature; as a son-in-law of the Gaos he enjoyed considerable favor.
entries.literal: Shao by nature and conduct was mild and generous; as son-in-law of the Gao clan he enjoyed considerable favor of the times.

source.zh: 韶性行溫裕，以高氏婿，頗膺時寵。

translations.literal: Shao by nature and conduct was mild and generous; as son-in-law of the Gao clan he enjoyed considerable favor of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was mild and generous by nature; as a son-in-law of the Gaos he enjoyed considerable favor.

entries.zh: 能自謙退，臨人有惠政。
entries.en: He knew how to yield; in office he governed with kindness.
entries.literal: He could humble himself and yield; in governing men he had policies of kindness.

source.zh: 能自謙退，臨人有惠政。

translations.literal: He could humble himself and yield; in governing men he had policies of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to yield; in office he governed with kindness.

entries.zh: 好儒學，禮致才彥。
entries.en: He loved Confucian learning and with proper ceremony welcomed men of talent.
entries.literal: He loved Confucian learning and with ritual received men of talent.

source.zh: 好儒學，禮致才彥。

translations.literal: He loved Confucian learning and with ritual received men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Confucian learning and with proper ceremony welcomed men of talent.

entries.zh: 愛林泉，修第宅，華而不侈。
entries.en: He loved forests and springs and built mansions splendid but not extravagant.
entries.literal: He loved forests and springs, built mansions and residences — splendid yet not extravagant.

source.zh: 愛林泉，修第宅，華而不侈。

translations.literal: He loved forests and springs, built mansions and residences — splendid yet not extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: He loved forests and springs and built mansions splendid but not extravagant.

entries.zh: 文宣帝剃韶鬚髯，加以粉黛，衣婦人服以自隨曰：「我以彭城為嬪御。」
entries.en: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard, painted his face, dressed him in women's clothes and kept him at his side, saying, "I take Prince of Pengcheng as my consort."
entries.literal: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard and whiskers, applied powder and rouge, dressed him in women's garments to keep at his side, saying: "I take Pengcheng as my palace woman."

source.zh: 文宣帝剃韶鬚髯，加以粉黛，衣婦人服以自隨曰：「我以彭城為嬪御。」

translations.literal: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard and whiskers, applied powder and rouge, dressed him in women's garments to keep at his side, saying: "I take Pengcheng as my palace woman."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard, painted his face, dressed him in women's clothes and kept him at his side, saying, "I take Prince of Pengcheng as my consort."

entries.zh: 譏元氏微弱，比之婦女。
entries.en: He mocked the Yuan for their weakness, likening them to women.
entries.literal: He mocked the weakness of the Yuan clan, comparing them to women.

source.zh: 譏元氏微弱，比之婦女。

translations.literal: He mocked the weakness of the Yuan clan, comparing them to women.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked the Yuan for their weakness, likening them to women.

entries.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺東苑，慕義如林，馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。
entries.en: In former times, at the Western Capital of Han and when Liang founded its state, the Level Terrace and Eastern Park drew men of virtue like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Feathered Cavalry, and Mei Sheng gave up his governorship of Hongnong.
entries.literal: In former times the Western Capital of Han and the founding of Liang's state, the Level Terrace and Eastern Park drew men of virtue like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Feathered Cavalry, Mei Sheng gave up his governorship of Hongnong.

source.zh: 昔漢氏西京，梁王建國，平臺東苑，慕義如林，馬卿辭武騎之官，枚乘罷弘農之守。

translations.literal: In former times the Western Capital of Han and the founding of Liang's state, the Level Terrace and Eastern Park drew men of virtue like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Feathered Cavalry, Mei Sheng gave up his governorship of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In former times, at the Western Capital of Han and when Liang founded its state, the Level Terrace and Eastern Park drew men of virtue like a forest; Sima Xiangru resigned his post in the Feathered Cavalry, and Mei Sheng gave up his governorship of Hongnong.

entries.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗竊怪之：何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？
entries.en: Whenever I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger in princely residences?
entries.literal: Whenever I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger in princely residences?

source.zh: 每覽史傳，嘗竊怪之：何乃脫略官榮，棲遲籓邸？

translations.literal: Whenever I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger in princely residences?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the histories I have privately wondered: why did they cast off official glory and linger in princely residences?

entries.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。
entries.en: Looking from the present back to antiquity, I now understand their lofty intent.
entries.literal: Looking from the present back to antiquity, I now understand their lofty intent.

source.zh: 以今望古，方知雅志。

translations.literal: Looking from the present back to antiquity, I now understand their lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from the present back to antiquity, I now understand their lofty intent.

entries.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！
entries.en: Those two men were not acting in vain!
entries.literal: Those two men—were they merely acting in vain!

source.zh: 彼二子者，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Those two men—were they merely acting in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Those two men were not acting in vain!

entries.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似陟蒙山；
entries.en: You, sir, are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing the deep to reach the far; compared with the three baskets of a Han minister, it is like ascending Mount Meng;
entries.literal: You, sir, are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing the deep to reach the far; compared with the three baskets of a Han minister, it is like ascending Mount Meng;

source.zh: 足下博聞強記，鉤深致遠，視漢臣之三篋，似陟蒙山；

translations.literal: You, sir, are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing the deep to reach the far; compared with the three baskets of a Han minister, it is like ascending Mount Meng;
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, are broadly learned with a strong memory, probing the deep to reach the far; compared with the three baskets of a Han minister, it is like ascending Mount Meng;

entries.zh: 對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。
entries.en: faced with the five cartloads of a Liang chancellor, it is like swallowing Lake Yunmeng whole.
entries.literal: faced with the five cartloads of a Liang chancellor, it is like swallowing Lake Yunmeng.

source.zh: 對梁相之五車，若吞雲夢。

translations.literal: faced with the five cartloads of a Liang chancellor, it is like swallowing Lake Yunmeng.
translations.idiomatic: faced with the five cartloads of a Liang chancellor, it is like swallowing Lake Yunmeng whole.

entries.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。
entries.en: My elder brother cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring them without weariness; he first built a palace for Guo Kui and always kept the wine of Mu Sheng ready.
entries.literal: My elder brother cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring and loving them without weariness; he first built a palace for Guo Kui and always kept the wine of Mu Sheng ready.

source.zh: 吾兄欽賢重士，敬愛忘疲，先築郭隗之宮，常置穆生之醴。

translations.literal: My elder brother cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring and loving them without weariness; he first built a palace for Guo Kui and always kept the wine of Mu Sheng ready.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother cherishes the worthy and esteems scholars, honoring them without weariness; he first built a palace for Guo Kui and always kept the wine of Mu Sheng ready.

entries.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河。
entries.en: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over mountains and rivers.
entries.literal: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over mountains and rivers.

source.zh: 今者重開土宇，更誓山河。

translations.literal: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Now he has reopened his domain and renewed his oath over mountains and rivers.

entries.zh: 地方七百，牢籠曲阜；
entries.en: His territory spans seven hundred li and encloses Qufu;
entries.literal: His territory spans seven hundred li and encloses Qufu;

source.zh: 地方七百，牢籠曲阜；

translations.literal: His territory spans seven hundred li and encloses Qufu;
translations.idiomatic: His territory spans seven hundred li and encloses Qufu;

entries.zh: 城兼七十，包舉臨淄。
entries.en: his cities number seventy and embrace Linzi.
entries.literal: his cities number seventy and embrace Linzi.

source.zh: 城兼七十，包舉臨淄。

translations.literal: his cities number seventy and embrace Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: his cities number seventy and embrace Linzi.

entries.zh: 大啟南陽，方開東閤。
entries.en: Greatly opening Nanyang, he is just now opening the Eastern Gate to welcome guests.
entries.literal: Greatly opening Nanyang, he is just now opening the Eastern Gate.

source.zh: 大啟南陽，方開東閤。

translations.literal: Greatly opening Nanyang, he is just now opening the Eastern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly opening Nanyang, he is just now opening the Eastern Gate to welcome guests.

entries.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。
entries.en: I imagine you will ride beneath a flying canopy, trail a long robe, recline on a tortoiseshell mat, step in pearl slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's lofty grace, and compose verses on the pool bamboo's elegant clusters.
entries.literal: I imagine you will ride beneath a flying canopy, trail a long robe, recline on a tortoiseshell mat, step in pearl slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's lofty grace, and compose on the pool bamboo's elegant clusters.

source.zh: 想得奉飛蓋，曳長裾，藉玳筵，躡珠履，歌山桂之偃蹇，賦池竹之檀欒。

translations.literal: I imagine you will ride beneath a flying canopy, trail a long robe, recline on a tortoiseshell mat, step in pearl slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's lofty grace, and compose on the pool bamboo's elegant clusters.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine you will ride beneath a flying canopy, trail a long robe, recline on a tortoiseshell mat, step in pearl slippers, sing of the mountain cassia's lofty grace, and compose verses on the pool bamboo's elegant clusters.

entries.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！
entries.en: Your lofty dignity is like that, your elegant spirit like this—how fortunate, how fortunate! What joy could equal it!
entries.literal: Your lofty dignity is like that, your elegant spirit like this—how fortunate, how fortunate! What joy could equal it!

source.zh: 其崇貴也如彼，其風流也如此，幸甚幸甚，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Your lofty dignity is like that, your elegant spirit like this—how fortunate, how fortunate! What joy could equal it!
translations.idiomatic: Your lofty dignity is like that, your elegant spirit like this—how fortunate, how fortunate! What joy could equal it!

entries.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖；
entries.en: Looking up to the capital, I think of Dezuo;
entries.literal: Looking up to the capital, I think of Dezuo;

source.zh: 高視上京，有懷德祖；

translations.literal: Looking up to the capital, I think of Dezuo;
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the capital, I think of Dezuo;

entries.zh: 才謝天人，多慚子建。
entries.en: in talent I fall short of heaven and man, and am much ashamed before Zijian.
entries.literal: in talent I fall short of heaven and man, and am much ashamed before Zijian.

source.zh: 才謝天人，多慚子建。

translations.literal: in talent I fall short of heaven and man, and am much ashamed before Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: in talent I fall short of heaven and man, and am much ashamed before Zijian.

entries.zh: 書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。
entries.en: A letter cannot exhaust my meaning; why wait for more words?
entries.literal: A letter cannot exhaust my meaning; why wait for more words?

source.zh: 書不盡意，寧俟繁辭。

translations.literal: A letter cannot exhaust my meaning; why wait for more words?
translations.idiomatic: A letter cannot exhaust my meaning; why wait for more words?

entries.zh: 豫章得書，齎米五十石，並衣服、錢帛。
entries.en: The Prince of Yuzhang received his letter and sent fifty piculs of rice, along with clothing, money, and silks.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang received his letter and sent fifty piculs of rice, along with clothing, money, and silks.

source.zh: 豫章得書，齎米五十石，並衣服、錢帛。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang received his letter and sent fifty piculs of rice, along with clothing, money, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang received his letter and sent fifty piculs of rice, along with clothing, money, and silks.

entries.zh: 時晉邸文翰，多成其手。
entries.en: At the time the documents of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his own hand.
entries.literal: At the time the documents of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his own hand.

source.zh: 時晉邸文翰，多成其手。

translations.literal: At the time the documents of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the documents of the Prince of Jin's residence were largely written by his own hand.

entries.zh: 王入東宮，除太子齋帥，俄兼舍人。
entries.en: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Master of the Crown Prince's Fast, and soon also served as Attendant Gentleman.
entries.literal: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Master of the Crown Prince's Fast, and soon also served as Attendant Gentleman.

source.zh: 王入東宮，除太子齋帥，俄兼舍人。

translations.literal: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Master of the Crown Prince's Fast, and soon also served as Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Ze was appointed Master of the Crown Prince's Fast, and soon also served as Attendant Gentleman.

entries.zh: 及元德太子薨，以疾歸於家。
entries.en: When Crown Prince Yuande died, he returned home on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Yuande died, he returned home on grounds of illness.

source.zh: 及元德太子薨，以疾歸於家。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yuande died, he returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yuande died, he returned home on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 後征起居舍人。
entries.en: Later he was summoned as Imperial Diarist.
entries.literal: Later he was summoned as Imperial Diarist.

source.zh: 後征起居舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Imperial Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned as Imperial Diarist.

entries.zh: 冬，詔曰：「國之將興，尊師而重傅。
entries.en: In winter, an edict declared: 'When a state will rise, it honors teachers and values tutors.
entries.literal: Winter, edict said: 'State will rise, honor teacher and weight tutor.

source.zh: 冬，詔曰：「國之將興，尊師而重傅。

translations.literal: Winter, edict said: 'State will rise, honor teacher and weight tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, an edict declared: 'When a state will rise, it honors teachers and values tutors.

entries.zh: 故前將軍望之傅朕八年，道以經書，厥功茂焉。
entries.en: Therefore the former general Wangzhi tutored me for eight years, guided me with the classics and books—his merit flourished there.
entries.literal: Therefore former general Wangzhi tutored me eight years, guided with classics books, his merit flourishing there.

source.zh: 故前將軍望之傅朕八年，道以經書，厥功茂焉。

translations.literal: Therefore former general Wangzhi tutored me eight years, guided with classics books, his merit flourishing there.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former general Wangzhi tutored me for eight years, guided me with the classics and books—his merit flourished there.

entries.zh: 其賜爵關內侯，食邑八百戶，朝朔望。」
entries.en: Cause him to be granted the noble rank of Guannei Marquis, a food fiefdom of 800 households, and to court on new moon and full moon.'
entries.literal: Cause grant noble rank Guannei Marquis, food fiefdom 800 households, court new moon full moon.'

source.zh: 其賜爵關內侯，食邑八百戶，朝朔望。」

translations.literal: Cause grant noble rank Guannei Marquis, food fiefdom 800 households, court new moon full moon.'
translations.idiomatic: Cause him to be granted the noble rank of Guannei Marquis, a food fiefdom of 800 households, and to court on new moon and full moon.'

entries.zh: 建始元年春正月乙丑，皇曾祖悼考廟災。
entries.en: On Yichou of the first month of spring in the first year of Jianshi, the temple of the imperial great-grandfather Daokao suffered a disaster.
entries.literal: Jianshi first year, spring, first month, Yichou: the temple of the imperial great-grandfather Daokao suffered a disaster.

source.zh: 建始元年春正月乙丑，皇曾祖悼考廟災。

translations.literal: Jianshi first year, spring, first month, Yichou: the temple of the imperial great-grandfather Daokao suffered a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On Yichou of the first month of spring in the first year of Jianshi, the temple of the imperial great-grandfather Daokao suffered a disaster.

entries.zh: 後以安為騎馬令。
entries.en: Afterward Yan An was appointed Master of the Imperial Horse.
entries.literal: Later, Yan An was made Master of Horse.

source.zh: 後以安為騎馬令。

translations.literal: Later, Yan An was made Master of Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Yan An was appointed Master of the Imperial Horse.

entries.zh: 是後，寵臣大氐外戚之家也。
entries.en: From then on, "favorites" tended to be in-laws of the throne.
entries.literal: After this, favorites were for the most part from affinal families.

source.zh: 是後，寵臣大氐外戚之家也。

translations.literal: After this, favorites were for the most part from affinal families.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, "favorites" tended to be in-laws of the throne.

entries.zh: 衛青、霍去病皆愛幸，然亦以功能自進。
entries.en: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing enjoyed imperial favor, but they also earned their place by real achievement.
entries.literal: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were both beloved and favored, yet they also advanced themselves by merit and achievement.

source.zh: 衛青、霍去病皆愛幸，然亦以功能自進。

translations.literal: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were both beloved and favored, yet they also advanced themselves by merit and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing enjoyed imperial favor, but they also earned their place by real achievement.

entries.zh: 章帝建初四年冬，京都牛大疫。
entries.en: Jianchu 4 (79 CE), winter: cattle plague struck the capital herds.
entries.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Jianchu, Emperor Zhang, the capital's cattle suffered a great plague.

source.zh: 章帝建初四年冬，京都牛大疫。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Jianchu, Emperor Zhang, the capital's cattle suffered a great plague.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchu 4 (79 CE), winter: cattle plague struck the capital herds.

entries.zh: 是时，窦皇后以宋贵人子为太子，宠幸，令人求伺贵人过隙，以谗毁之。
entries.en: Empress Dou's son sat as heir; she set agents to sniff out Lady Song's slips and ruin her with lies.
entries.literal: At that time Empress Dou had the son of Worthy Lady Song as heir apparent, favored and beloved; she ordered people to seek out the worthy lady's faults and destroy her with slander.

source.zh: 是时，窦皇后以宋贵人子为太子，宠幸，令人求伺贵人过隙，以谗毁之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dou had the son of Worthy Lady Song as heir apparent, favored and beloved; she ordered people to seek out the worthy lady's faults and destroy her with slander.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dou's son sat as heir; she set agents to sniff out Lady Song's slips and ruin her with lies.

entries.zh: 章帝不知窦太后不善，厥咎霿也。
entries.en: Zhang never saw Dou's malice—the fault named obscuration in the omen text.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhang did not realize Empress Dowager Dou was not good—the blame was obscuration.

source.zh: 章帝不知窦太后不善，厥咎霿也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang did not realize Empress Dowager Dou was not good—the blame was obscuration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang never saw Dou's malice—the fault named obscuration in the omen text.

entries.zh: 或曰，是年六月马太后崩，土功非时兴故也。
entries.en: Another gloss ties the plague to Ma's death that sixth month and the untimely earthworks her tomb demanded.
entries.literal: Another view says that in that year in the sixth month Empress Dowager Ma died, and earthworks were raised out of season for that reason.

source.zh: 或曰，是年六月马太后崩，土功非时兴故也。

translations.literal: Another view says that in that year in the sixth month Empress Dowager Ma died, and earthworks were raised out of season for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss ties the plague to Ma's death that sixth month and the untimely earthworks her tomb demanded.

entries.zh: 二十一年閏三月，奉旨昭祖、景祖奉安燕昌閣上，肅宗、穆宗、康宗奉安閣下，明肅皇帝奉安崇聖閣下。
entries.en: In the intercalary third month of the twenty-first year, by imperial command the portraits of Ancestor Zhao and Ancestor Jing were installed in the upper story of Yanchang Pavilion, those of Emperor Suzong, Emperor Muzong, and Emperor Kangzong in the lower story, and Emperor Mingsu in the lower story of Chongsheng Pavilion.
entries.literal: In the intercalary third month of the twenty-first year, by imperial command the portraits of Ancestor Zhao and Ancestor Jing were reverently installed in the upper story of Yanchang Pavilion, those of Emperor Suzong, Emperor Muzong, and Emperor Kangzong in the lower story, and Emperor Mingsu in the lower story of Chongsheng Pavilion.

source.zh: 二十一年閏三月，奉旨昭祖、景祖奉安燕昌閣上，肅宗、穆宗、康宗奉安閣下，明肅皇帝奉安崇聖閣下。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the twenty-first year, by imperial command the portraits of Ancestor Zhao and Ancestor Jing were reverently installed in the upper story of Yanchang Pavilion, those of Emperor Suzong, Emperor Muzong, and Emperor Kangzong in the lower story, and Emperor Mingsu in the lower story of Chongsheng Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of the twenty-first year, by imperial command the portraits of Ancestor Zhao and Ancestor Jing were installed in the upper story of Yanchang Pavilion, those of Emperor Suzong, Emperor Muzong, and Emperor Kangzong in the lower story, and Emperor Mingsu in the lower story of Chongsheng Pavilion.

entries.zh: 每位設黃羅幕一、黃羅明金柱衣二、紫羅地褥一、龍床一、踏床二、衣全，前期奏告。
entries.en: For each seat there was one yellow-silk curtain, two yellow-silk pillar garments with bright gold, one purple-silk ground mat, one dragon bed, two footstools, and a complete set of garments, with a report to the temple made beforehand.
entries.literal: For each seat were set one yellow-silk curtain, two yellow-silk pillar garments with bright gold, one purple-silk ground mat, one dragon bed, two footstools, and a complete set of garments; a report was made to the temple beforehand.

source.zh: 每位設黃羅幕一、黃羅明金柱衣二、紫羅地褥一、龍床一、踏床二、衣全，前期奏告。

translations.literal: For each seat were set one yellow-silk curtain, two yellow-silk pillar garments with bright gold, one purple-silk ground mat, one dragon bed, two footstools, and a complete set of garments; a report was made to the temple beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: For each seat there was one yellow-silk curtain, two yellow-silk pillar garments with bright gold, one purple-silk ground mat, one dragon bed, two footstools, and a complete set of garments, with a report to the temple made beforehand.

entries.zh: 四月一日奉安，五日親祀。
entries.en: On the first day of the fourth month the installation was performed; on the fifth day the emperor sacrificed in person.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fourth month the reverent installation was performed; on the fifth day the emperor sacrificed in person.

source.zh: 四月一日奉安，五日親祀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month the reverent installation was performed; on the fifth day the emperor sacrificed in person.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month the installation was performed; on the fifth day the emperor sacrificed in person.

entries.zh: 是年五月，遷聖安寺睿宗皇帝禦容于衍慶宮，皇太子親王宰執奉迎安置。
entries.en: In the fifth month of that year, Emperor Ruizong's portrait was moved from Sheng'an Temple to Yansqing Palace; the crown prince, princes, and chief councillors welcomed and installed it.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of that year, the imperial portrait of Emperor Ruizong was transferred from Sheng'an Temple to Yansqing Palace; the crown prince, princes, and chief councillors welcomed and installed it.

source.zh: 是年五月，遷聖安寺睿宗皇帝禦容于衍慶宮，皇太子親王宰執奉迎安置。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, the imperial portrait of Emperor Ruizong was transferred from Sheng'an Temple to Yansqing Palace; the crown prince, princes, and chief councillors welcomed and installed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year, Emperor Ruizong's portrait was moved from Sheng'an Temple to Yansqing Palace; the crown prince, princes, and chief councillors welcomed and installed it.

entries.zh: 右景宣子，與熈宗，凡三人。
entries.en: Listed at right: sons of Jingxuan—three in all, with Xizong.
entries.literal: At right: sons of Jingxuan—three in all, with Xizong.

source.zh: 右景宣子，與熈宗，凡三人。

translations.literal: At right: sons of Jingxuan—three in all, with Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: Listed at right: sons of Jingxuan—three in all, with Xizong.

entries.zh: 頃之，轉太宰從事中郎。
entries.en: Soon he was shifted to retainer clerk under the grand steward.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to retainer clerk with the grand steward.

source.zh: 頃之，轉太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to retainer clerk with the grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was shifted to retainer clerk under the grand steward.

entries.zh: 遭母憂，以至孝稱。
entries.en: His mother's death plunged him into mourning famed for its grief.
entries.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and was famed for utmost filial piety.

source.zh: 遭母憂，以至孝稱。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and was famed for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death plunged him into mourning famed for its grief.

entries.zh: 服闕，復為太宰中郎。
entries.en: When the mourning term ended he returned as the steward's clerk.
entries.literal: When mourning was ended, he again became steward's retainer.

source.zh: 服闕，復為太宰中郎。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, he again became steward's retainer.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning term ended he returned as the steward's clerk.

entries.zh: 齊王芳被廢，遷于金墉城，粲素服拜送，哀慟左右。
entries.en: When Cao Fang, the prince of Qi, was cast down and sent to the Metal Rampart palace, Can went in undyed linen to bow him off and wept until bystanders wept with him.
entries.literal: When Prince Qi of Cao Fang was deposed and moved to the Metal-walled City, Can in plain garb bowed in farewell, grieving so that those around him were moved.

source.zh: 齊王芳被廢，遷于金墉城，粲素服拜送，哀慟左右。

translations.literal: When Prince Qi of Cao Fang was deposed and moved to the Metal-walled City, Can in plain garb bowed in farewell, grieving so that those around him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Fang, the prince of Qi, was cast down and sent to the Metal Rampart palace, Can went in undyed linen to bow him off and wept until bystanders wept with him.

entries.zh: 時景帝輔政，召群官會議，粲又不到，朝廷以其時望，優容之。
entries.en: Emperor Jing called a plenary council; Can stayed away again, yet the court indulged him because of his moral weight.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Jing assisted the government, he summoned the officials to a joint conference; Can again did not arrive; the court, because of his contemporary prestige, treated him leniently.

source.zh: 時景帝輔政，召群官會議，粲又不到，朝廷以其時望，優容之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Jing assisted the government, he summoned the officials to a joint conference; Can again did not arrive; the court, because of his contemporary prestige, treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing called a plenary council; Can stayed away again, yet the court indulged him because of his moral weight.

entries.zh: 粲又稱疾，闔門不出。
entries.en: He pleaded illness once more and barred his gate.
entries.literal: Can again pleaded illness and shut his gate, not going out.

source.zh: 粲又稱疾，闔門不出。

translations.literal: Can again pleaded illness and shut his gate, not going out.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness once more and barred his gate.

entries.zh: 於是特詔為侍中，持節使於雍州。
entries.en: A special edict named him palace attendant with credentials and ordered him to Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon a special edict made him palace attendant with staff of authority and sent him on mission to Yongzhou.

source.zh: 於是特詔為侍中，持節使於雍州。

translations.literal: Thereupon a special edict made him palace attendant with staff of authority and sent him on mission to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict named him palace attendant with credentials and ordered him to Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 粲因陽狂不言，寢所乘車，足不履地。
entries.en: He feigned madness and fell silent, living in his carriage so his feet never touched earth.
entries.literal: Can therefore feigned madness and would not speak; he slept in the carriage he rode and his feet did not touch the ground.

source.zh: 粲因陽狂不言，寢所乘車，足不履地。

translations.literal: Can therefore feigned madness and would not speak; he slept in the carriage he rode and his feet did not touch the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned madness and fell silent, living in his carriage so his feet never touched earth.

entries.zh: 子孫恆侍左右，至有婚宦大事，輒密諮焉。
entries.en: Sons and grandsons waited on him always; even weddings and appointments they settled only after whispered questions at his pillow.
entries.literal: His sons and grandsons constantly attended at his side; even for great matters of marriage or office they secretly consulted him.

source.zh: 子孫恆侍左右，至有婚宦大事，輒密諮焉。

translations.literal: His sons and grandsons constantly attended at his side; even for great matters of marriage or office they secretly consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons waited on him always; even weddings and appointments they settled only after whispered questions at his pillow.

entries.zh: 合者則色無變，不合則眠寢不安，妻子以此知其旨。
entries.en: If he approved, his face stayed calm; if not, he tossed all night—so his household read his mind.
entries.literal: If it agreed, his color did not change; if it did not agree, then his sleep was restless; by this his wife and children knew his intent.

source.zh: 合者則色無變，不合則眠寢不安，妻子以此知其旨。

translations.literal: If it agreed, his color did not change; if it did not agree, then his sleep was restless; by this his wife and children knew his intent.
translations.idiomatic: If he approved, his face stayed calm; if not, he tossed all night—so his household read his mind.

entries.zh: 董璋，本梁之驍將也。
entries.en: Dong Zhang had been one of the Liang's fiercest generals.
entries.literal: Dong Zhang was originally a fierce general of the Liang.

source.zh: 董璋，本梁之驍將也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang was originally a fierce general of the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang had been one of the Liang's fiercest generals.

entries.zh: 幼與高季興、孔循俱事豪士李七郎為童仆。
entries.en: As a boy he served the swaggering Master Li the Seventh alongside Gao Jixing and Kong Xun as a household page.
entries.literal: In youth he with Gao Jixing and Kong Xun all served the bold man Master Li the Seventh as child servants.

source.zh: 幼與高季興、孔循俱事豪士李七郎為童仆。

translations.literal: In youth he with Gao Jixing and Kong Xun all served the bold man Master Li the Seventh as child servants.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he served the swaggering Master Li the Seventh alongside Gao Jixing and Kong Xun as a household page.

entries.zh: 李初名讓，常以厚賄奉梁祖，梁祖寵之，因畜為假子，賜姓朱，名友讓。
entries.en: Li, originally named Rang, lavished bribes on the Liang founder until the emperor favored him, adopted him as a son, granted the Zhu surname, and named him Yourang.
entries.literal: Li's original name was Rang; he constantly offered rich bribes to the Liang founder, who favored him and thereupon raised him as an adopted son, granting the surname Zhu and the name Yourang.

source.zh: 李初名讓，常以厚賄奉梁祖，梁祖寵之，因畜為假子，賜姓朱，名友讓。

translations.literal: Li's original name was Rang; he constantly offered rich bribes to the Liang founder, who favored him and thereupon raised him as an adopted son, granting the surname Zhu and the name Yourang.
translations.idiomatic: Li, originally named Rang, lavished bribes on the Liang founder until the emperor favored him, adopted him as a son, granted the Zhu surname, and named him Yourang.

entries.zh: 璋既壯，得隸於梁祖帳下，後以軍功遷為列校。
entries.en: When Zhang came of age he entered the Liang founder's service and rose through battlefield merit to company commander.
entries.literal: When Zhang had grown strong he came under the Liang founder's banner, and later through military merit was promoted to company commander.

source.zh: 璋既壯，得隸於梁祖帳下，後以軍功遷為列校。

translations.literal: When Zhang had grown strong he came under the Liang founder's banner, and later through military merit was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang came of age he entered the Liang founder's service and rose through battlefield merit to company commander.

entries.zh: 梁龍德末，潞州李繼韜送款於梁。
entries.en: Near the end of the Longde reign Li Jitao of Luzhou surrendered to the Liang.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang Longde, Luzhou's Li Jitao offered surrender to the Liang.

source.zh: 梁龍德末，潞州李繼韜送款於梁。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang Longde, Luzhou's Li Jitao offered surrender to the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Longde reign Li Jitao of Luzhou surrendered to the Liang.

entries.zh: 時潞將裴約方領兵戍澤州，不徇繼韜之命，據城以自固。
entries.en: The Lu general Pei Yue was then garrisoning Zezhou, refused Jitao's orders, and held the city on his own account.
entries.literal: At that time the Lu general Pei Yue was just leading troops garrisoning Ze Prefecture, did not follow Jitao's order, and held the city to firm himself.

source.zh: 時潞將裴約方領兵戍澤州，不徇繼韜之命，據城以自固。

translations.literal: At that time the Lu general Pei Yue was just leading troops garrisoning Ze Prefecture, did not follow Jitao's order, and held the city to firm himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu general Pei Yue was then garrisoning Zezhou, refused Jitao's orders, and held the city on his own account.

entries.zh: 梁末帝遣璋攻陷澤州，遂授澤州刺史。
entries.en: The last Liang emperor sent Zhang to capture Zezhou and appointed him its prefect.
