entries.literal: The Liang final emperor sent Zhang to attack and take Ze Prefecture, and thereupon appointed him prefect of Ze.

source.zh: 梁末帝遣璋攻陷澤州，遂授澤州刺史。

translations.literal: The Liang final emperor sent Zhang to attack and take Ze Prefecture, and thereupon appointed him prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: The last Liang emperor sent Zhang to capture Zezhou and appointed him its prefect.

entries.zh: 是歲，莊宗入汴，璋來朝，莊宗素聞其名，優以待之。
entries.en: That year, when Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhang came to court; Zhuangzong had long known his reputation and received him generously.
entries.literal: That year Zhuangzong entered Bian; Zhang came to court; Zhuangzong had long heard his name and treated him with favor.

source.zh: 是歲，莊宗入汴，璋來朝，莊宗素聞其名，優以待之。

translations.literal: That year Zhuangzong entered Bian; Zhang came to court; Zhuangzong had long heard his name and treated him with favor.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhang came to court; Zhuangzong had long known his reputation and received him generously.

entries.zh: 尋令卻赴舊任，歲餘代歸。
entries.en: He was soon sent back to his former post and returned to court a year later when relieved.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered to return to his old post; after more than a year he was replaced and came back.

source.zh: 尋令卻赴舊任，歲餘代歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to return to his old post; after more than a year he was replaced and came back.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent back to his former post and returned to court a year later when relieved.

entries.zh: 時郭崇韜當國，待璋尤厚。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao then dominated the government and treated Zhang with exceptional favor.
entries.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao held power and treated Zhang especially generously.

source.zh: 時郭崇韜當國，待璋尤厚。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao held power and treated Zhang especially generously.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao then dominated the government and treated Zhang with exceptional favor.

entries.zh: 同光三年夏，命為邠州留後，三年秋，正授旄鉞。
entries.en: In the summer of Tongguang 3 he was named acting governor of Binzhou; that autumn he received the full commissioner's insignia.
entries.literal: In summer of Tongguang year three he was ordered acting governor of Bin Prefecture; in autumn of year three he was formally given the banner and axe.

source.zh: 同光三年夏，命為邠州留後，三年秋，正授旄鉞。

translations.literal: In summer of Tongguang year three he was ordered acting governor of Bin Prefecture; in autumn of year three he was formally given the banner and axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tongguang 3 he was named acting governor of Binzhou; that autumn he received the full commissioner's insignia.

entries.zh: 九月，大舉伐蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬步都虞候。
entries.en: In the ninth month a major expedition against Shu was launched, with Zhang as superintendent of the right wing of the field army.
entries.literal: In the ninth month a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhang was made right-wing horse-and-foot superintendent of the field camp.

source.zh: 九月，大舉伐蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: In the ninth month a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhang was made right-wing horse-and-foot superintendent of the field camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month a major expedition against Shu was launched, with Zhang as superintendent of the right wing of the field army.

entries.zh: 時郭崇韜為招討使，凡有軍機，皆召璋參決。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao commanded the expedition and summoned Zhang to every council on military affairs.
entries.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao was campaign commissioner; whenever there was military planning Zhang was summoned to join in the decision.

source.zh: 時郭崇韜為招討使，凡有軍機，皆召璋參決。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao was campaign commissioner; whenever there was military planning Zhang was summoned to join in the decision.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao commanded the expedition and summoned Zhang to every council on military affairs.

entries.zh: 是冬，蜀平，以璋為劍南東川節度副大使，知節度事。
entries.en: Shu fell that winter, and Zhang was made deputy military governor of Eastern Chuan with full control of circuit affairs.
entries.literal: That winter Shu was pacified; Zhang was made deputy military governor of Eastern Chuan of Jiannan and managed circuit affairs.

source.zh: 是冬，蜀平，以璋為劍南東川節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: That winter Shu was pacified; Zhang was made deputy military governor of Eastern Chuan of Jiannan and managed circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shu fell that winter, and Zhang was made deputy military governor of Eastern Chuan with full control of circuit affairs.

entries.zh: 天成初，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: At the opening of the Tiancheng reign he was promoted to acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was added acting Grand Tutor.

source.zh: 天成初，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was added acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiancheng reign he was promoted to acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 二年，加同平章事。
entries.en: In the second year he was made a Fellow of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the second year he was added Fellow of the Secretariat.

source.zh: 二年，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was added Fellow of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made a Fellow of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 朕承先帝之靈，居至尊之位，涉道猶淺，經事未深，常懼昏蒙，不克負荷。
entries.en: Having inherited the late Emperor’s mandate and taken the throne, I am still shallow in the Way and inexperienced in governance, and I constantly fear that my dullness will leave me unequal to the burden.
entries.literal: We have received the spirit of the late Emperor and occupy the supreme position; our acquaintance with the Way is still shallow, our experience in affairs not yet deep, and we constantly fear dullness and obscurity, unable to bear the burden.

source.zh: 朕承先帝之靈，居至尊之位，涉道猶淺，經事未深，常懼昏蒙，不克負荷。

translations.literal: We have received the spirit of the late Emperor and occupy the supreme position; our acquaintance with the Way is still shallow, our experience in affairs not yet deep, and we constantly fear dullness and obscurity, unable to bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Having inherited the late Emperor’s mandate and taken the throne, I am still shallow in the Way and inexperienced in governance, and I constantly fear that my dullness will leave me unequal to the burden.

entries.zh: 自臨宸極，已過周星，至於刑政取舍之間，國家措置之事，豈能盡是，須有未周，朕猶自知，人豈不察。
entries.en: Since I ascended the throne more than a year has passed; in criminal law, policy, and state measures, not everything can be right—there are bound to be gaps. I know this myself; surely others see it too.
entries.literal: Since We took the imperial seat, a full year has passed; as to choices in punishments and government and measures for the state, how could all be correct? There must be points not fully covered—We ourselves still know this; would people not perceive it?

source.zh: 自臨宸極，已過周星，至於刑政取舍之間，國家措置之事，豈能盡是，須有未周，朕猶自知，人豈不察。

translations.literal: Since We took the imperial seat, a full year has passed; as to choices in punishments and government and measures for the state, how could all be correct? There must be points not fully covered—We ourselves still know this; would people not perceive it?
translations.idiomatic: Since I ascended the throne more than a year has passed; in criminal law, policy, and state measures, not everything can be right—there are bound to be gaps. I know this myself; surely others see it too.

entries.zh: 而在位者未有一人指朕躬之過失，食祿者曾無一言論時政之是非，豈朕之寡昧不足與言邪？
entries.en: Yet not one official in office has pointed out my personal faults, and not one salaried officer has spoken on whether current policy is right or wrong. Is my ignorance so complete that I am not worth addressing?
entries.literal: Yet among those in office not one has pointed out faults in Our person; among salary recipients not one word on whether current policy is right or wrong—Is it that Our scant understanding is unworthy of speech?

source.zh: 而在位者未有一人指朕躬之過失，食祿者曾無一言論時政之是非，豈朕之寡昧不足與言邪？

translations.literal: Yet among those in office not one has pointed out faults in Our person; among salary recipients not one word on whether current policy is right or wrong—Is it that Our scant understanding is unworthy of speech?
translations.idiomatic: Yet not one official in office has pointed out my personal faults, and not one salaried officer has spoken on whether current policy is right or wrong. Is my ignorance so complete that I am not worth addressing?

entries.zh: 豈人之循默未肯盡心邪？
entries.en: Or are men merely following custom and holding back their full loyalty?
entries.literal: Is it that people follow silence and are unwilling to give their full hearts?

source.zh: 豈人之循默未肯盡心邪？

translations.literal: Is it that people follow silence and are unwilling to give their full hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Or are men merely following custom and holding back their full loyalty?

entries.zh: 豈左右前後有所畏忌邪？
entries.en: Or do those around me harbor fears that keep them silent?
entries.literal: Is it that those at Our left and right, before and behind, have some fear and restraint?

source.zh: 豈左右前後有所畏忌邪？

translations.literal: Is it that those at Our left and right, before and behind, have some fear and restraint?
translations.idiomatic: Or do those around me harbor fears that keep them silent?

entries.zh: 豈高卑疏近自生間別邪？
entries.en: Or do rank and distance themselves create barriers between us?
entries.literal: Is it that high and low, distant and near, of themselves create separation and distinction?

source.zh: 豈高卑疏近自生間別邪？

translations.literal: Is it that high and low, distant and near, of themselves create separation and distinction?
translations.idiomatic: Or do rank and distance themselves create barriers between us?

entries.zh: 有司奏諡曰穆。
entries.en: The responsible offices memorialized posthumous title: Mu.
entries.literal: The responsible offices memorialized posthumous title: Mu.

source.zh: 有司奏諡曰穆。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized posthumous title: Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized posthumous title: Mu.

entries.zh: 太宗卽位，追崇曰穆太后。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Mu.
entries.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Mu.

source.zh: 太宗卽位，追崇曰穆太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Mu.

entries.zh: 三月，滄州節度使劉守文為弟守光所攻，遣人來乞兵討之。
entries.en: In the third month Liu Shouwen, governor of Cangzhou, came under attack from his brother Shouguang and sent asking for troops to strike back.
entries.literal: In the third month, Liu Shouwen, Military Governor of Cangzhou, was attacked by his brother Shouguang and sent men to request troops to campaign against him.

source.zh: 三月，滄州節度使劉守文為弟守光所攻，遣人來乞兵討之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Liu Shouwen, Military Governor of Cangzhou, was attacked by his brother Shouguang and sent men to request troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liu Shouwen, governor of Cangzhou, came under attack from his brother Shouguang and sent asking for troops to strike back.

entries.zh: 命皇弟舍利素、夷離蕭敵魯以兵會守文於北淖口。
entries.en: He commanded his brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to march and rendezvous with Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.
entries.literal: He ordered his imperial brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to lead troops to join Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.

source.zh: 命皇弟舍利素、夷離蕭敵魯以兵會守文於北淖口。

translations.literal: He ordered his imperial brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to lead troops to join Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded his brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to march and rendezvous with Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.

entries.zh: 進至橫海軍近澱，一鼓破之，守光潰去。
entries.en: Pushing to the flats near the Henghai garrison, they shattered the foe at a single drumbeat and Shouguang broke and ran.
entries.literal: Advancing to the marshland near the Henghai Army, they broke the enemy at the first assault and Shouguang fled in rout.

source.zh: 進至橫海軍近澱，一鼓破之，守光潰去。

translations.literal: Advancing to the marshland near the Henghai Army, they broke the enemy at the first assault and Shouguang fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing to the flats near the Henghai garrison, they shattered the foe at a single drumbeat and Shouguang broke and ran.

entries.zh: 因名北淖口為會盟口。
entries.en: Beinao Mouth was therefore renamed Alliance Mouth.
entries.literal: Because of this, Beinao Mouth was renamed Alliance Mouth.

source.zh: 因名北淖口為會盟口。

translations.literal: Because of this, Beinao Mouth was renamed Alliance Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Beinao Mouth was therefore renamed Alliance Mouth.

entries.zh: 二月戊午，以從弟迭栗底為迭烈府夷離。
entries.en: On wuwu day of the second month he named his cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Diela Prefecture.
entries.literal: On wuwu day in the second month, he appointed his younger cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Diela Prefecture.

source.zh: 二月戊午，以從弟迭栗底為迭烈府夷離。

translations.literal: On wuwu day in the second month, he appointed his younger cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Diela Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day of the second month he named his cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Diela Prefecture.

entries.zh: 是月，征黑車子室韋，降其八部。
entries.en: That same month he marched on the Black-Cart Shiwei and received the submission of all eight of their tribes.
entries.literal: That month, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei and brought their eight tribes to submission.

source.zh: 是月，征黑車子室韋，降其八部。

translations.literal: That month, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei and brought their eight tribes to submission.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he marched on the Black-Cart Shiwei and received the submission of all eight of their tribes.

entries.zh: 二月甲戌朔，梁均王友貞討殺其兄友，嗣立。
entries.en: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Zhu Youzhen, Liang's Prince of Jun, struck down his elder brother Zhu You and seized the throne.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Youzhen, Prince of Jun of Liang, attacked and killed his elder brother You, and succeeded to the throne.

source.zh: 二月甲戌朔，梁均王友貞討殺其兄友，嗣立。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Youzhen, Prince of Jun of Liang, attacked and killed his elder brother You, and succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Zhu Youzhen, Liang's Prince of Jun, struck down his elder brother Zhu You and seized the throne.

entries.zh: 章肅皇帝李胡。
entries.en: Li Hu, Emperor the Solemn and Respectful.
entries.literal: Emperor Li Hu the Solemn and Respectful.

translations.literal: Emperor Li Hu the Solemn and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu, Emperor the Solemn and Respectful.

source.literal: Emperor Li Hu the Solemn and Respectful.
source.idiomatic: Li Hu, Emperor the Solemn and Respectful.
source.translation: Li Hu, Emperor the Solemn and Respectful.

entries.zh: 宋王喜隱。
entries.en: Xiyin, Prince of Song.
entries.literal: Prince of Song, Xiyin.

translations.literal: Prince of Song, Xiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin, Prince of Song.

entries.zh: 留禮壽。
entries.en: Liulishou.
entries.literal: Liulishou.

translations.literal: Liulishou.
translations.idiomatic: Liulishou.

entries.zh: 衛王宛。
entries.en: Wan, Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Prince of Wei, Wan.

translations.literal: Prince of Wei, Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 魏王合祿。
entries.en: Helu, Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Prince of Wei, Helu.

translations.literal: Prince of Wei, Helu.
translations.idiomatic: Helu, Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 燕王吳哥。
entries.en: Wuge, Prince of Yan.
entries.literal: Prince of Yan, Wuge.

translations.literal: Prince of Yan, Wuge.
translations.idiomatic: Wuge, Prince of Yan.

entries.zh: 敵烈，朮烈，稱帝。
entries.en: Dilie and Shulie declared themselves emperors.
entries.literal: Dilie, Shulie—declared themselves emperors.

translations.literal: Dilie, Shulie—declared themselves emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Dilie and Shulie declared themselves emperors.

source.idiomatic: Dilie and Shulie declared themselves emperors.
source.translation: Dilie and Shulie declared themselves emperors.

entries.zh: 五月丙午，進河南王吐谷渾拾寅號驃騎大將軍。
entries.en: Fifth month, day bingwu: Murong Shibin of Henan was promoted to general-in-chief who spreads might.
entries.literal: Fifth month, day bingwu: Prince Murong Shibin of Henan was advanced to General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might.

source.zh: 五月丙午，進河南王吐谷渾拾寅號驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingwu: Prince Murong Shibin of Henan was advanced to General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day bingwu: Murong Shibin of Henan was promoted to general-in-chief who spreads might.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「宸運革命，引爵改封，宋氏第秩，雖宜省替，其有預效屯夷、宣力齊業者，一仍本封，無所減降。」
entries.en: An edict said: "The dynasty has turned; titles must be refitted. Song ranks should shrink—but men who proved themselves on the border or helped found Qi keep their old fiefs whole."
entries.literal: An edict said: "With the imperial fortune revolutionized, ranks and fiefs are changed; Song titles should indeed be reduced with the times—yet those who early showed merit on the frontiers or labored for Qi's founding shall keep their original fiefs without reduction."

source.zh: 詔曰：「宸運革命，引爵改封，宋氏第秩，雖宜省替，其有預效屯夷、宣力齊業者，一仍本封，無所減降。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "With the imperial fortune revolutionized, ranks and fiefs are changed; Song titles should indeed be reduced with the times—yet those who early showed merit on the frontiers or labored for Qi's founding shall keep their original fiefs without reduction."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The dynasty has turned; titles must be refitted. Song ranks should shrink—but men who proved themselves on the border or helped found Qi keep their old fiefs whole."

entries.zh: 有司奏留襄陽郡公張敬兒等六十二人，除廣興郡公沈曇亮等百二十二人。
entries.en: The ministries listed sixty-two men, including Zhang Jing'er of Xiangyang, whose titles stood; one hundred twenty-two, including Shen Tanliang of Guangxing, were struck.
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that sixty-two men including Zhang Jing'er, Marquis of Xiangyang, were retained; one hundred twenty-two men including Shen Tanliang, Duke of Guangxing, were removed.

source.zh: 有司奏留襄陽郡公張敬兒等六十二人，除廣興郡公沈曇亮等百二十二人。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that sixty-two men including Zhang Jing'er, Marquis of Xiangyang, were retained; one hundred twenty-two men including Shen Tanliang, Duke of Guangxing, were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries listed sixty-two men, including Zhang Jing'er of Xiangyang, whose titles stood; one hundred twenty-two, including Shen Tanliang of Guangxing, were struck.

entries.zh: 改《元嘉曆》爲《建元曆》，木德盛卯終未，以正月卯祖，十二月未臘。
entries.en: The Yuanjia calendar became the Jianyuan calendar. Wood ruled from mao to wei; the year opened in mao and closed with the wei sacrifice.
entries.literal: The Yuanjia Calendar was changed to the Jianyuan Calendar; the Wood phase flourished from mao through wei; the first month took mao as ancestor, the twelfth month had wei as year-end sacrifice.

source.zh: 改《元嘉曆》爲《建元曆》，木德盛卯終未，以正月卯祖，十二月未臘。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia Calendar was changed to the Jianyuan Calendar; the Wood phase flourished from mao through wei; the first month took mao as ancestor, the twelfth month had wei as year-end sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia calendar became the Jianyuan calendar. Wood ruled from mao to wei; the year opened in mao and closed with the wei sacrifice.

entries.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「設募取將，懸賞購士，蓋出權宜，非曰恆制。
entries.en: Day dingwei: an edict said: "Bounty lists for captains and price tags for soldiers are expedients, not permanent law.
entries.literal: On day dingwei an edict said: "Setting rewards to take generals and posting bounties to buy warriors are measures of expediency, not the constant system.

source.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「設募取將，懸賞購士，蓋出權宜，非曰恆制。

translations.literal: On day dingwei an edict said: "Setting rewards to take generals and posting bounties to buy warriors are measures of expediency, not the constant system.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingwei: an edict said: "Bounty lists for captains and price tags for soldiers are expedients, not permanent law.

entries.zh: 頃世艱險，浸以成俗，且長逋逸，開罪山湖。
entries.en: Hard times made the practice common; men fled for years and crime hid in the hills.
entries.literal: In recent generations hardship has deepened until it became custom, and long flight opened the mountains and lakes to crime.

source.zh: 頃世艱險，浸以成俗，且長逋逸，開罪山湖。

translations.literal: In recent generations hardship has deepened until it became custom, and long flight opened the mountains and lakes to crime.
translations.idiomatic: Hard times made the practice common; men fled for years and crime hid in the hills.

entries.zh: 是爲黥刑不辱，亡竄無咎。
entries.en: Branding no longer shamed them; outlaw life carried no stain.
entries.literal: Thus tattoo punishment did not shame them, and flight brought no blame.

source.zh: 是爲黥刑不辱，亡竄無咎。

translations.literal: Thus tattoo punishment did not shame them, and flight brought no blame.
translations.idiomatic: Branding no longer shamed them; outlaw life carried no stain.

entries.zh: 自今以後，可斷衆募。」
entries.en: Hereafter, open recruiting is forbidden."
entries.literal: From this time forward, mass recruitment may be ended."

source.zh: 自今以後，可斷衆募。」

translations.literal: From this time forward, mass recruitment may be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, open recruiting is forbidden."

entries.zh: 壬子，詔封佐命文武功臣新除司徒褚淵等三十一人，進爵增戶各有差。
entries.en: Day renzi: thirty-one founding ministers, including the new grand minister Chu Yuan, were enfeoffed; rank and household quotas rose by merit.
entries.literal: On day renzi an edict enfeoffed thirty-one men including the newly appointed Grand Minister Chu Yuan, meritorious civil and military ministers who aided the founding, with advancement of rank and increase of households each according to grade.

source.zh: 壬子，詔封佐命文武功臣新除司徒褚淵等三十一人，進爵增戶各有差。

translations.literal: On day renzi an edict enfeoffed thirty-one men including the newly appointed Grand Minister Chu Yuan, meritorious civil and military ministers who aided the founding, with advancement of rank and increase of households each according to grade.
translations.idiomatic: Day renzi: thirty-one founding ministers, including the new grand minister Chu Yuan, were enfeoffed; rank and household quotas rose by merit.

entries.zh: 乙卯，河南王吐谷渾拾寅奉表貢獻。
entries.en: Day yimao: Murong Shibin of Henan sent tribute with a memorial.
entries.literal: On day yimao Prince Murong Shibin of Henan presented a memorial with tribute.

source.zh: 乙卯，河南王吐谷渾拾寅奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: On day yimao Prince Murong Shibin of Henan presented a memorial with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Day yimao: Murong Shibin of Henan sent tribute with a memorial.

entries.zh: 丙辰，詔遣大使分行四方，遣兼散騎常侍十二人巡行。
entries.en: Day bingchen: great envoys were sent on circuit through the realm, twelve of them bearing the concurrent title of regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: On day bingchen an edict sent great envoys to tour the four quarters, dispatching twelve men as concurrent Regular Attendants of Scattered Cavalry to make the rounds.

source.zh: 丙辰，詔遣大使分行四方，遣兼散騎常侍十二人巡行。

translations.literal: On day bingchen an edict sent great envoys to tour the four quarters, dispatching twelve men as concurrent Regular Attendants of Scattered Cavalry to make the rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingchen: great envoys were sent on circuit through the realm, twelve of them bearing the concurrent title of regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

entries.zh: 以交寧道遠，不遣使。
entries.en: Jiao and Ning were too distant; no envoys went there.
entries.literal: Because Jiao and Ning were far, no envoys were sent.

source.zh: 以交寧道遠，不遣使。

translations.literal: Because Jiao and Ning were far, no envoys were sent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and Ning were too distant; no envoys went there.

entries.zh: 己未，汝陰王薨，追諡爲宋順帝，終禮依魏元、晉恭帝故事。
entries.en: Day jiwei: the Prince of Runan died and was posthumously styled Emperor Shun of Song; his funeral followed Wei's Emperor Yuan and Jin's Emperor Gong.
entries.literal: On day jiwei the Prince of Runan died; he was posthumously titled Emperor Shun of Song; final rites followed the precedents of Emperor Yuan of Wei and Emperor Gong of Jin.

source.zh: 己未，汝陰王薨，追諡爲宋順帝，終禮依魏元、晉恭帝故事。

translations.literal: On day jiwei the Prince of Runan died; he was posthumously titled Emperor Shun of Song; final rites followed the precedents of Emperor Yuan of Wei and Emperor Gong of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiwei: the Prince of Runan died and was posthumously styled Emperor Shun of Song; his funeral followed Wei's Emperor Yuan and Jin's Emperor Gong.

entries.zh: 辛酉，陰安公劉燮等伏誅。
entries.en: Day xinyou: Liu Xie, Duke of Yin'an, and his party were put to death.
entries.literal: On day xinyou Liu Xie, Duke of Yin'an, and others were executed.

source.zh: 辛酉，陰安公劉燮等伏誅。

translations.literal: On day xinyou Liu Xie, Duke of Yin'an, and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinyou: Liu Xie, Duke of Yin'an, and his party were put to death.

entries.zh: 追封諡上兄道度爲衡陽元王，道生爲始安貞王。
entries.en: The elder brothers were honored after death: Daodu as Prince Yuan of Hengyang, Daosheng as Prince Zhen of Shian.
entries.literal: Posthumous enfeoffment was granted: the Emperor's elder brother Daodu was titled Prince Yuan of Hengyang; Daosheng was titled Prince Zhen of Shian.

source.zh: 追封諡上兄道度爲衡陽元王，道生爲始安貞王。

translations.literal: Posthumous enfeoffment was granted: the Emperor's elder brother Daodu was titled Prince Yuan of Hengyang; Daosheng was titled Prince Zhen of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: The elder brothers were honored after death: Daodu as Prince Yuan of Hengyang, Daosheng as Prince Zhen of Shian.

entries.zh: 丙寅，追尊皇考曰宣皇帝，皇妣爲孝皇后，妃爲昭皇后。
entries.en: Day bingyin: the imperial father was styled Emperor Xuan, the imperial mother Empress Xiao, the consort Empress Zhao.
entries.literal: On day bingyin the Imperial Father was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan; the Imperial Mother as Empress Xiao; the consort as Empress Zhao.

source.zh: 丙寅，追尊皇考曰宣皇帝，皇妣爲孝皇后，妃爲昭皇后。

translations.literal: On day bingyin the Imperial Father was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan; the Imperial Mother as Empress Xiao; the consort as Empress Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingyin: the imperial father was styled Emperor Xuan, the imperial mother Empress Xiao, the consort Empress Zhao.

entries.zh: 衡陽元王道度，太祖長兄也。
entries.en: Prince Daodu of Hengyang (posthumous title Yuan) was Emperor Gao's elder brother.
entries.literal: Prince Yuan of Hengyang Daodu was the founding emperor's elder brother.

source.zh: 衡陽元王道度，太祖長兄也。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan of Hengyang Daodu was the founding emperor's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daodu of Hengyang (posthumous title Yuan) was Emperor Gao's elder brother.

entries.zh: 與太祖俱受學雷次宗。
entries.en: He and Emperor Gao both studied under Lei Cizong.
entries.literal: Together with the founding emperor he studied under Lei Cizong.

source.zh: 與太祖俱受學雷次宗。

translations.literal: Together with the founding emperor he studied under Lei Cizong.
translations.idiomatic: He and Emperor Gao both studied under Lei Cizong.

entries.zh: 宣帝問二兒學業，次宗答曰：「其兄外朗，其弟內潤，皆良璞也。」
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan inquired about the two boys' studies, Cizong answered, "The elder is bright in manner, the younger rich in inner quality—both are fine uncut jade."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan asked about the two sons' studies; Cizong replied: "The elder is outwardly bright, the younger inwardly rich; both are fine uncut jade."

source.zh: 宣帝問二兒學業，次宗答曰：「其兄外朗，其弟內潤，皆良璞也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan asked about the two sons' studies; Cizong replied: "The elder is outwardly bright, the younger inwardly rich; both are fine uncut jade."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan inquired about the two boys' studies, Cizong answered, "The elder is bright in manner, the younger rich in inner quality—both are fine uncut jade."

entries.zh: 隨宣帝征伐，仕至安定太守，卒於宋世。
entries.en: He followed Emperor Xuan on campaign, rose to Administrator of Anding, and died during the Song.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor Xuan on campaigns, served up to Administrator of Anding, and died in the Song period.

source.zh: 隨宣帝征伐，仕至安定太守，卒於宋世。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xuan on campaigns, served up to Administrator of Anding, and died in the Song period.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xuan on campaign, rose to Administrator of Anding, and died during the Song.

entries.zh: 建元二年，追加封謚。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianyuan he received a posthumous enfeoffment and title.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.

source.zh: 建元二年，追加封謚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan he received a posthumous enfeoffment and title.

entries.zh: 無子，太祖以第十一子鈞繼道度後。
entries.en: He had no sons, so Emperor Gao had his eleventh son, Jun, succeed Daodu as heir.
entries.literal: He had no sons; the founding emperor had his eleventh son Jun succeed Daodu's line.

source.zh: 無子，太祖以第十一子鈞繼道度後。

translations.literal: He had no sons; the founding emperor had his eleventh son Jun succeed Daodu's line.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, so Emperor Gao had his eleventh son, Jun, succeed Daodu as heir.

entries.zh: 杞，字集功。
entries.en: His son Qi, styled Jigong.
entries.literal: Qi, styled Jigong.

source.zh: 杞，字集功。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Jigong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, styled Jigong.

entries.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，官編修。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-first year of Kangxi and served as a Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: A jinshi of the fifty-first year of Kangxi; he served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

source.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifty-first year of Kangxi; he served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-first year of Kangxi and served as a Hanlin compiler.

entries.zh: 由甘肅布政使巡撫陝西，入為宗人府府丞。
entries.en: After serving as Gansu treasurer and governor of Shaanxi, he was recalled to the capital as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court.
entries.literal: From Gansu provincial treasurer he became governor of Shaanxi; he then entered the capital as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court.

source.zh: 由甘肅布政使巡撫陝西，入為宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: From Gansu provincial treasurer he became governor of Shaanxi; he then entered the capital as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Gansu treasurer and governor of Shaanxi, he was recalled to the capital as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 予休致，卒。
entries.en: He retired from office and later died.
entries.literal: He was granted retirement, then died.

source.zh: 予休致，卒。

translations.literal: He was granted retirement, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and later died.

entries.zh: 武進升，山西寧鄉人，其後改籍江南江寧。
entries.en: Wu Jinsheng was a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi and later transferred his household register to Jiangning in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Wu Jinsheng, a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi, later changed his registration to Jiangning in Jiangnan.

source.zh: 武進升，山西寧鄉人，其後改籍江南江寧。

translations.literal: Wu Jinsheng, a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi, later changed his registration to Jiangning in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jinsheng was a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi and later transferred his household register to Jiangning in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 初以張姓入伍。
entries.en: He first enlisted under the surname Zhang.
entries.literal: At first he entered the ranks under the surname Zhang.

source.zh: 初以張姓入伍。

translations.literal: At first he entered the ranks under the surname Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He first enlisted under the surname Zhang.

entries.zh: 稍遷浙江溫州鎮標守備。
entries.en: He rose gradually to garrison commander of the Wenzhou garrison standard in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to garrison commander of the Wenzhou garrison standard in Zhejiang.

source.zh: 稍遷浙江溫州鎮標守備。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to garrison commander of the Wenzhou garrison standard in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to garrison commander of the Wenzhou garrison standard in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 雍正初，閩浙總督滿保疏薦，引見，授三等侍衛，屬怡親王允祥。
entries.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign, Fujian–Zhejiang Governor-General Manbao recommended him by memorial; after audience he was made a third-rank guardsman and assigned to Prince Yi Yinxiang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Fujian–Zhejiang Governor-General Manbao memorialized recommending him; after audience he was appointed a third-rank guardsman and attached to Prince Yi Yinxiang.

source.zh: 雍正初，閩浙總督滿保疏薦，引見，授三等侍衛，屬怡親王允祥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Fujian–Zhejiang Governor-General Manbao memorialized recommending him; after audience he was appointed a third-rank guardsman and attached to Prince Yi Yinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign, Fujian–Zhejiang Governor-General Manbao recommended him by memorial; after audience he was made a third-rank guardsman and assigned to Prince Yi Yinxiang.

entries.zh: 尋外授江寧游擊。
entries.en: He was soon posted outside the capital as colonel at Jiangning.
entries.literal: Soon he was sent outside the capital as colonel at Jiangning.

source.zh: 尋外授江寧游擊。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent outside the capital as colonel at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted outside the capital as colonel at Jiangning.

entries.zh: 累遷福建陸路提督。
entries.en: He rose through several posts to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.
entries.literal: He was promoted through several posts to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.

source.zh: 累遷福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.

entries.zh: 言：「閩省不習騎射，加意督率，弓力漸增。
entries.en: He reported: "Fujian troops were unskilled in mounted archery, but under close supervision bow strength has steadily improved.
entries.literal: He reported: "Fujian troops are unaccustomed to mounted archery; with special attention to training and command, bow strength has gradually increased.

source.zh: 言：「閩省不習騎射，加意督率，弓力漸增。

translations.literal: He reported: "Fujian troops are unaccustomed to mounted archery; with special attention to training and command, bow strength has gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Fujian troops were unskilled in mounted archery, but under close supervision bow strength has steadily improved.

entries.zh: 馬兵出馬收馬較前改觀。」
entries.en: Cavalry turnout and the return of mounts are markedly better than before."
entries.literal: Cavalry turnout and return of horses show marked improvement over before."

source.zh: 馬兵出馬收馬較前改觀。」

translations.literal: Cavalry turnout and return of horses show marked improvement over before."
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry turnout and the return of mounts are markedly better than before."

entries.zh: 高宗諭以「如此方不負任使，然亦不可欲速，尤貴為之以實，要之以久」。
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor replied: "That is how you fulfill your charge—but do not hurry. What matters is solid effort sustained over the long term."
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor instructed him: "Only thus do you not fail your commission; yet you must not seek speed—what matters most is doing the work in earnest and sustaining it over time."

source.zh: 高宗諭以「如此方不負任使，然亦不可欲速，尤貴為之以實，要之以久」。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor instructed him: "Only thus do you not fail your commission; yet you must not seek speed—what matters most is doing the work in earnest and sustaining it over time."
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor replied: "That is how you fulfill your charge—but do not hurry. What matters is solid effort sustained over the long term."

entries.zh: 進升與總督喀爾吉善忤，疏言：「喀爾吉善外似和平，心實剛愎。
entries.en: Jinsheng fell out with Governor-General Ka'erjishan and memorialized: "Ka'erjishan seems mild in manner but is in fact stubborn and overbearing.
entries.literal: Jinsheng clashed with Governor-General Ka'erjishan and memorialized: "Ka'erjishan appears mild outwardly but is in fact stubborn and self-willed.

source.zh: 進升與總督喀爾吉善忤，疏言：「喀爾吉善外似和平，心實剛愎。

translations.literal: Jinsheng clashed with Governor-General Ka'erjishan and memorialized: "Ka'erjishan appears mild outwardly but is in fact stubborn and self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsheng fell out with Governor-General Ka'erjishan and memorialized: "Ka'erjishan seems mild in manner but is in fact stubborn and overbearing.

entries.zh: 令臣密察水師提督張天駿營伍，臣辭以水師非所轄。
entries.en: He ordered me to inspect Naval Commander Zhang Tianjun's camps in secret, but I declined because the navy is outside my jurisdiction.
entries.literal: He ordered me secretly to inspect the camps of Naval Commander Zhang Tianjun, but I declined on the ground that the navy is outside my jurisdiction.

source.zh: 令臣密察水師提督張天駿營伍，臣辭以水師非所轄。

translations.literal: He ordered me secretly to inspect the camps of Naval Commander Zhang Tianjun, but I declined on the ground that the navy is outside my jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered me to inspect Naval Commander Zhang Tianjun's camps in secret, but I declined because the navy is outside my jurisdiction.

entries.zh: 督臣正言厲色，必令臣密察。
entries.en: The governor spoke sternly and insisted that I carry out the secret inspection.
entries.literal: The governor spoke sternly and insisted that I conduct the secret inspection.

source.zh: 督臣正言厲色，必令臣密察。

translations.literal: The governor spoke sternly and insisted that I conduct the secret inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The governor spoke sternly and insisted that I carry out the secret inspection.

entries.zh: 及察知水師陋規，告之督臣，督臣置不問，反與天駿契合。
entries.en: When I uncovered corrupt practices in the navy and reported them, the governor ignored them and instead grew close to Tianjun.
entries.literal: When I found corrupt practices in the navy and reported them to the governor, he ignored them and instead became intimate with Tianjun.

source.zh: 及察知水師陋規，告之督臣，督臣置不問，反與天駿契合。

translations.literal: When I found corrupt practices in the navy and reported them to the governor, he ignored them and instead became intimate with Tianjun.
translations.idiomatic: When I uncovered corrupt practices in the navy and reported them, the governor ignored them and instead grew close to Tianjun.

entries.zh: 臣察漳州營馬值，總兵馬負書為督臣舊部，巧為徇私。
entries.en: When I inspected horse prices in the Zhangzhou garrison, Regional Commander Ma Fushu—an old subordinate of the governor—cleverly bent the rules in his favor.
entries.literal: When I inspected horse prices in the Zhangzhou garrison, Regional Commander Ma Fushu, an old subordinate of the governor, artfully showed favoritism.

source.zh: 臣察漳州營馬值，總兵馬負書為督臣舊部，巧為徇私。

translations.literal: When I inspected horse prices in the Zhangzhou garrison, Regional Commander Ma Fushu, an old subordinate of the governor, artfully showed favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: When I inspected horse prices in the Zhangzhou garrison, Regional Commander Ma Fushu—an old subordinate of the governor—cleverly bent the rules in his favor.

entries.zh: 令臣無地自容。」
entries.en: I was left utterly humiliated."
entries.literal: This left me with no place to hide my shame."

source.zh: 令臣無地自容。」

translations.literal: This left me with no place to hide my shame."
translations.idiomatic: I was left utterly humiliated."

entries.zh: 又疏言喀爾吉善衰憊狀，上斥進升支離狂率。
entries.en: He also memorialized on Ka'erjishan's declining health; the emperor rebuked Jinsheng for rambling and reckless accusations.
entries.literal: He also memorialized on Ka'erjishan's enfeebled condition; the emperor rebuked Jinsheng for incoherent and reckless speech.

source.zh: 又疏言喀爾吉善衰憊狀，上斥進升支離狂率。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on Ka'erjishan's enfeebled condition; the emperor rebuked Jinsheng for incoherent and reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on Ka'erjishan's declining health; the emperor rebuked Jinsheng for rambling and reckless accusations.

entries.zh: 喀爾吉善亦劾進升徇所屬，縱兵行竊。
entries.en: Ka'erjishan also impeached Jinsheng for favoring his men and allowing troops to plunder.
entries.literal: Ka'erjishan also impeached Jinsheng for indulging his subordinates and allowing troops to steal.

source.zh: 喀爾吉善亦劾進升徇所屬，縱兵行竊。

translations.literal: Ka'erjishan also impeached Jinsheng for indulging his subordinates and allowing troops to steal.
translations.idiomatic: Ka'erjishan also impeached Jinsheng for favoring his men and allowing troops to plunder.

entries.zh: 因左授江南狼山鎮總兵，進升疏謝，諭曰：「汝無他過，祗好勝多事，故左授示薄懲。
entries.en: He was demoted to regional commander of the Langshan garrison in Jiangnan; in his memorial of thanks he was told: "You have no other fault except competitiveness and meddling; the demotion is meant as a mild warning.
entries.literal: He was therefore demoted to regional commander of the Langshan garrison in Jiangnan; Jinsheng memorialized thanks, and was instructed: "You have no other fault—only love of rivalry and meddling—so the demotion is a light punishment.

source.zh: 因左授江南狼山鎮總兵，進升疏謝，諭曰：「汝無他過，祗好勝多事，故左授示薄懲。

translations.literal: He was therefore demoted to regional commander of the Langshan garrison in Jiangnan; Jinsheng memorialized thanks, and was instructed: "You have no other fault—only love of rivalry and meddling—so the demotion is a light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to regional commander of the Langshan garrison in Jiangnan; in his memorial of thanks he was told: "You have no other fault except competitiveness and meddling; the demotion is meant as a mild warning.

entries.zh: 若不知改，或遂委靡，一切姑息，皆不可也。」
entries.en: If you fail to reform, or sink into slack indulgence, either course is unacceptable."
entries.literal: If you do not reform, or instead become slack and indulge everything, neither is acceptable."

source.zh: 若不知改，或遂委靡，一切姑息，皆不可也。」

translations.literal: If you do not reform, or instead become slack and indulge everything, neither is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to reform, or sink into slack indulgence, either course is unacceptable."

entries.zh: 居數月，擢江南提督，以老罷。
entries.en: Within a few months he was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan; he later retired on account of age.
entries.literal: After several months he was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan; later he retired because of age.

source.zh: 居數月，擢江南提督，以老罷。

translations.literal: After several months he was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan; later he retired because of age.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan; he later retired on account of age.

entries.zh: 再起，終浙江提督。
entries.en: Called back to service, he ended his career as provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Recalled to service, he ended as provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

source.zh: 再起，終浙江提督。

translations.literal: Recalled to service, he ended as provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to service, he ended his career as provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 卒，年八十餘，諡良毅。
entries.en: He died in his eighties and was posthumously titled Liangyi.
entries.literal: He died at over eighty and was given the posthumous title Liangyi.

source.zh: 卒，年八十餘，諡良毅。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty and was given the posthumous title Liangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties and was posthumously titled Liangyi.

entries.zh: 族孫瑞昌，充北路營官，俄陷黑河，與統領崇玉同戰歿。
entries.en: His clansman Ruichang served as northern-route camp officer; when the Russians took Heihe he died fighting beside Commander Chongyu.
entries.literal: His clansman Ruichang served as northern-route camp officer; when the Russians took Heihe he fell in battle with Commander Chongyu.

source.zh: 族孫瑞昌，充北路營官，俄陷黑河，與統領崇玉同戰歿。

translations.literal: His clansman Ruichang served as northern-route camp officer; when the Russians took Heihe he fell in battle with Commander Chongyu.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Ruichang served as northern-route camp officer; when the Russians took Heihe he died fighting beside Commander Chongyu.

entries.zh: 湣公六年，孔子適陳。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Duke Min's reign, Confucius went to Chen.
entries.literal: In Duke Min's sixth year, Kong Qiu went to Chen.

entries.zh: 吳王夫差伐陳，取三邑而去。
entries.en: King Fuchai of Wu attacked Chen, took three cities, and left.
entries.literal: King Fu Cha of Wu attacked Chen, took three cities, and left.

entries.zh: 十三年，吳復來伐陳，陳告急楚，楚昭王來救，軍於城父，吳師去。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, Wu again attacked Chen. Chen urgently appealed to Chu, and King Zhao of Chu came to its rescue, stationing his army at Chengfu. The Wu troops withdrew.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, Wu again came to attack Chen. Chen reported urgently to Chu. King Zhao of Chu came to save them and stationed at Cheng Fu. The Wu troops left.

entries.zh: 楚王宣言曰：「我先元王，高帝少弟也，封三十二城。
entries.en: The King of Chu openly proclaimed: "My ancestor, King Yuan, was the younger brother of Emperor Gao and was enfeoffed with thirty-two cities.

entries.zh: 今地邑益少，我欲與廣陵王共發兵云。
entries.en: Now our territory and towns grow ever fewer. I intend to join with the King of Guangling in raising troops.
entries.literal: Now land and townships increasingly few, I wish to together with the King of Guangling raise troops.

entries.zh: ［立］廣陵王為上，我復王楚三十二城，如元王時。」
entries.en: We shall set up the King of Guangling as the supreme ruler, and I shall once again reign over Chu with thirty-two cities, as in the days of King Yuan."

entries.zh: 天子以骨肉之故，不忍致法於胥，下詔書無治廣陵王，獨誅首惡楚王。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven, out of consideration for their bond of blood, could not bear to apply the full force of the law to Xu. He issued an edict sparing the King of Guangling from prosecution and executed only the chief culprit, the King of Chu.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven because of flesh and blood, could not bear to apply law to Xu, issued edict not to punish King Xu of Guangling, alone execute chief evil King of Chu.

source.zh: 天子以骨肉之故，不忍致法於胥，下詔書無治廣陵王，獨誅首惡楚王。

entries.en: Later, Xu again resorted to sorcerous curses and plotted rebellion. He committed suicide, and his kingdom was abolished.

entries.en: In office he was lax and brought no impeachments.

entries.en: He was transferred to Director of the National University and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education. For memorializing to buy another man's field and refusing to pay the price, Left Assistant Xun Chisong of the Department of State Affairs memorialized: "To seek fields and houses was despised by the worthies of old.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Director of the National University and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; for memorializing to buy someone's field and refusing to return payment, Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs Xun Chisong memorialized saying: "Seeking fields and houses—former worthies despised this.

entries.zh: 延之唯利是視，輕冒陳聞，依傍詔恩，拒捍餘直，垂及周年，猶不畢了，昧利苟得，無所顧忌。
entries.en: Yanzhi looks only to profit, rashly petitioned the throne, leaned on imperial grace, and resisted paying the balance. Nearly a year has passed and the matter is still unsettled. Blinded by gain, he grasps without scruple.
entries.literal: Yanzhi looks only to profit, rashly ventured memorial, leaning on edict grace, resisting the remaining payment—nearly a full year and still not concluded; blinded by profit and grasping gain, without regard for anything.

source.zh: 延之唯利是視，輕冒陳聞，依傍詔恩，拒捍餘直，垂及周年，猶不畢了，昧利苟得，無所顧忌。

entries.zh: 延之昔坐事屏斥，復蒙抽進，而曾不悛革，怨誹無已。
entries.en: Yanzhi was once dismissed for an offense, then favored again with promotion, yet he never reformed and his resentment and slander never ceased.
entries.literal: Yanzhi once for an affair was expelled and screened, again received selection and advancement, yet never reformed, resentment and slander without end.

source.zh: 延之昔坐事屏斥，復蒙抽進，而曾不悛革，怨誹無已。

entries.en: His companions were vulgar rabble; he wallowed in wine and brew, recklessly spread ridicule, and slandered court officials.
entries.literal: Companions were vulgar rabble, sunk in yeasts and brews, recklessly raising ridicule, calumniating court gentlemen.

entries.zh: 外示寡求，內懷奔競，干祿祈遷，不知極已，預讌班觴，肆罵上席。
entries.en: Outwardly he showed few desires; inwardly he raced for advancement, sought salary and prayed for promotion, and knew no limit. At banquets by rank he wantonly reviled his superiors.

entries.zh: 山海含容，每存遵養，愛兼彫蟲，未忍遐棄，而驕放不節，日月彌著。
entries.en: Like mountains and seas the throne contains and tolerates, always nurturing those it keeps; it loves even the smallest talent and is loath to cast them off—yet his pride and license grow more flagrant day by day.
entries.literal: Mountains and seas contain and tolerate, always preserving followed nurture; love extending even to carved insects, not bearing to cast far away—but pride and license without restraint grow day by day.

entries.zh: 臣聞聲問過情，孟軻所恥，況聲非外來，問由己出，雖心智薄劣，而高自比擬，客氣虛張，曾無愧畏，豈可復弼亮五教，增曜台階。
entries.en: Your servant has heard that reputation exceeding the truth was what Mencius despised—how much more when the reputation is not given from outside but sought by oneself! Though his mind and talent are slight, he compares himself to the great; his manner is inflated with false pride and he knows no shame. How can he again assist and illumine the five teachings and add luster to the terrace steps?
entries.literal: Your servant hears: reputation and inquiry exceeding truth—Mencius was ashamed of this; how much more when reputation is not from outside but inquiry from oneself issuing! Though mind and wisdom are thin and inferior, yet he highly compares himself; guest air vainly inflated, never having shame and fear—how could he again assist and brighten the five teachings, add luster to the terrace steps?

source.zh: 臣聞聲問過情，孟軻所恥，況聲非外來，問由己出，雖心智薄劣，而高自比擬，客氣虛張，曾無愧畏，豈可復弼亮五教，增曜台階。

entries.en: Moreover, my ceremonial robes surpass those of the emperor's sons, my post as Metropolitan Governor ranks second only to the imperial branches, lands are granted to make me a feudatory lord, and gold seals establish a state—how am I to comport myself? By the world's measure it violates proper allotment.

entries.en: He begged audience; the emperor was flying hawks in the park. Weihan withdrew: “Jin’s altars will run dry!”
entries.literal: He asked audience again; the emperor was training hawks in the park and had no time. Weihan withdrew and sighed: “Jin will offer no blood at the altars!”

source.zh: 又求见帝，帝方调鹰于苑中，不暇见，维翰退而叹曰：「晋不血食矣！」

translations.literal: He asked audience again; the emperor was training hawks in the park and had no time. Weihan withdrew and sighed: “Jin will offer no blood at the altars!”
